ABSTRACT

This study, entitled *Noun Phrases in the Journal Article Beyond Film: Exploring the Content of Movie* by John Scacco, aims to identify and classify various types of noun phrases, as well as to analyze their internal functions within the text. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data comprising noun phrases were extracted from the four-page article by John Scacco. Subsequently, the internal functions of these noun phrases were examined based on the theoretical framework proposed by Aarts and Aarts (1982). 

The findings reveal that a total of 90 noun phrases occur within the article. These noun phrases function in three primary roles: head, determiner, and modifier. Among these, the head function is the most prevalent, with 65 occurrences. Determiners appear 22 times, which include 12 pre-determiners, 5 central determiners, and 3 post-determiners. Modifiers account for 9 instances, comprising 3 pre-modifiers and 6 post-modifiers, while discontinuous modifiers were absent in the data. Furthermore, the study categorizes internal noun phrase functions into pre-modifier, post-modifier, and discontinuous modifier types. Specifically, pre-modifiers identified include adjective phrases (1 occurrence), noun phrases (1 occurrence), and classifying genitives (2 occurrences). Post-modifiers are realized through prepositional phrases (1 occurrence), finite clauses (2 occurrences), and infinitive clauses (1 occurrence). Notably, neither adjective phrases nor adverb phrases were observed as modifiers in this analysis.

KEYWORDS: Internal Function, Noun Phrase, Beyond Film: Exploring the Content of Movie, John Scacco

This study aims to examine the extent to which the leadership of the village head influences the enhancement of public awareness regarding the payment of land and building taxes in Kaayuran Village, South District, within Langowan District, Minahasa. Specifically, the research seeks to analyze the impact of the village head's leadership on increasing tax payment awareness among the local community.

Employing a quantitative research design, the study utilizes descriptive analysis based on data collected through questionnaires distributed to 53 respondents. The data collection was complemented by observational techniques. The analysis involved frequency distribution tables, product-moment correlation, and simple linear regression methods.

The results indicate that respondents' perceptions of the village head's leadership fall predominantly within the class interval of 22–25, with a frequency of 25 respondents (47.2%), categorizing the leadership variable (X) as "high." Similarly, public awareness regarding payment of land and building taxes (Y) falls within the same class interval, with 23 respondents (43.4%) indicating a "high" level of awareness.

Consequently, the findings suggest that the leadership of the village head in Kaayuran Village, South District, Langowan, exerts a significant positive influence on public awareness concerning property tax payment. The village head's application of a transformational leadership style appears to be particularly effective in fostering greater tax payment awareness among residents. This study underscores the critical role of leadership in promoting civic compliance within rural settings.

Keywords: village head leadership, public awareness, property tax payment

ABSTRACT The research aims to determine the population and attacks Cnaphalocrocis medinalis on paddy rice vegetative phase in District East Dumoga, Bolaang Mongondow. Results are expected to be used as consideration in the preparation of pest control strategies C. medinalis on rice crops in the future. Research using survey method in several centers of rice cultivation in the district of East Dumoga Bolaang Mongondow, then set the 3 villages as research locations or as a sampling. Location criteria based on the presence of the rice research under the age of one week. Sampling using Method Diagonal slices and set up five sub-plot. Observations population conducted by randomly selecting ten clump of rice plants in each sub-plot. C. medinalis larvae contained in the leaf roll is taken, and then collected in a bottle containing 70% alcohol. Samples are labeled according to location and time of uptake, later identified in the Laboratory of Entomology and Pest Plants, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Sam Ratulangi. Observations percentage of attacks carried out by observing each of the 200 plants per sub-plot. Clumps were attacked recorded and calculated to determine the percentage of C. medinalis attack. Sampling was performed four times at intervals of two weeks. The results showed that the population of pests C. medinalis varies at different locations and the highest research found in two locations in the village Dumoga which reached an average of 15.33 tail, then in the village Dumoga Three reached an average of 13.66 tail and in the village of Dumoga Four reached an average of 5.33 birds. Observations highest percentage of attacks was found in the village of Dumoga Two sample sites, reaching 10.54%, then the village of Three Dumoga 9.95% and the lowest is Village Dumoga Four reached 1.53%. Keywords : Cnaphalocrosis medinalis, percentage of attacks and populations

Interest in becoming a civil servant has persisted among the Indonesian population for several years. The number of civil servants in Indonesia exceeds 4 million, surpassing the approximately 3 million entrepreneurs. The appeal of civil service is largely attributed to the benefits and retirement security it offers. This perspective often leads to the assumption that civil servants' motivation is primarily driven by material incentives. This study aims to examine the impact of intrinsic motivation for public service, originating from individual factors such as job stress, organizational factors including job rotation, and environmental factors represented by feedback. Employing a quantitative approach, the research utilizes multiple linear regression analysis. The population comprises civil servants at the Service Office of State Property and Auction (KPKNL) in Manado, with a sample of 37 respondents. Findings reveal that job stress, job rotation, and feedback significantly affect public service motivation both simultaneously and individually within the studied office. Consequently, it is recommended that organizations take into account the interests of civil servants during decision-making processes, while civil servants themselves should effectively manage their time to optimize work performance.  
Keywords: stress, rotation, feedback, motivation

Abstract:  
Tourism development is perceived and experienced by local communities primarily through visual observation; however, opinions regarding its benefits or drawbacks vary among individuals due to differing perspectives. This study aims to examine public perceptions of tourism development on Lembeh Island, specifically within the South Lembeh Subdistrict of Bitung City. Employing a descriptive qualitative research approach, the study analyzes data derived from observations, in-depth interviews, and documentation to explore community attitudes towards tourism development in the region. Tourism development is conceptualized as an initiative aimed at enhancing societal welfare by leveraging tourism potentials while simultaneously preserving cultural heritage through the improvement of tourism products and services. Moreover, such development necessitates a focus on protecting cultural assets that are closely tied to both local residents and visitors. The findings indicate that public perception of tourism development in the South Lembeh Subdistrict of Bitung City is generally unfavorable, as reflected by limited community absorption, comprehension, and positive evaluation of the tourism initiatives. In conclusion, the current state of tourism development management on Lembeh Island is inadequate and requires enhanced governmental intervention. It is therefore recommended that authorities implement more effective management strategies and undertake immediate efforts to rehabilitate tourist sites, alongside initiatives that foster environmental cleanliness benefiting both visitors and the local population.

Keywords: Public Perception, Tourism Development

MACROSCOPIC TEST OF FRESH SEMEN IN GOAT BREEDS OF ETTAWAH, BOER AND SAANEN AT LEMBANG ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION CENTER. Research aim to evaluate the macroscopic quality of fresh semen in goat breeds of Ettawah, Boer and Saanen at Lembang Artificial Insemination Center. Direct observation was done to obtain primer data. Secondary data were found as additional data supporting primer data. Variables included in observation were involving semen volume, ejaculates, color, consistence, pH and smell. Semen qualities of three breed groups collected on three sequent months were analyzed by t-test method. Results showed that semen qualities for ejaculates from three breed groups of Ettawah, Boer and Saanen collected on different months of September, October and November were not significantly different with the averages of 2.47 ml, 2.64 ml and 2.70 ml respectively. Semen volume from three breed groups of Ettawah, Boer and Saanen collected on those different months were also not significantly different with the averages of significantly different with the averages of 2,30 2,64 and 2,60 mL, respectively. The percentages of color of fresh semen from Ettawah, Boer and Saanen collected on those different months were indicating cream of semen collected on September, October in Ettawah Grade, Boer and Saanen. Fresh semen of these breeds was indicating yellow color collected on November, but it was showing normal condition. Fresh semen of these breeds collected on those months were totally indicating thick consistency. However, pH of fresh semen in all three breeds of goat collected on September and October were significantly different with those collected on November. The pH of fresh semen in these breeds collected on September and October were not significantly different. Values of pH in these breeds collected on September, October and November were 6.63, 6.65 and 6.70, respectively. These values were ranging in normal condition. The smell of fresh semen in these breeds collected on those series of months was indicating specific rancid smell.Key words: Fresh semen quality, goat breed, semen collection period

ABSTRACT  
Accounting information systems involved in fixed asset procurement are susceptible to various security vulnerabilities that may disrupt system functionality. The implementation of security protocols within these systems serves to safeguard fixed asset procurement processes from potential operational, equipment-related, and data-associated threats. This study seeks to investigate the security measures of the accounting information system, specifically those reinforced by internal controls, and to assess how these measures protect the system against threats and risks in the context of PT. Bank SulutGo's head office. Additionally, the findings are compared with established theoretical frameworks. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, this study analyzes relevant data to evaluate the effectiveness of existing security controls. The results reveal that, overall, the accounting information system security concerning fixed asset procurement at PT. Bank SulutGo’s head office is reasonably sufficient, as evidenced by control activities consistent with theoretical expectations. Nonetheless, deficiencies were identified during data processing, particularly in internal control mechanisms. Specifically, the absence of a backup archive undermines the ability of internal controls to fully ensure the security of the accounting information system in this context. Consequently, the establishment of a backup archive is recommended to enhance the effectiveness of internal control activities and thereby optimize the security framework governing fixed asset procurement within the organization.

APPLICATION OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR CATTLE BREEDING GROUP IN TUMALUNTUNG VILLAGE KAUDITAN SUB DISTRICT NORTH MINAHASA. Cattle's breeding in Indonesia is generally still done traditionally, which the cattle are allowed to feed themselves, while the numbers of grass / forage become less and lower in nutritional value. This will affect on cattle productivity adversely. To overcome this, it is necessary to peform of a grass silage preservation and supplemental feeding using an urea-sugar palm-block (UGB), so the feed remains available all the time and the nutritional value becomes better. Tumaluntung is a village in KauditanSubdistrict of North Minahasa Regency, which produces brown sugar as its main crop. In this village there are several groups of cattle bereeders, among them group Mateluntung I and Mateluntung II.Pre-survey showed that the problems faced by the cattle breeders in this village were lack of knowledge by group members to raise cattle, lack of knowledge to provide qualified of forage sustainability, lack of knowledge about making silage and UGB. Therefore, we had done an empowerment cattle breeder groups to increase their knowledge, skills and their income. Method was carried out through counselling and training. Members of the group responded well to this application of science and technology, this can be seen from the availability of elephant grass and dwarf grass. Other products produced were silage and UGB. Keywords : Group of breeders, cattle, silage, UGB

Article 1, point 1 of Law Number 39 of 2009 concerning Special Economic Zones (KEK) defines KEK as territorially bounded areas within the jurisdiction of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, designated to perform economic functions and to receive specific facilities. In recent years, the Indonesian government has implemented policies aimed at enhancing investment, accelerating development—particularly outside the island of Java—and improving economic competitiveness through the establishment of Special Economic Zones (KEK), Industrial Estates (KI), and National Tourism Strategic Areas (KSPN). The legal framework underpinning the establishment of KEK includes Law Number 39 of 2009 on Special Economic Zones, Government Regulation Number 96 of 2015 regarding Facilities in KEK, and the Regulation of the Minister of Finance Number 104/PMK.010/2016 pertaining to tax, customs, and excise treatments in KEK. A prerequisite for a region to administer a special economic zone is the formation of a development and management enterprise. Accordingly, in 2016, the local government issued Governor Decree Number 6 of 2016 of North Sulawesi Province to establish PT. Pembangunan Sulut Hebat, a Regional-Owned Enterprise designated to manage the Bitung Special Economic Zone. As of 2019, PT Pembangunan Sulut Hebat manages only 92 hectares of land—still under the authority of the North Sulawesi Provincial Government—out of the total 441 hectares designated within the Bitung SEZ.

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Special Economic Zones (KEK), Bitung City, Economic Development.

East Likupang District is designated as a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) for Tourism according to Government Regulation Number 84 of 2019 concerning the Likupang Special Economic Zone. However, the problem is that the citizen does not actively participate in the development process. The purpose of this study is to identify citizen participation and to analyze the relationship between the factors that influence citizen participation in the Tourism Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in East Likupang District. The analytical method used is the likert scale analysis and the chi square test. Likert scale analysis with manual calculations uses a formula to measure the opinion of each respondent about citizen participation in the development stage and the forms of participation given. Meanwhile, the chi square test is used to analyze the relationship between the factors that influence citizen participation with the help of SPSS. The results showed that the citizen was involved in the development stages from planning, implementation, monitoring to evaluation. However, the participation given is still not good in the aspects of involvement in meetings, giving ideas, energy, expertise and materials. In the development stage, citizen participation is influenced by external factors in the form of government and community groups but is not influenced by community leaders and internal factors. Meanwhile, forms of citizen participation are influenced by external factors in the form of government, community groups and community leaders as well as internal factors such as age and marital status but not influenced by gender, education level and type of work Keyword: Citizen Participation; Tourism SEZ; Likert Scale; Chi Square

The clove stem borer, Hexamitodera semivelutina Hell., constitutes a significant phytophagous pest affecting clove plants in North Sulawesi. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and extent of damage caused by H. semivelutina on clove plants across different altitudinal zones within Minahasa Regency. Employing a survey methodology, observations were conducted at three altitude intervals above sea level: 0–300 meters, 301–600 meters, and 601–900 meters. The primary variables assessed included the percentage of infestation by H. semivelutina and the degree of damage to clove stems, quantified through the enumeration of active and inactive boreholes. Results indicated that in Koha Village (0–300 m asl), infestation rates ranged from 73.30% to 93.30%, with a mean value of 83.30%. In Agotey Village (301–500 m asl), infestation varied between 56.60% and 100.00%, averaging 78.30%, whereas Eris Village (501–900 m asl) exhibited infestation levels from 83.30% to 100.00%, with a mean of 89.30%. Correspondingly, the number of active burrows in Koha Village ranged from 34 to 46 (mean 38.25), and inactive burrows numbered between 40 and 55 (mean 47.25). In Agotey Village, active burrows ranged from 25 to 49 (mean 35.00), while inactive burrows ranged from 34 to 57 (mean 45.75). In Eris Village, active burrows ranged from 30 to 49 (mean 36.25), with inactive burrows between 36 and 56 (mean 43.50). These findings underscore the influence of altitude on the infestation intensity and consequent damage caused by H. semivelutina in clove plantations within the region.

Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, various activities have been significantly impacted due to government-imposed regulations mandating that individuals remain at home. Consequently, people have predominantly chosen to stay indoors rather than engage in outdoor activities, resulting in increased time spent on smartphones and internet browsing. In Indonesia, internet usage experienced a substantial rise during this period. Survey findings indicate an overall increase in public expenditure on internet services, with YouTube emerging as the most widely utilized platform compared to other social media channels. This trend presents a strategic opportunity for beauty vloggers, as the extended time spent on social media has amplified their influence in attracting consumer attention toward cosmetic products. The objective of this study is to examine the effect of beauty vloggers' credibility and attractiveness on consumers’ purchasing decisions regarding beauty products in Manado. Employing a quantitative research design, the study utilizes Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) analysis as the primary analytical method. Data was collected via questionnaires distributed to a sample of 100 Generation Z respondents who regularly view beauty vloggers’ content focused on face masks.  
Keywords: purchase decision, multiple regression analysis

PRODUCTION PERFORMANCE OF LAYING HENS MB 402 FED RATION COINTAINING OIL OF CAKALANG FISH WASTE (Skipjack Tuna). This study was conducted to determine the production performance of laying hens (MB 402) fed ration containing fish oil waste. The materials used in this study were 100 laying hens at the age of 36 weeks. The treatments used were: 100% basal feed (R0), basal feed 99 % with 1% FOW (R1), basal feed 98% with 2% FOW (R2), basal feed 97% with 3% FOW (R3), basal feed 96% with 4% FOW (R4). Variables observed were including feed consumption (g/bird), Hen Day Production (%), feed conversion. Method used was the completely randomized design (CRD) continued by Duncan's test for the significant analysis of variance. Treatments were replicated 5 times consist of 4 laying hens per replication. Results showed that the use of fish oil waste had no significant effect (P < 0.05) on feed consumption, Hen Day Production and feed conversion. Based on the results of this study, it was concluded that use of fish oil waste in the diet as much as 4 % could be recommended in ration to give the sama production performance of laying hens (MB 402). Keywords: Performance production, laying hens, fish oil waste.

This study investigates the concentration levels of copper (Cu), zinc (Zn), and pH in mining wastewater from the Osela Pit at PT J Resources Bolaang Mongondow (JRBM), as well as the impact of water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) and water lettuce (Pistia stratiotes) on the uptake of these heavy metals and pH modulation within plant tissues. The research was conducted within a greenhouse facility of PT JRBM located in Bolaang Mongondow Regency, utilizing mining wastewater (ALP) sourced from the Osela Pit.

Initially, the concentration of Cu in the ALP from the Osela Pit measured 15.59 mg/L. Treatment with water hyacinth resulted in a decrease of Cu concentration ranging between 7.02 mg/L and 15.48 mg/L, corresponding to an efficacy rate of 45% to 99.3%. When exposed to water lettuce, the Cu concentration on the third day (day 38 of the study) was reduced to 0.12 mg/L, while in the third-day treatment group, it measured 8.51 mg/L. Regarding Zn concentrations, the initial measurement in ALP was 7.03 mg/L, which was reduced to 0.00 mg/L after treatment with either water hyacinth or water lettuce by the third day. The control group, which did not receive any aquatic plant treatment, exhibited stable Zn concentrations of approximately 7.01 mg/L throughout the first to third day.

The initial pH of the mining wastewater was acidic, recorded at 3.03. However, after treatment with the aquatic plants, the pH gradually increased, eventually meeting the environmental quality standard (BML) range of 6 to 9. Conversely, the control group’s pH only increased slightly from 3.03 to 3.30 on the first day, remaining constant at 3.30 on the subsequent days.

Furthermore, the absorption of Cu and Zn by water hyacinth and water lettuce was evident in their tissues, including both leaves and roots. These findings suggest that both aquatic plants play a significant role in the phytoremediation of heavy metals in mining wastewater, contributing to the improvement of water quality parameters such as metal concentration and pH.

Employee empowerment emerges as a highly significant concept in contemporary human resource management, particularly in environments demanding qualified and competent personnel. Through the implementation of empowerment strategies, middle-level managers are entrusted with additional responsibilities and autonomous authority over their tasks, without undue influence from senior management, thereby enhancing their commitment to the organization. This study aims to examine the effect of employee empowerment on organizational commitment within the Bank Indonesia Representatives office in North Sulawesi. Employing a descriptive methodology with a qualitative approach, the research sample comprises eight middle-level management employees who both exercise and receive empowerment, selected via purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and subsequently analyzed. The findings reveal a substantial influence of employee empowerment on organizational commitment, notably within the normative dimension. This effect is attributed to empowerment initiatives such as training, education, motivation, and reward systems implemented by Bank Indonesia, which foster employees’ self-determination and self-efficacy, thus encouraging responsibility towards assigned duties. The study recommends that the Bank Indonesia Representatives in North Sulawesi continue to uphold their empowerment strategies and additionally focus on strengthening employees' affective commitment to the institution.  

Keywords: human resources, empowerment, organizational commitment

Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is one type of horticultural crop with high economic value. One of the diseases of potato plants is bacterial wilt. Bacterial wilt is caused by the bacterium Ralstonia solanacearum. This study aims to determine the incidence of bacterial wilt disease on potato plants in Insil Village, Bolaang Mongondow Regency, which was carried out from August to October 2021, located in Insil Village, Bolaang Mongondow Regency and at the Plant Pests and Diseases Laboratory, Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University. The research was conducted using a survey method with purposive sampling observations. Observations were made on potato plants four weeks after planting. The research was conducted in three different planting locations. Each location measured 30 m x 30 m. In each location, plots were made with diagonal lines measuring 3 m x 3 m and 36 plants were taken from each plot. Plots were made to determine the symptoms of attack caused by R. solanacearum bacteria. The results showed that the highest incidence occurred in location C at 24.44%, followed by location B at 16.66% and the lowest incidence occurred in location A at 16.10%. The average incidence of bacterial wilt disease in potato plants in Insil Village, Bolaang Mongondow Regency is in location A with an average of 8.88%, location B with an average of 7.49% and location C with an average of 14.71%. Further research is needed to determine the factors that influence the development of wilt incidence in potato plants in Insil Village, Bolaang Mongondow Regency.

This study aimed to investigate the impact of pruning lower leaves on maize production. The experiment was carried out in Malalayang Satu Timur, Manado City, North Sulawesi, from March to July 2018. A Randomized Block Design was employed with three treatment groups: P1 (no pruning), P2 (pruning of three lower leaves), and P3 (pruning of five lower leaves). The findings revealed that pruning the lower leaves did not significantly influence cob diameter or length, seed count per cob, the weight of 1000 seeds, or seed weight per cob. The ineffectiveness of lower leaf pruning is attributed to the role of these leaves in supplying assimilates predominantly to root development. This observation is likely linked to the hybrid maize varieties used, which possess traits enabling them to maintain plant quality despite leaf removal. Consequently, pruning three or five lower leaves had no significant effect on seed weight per cob or the weight of 1000 seeds. Although lower leaf pruning did not markedly affect overall maize yield, the weight of 1000 seeds increased relative to the reference weight reported for pioneer varieties. Specifically, the average weight of 1000 seeds measured 375.85 g following pruning of three lower leaves, 361.13 g after pruning five lower leaves, compared to 311 g documented for pioneer varieties, indicating a positive increment. Further investigations are recommended to evaluate the effect of pruning based on specific leaf positions.

The incorporation of fats and oils in swine nutrition is critical due to their elevated energy density. Virgin coconut oil (VCO), derived through cold-press extraction of the coconut kernel, represents a potential dietary supplement for pigs. This study aimed to investigate the effects of dietary VCO inclusion on the energy and protein digestibility as well as overall performance of growing pigs. The experiment involved 20 castrated male pigs, aged between 1.5 and 2.0 months, with an average weight of 12.0 ± 2.0 kg. Data were subjected to analysis of variance using a linear model suitable for a Randomized Block Design comprising five treatments with four replicates each. The dietary treatments were as follows: R0 (100% control diet, 0% VCO), R1 (99.5% control diet, 1.0% VCO), R2 (98.0% control diet, 2.0% VCO), R3 (97.0% control diet, 3.0% VCO), and R4 (96.0% control diet, 4.0% VCO). Performance parameters assessed included daily feed intake, daily weight gain, and daily water consumption. The findings demonstrated that VCO supplementation up to 4% of the diet exerted no statistically significant influence (P > 0.05) on these performance metrics. Consequently, it is inferred that the inclusion of VCO at levels up to 4.0% does not markedly affect growth performance in growing pigs.

Keywords: Virgin coconut oil (VCO), Growth performance, Growing pigs

This study addresses two primary research questions: first, how the inflation rates in the city of Manado compare to those in rural areas of North Sulawesi; and second, the extent to which the inflation rates of various expenditure categories affect the overall inflation rate in both urban and rural contexts. The investigation was carried out over a period of three months in Manado, North Sulawesi. The analysis utilized inflation data spanning from January 2009 to December 2014. Both qualitative and quantitative descriptive methods were employed, including statistical techniques such as mean difference testing and multiple linear regression analysis. The findings indicate that the average inflation rate in rural areas is relatively higher than that observed in urban areas. Examination of seven expenditure groups over the 2009–2014 period revealed that four groups exhibited higher mean inflation rates in the city compared to rural areas; these groups are foodstuffs; housing, electricity, gas, and fuel; education, recreation, and sports; and transport, communications, and financial services. Conversely, the remaining three groups—namely food, beverages, cigarettes and tobacco; clothing; and health—displayed higher average inflation rates in rural areas than in the city. Furthermore, the inflation patterns in Manado closely parallel those observed in the rural regions. It was also determined that the general inflation rate in both urban and rural settings is significantly influenced by the inflation rates of the seven expenditure groups, encompassing foodstuffs, food, clothing, housing, health, education, and transport.

Keywords: Inflation Rate, Expenditure Groups

This study, entitled "Inflectional Affixes in the Book of Luke in the Bible," was conducted as a requirement for the fulfillment of a bachelor's degree at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. The primary objective of this research is to identify, classify, and analyze the various forms and functions of inflectional affixes present in the Book of Luke, as well as to describe the morphophonemic processes involved in their role in word formation. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology as outlined by Gunawan (2017), and grounded in the theoretical frameworks provided by O'Grady and Dobrovolsky (1997) and Gleason (1962), the study reveals eight distinct types of inflectional affixes within the odd chapters of the Book of Luke. These affixes include: {-s}, functioning to indicate plurality; {-’s}, marking possession; {-es}, denoting the third person singular non-past tense; {-ing}, expressing the progressive aspect; {-ed}, signaling the past tense; {-ed/en}, serving as the past participle; {-er}, indicating the comparative degree; and {-est}, representing the superlative degree. Furthermore, the research identifies specific morphophonemic variations that arise when these affixes attach to root words. In particular, the plural suffix {-s} manifests in the allomorphs /s/, /z/, and /ɪz/; the possessive {-’s} appears as /z/ or /s/; the third person singular {-es} surfaces as /s/, /z/, or /ɪz/; the progressive {-ing} is realized as /ɪŋ/; the past tense {-ed} varies among /t/, /d/, and /ɪd/; the past participle {-ed/en} exhibits allomorphs /d/, /t/, /ɪd/, and /n/; the comparative {-er} is pronounced as /r/; and the superlative {-est} takes the form /ɪst/. 

Keywords: Inflectional affixes, forms, functions, morphophonemic processes, Book of Luke, Bible.

The declining performance of the bureaucracy in Indonesia presents a pessimistic outlook regarding the preparedness of government apparatuses to effectively engage in global dynamics. This scenario underscores the imperative for comprehensive bureaucratic reform. In the context of governance reform, the enhancement of local government administration is critically relevant to improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability of the public sector. Such improvements necessitate the full implementation of regional autonomy and the proactive utilization of regional resources to harness local potential. Addressing regional circumstances and adapting to shifts in global dynamics require the restructuring, revitalization, and reinvention of regional institutions as strategic efforts to establish competitive advantages amid global competition, thereby advancing towards becoming global learning organizations (Marquards and Reynolds, 1994). Furthermore, the emergence of global democracy represents a paradigmatic shift influencing regional autonomy and local government representation. The liberalization and deglobalization of local governments grant greater autonomy for regions to develop localized responses to ongoing global environmental changes. This adaptive capacity is fundamentally reliant on the ability of local governments to leverage intangible assets, including conceptual frameworks, competencies, and networks (Kanter, 1995).

Keywords: Internationalisation, Local Government, Bureaucratic Reform

Tomato had been used in coconut oil production. Lycopene and other nonpolar antioxidants of tomato cansolve in the oil. The aims of this study were to determine the composition of fatty acid of coconut oil atseveral tomato extract concentrations, heat temperatures and storage times. In this study, theconcentrations of tomato extract in milk coconut were varied (0, 10, 20, 30,40, 50% (v/v) or the ratiobetween tomato extract and milk coconut were 0:10, 1:9, 2:8, 3:7, 4:6, 5:5). After that, the highestrendemen coconut oil that yielded from treatment of tomato extract concentrations was heated at severaltemperatures (40, 60, 80, 100, dan 1200C for 1 hour, and room temperature), also it was kept for onemonth (1, 2, 3, 4 weeks). Every oil treatment was measured the composition of oil fatty acid with GC. Inconclusion, in all treatments of tomato extract concentrations, the highest fatty acid component in coconutoil was lauric acid, followed by myristic, caprilic, capric, palmitic, oleic, linoleic, and stearic acid. Theheating of the oil over 60OC decreased the composition of medium chain fatty acid and increased thecomposition of long chain fatty acid. The storaging of the oil containing tomato extract after three weeksincreased the composition of medium chain fatty acid and decreased the composition of long chain fattyacid.

Marketing is an important thing for marketer in order to achieve the organizational goals. Marketing nowadays has entered modern phase, consumer can buy products from virtual store as one of shopping channels. With a good implementation of marketing strategies can affect a good communication between organization and target markets. This research is designed to analyze the factors influence the buying decision on online shopping clothing for consumer in Manado using Factor Analysis for data reduction that summarizes the observed factors. The finding resulted all factors are qualified, and the three most dominant factors based on communality test are Available Products (0.836), followed by Refund (0.812) and Perceived Ease of Use (0.810). This research endeavors to identify both internal and external factors affecting the bamboo handicraft home industry in Kinilow and to formulate appropriate development strategies. The investigation was carried out between March and May 2017, employing both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected via observations and interviews with two distinct groups: internally, six bamboo handicraft business owners who are directly involved in production and sales; externally, representatives from local government and consumers. Secondary data were acquired through a comprehensive review of relevant literature. The data were analyzed using SWOT analysis.

Findings indicate that the internal strengths include the easy availability and relatively low cost of raw materials, superior raw material quality, a skilled workforce, participation in skills training, the use of personal capital, rapid production processes, low difficulty levels, product durability, and affordable pricing. However, weaknesses were identified, such as the absence of financial record-keeping, limited engagement with financial institutions, reliance on traditional production equipment, lack of media-based promotional methods (both online and print), no mechanization in production, inadequate transportation facilities, and suboptimal product display. 

Externally, opportunities encompass increased demand stemming from international buyers facilitated by the TIFF event in Tomohon city, heightened local demand, prospects for exhibitions, and broad market potential. Conversely, threats include diminished interest among younger generations in sustaining the craft, the emergence of new competitors in the North Sulawesi region, competition from substitute materials such as plastic, vulnerability of business locations to landslide hazards, and governmental proposals to relocate production sites.

Based on the SWOT matrix, the recommended strategic approach combines SO (Strengths-Opportunities) strategies, specifically: (1) innovating and developing new bamboo handicraft products to enhance the industry in Kinilow, and (2) collaborating with government entities to broaden marketing networks and expand market reach.

Keywords: Household Industry, Bamboo Handicraft, SWOT Analysis.

ABSTRACT: The quality of public services is largely contingent upon the extent to which village government officials actively participate and fulfill their roles and responsibilities in service delivery. This involvement is essential to ensure public satisfaction and the effective functioning of village services. This study was conducted in Pitu Village, Central Halmahera, North District, with the objective of examining the role of village government apparatus in providing public services and identifying the challenges encountered in this process. Employing a qualitative research methodology, data were collected from multiple informants, including the village head, village officials, and community members. The data collection techniques comprised interviews, observations, and documentation. Data analysis followed a systematic process involving data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. Findings reveal that the role of government agencies in Pitu Village in delivering services remains suboptimal. Various challenges were identified, including procedural simplicity, clarity, completeness of facilities and infrastructure, as well as issues related to discipline, politeness, friendliness, and comfort. Among the evaluated indicators, four reflected unsatisfactory service quality, while one indicated a fairly good level of service. Consequently, it is concluded that public services in Pitu Village have yet to achieve optimal performance.

Keywords: Role of Village Government Personnel, Public Service

The rapid advancement of technology inevitably brings about changes in various aspects of life. This study aims to investigate the impact of the work environment on employee performance at PT. Maumbi Expedition Company in Manado City. The work environment refers to the setting in which employees carry out their daily tasks. A supportive and conducive work environment fosters a sense of security among employees, thereby enabling them to perform their duties optimally. Employee performance is defined as the tangible outcomes and work accomplished by individuals, often serving as a basis for employee evaluation.

To effectively analyze this relationship, an appropriate methodological approach is required for accurate data processing. Due to constraints in funding, time, and resources, the researchers employed a sampling technique, selecting 39 employees from PT. Maumbi Expedition Company for this study. The results of the simple linear regression analysis yielded the equation Y = 37.35 + 0.12X, indicating a statistically significant and strong positive correlation between the work environment and employee performance variables. Therefore, it is recommended that PT. Maumbi Expedition Company in Manado City continue to enhance employee performance through stringent supervision, encouraging greater adherence to company regulations.  

Keywords: work environment, employee performance

The aim of this study is to evaluate the financial feasibility of the dodol production business operated by UD Mandiri in Pangu Satu Village, Ratahan Timur Sub-District, Southeast Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted over the period from November 2018 to April 2019, employing a case study methodology. The data utilized comprise both primary and secondary sources. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with the business owners of UD Mandiri. Secondary data were gathered from company records, locally available literature, and online resources such as Google Scholar, which provided access to relevant scholarly articles and theses from various academic institutions, with a focus on financial analysis. 

Data analysis involved both qualitative and quantitative approaches. The qualitative analysis sought to identify the characteristics of the dodol business by examining non-financial aspects, which were presented descriptively and illustrated using tables, charts, images, and graphics pertaining to production processes, marketing strategies, legal considerations, and environmental factors. The quantitative analysis involved the evaluation of financial feasibility indicators, including Net Present Value (NPV), Net Benefit/Cost (B/C) Ratio, Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and Payback Period (PP). 

Findings indicated that, when financed with its own capital, UD Mandiri’s salak dodol business is financially viable. This conclusion is supported by an NPV of Rp 103,045,440, an IRR of 60%—substantially exceeding the prevailing Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) interest rate of 6%—a Net B/C Ratio of 1.012, which is greater than one, and a payback period of two years.

This study assessed the abundance and species richness of bats (Order Chiroptera) inhabiting caves in three KBAs (Key Biodiversity Areas) of Central Visayas: Mt. Bandilaan in Siquijor (13 caves), Mabinay, Negros Oriental (11 caves), and Rajah Sikatuna Protected Landscape(RSPL) in Bohol (31 caves). The study was conducted between February 14 to September 20, 2019. Of the 55 caves surveyed, 35 caves were inhabited by bats. Field survey methods included mist-netting at the cave entrances and direct observations of roosting sites in each cave. This study captured 754 individuals of bats belonging to 16 species, majority of which are insectivorous species (13 species) and only three species are fruitbats (Pteropodidae). Mabinay caves had the highest number of species (11) and captured bats (271 individuals) while RSPL had 9 species (221 individuals) while Mt. Bandilaan only had five species but relatively high captured bats (262 individuals). Five species are Philippine endemics (Hipposideros obscurus, Hipposideros pygmaeus, Ptenochirus jagori, Rhinolophus inops, and R. rufus) and three Near-threatened species (H. lekaguli, M. schreibersii, and R. rufus). The rare bat species (Dobsonia chapmani) may be locally extirpated in Mabinay, where it last documented at Mambajo cave in the 1960s. The survey also noted the absence of fruit bats (observed in 2011 study) in all of the caves in Mt. Bandilaan, probably due to on-going anthropogenic activities (treasure hunting, bat hunting, guano extraction, land conversion, locals illegal entry, graffiti, etc) in caves surveyed. Large colonies of fruitbats and insect bats in RSPL may have been affected by anthropogenic activities inside the caves. Most of the caves surveyed have been promoted for ecotourism activities.Keywords: cave; chiropteran; extraction; karst; limestone

This study addresses the issue of identifying the basic and potential economic sectors within South Minahasa District that could serve as catalysts for regional economic growth. The objective of the research is to conduct an analysis of these fundamental and emerging sectors in South Minahasa. The investigation was carried out over a four-month period, from June to September 2016, beginning with preparatory activities leading up to the formal research phase. Secondary data were sourced from the Central Bureau of Statistics of North Sulawesi Province and the Central Bureau of Statistics of South Minahasa District. The analytical methods employed included Location Quotient (LQ), Shift Share, and Modified Regional Potential (MRP) analyses. Findings indicate that the foundational sectors contributing to the Gross Regional Domestic Product of South Minahasa District comprise agriculture, mining and quarrying, manufacturing, and construction. Shift Share analysis suggests that the district's economy is projected to experience relatively slow growth and lacks significant competitive advantages. Conversely, the MRP analysis highlights two sectors—construction, and health services and social activities—as particularly prominent within both North Sulawesi Province and South Minahasa District. Additionally, the manufacturing sector and the administration sector, encompassing government, defense, and compulsory social security, demonstrate potential for economic expansion. These identified sectors are anticipated to play a vital role in stimulating economic growth in North Sulawesi Province, signifying their potential for development within South Minahasa District.

This study analyzed the effect of variables such as distributive justice, tax morality on taxpayer compliance with taxpayer satisfaction as an intervening variable. This study examined whether a person's morale affects taxpayer compliance in tax paying. The method used in this study was the quantitative method. The sample in this study was hotel taxpayers in Manado City that were registered at the Manado City Revenue Service office. This study used a quantitative method with an associative design that examined the influence among independent variables, are distributive justice, tax morality, and taxpayer satisfaction on the dependent variable, namely hotel taxpayer compliance. The number of samples used as many as 53 hotel taxpayer respondents, collected by distributing questionnaires to each hotel owner or general manager. The test equipment used in this study was Partial Least Square (PLS) using the SmartPLS program.The results of this study indicate that distributive justice, tax morality, and taxpayer satisfaction have a direct positive effect on taxpayer's compliance. In addition, it is found during this study that the indirect effect through variable mediating produces a positive effect on taxpayers compliance. Therefore, Distribution justice and Tax morality both are making a positive impact on taxpayers compliance mediated through taxpayer's satisfaction.

The repositioning of structural roles represents a viable strategy for enhancing the quality of public services. Such structural changes, as manifestations of organizational dynamics, serve as mechanisms for achieving organizational objectives. These changes are implemented with the intent to alleviate job monotony, enhance employees’ knowledge and skills, and improve motivation and morale. Furthermore, they ensure that officials with the appropriate expertise are assigned to roles aligned with their competencies. This study investigates the effects of policies related to structural position mutations within the public service sector of the local government in the Sangihe Islands district. Employing qualitative research methods, the study aims to describe, analyze, and ascertain the impact of structural position mutation policies on public service, measured through indicators such as work experience, knowledge and skills, and employee utilization. Data collected via observation and interviews reveal the following findings: (1) employees exhibit increased work experience maturity after serving in designated roles for specific periods; (2) structural mutations facilitate the acquisition of knowledge and skills; and (3) employee empowerment occurs through positional changes, enabling the optimization of individuals who previously performed routine tasks in static positions. The study concludes that structural position mutations in Sangihe Regency are conducted normatively and are intended to enhance organizational efficacy and public service quality. These policies positively affect public service performance. Accordingly, it is recommended that the government implement cluster-based positional management and monitor the working environment within local government institutions to ensure effective handling and facilitate the implementation of structural position mutations.

Keywords: policy, mutation, structural positions, public service

This study aimed to examine the relationship between the promotion system and employee motivation among staff members of the Secretariat of South Halmahera District. Employing a quantitative associative research design, the study selected a sample of 50 respondents—constituting approximately 52% of the total population of 97 civil servants—using a proportional random sampling technique. Data were collected through structured questionnaires complemented by interviews. The analyses involved descriptive statistics, including frequency distributions and percentages, alongside inferential statistical methods such as the chi-square test and contingency coefficient analysis.

The findings revealed the following: (1) the promotion system for civil servants within the South Halmahera District Secretariat is generally implemented satisfactorily, adhering to established criteria and basic promotion principles with objectivity, fairness, and accuracy; (2) employee motivation levels were found to be relatively high; and (3) a significant positive correlation exists between the promotion system and employee motivation, indicating that improvements in the promotion system are associated with enhanced employee motivation.

In light of these conclusions, it is recommended that: (1) the promotion system undergo further refinement, particularly concerning the consistent application of promotion criteria, objectivity, and fairness; (2) efforts be made to further enhance employee motivation; and (3) the promotion system be utilized strategically as an instrument to boost employee motivation.

Keywords: Promotion System, Work Motivation

The aim of this study is to assess the market orientation of the company, focusing specifically on customer orientation, competitor orientation, and interfunctional coordination. This investigation was carried out over a three-month period, from February to April 2016. Primary data were collected through a survey methodology utilizing questionnaires, which were distributed to both employees and managers. The questionnaire was designed to evaluate the dimensions of customer orientation, competitor orientation, and coordination between organizational functions. Findings from the research conducted at Five Star UD indicate that the company demonstrates a strong market orientation, with an overall market orientation score of 64.31 percent. Regarding customer orientation, Five Star UD exhibits a robust understanding of customer desires, awareness of customer needs, a commitment to customer satisfaction, and an ability to generate value for its clientele. In terms of competitor orientation, the company effectively responds to competitors’ actions, leverages competitive advantages to capitalize on opportunities, and actively develops strategies to contend with rivals. Concerning coordination between functions, employees contribute significantly to the strategic initiatives of Five Star UD and the creation of customer value, engage in cooperative efforts, and possess a clear understanding of customer requirements, thereby fostering customer satisfaction.

ABSTRACTThis research is entitled "Taboo Words in English and Mongondow Language: A Contrastive Analysis" is analyzed and describe in sociolinguistic field. The objectives of this research are to identify, classify and describe the types and meaning of taboo words and to analyze their differences and similarities in English and Mongondow Language. This research used a descriptive method. The data is analyzed using theory of Wardhaugh (1986:230) to find out the types, using Leech's theory (1981:19) to find out the meaning, and were contrasted to find out the differences using Lado's theory (1971:217). The significances of this research are theoretically, this research is expected to give contribution to the development of sociolinguistics especially in terms of taboo words and to practically, this research can be useful, for young Mongondow generation who want to learn taboo words in English and for foreign learners who want to study taboo words in Mongondow language. The result of this research shows that taboo words found in Mongondow language were classified into eight types, they are, sex, excretion, bodily function, death, animal, religion, supernatural and hollo. The simillaritiess in English and Mongondow Language is the use of this word can cause misunderstanding and the differences of English and Mongondow Language is taboo words in Mongondow have levels whereas in English there is no level. This shows that the causes of using taboo words are to express the happiness, such as anger, emotion, and surprise, to joke, to insult, and to talk about sex. Keywords : Taboo Words; English and Mongondow Language; Contrastive Analysis.

A distribution company was established with the objective of supplying products and services that fulfill consumer demands. Effective distribution operations necessitate proficient human resource management to ensure personnel adequately perform their duties and responsibilities. Strategic human resource management (SHRM) plays a crucial role in overseeing human resources and is pivotal in determining an organization's overall success. This study aims to examine the relationship between SHRM and organizational performance, considering employee relations as a mediating variable. Employing a quantitative research approach, the study population comprised all permanent employees at PT Borwita Citra Prima Manado, with a sample size of 67 individuals. Path analysis was utilized to assess the causal relationships among SHRM, organizational performance, and employee relations as a mediator. Additionally, the Sobel test was applied to evaluate the indirect effects. Findings indicate a positive association between SHRM and organizational performance, with employee relations serving as a partial mediator within PT Borwita Citra Prima Manado. It is recommended that the company enhance recognition programs for punctual employees and those with low absenteeism rates, while also striving to maintain stable employee relations to mitigate interpersonal conflicts. 

Keywords: strategic human resource management, organizational performance, employee relations.

Decentralization significantly impacts the accounting practices of local governments. One key aspect of decentralization is the transfer of authority from the central government to local entities, including states, provinces, counties, and towns. Nonetheless, the central government does not relinquish control entirely; it continues to provide intergovernmental grants to local governments. Among these transfers is the General Allocation Fund, which local governments may utilize flexibly for either operational or capital expenditures. Both the General Allocation Fund (Dana Alokasi Umum) and the Original Regional Revenue (Pendapatan Asli Daerah) constitute important sources of income for local governments, which are allocated to Local Expenditures (Belanja Daerah). A notable inefficiency in local expenditure can be exemplified by the flypaper effect, wherein the previous period’s General Allocation Fund (lagged DAU) tends to have a more pronounced impact on local spending than the previous period’s Original Regional Revenue (lagged PAD). However, this study provides empirical evidence from the North Sulawesi Provincial Government budget realizations for the period 2001 to 2010, indicating that the flypaper effect phenomenon does not manifest in this context. Statistical analysis using multiple regression reveals that the lagged PAD coefficient significantly influences local expenditures at α = 0.05 with a value of 0.006, whereas the lagged DAU coefficient does not exert a statistically significant effect.

This study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of the administrative service unit in managing data within the Regional Secretariat of North Sulawesi Province. Employing a qualitative research approach, the investigation is grounded in a theoretical framework comprising four key dimensions of public service effectiveness: timeliness, accuracy, courtesy and friendliness, and ease of access to services. The research utilizes both primary and secondary data sources. Data collection methods include interviews, observations, and documentation. Subsequently, the data derived from these diverse sources are analyzed to draw comprehensive conclusions regarding the research objectives.

The findings indicate that the administrative service unit demonstrates effectiveness in data management, particularly concerning the timeliness of services spanning from data processing to the authorization of pertinent documents and correspondence. Furthermore, the unit exhibits accuracy by minimizing errors throughout service transactions. The study also highlights the courteous and friendly demeanor of personnel engaged in data management activities. In terms of accessibility, the administrative service unit facilitates the prompt and straightforward procurement of services related to data management.

Nonetheless, several areas warrant attention for further enhancement. It is recommended that both employees and leadership participate in training programs to augment human resource capabilities in system-based data management. Additionally, the provision of supplementary facilities and the improvement of network infrastructure and administrative service applications are essential. These advancements aim to ensure that the data management process not only meets but potentially exceeds established performance targets.

Keywords: Effectiveness, Administrative Services, Data Management

The Finance Division Headquarters at Sam Ratulangi University is responsible for managing the financial operations related to both revenue and expenditure through a workforce of fourteen honorary employees. However, these contract-based staff face several challenges in the execution of their duties, including excessive overtime, lack of access to training, insufficient support and resources, misalignment between assigned tasks and job descriptions, and frequent reassignment of responsibilities by permanent employees. These conditions highlight a clear absence of effective empowerment practices by the organizational leadership toward temporary employees. 

This study aims to analyze the underlying factors contributing to the stagnation of empowerment efforts for temporary staff. The findings indicate that the principal causes include the leadership's failure to perform key functions essential to empowerment, such as enabling, facilitating, consulting, collaborating, mentoring, and providing necessary support to honorary employees. 

Based on these findings, the study recommends several measures to enhance empowerment. These include providing targeted training in financial management both prior to employment and through ongoing participation in institutional training programs, improving material support by organizing the work environment, increasing the availability of computers, relocating financial document archives for better accessibility, imposing sanctions on civil servants who delegate tasks beyond the authority of honorary workers, and advocating for adjustments to compensation to align with the provincial minimum wage standards, including overtime pay and expanded health insurance benefits.

Keywords: Empowerment, Honorary Staff, Finance

The objective of this study was to assess the competence of the administrative apparatus in organizational structuring within Wawali Pasan Village, Ratahan District, Southeast Minahasa Regency. Furthermore, the knowledge and information possessed by village staff concerning the organization and implementation of village administration are adequate. Standard operating procedures are well comprehended, beginning with the collection of community data by respective ward heads, followed by submission through the village secretary to the village head for authorization, and finally, the dissemination of approved information back to community members according to their individual needs.

Additionally, the skills, defined as the ability to execute certain physical and mental tasks, are assessed as sufficiently competent. This assessment is corroborated by community members who express confidence in the officials’ performance of their duties. However, some deficiencies remain in terms of the efficiency with which tasks and community complaints are resolved. This inefficiency is understood within the community, given the diverse nature and varying levels of difficulty associated with different tasks and complaints, which often require extended time for resolution.

Keywords: Apparatus Competence, Administrative Structuring

This study aimed to evaluate the financial performance of the North Sulawesi Provincial Government, utilizing indicators such as the Independence Ratio, Effectiveness Ratio, Degree of Fiscal Decentralization, Harmony Ratio, and Growth Ratio. Findings indicate that between 2010 and 2015, the Independence Ratio of North Sulawesi Province showed an upward trend, categorizing the region as participatory. This status suggests a moderate level of financial autonomy characterized by reduced reliance on external sources and effective management of internal funds, including Domestic Revenue. Furthermore, this implies a relatively prosperous population capable of contributing significantly to tax revenues, which constitute a major portion of regional income. Regarding the Effectiveness Ratio of Domestic Revenue, the results generally demonstrated effectiveness over the six-year period, with the exception of 2014 and 2015, when the ratio declined into the non-effective range, reflecting a downturn in the local government’s financial performance during those years. Analysis of the Degree of Fiscal Decentralization revealed that the provincial government had not yet achieved full self-sufficiency in covering total expenditures through locally generated revenues. The Harmony Ratio indicated a higher realization of operating expenditures relative to capital expenditures, a pattern considered suboptimal for a developing region such as North Sulawesi. Lastly, the Growth Ratio exhibited instability throughout the examined period, a phenomenon attributed to the suboptimal implementation of the "money follows function" policy. This has led to challenges in coordinating concurrent tasks among Regional Work Units in alignment with their expertise and mandated responsibilities.  
Keywords: regional financial performance, APBD

This study, entitled "Figurative Language in Carl Sandburg’s Poems," examines the use of figurative language within selected poems by Sandburg, aiming to classify the types employed and explicate their meanings. Five notable and representative poems by Carl Sandburg were selected for analysis based on their distinctive titles and recognition. Employing a content analysis methodology with an intrinsic approach, the study seeks to comprehend the significance of figurative expressions in each poem. The primary objectives are to identify and categorize the various forms of figurative language present and to analyze their interpretative meanings as manifested in Sandburg’s poetry. The theoretical framework is grounded in Perrine’s (1983, pp. 576–645) work, *Literature: Structure, Sound, and Sense*, where figurative language is defined as a mode of expression that conveys meaning beyond literal interpretation. Perrine further delineates several categories of figurative language, including personification, metaphor, simile, symbol, synecdoche, metonymy, and hyperbole. The findings reveal that Carl Sandburg’s poems incorporate seven distinct types of figurative language: personification, metaphor, symbol, simile, metonymy, hyperbole, and synecdoche, with metaphor and personification predominating throughout the selected works. Additionally, the figurative devices employed by Sandburg generally reflect the poet’s reverence for the existence and significance of ordinary people, as well as the dynamics between the populace and government in urban or national contexts.

Keywords: Poems, Figurative Language, Carl Sandburg

This study investigated the effects of varying nitrogen fertilization levels and shading conditions on the morphological characteristics of Dwarf Elephant Grass (Pennisetum purpureum cv. Mott). Employing a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with a factorial arrangement, two factors were examined: nitrogen fertilization (Factor A) at four levels—P1: 0% (no fertilization), P2: 200 kg urea/ha, P3: 400 kg urea/ha, and P4: 800 kg urea/ha—and shading conditions (Factor B) at two levels—N1: no shading (0%) and N2: 70% shading. The measured morphological parameters included leaf length, the number of mature leaves, and plant height. The results indicated that under shaded conditions, a nitrogen application of approximately 200 kg urea/ha was sufficient to optimize leaf length, whereas in unshaded environments, a higher application rate of 800 kg urea/ha was required to attain similar results. Furthermore, to maximize the number of mature leaves in unshaded conditions, around 800 kg urea/ha was necessary, while under shading, nitrogen fertilization did not significantly influence this parameter. The greatest plant height in open (unshaded) areas was achieved with 400 kg urea/ha, while in shaded environments, nitrogen supplementation did not enhance plant height. These findings suggest that shading enhances the effective availability of nitrogen for Dwarf Elephant Grass, thereby reducing the fertilizer requirements to achieve optimal morphological growth. Consequently, plants cultivated in open, unshaded areas demand higher nitrogen inputs to attain comparable leaf length, mature leaf number, and height relative to those grown under shaded conditions.

Keywords: Nitrogen fertilization, shading, Pennisetum purpureum, plant morphology, dwarf elephant grass.

The present study aimed to investigate the impact of tomato starch (Solanum lycopersicum L.) supplementation on the internal egg quality of laying hens. A total of 100 laying hens, aged 36 weeks, were allocated to five dietary treatments as follows: P0, a basal ration without tomato starch; P1, 98% basal ration supplemented with 2% tomato starch; P2, 96% basal ration plus 4% tomato starch; P3, 94% basal ration with 6% tomato starch; and P4, 92% basal ration supplemented with 8% tomato starch. The experimental design employed was a completely randomized design (CRD) consisting of five treatments and five replications. Data were analyzed using Duncan’s multiple range test for mean comparisons. The internal egg quality parameters measured included yolk index, yolk color, and Haugh units (HU). The findings indicated that dietary inclusion of tomato starch exerted no significant influence (P > 0.05) on the yolk index or Haugh units. However, a highly significant effect (P < 0.01) was observed on yolk color. From these results, it is concluded that incorporation of tomato starch at an 8% inclusion level in the ration positively affects egg yolk color while maintaining acceptable yolk index and Haugh units in laying hens.  
Keywords: laying hens, internal egg quality, tomato starch

This thesis was conducted to fulfill the requirements for obtaining a Bachelor's degree in English at Sam Ratulangi University. The study is entitled "Discourse Analysis of King George VI’s Speech: 'With God's Help, We Shall Prevail' (First Radio Address, Britain, September 3, 1939)." The research aims to analyze and elucidate the discourse analysis norms present within King George VI’s speech. The investigation was carried out in three stages. The initial stage involved preparation, during which the researcher reviewed literature on language, linguistics, and discourse analysis to identify pertinent theoretical frameworks. The second stage comprised data collection, where the researcher located the text of King George VI’s speech and examined it multiple times to achieve a comprehensive understanding. The final stage entailed data analysis, involving the collection, identification, classification, and examination of linguistic elements within the speech.

The methodology employed in this study draws primarily on the framework proposed by Alba-Juez (2008:20), supplemented by theoretical insights from De Beaugrande and Dressler (1986:8) and Aarts and Aarts (1982:4). This theoretical approach encompasses seven discourse norms: cohesion (including pronouns, substitution, ellipsis, conjunction, and lexical cohesion), coherence (marked and unmarked), intentionality, acceptability, informativity, situationality, and intertextuality.

The findings indicate that, within the cohesion category, the speech includes 50 instances of pronouns, 7 occurrences of substitution, no ellipsis, 34 conjunctions, and 10 lexical cohesion elements. Regarding coherence, 21 instances of marked coherence were identified, with no occurrences of unmarked coherence. The norm of intentionality reveals a focus on the speaker, expressing sentiments of disappointment and sorrow. Acceptability is generally affirmed, as evidenced by historical accounts showing the speech was warmly received by both the public and members of the royal family. Informativity is demonstrated through the provision of comprehensive information, reflecting the historical context of the address. Situationality is closely linked to the wartime circumstances prevailing at the time, while intertextuality pertains to references affirming Britain’s commitment to defending Polish independence.

Keywords: discourse analysis, speech, seven discourse norms, King George VI

This study aims to present the outcomes of modeling and simulation conducted on an H-Darrieus wind turbine equipped with straight blades. Two methodological approaches were employed: manual calculations and software-based analysis. The study utilized wind speed data specific to Manado City. Prior to performing the software analysis, the data were processed to determine the lift and drag forces acting on the turbine blades, as well as other forces impacting the overall wind turbine structure. Subsequently, a comparative evaluation between the results obtained from manual calculations and software simulations was carried out to validate the modeling outcomes.

The analysis revealed that the turbine’s average calculated power output is 181.81 watts. The wind turbine features a diameter of 2260 mm and a height of 2350 mm. At an angle of attack of 8.95 degrees, the lift force was computed to be 143.257 N, while the drag force measured 3.978 N. The maximum Von Mises stress within the wind turbine structure was found to be 184.96 MPa. This stress level remains below the material’s allowable stress limit, indicating that structural failure is unlikely.

In conclusion, the modeling and simulation of the H-Darrieus wind turbine with straight blades were successfully conducted, resulting in validated performance predictions. The final output of this research includes comprehensive turbine design drawings.

**Keywords:** Darrieus Wind Turbine, Modeling, Simulation, Lift Force, Drag Force

Adverse weather conditions, such as rain, have traditionally posed significant challenges for individuals relying on outdoor clotheslines. Frequently, clothes are left hanging without being retrieved promptly, especially when unexpected rain or nighttime occurs, leading to potential damage or prolonged drying times. To mitigate these issues, this study presents the development of an automated control system designed to operate a clothesline actuator. The system integrates various components, including a light-dependent resistor (LDR) sensor for sunlight detection, a water sensor for rain detection, a DC motor as the actuator, and an Arduino Uno microcontroller serving as the central control unit. The coordinated function of these components enables the automatic retraction or extension of the clothesline based on environmental conditions. Experimental evaluations demonstrated that the system effectively responds to sensor inputs: absence of light is interpreted by the Arduino as cloudy or nighttime conditions, prompting the DC motor to retract the clothesline indoors; detection of sunlight results in the automatic extension of the clothesline; and sensing of raindrops triggers retraction to protect the laundry. The results affirm that the Arduino Uno ATmega328-based automatic clothes drying system operates reliably, providing a practical solution for the timely management of clotheslines during inclement weather and nighttime. 

Keywords: Automatic clothesline, LDR sensor, Water sensor, DC motor
