This study aims to examine the impact of the marketing mix components—Product, Promotion, Place, Price, Process, People, and Physical Evidence—on the savings decisions of consumers at PT. BPR Dana Raya Manado. Additionally, it seeks to identify the most influential variable among these factors in shaping consumer savings behavior. The investigation was carried out at PT. BPR Dana Raya Manado, utilizing both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected through structured interviews employing questionnaires administered to respondents, while secondary data were obtained from relevant institutional sources. Data analysis was conducted using multiple regression techniques with the assistance of SPSS version 20 software. Prior to regression analysis, validity and reliability tests were performed. The overall influence of the independent variables on consumer decisions was evaluated using F-tests, and the significance of each variable was assessed through t-tests. The findings reveal that 70.3% of the variance in consumers’ savings decisions can be explained collectively by the marketing mix variables (X1 through X7), leaving 29.7% attributable to other external factors beyond this study’s scope. The F-test results demonstrate a calculated F-value of 17.578, exceeding the critical F-value of 2.2371, which indicates a statistically significant effect of the marketing mix on consumer choices. Furthermore, t-test outcomes show that all independent variables have t-values greater than the corresponding critical values, with Promotion (X2) identified as the most dominant factor, exhibiting a standardized coefficient of 0.291 (29.1%).

Nicknaming and its uses in daily communication by the people of Rumoong-Lansot villages are considered as both social and lingual phenomena that have existed since a very long time ago and unconsciously have become the internal part of daily interaction of the people. A well-maintained relationship among the individuals in the society is one of the major factors that endorsed them to address each other by using proper nicknames. No matter old or young people, male or female, wealthy or destitute, indigenous or non indigenous, are all unexceptional unrestrained for nicknaming and employing nicknames between one another. The results of this research showed that term of nicknames employed by the people of Rumoong-Lansot villages concealed nearly the entire elements of internal linguistics and external linguistics. In term of types, all those nicknames that have been successfully collected and analyzed can be categorized into the following aspects: physical state, home and place of birth, occupation, particular moment, and every other feature that promotes the creation of the nicknames. Generally speaking, every single nickname employed by the people is conditioned to identify one specific member of the society in order to generate a clear and unimpeded sort of communication. Specifically, every single nickname is responsible to provide a distinguished portrayal of any peculiar individual in the society, and even more definite, about his most dominating distinctive characteristics.

This study seeks to identify both external and internal factors influencing the agro-industry "Sop Buah Ica" and to develop strategic recommendations for its advancement within the designated study area. The research was conducted at the "Sop Buah Ica" location on Manado Boulevard over a three-month period, spanning May to July 2015. The data utilized in this study comprised both primary and secondary sources. Primary data were collected through interviews and surveys involving key stakeholders, including business owners, customers, and employees directly associated with the enterprise. Secondary data were obtained from official documents provided by relevant authorities, as well as from internet sources, library materials, and literature relevant to the subject matter. The data were subsequently analyzed using SWOT analysis. 

Findings from the SWOT analysis indicate that the Sop Buah Ica business is situated in quadrant I, representative of an aggressive strategic position. This placement reflects a highly favorable environment for the enterprise, characterized by considerable internal strengths and significant external opportunities, suggesting a promising future outlook. Accordingly, specific strategies are recommended to capitalize on these advantages. These include ensuring the availability of consistent capital to support procurement activities, leveraging market opportunities through competitive pricing, promoting the Fruit Sop product in public venues to attract new customers, utilizing a variety of market-available fruits for product diversification to enhance the appeal of Fruit Sop, and identifying alternative suppliers to optimize resource acquisition.

This study examines the use of the newspapers *Malut Post* and *Posko Malut* as mass media outlets with journalistic objectives. The research aims to (1) identify and classify the types of pragmatic meanings found in the titles of articles published in *Malut Post* and *Posko Malut*; (2) identify and analyze the pragmatic meanings conveyed within the newspaper articles; and (3) explain the reasons underlying the use of these pragmatic meanings in the titles of both newspapers. A descriptive qualitative methodology was employed in this investigation. Data collection involved the use of observation, note-taking, and interview techniques to identify various types of pragmatic meanings based on pragmatic theories including implicature, presupposition, and speech acts. 

The analysis revealed the presence of implicature, speech acts, presuppositions, as well as illocutionary and perlocutionary acts in the article titles. The articles themselves addressed diverse themes such as politics and government, crime, moral issues, economic and developmental activities, public health and welfare, education, technology, sports, human interest stories, and matters relating to war and diplomacy. 

The study concludes that the application of pragmatic meanings in titles should be concise, effective, and engaging, ensuring that the conveyed message is clear, straightforward, and comprehensible. Furthermore, it is recommended that instruction on pragmatic meanings be incorporated into language learning curricula from primary education through to the university level. 

Keywords: pragmatic meaning, titles, newspaper articles

Pulisan Village is situated in the East Likupang District of North Minahasa Regency, within North Sulawesi Province. Covering an area of 402 hectares and positioned at an elevation of 200 meters above sea level, Pulisan Village constitutes a highland region in North Minahasa. The travel time from the provincial capital of North Sulawesi to the Pulisan beach resort is approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes, accessible by various modes of transportation. Pulisan Village is renowned for its tourist attraction, Pulisan Beach, which is widely recognized throughout North Sulawesi for its scenic marine beauty that attracts numerous visitors. Located at the northern tip of North Sulawesi Island, the village experiences the convergence of west and east winds, leading to the formation of thousands of swirling seawater currents during high and low tides. This distinctive phenomenon inspired the local residents to name the area Pulisan, which today serves as a popular beach tourism destination. 

Consistent with the general tropical climate of Indonesia, Pulisan experiences distinct dry and rainy seasons. This study employs a descriptive research approach, which seeks to portray issues or situations as they naturally occur, revealing factual information with occasional interpretation or analysis (Tika, 2005). According to Kusmayadi (2004), descriptive research aims to systematically, factually, and accurately depict the phenomena and relationships under investigation. The methodology applied involves a survey technique, characterized by structured observation and investigation designed to collect relevant data from a specific location. Data collection primarily utilized questionnaires distributed to a large sample of respondents, enabling the possibility of generalizing findings to a broader population. 

The findings regarding visitor perceptions of tourism services at Pulisan Beach indicate that overall perceptions are favorable. Pulisan Beach is assessed as being highly competitive relative to other tourist destinations within North Sulawesi. Furthermore, East Likupang continues to be recognized as one of Indonesia’s Super Priority Destinations.

Keywords: perception, tourism, visitor service, attraction, beach tourism

ABSTRACKThis study aimed to quantify the incidences of dry-rot and wet-rot fruit diseases in some centers of nutmeg plantations, namely the Village of Talawid, Kendahe Satu, and Kendahe Dua, Kendahe Sub-District, The District of Sangihe Islands. This study was done for 4 months from October 2015 to January 2016. This study used a survey method with a purposive sampling in nutmeg plantations owned by the farmers in the village of Talawid, Kendahe Satu, and Kendahe Dua, each village was assigned one farm as a sample. The nutmeg tree was divided into two sectors, namely the upper and lower sector. The number of sample nutmeg trees were 20 trees; each sector of the tree was randomly observed 30 nutmeg. Observations were made three times at intervals of two weeks, of different nutmeg trees.The results of this study showed that early symptoms of dry-rot fruit disease appeared small brown rounded patches, with a diameter of approximately 0.3 cm, this section become brown and sunken (concave), while the wet-rot fruit disease, symptoms generally begin to appear at the base of the fruit, in which the diseased part started to become brown. The causal agent of dry-rot fruit disease is Stigmina myristicae, while wet-rot fruit disease caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides. The incidences of fruit rot disease in the observed center nutmeg plantations showed diffrent disease incidences. The highest average incidences of wet-rot fruit disease was 3.92%, while the highest average incidences of dry-rot fruit disease was 56.18%.Key Words: Nutmeg, Stigmina myristicae, Colletrotrichum gloeosporiodes, Incidences

ABSTRACT VEGETATIVE GROWTH OF BROWN MIDRIB (BMR) SORGHUM ON THE DIFFERENT LEVELS SHADE OG SHADE AND POPULATIONS DENSITY. The present study was conducted to determine the effect of shading area and plant population density and their interaction on vegetative growth of Brown Midrib (BMR) Sorghum. A Completely Randomized Design (CRD) in a Factorial arrangement with 2 factors of nitrogen level and shading area, as follows: factor A = shading area of A1 = no shading area (0%), and N2 = shading area; whereas factor B = plant population density of B1 = 4 plants, B2 = 6 plants, B3 = 8 plants, and B4 = 10 plants. Variables measured were: leaves number, plant height, and the correlation between leaves number and plant population density. Research results showed that plant height in open area (no shading) was about 86.33 cm and significantly higher (P < 0.05) compared to other treatments. Leaves number in open area was about 7.55 sheats and significantly higher (P < 0.05) compared to other treatments. It can be concluded that shading positively decreased or retarded Brown Midrib (BMR) Sorghum growth as indicated by lower plant heights in shading area. In a limited daylight, plants needs an adaptation period to fulfill their needs for photosyntesis processes. Key words: brown midrib (BMR) sorghum, growth, population density, shading

This study aims to examine the Community of Practice within PT. Putra Karangetang by focusing on the elements of Domain/Shared Repertoire, Community/Mutual Engagement, and Practice/Shared Repertoire as key factors. The research was conducted over the period from November 2015 to January 2016, encompassing all stages from preparation to the compilation of the report. Primary data served as the basis for analysis, with a stratified random sampling technique employed to select 40 members from the target population. Data were analyzed descriptively using a Likert scale. The findings indicate that the elements of Domain/Shared Repertoire, Community/Mutual Engagement, and Practice/Shared Repertoire constitute strong foundational components in the Community of Practice among official employees at PT. Putra Karangetang, accounting for 93.37% of the observed variance. The Domain element represents a defined identity centered on specific interests, with membership implying a commitment to shared goals and the development of connections or networks aimed at achieving sustainability. The Community element serves as a platform for individuals with common interests to engage in discussions, share knowledge, and learn collectively. Finally, the Practice element reflects the ongoing process by which employees enhance their skills, not only through general work activities but also by exchanging methods, techniques, and experiences, thereby establishing behavioral patterns and fostering professional improvement.

Background: Limited awareness among mothers, families, and the broader community regarding the significance of breastfeeding for infants, coupled with the absence of supportive regulations or initiatives at the district or city level, has hindered the effective implementation of exclusive breastfeeding programs. This study aims to examine the enactment of Government Regulation No. 33/2012 concerning exclusive breastfeeding practices in Bitung City.

Methodology: Employing qualitative research methods, this study utilized both primary and secondary data sources. A total of 13 informants participated in the research. Data collection was conducted through in-depth interviews and document analysis, with all information transcribed and subsequently organized into a data matrix. The analysis incorporated source triangulation, method triangulation, and data triangulation to enhance validity.

Results: Findings revealed the absence of regulations supporting the enforcement of Government Regulation No. 33/2012 on exclusive breastfeeding within Bitung City. Additionally, there is a lack of trained counselors and insufficient dissemination of information regarding exclusive breastfeeding. Furthermore, Posyandu cadres have not been engaged in outreach activities promoting exclusive breastfeeding. Supervision and guidance for midwives are inadequate, contributing to the continued sale of formula milk to breastfeeding mothers. Moreover, facilities such as nursing rooms are unevenly available, being primarily confined to the puskesmas level.

Conclusion: It is concluded that the policy regarding exclusive breastfeeding in Bitung City has not been implemented in accordance with the mandates stipulated in Government Regulation No. 33 of 2012.

The present study aimed to investigate the effects of replacing fish meal with snail meal (Pila ampulacea) in the diet on the quality of quail eggs (Coturnix coturnix Japonica). A total of 60 quails, each five weeks of age, were observed over an eight-week experimental period. A completely randomized design was employed, comprising four treatment groups with five replications per treatment. The experimental diets varied in the level of snail meal substitution for fish meal as follows: R0 (0% snail meal + 15% fish meal), R1 (5% snail meal + 10% fish meal), R2 (10% snail meal + 5% fish meal), and R3 (15% snail meal + 0% fish meal). The parameters assessed included egg weight, yolk index, albumen index, yolk color, and shell thickness. The findings demonstrated that the incorporation of snail meal significantly influenced (P<0.05) both egg weight and albumen index, while no significant effects were observed on yolk index, yolk color, or shell thickness. Consequently, it can be inferred that substituting fish meal with up to 15% snail meal in the quail diet yields eggs of satisfactory quality in terms of weight, yolk index, albumen index, yolk color, and shell thickness.

Keywords: Snail meal, fish meal, quail egg quality.

The objective of this study was to isolate and select probiotic Lactobacillus strains from the intestines of carp, with the potential application in aquaculture. Carp specimens weighing approximately 200 grams were sourced from the Center for Fish Hatchery and Disease Control (BP3I) in Tateli. Following aseptic dissection, the intestines were excised, cleaned, and 1 gram samples were homogenized using a mortar. The resulting homogenate was transferred into tubes containing 9 mL of NaCl solution to achieve a 1:10 dilution ratio. Subsequently, the tubes underwent centrifugation at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes, repeated twice, to obtain a clarified supernatant free from debris. The supernatant was then serially diluted to concentrations ranging from 10⁻² to 10⁻³. Aliquots of these dilutions were spread plated onto De Man, Rogosa, and Sharpe (MRS) agar medium and incubated at 28°C for 24 to 48 hours. Emerging bacterial colonies were subjected to repeated re-isolation to secure pure single colonies. These pure isolates were cultured in the same medium and subjected to further identification procedures including Gram staining, biochemical assays, and evaluations of proteolytic, amylolytic, cellulolytic activities, antibiotic resistance profiles, antagonistic properties, and pathogenicity. The isolated colonies exhibited milky white pigmentation, were round and convex in morphology, and comprised elongated Gram-positive cells. Biochemical testing identified the isolates as belonging to the genus Lactobacillus. Furthermore, the strains demonstrated enzymatic activities (proteolytic, amylolytic, cellulolytic), antagonistic effects against target organisms, sensitivity to antibiotics indicated by clear inhibition zones around probiotic discs, and showed no pathogenic or toxic effects in tested models. These findings collectively suggest that Lactobacillus species isolated from carp intestines possess characteristics suitable for development as probiotic agents in aquaculture practices.

The present study, entitled "Deiksis dalam film God's Not Dead Karya Harold Cronk," aims to identify and categorize the various types of deixis and to examine their usage within the film God's Not Dead, directed by Harold Cronk. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data for this investigation were extracted from utterances appearing throughout the film. Data analysis was conducted based on Levinson’s theoretical framework.

Findings reveal the presence of five distinct types of deixis within the film: person deixis, encompassing first-person pronouns (e.g., I, I'm, mine, me, we), second-person pronouns (e.g., you, your, yourself), and third-person pronouns (e.g., they, them, he, she’s, his, everyone); place deixis, including locations such as the world, podium, classroom, pool, Roman Colosseum, La Rive Gauche, park, class, in front of a room, Dakar, Zurich, Frankfurt, and Carter International; time deixis, with temporal references such as next Friday, three sessions, twenty minutes, approximately 13.7 billion years ago, 2,500 years, next week’s, tomorrow, 2,000 years ago, year, one day, and all the time; discourse deixis, featuring demonstratives like that, this, those, and it’s; and social deixis, which includes titles and forms of address such as prosecutor, defense attorney, jury, my friend, ladies, gentlemen, brave young freshman, my father, honey, merciful father, silly boy, minority, and freshman.

Additionally, the analysis highlights the utilization of gestural and symbolic deixis within the film’s dialogue and scenes. This research aspires to contribute to the enhancement of readers’ understanding of pragmatics, with a particular focus on deixis.

Keywords: Pragmatic Analysis, Deixis, Film, God’s Not Dead

The primary objective of this study is to assess the capacity of agricultural land in supporting food self-sufficiency within South Minahasa Regency. Specifically, the research seeks to identify particular areas within South Minahasa that serve as a foundation for the carrying capacity related to food security, thus enabling these regions to function as baseline references in the context of population growth. The anticipated contribution of this research lies in providing valuable insights to local government authorities and relevant agencies involved in food security, facilitating informed land use planning to prevent challenges associated with the land’s carrying capacity for food self-sufficiency. Furthermore, the study aims to enrich the body of knowledge concerning regional economic development and land resource management. To achieve these objectives, the research employs a methodology that evaluates the carrying capacity of croplands by integrating theoretical frameworks proposed by Odum, Cristeiler, E. Howard, and Issard. The findings indicate that the overall average carrying capacity of croplands in South Minahasa Regency is 0.414, suggesting that the current agricultural land is insufficient to achieve food self-sufficiency and fails to adequately meet the population’s food demands.

Abstracts: Right ventricular (RV) function provides strong prognostic information in patients treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) due to myocardial infarction. Longitudinal RV systolic function can be assessed by the measurement of the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE). This study aimed to evaluate the correlation between TAPSE and revascularization time with 30-day mortality using TIMI risk score in patients presenting STEMI who underwent revascularization of right coronary artery (RCA). This was a descriptive amd analytical study. Data were collected from iSTEMI Registry database which consisted of 49 STEMI patients undergoing PCI in RCA and TAPSE measurement at Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou General Hospital from October 3rd, 2018 to July 28th, 2019. Echocardiographic examination was done within 48 hours of hospitalization. A descriptive analysis and bivariate correlation with Spearman's rho were applied between given variables. P-value of <0.05 was considered to be statistically significant. The results showed that the mean age of the patients was 57.92 10.345 years old and 79.2% were male. The mean TAPSE measurement was 18.51 mm +/- 3.63 mm. The median revascularization time was 357.5 minutes while median TIMI score was 4. Shorter treatment time (p=0.708) and lower TIMI score (p=0.923) were not associated with better right ventricular function measured with TAPSE in patients undergoing RCA intervention. In conclusion, right ventricular function is not associated with revascularization time and thirty days mortality in patients presenting with ST-elevation acute myocardial infarction involving right coronary artery.Keywords: tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion; revascularization time; right coronary artery; ST-elevation myocardial infarction

This study aims to evaluate the performance of civil servants and employees at the Wenam medical clinic in Atwenam district, Lanny Jaya regency, in delivering healthcare services to the local community. Employing a qualitative research approach, the study involved six informants: four civil servants/employees from the Wenam medical clinic—including the person in charge, nurses, and a midwife—and two residents of Wenam village. Data were collected through interviews, and the analysis was conducted using the interactive model developed by Miles and Huberman.

The findings indicate that the performance of the Wenam medical clinic employees remains suboptimal. This conclusion is derived from several factors: (1) the quality of healthcare services provided, assessed in terms of precision, timeliness, and accuracy; (2) the quantity or volume of healthcare services delivered; (3) the utilization of working hours, taking into account absenteeism, delays, and loss of effective working time; and (4) collaboration among co-workers in executing healthcare duties. 

Based on these results, it is recommended that targeted measures be implemented to enhance employee performance at the Wenam medical clinic. These measures include: (1) improvement of clinic infrastructure, particularly through the provision of medical equipment and other health facilities; (2) increasing employee motivation by offering special or additional allowances; and (3) supplying housing facilities for clinic employees in close proximity to the clinic.

Keywords: employee performance, healthcare service, medical clinic, qualitative study

The contemporary lifestyle has undergone rapid transformation in tandem with the progression of globalization. Annually, the concept of beauty continues to evolve, transcending mere desire to become an essential daily requisite for women, thereby representing one of the most significant indicators of beauty. It can be asserted that the relationship between women and cosmetics is inherently inseparable. Women exhibit considerable concern for their skin and overall appearance, consistently striving to maintain a fresh and attractive look. This study aims to examine the differences in purchase decisions between Korean and Indonesian cosmetic brands, focusing on variables such as price, social influences, celebrity endorsement, and product packaging. The research employs an Independent T-Test analysis to compare consumer preferences between Korean and Indonesian cosmetic brands within the city of Manado. Convenience sampling was utilized to gather data from 200 respondents. The findings indicate no significant difference in purchase decisions related to price and social influence between the two brands. However, significant differences were observed concerning celebrity endorsement and product packaging. It is recommended that marketers representing both Korean and Indonesian cosmetic brands place greater emphasis on the specific factors that impact consumer purchase decisions.

This study sought to evaluate the impact of stocking density on both the growth performance and survival rates of saline tilapia. The research was carried out at the Aquaculture Technology Laboratory over the period from February to August 2021. Employing a completely randomized design (CRD), the experiment included four treatments with three replications each, resulting in a total of twelve experimental units. The variable under investigation was the stocking density of tilapia, with the following treatments: A (10 fish per 20 liters), B (15 fish per 20 liters), C (20 fish per 20 liters), and D (25 fish per 20 liters). Growth and survival rate (%) data were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA) for CRD, followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test. Water quality parameters monitored throughout the study comprised temperature, dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, and salinity. The ANOVA results indicated that variations in stocking density significantly influenced growth but did not have a significant effect on survival rates. The LSD test revealed that growth in treatment A did not differ significantly from treatments B and C, whereas treatments A, B, and C showed a statistically significant difference compared to treatment D. Environmental conditions during the experiment included a temperature range of 29 °C to 30.9 °C, DO levels from 4.07 to 6.80 ppm, pH values between 6.78 and 7.95, and salinity maintained at 25 ppt.

The research intends to determine the optimal concentration of honey addition in sperm dilution on sperm motility, fertilization and eggs hatchability of Nile Tolapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Experimental design used was a Complete Randomized Design (CRD) with three times repetition of four treatments. The concentration of honey addition used for treatment are A (0 ml of honey in 100 ml of physiological NaCl), B (0.60 ml of honey in 99.40 ml of physiological NaCl), C (0.65 ml of honey in 99.35 ml of physiological NaCl), D (0.70 ml of honey in 99.30 ml of physiological NaCl). Parent used consisted of five female parent and five male parent with 250 500 mg weight. Sperm dilution containers used was 12 plastic cups and the container fertilization and hatching eggs container used was 12 brass plates. Spermatozoa motility observation performed immediately after dilution process. Fertilization observation was performed after 12 hours of fertilization process, and Egg Hatchability observation was performed after 60 hours of fertilization. The observation results showed that the addition of honey in sperm dilution contributed significant effect on spermatozoa motility, fertilization and eggs hatchability of Nile Tolapia (Oreochromis niloticus). This observation showed that the addition of 0.70 ml of honey in a sperm dilution was the best treatment seen from the average percentage of spermatozoa motility (73,33 %), fertilization (80,00%) and eggs hatchability (77,33 %.) Keywords: Honey, sperm dilution, spermatozoa motility, fertilization, eggs hatchability Nile Tolapia

The government in this case the Directorate General of Tax (DJP) always wanted to perform the task in terms of collecting tax revenue so that the nation's survival is maintained. Therefore, the Directorate General of Tax (DJP) is trying to get the tax collection in Indonesia on target by always trying to improve the service by updating the rules of tax collection that meet the requirements of justice, juridical, economic, financial and simple. Telaga Bakti Persada Ternate whether it is in compliance with the provisions of the Taxation Law. No. 36 of 2008 Income Tax Income. This research uses Descriptive Research Method. The aim of this study was to analyze the individual and combined effects of trust, commitment, communication, and complaint handling on customer retention for mobile products, as well as to identify the most influential variable among these factors at PT Erafone Mega Mall. It is imperative for companies to implement effective strategies to attract and retain customers, such as relationship marketing, which encompasses four key variables: trust, commitment, communication, and complaint resolution. Successful execution of these strategies enhances customer satisfaction and comfort with the products and services offered, which subsequently increases the likelihood of repeat purchases and customer recommendations.

This research employed a descriptive verification design. Data were collected through questionnaires and relevant literature review. To assess the impact of the independent variables on customer retention, multiple linear regression analysis was conducted. The validity and reliability of the instruments were confirmed, and assumption tests—including normality, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity tests—were performed to ensure the robustness of the analysis. The findings reveal that all four independent variables exert a significant simultaneous influence on customer retention. Notably, customer trust emerged as the most dominant factor affecting retention in the context of PT Erafone Manado products.

In an endeavor to enhance the efficiency of regional financial management systems, the government promulgated the Minister of Home Affairs Circular No. 910/1866/SJ on April 17, 2017, which addresses the implementation of non-cash transactions. This circular aligns with the provisions stipulated in Article 283, paragraph (2) of Act Number 23 of 2014, as well as Presidential Instruction Number 10 of 2016 concerning the Prevention and Eradication of Corruption. Non-cash transactions refer to payment processes conducted not in physical cash but through account transfers from one party to another. This study aims to assess the preparedness of the Bitung City Environmental Agency in adopting the non-cash transaction system within regional financial management, as well as to identify the challenges encountered during its implementation. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, the research findings indicate that the Bitung Environmental Office has progressively implemented the non-cash transaction system in the APBD, in accordance with the Minister of Home Affairs Circular No. 910/1866/SJ. However, several obstacles have been observed, including occasional disruptions in administrative procedures, limited effectiveness of socialization efforts, and difficulties applying the system to levy collections involving small nominal amounts.

Environmental issues constitute a significant and complex concern, particularly as population growth and urban development substantially influence the environmental quality in Manado City. Environmental quality refers to the condition of the environment that supports an optimal carrying capacity for human habitation in a given area. This quality encompasses various components, including water quality, air quality, and land cover quality. The present study aims to analyze the Environmental Quality Index of Manado City by evaluating three specific indices: the Water Quality Index, the Air Quality Index, and the Land Cover Quality Index.

This research employs a descriptive quantitative methodology. Water quality measurements were conducted at six points across three major rivers in Manado City—the Tondano River, the Sario River, and the Malalayang River—covering both upstream and downstream locations. The parameters assessed included Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Total Suspended Solids (TSS), Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), and Dissolved Oxygen (DO). Water quality was analyzed utilizing the Pollution Index (PI) method, which was then converted into the Water Quality Index value. Air quality measurements were taken at three distinct locations representing office, transportation, and residential environments, focusing on sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) concentrations. The European Union (EU) Air Quality Index model was applied to calculate the Air Quality Index. Land cover quality was determined by calculating the Land Cover Index through the measurement of Manado City's total area alongside the green land or forested regions, using ArcGIS software. The ratio of green land area to total city area was converted into the Land Cover Quality Index.

The overall Environmental Quality Index was derived by weighted aggregation of the Water Quality Index (30%), Air Quality Index (30%), and Land Cover Quality Index (40%). Results indicated a decline in water quality, as BOD, COD, and DO parameters exceeded the standards established by Government Regulation No. 82 of 2001. Consequently, water quality was classified as mildly polluted according to the Ministerial Decree on Environment No. 115 of 2003, with a Water Quality Index value of 80. Air quality assessment revealed the highest concentrations of SO2 and NO2 in transportation areas, resulting in an Air Quality Index value of 30.56. The Land Cover Quality Index was calculated at 89.60, derived from a Land Cover Index value of 0.72. The composite Environmental Quality Index for Manado City was determined to be 69, categorized as fairly good.

In conclusion, the study finds that the Environmental Quality Index of Manado City is moderately satisfactory. It is recommended that the local government enhance environmental management and protection activities to promote further improvements in the city’s environmental condition.

Keywords: Environmental Quality Index, Water Quality Index, Air Quality Index, Land Cover Quality Index, Manado City

Irrigation encompasses the provision, regulation, and disposal of water necessary to support various agricultural practices, including swamp irrigation, subsurface aeration irrigation, pump irrigation, and pond irrigation. This study focuses on the development of irrigation infrastructure in the Sangkub and Bintauna sub-districts of North Bolaang Mangondow Regency, North Sulawesi Province, specifically targeting the irrigated rice fields of Sangkub Kanan and Sangkub Kiri. Notably, the construction of the Left Sangkub Irrigation Network has experienced delays, thereby necessitating a systematic identification, analysis, mitigation, and allocation of potential risks associated with the project. Risk modeling has been employed as a foundational tool to guide decision-making processes among stakeholders, aiming to address and alleviate any adverse outcomes during the irrigation network construction.

The principal objectives of this research are to: (1) identify the various types of risks encountered during the construction of the Left Sangkub Irrigation Network; (2) determine the dominant or major risk categories impacting project implementation; and (3) design models for the existing system and risk mitigation management to minimize potential negative consequences. The study utilized a qualitative risk analysis approach, engaging ten participants representing the owner, contractor, and consultant. This method facilitates a systematic, factual, and accurate depiction of phenomena and their interrelations relevant to the investigation.

The findings revealed a total of 47 distinct risks associated with the Sangkub Kiri Irrigation Project, classified into ten categories: political (5 risks), environmental (5), economic (3), financial (5), natural (3), project-specific (6), human (5), technical (9), criminal (3), and safety-related (3). Risk analysis results further indicated that 13 risks (27.66%) were categorized as unacceptable, 25 risks (53.19%) as undesirable, 7 risks (14.89%) as acceptable, and 2 risks (4.26%) as negligible. The unacceptable risks were predominantly human-related, notably including labor delays attributed to holidays. In contrast, the undesirable risks were primarily technical, such as discrepancies between contracted work volumes and field conditions necessitating review and adjustment.

Risk mitigation strategies aimed to reduce the adverse impact of identified risks, particularly those classified as major. Among the 13 mitigation measures addressing unacceptable risks, one involved enforcing workforce discipline and implementing a rotational work schedule to allow workers adequate recovery time. For the 25 risks deemed undesirable, mitigation actions included discussions and proposals to revise contract work volumes, incorporating reductions where appropriate to better align contract specifications with actual field conditions.

Keywords: risk management, irrigation network, risk mitigation, dominant risk category

This study examines local taxes imposed by municipal authorities, which serve as a financial foundation for local governance and regional development initiatives. The implementation of local taxation is anticipated to generate substantial fiscal revenues for local governments. Among various local taxes, the advertisement tax is identified as a promising source for enhancing regional financial income. The primary objective of this research is to assess the potential revenue from advertisement tax, evaluate its effectiveness and efficiency levels, and determine its contribution to local tax revenues in North Minahasa District. A descriptive analytical approach was employed for this study. Findings reveal that the potential advertisement tax revenue in 2017 was approximately Rp. 1,250,560,290, as estimated through an analysis of realized revenue growth. The effectiveness of the advertisement tax between 2012 and 2016 exhibited fluctuations; however, it reached the categorization of "very effective" in 2015 and 2016, with effectiveness percentages of 118.16% and 199.59%, respectively. This high effectiveness is attributed to the implementation incurring minimal costs. Conversely, the contribution of the advertisement tax to local tax revenue from 2012 to 2016 was relatively low, ranging between 0.5% and 3.32%. To enhance revenue collection, it is recommended that the collection system be subjected to increased supervision and control, coupled with efforts to encourage taxpayer re-registration and enforce sanctions, thereby optimizing the tax's revenue potential.

Keywords: advertisement tax, local tax, revenue potential, effectiveness, efficiency, contribution

This study seeks to evaluate the perceptions of farmer groups regarding the role of agricultural extension officers in Tatengesan Satu Village, Pusomaen Sub-district, Southeast Minahasa Regency. The research was carried out over the period from June to August 2019. Both primary and secondary data sources were employed. Primary data were collected through structured interviews using questionnaires directed at two farmer groups, involving each group's chairman, secretary, treasurer, one regular member, and one agricultural extension officer, resulting in a total of nine respondents. Secondary data were gathered from pertinent institutions, including the Agricultural Extension Office (BPP), the Village Head Office, and the Pusomaen Sub-district Office of Southeast Minahasa Regency. Additional secondary data comprised literature obtained from local bookstores and digital sources, notably Google Scholar, providing access to books, journal articles, and theses pertinent to the assessment of farmer groups concerning the implementation of agricultural extension functions.

The findings indicate that the farmer groups perceive the functions of agricultural extension officers to be only partially fulfilled. Specifically, extension officers have effectively assumed their roles as initiators, facilitators, and motivators. However, their functions as intermediaries, analysts, and agents of change have not been fully realized from the perspective of the farmer groups. Conversely, extension officers reported that they have executed their duties to the best of their abilities, with the exception of the agent of change role, which they assert is limited by the farmers’ own capacity for self-initiated improvements in their agricultural enterprises to enhance profitability.

Identification of individuals at high risk is essential for the prevention of coronary heart disease. Physical signs such as earlobe creases and forehead wrinkles are readily observable and may serve as potential indicators of the severity of coronary artery lesions. This study sought to investigate the association between the morphology of earlobe creases and forehead wrinkles and the severity of coronary artery stenosis in patients diagnosed with stable angina pectoris, utilizing the modified Gensini scoring system. Employing a cross-sectional observational design, photographs of the forehead and both ears were taken from all participants who met the inclusion criteria. Subsequent scoring and correlation analyses were conducted to examine the relationship between earlobe crease and forehead wrinkle assessments and the severity of coronary artery stenosis as measured by the modified Gensini scores. Among the 40 participants, 28 (70%) were male. Forehead wrinkle scores were predominantly categorized as score 1 or 2, encompassing 32 patients (80%). Earlobe crease morphology was primarily composed of type A (65%) compared to type B (35%). Notably, patients exhibiting type B earlobe creases had an average modified Gensini score that was 9 points lower than those with type A creases (used as the reference group), with statistical significance (p < 0.001). Regarding forehead wrinkle scores, patients with non-zero scores demonstrated modified Gensini scores approximately 4 to 5 units higher than those with a zero score; however, the small subgroup with zero wrinkle scores (n = 3) limited the statistical power, rendering this difference non-significant (p = 0.507). In summary, the study found a significant positive correlation between the presence of earlobe creases and the severity of coronary artery stenosis among patients with stable angina pectoris. Conversely, no robust relationship was identified between forehead wrinkle morphology and coronary artery stenosis severity as assessed by the modified Gensini score in this population.

Keywords: stable angina; earlobe crease; forehead wrinkles; modified Gensini score

Nonetheless, continuous improvements are necessary to address the weaker service elements and to elevate the quality of all service aspects toward exemplary standards.

This study focuses on the analysis of the river roughness coefficient of the Sario River, the main watercourse within the Sario Watershed. Rapid population growth has led to the transformation of protected areas along the riverbanks into residential settlements, resulting in a reduced channel capacity and increased flood risk, exemplified by the flood event in January 2014. The Manning equation, widely employed to estimate the flow capacity of open channels, was utilized to determine the roughness coefficient of the Sario River. Data collection was conducted over a three-month period from January to March 2015. Key measured parameters included river width, top width, bottom width, water depth, channel depth, pseudosection profiles, flow velocity, channel bed slope, and channel characteristics. A survey methodology was implemented, with measurement and observation points selected through purposive sampling. The mean roughness coefficients calculated for the Sario River were 0.049 upstream, 0.050 midstream, and 0.060 downstream, with an overall average of 0.048. The observed increase in roughness coefficient relative to secondary data for natural channels was attributed to the presence of debris and suspended particles within the water. 

Keywords: River Roughness, Manning Equation, Sario River

This study seeks to evaluate customer satisfaction regarding pharmaceutical services at Syalom Amurang Pharmacy. The research primarily concentrates on the dimensions of product quality, service quality, emotional factors, cost, and price. The theoretical framework employed is Lupyoadi's Consumer Satisfaction Theory. Utilizing qualitative research methods, data were gathered through observations, interviews, and document analysis. The participants comprised members of the Amurang City community who had procured medications from the Syalom Pharmacy. The research was conducted on-site at Syalom Amurang Pharmacy, guided by Law No. 25 of 2009, which establishes standards for public service. These standards emphasize the obligation of service units to provide citizens with their rights and essential needs within the scope of service delivery. The pharmacy’s role in the community is critical, as customer satisfaction with pharmaceutical services can be assessed based on predetermined criteria, including service requirements, product quality, price, service quality, emotional engagement, and cost. Analysis of the five service criteria reveals that customers expressed dissatisfaction with both product and service quality, whereas they reported emotional satisfaction related to brief service times. Additionally, customers considered fees and rates appropriate and expressed overall satisfaction concerning service, price, and cost, as corroborated by direct field observations at Syalom Amurang Pharmacy.

Two-wheeled vehicles, locally known as Ojek, constitute an informal mode of transportation essential to the residents of Bitung City’s Madidir subdistrict. These motorcycles are predominantly utilized to access areas that are difficult to navigate using four-wheeled public transport vehicles. The transportation of both passengers and goods operates on an agreement between service users and Ojek riders. Typically, Ojek drivers work collectively in groups, congregating at designated points alongside other two-wheeled vehicle operators. An Ojek rider, often referred to as an Ojek base, generally functions as an independent, conventional operator not affiliated with any formal company.

Engaging in Ojek driving is a livelihood chosen by many individuals despite its typically low and unstable income. Nevertheless, this occupation serves as a primary source of sustenance, enabling riders to support their families’ economic needs. Economic challenges are prevalent across various sectors, including both formal and informal domains. Within the informal sector, two-wheeled transportation services face particular difficulties. Advances in technology have facilitated public access to online transportation services, further impacting traditional Ojek bases. Moreover, the majority of Ojek riders in Bitung City do not own private homes or land within the urban area, often relying on rented, borrowed, or otherwise temporary arrangements. This phenomenon is partially due to many motorcycle taxi drivers originating from rural villages throughout North Sulawesi province.

Keywords: transportation, informal sector, livelihood

This study addresses the issues previously identified and aims to investigate the impact of education and training on the job performance of civil servants at the Regional Personnel Board of Bitung City. Education and training are fundamentally understood as processes designed to enhance the potential, competencies, and career development of employees. In addition to elevating cognitive abilities such as reasoning, IQ, and professional skills, development programs also seek to foster improvements in ethical values, morality, and spiritual quotient (SQ).

The overarching goal of education and training initiatives is to advance organizational productivity. Achieving this broad objective requires the accomplishment of specific, targeted aims. Employing an exploratory research design, this study reveals a notable relationship between education and training and the work performance of civil servants in the Regional Personnel Board of Bitung City. This is evidenced by a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.68, which approaches the maximum value of 1.00, and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.46. Consequently, 46% of the variance in civil servant performance at the Bitung City Personnel Board is accounted for by education and training, while the remaining 54% is influenced by other factors.

These findings suggest that higher levels of education and training are associated with enhanced job performance among civil servants. The study concludes that education and training exert a significant influence on the performance of civil servants at the Regional Personnel Board of Bitung City, impacting both their attitudes and behaviors in fulfilling official responsibilities.

Keywords: education and training, job performance, civil service apparatus (ASN)

At Bank Mandiri KC Dululolong Lasut Manado, an issue has arisen concerning the instability of the customer savings rate. This fluctuation in subscriber numbers is attributed primarily to a decline in the clients' economic conditions, as well as other factors such as service deficiencies that fail to meet customer expectations, including unsatisfactory interest rates or inadequate facilities, which prompt customers to shift to competing banks. Establishing the company’s credibility is a complex task that requires the implementation of appropriate strategies to achieve organizational objectives effectively, particularly in the domain of marketing. Fundamentally, relationship marketing involves fostering long-term connections and bonds among producers, consumers, suppliers, and other stakeholders. Customer loyalty refers to behaviors linked to a product’s brand, encompassing actions such as the potential renewal of contracts in the future. 

This study employs a quantitative research methodology, utilizing a Simple Random Sampling technique for data collection. The product moment formula was applied to calculate the simple correlation coefficient. Statistical analysis clearly indicates that the independent variable, relationship marketing, significantly influences the dependent variable, customer loyalty. The direction of this relationship is positive, suggesting that increased engagement in relationship marketing activities results in enhanced customer loyalty. These findings align with the initial hypothesis, underscoring that relationship marketing constitutes a critical determinant of customer loyalty, as effective relationship marketing fosters the creation and sustenance of loyal customers. Consequently, the application of robust relationship marketing strategies is positively correlated with improvements in customer loyalty.

Keywords: Relationship Marketing, Customer Loyalty

Rapid development of building growth resulted in the decline of the green area around Tondano Lake. Tondano lake as a conservation area also acts as a tourist area and watershed. The reduction of green land with the increasing number of buildings causes the ground surface to absorb more hot temperatures from the sun, this will cause an increase in surface temperature on land. This research was conducted with spatiotemporal to analyze land cover in Tondano lake using Landsat-8 Imagery with TIRS (Thermal Infrared Red Sensor) and OLI (Operation Land Imager) bands in the period 2015, 2019, and 2021. The model is based on LST (Land Surface Temperature), NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), and NDBI (Normalized Difference Built-up Index) algorithms. Variations in the vegetation greeness index ranged from -0.30 0.86 in 2015, -0.21 0.86 in 2019 and -0.06 0.84 in 2021. Meanwhile, the highest building density index ranged from 0.22 in 2015, 0.29 in 2019, and 0.18 in 2021. Pearson Product Moment correlation is used to determine the relationship between land surface temperature or LST affecting greenish levels or NDVI and building density levels or NDBI. The results of the correlation test showed the relationship between LST and NDVI is that the higher the land surface temperature in one region, the lower the level of vegetation in the region, in contrast to the relationship between LST and NDBI.

Background: This research was undertaken at PT. Trans Samudera Sulut Service, a company specializing in expedition services commonly referred to as freight forwarding. The firm offers freight forwarding services involving the transportation of cargo both domestically and internationally. The objective of this study is to examine the role of freight forwarders in the execution of import-export operations. The research methodology employed involves data analysis conducted concurrently with data collection processes, including data reduction, presentation, and verification. In this context, a freight forwarder is defined as a business entity that provides comprehensive services for all activities related to the delivery, transportation, and receipt of goods by means of multimodal transport, encompassing land, sea, and air routes. The functions of the freight forwarder within the import-export business encompass cargo consolidation, carrier responsibilities, documentation handling, packaging, and insurance management. The findings indicate that the freight forwarder's role in import-export operations is generally well-executed; however, certain challenges persist, such as discrepancies between documentation and inspected goods, adverse weather conditions, and the reliance on external shipping facilities rather than owned aircraft or vessels. Consequently, it is recommended that companies enhance their focus on the strategic roles performed by freight forwarders during import-export activities. Additionally, PT. Trans Samudera Sulut Service actively contributes to facilitating the delivery of goods for various entrepreneurs in North Sulawesi by providing reliable freight forwarding services for both domestic and international shipments.

Keywords: Freight Forwarder Role, Import, Export

This study, entitled "Derivational Affixes in English and the Nanusa Dialect of the Talaud Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to describe and analyze the derivational affixes in English and the Nanusa dialect of the Talaud language with respect to their form, function, and meaning across verbs, nouns, adjectives, and adverbs. The primary objective is to identify the similarities and differences between the derivational affixation systems in English and the Nanusa dialect by applying William O’Grady’s (1987) theoretical framework, complemented by Lado’s contrastive analysis method. Employing a descriptive research design, the data on English derivational affixes were extracted from the textbook *Contemporary Linguistic Analysis: An Introduction* (O’Grady, 1987), while data for the Nanusa dialect were obtained through fieldwork with four native speakers residing in Mamahan village, Talaud Island. The findings indicate that both English and the Nanusa dialect utilize derivational affixes in verb, noun, adjective, and adverb formation. English derivational processes predominantly involve prefixes and suffixes, whereas the Nanusa dialect employs prefixes, infixes, suffixes, and confixes. Notably, both languages feature derivational prefixes conveying negative meanings. Additionally, in the semantic domain of professions or occupations, English derives related terms mainly through suffixation, whereas the Nanusa dialect employs infixation. 

Keywords: Derivational Affixes, English, Nanusa Dialect of Talaud Language, Contrastive Analysis

This study, entitled *Analysis of Signs in The Crucifixion Film: A Semiotic Analysis,* aims to identify, categorize, and interpret the various types and meanings of signs present within *The Crucifixion* film. Employing Peirce’s semiotic theory as the analytical framework, the research involves the systematic identification, classification, and examination of signs across multiple scenes. The methodology adopted in this study is descriptive in nature. To support the analysis, the researcher reviewed relevant literature including books and academic journals concerning semiotics. Data collection was conducted by extracting signs from each scene containing semiotic elements, which were subsequently analyzed through the lens of Peirce’s triadic model of signs.

The findings indicate the presence of three primary categories of signs within the film: icons, indexes, and symbols. Iconic signs were identified in five scenes, representing elements such as a man and woman, a book, Sister Adelina and Vaduva, the book again, and Agares. Indexical signs appeared in nine scenes, encompassing objects and phenomena such as a prison cell iron, blood, black attire, light, an insect, strangulation, rain, and additional instances of blood. Symbolic signs were observed in five scenes, including prayer candles, crosses, prohibitory signs, masks, and crosses once more.

Each category of sign conveys distinct meanings. For example, the icons of the man and woman symbolize Father Phil and Nicole, respectively. The icons representing Sister Adelina and Vaduva denote their respective characters. The icon of the exorcism book is characterized as a brown, square-shaped volume. The icon of Agares is depicted as a demon with a bald head and a skull-like body. Regarding indexes, the prison cell symbolizes confinement due to Father Dimitru’s murder; the blood indexes reflect physiological reactions of Sister Adelina and the fall of Father Gabrielle; the black attire indicates mourning; the flashlight connotes darkness; the insect signifies Agares’ malice toward Nicole; strangulation represents Satan Agares’ resentment over Sister Vaduva’s visitation; and rain is interpreted as a mockery involving holy water. Symbols such as prayer candles represent the light of Christ; crosses signify life and strength; prohibitory signs denote boundaries that cannot be crossed; masks are associated with costumes worn during the Strigoi festival.

In summary, this research elucidates the complex semiotic dimensions embedded within *The Crucifixion* film, highlighting how varied signs contribute layered meanings to the narrative.

Keywords: Signs, The Crucifixion Film, Semiotic Analysis

This study aims to examine the control and supervision mechanisms involved in the issuance of the Approval Letter of Expenditure of Goods (SPPB) for imports, by adhering to the applicable procedures and regulations. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the findings indicate that the current procedures for issuing the SPPB conform to the standards stipulated in the Director General of Customs and Excise Regulation No. PER-16/BC/2016. Keywords: procedures, regulations, SPPB, import.

DIGESTIBILITY OF THE ORGANIC MATTER, CRUDE FIBER AND CRUDE FAT IN BROILERS RATION CONTAINING PUMPKIN WASTE MEAL (Cucurbita moschata). A research was done to determine the digestibility values of feed in term of organic matter, crude fiber and crude fat containing pumpkin waste meal (PWM) fed to broilers. The research was conducted by involving 20 unsexed broilers, strain CP 707 at 5 weeks old with an average body weight of 1073 g. Experiment design of the Completely Randomized Designed (CRD) was applied with 4 treatments and 5 replications at each treatment. Honestly significant difference test (HSD) was used to define higher significant effects of the treatments. The treatments consist of 100% basal ration (BR) + 0% PWM (R0), 95% BR + 5% PWM (R1), 90% BR + 10% PWM (R2) and 85% BR + 15% PWM (R3). Results showed that digestibility of crude fiber was significantly affected by treatments (P<0.01), but digestibility values of organic matter and crude fat were not influenced by these treatments. The statistical test showed that the crude fiber digestibility of R0 (56.92%) was lower than those of R1 (63.10%), R2 (67.71%) and R3 (66.30%). Furthermore, there was no difference among digestibility values of R1, R2 and R3. Based on this research, it can be concluded that pumpkin waste meal could be utilized to replace some parts up to 15% in ration of broilers. Keyword: Pumpkin waste meal, digestibility, broiler

Employees, regarded as the most critical components within an organization, serve as essential instruments for enhancing corporate performance. Consequently, it is imperative to allocate significant attention toward optimizing employee performance. This study aims to examine the influence of Work Discipline and Employee Loyalty on the performance of employees at the PT. Columbindo Perdana Branch Office in Manado. Work Discipline is defined as a psychological attitude manifested through the behaviors of individuals, groups, or communities, characterized by compliance with established rules and regulations. Employee Loyalty constitutes a key factor in employee evaluation, encompassing commitment to one’s job, position, and the organization as a whole. Employing a descriptive quantitative research design, data analysis was conducted utilizing validity and reliability tests, multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination via SPSS software. The statistical findings reveal that Work Discipline and Employee Loyalty collectively exert a significant effect on Employee Performance at the PT. Columbindo Perdana Branch Office Manado. However, Employee Loyalty alone does not demonstrate a significant partial impact on employee performance. Overall, Work Discipline is observed to be satisfactory and should be maintained, whereas Employee Loyalty warrants further investigation to enable both variables to positively influence Employee Performance.  
Keywords: Discipline, Loyalty, Employee Performance

Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study included structural and staff employees, religious leaders, students, and community members as informants. The results indicate that the public services delivered by the personnel at the Airmadidi Head Office are generally effective, as reflected in the applicants’ service experiences. Notably, there exists a strong commitment among employees and a resolute determination to enhance service quality. Nonetheless, certain services have not fully met expectations due to various challenges and obstacles encountered by employees within the office. The Indonesian banking sector holds a pivotal position in the nation’s economic framework, serving as a fundamental mechanism for financial intermediation. Since 2010, there has been remarkable growth in both the total assets and credit distribution of commercial banks. This expansion aims to broaden the customer base but has concurrently led to increased operational costs necessary to sustain such development. Furthermore, the economic downturn experienced in 2012 adversely impacted credit growth, followed by a rise in non-performing loans starting in 2014. Commercial banks’ profitability, measured by return on assets (ROA), demonstrated an upward trend from 2008 until it began to decline in 2013, with the downward trajectory persisting in subsequent years. This study investigates the determinants of profitability in Indonesian commercial banks over the period from 2010 to 2015. Employing a sample of 71 commercial banks and utilizing panel data regression with fixed effects, the analysis reveals that ROA has experienced a decline since 2013. The findings indicate that elevated operating costs resulting from expansion activities, alongside increasing non-performing loans, have contributed to inefficiencies and the reduction in profitability. Additionally, net interest margin exhibits a positive influence on ROA, whereas the capital-to-total-assets ratio is negatively associated. Conversely, total assets and income diversification appear to have an insignificant effect on profitability.  
Keywords: profitability, commercial banks, return on assets (ROA), efficiency

The present study, titled "The Interrogative Sentence in the Film *Man of Steel* by David S. Goyer," aims to identify and analyze the interrogative sentences employed within the film. Data were gathered by examining the dialogues between characters and subsequently analyzed using the theoretical frameworks proposed by Frank and Aarts. An interrogative sentence is defined as one containing a subject and introduced either by an auxiliary verb or a wh-word. Those interrogative sentences initiated by an auxiliary verb are classified as yes/no questions, while a variant of these, consisting of a statement followed by a question, is termed a question tag. The findings reveal that three distinct forms of interrogative sentences appear in the film: yes/no questions, tag questions, and interrogative-word questions. Yes/no questions elicit responses of affirmation or negation; tag questions involve an appended query at the sentence's end; and interrogative-word questions commence with interrogative terms such as what, who, why, when, where, how, whom, or which. Notably, characters in the film also utilize interrogative sentences lacking question words but marked by rising intonation. In terms of communicative function, interrogative sentences serve both as questions and as requests.

Keywords: Interrogative Sentence, Grammatical Analysis, Film *Man of Steel* by David S. Goyer

ABSTRACT:  
The Organization of Indigenous Peoples functions as a mechanism to aggregate indigenous communities, often complicating the direct involvement of traditional leaders in supporting governmental processes related to development implementation and public guidance, as mandated. According to Law No. 21 of 2001 concerning Special Autonomy for Papua Province, indigenous peoples are entitled to self-governance and self-management of their local affairs. Although traditional chieftaincy is not explicitly regulated by legislation, Article 1, Paragraph 13 of the aforementioned law defines a "Consultative Council of Kampung" (or by any other name) as a collective body comprising various elements within a village, selected and acknowledged by local residents to provide advice and considerations to local government authorities.

This study aims to examine the role of the Moni chief in executing road infrastructure development within the Wandai District, Intan Jaya Regency, Papua Province. Employing a qualitative research methodology, data were collected from ten informants representing diverse stakeholders, including district heads, members of the traditional council, village leaders, chiefs, religious figures, and community members. Interviews were conducted for data collection, and the analytical process utilized Miles and Huberman’s interactive model.

Findings reveal that the Moni chief’s involvement in road infrastructure development manifests in three primary aspects: participation in decision-making, dissemination of information to the community, and facilitation of community engagement and mobilization. Consequently, this study concludes that the Moni chief holds a pivotal role in the developmental initiatives undertaken in Wandai District, Intan Jaya Regency.

In light of these findings, it is recommended that district and village governments consistently engage traditional chiefs in decision-making processes, public information dissemination, and efforts to foster and mobilize community participation during road infrastructure projects in Wandai District.

Keywords: Role of Moni Chief, Road Infrastructure Development

The process of modernization has introduced contemporary values across societies worldwide. These modern values generally promote a hedonistic lifestyle, encouraging communities to adopt fashionable and modern ways of living, often described as the lifestyle of modern society. In Indonesia, clubbing—commonly referred to as "dugem" or the "glitter world"—is characterized by the presence of flashing disco lights and pulsating techno music played by DJs, some of whom come from abroad. Clubbers originate from diverse social strata and encompass a broad age range, from teenagers to the elderly, all actively engaged in the nightlife culture.

Among these clubbers, a significant number identify as college students who perceive themselves as modern and refuse to be considered outdated or ostentatious by failing to keep pace with current trends. Notably, college students in Kota Manado show considerable interest in participating in dugem activities as part of their modern lifestyle. The participation of young women in this nightlife scene is influenced by both internal and external factors. Internally, factors include boredom with routine activities, academic pressures, perceptions of clubbers as slang users, and personal issues. Externally, influences consist of peer or acquaintance solicitation, interests sparked by social media, environmental changes promoting promiscuity, and inadequate supervision by parents or guardians.

Keywords: dugem, lifestyle, clubbers.

The purpose of this study was to determine the type, dimensions and composition of nematocytes in Scleractinia, Acropora florida and Acropora divaricata. This research was conducted in South Motandoi Beach, East Pinolosian District, South Bolaang Mongondow Regency, North Sulawesi for five (5) months; from February to June 2019. The method of this research was observation using student-t statistical data analysis. Microbasic p-Mastigophore type-II (MpM-II) and Holotricous isorhiza (HI), while A. divaricata only has type-II Microbasic p-Mastigophore (MpM-II) nematocytes. The nematocytes dimension showed an average capsule length of MpM II in A. florida of was 262.32 µm and A. divaricata was 125.15 µm, mean capsule width of MPM II in A. florida was 67.01 µm and A. divaricata was 31.95 µm, and the average length of mpM II on A. florida was 154.44 µm, and A. divaricata was 70.97 µm. Nematocytes composition showed that MPM II in A. florida was 95.56% and HI was 4.44%, while the composition of MPM II nematocytes in A. divaricata was 100% and HI was 0%. Student t-test showed that the ratio of 2 average values of capsule length, capsule width, and MPM II stem length from two populations of A. florida and A. divaricata were not significantly different (P> 0.05). It can be concluded that both types of A. florida and A. divaricata corals have different types and composition of nematocytes however their size dimensions are not significantly different. Further studies are important to examine genetic and environmental factors to find out how much the kinship relationship between the two types of those coral.Keywords: Acropora florida, Acropora divaricata, HI, Scleractinia coral, MpM II, nematocytes

Abstract:  
The operational organization of existing employees in the District of Kaimana has demonstrated inefficiencies, as evidenced by delays in administrative services, particularly in data processing within several wards of the district. Additionally, coordination related to community empowerment activities remains suboptimal. In response to these challenges, this study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of clerical duties performed in the District of Kaimana, Regency of Kaimana, West Papua Province. Employing a qualitative descriptive research design, this approach was selected to thoroughly describe the effectiveness of clerks’ performance within the specified region. Informants included individuals who possess relevant knowledge and data necessary to provide comprehensive insights into clerical task implementation. A total of ten participants were interviewed for this study. Findings indicate that the effectiveness of employee performance in the District of Kaimana has not yet been fully realized, as reflected in aspects such as productivity, efficient resource utilization, job satisfaction, adaptability, and professional development.  

Keywords: effectiveness, performance, employee

One of the diseases that often affects the production rate of cabbage is clubroot disease caused by the fungus Plasmodiophora brassicae Wor. This study aims to determine the effect of the application of Trichoderma sp. and PGPR in controlling clubroot disease in cabbage. The research was carried out from August to November at the Laboratory of Biological Agency for the Protection of Food Crops and Horticulture in Kalasey and in Kakaskasen Village, North Tomohon District, Tomohon City. The study was conducted using a randomized block design (RAK) with 4 treatments and 4 replications, namely Treatment A = Trichoderma sp. (250ml/plant), Treatment B = PGPR (250ml/plant), Treatment C = Trichoderma sp. and PGPR (250ml+250 ml/plant), Treatment K = Control. Based on the results of observations of clubroot disease symptoms on cabbage plants, above the ground the leaves appear pale green to yellowish and wilted during the day and look fresh again in the afternoon. In further attacks the affected cabbage plants become stunted. Typical symptoms of this disease can be seen in the swollen roots of the plant. The results showed that the application of Trichoderma sp. and PGPR effect in controlling clubroot disease in cabbage plants. Data were collected via a questionnaire distributed through Google Forms, and the analysis was conducted using Multiple Linear Regression. The findings reveal that, collectively, brand image (X1) and service quality (X2) exert a significant positive influence on purchase decisions (Y), indicated by a test value of 93.046. Keywords: Brand Image, Service Quality, Purchase Decision, Logistics Service

This study seeks to describe and interpret the efforts involved in empowering human resources to optimize the functions of Village Owned Enterprises (BUMDes). Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, data were gathered through observation, interviews, and document analysis. The research included five informants. The empowerment model applied in this study focuses on the strengthening of human resources within the organization of BUMDes.

Findings reveal that the initial stage of the empowerment model, which pertains to the cultivation of desire, is being effectively implemented. Currently, efforts to foster this desire are predominantly undertaken by the village government, specifically Sangadi, directed toward the BUMDes board, as evidenced by activities such as external outreach. However, the subsequent stage—building confidence—has not yet been fully realized. Although the government and the community place considerable trust in individuals appointed explicitly to manage and develop BUMDes, comprehensive trust-building through education and training programs has yet to be systematically extended to all board members.

Moreover, the confidence stage requires further enhancement; while board members demonstrate adequate management capabilities, their engagement in creative and innovative practices concerning BUMDes management and development remains limited. The final stage of the empowerment model, credibility, does not present significant challenges. The board has demonstrated satisfactory performance in ongoing BUMDes activities. Nevertheless, there is a need to strengthen the board’s accountability by ensuring that tasks and responsibilities are completed independently, despite occasional governmental support. Attention must also be given to intra-organizational communication, wherein formal meetings involving the Village Consultative Body (BPD), the government, and the board should be regularly convened to discuss performance reports and agendas related to BUMDes.

Keywords: Empowerment (strengthening), Human Resources, Village Owned Enterprises (BUMDes)

EEFCT OF COFFEE HUSK WASTE PRODUCT TREATED BY SIMPLE PROCESSING SUBSTITUTED WITH PART OF CORN IN RATION ON PERCENTAGE OF BROILER INTERNAL ORGAN. This study was conducted to evaluate the use of coffee husk waste product treated by simple processing substituted with part of corn in ration on percentage of broiler internal organ. Study was applied at Faculty of Animal Science, Sam Ratulangi University during 35 days. Total of 144 day old chick unsexed broilers, strain of CP 707, involving 36 experimental units of battery pens were used in this study. Each unit of pen was filled 4 birds under completely randomized design on factorial patter of 3x4. Factor A was focused on three processing treatments including coffee husk heated under sun light (A1), coffee husk immersed in the water (A2), and coffee husk boiled under water (A3). Factor B was focused on four treatments of substitution levels including ration containing corn without coffee husk substitution (B0), ration containing corn substituted with 25% coffee husk (B1), ration containing corn substituted with 50% coffee husk(B2), ration containing corn substituted with 75% coffee husk (B3). Analysis of variance showed that interaction of processing treatments did not affect significantly on the percentages of lung, heart and gizzard. This study indicated that simple processing of coffee husk were not affected the percentages of broiler internal organ. The substitution levels significantly affected percentage of internal organ. Percentages of lung, heart and gizzard were 1.38-1.86%, 0.31-0.72% and 1.6-2.77%, respectively. This study showed that utilization of coffee husk waste product by above simple processing could substitute part of corn in ration of 25% producing high percentage of broiler internal organ. Keywords: Broiler, Coffee husk by product, broiler internal organ
