Rice constitutes the second most significant staple food in Jayawijaya Regency, Papua, following sweet potato. The cultivation area dedicated to rice spans approximately 250 hectares, yielding a production volume of 655 tons, according to data from the Department of Agriculture of Food Crops and Horticulture of Papua Province (2014). Jayawijaya Regency encompasses a total area of 13,925.31 km² and is administratively divided into 40 districts, including 4 Kelurahan and 328 villages. The population of the region is approximately 241,280 inhabitants, the majority of whom reside on hillside slopes characterized by difficult accessibility and extended periods of dryness.

This research employs a plant simulation model to estimate monthly evapotranspiration for wetland rice cultivation in Jayawijaya Regency. The use of this simulation model presents several advantages, including reduced time requirements for obtaining results and favorable cost-efficiency. Specifically, the study utilizes the Shierary Rice.Ve2 2, 1 model to perform the estimations. The findings offer practical applications for optimizing rice cultivation, particularly in the domain of water management. The growth model constitutes a simplified yet effective mathematical representation of plant growth dynamics, which is statistically analyzed. One primary benefit of employing such model simulations is the capability to expedite predictions regarding crop production potential.

Keywords: Evapotranspiration estimation, simulation model, rice cultivation, Jayawijaya Regency, water management

This study aimed to examine the supervisory functions performed by junior high school supervisors under the Ciamis District Education Office during the COVID-19 pandemic. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, the investigation utilized both primary and secondary data sources. Data collection methods included observation, interviews, and documentation, with the gathered information subsequently analyzed to draw conclusions pertinent to the research objectives. The findings reveal that the execution of supervisory functions by junior high school supervisors in the Ciamis Regency Education Office throughout the pandemic was suboptimal and lacked full effectiveness across four key dimensions. Specifically, the quality and implementation of the supervision program, the creativity and innovation demonstrated in developing supervisory and disciplinary activities, the reporting on program execution, as well as the supervisors’ commitment, problem sensitivity, and problem-solving abilities were deemed insufficient in practical application. Consequently, it is recommended that school supervisors enhance their human resource capabilities, improve the quality of supervision programs, and strengthen their dedication to supervisory duties to ensure effective supervision and thereby promote the attainment of high-quality school outcomes. 

Keywords: Supervisory Function, Supervisory Personnel, COVID-19

This study aims to examine the extent to which employee competence influences employee performance in the North Kawangkoan Subdistrict, utilizing five competency indicators. The research focuses on the impact of competence on employee performance within this subdistrict, which is responsible for executing and coordinating the implementation of local government affairs through various regional apparatuses. To address the primary research problem, the researcher employed a descriptive analytical approach alongside simple linear regression analysis, with data collected quantitatively. The primary data were obtained directly from the research site via questionnaires distributed to respondents relevant to the study. Additionally, secondary data were gathered through a review of literature, articles, scientific papers, and other pertinent analytical materials.

The findings indicate that competence accounts for 37.21% of the variance in employee performance within North Kawangkoan Subdistrict, while the remaining 62.79% of the variation is attributable to factors outside the scope of the regression model. Collectively, the dimensions of knowledge, skills, self-concept and values, personal characteristics, and motivation exert an influence on employee performance. Among these, self-concept and values demonstrate the most significant individual impact, whereas motivation does not show a statistically significant effect on employee performance in the subdistrict.

Keywords: Competence, Employee Performance

This study investigates the interactions between papaya varieties and watering regimes on the population dynamics of the papaya mealybug (Paracoccus marginatus) in Bangkok and local papaya plants. The research was conducted using a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with treatments involving two papaya varieties—Bangkok and local—and three watering intervals. The parameters evaluated included the populations of nymphs and adults (imago), as well as the infestation rate of P. marginatus on different plant parts: the trunk, upper leaves, middle leaves, and lower leaves. Findings revealed that the highest nymph population occurred on the upper leaves of locally grown papayas watered daily, averaging 71.85 individuals per leaf, while the lowest nymph density was observed on the underside of leaves of Bangkok variety papayas watered every three days, with 1.85 individuals per leaf. Regarding adult populations, the greatest density was recorded on the middle leaves of locally grown papayas subject to daily watering (27.85 individuals per leaf), whereas the lowest was found on the lower leaves of Bangkok papayas watered every three days (1.71 individuals per leaf). The attack rates of the mealybug were highest in the local papaya variety subjected to daily watering (90.89%), followed sequentially by local papayas watered every two days (70.35%), Bangkok papayas watered daily (67.92%), local papayas watered every three days (57.32%), Bangkok papayas watered every two days (42.72%), and Bangkok papayas watered every three days (40.04%).  
 
**Keywords:** Paracoccus marginatus, mealybug, papaya, population dynamics, watering regimes

The present study aims to elucidate the daily behavioral patterns of the Timor deer (Cervus timorensis) within the Tandurusa Wildlife Sanctuary located in Aertembaga, Bitung City, North Sulawesi Province. The findings are intended to serve as a valuable resource for both local communities and relevant agencies by enhancing understanding of the species' behavior to support captive breeding initiatives. Employing an observational methodology, the research involved direct field observations utilizing the Instantaneous Sampling technique. Data collection was conducted over 14 sessions, with daily activities recorded at one-minute intervals. Results indicated that feeding behavior accounted for 17.01% of the Timor deer's daily activities, corresponding to 32.86 minutes in the morning, 37.86 minutes at midday, and 51.79 minutes in the afternoon. Resting behavior predominated, constituting 57.52% of total observed activity time, distributed as 143.57 minutes in the morning, 141.92 minutes at midday, and 128.64 minutes in the afternoon. Social interactions comprised 18.31% of daily activity, with 46.78 minutes occurring in the morning, 44.5 minutes at midday, and 40.57 minutes in the afternoon. Locomotion accounted for 7.15% of the total activity duration, with 16.78 minutes in the morning, 15.71 minutes at midday, and 19 minutes during the afternoon period. These observations provide comprehensive insight into the temporal allocation of activities by Cervus timorensis within the sanctuary setting.

Keywords: Daily activity, Timor deer, Tandurusa Wildlife Sanctuary, North Sulawesi

Recent economic developments in Indonesia have intensified the demand for accounting practices capable of providing the financial information necessary for effective economic decision-making by society. This necessity is increasingly acknowledged by entrepreneurs, as accounting significantly facilitates the efficiency of management activities. This study was conducted on 30 travel agency service companies located in Manado City. The primary objective was to investigate the effects of accounting proficiency and entrepreneurial innovation on managerial performance within these travel agencies. Multiple linear regression analysis, utilizing SPSS version 12.0 software, was employed as the analytical method. The findings indicate that both accounting proficiency (X1) and entrepreneurial innovation (X2) individually exert a significant influence on managerial performance (Y) in travel service companies in Manado. Furthermore, the combined effect of accounting proficiency and entrepreneurial innovation variables significantly impacts managerial performance. Consequently, the alternative hypothesis (Ha) is accepted, and the null hypothesis (H0) is rejected, demonstrating that accounting proficiency and entrepreneurial innovation significantly affect managerial performance in travel service companies in Manado City.  

Keywords: Accounting, Innovation, Entrepreneurship, Managerial Performance

This study, entitled "The Traditional Symbols of Marriage in Buru and Ireland: A Semiotic Analysis," aims to identify, categorize, analyze, and interpret the various traditional symbols associated with marriage in both Buru and Ireland. Additionally, the research seeks to elucidate the similarities and differences in marital symbols between these two cultures. Employing a descriptive research methodology, data regarding Buru's marriage symbols were collected through interviews with four native informants to clarify unfamiliar concepts. Conversely, information on Irish marriage symbols was derived from a variety of scholarly articles. The analysis was grounded in Peirce’s semiotic theory, while Lado’s framework was utilized to contrast the cultural elements and discern points of convergence and divergence. The findings reveal that Buru’s marriage customs feature six principal symbols: the areca nut signifying agreement; spear and machete representing the marriage proposal; dowry presented to the bride’s parents; symbolic markers denoting the daughter and son-in-law as husband and wife; dowry extended to the bride’s entire family; and the gong. In contrast, Irish marriage traditions encompass nine key symbols: the Claddagh ring embodying love, loyalty, and friendship; bouquet symbolizing fertility; blue wedding dress associated with luck; wedding cake as a fertility emblem; honeymoon representing the newlyweds; magic hanky linked to fertility; makeup bells serving as reminders of wedding vows and harmony restoration; the lucky horseshoe symbolizing fortune; and braided hair reflecting feminine power and luck. Commonalities between the two cultures include symbols related to the marriage proposal, wedding ring, and the giving of coins, all sharing analogous meanings. Divergences are evident in that Irish traditions include symbols such as the wedding dress, wedding cake, honeymoon, bouquet, makeup bells, lucky horseshoe, magic hanky, and braided hair, which are not present in Buru. Conversely, Buru’s traditional symbols—such as the areca nut, spear, machete, dowry, and gong—are absent from Irish cultural practices. 

Keywords: Symbols, Marriage, Buru, Ireland, Semiotic Analysis

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Ministry’s academic services as provided by officers and honorary employees at the Academic Headquarters of Sam Ratulangi University (Unsrat). In accordance with Government Regulation No. 49 of 2013 concerning higher education, Article 11 stipulates that academic units are responsible for delivering education, research, and community service. This regulatory framework underscores the critical role of the academic section at Unsrat University.

The research employed a qualitative and descriptive methodology, utilizing observation and questionnaires to collect data. The sample comprised 20 informants, including five officers, five honorary employees, and ten students. 

Findings reveal that 50% of the student respondents expressed dissatisfaction with the service provided by the academic officers at Unsrat. This discontent stemmed primarily from perceptions of unfriendliness and inadequate information delivery by the staff. Furthermore, 50% of the students reported difficulties and dissatisfaction with the online tuition fee payment system, primarily due to frequent internet disruptions which adversely affect the payment process. Additionally, students voiced concerns regarding the closure of online graduation registration two weeks prior to the ceremony, as internet connectivity issues often result in delayed graduation clearance.

Based on these findings, it is recommended that staff enhance their service provision by adopting a more student-friendly approach, recognizing students as the primary stakeholders of the university. Accurate and timely information should be communicated effectively, with academic leadership, particularly the Provost of Academics, taking a proactive role in overseeing service delivery and disseminating current information pertaining to academic services. Moreover, to mitigate the impact of internet disruptions, it is suggested that alternative manual service options be made available for processes such as fee registration and graduation, thereby minimizing inconvenience to students.

Keywords: Service, Effectiveness

This study aims to evaluate the added value and benefits associated with the processing of soybeans into tempeh and tofu. The research was carried out over a three-month period from September to November 2019 at Pak Sutikno's Tempeh and Tofu Industry, located in the Batukota Bawah Sub-District, Malalayang Sub-District, Manado City. Primary data were collected through interviews with the business owner. The analytical approach focused on assessing added value and profitability derived from the processing activities.

The findings indicate that Pak Sutikno's tempeh production yields an added value of IDR 21,676,533 per month, with an added value of IDR 722.55 per production cycle and IDR 9,032 per kilogram of raw soybeans. In comparison, the added value from soybean processing into tofu amounts to IDR 101,399,733 monthly, IDR 3,379,991 per production cycle, and IDR 12,426 per kilogram of raw material. Profitability analysis reveals that tempeh production generates a profit of IDR 160,885 per production cycle and IDR 4,826,550 per month, whereas tofu production yields a profit of IDR 2,818,325 per production cycle and IDR 84,549,750 monthly.

Keywords: added value, profit, soybean, tofu, tempeh

Regional Original Revenue (PAD) constitutes revenue generated from local taxes, regional levies, the management of autonomous regional assets, and other lawful regional income sources. Such regional levies serve as a critical funding mechanism for regional development and the facilitation of regional autonomy. Among the various types of regional levies implemented by the Tomohon City Government is the waste collection fee. This study aims to examine both the effectiveness of waste collection fees in Tomohon City and the extent to which solid waste levies contribute to PAD. Employing a quantitative descriptive methodology, the study utilizes contribution and effectiveness analyses. Findings indicate that the effectiveness of solid waste levy receipts during 2015-2016 was suboptimal and exhibited a declining trend; however, in 2017, despite remaining ineffective, there was a marked and substantial increase. Similarly, the contribution of solid waste levies to regional levies was relatively minor in 2015 and 2016 but became considerably more significant in 2017. In contrast, the contribution of solid waste levies to Tomohon City’s PAD from 2015 to 2017 remained minimal throughout the three-year period. It is recommended that the leadership of the Regional Revenue Service and the Environmental Agency intensify and expand efforts to optimize the collection of solid waste fees, thereby fostering continuous improvement in the regional levy collection system. 

Keywords: effectiveness, contribution, local government revenue

The facial nerve, recognized as the seventh cranial nerve, innervates four primary components: tactile sensation of portions of the external ear, taste sensation in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, muscles responsible for facial expression, and the salivary and lacrimal glands. Peripheral facial nerve palsy (FNP) arises from diverse etiologies, with Bell’s palsy being the most prevalent. Secondary causes encompass local trauma to the facial nerve, neoplasms, postoperative complications, and reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus in the geniculate ganglion, as observed in Ramsay Hunt’s syndrome. 

Salivary gland tumors account for approximately 3–10% of all head and neck neoplasms and predominantly affect the major salivary glands, with the parotid gland being the most frequently involved site, exhibiting a prevalence range of 36.6 to 83%. Malignant neoplasms constitute a smaller proportion, representing 15–32% of cases. Impairment of facial nerve function may manifest as either complete paralysis or partial paresis, resulting from injury to the main nerve trunk or individual branches.

The initial description of a parotidectomy procedure with preservation of the facial nerve was reported by Johann Ferdinand Heyfelder in 1825. Treatment strategies for peripheral facial palsy should be tailored to optimize the restoration of nerve function, taking into consideration the underlying cause and the severity of the condition. In this context, the post-parotidectomy facial nerve grading system (PPFNGS) has been developed by integrating elements from three prior grading systems. This novel scale evaluates the functional status of the four branches of the facial nerve following parotidectomy. Various therapeutic modalities, including physical exercise, electrical stimulation, biofeedback, and motor re-education, have been documented as interventions for patients experiencing facial paresis.

Crack control plays a crusial role in the performance life of concrete structures. It present a serious treat to the performance of concrete structures. Micro-cracking will appear when the strength of concrete is approached. Each of micro-crack occured inside concrete will produce a transient elastic wave which could be used to detect and localize cracks as well as to analize kinematically the fracture mechanisms in concrete. In this scientific paper, the SiGMA analysis is applied to the split-tensile tests of FRC to study the relation between the generation of macro-scale tensile crack and accumulation of meso-scale cracks as well as to know the role of the applied fiber on the cracking process of concrete. Results showed that the relation between macro-scale tensile failure and nucleation of AE sources in meso-scale is clarified in Split-tensile test. At the macro-scale, tensile-type cracks are only observed, while all kinds of tensile, mixed-mode and shear cracks are identified at the meso-scale. During propagation of tensile cracks at the macro-scale, other types of AE sources of mixed-mode and shear cracks were actively identified. Thus, nucleation of the fracture process zone is confirmed around the final failure surface.Mechanisms of macro-scale tensile failure process in concrete are clarified as the crack accumulation process at meso-scale determined by the SiGMA analysis. This study aimed to examine the implementation of the Regional Management Information System (SIMDA) and its impact on the quality of financial reporting within the Agency of Revenue, Finance, and Asset Management (DPPKAD) of Southeast Minahasa Regency. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews and document analysis using a cross-sectional approach. Interviews were conducted with the Southeast Minahasa District Secretary regarding the implementation of SIMDA, alongside surveys administered to five respondents within DPPKAD and 30 treasurers in various SKPD units concerning the preparation of financial statements. The findings indicate that the utilization of SIMDA aligns with the provisions stipulated in Ministerial Regulation No. 13 of 2006 concerning Regional Financial Management Guidelines. Although participation from SKPD units remains relatively low, user engagement by category has been satisfactory. The data further demonstrate a positive correlation between the opinions of the Supreme Audit Board (BPK) and the increased adoption of SIMDA across the SKPD units. In addition to SIMDA, several factors were identified as influencing the quality of financial statements, including human resource capacity, the role of the inspectorate, leadership from regional authorities, responses to BPK recommendations, and consistency in SIMDA application. Evaluation of human resources revealed classifications based on SIMDA-related educational background and the frequency of technical training (Bimtek). While the inspectorate’s personnel were assessed as highly competent, their numbers were insufficient to adequately support all SKPD units. Regional leadership performance was evaluated as satisfactory, feedback on BPK recommendations was deemed adequate, and consistent application of SIMDA was observed to be favorable.

South Minahasa district is geographically situated between 1°17'18.22" north latitude and 124°54'48.84" east longitude, encompassing a total area of 1,188.67 km², which constitutes approximately 8% of North Sulawesi’s total land area of 15,069.00 km². The district is characterized by coastal regions to the north and south, as well as highland plains, where irrigated rice fields yield substantial harvests. The region’s natural environment and climatic conditions are conducive to agriculture, enabling the cultivation of diverse crops across nearly all sub-districts. Predominantly, rice cultivation relies on irrigation systems, although rainfed methods are also practiced. Typically, planting occurs two to three times per year, often integrating crop rotation with other food crops. The agricultural produce cultivated by local farmers includes rice, maize, potatoes, and various other horticultural crops. Besides rice, maize and cassava are produced in considerable quantities within South Minahasa. Consequently, farmers engaged in food crop production have access to a variety of crop options suitable for their agricultural land.  

This research was conducted from August to September 2016 in the South Minahasa regency. Data collection was performed through survey techniques, and linear programming facilitated by the Solver application in Microsoft Excel was employed for data analysis. The findings indicate that, with an increase of two laborers per farming family and the adoption of mechanical harvesting, annual farmer income could rise markedly. Specifically, income for the Musafir 4 farmer groups increased from approximately Rp 720 million to Rp 1.84 billion, corresponding to a cropping pattern involving 15 hectares of rice and 10 hectares of maize. Similarly, the Torout Jaya farmer groups experienced an increase in annual income from Rp 582 million to Rp 2.3241 billion, associated with a cropping pattern of 17 hectares of rice and 20 hectares of soybeans.  

Keywords: Agricultural Optimization, Linear Programming, Solver Application

This study seeks to examine the function of the categorical or economic base sectors and to evaluate the efficiency of investment accumulation within North Minahasa Regency. The research was geographically focused on North Minahasa Regency, located in North Sulawesi Province, and was conducted over the period from April to October 2018. Secondary data utilized in the analysis include the Regional Gross Domestic Product (RGDP) at constant prices for both North Minahasa Regency and North Sulawesi Province, as well as data on changes in Regional Gross Fixed Capital in North Minahasa Regency. Analytical tools applied in this study comprise the Location Quotient (LQ), Shift Share Analysis, and the Incremental Capital Output Ratio (ICOR).

Findings derived from the LQ analysis indicate that the sectors of agriculture, forestry, and fishery; mining and excavation; manufacturing; construction; electricity and gas; real estate; and education services constitute the base categories in North Minahasa Regency, each exhibiting an LQ value exceeding 1. These base sectors have played a positive role in contributing to the formation of the RGDP in North Minahasa Regency, with agriculture, forestry, and fishery identified as the most significant contributors during the period from 2013 to 2017. Moreover, the contribution of these base sectors, as reflected through regional share analysis, also manifests positively at the provincial level, suggesting that the economic base of North Minahasa Regency substantially supports the RGDP formation of North Sulawesi Province.

The proportional shift analysis revealed that certain base sectors in North Minahasa Regency—specifically agriculture, forestry and fishery, manufacturing, and education services—experienced negative values. Furthermore, differential shift analysis demonstrated that electricity and gas was the sole sector exhibiting a negative differential shift, indicating its inability to compete effectively with analogous sectors at the provincial level. Additionally, the ICOR, calculated using standard methods with lag0, lag1, and mean approaches for the period 2013–2017, indicated inefficiency in capital investment within North Minahasa Regency.

This study, entitled "Profanity in the Movie 21 Jump Street," aims to identify and categorize the types of profanity present in the film, as well as to examine the various expressions conveyed through the use of profane language. The theoretical framework for this analysis is based on the works of Jay (1992) and Staley (1978). Employing a descriptive research methodology, the investigation was conducted in three stages. Initially, the entire movie was viewed to gather relevant data. Subsequently, during the data collection phase, the profane terms were extracted and cross-referenced with the original script for accuracy. Finally, in the analysis stage, the identified profanities were classified according to Jay’s typology, and the contextual expressions were interpreted following Staley’s theoretical approach. The findings reveal the presence of 31 distinct types of profanity out of a total of 42 instances, alongside 19 different expressions emerging from contextual dialogue situations. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that profanity functions not solely as a marker of fear or embarrassment but also serves purposes such as expressing intimacy, offering compliments, and other varied communicative intentions. These results substantiate the applicability of Jay’s and Staley’s theories regarding the use of profanity in cinematic discourse.  

Keywords: Profanity, Types of profanity, Expressions, 21 Jump Street, Jay, Staley

PRODUCTION ANALYSIS OF FOOD CROP WASTE PRODUCT AS CATTLE FEED IN NORTH BOLAANGMONGONDOW REGENCY. Cattle can be used as the main economical source giving added value in farm of the farmers to support their family needs in North Bolaang Mongondow regency. Farmers utilized food crop waste product for cattle feed maintenance. The problem was that the food crop waste product potential was unknown to support cattle development in the farm of the farmers. The objective of this study was to analyze food crop waste product potential. Materials in this study were involving food crop area, type of food crop waste product, and cattle. Research method was applied by survey method involving primer and secondary data. Data were analyzed by proximate analysis conducted by Research Institution and Industrial Standardization, Manado and descriptive analysis. Agricultural waste product was local feedstuff as crude fiber source that can be used for cattle feed. The potential feedstuff was calculated on the basis of feedstuff production multiplied by crop cultivation area size and expressed in dry matter (DM). The highest potential of DM was the wet rice paddy straw, followed by dry rice paddy straw, corn straw, sweet potato leaves, cassava leaves, green bean straw, and peanut straw. This study concluded that dry matter productions of wet rice paddy straw, corn straw and peanut straw were highly produced in Sanggkub district. Background: Attitudes and actions of doctors, nurses, administration as well as inaction in services, drug supplies, inadequate infrastructure and medical equipment are still problems that become complaints by service users. Hospitals must have the ability to attract and retain customers who do not only come from the product or service itself. The purpose of this study was to analyze the factors related to customer loyalty in the outpatient installation of the UPTD Hospital Type C Manembo-nembo Bitung. Methods: This research is an observational study with a cross sectional study design. A total of 100 outpatients who have received health services at the UPTD Outpatient Installation of Type C Hospital, Manembo-nembo Bitung participated in this study. Data were analyzed using univariate, bivariate and multivariate and logistic regression statistical calculations. Presentation of data is made in table and narrative form. Results: The results showed that a significant relationship between products and customer loyalty with a value of p = 0.024, between processes and customer loyalty with a value of p = 0.000, between location and customer loyalty with a value of p = 0.061, between promotion and loyalty with a value of p = 0.435 , between employees with loyalty with a value of p = 0.000, between physical evidence and loyalty with a value of p = 0.005. However, there is no promotion relationship with loyalty. The results of the mutivariate analysis showed that the product factor was the most dominant factor influencing the loyalty of outpatients at Manembo-nembo Hospital Type C Bitung.Conclusion: This research can be conclude that the process factors are the most dominant factors related to customer loyalty in the Outpatient Polyclinic of the UPTD Type C Hospital, Manembo-nembo, Bitung.

This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of leaf and fruit extracts of *Excoecaria agallocha* in inducing mortality in the larvae of *Cropera pavonana* and to identify the optimal concentration and dosage of these extracts for effective pest management of *C. pavonana*. The research was conducted through several stages: (1) exploration and collection of plant material for extraction; (2) preparation of host plant feed; (3) acquisition of test larvae; (4) extraction of bioactive compounds from the plant material; and (5) application of the extracts to the larvae. Field sampling of test insects and maintenance of feed were carried out in the Plantation area of Rurukan Village, East Tomohon Subdistrict, Tomohon City. Extraction procedures and application assays were performed at the Microbiology and Plant Pathology Laboratory, Department of Plant Pests and Diseases, Tomohon, while initial plant material exploration was conducted in Rerer Village, Kombi Subdistrict, Minahasa District. Results demonstrated that both leaf and fruit extracts of *E. agallocha* effectively caused mortality in *C. pavonana* larvae, which exhibited a color change from pale yellow to brown and eventually black following treatment. The study confirms the potential of *E. agallocha* leaf and fruit extracts as botanical insecticides against *C. pavonana* larvae, with a concentration of 0.04% showing optimal efficacy for both leaf and fruit extract treatments.  

Keywords: *Excoecaria agallocha* extract, *Cropera pavonana* pest, white mustard plants

This research seeks to examine the determinants affecting tomato demand in Maesaan District, located within South Minahasa Regency. The investigation was conducted over a three-month period, spanning from June to August, within the specified district. The study utilized both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with tomato consumers present in the market. In contrast, secondary data were gathered from relevant institutional records and prior scholarly publications. The sampling technique employed was convenience sampling, through which data were obtained from a population subset comprising 30 tomato consumers. The variables under consideration included tomato price, consumer income level, prices of complementary goods, and household size. To assess the influence of these variables on tomato demand, a multiple linear regression analysis was utilized. The findings indicate that both tomato price and income levels exert a significant impact on demand, whereas the price of complementary goods and the number of family members do not significantly influence tomato demand within Maesaan District.

This research investigates the effects of incorporating 2% turmeric (Curcuma domestica Val.), ginger (Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb.), and white ginger (Curcuma zedoaria Rosc.) rhizomes into commercial feed on the quality of quail eggs. The study utilized 120 female Coturnix coturnix japonica quails, aged six weeks. A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed, consisting of four treatment groups with five replications each, and six birds per replication. The treatments were as follows: R0 (control diet), R1 (diet supplemented with 2% turmeric), R2 (diet supplemented with 2% ginger), and R3 (diet supplemented with 2% white ginger). The results indicated that supplementation with 2% turmeric, ginger, or white ginger did not produce a statistically significant impact on egg weight, yolk color, or eggshell thickness. Consequently, it is concluded that the addition of 2% turmeric, ginger, or white ginger to commercial feed does not enhance these specific parameters of quail egg quality.

**Keywords:** feed, turmeric, ginger, white ginger, quail eggs

ABSTRACT POTENTIAL ANALYSIS OF NATURE RESOURCES, LABORS, AGRICULTURE AND PLANTATION ON BEEF DEVELOPMENT AT ERIS DICTRICT, MINAHASA REGENCY. Beef population at Eris district of Minahasa regency was decreasing. On the other hand, the areas of Eris district have the potential support in terms of nature resource availability, local labors, agriculture and plantation. The problems were that those supporting factors for beef development had not been evaluated at each village at Eris district. The objective of this study was to identify supporting factors for beef development and to define basis village at Eris district for beef farm development. Survey method was applied for data collection. Results showed that Eris district had productive labor resources with the average age of 44 years old, although the average education level of elementary school. Big geographical potential aspects of agriculture and plantation around Eris district were low land and mountain land. The calculation of Location Quation (LQ) found five villages for beef development having LQ of more than 1.0, including Telap village (2.545), Tandengan I village (1.636), Maumbi village (1.512), Watumea village (1.091), and Eris village (1.091). Three villages at Eris district had no potency for beef development with LQ values of less than 1.0, including Tandengan village (0.364), Ranomerut village (0.909), and Toliang Oki village (0.182). Therefore, it can be concluded that Eris district had potency for beef development supported by the availabilities of nature resources, labor (household farmers) and agriculture as well as plantation areas spreading on five basis villages of Telap village, Tandengan I village, Maumbi village, Watumea village, and Eris village. Key words: Nature resource, Labor resource, Agriculture, Plantation, LQ, Eris Minahasa.

This study aims to evaluate the soil fertility of land designated for the cultivation of Hebras (Gerbera jamesonii) decorative plants in Lansot District, South Tomohon, to support the local government's initiatives promoting Tomohon as a City of Tourism and a City of Flowers. The investigation focused on both soil physical properties, including texture and permeability, and soil chemical characteristics, specifically pH, organic matter, nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K). Conducted from September to November 2019, the research involved the collection of soil samples from Lansot District, followed by laboratory analysis at the Soil Science Laboratory, Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. Employing a survey methodology based on land use maps, data were analyzed descriptively. Findings indicate that the soil in Lansot District primarily exhibits a silt loam texture with moderate permeability. The soil pH was found to be slightly acidic, ranging from 6.19 to 6.35. Organic matter content varied between low and high levels, while nitrogen content was moderate. Phosphorus and potassium were present at sufficient levels. In conclusion, the soil fertility conditions in Lansot District are deemed suitable for the successful cultivation of Hebras (Gerbera jamesonii) as a decorative plant, owing to the adequate availability of essential nutrients. This development is expected to further bolster Tomohon's governmental objectives to enhance its status as a prominent City of Tourism and City of Flowers.

Keywords: Soil Physical Properties, Soil Chemical Properties, Hebras Plant (Gerbera jamesonii)

In the English language, verbs are classified into two main categories: lexical verbs and auxiliary verbs. Auxiliary verbs serve as helping verbs that function grammatically to form or modify the meaning of a verb phrase. This study aims to examine and analyze the auxiliary verbs present in Ed Sheeran’s albums Divide and No.6 Collaborations Project. The primary objective is to identify and analyze both the forms and meanings of auxiliary verbs utilized within these albums. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study collects data by extracting auxiliary verbs from the lyrical content of the aforementioned albums. The analysis is guided by the theoretical framework established by Quirk and Greenbaum. The findings reveal that auxiliary verbs in these two albums fall into two categories: primary auxiliary verbs (am, is, are, was, were) and modal auxiliary verbs (can, could, may, might, will, would, should). Notably, certain auxiliary verbs such as must, shall, used to, need, be supposed to, and dare do not appear in the selected albums. Regarding semantic interpretation, primary auxiliary verbs typically do not bear inherent meaning and their interpretation depends on the context. Modal verbs express various nuanced meanings; for instance, "can" denotes ability, while its negative form indicates inability, and "could" carries similar connotations. The modal "will" conveys notions of willingness, hypothetical situations, promises, and agreements, whereas "would" suggests willingness, and "should" implies obligation.

Keywords: Auxiliary verbs, Divide, No.6 Collaborations Project, Ed Sheeran, albums

The objective of this study was to examine the implementation of advertisement tax policy within the Tax and Retribution Management Body in Minahasa Regency. This research employed a qualitative methodology, involving five informants: the head of the agency, the head of the data collection field, an executor, and an advertisement taxpayer. Data were gathered through interviews and observational guidelines. The analytical process utilized the interactive analysis model developed by Miles and Huberman. 

Findings from the data analysis indicate that the implementation of advertisement tax policy, when viewed through the lenses of idealized policy, target groups, implementing organization, and environmental factors, was suboptimal within the Tax and Retribution Management Body of Minahasa Regency. 

Based on these conclusions, the study recommends the following measures: (1) enhancement of the "idealized policy" dimension by establishing more effective communication with advertisement tax subjects and improving coordination with relevant stakeholders; (2) strengthening the "target groups" dimension through more proactive efforts aimed at raising tax compliance awareness among taxpayers; (3) optimization of the "implementing organization" dimension by improving the performance of units responsible for managing advertisement tax functions; (4) advancement of the "environmental factors" dimension by fostering social and cultural conditions that are more conducive to policy implementation. 

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Advertisement Tax

This study seeks to assess the infestation of the pest Cnaphalocrosis medinalis in rice crops during the vegetative phase within the Ranoyapo districts of South Minahasa Regency. Employing a survey methodology, research was conducted across four villages in the Ranoyapo district: Ranoyapo Village, West Poopo Village, North Poopo Village, and Mopolo Village. In each village, three distinct rice fields were selected as replicates for observation and sampling purposes. Sampling was carried out along the diagonals of these fields, with five sampling sites chosen per sub-plot clump of rice plants. Data collection occurred weekly over a six-week period during the vegetative phase. The findings revealed that C. medinalis is widespread throughout the district, with the highest infestation rate observed in Ranoyapo Village at 18.66%, followed by West Poopo at 8.07%, North Poopo at 4.29%, and Mopolo at 4.07%. The greatest percentage of infestation was recorded in rice plants aged six weeks after planting (WAP), reaching 20.66%, with progressively lower percentages found in five-week-old plants (13.55%), four-week-old plants (10.88%), and three-week-old plants (7.55%), whereas plants at one and two weeks after planting exhibited no signs of infestation. Furthermore, the highest population density of C. medinalis was recorded in Ranoyapo Village, averaging 12.7 individuals per sample, followed by West Poopo Village with 4.3, North Poopo Village with 3.5, and Mopolo Village with 3.2 individuals. 

Keywords: Cnaphalocrosis medinalis, rice fields, pest infestation, vegetative phase

Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is the causative agent of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), a condition characterized by damage to lymphocytes and white blood cells, leading to a compromised immune system. According to cumulative data reported by the National AIDS Commission (KPA) of North Sulawesi Province for the period January to December 2011, there were 1,928 documented cases of HIV/AIDS in North Sulawesi. This study aimed to examine the demographic and clinical characteristics of individuals with HIV/AIDS attending Voluntary Counseling and Testing (VCT) clinics at hospitals in Manado city, as well as to evaluate the therapeutic management of these patients in accordance with the 2007 National Guidelines for Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) in Adults and Adolescents issued by the Ministry of Health.

A descriptive survey design with retrospective data collection was employed over a three-month period from June to August 2012 at a specialized VCT clinic in Manado. A total of 71 medical records of HIV/AIDS patients receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) were analyzed using descriptive statistical methods. The findings revealed four distinct ART regimens: 32 patients (45.07%) were treated with the mainline regimen (Duv-Nev), 17 patients (23.94%) received Alternative Line I (Duv-Efv), 9 patients (12.67%) were administered Alternative Line II (Stav-Hiv-Nev), and 13 patients (18.30%) followed Alternative Line III (Stav-Hiv-Efv).

Keywords: HIV, AIDS, Voluntary Counseling and Testing clinics, antiretroviral therapy

Marketing and advertising trends exhibit cyclical patterns, varying across seasons and decades. Historically, advertisements predominantly comprised text-based content. However, advancements in camera technology, printing quality, and the rise of digital marketing have collectively facilitated a transition toward visually oriented advertising mediums. An analysis of leading companies in the United States reveals a discernible movement towards simpler, often minimalist, design strategies. Objectively categorizing designs along a spectrum of simplicity to complexity necessitates the consideration of multiple factors. Employing visual content analysis, this study investigated the evolution of logos from twenty prominent U.S. companies through four distinct design iterations. By comparing logo design trends over time, the research assessed simplicity as influenced by a range of design variables, including textual components integrated within the logos. Owing to the exploratory nature of this inquiry, the study was unable to establish statistically significant correlations between visual design factors and the trend toward simplification. Nonetheless, findings indicated alterations in the textual elements, particularly regarding the number of characters incorporated into logo designs. Although several initial hypotheses were not empirically supported, this study offers a foundational framework that may inform future investigations.  
Keywords: trend, startup, logo, design

The advent of leasing agencies has become particularly appealing to entrepreneurs, as businesses increasingly prefer to utilize cash rupiah funds for their operational activities. Leasing provides a mechanism through which companies can secure financing for the acquisition of capital goods, typically offering repayment terms ranging from three to five years or longer. This study focuses on Astra Credit Companies, recognized as the largest automobile financing firm in Indonesia. The primary objective of this research is to examine the accounting treatment and financial reporting practices related to leasing at Astra Credit Companies in Manado. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study aims to identify the data associated with assets involved in vehicle leasing, analyze the systems for recording and reporting leasing transactions, assess the advantages and disadvantages inherent in the accounting and reporting processes, and ultimately draw informed conclusions. The findings reveal the existence of various types and classifications of leasing, along with criteria for determining the appropriate accounting frameworks. Astra Credit Companies applies the capital lease accounting approach, wherein ownership of the leased asset may be transferred upon the lease’s conclusion. In terms of recording, reporting, and disclosure, the accounting treatment of leasing activities at Astra Credit Companies complies with the relevant standards outlined in Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (SFAS).  

Keywords: consumer finance lease application, PSAK No. 30

The aim of this study is to assess the extent of traders’ involvement in waste management activities at Pinaesaan Market, located in the Tompasobaru District. The investigation was carried out over a period of three months, from February to May 2021. A sample of 42 traders was selected using a simple random sampling technique to serve as respondents. The research relied on both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected through structured interviews with the traders at Pinaesaan Market, employing a pre-designed questionnaire. Secondary data were obtained from the Head of Pinaesaan Market in Tompasobaru District. Data analysis was performed descriptively and results were presented using frequency distribution tables. Findings revealed that, overall, traders’ participation in waste management was categorized as “Medium Participation,” with a total score of 770 out of a maximum possible score of 1260. Among the ten participation indicators examined, two were classified as exhibiting high participation levels, four were identified as low, and the remaining four were within the medium range. Consequently, measures to enhance traders’ awareness and engagement are warranted. Such interventions may be implemented through persuasive strategies, which involve increasing socialization efforts to emphasize the collective importance of waste management, and/or through repressive measures, including the imposition of strict sanctions on non-compliant traders.

ABSTRACT PRODUCTION AND PROTEIN CONTENT OF MAGGOT (HERMETIA ILLUCENS)USING DIFFERENT GROWTH MEDIA. This study aims to analyze the leading sectors in the absorption of labor and to know the contribution of the leading sector in the absorption of labor in south Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted for two months starting from months January to months Ferbruay 2018. The date used in this study is secondary date obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) South Minahasa Regency. The date is processed using location quotient analysis (LQ) and the date is presented in table and described descriptively. Driving forces mean the forces that can give the stimulus to the subject; in this case the stimulus for the student's entrepreneurial intention. Without the right driving forces; student's entrepreneurial intention cannot be achieved in the end and thus students in the future may not consider entrepreneur as one of the alternatives for their careers. The research aims to gain more comprehensive understanding regarding the driving force of entrepreneurship intention among students in IBA. This study uses a qualitative method and using interview as the tool to collect data from informants. The findings of this study show that all of the driving forces which are flexibility, family influence and responsibility, teamwork, financial needs and control act as an important driving force that can affect the entrepreneurial intention of college students. Meaning that by emphasizing these driving forces; it can create a better chance for college students to choose entrepreneurship as a major career choice in the future. Based on the result, the major recommendation is regarding the emphasis of these driving forces within college or other educational institution in order to increase the chance of people choosing entrepreneurs as their career path in the future. Keywords: entrepreneurial intention, financial needs, family influence, flexibility, teamwork, control

ABSTRACT This research is entitled "Compliments in English and Sangirese Language: A Contrastive Analysis." The objectives of this research are to classify, to identify, and to describe the topic of compliments and compliment responses in English and Sangirese language, and to analyze the similarities and the differences of the compliments and compliment responses in both languages. This research uses a descriptive method. The data of compliments and compliment responses in English language were collected from films, novel, and journals, while the data in Sangirese language were collected from the informants of native speaker by doing observation. The data that have been collected then analyze by using the theory of Wolfson in Richard and Schmidt (1986) and the theory of Richard and Schmidt (1986), the writer uses Lado (1957) theory to make a contrastive analysis of both languages in finding out the similarities and differences of compliments and compliment responses in English and Sangirese language. The result shows that the topics of compliment in English consist of personal attribute, possession, pet, children, accomplishment, and change in appearance and the topic of compliments in Sangirese language consists of personal attribute, possession, pet, children, accomplishment, and change in appearance. The compliments responses in English are acceptance, agreement, rejection, shift, and return, and the compliments responses in Sangirese are acceptance, agreement, rejection, shift, and return. The differences of both languages namely the topics of compliment in Sangirese language is found about food, while English language isn't. The responses in Sangirese language about plants, while English language about smile. The adjectival words which are used in English compliments namely beautiful, nice, handsome, increadible, great, cool, awesome, extraordinary, good, amazing, attractive, accomplished, interesting, annoyed, happy, perfect, dear, real, and cute, while in Sangirese namely masadada, mapaele, buhu, lucu, mantape, geguwa, natawa, marange, magurang, pandang, segare, and masedape. The verbal words used in English compliments namely love and like, in Sangirese language namely mapulu. The adjectival used frequently in English are beautiful, great, good, and in Sangirese namely masadada and mapaele.Keywords: Compliments, English and Sangirese Language, Contrastive Analysis.

Following the enactment of Government Regulation No. 41 of 2007 concerning Regional Organizations, the local government of Tomohon has undertaken a reorganization of its regional secretariat. This study aims to assess the effectiveness of the current organizational arrangement of the Tomohon Regional Secretariat. Employing qualitative research methods, data were collected through interviews with key informants, including executive officers and employees of the Tomohon Regional Secretariat, the district secretary, assistant secretaries, two section heads, two subsection heads, and two executive staff members. Data analysis was conducted using the interactive model proposed by Miles and Huberman.

The findings indicate that the organizational structuring of the Tomohon Regional Secretariat has been effective. Specifically, the secretariat is capable of successfully executing its fundamental duties and functions. The effectiveness of the organizational arrangement is evidenced by several criteria: logical structuring, alignment with organizational needs, operational efficiency, optimal functionality, achievement of intended outcomes, prudent and efficient budget utilization, adaptability to task development and expansion, and the capability to address challenges encountered during task implementation.

Based on these conclusions, it is recommended that organizational analyses be conducted periodically and continuously to ensure that the future organizational structure of the Tomohon Regional Secretariat remains effective in fulfilling its legally mandated responsibilities.

Keywords: effectiveness, organizational management

This study was conducted in Manado city in 2017. The population comprised individuals residing in Manado who have consumed and possess experience with the beer brands Bir Bintang, Bali Hai, and Anker. The research sample included approximately 50 consumers who have consumed and are familiar with these three beer brands. Consumer preferences were assessed based on satisfaction levels derived from the consumption of the respective beer brands. The evaluation criteria for the beer brands encompassed price, taste, packaging, advertisement, and peer influence. The findings and subsequent discussion led to two primary conclusions: price is the most influential criterion affecting the selection of beer brands, followed in descending order by taste, peer influence, packaging, and advertisement. Bir Bintang emerged as the most preferred beer brand in Manado, attributed to its strong performance across four criteria—taste, advertising, packaging, and peer influence. Anker ranked second, with Bali Hai occupying the last position. To enhance its market position, Bali Hai should focus on improving taste quality, as a lower price alone does not guarantee consumer selection.  
Keywords: consumer preference, brand selection, beer brand, influential criteria

Background: A survey conducted by the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence and Collaborative for Social Emotional and Academic Learning in 2020 among more than 5000 teachers in the United States showed that teachers experienced work stress in carrying out learning activities and working from home during this pandemic. Various countries in the world, including Indonesia, have taken policies by presenting alternative education processes online and it is very influential not only for students but also for teachers. UNESCO (2020) states that around 63 million teachers around the world must be faced with an educational process that is very different from before this can be done by school closures in around 165 countries and this can trigger work stress on teachers. This study aims to analyze the relationship between workload, role conflict, and social support with work stress among teachers at SMA N 1 Manado during the Covid-19 pandemic. Method: This research was a quantitative analytic survey research using a cross sectional design. The research sample was 76 teachers who were willing to be respondents. The instrument used was the NIOSH Job Stress Questionnaire (1999) in the form of googleform. Univariate analysis was conducted to see the response of each variable under study, the bivariate analysis used the chi-square test to see the relationship between 2 variables and multivariate analysis used logistic regression to see which variables had the most influence on work stress. Results: The results showed that there was a relationship between workload and work stress (p = 0,000), there was a relationship between role conflict and social support (p = 0,000), there was a relationship between social support and workload (p = 0,002). The results of the multivariate test showed that social support (p = 0,007; OR = 25,402) was the most influential variable with work stress on teachers at SMA N 1 Manado. Conclusion: It can be concluded that there is a significant relationship between workload, role conflict, and social support with work stress among teachers at SMA N 1 Manado. The variable that most influences work stress is social support.

This study, entitled "Conjunctions in the Book of Joshua," aims to identify, classify, and analyze the forms, functions, and meanings of conjunctions present in the Book of Joshua from the Bible. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data were collected directly from the text of the Book of Joshua. The analysis was conducted with reference to the theoretical frameworks established by Aarts and Aarts (1982) and Quirk and Greenbaum (1999). The findings reveal various conjunction forms, which include coordinating conjunctions such as and, or, for, and but, as well as subordinating conjunctions including that, if, as, because, until, when, where, after, and before. Functionally, coordinating conjunctions serve to link sentences, phrases, and words, whereas subordinating conjunctions connect sentences, clauses, and phrases. In terms of semantic meaning, coordinating conjunctions convey sequences of ideas, causal relationships between clauses, alternative combinations, sequential implications, unexpected contrasts, and affirmations that counter previous negative statements. Conversely, subordinating conjunctions express reason or purpose, indicate effects of future events, introduce statements or topics, specify reasons, describe ongoing actions, denote times and places of occurrences, and express temporal relations such as anteriority relative to the event described.  

Keywords: Conjunctions, Forms, Functions, Meanings, Book of Joshua

In the context of contemporary global competition, numerous companies have adopted business models that prioritize customers, positioning customer advocacy as a central strategy and source of competitive advantage. However, merely acquiring customers is insufficient; firms increasingly focus on enhancing customer attraction and fostering repurchase intention. Elevated purchase frequency by consumers directly correlates with increased corporate revenue. This study aims to examine the influence of perceived value and brand experience on customers' repurchase intention, as well as to explore the nature and extent of these effects. The theoretical framework underpinning this research includes the constructs of perceived value, brand experience, and repurchase intention. The study population comprised residents of Manado, with a sample size of 60 respondents selected through accidental sampling. The findings indicate that (1) perceived value exerts a more significant impact on repurchase intention than brand experience, and (2) although brand experience affects repurchase intention, this influence is statistically insignificant within the Manado context. The results suggest that perceived value constitutes a critical determinant of customers’ repurchase intentions, as consumers’ decisions to repurchase products largely depend on their evaluation of perceived value. Conversely, brand experience does not significantly influence repurchase behavior; this may be attributed to the widespread global recognition of Coca-Cola, whereby consumers’ repurchase decisions are less dependent on brand experience.  
Keywords: perceived value, brand experience, repurchase intention

Transparency denotes the openness and accessibility of organizational information readily available to stakeholders. This concept has effectively established horizontal accountability among local governments characterized by cleanliness, efficiency, effectiveness, accountability, and responsiveness to community aspirations and interests. Within the context of this study, transparency refers specifically to the community’s access to health services at Mimika Regional Hospital. The central research question addresses how work transparency impacts the quality of health services provided by this institution. Employing quantitative research methods, the study examines two variables: Variable X (Work Transparency) and Variable Y (Quality of Health Services). Work transparency is evaluated through multiple dimensions, including the informative and disclosure aspects. In contrast, the quality of health services is assessed across five dimensions: reliability, assurance, tangibility, empathy, and responsiveness. Both variables were measured using appropriately adapted dimensions and indicators. The findings reveal that work transparency exerts a positive and significant influence on the quality of health services at Mimika Regional Hospital. Consequently, it can be concluded that enhanced transparency contributes to improvements in the quality of health services, particularly within this hospital. In light of these results, it is recommended that Mimika Regional Hospital uphold the principle of work transparency to further elevate the standard of health service quality.  
 
Keywords: Influence, Transparency, Work, Quality of Health Services

In the fashion industry, product attributes serve as critical differentiators and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the perceived importance and performance of Quicksilver’s apparel attributes, focusing on key variables such as brand name, style, retail store, and price. Employing a quantitative methodology, primary data were collected through questionnaires administered to a sample of 100 respondents. Tailings, a form of waste generated by mining operations, exhibit extremely low physical, chemical, and biological fertility, thereby necessitating remediation efforts to improve their quality. One such approach involves the incorporation of organic materials as soil ameliorants to facilitate the rehabilitation of these degraded sites. The present study aims to evaluate the impact of ameliorant application on the growth and yield of sweet corn, identify the optimal dosage for maximizing growth and yield, and assess the presence of residual mercury in the harvested sweet corn. The experimental design employed was a randomized block design comprising six treatment groups: A) 40 tons per hectare of organic fertilizer; B) 50 tons per hectare of organic fertilizer; C) 60 tons per hectare of organic fertilizer; D) 40 tons per hectare of organic+ fertilizer; E) 50 tons per hectare of organic+ fertilizer; and F) 60 tons per hectare of organic+ fertilizer. The organic fertilizer consisted of an equal mixture (50:50) of water hyacinth and chicken manure, whereas the organic+ fertilizer was formulated from five components mixed in equal proportions (20% each): water hyacinth, cow manure, chicken manure, traditional market waste, and rice straw. Each treatment was replicated four times, resulting in a total of 24 experimental units. The measured variables included cob length, cob diameter, and cob weight. Data analysis was performed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test at a 5% significance level. The findings indicate that the organic+ fertilizer significantly enhances sweet corn yield, with the highest dosage of 60 tons per hectare producing the most substantial cobs, averaging 199.89 grams per cob.

This thesis seeks to examine the contribution of local tax revenues to the Original Regional Revenue (Pendapatan Asli Daerah, PAD) managed by the Department of Finance and Asset Management of South Halmahera District over the fiscal years 2010 to 2012. Additionally, it explores the enabling and inhibiting factors influencing the enhancement of local tax revenues within South Halmahera. The findings reveal that local taxes constitute a significant portion of PAD, with their contribution increasing annually and serving as a primary source of district revenue. Specifically, in 2010, local taxes accounted for Rp 1,223,577,233.00, representing 10.51% of the total revenue of Rp 11,735,130,069.82. This share rose to Rp 2,333,993,323.00, or 29.93%, out of a total revenue of Rp 32,296,618,479.35 in 2011, and further increased to Rp 3,368,905,822.00, or 40.59%, of the total revenue of Rp 43,965,874,804.28 in 2012. Factors facilitating the growth in PAD from local taxes include organizational and managerial efficiency, availability of adequate facilities and infrastructure, as well as intensification and extension efforts carried out by the South Halmahera Department of Finance and Asset Management. Conversely, limiting factors comprise low community participation in tax payments, challenges related to data collection and verification processes, and personnel inadequacies, notably reflected in mismatches between educational qualifications and the competencies required for effective local tax administration.  
 
Keywords: Local Taxes, Original Regional Revenue (PAD), South Halmahera, Revenue Management

The motorcycle chain constitutes a critical component of the motor, functioning primarily to transmit power from the engine to the wheels. This study undertook a comprehensive analysis of the mechanical properties and chemical composition of the plates and pins of the Yamaha MX 135 type 428 motorcycle chain, alongside those of other motorcycle chain products. The employed methodology included hardness testing, microstructural examination, and chemical composition analysis of both chain products, the results of which were subsequently compared against relevant standards.

The findings reveal that the hardness values of the chain plates are 44.35 HRC for the Yamaha product and 44.4 HRC for other products, both surpassing the SAE 1050 hardness standard of 30 HRC. Furthermore, the hardness of the Yamaha motorcycle chain pins measured 427 HB, whereas that of other products was 428 HB, each meeting the AISI 15B25 hardness criterion of 131 HB. Correspondingly, the tensile strength values for both the plates and pins of the Yamaha and other motorcycle chains, derived through conversion from hardness measurements, also exceeded the prescribed standards.

Microstructural analysis of the plates and pins from both Yamaha and other products identified the presence of ferrite and pearlite phases, albeit with uneven distribution. Chemical composition testing indicated that the Yamaha motorcycle chain plate complies with the SAE 1050 standard, whereas the chain plate from another product exhibited a carbon content of 1.44%, exceeding the specified standard range of 0.48–0.55%. Regarding the chain pins, the Yamaha product demonstrated a carbon content of 0.4%, while the other product showed 0.43%, both of which surpass the AISI 15B25 standard range of 0.22–0.3%.

In summary, the mechanical and chemical characterization confirms that the Yamaha MX 135 type 428 motorcycle chain and comparable products exhibit superior hardness and tensile strength relative to established standards, though some variations in carbon content warrant further consideration.

Abstract:  
The vision and mission of Bitung City aim to establish it as an international port city excelling in industry, trade, services, and environmentally sustainable tourism within the context of globalization. Central to the city government’s mission is the Panca Bina framework, which includes a focus on Human Development. One key program under this mission is designed to equip the population with qualifications and advanced skills to remain competitive globally, while simultaneously upholding ethical values, morals, and religious norms. Nonetheless, the attention given by the government to the development of Bitung’s tourism industry remains limited. The limited success in tourism growth within Bitung can be largely attributed to the continued reliance on a top-down policy approach, where decision-making authority is concentrated at higher levels, marginalizing input from lower levels of bureaucracy and other stakeholders. This approach tends to overlook valuable strategic initiatives from subordinate administrative levels and excludes public participation across all stages of policymaking—planning, organization, implementation, and supervision.

This study employed qualitative research methods to examine the role of the government in tourism development, with the researcher serving as the principal instrument of data collection. The data were gathered through guided interviews, documentation review, and direct observation, focusing on the Department of Tourism and Culture of Bitung City. The findings indicate that the Department of Tourism plays a critical role in fostering tourism growth, significantly contributing to the economic advancement of Bitung. The department’s influence is evident in its capacity to attract both tourists and investors to the local tourism sector, as well as in its provision of recommendations and monitoring mechanisms for tourism development.

Based on the study, it is recommended that the Bitung City Tourism Office increase efforts to disseminate information to the public regarding the importance of tourism development. Furthermore, the government should adopt more proactive strategies in promoting local attractions not only domestically but also to international audiences to enhance the city’s visibility as a tourist destination. Additionally, it is advisable for the tourism department to strengthen coordination and cooperation with central government agencies to address challenges and remove barriers hindering tourism development.  

Keywords: Role of the Department, Tourism

The framework of local financial management at both provincial and district/city levels has undergone substantial transformation in response to the implementation of regional autonomy. In the context of decentralization, local governments are mandated to operate in a manner that is effective, efficient, and capable of enhancing community participation to promote equity and justice by fully developing the potential inherent in each region. The financial capacity of a region can be assessed by examining the magnitude of local revenues generated, particularly in relation to the delegation of regional autonomy. This study aims to evaluate the financial capacity of Bitung city during the period 2008-2012 to determine its ability to support the implementation of regional autonomy. Secondary data were utilized for this analysis. The methodological approach involved calculating various financial ratios, including the independence ratio, fiscal decentralization degree ratio, harmony ratio, routine capability index ratio, dependency ratio, and growth ratio. The findings indicate that (1) the independence ratio remains low, (2) the fiscal decentralization degree ratio is insufficient, (3) the harmony ratio is comparatively low relative to routine development expenditure, (4) the routine capability index ratio is markedly low, (5) the dependency ratio is considerably high, and (6) the average growth ratio exhibits both positive and negative trends. Based on the analysis, it can be concluded that the fiscal capacity of Bitung city to support regional autonomy during 2008-2012 is relatively inadequate.

ABSTRACTBreadfruit flour can be utilized as a food diversification material that can be processed into various products such as noodles, bread and biscuits. The addition of tapioca to the making of breadfruit biscuits is used as a thickening agent or a filler and binder in the manufacture of biscuits. The purpose of this study was to determine the exact amount of substitution of tapioca flour based on the sensory properties and chemical properties of breadfruit biscuits. This research uses Completely Randomized Design (RAL) with substitution of breadfruit flour and tapioca flour. The study was conducted with 3 replications and analyzed using a variety of scans (Anova). Influential treatment was carried out by BNT advanced test. The substitution treatment formulation is as follows: A (100% Flour Bread), B (95% Flour + 5% Tapioca Flour), C (90% Flour + 10% Tapioca Flour), D (85% Flour + 15 % Tapioca Flour), E (80% Flour + 20% Tapioca Flour). Parameters observed for water content, ash content, protein content, fat content, carbohydrate, caloric value and sensory properties. The result of the research showed that the treatment of D is biscuit with 85% breadfruit flour and 15% tapioca flour is the preferred biscuit panel with the hardness of biscuit 16.00 mm / g / second, water content 3,44%, ash content 2,92%, Fat content 11,87%, protein content 3,74%, carbohydrate 78,03%, and calorific value 433,91 kcal.Keywords: Biscuit, Breadfruit Flour and Tapioca Flour

ABSTRACT This research is entitled "Suffixes in English and Tontemboan language (A Contrastive Analysis)". The objectives of this research are to identify, classify and describe the suffixes and to analyze the similarities and differences of suffixes used in both languages. This research uses a descriptive method. There are three steps to finish this research, the first step is preparation. In this step, the writer reads some books about suffixes. The second step is data collection. In this step, the writer collect the kind of suffixes that include in suffixes in English and Tontemboan language. The third step is data analysis. In this step, the writer identifies, classifies, and describes the data about suffixes in English and Tontemboan language according to O'Grady and Dobrovolsky's (1992) theory and then the writer uses Lado (1957) and Whitman (1970) theory to find out the similarities and the differences of the structures in this case the suffixes of both languages in terms of forms, functions and meanings. The result shows that English and Tontemboan language have suffixes. The functions of English Suffixes are to form nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs. While the function of Tontemboan suffixes are nouns, verbs, and adjectives. Keywords: Suffixes, English and Tontemboan language, Contrastive analysis.

This study investigates the influence of the internal control system and financial accounting system on the quality of financial statements within the local government of Manado City. Financial statements prepared by local governments serve to present comprehensive information regarding their financial position and all conducted transactions. To be considered qualified, these statements must exhibit characteristics such as relevance, reliability, comparability, and comprehensibility. The quality of local government financial statements may be affected by several factors, notably the internal control system and the financial accounting system employed.

The research sample comprised 40 financial management personnel selected from 10 regional work units (SKPD) of Manado City, drawn from a total population of 168 personnel. Employing a quantitative methodology, primary data were gathered via questionnaires. The study’s independent variables included the internal control system and the financial accounting system, while the dependent variable was the quality of the local government financial statements. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS version 23.0, with multiple linear regression analysis applied to test the proposed hypotheses.

The findings reveal that the internal control system exerts a significant positive effect on the quality of financial statements of Manado City’s local government. Conversely, the implementation of the financial accounting system did not demonstrate a significant positive impact on financial statement quality. However, when considered jointly, both the internal control system and the financial accounting system significantly and positively influence the quality of the local government’s financial statements.

**Keywords:** Internal control system, financial accounting system, local government financial statements, financial statement quality
