This study aims to examine the effectiveness of coordination within the governance structure of Kecamatan Malalayang, Manado City. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the study involved eight informants comprising the Head of Malalayang Sub-district, four leaders from various UPTD departments, two heads of vertical institutions operating within the Kecamatan Malalayang area, and one Lurah. Data were collected through structured interviews, and the analysis was conducted using Miles and Huberman’s interactive model.

The findings indicate that the coordination of government administration in Kecamatan Malalayang, when evaluated across dimensions of communication, cooperation, synchronization, and integration or unity of action, has not been optimally effective, though it remains at a moderate level of adequacy. Based on these outcomes, the study recommends that: (1) communication between work units within the kecamatan be enhanced through the regular or periodic convening of coordination meetings, alongside the timely and clear dissemination of information regarding program plans and implementation to all involved units; (2) inter-unit cooperation be strengthened by establishing cooperation forums; (3) synchronization of programs and activities be improved by engaging in joint planning processes; and (4) integration or unity of action be promoted by collaboratively organizing program plans and their execution.

Keywords: Coordination, District Government Implementation.

Background: Low back pain constitutes a significant concern within the realm of occupational health, often signaling underlying issues related to the work environment. This condition is influenced by numerous factors, including but not limited to age and duration of employment. The present study aims to elucidate the relationship between age, length of employment, and the prevalence of low back pain complaints among tofu factory workers located in Batukota village, Malalayang district, Manado city.

Method: Employing a descriptive study design, this research was conducted in the Batukota sub-district of Malalayang district, Manado city, over the period from November 2020 to January 2021. A total of 32 tofu factory workers participated as respondents in this study. The primary variables investigated included age, length of work, and complaints of low back pain. Data collection instruments comprised questionnaires, cameras, and writing tools. Univariate analysis techniques were utilized to analyze the collected data.

Results: Findings revealed that the majority of respondents were within the 21 to 30-year age bracket, accounting for 13 individuals (40.6%), whereas the smallest proportion was observed in the group aged over 40 years, with 3 respondents (9.4%). Regarding length of employment, most participants had worked for 1 to 5 years, totaling 26 respondents (81.3%). Additionally, a predominant number of respondents (17 individuals, 53.1%) were classified as experiencing poor low back pain complaints (NPB), indicative of frequent and persistent pain in the lower back region during work activities.

Conclusion: The study concludes that the majority of tofu factory workers examined were aged between 21 and 30 years, had a tenure of 1 to 5 years, and reported poor NPB status. These findings underscore the necessity for further comprehensive health assessments focused on low back pain among workers in tofu factories.

Urban Heat Island (UHI) is a phenomenon where urban areas experience hotter temperatures than the surrounding rural areas. Changes in land cover that occur include the establishment of buildings and infrastructure that replace open areas and vegetation, where the land cover that was originally permeable and moist has changed to impermeable and dry as a result of urban development which led to the formation of the Urban Heat Island. UHI is formed by various factors such as weather, geographic location, vegetation, materials, geometry and anthropogenic heat. Bitung city experienced population growth from 2008-2017 of 2.12% per year as well as various land use changes resulting in decreased open space and vegetation which led to an increase in surface temperature. Therefore this research was conducted to identify the distribution of surface temperature in the Bitung city and its forming factors. This study aims to find out how the surface temperature in the city of Bitung and the conditions of land use, building materials and urban geometry at high surface temperatures. The data analysis used is in the form of spatial analysis with GIS software in the form of ArcGIS 10.3. In determining the surface temperature, data from Landsat 8 imagery is used. From image processing in Bitung city, it was found that the lowest surface temperature was 15.47 ºC and the highest surface temperature was 43.34 ºC. The highest average surface temperature in the city of Bitung is in the sub-districts of Girian, Madidir, and Maesa with land use for housing, trade, industry and services; with the use of zinc roofing material and concrete walls and a building distance of 0.82m to 8.47m. Keyword: Urban heat island; Land use; Building materials; Urban geometry

Pegadaian is a state-owned financial institution under BUMN, primarily engaged in providing credit secured by pawned items in accordance with financial law. These pawned items serve as collateral, granting absolute rights over specific assets that function as guarantees for the debt. In the event of non-payment, these collateral items can be liquidated to satisfy the outstanding obligations as stipulated in the agreement. An auction constitutes a public sale wherein items are offered at prices that are either publicly announced or directly presented, with bids increasing or decreasing until the highest price is achieved. Auctions are conducted when a customer fails to fulfill their repayment or extension obligations for the pawned items, and such sales occur at a public venue. PT Pegadaian (Persero) possesses the legal right to auction off customers’ pawned goods. Prior to conducting the auction, the Karombasan Branch of PT Pegadaian (Persero) ensures that the customer is notified or reminded that their pawned items have either expired or surpassed the payment deadline. This procedure is implemented to prevent any potential misunderstandings between the institution and its clients.

Keywords: auction procedures, pawned goods, collateral liquidation

This study, titled "Code Mixing in the Social Media Facebook," endeavors to examine and elucidate the phenomenon of code mixing as it occurs on the Facebook platform. The primary aim of the research is to identify, categorize, and analyze instances of code mixing within Facebook statuses and photo/video captions. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data were collected directly from user-generated content on Facebook. For the purposes of identification and classification, the study utilizes the frameworks established by Muysken (2000) and Suwito (1985), while analytical descriptions are grounded in the theoretical perspectives of Hoffman (1991) and Suwito (1983). The findings reveal a total of 65 instances of code mixing. According to Muysken’s (2000) typology, four types of code mixing were identified, including word insertion, phrase insertion, and alternation. Further analysis based on Suwito’s (1985) classification indicates that all observed data represent external code mixing, specifically involving the integration of English into Indonesian. Concerning the motivations behind code mixing, thirteen causative factors were discerned in accordance with the theories posited by Hoffman (1991:96) and Suwito (1983). These factors include, but are not limited to, addressing a specific topic, quoting others, expressing emphasis, interjections, repetition for clarification, intentions to clarify, signaling group identity, modulating requests or commands, fulfilling lexical needs, excluding others from communication, role-related influences, variability in use, and the desire to explain or interpret. 

Keywords: Sociolinguistics, Code Mixing, Facebook

The result of this study The Writer have found 16 forms of primary auxiliary verbs those are 8 forms of be (am, is, are, was, were, be, been, being), 3 forms of have (have, had, has), and 5 forms of do (do, did, does, doing, and done) with 4 main criteria include negation, inversion, substitution, and marked positive. The preservation of nutrient inputs essential for soil fertility within forest ecosystems is crucial to mitigate potential declines in land productivity. Litter decomposition constitutes the breakdown of organic matter, converting litter into soil-available nutrients. This research was undertaken to evaluate and compare the decomposition rates of leaf litter from Palaquium obovatum, Spathodea campanulata, and Calophyllum soulattri within the Bron Warembungan Forest, Minahasa Regency. The study utilized leaf litter of the three species, employing a completely randomized design with two factors: tree species and decomposition duration. A total of 36 litter bags were randomly placed on the forest floor and collected weekly over a four-week period. Simultaneously, temperature and humidity were measured to contextualize the decomposition process. Findings indicate that among the studied species, Spathodea campanulata exhibited the highest average weekly decomposition rate at 15.49%, followed by Palaquium obovatum at 11.74%, and Calophyllum soulattri at 3.07%. Notably, the initial week demonstrated a rapid decomposition phase across all species, correlating with elevated moisture content observed in the litter. 

Keywords: tropical rainforest, litter decomposition, leaf litter

This study aims to examine the density and net calorific value of traditional market waste, alongside an analysis of the leachate produced from this waste. Sampling was conducted across traditional markets located in five districts/cities: Manado City, Bitung City, North Minahasa Regency, Minahasa Regency, and Tomohon City. The research took place between May and August 2021. A quantitative descriptive survey methodology was employed, complemented by tabulated analyses and histogram visualizations. Data collection involved site visits and direct observations, integrated with both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data consisted of collected waste samples subjected to analysis, while secondary data comprised relevant information and supporting documentation obtained from associated agencies. The parameters measured included the density of traditional market waste, calculation of the net calorific value for each waste sample, and assessment of the leachate’s pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), total suspended solids (TSS), and electrical conductivity (EC). The findings indicate that organic waste exhibits the highest density across the five districts/cities. Furthermore, the average net calorific values recorded ranged between 7000 kcal/kg and 8000 kcal/kg. Analysis of the leachate revealed elevated TDS levels, and EC measurements suggested the presence of cation ions within the leachate. Notably, the leachate is interpreted not merely as a pollutant but rather as a potential source of nutrients beneficial for plant growth.

The present study, entitled "Derivational Affixes in English and Toba Batak Languages: A Contrastive Analysis," is formulated as a research report aimed at describing and analyzing the derivational affixes in both English and the Toba Batak language with respect to their form, function, and meaning across verbs, nouns, adjectives, and adverbs. The primary objective of this investigation is to identify the similarities and differences between the derivational affix systems of English and Toba Batak by applying O'Grady’s (1987) theoretical framework and employing Lado’s (1971) contrastive analysis methodology. English data were sourced from various linguistic textbooks, specifically O'Grady’s Contemporary Linguistic Analysis: An Introduction (1987), whereas data for Toba Batak were obtained through elicitation from four native speakers who were carefully selected based on criteria such as age, gender, and cognitive capability, all of whom originated from the Toba Batak region. The findings indicate that English derivational affixes primarily comprise prefixes and suffixes, while those in Toba Batak include prefixes, suffixes, infixes, and confixes. Functionally, derivational affixes in both languages serve to form new lexemes, which may or may not involve a change in grammatical category. Convergently, both languages utilize prefixation and suffixation processes; however, a notable divergence is evident in that English derivational morphology relies exclusively on prefixation and suffixation, whereas Toba Batak also employs infixation and confixation. Furthermore, in terms of semantic function, English prefixes can carry negative connotations, a feature absent among Toba Batak derivational prefixes.  

Keywords: English Derivational Affixes, Toba Batak Language, Contrastive Analysis

Association refers to the interaction among multiple individuals, which may take the form of familial, organizational, or communal relationships. Through such associations, individuals develop an understanding of the principles governing social interaction, thereby enhancing their social nature, as humans are inherently social beings. Findings indicate that while the Bitung City Public Works Department has largely implemented the Governmental Accounting Standard PP. 71 of 2010, its application remains suboptimal due to certain incomplete elements in the financial reporting, particularly concerning the Budget Change Report (Surplus and Deficit Report, SAL). This study aims to describe, classify, and analyze the use of modal verbs in the film script *Ted*, authored by Seth MacFarlane, Alec Sulkin, and Wellesley Wild. Modal auxiliary verbs function as "helping verbs" that enhance and modify the meaning of the main verb. Unlike main verbs, the tense effects of modal verbs differ significantly. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data comprising modal verbs were extracted from sentences within the script. The theoretical framework adopted in this research is based on Robert’s classification, which distinguishes among pure modals, special modals, and semi-modals. Pure modals include can, could, will, would, shall, should, may, might, and must; special modals encompass forms such as be going to, have to, had better, had rather, be to, be able to, and ought to; semi-modals refer to verbs like dare and need. The analysis predominantly focuses on the pure modals. The meanings of these modal auxiliaries as used in the script are as follows: can expresses ability, permission, and suggestion; could indicates ability, possibility, permission, suggestion, and request; may denotes request and possibility; might conveys possibility and permission; will signifies willingness, intention, and request; would expresses willingness, certainty, intention, and offering; shall is used for making requests; should indicates obligation, possibility, and necessity; and must conveys necessity, possibility, obligation, and request.

Keywords: Modal Auxiliary Verbs; Film Script; *Ted*; Seth MacFarlane; Alec Sulkin; Wellesley Wild; English Language; Descriptive Study

Various obstacles faced by policymakers and implementers have hindered the successful execution of tourism development policies on Kumo Island.

The primary aim of this study is to assess the availability and appropriateness of standardization for governmental, social, and economic facilities within Bitung City. The secondary objective involves examining the hierarchical structure of service centers in Bitung City. Lastly, the study seeks to evaluate the alignment of the service centers stipulated in the Bitung City Spatial Plan (RTRW) for 2013–2033 with the prevailing conditions. This research utilizes secondary data, collected through methods including observation, literature review, and document analysis. The data were subsequently analyzed employing scalogram analysis, centrality index calculations, and gravity analysis. The findings reveal that, according to the service standardization specified in SNI 03-1733-2004, the majority of service facilities in Bitung City comply with the established standards. Scalogram analysis indicates that Madidir District constitutes the first-order service center. Additionally, analysis using the Marshal centrality index identifies Madidir and Maesa sub-districts as holding the primary positions in the hierarchy. Gravity analysis further indicates that three sub-districts exhibit weak regional interaction values with Madidir and Maesa. Finally, the study finds that the Bitung City Spatial Plan (RTRW) 2013–2033 has been modified in response to the city’s dynamic development patterns.

This study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of the pre-employment card program designed for fresh graduates in Manado City. The research was conducted over a period spanning from November 2021 to February 2022, employing a descriptive qualitative methodology. Findings indicate that the pre-employment card program has not been implemented effectively or optimally. This inefficacy is attributed to several factors, including the program's failure to meet its intended targets, inaccuracies and outdated information in the data verification and control processes, which allowed participants who did not meet the eligibility criteria to receive incentives. Furthermore, the dissemination efforts by the North Sulawesi Province Manpower and Transmigration Office were suboptimal, relying primarily on communications from the central Pre-Employment Implementing Team and Management. Participants exhibited a predominant focus on the incentives, which were largely allocated toward daily necessities and contributed to consumptive behavior. Additionally, completion certificates issued upon training did not guarantee improved employment prospects, as the training consisted solely of video presentations without live instruction. The absence of adequate supervision and monitoring adversely impacted participant discipline, and the lack of opportunities for interaction or discussion hindered comprehension of the training material. The program’s deficiency in providing ongoing support to participants further diminished its effectiveness. Consequently, it can be concluded that the pre-employment card program for fresh graduates in Manado City is neither effectively executed nor achieving its full potential. Therefore, continuous and systematic evaluation and enhancement of program management are imperative, specifically addressing the data verification process, dissemination strategies, implementation outcomes, and monitoring mechanisms.

Electronic Data Processing (EDP) refers to the utilization of automated techniques in the commercial processing of data. As a subset of information technology, EDP facilitates the repetitive processing of similar data types through relatively straightforward methods. The Standar Profesional Akuntan Publik (SPAP) underscores the importance of auditors’ comprehension when examining computer-based accounting systems. In Indonesia, this approach is termed Teknik Audit Berbantuan Komputer (TABK), or Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs), as outlined in PSA No. 59 concerning Computer-Assisted Auditing Techniques (SA Section 327). This research employs a qualitative descriptive methodology, involving data collection, analysis, and subsequent conclusion drawing. Findings indicate that younger auditors demonstrate greater adaptability to advancements in information technology, particularly in the execution of computerized internal audits and controls. The audit process benefits from enhanced auditor independence, improved accuracy and efficiency in data management, and the generation of outputs grounded in more precise audit data processing. With respect to internal controls, auditors conduct control procedures post-EDP implementation to mitigate process errors, ensure the security of programs and data, and oversee the audit process to confirm its proper execution. Nevertheless, the audit practice incorporating EDP encounters risks, including data processing errors stemming from human mistakes, data loss due to technical computer issues, and vulnerability to computer viruses.  

**Keywords:** Analysis, Electronic Data Processing, Internal Audit

This study investigates the effectiveness of the Village Fund program in empowering the community of Kanawong Village during the 2017 fiscal year. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study utilizes both primary and secondary data sources. Data collection was conducted through observations, interviews, and document reviews. The obtained data were subsequently analyzed using a systematic process involving data reduction, data presentation, and drawing of conclusions.

Findings indicate that the utilization of funds in Kanawong Village, located in the Western Islands Regency of Siau SITARO, yielded varying degrees of effectiveness in achieving community empowerment. Regarding transparency, the program demonstrated limited effectiveness, as the village government provided insufficient information concerning the allocation and use of the Village Fund. In terms of community participation, engagement was evident through involvement in integrated service post activities. However, the government’s commitment to training programs—specifically those targeting the village chief and Posyandu (integrated health service posts) activities—was relatively low. While government apparatus involvement was ongoing and positively received by the community, training initiatives have yet to gain similar acceptance.

Accountability was fully achieved in the implementation of Posyandu programs but remained deficient in training activities. The discontinuation of training programs is apparent in the 2018 village work plan, whereas the Posyandu empowerment agenda, including its budget allocation, continues to expand. 

In conclusion, transparency regarding training activities for village chiefs and local officials, as well as the management of Posyandu initiatives in Kanawong Village, was found to be inadequate. Despite this, community participation in these programs was actively realized. Training activities for village leadership remain underutilized by the community, in contrast to the more accessible Posyandu programs. Accountability measures were lacking in the training sector but satisfactory for Posyandu activities. Furthermore, training programs were not sustained, whereas empowerment efforts related to Posyandu continued to progress.

Keywords: effectiveness, Village Fund, community empowerment

This study investigates: (1) the maternal influence on the inheritance of yield components in Manado Yellow Corn, and (2) the genetic transmission of seed color and seed type in the same variety. The research was conducted in Kalasey Village, Mandolang Subdistrict, Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi Province, from April to September 2016. The plant material comprised a local variety of Manado Yellow Corn, obtained from the Plant Science Laboratory, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Sam Ratulangi, Manado. The experimental design involved comparing two hybridization treatments, each derived from two parental populations: (1) local corn with yellow seed color and flint seed type, and (2) local corn with yellow seed color and dent seed type. Each treatment included four replicates, with six female plants per replicate, resulting in a total of 24 ears from direct hybridization (F1) and 24 ears from reciprocal hybridization (F1R). The findings revealed that (1) no maternal effect was observed in the inheritance of yield components—ear weight, ear length, ear diameter, number of seed rows per ear, number of yellow seeds, and number of dent seed types—when crossing Manado Yellow Corn parents; (2) a maternal effect was present in the inheritance of the flint seed type; and (3) the highest frequency of yellow seed color and flint seed type, characteristic of Manado Yellow Corn, was achieved through crosses involving female plants with the flint seed type and male plants with the dent seed type (♀ Flint × ♂ Dent).  

Keywords: dent, flint, Manado Yellow Corn

Since the inception of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), it has taken Indonesia and other member states 48 years to achieve the establishment of the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC). This study aims to assess the performance of export values, which represent a key objective and expectation for countries engaging in economic integration. Specifically, the research analyzes the changes in Indonesia’s export values to the other nine ASEAN members during the period spanning one year prior to and one year following the establishment of the AEC, employing the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for statistical evaluation. Findings indicate a statistically significant positive increase in Indonesia’s export values to ASEAN member countries post-AEC, with an observed year-on-year growth rate of 90%. Among the member states, Thailand emerges as the leading contributor, accounting for 84% of the total export value, whereas the remaining ASEAN countries collectively contribute only 16% (Singapore 5%, Malaysia 2%, the Philippines 2%, Vietnam 2%, Myanmar 2%, and Cambodia, Brunei Darussalam, and Lao PDR showing negligible contributions). Moreover, mineral fuels, mineral oils and their derivatives, and bituminous substances constitute the predominant export commodities from Indonesia to ASEAN countries following AEC implementation, representing 22% of the total export value. The formation of the AEC has facilitated improved access for Indonesia to the nine other member states; however, the heavy reliance on the Thai market poses potential risks, as underscored by established investment principles advising against concentrated exposure. Finally, the government is urged to prioritize the development of domestic value-added industries, considering the continued predominance of raw material exports.  
 
**Keywords:** ASEAN Economic Community (AEC), economic integration, export performance, Wilcoxon signed-rank test

The tradition of circumcision feasts, which was previously conducted in a modest manner, has undergone significant transformation over the past decade, now involving substantial financial expenditures that are comparable to those of wedding celebrations. This study aims to examine the culture surrounding circumcision parties, the cooperative systems involved, and the responses of the Muslim community in Motoboi Kecil Village towards these events. Findings indicate that the circumcision feast culture in Motoboi Kecil is consistent with that observed in other regions of Mongondow Bolaang. In this community, the circumcision feast serves primarily as a form of thanksgiving prayer for the child's circumcision. The existing system of cooperation within the society facilitates collective efforts and social gatherings. Community responses reveal that not all members participate in assisting families; instead, involvement is often influenced by considerations of social status. The study concludes that the circumcision feast culture among Muslims in Motoboi Kecil has remained stable and does not differ markedly from practices in other areas of Bolaang Mongondow. It is recommended that such celebrations avoid excessive spending and prioritize religious values.  

Keywords: Muslim, party culture, Motoboi

The Land Tax on Rural and Urban Buildings (PBB-P2) represents a newly introduced form of regional taxation. Pursuant to the enactment of Law Number 28 of 2009, all revenues generated from PBB-P2 are designated as regional income, as the processes of data collection, appraisal, determination, administration, collection, and service delivery of PBB-P2 are entirely managed by local governments at the regency or municipal levels. The transfer of management authority over PBB-P2 to local governments was mandated to be completed by no later than January 1, 2014. This study aims to examine the procedures involved in the collection and recording of the Land and Rural and Urban Buildings Tax within Manado City. Employing a descriptive qualitative research methodology, the study provides a detailed account of the observable conditions directly related to the research subject. Findings indicate that the collection and administration of PBB-P2 as a local tax in Manado City have been conducted effectively and in alignment with established procedures, despite certain deficiencies and challenges encountered during implementation. Furthermore, accounting practices by the Manado Regional Tax and Retribution Board conform to Government Regulation No. 71 of 2010; however, some journal entries remain unexecuted, specifically those involving the recording of income transfers from the treasurer’s cash to the local treasury and instances of direct taxpayer payments into regional cash accounts.  

Keywords: collection, recording, PBB-P2

Abstract:  
National development fundamentally constitutes a comprehensive effort to enhance all facets of society, the nation, and the state, thereby forming an integral process within the organization of the state system aimed at achieving national objectives. This study investigates the relationship between planning and community participation and their impact on successful development in Lompad Ranoyapo Village, District Lompad. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the research focused on the residents of Lompad Village, with a sample size of 38 individuals. Data collection was conducted through the administration of questionnaires, and data analysis was performed using Multiple Regression Analysis coupled with Multiple Correlation Analysis. The findings reveal that the regression coefficients for the planning variable (X1) and participation variable (X2) in relation to successful development (Y) are both positive and statistically significant, with the multiple correlation and determination coefficients categorized as high. These results indicate that both planning and community participation substantially contribute to rural development success, demonstrating a significant correlation within Lompad Ranoyapo Village. Accordingly, it is recommended that (1) the village government actively involve all societal elements in the implementation of rural development planning, and (2) governmental authorities encourage greater community engagement throughout the development process, encompassing planning, execution, evaluation, and maintenance phases.  
Keywords: Planning, Community Participation, Development Success

The aim of this study was to examine the impacts of the increase in soybean prices on small-scale tofu processing industries located in Batu Kota Village, Malalayang Subdistrict, Manado. Data collection was carried out over a six-month period, from February 2014 to July 2014, involving both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were gathered through direct surveys conducted with tofu enterprises in Batu Kota Village, while secondary data were obtained from relevant institutional agencies. The sampling process employed a simple saturated sampling technique, resulting in a total of four respondents from small processing industries. The methodology for assessing the effects before and after the price increase comprised descriptive analysis involving data tabulation, editing, and processing using Microsoft Excel software. The findings reveal that the rise in soybean prices had significant effects on the input costs, production volume, overall industry expenses, tofu pricing, tofu size, as well as the revenue and profitability of tofu entrepreneurs in the study area. Despite a 35.84% increase in soybean prices, tofu production in Batu Kota Village remained sustainable. This resilience is attributed to modifications in tofu size and the presence of informal partnerships for raw material supply between tofu producers and their suppliers, which ensured the continued feasibility and operation of the industries. 

Keywords: production frequency, informal partnership, tofu size variation

The purpose of this study was to detect the presence of bacteria Aeromonas sp in tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Nine fish with an average body weight of 150-200 g were used in this study as samples. Sampling was conducted at three different locations which were representative of fish culture sites located on Lake Tondano. The number of sample gathered from each location was and 3 fish which were taken randomly. Fish samples were taken by using a scoop, then the samples were taken alive by placing in an oxygen-filled plastic separately and taken direcly to lab Fish Disease Control and Environmental Center, Tateli, Department of Marine and Fisheries of North Sulawesi province, for examination the presence of bacteria. Isolation of bacteria were conducted by taking samples from gill and kidney. This study was carried out from April - July 2013. Identification of the presence of bacteria was done through a series of observations of colony morphology and gram staining of bacteria, followed by a series of biochemical tests: oxidase test , catalase test , test TSIA , H2S production test , indole test , motility test , citrate test, and test O/F. It could be concluded that 22.22 % of farmed nile tilapia in Lake Tondano were infected with the Aeromonas sp with the following percentage from each site: Paleloan village 7.40% , 7.40% Toulimembet village, and 7.40% Eris village. Keywords: Aeromonas sp, isolation, nile tilapia, floating net cage, Lake Tondano

ABSTRACTThe objectives of the study were to measure the changes of water content, the weight losses, changes in color, texture and to determine the level of damage that occurs during storage chili pepper in a cold room and get the right kind of packaging to preserve the quality of chili pepper. The research uses descriptive method with three packaging treatments and three replications. The treatment consisted of (1) packing within bamboo baskets, (2) packaging in the nets sacks, and (3) packing within plastic bags, HDPE (high density polyethylene). The results showed that chili stored at cold temperatures (6-10 oC) using plastic bags deliver the lowest lost 1.37% after being stored for 20 days compared to the net bag packaging with the losses of 35.98% and packaging bamboo basket with a loss of 18.22%. Chili packed with plastic bag showed the water content of 57.8% higher than net bag packaging of 40.73% and a bamboo basket with a water content of 52.85%. The hardness value of the base was 0.00025 mm/g, the middle section of 9.89 m/g, and the end of 75.20 mm/g. The damage percentage of chili pepper stored by using bamboo basket packaging was 10.09%, and within the net bag packaging was 16.32% while packaging in the plastic bag was 8.13%.Keywords : Packaging, chili pepper, cold storage

Thus far, the CSR initiatives targeting farmers have been well received and effective, encompassing activities such as addressing agricultural challenges, providing training, allocating land to those without agricultural plots, and supplying transportation means to facilitate access to farmland.

The implementation of PT Antam’s CSR program for farmer community empowerment has proceeded successfully and aligns with corporate policies, allowing adaptation to the region’s human and natural resource conditions to ensure program sustainability. Looking ahead, the enhancement of CSR efforts is expected to further actualize company policies and comply with legal mandates.

POTENTIAL ANALYSIS AND STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT PATTERN OF CATTLE WITH INTEGRATED COCONUT-COW IN SOUTH DISTRICT HALMAHERA NORTH MALUKU PROVINCE. Animal agricultural integration often found in South Halmahera district is the integration using coconut plantation and local beef pattern called coco-beef integration. Expected potential of land area, population of cattle supported by human and natural resources as well as market opportunities could develop coco-beef integration patterns providing the increasing economic impact for farmer welfare. This study aims to analyze the potential and development strategy of beef integration with coconut plantations in South Halmahera district. The research was conducted in South Halmahera district of North Maluku Province since November 2014 to February 2015. The determination of respondents was performed using simple random sampling method. Criteria of respondents involved in this study were household farmers running a coco-beef integration, at least animal maintenance of more than one year and they had sold cattle. The results showed the particular characteristics of household farmers including coconut plantation ownership of 3.2 ha with the average number of animals of 8.7 heads, the average education level of junior high school, the animal breeding experience of 7.9 years and animal maintenance purposes as beef production and animal labor . Management aspects of farm animals were still under the traditional maintenance systems, animals were resistant to disease, and house hold farmer knowledge on animal reproduction was still limited. Aspects of feed resources were positively supporting in the development of beef cattle under integration pattern, especially the nutritional value of forage and land carrying capacities. Livestock productivity aspects had quite well potential and supported facilities, including infrastructures. Therefore, it can be concluded that South Halmahera District has potential in the development of beef cattle farm applying cattle integration patterns in form of coco-beef natural resources supported by potentials of human resources, good government policy, infrastructure availability and market opportunities based on the analysis of the potential of South Halmahera district located in a strategic position as a development area of beef and coconut plantation integration patterns. ABSTRACT

This study, entitled "Kompositum dalam Film Game of Thrones Season 8," was conducted to fulfill the requirements for obtaining a bachelor's degree in the English Department, Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University. The primary objective of this research is to investigate the processes involved in the formation of compound words featured in Season 8 of the television series Game of Thrones. To analyze the compound word formation, the researcher employs O'Grady's (1997:143) theoretical framework, which defines compounding as the combination of various lexical categories such as nouns, adjectives, verbs, and prepositions (O'Grady, 1996:26).

The findings reveal a diverse range of compound word forms across different categories. Compound nouns manifest in five distinct structures: Noun+Noun→Noun, Verb+Verb→Noun, Adjective+Noun→Noun, Adjective+Verb→Noun, and Adjective+Noun→Noun. Compound verbs occur in two forms: Noun+Noun→Verb and Verb+Noun→Verb. Compound adjectives are identified in four forms: Noun+Adjective→Adjective, Verb+Noun→Adjective, Adjective+Adjective→Adjective, and Adjective+Noun→Adjective. Additionally, compound adverbs appear in six structural patterns: Noun+Adverb→Adverb, Verb+Adverb→Adverb, Adjective+Adjective→Adverb, Adverb+Noun→Adverb, Preposition+Noun→Adverb, and Preposition+Verb→Adverb.

The researcher analyzed forty-nine compound words extracted from six episodes of Game of Thrones Season 8 through morphological analysis to classify their types and interpret their meanings. Results indicate the presence of four categories of compound words with varying forms: thirty compound nouns, two compound verbs, nine compound adjectives, and eight compound adverbs. Moreover, this study identifies two forms of endocentric compounds and three forms of exocentric compounds among the data. These findings suggest that compound words are abundant within the film's linguistic context.

Keywords: Morphology, Compound Words, Compounding, Types of Compounds, Game of Thrones Season 8

The financial statements of a company serve as a critical tool for informed decision-making; therefore, the components within these statements must be accurate and reliable. In corporate decision-making processes, the Cash Flow Statement holds particular importance, as the income statement and balance sheet may not always accurately reflect the company’s true financial condition. This study aims to examine the implementation of the Cash Flow Statement in accordance with SFAS No. 2 within corporate decision-making frameworks. Employing a quantitative descriptive research methodology, the findings indicate a decline in the net cash provided by the company during the year compared to the previous fiscal period. The study utilizes ratio analysis as a basis for corporate decisions. Specifically, the Operating Cash Flow to Total Liabilities ratio serves as an indicator for assessing the company’s capacity to repay its total liabilities within one year of operations. Similarly, the Cash Flow to Current Liabilities ratio provides a measure of the company’s ability to settle current liabilities using net operating cash flow. Furthermore, the Cash Flow to Sales ratio evaluates the company’s efficiency in generating cash from sales activities. It is recommended that the leadership at Perum Bulog, particularly within the finance department, adopt the Cash Flow Statement as a foundational tool for financial analysis, thereby facilitating a clearer understanding of the financial position and supporting more effective decision-making.

The number of internet users has been increasing substantially each year. The internet serves not only as a platform for information retrieval and communication but also as a medium for activities such as browsing fashion products. Many consumers favor online shopping due to its convenience, time-saving nature, and comfort. Currently, e-commerce in Indonesia is experiencing rapid growth, with numerous online stores offering a variety of options for purchasing and selling goods. An online shop functions as a platform enabling customers to buy goods or services directly from sellers through internet-based web browsers. In the contemporary market, online shops actively compete to capture customer attention. Zalora is a prominent online shopping site widely favored by consumers in Indonesia, particularly in Manado city, as it offers a diverse range of fashion products for both men and women from various brands.

This study aims to analyze both the simultaneous and partial effects of customer perception and customer attitude on the purchase intentions of Zalora online shop customers. The theoretical framework underpinning this research includes constructs of customer perception, customer attitude, and customer purchase intention. The population of the study comprises Zalora customers in Manado city, with a sample of 150 respondents selected through random sampling to ensure rapid and efficient data collection. Quantitative methodology was employed, utilizing questionnaires and ordinal regression analysis. The findings indicate that both customer perception and customer attitude exert a significant and positive influence on customers’ purchase intentions. It is recommended that future research incorporate additional variables or qualitative approaches such as interviews to enhance the understanding of factors influencing purchase intention.

Promotion constitutes a key element within the marketing toolkit aimed at introducing products to consumers. Marketers employ diverse promotional strategies to influence consumer decision-making processes. Common components of the promotional mix include advertising, sales promotion, publicity or public relations, and personal selling. This study was conducted in Manado with the primary objective of examining the effects of sponsorship, events, and publicity on consumer decision-making, both individually and collectively. Employing a causal research design, the investigation sought to determine the impact of sponsorship, events, and publicity on consumer decision-making. A multiple regression model was utilized to address the research questions. The study population comprised customers of PT. Hasjrat Abadi in Manado, with a sample size of 100 respondents selected for analysis. Hypothesis testing revealed that sponsorship and publicity each exert a significant partial effect on consumer decision-making, while the combined effect of sponsorship, events, and publicity was also found to be significant. Conversely, events alone did not demonstrate a significant partial impact on consumer decision-making. The findings suggest that sponsorship activities and product publicity play substantial roles in guiding consumers through the processes of product investigation, selection, and purchase, with a preference observed for products associated with well-known brands.  
Keywords: promotional mix, sponsorship, publicity.

In contemporary times, there is an increasing demand for rapid and efficient computational methods, often realized through simulation techniques. This study employs SolidWorks 2016 software to conduct the simulation analysis. SolidWorks is a solid modeling program based on the Parasolid kernel and utilizes a parametric modeling approach for both design and assembly processes. Parameters within this context serve as constraints critical for defining the shape or geometry of the modeled components. The present investigation focuses on kinematic simulation, specifically covering the entire workspace of an excavator arm. The subject of this research is the backhoe excavator arm mechanism of the Hitachi ZX-series, model ZX-200. The primary objective is to determine the velocity, tangential acceleration, and normal acceleration of the excavator arm mechanism during operation.

Simulation results indicate that the boom bar attains a maximum velocity of 2948.82 mm/s at a boom angle of 16.64° (corresponding to t = 3.83 s), which represents the minimum angle within the workspace. These simulated velocities have been corroborated through manual calculations. Furthermore, the peak tangential acceleration and normal acceleration of the boom bar were found to be 2430.12 mm/s² and 3705.11 mm/s², respectively. For the arm shaft, the maximum velocity recorded was 1778.06 mm/s at an arm rod angle of 140.86°, with corresponding maximum tangential and normal accelerations of 4594.03 mm/s² and 6665.24 mm/s². The bucket rod exhibited a maximum velocity of 473.61 mm/s, with tangential and normal accelerations reaching 90.09 mm/s² and 297.89 mm/s², respectively.

Keywords: Kinematic Analysis, Excavator Arm, Hitachi ZX-200

This study aims to directly examine the optimization of labor inspectors’ performance following the establishment of the UPTD Balai Pengawas within the Department of Manpower and Transmigration of North Sulawesi Province. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative approach, the investigation centers on key dimensions including work quality, work quantity, time utilization, and employee cooperation. A purposive sampling technique was utilized to select ten informants, and data were gathered through interviews, observations, and document analysis. The collected data were processed through data reduction, data display, and verification stages. Findings reveal that optimizing employee performance is a paramount concern for all governmental bodies and organizations in fulfilling their responsibilities. Effective performance constitutes a valuable asset and competitive advantage, as employees represent critical human resources contributing to organizational objectives. The study concludes that the performance of supervisory staff within the Manpower and Transmigration Office of North Sulawesi Province requires enhancement, specifically through direct oversight by the head of the supervisory office. Such supervision is intended to elevate performance outcomes, ensuring that goals are achieved efficiently and effectively, reflecting the anticipated standards of accomplishment.

This study aims to investigate the opportunistic behavior exhibited by the Manado City Government in response to changes in the General Allocation Fund (DAU), as conceptualized by Maryono (2013). Additionally, it seeks to provide empirical evidence concerning the variations in DAU allocations received from the Central Government and the corresponding opportunistic responses by the Manado City Government over the fiscal years 2014 to 2018. Employing a qualitative methodology, key informants were selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data collection methods included unstructured interviews, passive participant observation, and document analysis. The data were analyzed via processes of reduction, presentation, and drawing of conclusions or verification. Findings reveal that the Manado City Government’s opportunistic behaviors in relation to DAU changes manifest in several ways: (1) budgeting regional expenditures that surpass local own-source revenue (PAD), demonstrating a high dependency on DAU—approximately 70% compared to PAD; (2) a non-proactive stance towards enhancing resource potentials to increase PAD contributions to levels that would equal or exceed regional expenditures, despite PAD currently financing only 30% and being inherently unstable; (3) insufficient adoption of realistic approaches in establishing savings criteria within regional budgets, particularly concerning operational expenditure reductions to prioritize funding for community services; and (4) a conventional acceptance of the city’s reliance on the service sector, attributed to limited natural resource endowments.  
Keywords: Opportunistic Behavior, Local Government, General Allocation Funds.

Background: Hypertension is one of the health problems in Indonesia, especially the City of Tomohon. The prevalence of hypertension continues to increase every year. The death rate due to hypertension is quite high. One of the risk factors for hypertension is excess nutritional status. The purpose of this study was to describe the nutritional status of hypertension sufferers in the working area of the Puskesmas Tinoor, Tomohon City. Methode: This is a descriptive research. This is research was carried out in the working area of the Puskesmas Tinoor, Tomohon City in October-December 2021. A total of 72 hypertension patient were the subjects in this study. The instrument of this research is the filling sheet. Data were analyzed univariately. Result: The results showed that the average body weight (BW) was 66.6 kg, the median was 66 kg with a range of 43-120 kg. Based on height (BH) obtained an average of 162.3 cm, median 165 cm with a range of 142-181 cm. Based on the body mass index (BMI), the average BMI was 25.33, the median was 24.8 with a range of 17.2-42.1. Conclusion: That can be conclude that the average nutritional status of hypertension sufferers in the working area of the Puskesmas Tinoor, Tomohon City, is in the pre-obesity category. Therefore, patients can make efforts to maintain an ideal BMI through physical activity and regulating food intake.

Background: Gout arthritis is a metabolic disorder characterized by acute inflammation resulting from the deposition of urate crystals within the joints. Common clinical manifestations include joint pain and swelling. Non-pharmacological management strategies such as the application of warm compresses have been employed to alleviate these symptoms. 

Objective: This study seeks to evaluate the efficacy of warm compress therapy in reducing pain intensity among patients suffering from gout arthritis.

Methods: A quasi-experimental design employing a one-group pre-test and post-test approach was utilized. The study sample consisted of 44 participants diagnosed with gout arthritis. Pain levels were assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), supplemented by colored paper visual aids to represent pain intensity according to NRS scores. Data analysis was performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

Results: Findings revealed a statistically significant reduction in pain levels following the application of warm compresses, with an asymptotic significance value of 0.000 (p < 0.005). This supports the rejection of the null hypothesis and acceptance of the alternative hypothesis, indicating that warm compress treatment effectively diminishes pain in gout arthritis patients.

Conclusion: The application of warm compresses constitutes an effective intervention for pain relief in individuals with gout arthritis and can be self-administered by patients.

Keywords: gout arthritis; warm compress; pain management

This study aims to elucidate the role of the Technical Implementing Unit of Manado City, commonly known as Samsat Manado, in the prevention and mitigation of motor vehicle document counterfeiting. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, data were gathered through observations, interviews, and document analysis. The study involved ten informants. The investigation focused on assessing Samsat’s duties and functions through an evaluative framework encompassing four key process stages: (i) planning, (ii) coordination, (iii) guidance, and (iv) service task control. Findings reveal that Samsat Manado’s preventive measures against motor vehicle document forgery include: (a) conducting thorough document verification by cross-checking vehicle frame and engine numbers; (b) receiving and scrutinizing physical inspection outcomes to ensure consistency with vehicle documentation; and (c) selecting secure safety features in vehicle documents to hinder forgery attempts. In combating counterfeit document crimes, Samsat Manado undertakes the blocking of illegal motor vehicle documents. However, Samsat’s role is limited to reporting, as it does not possess investigative authority over counterfeit cases. Furthermore, Samsat maintains collaborative relations with the police, providing assistance upon request, particularly in completing vehicle registration files or serving as expert witnesses.

Keywords: Role, SAMSAT, Document Counterfeiting

ABSTRACT This study aims to determine insect pests on cayenne pepper (Capsicum frutescent L.) in Dunu Village, Monano District, North Gorontalo Regency, Gorontalo Province. This research was carried out for three months, from April to June 2021. The research method used was descriptive exploratory with 2 stages, namely sampling in the field and observations in the laboratory which were then presented in descriptive form in the form of tables, pictures, and graphs. Samples were obtained by catching using light traps and nets carried out for 6 consecutive days on 500 m2 area of cayenne pepper which was used as an experimental or observation area. The area consists of 1 light trap which is placed in the cayenne pepper plant and the lights are turned on every day from 18:00-06:00 WITA, then nets are used at 06:00-07:00 WITA and 16:00-18:00 WITA with the help of hands. Insects caught were taken and then observed the type and number of insects. Based on the results of research conducted, it showed that 8 types of insect pests were found, namely Nezara sp., Faneroptera sp., Gryllus sp., Acrida sp., Valanga sp., Bactocera sp., Circulifer sp., which belong to 4 orders and 6 families. The number of individuals found was 454 individuals, the highest was in the genus Nezara sp. namely 138 individuals and the lowest in the genus Gryllus sp. namely 11 individuals. Keyword : Insect, Pests, Cayenne pepper

ABSTRACT This research is entitled "Written Language Production of Student with Disgraphia in Faculty of Humanity Sam Ratulangi University". In this step, the writer reads the related theories of psycholinguistics in concern with language disorder, in this case dysgraphia. The second step is data collection. The writer gathers several students of English Student Association who are the participants of English debate and speech club, then examines them with the proper test suggested by Gvion and Friedman (2008:5). The third step is data analysis. The writer analyze the influences on the written language production of the student with dysgraphia by using the theories of Caplan (1992:192), Hatch (1983:1), Marcie dan Hecaen (1973:3), and Fanis dan Linda (2011:2). The results of this research show that dysgraphia is an impairment in writing which caused not only by the brain damaged but also by the cognitive and linguistic disorder. The student has a lexical dysgraphia. Dysgraphia also affects the written language production of the student orthographically. The student makes errors while writing, mostly the vowels. It does not affect his intelligent but his academic grade. Keywords : Psycholinguistics, Language Production, Language Disorder, Dysgraphia.

Indonesia has temperatures 24-32°C, air humidity 60-95% and low wind speeds. Thermally comfortable zone boundary is 24oC<T<26°C, 40% <RH<60%, 0,6<V<1,5m/s. This condition causing the climate of Indonesia becomes uncomfortable. Air conditioning system (AC) is needed to help maintain thermal comfort. The drawback using air conditioning is the wasteful energy use, can reach 60% of total building energy. The amount of electricity used by AC depends on the amount of heat that must be removed to produce cool air. This research aims to analyze the factors that affect the cooling load on the building and get a reference to the way reducing the cooling load, so that the use of electricity more effectively and efficiently. This research conducted by quantitative method with using a case study approach. The focus of research on the orientation of the building as well as the materials and construction techniques used in building walls. The data field collection in object research of Central Office Building of Manado State Polytechnic. Data processing and analysis using descriptive analysis. Data collection are divided on primary data that used in analysis, and secondary data that used as standards/ guidelines for analysis. The results are cooling load on the object of study largely derived from solar radiation heat that into the building, occurred because the building elongated facade orientation tends to block the paths of the sun. Affect the amount of solar radiation intensity received of the building. Most of the walls of buildings using glass and no horizontal exterior shading to protect the vertical rays, thus allowing direct solar radiation through the glass and into the building. The conclusions are that the biggest influenced on the cooling load in the Central Office Building of Manado State Polytechnic caused by the orientation of the building that allows the large amount of solar radiation touch the surface area of the glass. Cooling load reduction could be done in a way; make the horizontal exterior shading but it could change the look of the building facade, or improve the quality of glass within; replacing single glass with double glass or changing the type of glass material, or paste the window film on glass that could be rejected infrared rays. Keywords : cooling load, air conditioning system

This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of colored light traps as a sustainable and environmentally benign strategy for managing the rice pest Sitophilus oryzae L. A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed, incorporating five treatments with three replications each. The treatments consisted of LED light color traps: A) white, B) red, C) blue, D) yellow, E) green, and F) a control group utilizing a trap without any light source. The test subjects were adult (imago stage) S. oryzae individuals, with a total population of 150 specimens. Findings indicated that the white light trap captured the highest number of adult S. oryzae, averaging 52.33 individuals (34.88%), followed by yellow light traps at 37.0 individuals (24.67%), blue light traps at 24.0 individuals (16.00%), green light traps at 20.0 individuals (13.33%), and red light traps with the lowest capture rate of 13.33 individuals (8.88%). These results suggest that incandescent light traps, particularly those emitting white and yellow light, hold significant promise as an effective method for controlling populations of S. oryzae.  

Keywords: Environmentally friendly pest control; Colored light traps; Rice pest Sitophilus oryzae L.

Abstract:  
The teacher plays a pivotal role in the teaching and learning process. However, the assessment of teacher performance has not been fully optimized, partly due to the leadership role not functioning as anticipated. This study aims to examine the effects of leadership, self-efficacy, and organizational commitment on teacher performance. Employing a quantitative research design, the data were collected through observations, questionnaires, and literature reviews. The study population consisted of 63 teachers from Junior High School Negeri 7 Manado. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that self-efficacy, leadership, and organizational commitment significantly influence the performance of teachers at Junior High School Negeri 7 Manado. A correlation coefficient of r = 0.896 signifies a very strong and significant relationship between these variables and teacher performance. Additionally, the coefficient of determination (r² = 0.802) reveals that 80.2% of the variation in teacher performance at Junior High School Negeri 7 Manado can be explained by leadership, self-efficacy, and organizational commitment, with the remaining 19.8% attributed to other factors.  

Keywords: Leadership, Self-Efficacy, Organizational Commitment, Teacher Performance

The objective of this research is to analyze community perceptions on sporadic land registration services at the Land Office of North Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted from July to December 2019. The data used in this study were primary data and secondary data. Primary data were obtained directly from the source directly through interviews/questionnaire filling out, namely people who did sporadic land registration at the Land Office of North Minahasa Regency. Meanwhile, secondary data was obtained through literature and scientific work documents related to the object of this research. The method used in this research is descriptive quantitative method using data from samples obtained from the research population and analyzed and described using statistical methods. The data analysis method used is a Likert Scale. Determination of the sample was carried out by purposive sampling, with the consideration that those who were selected were truly those who could answer the question, namely the people themselves without the power of a notary who submitted applications for land registration sporadically, which amounted to 65 people. The research results showed that the public's perception of sporadic land registration services at the Land Office of North Minahasa Regency was based on 10 service principles, namely the principle of simplicity, clarity, certainty of time, accuracy, security, responsibility, completeness of infrastructure, ease of access, discipline, courtesy, friendliness and comfort. , using 27 question indicators, the result of interpretation is 6454 and the result of the percentage level is 73.54% with a "good" interpretation. This means that the public's perception of sporadic land registration services at the North Minahasa Regency Land Office has received a good category. Public perception when viewed from each service principle, almost all of them already have a good perception interpretation value. There is only one service principle whose perception interpretation value is "good enough", namely the public's perception of the ease of access with an average perception score of 194.5 and the result of a percentage level of perception of 59.84%. Although currently the public's perception of sporadic land registration services is good, the North Minahasa Regency Land Office still needs 26.46% to improve its services so as to obtain an ideal or very good level of public perception.

The present study aimed to evaluate the growth rate of Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) cultured using biofloc technology and to analyze the dynamics of various water quality parameters throughout the culture period. The experiment was conducted in the Laboratory of Aquaculture Technology, Faculty of Fisheries and Marine Sciences, Sam Ratulangi University (FPIK, UNSRAT). To promote biofloc development, the following substances were administered: 0.3 mL of EM-4 containing probiotic bacteria Lactobacillus casei and yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae; 15 mL of molasses; 0.5 g of yeast typically employed in soybean fermentation; and 12 g of dolomite. Each container was stocked with 60 Nile Tilapia fry, each weighing approximately 6 g. The fish were fed at an initial rate of 3% of the total biomass per day during the first week, which was subsequently reduced to 1% for the remainder of the culture period. Fish body weights were recorded on days 1, 15, and 30. Concurrently, water color changes and biofloc density were systematically monitored using an Imhoff cone.

Initial average fish weight was 6.00 g, which increased to 7.37 g after 15 days and reached 11.47 g by the conclusion of the experiment. The absolute growth of the fish was therefore 5.47 g, with a specific growth rate (SGR) of 9.1% and a daily growth rate (DGR) of 2.11%. Biofloc density peaked at 9.5 mL/L at the beginning of the second week, a value classified as very high, before declining to approximately 4 mL/L and stabilizing around 5 mL/L for the remainder of the study. Water temperature ranged between 26°C and 30°C. Ammonia concentrations remained low at 0.03 mg/L, whereas nitrite levels fluctuated between 0.15 and 3 mg/L, both within safe and acceptable ranges for biofloc systems. Nitrate concentrations varied from 4 to 55 mg/L, levels that, although relatively elevated for biofloc environments, did not pose a threat to fish health.

Keywords: Biofloc, Nile Tilapia, growth performance, floc density, water quality

ABSTRACT

Agricultural development fundamentally seeks to enhance production to achieve self-sufficiency. To fulfill these goals, the introduction of innovations that augment agricultural output is essential. Nutrients play a critical role in supporting agricultural productivity. This study employed a survey methodology combined with laboratory analyses. Livestock manure samples were collected from two distinct locations: the highlands and lowlands, with one sample obtained from each site. The parameters observed included pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and organic carbon content. The findings indicated variation in nutrient composition of cow dung across the sampling sites. The highest organic carbon content was recorded at the Tomohon site, measuring 10.42%, whereas the lowest was observed in Kalasey Village, at 8.69%. Regarding total nitrogen (N-total), the maximum concentration was found in the lowland area (Kalasey) at 0.88%, while the minimum was noted in Tomohon at 0.68%. For total phosphorus (P-total), the greatest value was 0.34% in Tomohon, classified within the moderate range, whereas the lowest, 0.22%, was detected in Kalasey, categorized as low. Potassium (K2O) content was highest in the cow dung from the lowlands (Kalasey 1) at 0.56%, with the lowest value of 0.36% identified in Tomohon. Additionally, the Tomohon plateau exhibited elevated moisture content, attributed to its history as a former paddy field zone.

Keywords: Nutrients, cow dung, organic fertilizer

This qualitative study aims to evaluate the performance of the Manado City Social and Community Empowerment Agency in managing homelessness within Manado City, employing performance indicators as outlined by Dwiyanto: productivity, service quality, responsiveness, responsibility, and accountability. Data were collected primarily through interviews and supplemented with secondary sources, including records from the Manado Social Service and articles from local newspapers. The research involved seven informants, comprising two employees from the Manado City Social Service, three homeless individuals residing in Manado, and two observers familiar with the daily experiences of the homeless population. Qualitative research is deployed and using exploratory research to define the nature of Micro and Small Enterprises in Manado and using Descriptive-Study Case approach. The results of this research shows marketing & promotion, human resources & structure of the firm, technology & capital, product & services, financial resources, external environment and entrepreneurial readiness are the success factors while limited resources, mastery of Information & Technology, marketing, business license & legality, and labors become the challenges and problems of Micro and Small Enterprises in Manado. Keywords: micro and small enterprises, success factors, problems and challenges

The purpose of this study was to use rainwater, ketapang leaves and kepok banana peels as a culture medium for mosquito larvae 1 mm. Rainwater was filtered using fine sand, small gravel, large gravel, GAC (Granular Activated Carbon) and zeolite. As treatments for mosquito larvae culture media are: treatment A: 3 liters of filtered rainwater, 50 grams of green ketapang leaves and 1 kepok banana peel; treatment B: 3 liters of filtered rain water, 50 grams of yellow ketapang leaves and 1 kepok banana peel; treatment C: 3 liters of filtered rain water, 50 grams of red ketapang leaves and 1 kepok banana peel; treatment D: 3 liters of filtered rainwater, 50 grams of brown ketapang leaves and 1 kepok banana peel, treatment E: 3 liters of filtered rainwater, and treatment F: 3 liters of well water. Mosquito larvae were harvested on size of 1 mm. Measurement of water quality parameters is temperature and pH. The results of the analysis of variance showed that the difference in media had a significant effect (p-value < α) on the cultivation of 1 mm mosquito larvae. Culture of mosquito larvae on 3 liters of rainwater, 50 grams of green ketapang leaves and 1 kepok banana peel gave the best results based on the Tukey test. The results of water quality parameters for temperature were 28°C and pH 6.

This study, entitled "Quantifiers in the Novel *Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children* by Ransom Riggs," was conducted to fulfill the requirements for the completion of a Bachelor’s degree in the English Department, Faculty of Letters, Sam Ratulangi University. The primary objectives of this research are to identify, classify, and analyze the quantifiers found within the novel *Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children* by Ransom Riggs, focusing on their function, category, and form. Employing a descriptive methodology, the analysis is grounded in the theoretical framework proposed by Flor Aarts and Jan Aarts in *English Syntactic Structure: Function and Categories in Sentence Analysis*. The findings reveal that three forms of quantifiers appear in the novel: simple, compound, and complex. From a functional perspective, quantifiers in the text exhibit multiple roles. At the sentence or clause level, quantifiers function as subjects, subject attributes, predicator complements, direct objects, indirect objects, and adverbials. Within the phrase level, quantifiers serve variously as the head of noun phrases, both as heads and determiners of noun phrases, solely as determiners, and occasionally as post-modifiers of noun phrases. Illustrative examples of English quantifiers include terms such as someone, somebody, something, anyone, anybody, everyone, everybody, no one, none, some, any, each, all, both, either, few, little, every, and no, among others.

**Keywords:** function, category, form, novel, *Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children*

The telecommunications sector in Indonesia has undergone significant expansion in recent years. Mobile phones have transitioned from being considered luxury items to essential devices widely utilized across all age groups. This advancement is closely linked to the presence of cellular service providers, as the diverse features offered by mobile phone manufacturers would be ineffectual without the supporting infrastructure provided by these service providers. Among the newer entrants in this market, the cellular service provider "3" operating in Manado has steadily enhanced its service offerings and attracted a growing customer base. The objective of this study is to investigate the consumer purchasing behavior associated with "3" in Manado, focusing on the variables of price, quality, advertising, and brand awareness. Employing a multiple regression analysis framework, the study examines a sample of 100 users of "3" in the Manado region. The findings reveal that price, quality, and brand awareness significantly impact consumer purchasing behavior, with price identified as the most influential factor. Conversely, advertising was found to have no significant effect on purchasing decisions for the "3" cellular service provider. 

Keywords: price, quality, advertisement, brand awareness, consumer purchasing behavior

Advancements in industrial work are closely intertwined with the utilization of computers. However, prolonged computer use has been associated with various health issues, which are recognized as occupational diseases. Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS) encompasses a range of ocular and non-ocular symptoms that manifest following extended computer work. Surveys conducted in the United States and the United Kingdom indicate that 12.4% and 9% of individuals experiencing CVS, respectively, sought hospital care for eye examinations. Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), a condition affecting the hand, substantially impairs daily activities. The prevalence of CTS in adults is approximately 10%, with females exhibiting a threefold greater susceptibility compared to males. This study aims to examine the health implications of computer use among employees of CIMB Bank. Employing a descriptive and qualitative research design, the study involved 20 computer-using employees as informants. Findings revealed that not all participants were aware of the ocular side effects associated with computer use during work. Similarly, less than half of the informants possessed knowledge regarding the impact of computer use on hand health. 

Keywords: knowledge, behavior, employees, health effects of computer use

This research seeks to analyze the distribution of credit funds within the Partnership Program managed by culinary business partners affiliated with PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia Tbk in the Manado Region. The study’s respondents comprised all culinary business partners participating in the program. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in this investigation. Primary data were collected through direct interviews conducted with 14 foster partners, using a structured questionnaire. Meanwhile, secondary data were sourced from the PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia Tbk office in the Manado Region and supplemented by electronic books, journal articles, and theses obtained via Google Scholar that pertain to the topic of credit allocation within the Partnership Program. Descriptive statistical methods served as the primary analytical tool for this study. The findings reveal that the Partnership Credit Program funds were predominantly allocated to non-productive uses, specifically within the consumptive sector, encompassing household expenditures such as children’s education costs, home renovations, purchasing televisions, and savings. Specifically, 42.18% of the credit was directed toward productive purposes, 27.75% toward consumptive needs, and 30.07% was allocated to savings. These percentages correspond to a total loan disbursement of Rp. 369,000,000 distributed among the 14 culinary business partners evaluated.
