The advancement of science and technology has led to numerous novel discoveries across various domains. Among these technological innovations is the emergence of online games, which are electronic and visually-based interactive entertainment forms conducted via digital visual media. The use of online games is closely intertwined with individual attitudes, moral values, and language usage. For many students, online games serve as an alternative recreational activity during periods of boredom or fatigue resulting from academic study. However, these games inadvertently exert both positive and negative influences on players, including their motivation to engage in academic pursuits at the collegiate level.

This research seeks to explore the impacts of online gaming on the learning motivation of students enrolled in the Department of Sociology within the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through methods such as observation, interviews, and documentation. The analytical framework applied in this study is grounded in Max Weber's theory of social action.

Findings indicate that online games exert significant influence primarily when engagement is unidimensional; that is, when gaming activities are not balanced with meaningful, value-driven pursuits, the effects tend to be predominantly negative, particularly among students. While students may possess high academic competence, excessive prioritization of gaming over primary academic responsibilities adversely affects their motivation to learn.

Keywords: Impact; Online games; Learning motivation

THE EFFECT OF FALSE MOUNTING ON SEMEN QUALITY OF LIMOUSIN AND SIMMENTAL BULL IN LEMBANG ARTIFICAL INSEMINATION CENTER. The purpose of this study was to determine the effect of false mounting on the quality of Limosin and Simental bull semen at the Lembang Artificial Insemination Center. The 55 individu of Limousin and 55 Simmental bull aging 5-9 years old have been used in thos study. The data have been collected directly in the Artificial Insemination Center Lembang - West Java Province. The data obtained in the form of macroscopic and microscopic observations on Limousin and Simmental bull include volume, pH, mass movement, spermatozoa motility and spermatozoa concentration. Data were analyzed descriptively by calculating the standard deviations, correlations coefficients and the T test. The variables measured in this study were macroscopic and microscopic quality of semen. The results of this study indicate that the effect of false mounting on the average semen volume of Limousin and Simmental bull is maximum at 3, 4, and 5 times false mounting but there was not significantly difference between the amount of false mounting, as well as the average volume, pH, mass movement, motility of spemetozoa and concentration spermatozoa are not significantly different. It was concluded that false mounting in Limousin and Simmental bulls in Lembang Artificial Insemination Center had no significantly effect on the quality of macroscopic and microscopic semen. Keywords: False Mounting, Cement Quality, Limousin Cattle, Simmental Cows.

Purple sweet potato is recognized as a valuable food ingredient due to its favorable nutritional composition, particularly in terms of carbohydrates, minerals, and vitamins. Converting purple sweet potato into flour serves as an effective method for its storage and preservation. "Semprong" cakes, commonly marketed in plastic packaging, are typically produced using various flours and exhibit diverse flavors and colors. The availability of multiple "semprong" cake variants indicates the potential for incorporating different ingredients, such as purple sweet potato flour, into the formulation. This study aims to develop a high-quality "semprong" cake by optimally blending purple sweet potato flour with wheat flour, guided by panelists' sensory preferences and the product's nutritional attributes. Employing a Completely Randomized Design (CRD), the treatments comprised of five flour blends: A (10% purple sweet potato flour and 90% wheat flour), B (30% purple sweet potato flour and 70% wheat flour), C (50% purple sweet potato flour and 50% wheat flour), D (70% purple sweet potato flour and 30% wheat flour), and E (90% purple sweet potato flour and 10% wheat flour). Sensory evaluation revealed that the formulation containing 10% purple sweet potato flour and 90% wheat flour (treatment A) was most preferred in terms of color, taste, aroma, and texture. Proximate analysis of the resulting "semprong" cakes indicated moisture content ranging from 3.16% to 3.77%, ash content from 1.32% to 2.09%, fat content between 16.26% and 20.95%, protein content from 7.06% to 8.95%, and carbohydrate content spanning 66.31% to 71.21%.  
Keywords: Semprong Cake, Purple Sweet Potato Flour, Wheat Flour

An experiment was conducted to examine the effectiveness of curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb and curcuma zedoria Rosc flours added in Ration on High density lipoprotein (HDL), low density lipoprotein (LDL) and the viscera of broiler. Fifty-four of broiler CP 707® strain were used in this experiment and they were placed into cages (60cm x 45cm x 45cm), 3 birds per cage. There were 18 bulb lamp of 25 watt above each cages. Randomized completely design were used in this experiment; 3 treatments and 6 repetitions. The three treatments were R0 (ration without Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb and Curcuma zedoria Rosc flours ration with), R1 (ration with 2% of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb flours added in ration, and R2 (2% of Curcuma zedoria Rosc flours). The blood HDL level of broilers in this experiment were 133,58mg/dl (R0), 113,33mg/dl (R2) and 109mg/dl (R1), respectively. The blood LDL level of broiler were 45,66mg/dl (R0), 56,33mg/dl (R2) and 64,66mg/dl (R1), respectively. By using Chi square test, it showed that, there was a relations of addition of 2% of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb and Curcuma zedoria Rosc flours in ration with blood HDL level. However, there was not a relation of addition of 2% of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb and Curcuma zedoria Rosc flour in ration with blood LDL level. In short, the addition of 2% of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb and Curcuma zedoria Rosc flours in ration were not efectively increased the level of HDL and not efectively decreased the level of LDL in blood. Furthermore, the percentage of gizard weight, percentage of pancreas weight, percentage of small and large intestine weight of broiler in this experiment were not significantly different between treatments (P>0,05).

The identity of the Toraja people is intrinsically linked to their enduring cultural heritage, which continues to thrive to the present day. Symbolism and meaning are integral components of Toraja life, prominently exemplified by the tau-tau statues employed in their death rituals. The creation of tau-tau serves as a vital element within the Toraja burial tradition. Notably, the caste system persists among the Toraja, whereby only individuals of noble status are commemorated through tau-tau. These statues function as memorials, enabling the bereaved families to honor and remember the deceased. Furthermore, tau-tau represent a form of respect from both family members and the wider community, recognizing the contributions of the deceased during their lifetime. The tradition of tau-tau originates from Alukta, the ancestral code of conduct governing Torajan life, and has been transmitted through generations to the present era. Artistically, tau-tau possess considerable value due to their lifelike resemblance to the individuals they portray. These statues also adorn the tombs of Toraja nobility and are frequently encountered in the region’s natural tourist sites. Typically, tau-tau are arranged in front of the patane—graveyard structures resembling houses—and are neatly positioned against stone walls or cliffs. To prevent theft by art collectors, these statues are often grouped together and securely fastened. The tau-tau thus constitute an indispensable element of Toraja cultural customs, and their elimination would equate to the loss of the tribe’s cultural authenticity.  

Keywords: Tau-tau, Symbols, Cultural Significance

Abstract: The stock market is all about dynamics and that is why investors and fund managers have always been confronted with the problem of accurately predicting the stock prices so as to earn decent returns. Investment in shares offers the benefit of liquidity as well as the opportunity to beat the market and earn high returns. However, the task of predicting share prices is far from simple. Share price movement is not independent in nature and both intrinsic, as well as extrinsic factors, have been established to exercise influence over stock price movements. The purpose of this research is to analyze factors influencing stock price of the banking sector in the Indonesian Stock Exchange index. The objects of this research are banking stocks that are listed in Indonesia Stock Exchange. This research is an explorative study and uses a quantitative method which utilizes technical analysis and t-test as the tool of analysis. The research results show that the upward movement of banking stocks happened in the year 2008 and the factor influencing this movement is the increase in interest rate announcement by Bank Indonesia. Recommendation derived from this research is for investors and fund managers to give more attention towards announcement and interest rate of a sector in the country in their investment portfolio.Keywords: stock price, interest rate, political effects, economic effects

This study aims to evaluate the performance of the Regional Personnel Agency in the recruitment process of civil apparatus. Employing a qualitative methodology, the research framework is guided by Gibson's criteria, which include effectiveness, efficiency, accountability, and justice. The informants involved in this study consist of the Head of BK Service (1 individual), the Secretary of BKD (1 individual), three BKD employees, and five CPNS applicants. Data collection was conducted through semi-structured interviews, and the data were analyzed using an interactive model analysis technique.

The findings indicate that the performance of the Waropen Regency administration, specifically the Regional Personnel Agency of Waropen Regency, is suboptimal when assessed against the indicators of effectiveness, efficiency, accountability, and justice. Based on these results, the study proposes several recommendations: (1) the Waropen Regency Government, particularly the Regional Personnel Agency, should enhance its overall performance; (2) it is imperative to preserve and strengthen the integrity and ethical standards within the BKD, especially concerning the attitudes and consistent fulfillment of responsibilities to ensure successful implementation of work programs; (3) mechanisms of accountability should be further developed to secure public trust and uphold governmental authority at the community level; and (4) professionalism should be maintained rigorously to ensure that the process of recruiting civil servant candidates remains free from any indications of bias.

Keywords: Performance, Governmental Apparatus, Recruitment, Civil Service, Regional Personnel Agency

ABSTRACT

The present study, entitled "Obsesi Lara Cameron dalam Novel *The Star Shine Down* Karya Sidney Sheldon," fulfills a requirement for obtaining the Sarjana degree at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University Manado. This research aims to analyze the obsessive tendencies exhibited by the protagonist, Lara Cameron, as she pursues her goals through unconventional means, which ultimately result in her developing obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). The disorder in question significantly impacts her life, leading to noticeable alterations in her personality. The theoretical framework employed comprises Wellek and Werren’s extrinsic approach alongside psychological theories pertaining to obsession. Utilizing a descriptive method, this study analyzes data derived from the novel itself as well as from relevant scholarly articles. The findings reveal that Lara Cameron displays both obsessive-compulsive disorder and obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD). Specifically, Lara's obsessions manifest in two primary areas: her professional life and her romantic involvement with a man. These obsessions have consequential effects, contributing to the development of OCPD, characterized by a relentless pursuit of perfection, high standards, and a propensity to impose these exacting demands on others, often resulting in interpersonal difficulties. Additionally, Lara's obsession with the man engenders jealousy within her character. 

Keywords: Obsession, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD), Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder (OCPD), *The Star Shine Down* (novel)

This study seeks to (1) identify the production factors that influence copra output and (2) assess the elasticity of these production factors among copra farmers in the West Tomohon District. The research was carried out between January and April 2017. Primary data were collected through surveys involving direct observation and interviews with copra farmers. The data were analyzed employing the Cobb-Douglas production function model. Findings revealed that, collectively, the factors of planting area, plant population, labor input, equipment quantity, and farmer experience significantly impact copra production in the Tomohon Barat Sub-district. Individually, however, only the planting area, plant population, and labor input demonstrated statistically significant and positive effects on copra production. The scale analysis indicated increasing returns to scale, suggesting that farmers are able to enhance profitability by augmenting the input of production factors. Regarding the elasticity estimates, planting area, plant population, and labor exhibited positive elasticities greater than one, implying inefficient utilization since maximum profit levels have not yet been attained. Incremental increases in these inputs corresponded to proportionally greater increases in copra yield. Conversely, the production factors of equipment quantity and farmer experience yielded negative elasticities, signifying inefficiencies whereby additional inputs led to a reduction in copra output.

Background: COVID-19 is an infectious disease affecting the digestive tract, characterized by high morbidity and mortality rates due to its rapid transmission. Preventive measures include adherence to health protocols, among which hand hygiene plays a critical role. 

Objective: This study aims to examine the differences in vigilance behavior related to COVID-19 transmission before and after implementing a 6-step handwashing health education intervention among members of Aisyiyah during the New Normal era.

Methods: A quasi-experimental study employing a time series design was conducted in August 2020 with a total population of 31 participants from the Aisyiyah community. All members were sampled using a total sampling method. Behavioral changes were analyzed through bivariate analysis and further evaluated using the Cochran test, followed by Post Hoc McNemar tests to assess the significance of differences at three time points.

Results: The bivariate analysis revealed statistically significant improvements in COVID-19 transmission vigilance behaviors following the 6-step handwashing education, with a p-value of 0.000. Significant differences were observed between pre- and post-intervention handwashing behaviors (p = 0.000), as well as between pre-intervention and one month after education. These findings were substantiated through Cochran’s test and subsequent Post Hoc McNemar analysis confirming significant behavioral changes across the three measurement intervals.

Conclusion: The provision of health education on the 6-step handwashing technique significantly enhances individuals’ preventive behaviors against COVID-19 transmission. Repeated observations are necessary to sustain and reinforce the positive behavioral changes achieved.

Keywords: COVID-19; handwashing; health education

ABSTRACT THE VALUE OF NITROGEN RETENTION AND METABOLIZABLE ENERGY OF BROILER DIETS WITH MUSTARD MEAL (Brassica rapa L. subsp. pekinensis) This research was conducted to determine the value of nitrogen retention (NR) and nitrogen corrected metabolizable energy value (AMEn) of broiler diets containing waste of mustard meal. The interrelation between literature and society is inseparable, functioning as two complementary aspects of a single entity. Literature serves as a medium through which authors portray societal conditions and social contexts. It acts as a representation of life itself, illustrating or mirroring human experiences; thus, the subject matter of literature encompasses the diverse experiences of individuals and society (Wellek and Warren, 1949:89). Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice stands as one of her most distinguished works, focusing on themes of relationships, life, and love. Austen is renowned for her astute and precise depiction of British social life, particularly during the early nineteenth century. The manner in which Austen crafts Pride and Prejudice not only as a literary masterpiece but also as an authentic reflection of early nineteenth-century British society warrants thorough examination.

This study aims to: (1) identify, analyze, and elucidate how Pride and Prejudice portrays the social life and circumstances of early nineteenth-century British society; and (2) investigate and describe the depiction of social stratification within the novel. The analysis employs a sociological framework, drawing upon Aristotle’s mimetic theory, the theoretical perspectives on the relationship between sociology and literature as articulated by Wellek and Warren, and Max Weber’s theory of social stratification.

Pride and Prejudice offers a nuanced and realistic depiction of British social life during this period, utilizing devices such as correspondence to represent communication and ballroom dance parties to epitomize social interaction. Furthermore, through its thematic concerns, the novel highlights the prevailing social realities, including the societal perception of marriage as the paramount aspiration for women, the intrinsic value attributed to marriage, and the prescribed virtues expected of women.

In addition, the novel intricately portrays social stratification as conceptualized by Weber, wherein status, class, and power are essential components for attaining certain social positions. Various characters in Pride and Prejudice exemplify these dimensions, thereby manifesting Weberian social stratification within the narrative.

Keywords: Pride and Prejudice, sociological analysis, social stratification, literature-society nexus.

This study aims to evaluate the effects of public housing development policies in Sea Village, Minahasa Regency. Employing a descriptive-cumulative methodology, the research involved key informants including the village head, local residents, and community leaders. Data were analyzed using the interactive model developed by Miles and Huberman. The findings reveal several significant outcomes: (1) The housing development policies have yielded a positive influence on public welfare and the targeted community by facilitating access to affordable housing loans in locations that are convenient, safe, and comfortable. Importantly, these policies have not generated adverse effects on community security and comfort, although unintended negative consequences have been observed in the form of reduced agricultural land and community forestry areas. (2) The policies have also positively affected the economic and social conditions within Sea Village, demonstrated by increased household incomes and enhanced social progress, including improvements in education, community activities, social engagement, and participation in developmental initiatives. (3) Furthermore, the policies have contributed positively to the present and projected advancement of both the village and its community. (4) Lastly, the implementation of housing development policies has not imposed additional direct or indirect financial burdens on the community related to the construction process.  
Keywords: Policy Impact, Housing Development

ABSTRACT This research entitled "Enhancing Students' Speaking Skill Through the Use of Storytelling Technique". This study aims to identify, analyze, and describe the implementation of storytelling techniques in enhancing students English speaking skill. The use of storytelling technique besides make students enjoy the learning processes, but also develop their love in culture through the teaching material Toar and Lumimuut stories in "Written English IV: From the Local Perception of Minahasan Folklore" writted by Warouw (2019). The object of this research is class VIA, SD Kr. Eben Haezar 1 Manado. The theory of Nunan (1991) speaking, Haven (2000) storytelling, and Burns (2010) classroom action research are used to identify and analyze the data, and Sudaryanto's (1993) qualitative method used to describe the data. Classroom action research method used to find out the phenomenon in the process of children's learning activities in class from the begining until the end of the meeting, divisible into 2 cycles. Each of cycle has four stages: planning, action, observation and reflection. In cycle 1, the writer applied the storytelling techniques in 3 differences learning activities, such as: Pre-lesson activities (opening activities), Main lesson activities (core activities), and Post-lesson activities (closing activities). In cycle 2, the writer applies the learning process to students by modifying the learning activities using the picture series technique. In this research to enhance student speaking skill, writer also obtained the results from observation and tests. From observation, storytelling techniques can be used in classroom to train students for loving their own culture, to make them creative and innovative person. Furthemore, develop student's speaking skill and their confidence in using English language. From tests, the significant increase for the result of students', pre-test total 45 points, cycle 1 total 135 points, cycle 2 total 164 points, and post-test total 251 points.Keyword: Storytelling Technique, Speaking Skill, and Classroom Action Research.

ABSTRACT In North Sulawesi, there are several major insect pests of rice plants, one of which is green leafhoppers which often cause damage to the rice crop. Aside from being a green planthopper pests also act as an insect vector that can transmit the disease Tungro. The study aims to determine the intensity of pest populations of green leafhoppers N. virescens on rice crops in West Tomohon sub district. The research was conducted in two villages namely Tara-tara and Woloan in the District of West Tomohon Tomohon. The research was conducted from December 2014 through April 2015. This study used a survey method in two villages, namely Tara-tara and Woloan West Tomohon sub district Tomohon. The results showed that the population of green leafhopper pest Nephoettix virescens on rice crops in the district of West Tomohon, Tomohon, is highest in sub Tara tara on observations II, as many as 8.5 tails and lowest in sub Woloan on observations IV, namely 2.3 tail. In general, the population of planthoppers in paddy rice crops in the district of West Tomohon, Tomohon highest average of Tara-tara Village, which is 5.8 tails Woloan Village only 4.9 tails. The intensity of the green leafhopper pest N. virescens on rice crops in the district of West Tomohon, Tomohon, is highest in sub Tara-tara on observations IV, amounting to 29.83 % and the lowest in the sub Woloan the first observation, namely 9.83 %. In general, the intensity of plant hopper pest on rice crops in the district of West Tomohon Tomohon highest average in Tara-tara Village, which is 24.89 % and Woloan Village only 14.89 %. Keyword : Freen Planthopper Nephotettix virescens, Paddy, Tomohon

The openness of information between countries around the world is easier in this Globalization era, one country can share information through the internet as well as the economic condition of a country. A study about how is the influence of DJIA and NIKKEI 225 towards the JCI during 2011 to 2016 may help to identify the factors that make these indices related. The study aims to analyze the change of DJIA and NIKKEI 225 may influence the JCI during 2011 to 2016. The methodology used explanatory research which studying a situation to explain the relationship between variables. The sample used is the index historical data during 2011 to 2016 of the indices. The data analysis method using Granger's Causality test with Vector Auto Regressive basis analyzed in EViews 9. The study found that there is no significant influence of DJIA towards the movements of JCI during 2011 to 2016, and NIKKEI 225 was significantly influenced the JCI in the period. There are several factors affecting these results such as trade ties between these countries, currency, foreign exchange reserve and the investment grade which affecting investors investment decision. For further research, the author recommend to add other global indices variables. Keywords: Stock Market, DJIA, NIKKEI 225, JCI, IHSG, Vector Auto Regressive, Granger's Causality, Indonesia Stock Exchange.

Self-image refers to the perception individuals hold about themselves as human beings, encompassing their inner essence and identity. Often, people form judgments about their self-image based on external factors such as the attire and accessories they use. Moreover, self-image encompasses one’s feelings regarding personal appearance, with diverse criteria employed by individuals to evaluate their own self-perception. This study aims to examine the self-image of female consumers who use Korean skincare products in Manado. To achieve this objective, data were collected from ten respondents through qualitative methods, specifically in-depth interviews, employing purposive and snowball sampling techniques. The findings indicate that the self-image of female users has improved positively as a result of using Korean skincare products. Participants reported that the products met their expectations and complemented their needs, attributing value to the products due to their predominantly natural ingredients. Overall, respondents expressed favorable opinions about the influence of these foreign products on their self-image. It is recommended that consumers develop awareness of their self-image and the factors that motivate their use of Korean skincare products, as well as the elements that contribute to the enhancement of their self-perception.  

Keywords: self-image, female consumers, Korean skincare products

This study was conducted at the Beriman Market (Pasar Beriman) in Tomohon City with the objective of examining the influence of perceptions, attitudes, and the number of household members on the consumption of python snake meat among consumers. Employing a survey methodology and purposive sampling techniques, data were analyzed using Pearson Correlation analysis. The findings revealed that perceptions and python meat consumption exhibited a negative but statistically insignificant correlation. Similarly, attitudes toward python meat consumption demonstrated a negative yet insignificant association. Additionally, the number of family members was found to have a negative and non-significant relationship with the consumption of python meat. Collectively, these results suggest that perceptions, attitudes, and household size do not significantly affect the level of python meat consumption among consumers in the Beriman Market of Tomohon City.

Sausage produced from spent hen meat represents an alternative processed protein product of animal origin. This study aimed to determine the optimal formulation of culled laying hen sausage incorporating a mixture of carrot paste and baruk sago as fillers and to assess the resulting physical, chemical, and functional attributes of the sausage. The experimental design comprised five treatment groups varying in the proportion of carrot paste within a total filler content of 25%, specifically at 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% carrot paste. Findings revealed that the inclusion of carrot paste in the filler significantly enhanced (P < 0.05) physical properties, notably increasing sausage tenderness and reducing cooking shrinkage. Chemical analyses demonstrated significant effects on moisture, protein, fat, and carbohydrate levels, whereas ash content remained unaffected. Additionally, β-carotene concentration in the sausage correspondingly increased with higher carrot paste ratios in the filler blend. Sensory evaluation indicated that the proportion of carrot paste significantly influenced flavor and texture but did not appreciably affect color or aroma. Among the formulations tested, the mixture containing 10% carrot paste and 15% baruk sago (P2) achieved the highest mean scores from panelists. The compositional analysis of the P2 formulation revealed moisture, ash, protein, fat, carbohydrate, and β-carotene contents of 60.63%, 1.82%, 15.72%, 12.24%, 8.25%, and 0.04%, respectively.  

Keywords: sausage, culled laying hens, carrot, baruk sago, physicochemical properties, sensory evaluation

This study aims to find out how the perceptions of the peasant community towards the tradition of rambu solo / traditional funeral in Marinding Village. This study lasted for 4 (four) months starting from April 2018 to July 2018 in Marinding Village, Mengkendek Sub-district, Tana Toraja Regency. The data collection method used is primary data collected through direct interviews with the community members and secondary data obtained from the Marinding Village Office. The sampling method used the purposive sampling method. The number of respondents is 15 people. Data analysis used was descriptive analysis. The results showed that there were two types of perceptions from the farmers community towards the tradition of rambu solo / traditional funeral in Marinding Village, Mengkendek Sub-district, Tana Toraja District, namely not supporting and supporting. There are 8 out of 15 respondents who do not support the rambu solo tradition because it is considered a waste that costs very large and expensive and is often for showing their social status in the community. But there is also support in which 7 out of 15 respondents support this tradition because the tradition of the rambu solo tradition reflects the life of the Toraja people who like togetherness and family. In addition, the implementation of solo signs opened up markets and huge profits for the rice farmers, coffee, and cattleman, especially for buffalos and pigs, because they could sell their all agricultural products to people who carried out rambu solo tradition which were usually carried out after the harvest period.*eprm*.

UTILIZATION OF GOROHO BANANA PEEL FLOUR (Musa acuminafe, L) IN RATION ON EGG PRODUCTION PERFORMANCE OF LAYING HENS. The objective of this study was to evaluate the utilization goroho banana peel flour (Musa acuminafe, L) in ration on production performance of laying hens (strain of MB 402). Total of 100 laying hens (strain of MB 402) at the age of 36 weeks old were used in this study. Treatments were using basal ration without goroho banana peel flour (R0), basal ration of 98% added with goroho banana peel flour of 2% (R1), basal ration of 96% added with goroho banana peel flour of 4% (R2), basal ration of 94% added with goroho banana peel flour of 6% (R3), and basal ration of 92% added with goroho banana peel flour of 8% (R4). Each treatment was replicated in to 5 replications. Variables measured were including feed consumption (g/head/day), egg production (%), and feed conversion. Completely randomized design was applied the research method with Duncan's multiple range test for the significance treatments affecting variables. Results showed that utilization goroho banana peel flour (Musa acuminafe, L) in ration did not significantly affect on feed consumption, egg production and feed conversion. Therefore, it can be concluded that utilization goroho banana peel flour (Musa acuminafe, L) in ration up to 8 percents might be applied in ration of laying hens (strain of MB 402). Keywords: Egg production, performance, goroho banana peel flour, laying hens

This study aimed to assess the length and diameter growth of the coral species Acropora formosa cultivated from varying initial seed sizes in Talengen Bay, Tabukan District, Sangihe Island Regency. Data collection occurred over the period from May to June 2016. A Completely Randomized Design was employed, comprising three treatment groups with three replications per treatment. The seed sizes used as treatments were categorized as follows: A (5 cm), B (7 cm), and C (10 cm). The experiment utilized a bench system measuring 60 x 60 cm², with coral seeds sourced from the natural environment surrounding the study site. Growth measurements and water quality parameters were recorded biweekly. The findings indicated that the greatest absolute length growth was observed in treatment A, with an average increment of 0.70 cm, followed by treatment C (0.46 cm), and treatment B exhibiting the least growth (0.45 cm). Similarly, the largest increase in coral diameter was noted in treatment A (0.05 cm), with treatments C and B both averaging 0.03 cm. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences in either absolute length growth or diameter among the treatments. Overall, Acropora formosa cultivated from seeds of differing initial lengths in Talengen Bay demonstrated favorable growth, characterized by a more rapid increase in length relative to diameter expansion.

Keywords: Acropora formosa, absolute growth, Talengen Bay

This study seeks to (1) identify and critically evaluate the strategic priority issues associated with tourism in Bolaang Mongondow Regency, (2) examine, assess, and analyze the environmental impacts of the Regional Spatial Planning (RTRW) Program for tourism designation within Bolaang Mongondow Regency, and (3) review the measures implemented to mitigate the adverse effects resulting from the execution of the tourism designation program in this district. The research was carried out in Bolaang Mongondow Regency, located in North Sulawesi Province, during the period from September to October 2017. Employing a purposive sampling technique, the study utilized a semi-detailed approach grounded in field observations, Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and key informant interviews. Primary data were collected through interviews with key informants and the facilitation of FGDs. The findings reveal that (1) the foremost strategic issues pertaining to the tourism designation area include challenges related to biodiversity conservation, waste management, disruptions to security and comfort, enhancement of community welfare, and the degradation of mangrove and coral reef ecosystems; (2) the tourism designation program has positively contributed to increased local prosperity through the creation of business opportunities in the vicinity of tourism sites, whereas negative effects encompass threats to biodiversity, waste accumulation, security and comfort disturbances, as well as damage to mangrove forests and coral reefs; and (3) mitigation strategies to alleviate these negative impacts include the enactment of local regulations aimed at protecting biodiversity around tourism areas, the establishment of facilities for shelter and the treatment of solid and liquid waste generated by tourism activities, the deployment of security personnel and disaster management teams in tourism zones, and the implementation of local regulatory measures to restrict diving and coastal tourism activities in order to reduce harm to mangrove and coral reef habitats.

PT. Pegadaian (Persero) UPC Ratahan operates as a non-bank financial institution serving the public by providing credit loans secured by collateral. It is imperative that the collateral remains in good condition when returned to customers. Consequently, PT. Pegadaian (Persero) UPC Ratahan must implement robust internal control mechanisms governing the acceptance and return of collateral. This study aims to assess the application of internal control procedures related to collateral handling at PT. Pegadaian (Persero) UPC Ratahan, specifically evaluating their alignment with the five components of the COSO framework. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study’s findings indicate that the internal controls in place meet satisfactory standards. However, certain deficiencies were identified during the transaction process; notably, upon completion of transactions, collateral items were not immediately stored and recorded but were instead temporarily placed in drawers or on desks. Additionally, the organizational structure did not fully optimize the division of responsibilities, as managerial personnel concurrently performed the roles of warehouse clerk and estimator. It is recommended that PT. Pegadaian (Persero) UPC Ratahan enhance its organizational structure by increasing staffing levels and ensure that collateral items are promptly recorded and stored immediately upon receipt and evaluation.

Keywords: mortgage, internal control, collateral

The land has limited characteristics or does not increase and it is inversely proportional to the increasing demand for land use. In the RTRW of Bolaang Mongondow Regency in 2014 2034, Lolak District is designated as the center of an urban area (PKWp) which is sure to have a lot of development activities. So that changes in land use such as land that was originally undeveloped into the land that is built are definitely unavoidable. The purpose of this study is to analyze land capability and analyze land-use changes and provide land use direction. The method used in this research is a descriptive quantitative approach and spatial analysis using ArcGIS. The results showed that the land capability of Lolak District was divided into 5 (five) classes, namely very low development ability, low development ability, medium development ability, rather high development ability, and high development ability. The land capability that dominates Lolak District is the very low development capacity with a total area of 31,080.7 ha or 66% of the total area. During a period of 12 years (2009 - 2021) in Lolak Subdistrict, there was a significant increase in the area of residential land and activity sites of 664.7 ha due to the presence of the PT Semen CONCH factory in Solog Village and the construction of the Lolak Dam in Pindol Village which was followed by a decrease in area natural forest land, dryland forest, mixed gardens, mangroves, rice fields, shrubs, open land, and fields of 0.5 - 202.5 ha. Thus there is a conversion of protected land to the cultivation of 2.8 ha. The direction of land use can be further developed as a cultivation area and cannot be further developed as a cultivation area. The land that cannot be further developed as a cultivation area is 35,578.3 ha. While the land that can be developed as a cultivation area is 11,388.7 ha and develops around the coastal area. Keywords: Land Use, Land Use Change, Land Capability

This study aims to examine the implementation of the APB-Desa policy in Tobelos Village, South Mother District, West Halmahera Regency. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research evaluates policy implementation through the four established dimensions of public policy execution: communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure. The respondents comprised eight key informants, including the village head, village officials, members of BPD and LPMD, female representatives, community group members, and community leaders. Data were collected using structured interview guides, and analysis was conducted following the interactive model proposed by Miles and Huberman. The findings indicate that: (1) In terms of communication, the implementation of the APB-Desa policy remains suboptimal, with weak interactions observed among the village government, BPD, and LPM during the policy’s formulation and execution stages, accompanied by inadequate socialization efforts directed toward the community. (2) Regarding human resources, although certain village officials possess adequate competencies, their capabilities have not been fully leveraged to ensure optimal policy implementation. (3) From the disposition perspective, the commitment and consistency necessary for the accurate and proper implementation of the APB-Desa are deficient, as is the democratic engagement in both the formulation and execution processes. (4) Concerning bureaucratic structure, while mechanisms, procedures, and the division of labor related to the APB-Desa's implementation are clearly defined, actual practice frequently deviates from these established guidelines.  

Keywords: Policy Implementation, APB-Village

ABSTRACT Curly chili (Capsicum annum L.) is one of the many horticultural commodities needed in daily life so that its needs continue to increase along with population growth and technological progress. One of the main pest species that attacks fruits and vegetables in Indonesia is Bactrocera sp. Methyl eugenol is reported sp to be able to control fruit flies in mango, guava, starfruit, melon, jackfruit, guava, tomato, red pepper and bitter melon. The aim of this study was to determine the level of fruit damage by Bactrocera sp. Fruit flies. in the use of methyl eugenol in curly chili plants in Tomohon City, especially in the villages of Kinilow, Kakaskasen, and Matani. The duration of the study lasted for three (months), namely from February to April 2018. This research was carried out by survey method or by direct observation at the research location. Results of research on percentage of Bactrocera sp. in the land of methyl eugenol from the first and second weeks of 21.53% and 20.78%, while in the third week, the percentage of attacks was 18.86% followed by the observation of the fourth and fifth weeks increased by 24.34% and 33.86%. While the land of farmers experienced a decrease in the percentage of attacks from the first week, the second was 16.19% and 15.78%, then followed in the third, fourth and fifth weeks, the percentage of attacks increased by 17.47%, 18.54% and 18.7% . Whereas on land that is left to attack Bactrocera sp. from the first week of 16.09%, the second week was 21.9%, and in the third and fourth weeks the attack rate increased by 25.38% and 26.52%, followed by the fifth week of the attack level which increased to 30.56%. Keywords: Percentage, Bactrocera sp. Curly chili

The objectives of this study are: To study and analyze the availability of land in North Gorontalo District, Assessing and analyzing land requirements in North Gorontalo District, Analyzing and evaluating Carrying Capacity Ratio of agricultural land in North Gorontalo Regency. The research method is qualitative which is analyzed descriptively quantitative. The study was conducted covering 11 districts in North Gorontalo Regency. The data used in this study are primary data and secondary data, Data collection was obtained through direct observation at the research location and through literature studies from various trusted sources or related institutions namely the Central Statistics Agency of North Gorontalo Regency 2018, and the Department of Agriculture, Horticulture Plantation, North Gorontalo District 2018. The method for calculating the carrying capacity of land uses the method of analysis in accordance with Regulation of the Minister of Environment No. 17 of 2009. The results showed the availability of land (SL) of North Gorontalo Regency was 59,235,467 Ha, and the land requirement (DL) was 46,893,556 Ha. the value of land availability is greater than the need for land SL ˃ DL, carrying capacity for district level is categorized as surplus. Carrying capacity of agricultural land (CCR) in North Gorontalo District is obtained less than one or CCR <1 that is 0.36, the assumption is that the carrying capacity of agricultural land is deficit. Policy implications for the North Gorontalo District Government should emphasize sustainable agricultural development policies through intensification, extensification and revitalization programs, so that the carrying capacity of agricultural land can be increased in realizing self-reliance and sustainable regional food security.*eprm*

This study, entitled "Concepts of Feminism Explored in Pearl S. Buck’s Novel *The Mother*," aims to examine the representation of feminist ideas within the text. Feminism holds a significant position in both societal and cultural contexts. The primary research question addresses how feminist ideology is articulated through the narrative of *The Mother*. The objective is to identify, analyze, and elucidate the feminist concepts portrayed through the protagonist, the mother, in the novel. Employing a descriptive research design, the study utilizes an intrinsic approach to analyze the character of the mother based on Robert’s theory, considering elements such as character, setting, and plot. Furthermore, an extrinsic approach is adopted to interpret the feminist ideas by applying the theory of the relationship between literature and ideology as proposed by Wellek and Warren. The findings demonstrate that the mother’s actions predominantly depict her as a resilient and empowered female figure who assumes multifaceted roles within her life, including those traditionally associated with both motherhood and fatherhood, ultimately serving as the family’s pillar of strength. Despite frequently enduring mistreatment from her surroundings and even her own family, she assertively defends her rights as a woman. The study reveals that feminist ideas are manifested through characterization, plot development, and setting. Additionally, the interplay between traditional Chinese customs and the socio-historical context of 1930s China is examined to further illuminate the feminist themes within the novel.

Keywords: Feminism, Novel, Character

The purchase of pirated products is a prevalent phenomenon within consumer behavior and is notably widespread in Indonesia. The frequent occurrence of illicit buying and selling activities leads the community to perceive the acquisition of counterfeit goods as a normative behavior, rather than a violation of legal or ethical standards. In recent years, online transactions in Manado have become increasingly common; however, they are predominantly characterized by the proliferation of counterfeit products. This study seeks to (1) examine the impact of personal characteristics on consumers' attitudes toward purchasing counterfeit goods, and (2) determine which personal characteristic most significantly influences such attitudes among consumers in Manado. Employing multiple linear regression analysis, the research utilized a sample of 100 respondents from Manado who are consumers of counterfeit products. The findings indicate that occupation and economic situation, lifestyle, and personality significantly affect consumers' attitudes, whereas age and life-cycle stage do not exhibit a significant influence. Among these factors, lifestyle emerged as the most influential determinant of consumer attitudes toward the purchase of counterfeit goods in Manado. It is recommended that manufacturers and marketers incorporate the issue of counterfeiting into their advertising strategies to dissuade consumers from purchasing counterfeit items by highlighting the negative social implications associated with such behavior.  

Keywords: personal characteristics, consumer attitude

Growth-regulating substances, encompassing both organic and inorganic compounds, are integral to various biological processes within plant tissues, notably including embryonic callus formation and embryogenesis. This investigation sought to evaluate the influence of cytokinin growth regulators at specified concentrations on the induction of embryonic callus in chrysanthemum plants. The study was conducted over a four-month period, from June to October 2018, at the Genetics Laboratory of the Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. Employing a completely randomized design, the experiment utilized cytokinins zeatin (Z) and thidiazuron (TDZ) at concentrations of 2 ppm, 4 ppm, and 6 ppm, each supplemented with auxin indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) at 0.02 ppm and gibberellic acid (GA3) at 0.2 ppm. Each treatment was replicated five times. The parameters measured included the duration until callus formation, the wet weight of the callus, and callus coloration. Findings indicated that the shortest callus formation period was 7.8 days following culture initiation, observed under the 2 ppm zeatin treatment. The maximum callus wet weight recorded was 2.111 grams under the 2 ppm TDZ treatment, with the resulting callus exhibiting a green coloration.

Keywords: Growth-Regulating Substances, Embryonic Callus, Cytokinins, Chrysanthemum

Abstract:  
Law No. 6 of 2014 concerning villages stipulates that one of the functions of the Village Consultative Body (BPD) is to serve as a supervisory institution within the village. This study aims to examine the oversight role of the BPD in the implementation of rural development in the Galela district of North Halmahera. A qualitative research approach was employed, with informants selected from various stakeholders involved in village development, including village government officials (village heads), BPD members, village community organizations (such as LPM, PKK, among others), and residents of the rural communities. A total of twelve informants participated in the study. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using the interactive analytical model proposed by Miles and Huberman. The findings indicate that the BPD’s supervisory function in rural development implementation in Galela district has been carried out satisfactorily, though not to its full potential, based on fourteen dimensions of supervisory function assessment utilized in this study. In light of these findings, several recommendations are proposed: (1) the BPD should endeavor to perform its oversight responsibilities professionally and objectively, free from undue influence or intervention by the village head; (2) BPD members should possess adequate knowledge, education, experience, a strong mental attitude, and demonstrate commitment and integrity in fulfilling their supervisory roles; (3) effective cooperation and support from local villagers are essential to enable the BPD to execute its duties effectively.  
Keywords: supervisory functions, Village Consultative Body (BPD), rural development implementation

Entertainment has increasingly become a fundamental consumer need in recent times. The customer base for karaoke services has expanded rapidly over the past few years, leading to intensified market competition. In order to remain competitive, companies must formulate strategies that align with their resources and capitalize on available opportunities within the competitive environment. This study aims to identify the key criteria influencing user selection of karaoke services and to delineate the strengths of each service according to criteria established through the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Utilizing AHP, this research evaluates karaoke services based on service quality, social factors, facility, and price. The study focuses on two sample services: Inul Vizta KTV and DIVA Karaoke. To enhance the reliability of the analysis, Expert Choice 11 software was employed to process respondent data. Findings reveal that price constitutes the primary consideration for customers when selecting a karaoke service, with an average weight of 0.340, followed by social factors at 0.309 and service quality at 0.230. These results indicate that karaoke services should prioritize pricing strategies to attract customers, as price represents the most significant criterion in consumer decision-making.  
Keywords: service quality, social factors, facility, price

Title:  
**Effect of Blackfly Larvae-Degraded Manure (Hermetia illucens L) on the Performance of Laying Native Chickens**

Abstract:  
Native chickens represent a significant source of protein and are extensively reared throughout Indonesia. These chickens are primarily maintained for egg production, as their eggs provide substantial nutritional benefits for human consumption. Among the feed ingredients available for native chickens, manure flour derived from the degradation by blackfly larvae (Hermetia illucens L), hereafter referred to as MHD flour, presents a promising nutritional resource. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of incorporating MHD flour into the ration on feed intake, egg production, and feed conversion efficiency in native laying chickens. A total of 40 female native chickens, aged 56 weeks, were housed in battery cages measuring 50 × 50 × 75 cm, with random allocation to treatment units. The experimental design employed was a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with four treatments and five replications per treatment, as outlined by Steel and Torrie (1991). The treatments consisted of varying levels of MHD flour inclusion in the feed: R0 = 0%, R1 = 5%, R2 = 10%, and R3 = 15%. The response variables measured included feed consumption, egg production, and feed conversion ratio. Results indicated a highly significant effect (P < 0.01) of the treatments on both feed consumption and egg production, whereas no significant difference (P > 0.05) was observed in feed conversion ratios across treatments. The findings suggest that up to 15% inclusion of MHD flour in the ration is viable for enhancing the productive performance of native laying chickens.  

**Keywords:** Native chicken, Blackfly larvae, Hermetia illucens, manure-derived flour, feed utilization, egg production

This study, titled "Function and Category of Adjectival Phrases in Simple Sentences in the Novel *Sense and Sensibility* by Jane Austen," aims to identify, classify, and analyze adjectival phrases in simple sentences from the novel, focusing on their functions and categories. Employing a descriptive research method, the study was conducted in three phases. Initially, the researcher reviewed relevant literature on syntactic structures and examined journal articles concerning adjectival phrases available online. Next, data were collected from Jane Austen’s *Sense and Sensibility* to enable identification and classification of adjectival phrases according to the theoretical framework proposed by Aarts & Aarts (1982). Finally, the collected data were analyzed using tree diagrams. 

The findings reveal that adjectival phrases serve primarily two functions within sentences: as subject attributes and as object attributes. Externally, simple sentence structures encompass the functions of subject, predicate, and adverbial. Internally, the elements identified include predicator and complement, which are realized through subject and object attributes. The study also classifies the categories present in the simple sentences as noun phrases, verb phrases, and adjectival phrases, with the internal structure of adjectival phrases examined in detail. The internal structure comprises adjectivals realized by adjectives.

Quantitative analysis indicates the presence of 126 adjectival phrases functioning as subject attributes, which include seven serving as heads, sixty-four as premodifiers, twenty-four as postmodifiers, twenty-four combining pre- and postmodifiers, and seven discontinuous modifiers. Conversely, twenty-two adjectival phrases were identified as object attributes, comprising thirteen premodifiers, four postmodifiers, three combining pre- and postmodifiers, and two discontinuous modifiers. Notably, the head function of adjectival phrases as object attributes was not observed. 

Keywords: Function, Category, Adjectival Phrase, Sense and Sensibility

This study, entitled "Register Used in Beauty Pageants Pages on the Social Media Platform Instagram," aims to contribute to the theoretical framework within the field of linguistics, with a particular focus on advancing sociolinguistic research. It also seeks to provide valuable insights for enthusiasts of beauty pageants by examining the specific linguistic registers employed on Instagram pages dedicated to this domain. The primary objectives are to identify and categorize the registers present on beauty pageant Instagram pages, as well as to analyze the variations in language use and the linguistic forms of the registers encountered.

The theoretical foundation of this research is grounded in Martin Joos’s (1968) framework on language variation and George Yule’s (2006) theory regarding linguistic forms. Employing a descriptive methodological approach, the data were collected from Instagram posts made between January 2016 and July 2018 by 21 users followed by the researcher. 

The findings reveal that the registers used on Instagram include terms such as pride, winner, gown, wardrobe, top, sneakpeak, beauty class, close-up battle, catwalk class, bubbling up, placed, styled, crowned, brushed, cocktail dress, stunning, beauty queen, miss, yash, sist, shay, missosology, muses, sash, backtoback, backstage, wishlist, fasttrack, grandfinal, hotpick, funfact, photoshoot, titleholder, powerhouse, firstwalk, glamshoot, fitting, photo, asst, decor, pic, represent, roat to, opnum, MUA, PL, MGIO, BWAP, QNA, BTS, MUO, MS, RU, natcos, and TBA. The linguistic variation of these registers encompasses frozen, formal, consultative, casual, and intimate styles. Moreover, the linguistic forms manifested in the registers include coinage, borrowing, compounding, blending, clipping, backformation, conversion, and acronyms. Meanings of the identified register terms were verified using online dictionary resources.

Keywords: Register, Instagram, Beauty Pageants, Sociolinguistic Analysis

The contemporary market has emerged as a prominent shopping trend within society, despite the longstanding significance of traditional markets as primary venues for daily product purchases. This study aims to examine whether significant differences exist in customer dissatisfaction and behavioral displacement factors between modern and traditional markets. Employing a causal research design, data were collected through the administration of questionnaires and subsequently analyzed. The research hypothesis posits that disparities exist regarding customer dissatisfaction and shopping behavior displacement factors between modern and traditional markets. The study population consisted of customers shopping at Hypermart Mantos and Pinasungkulan Markets in Karombasan, Manado City, with a sample size of 100 respondents. The analysis involved comparing mean values using an independent samples t-test to evaluate differences between the two market types. Findings reveal significant differences between traditional and modern markets concerning consumer dissatisfaction and the behavioral displacement from traditional to modern markets. Consequently, vendors in traditional markets are advised to enhance product quality and service standards to mitigate customer displacement. 

Keywords: poor service, consumer dissatisfaction, consumer consideration, consumer switching behavior

Since the economic crisis of 1997, the adoption of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) has become a prominent issue in Indonesia. At that time, the country faced significant economic decline attributed to inadequate corporate governance practices. Consequently, there has been a consensus on the need to address Indonesia’s challenges through improved corporate governance frameworks. Good Corporate Governance is a control mechanism designed to evaluate and manage companies, with the primary aim of enhancing corporate accountability. It can be defined as a set of processes and organizational structures implemented by corporate entities to increase shareholder value.

The objectives of this study are threefold: (1) to examine and verify the impact of Good Corporate Governance on leverage; (2) to assess and confirm the influence of GCG implementation on profitability; and (3) to investigate and substantiate the effect of leverage on profitability. The study focuses on banking corporations listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange. A sample of 16 banking companies meeting specific research criteria was selected, with data spanning the period from 2009 to 2013. Path analysis was employed as the primary analytical method.

The findings revealed that the effect of GCG implementation (X) on leverage (Y1), as measured by the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) and Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR), was not statistically significant. Conversely, GCG (X) exhibited a significant positive influence on profitability (Y2), assessed through Return on Equity (ROE) and Net Profit Margin (NPM). The relationship between leverage (Y1) and profitability (Y2) among the sampled banking firms demonstrated variability. These results suggest that while improved GCG practices do not significantly alter the debt structure of banking institutions, they contribute positively to profitability, enhancing firms’ ability to generate earnings. It is therefore recommended that companies strive for consistent GCG implementation to promote productivity and operational efficiency, which in turn positively affects profitability and investor confidence.

Parking retribution constitutes a significant component of Regional Original Revenue (Pendapatan Asli Daerah, PAD) in Indonesia. The implementation of regional autonomy has positioned parking retribution as a key source of regional income. This study was conducted at the Transportation Institution Office (Dinas Perhubungan, DISHUB) of Manado City and the Parking Technical Executing Units (Unit Pelaksana Teknis, UPT) responsible for managing parking retribution. The objectives of this research are threefold: to analyze the trends in parking retribution revenue, to forecast the effectiveness of parking retribution realization from 2016 to 2020, and to provide recommendations for enhancing the effectiveness of parking retribution management in the future. A descriptive analytical approach was employed in this study. The findings indicate that the UPT under the DISHUB of Manado City has successfully achieved the revenue targets set by the regional government, demonstrating commendable effectiveness. The analysis of revenue realization over time reveals a consistent upward trend, increasing from 61.20% in 2008 to 111.46% in 2012. Forecasting data for parking retribution revenues between 2016 and 2020 further suggest a continuous increase, with revenue realization rising from 385.83% in 2016 to 361.04% in 2020. Based on these projections, several strategies are recommended to improve revenue effectiveness, including revising fee policies, enhancing human resource efficiency and effectiveness, conducting routine monitoring at parking locations, and upgrading resources by implementing computerized systems to reduce non-compliance and improve management practices.

This study, entitled *Mood in English and Manado Malay Language: A Contrastive Analysis*, aims to identify and classify the types and functions of mood, as well as to examine the similarities and differences between mood usage in English and Manado Malay. Employing a descriptive research method, the study relies on the theoretical frameworks of Aarts and Aarts (1982) and Frank (1972) to classify and analyze the types and functions of mood, while Lado’s (1957) theory serves as the foundation for a comparative contrast between the two languages. The findings reveal three categories of mood with corresponding functions in both languages. In English, the indicative mood is used to state all situations except for imperative and subjunctive moods; the subjunctive mood conveys uncertainty, wishes, and encouragement; and the imperative mood expresses commands, requests, and instructions. In Manado Malay, the indicative mood similarly serves to declare all situations, the subjunctive mood denotes uncertainty and encouragement, and the imperative mood is employed for commands, requests, and instructions. Both languages share analogous definitions and functions for moods that express factual situations (indicative) and non-factual or hypothetical contexts (subjunctive and imperative). However, they differ in that English distinguishes singular and plural through the use of regular and irregular verbs as well as the auxiliary verb "to be," whereas Manado Malay exhibits no morphological variation in verbs to indicate number. 

Keywords: Mood, Manado Malay Language, Contrastive Analysis

Abstract  
The drying process of thin layers of cassava slices, corresponding to the thickness of the slices, was conducted using an Experimental Dryer. The drying temperature was maintained at 60°C, with observations recorded every 15 minutes during the initial two hours, followed by hourly measurements until the samples reached equilibrium moisture content. This study aimed to characterize the drying behavior of cassava slices and to develop mathematical models relating moisture content to drying time, drying rate to time, and drying rate to moisture content, as well as to analyze temperature variations within the samples throughout the drying process. The research was performed at the Post Harvest Laboratory of Agricultural Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. An experimental methodology was employed, involving systematic observations and calculations, with data represented graphically and analyzed descriptively. Drying continued until the samples attained equilibrium moisture content. Instruments utilized included thermocouples, ovens, desiccators, analytical balances, and digital scales. The cassava slices tested had thicknesses of 3 mm and 6 mm. Results indicated that temperature fluctuations during drying differed between the two thicknesses. For the 3 mm slices, the moisture content of sample 2 decreased to 1.6% wet basis (WB) after 7 to 8 hours, fitting an exponential model described by y = 28.602e^(-0.44x) with R² = 0.8256. For the 6 mm slices, sample 1 reached 2% WB after 11 to 12 hours, modeled by y = 41.161e^(-0.327x) with R² = 0.8957. The drying rate as a function of time for the 3 mm thickness was characterized by y = 52.336e^(-0.729x) (R² = 0.9613), while for the 6 mm thickness it was y = 31.845e^(-0.677x) (R² = 0.9826). Additionally, the drying rate as a function of moisture content for the 6 mm slices was modeled by y = 0.3119e^(0.0992x), yielding R² = 0.7597.  
Keywords: Cassava bulbs, drying characteristics, thin layer drying, mathematical modeling

EVALUATION THE BIOLOGICAL VALUES OF CALCIUM AND PHOSPHORS TO GIVED COMPLETE FEED, CORN FORAGE, AND KING GRASS IN FH (fries Holland). This study aims to evaluate the biological value of calcium and phosphorus given complete feed, corn forage and king grass in FH (Fries Holland). The material used were 14 FH dairy cattle 7-8 years old, body weight 300-400 kg. The cages used were individual cages. The feed given were corn forage, king grass and concentrates. The analysis of t-test data (t-test two samples unequal variances) was used in this study, consisting of 2 types of treatment and 7 replications. They were Ra = 70% corn forage + 30% concentrate and Rb = 35% corn forage + 35% king grass + 30% concentrate. The observed variables were the consumption and digestibility of Ca and P of dairy cattle (FH). The present study investigates the diversity, population density, and temporal activity patterns of mosquito genera (Culicidae) within pig enclosures in Tolok Village, Tompaso District, Minahasa Regency, with a focus on their potential role as vectors of Japanese encephalitis. Field research was conducted over a two-month period at two distinct pig cage locations: Cage I, situated less than 10 meters from residential houses, and Cage II, located more than 50 meters away. Mosquito specimens were collected using light traps operated every two hours from 18:00 to 06:00, with three replicates performed biweekly at each site. Following collection, mosquitoes were identified to genus level and enumerated.

Findings revealed that both cage locations harbored three mosquito genera, namely Culex, Anopheles, and Armigeres. The total mosquito count in Cage I amounted to 128 individuals comprising 104 Culex, 20 Anopheles, and 4 Armigeres. In contrast, Cage II yielded 46 mosquitoes, including 40 Culex, 5 Anopheles, and 1 Armigeres. Peak mosquito activity was recorded between 22:00 and 24:00 hours, corresponding to the highest capture rates of 48 and 18 mosquitoes in Cage I and Cage II, respectively. These results suggest that mosquito abundance was greater in pig enclosures proximal to human dwellings, with maximal activity occurring during late evening hours.

In summary, the study identifies three Culicidae genera present in pig pens within Tolok Village and establishes a correlation between proximity to breeder houses and increased mosquito population density, alongside defining the time window of heightened mosquito activity. 

Keywords: Mosquito, pig livestock, activity, density, diversity.

SENSORICAL QUALITY AND PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF CHICKEN NUGGETS WHICH IS ADDED PURPLE ROAD UBI FLOUR (Ipomoea batatas L). This study aims to determine the benefits of using purple sweet potato flour (Ipomoea batatas L) on the sensory quality and physical properties of chicken nuggets. The research was carried out in 3 stages, namely (1) making purple sweet potato flour, (2) making chicken nugets with the addition of purple sweet potato flour, (3) testing chicken nuggets including sensory quality testing using 35 untrained panelists to measure the level of acceptance of aroma, color, texture and taste, physical properties test to determine water binding power and cooking losses. This research was conducted experimentally using a completely randomized design with 4 additional treatments of purple sweet potato flour, namely P1 = 10 g, P2 = 20 g, P3 = 30 g and P4 = 40 g, each treatment was repeated as many as 35 (panelists) for the test. sensory quality and 5 replications for physical characteristics test. Data from the observation of sensory quality test, physical properties were tabulated and analyzed by analysis of variance (Ansira) and if there were significant differences between treatments, it was continued with Duncan's multiple test (DMRT). The results of the research with analysis of variance showed that the addition of 10, 20, 30 and 40 grams of purple sweet potato had a very significant effect (P <0.01) on color, texture, water-binding capacity and cooking loss but had no significant effect. (P> 0.05) on aroma and taste. The results of Duncan's multiple further test showed that the P4 treatment of 40 g of purple sweet potato gave the best results on color, texture, water binding power and cooking loss. Based on the results and discussion, it can be concluded that the addition of 40 g of purple sweet potato flour in the manufacture of chicken nuggets provides good sensory quality and physical properties.Keywords: Chicken nuggets, purple sweet potato flour, sensory quality, physical properties

Abstract  
Convivial acts, as a subset of illocutionary acts, are observed not only in everyday interactions but also within various literary forms, including novels, dramas, short stories, novellas, and films. This research aims to identify, classify, and analyze the manifestations of convivial acts in the film *Hunger Games: Mockingjay*, directed by Francis Lawrence. Employing a descriptive research method, the study systematically identifies and analyzes relevant data. Initially, the researcher reviewed pragmatic literature related to convivial acts to establish a theoretical foundation. Subsequently, the film was carefully viewed in its entirety to gain a comprehensive understanding of the story’s context. The data were then extracted, classified according to pertinent categories of convivial acts, and analyzed descriptively with reference to Leech’s and Austin’s pragmatic theories. The findings indicate that convivial acts in the film can be divided into five categories: offering, inviting, greeting, congratulating, and thanking. Furthermore, the study elucidates how these acts are employed by various characters throughout the narrative. It is anticipated that this research will contribute to the pedagogical approaches employed by students and readers in the field of pragmatics, particularly in relation to convivial acts as illustrated in film.  

Keywords: Convivial Act, Hunger Games: Mockingjay, Pragmatic Analysis

This study aims to evaluate the efficiency of production factor utilization on chili farms in Marawas Village, North Tondano Subdistrict, Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted over a three-month period, from May 2011 to July 2011. The study site was selected through purposive sampling, given that the majority of Marawas Village residents rely on chili farming for their livelihood. A total of 40 farmers participated as respondents. Quantitative data analysis was performed using regression analysis. Primary data collected included production volume, land area, labor input, quantities of seed, organic and NPK fertilizers, pesticide use, and the application of growth stimulant substances (ZPT). 

The findings indicate that the regression model applied is appropriate for this study. The F-test results demonstrated that the utilization of land area, labor, seed, organic and NPK fertilizers, pesticides, and growth stimulant substances (ZPT) significantly influences production volume. However, the T-test results revealed that only land area, labor, and organic fertilizer exert a significant individual effect on production levels. In contrast, the quantities of seed, NPK fertilizer, and growth stimulant substances (ZPT) were found to have no significant impact on production. 

Furthermore, the utilization of production factors such as land area, labor, seed, organic and NPK fertilizers, and growth stimulant substances (ZPT) was technically efficient but not economically efficient. Conversely, pesticide use was determined to be neither technically nor economically efficient. Therefore, it is recommended that chili farmers in Marawas Village, North Tondano Subdistrict, Minahasa Regency, reduce excessive pesticide application and consider alternative pest and disease control methods that are environmentally friendly and free of chemical agents, such as manual, mechanical, or physical control techniques.

The hotel industry has emerged as a rapidly growing sector in Manado. This development is largely attributed to the Manado tourism city program initiated by the municipal government, which has indirectly fostered opportunities for the expansion of the hospitality sector in the area. The objective of this study is twofold: to identify the hotel criteria that influence consumer preferences and to determine which star-rated hotel is most favored by the local population. The research was conducted in Manado city from May to June 2015. A purposive sampling technique was employed to select 30 respondents, each of whom had prior experience spending at least one night in a three-star hotel, specifically Peninsula, Arya Duta, or Novotel. The Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) was utilized as the methodological approach to evaluate and compare the three-star hotels based on established star-rating criteria, with preferences quantified using a preference scale. The findings indicate that among four examined criteria, only two significantly affect consumer choice, with price being the most influential factor, followed by location in second place. Regarding the preferred hotel selection, Peninsula was ranked highest by respondents, succeeded by Arya Duta and Novotel. Consequently, hotel management within star-rating categories should strategically consider pricing aligned with location while ensuring superior service quality to meet consumer expectations.  
Keywords: Analytical Hierarchy Process, consumer purchase decision

The COVID-19 pandemic has engendered widespread anxiety within the community, a phenomenon that also affects adolescents, rendering them particularly vulnerable to compromised sleep quality. Inadequate sleep quality can adversely influence health by impairing the restorative processes essential for bodily function, thereby impacting the ability to perform daily activities and ultimately diminishing overall quality of life. This study aims to evaluate the quality of life alongside sleep quality among teenagers attending Rex Mundi Catholic High School in Manado during the COVID-19 pandemic. Employing a descriptive, cross-sectional design, this research recruited participants who met specified inclusion criteria via cluster random sampling. Data were collected online using the WHOQOL-BREF and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) questionnaires. A total of 87 students participated in the study. Findings indicated that the mean quality of life scores across the physical health, psychological wellbeing, social relationships, and environmental domains ranged between 51 and 75. Most respondents reported satisfactory subjective sleep quality, with latent sleep latency of 1–2, sleep duration of 6–7 hours, sleep efficiency exceeding 85%, sleep disturbance scores between 1 and 9, minimal use of sleep medications over the prior month, and daytime dysfunction scores of 1–2. The results suggest that the majority of participants experienced a moderate quality of life across all examined domains and maintained good sleep quality during the pandemic period.

Keywords: quality of life, sleep quality

This study, titled "Prefixes of Verbs and Nouns in English and Saluan Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify, classify, and examine the form, function, and meaning of prefixes attached to verbs and nouns in both English and the Saluan language. Additionally, the research seeks to elucidate the similarities and differences between the two languages by employing theoretical frameworks proposed by Brinton (2010), O'Grady and Dobrovolsky (1992), and Brown (1980). Data for English were sourced from O'Grady’s (1992) publication and the fourth edition of the Oxford Learner’s Dictionary (Oxford University Press, 2008), whereas Saluan language data were collected directly from native informants. The findings reveal both shared features and distinctions between English and Saluan. Specifically, the prefixes of nouns in Saluan include topo-, nong-, pong-, and ka-. Functionally, English prefixes can be affixed to verbs, nouns, and adjectives, whereas in Saluan, prefixes are attached to verbs, nouns, adjectives, and numerals. While both languages exhibit prefixes linked to verbs and nouns, a notable difference is that English noun prefixes typically attach only to noun bases, whereas in Saluan, prefixes may attach to both verb and noun bases. 

Keywords: English and Saluan language prefixes, contrastive linguistic analysis
