People have hundreds of options for any product or service in a crowded marketplace, marketers have had to come up with new ways to get people's attention. One such strategy that marketers have begun to utilize is product placement. This study aims to find out whether the three dimensions of product placement: visual dimension, auditory dimension, and plot connection dimension, influence the brand memory of audiences partially and simultaneously. The study was conducted on 100 students of Faculty of Economics and Business, Sam Ratulangi University using quantitative method and Multiple Linear Regression as the analysis tool. The results revealed the two of three dimensions of product placement which are visual and plot connection, partially has a positive and significant influence on brand memory. In contrast, the auditory dimension partially has no significant influence on brand memory. Simultaneously, all three dimensions of product placement have a positive and significant effect on brand memory. Therefore, Samsung or the other company can explore more the appearance of the auditory dimension and also maintain and improve the other two dimensions, namely the visual and the plot connection dimension, in order to have a greater influence. Keywords: product placement, visual dimension, auditory dimension, plot connection dimension, brand memory

The rapid advancement of technology has led to the widespread presence of digital platforms designed to fulfill various user needs. Among these platforms, social media has emerged as a significant arena for individuals to cultivate their personal branding. Personal branding is not limited to celebrities or entrepreneurs but is applicable to anyone seeking recognition for their unique skills or attributes. In the contemporary digital era, the value of personal branding is often measured by metrics such as "likes," "followers," and "subscribers," with influencer-driven social media serving as a potent catalyst for marketing and sales activities (James F., 2013). Accordingly, this study aims to examine the influence of personal branding on digital platforms, explore strategies for building and sustaining personal branding strength, and investigate how personal branding impacts public awareness to enhance economic value. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research yielded several findings: (1) the growth of personal branding on social media corresponds with increases in followers, likes, and comments; (2) shared interests, such as hobbies, preferences, or geographic origins, along with admiration for influencers, foster connections between influencers and their audiences; (3) the creation of personal branding begins with the dissemination of engaging activities, narratives, and experiences via social media; (4) maintaining personal branding effectiveness necessitates active engagement and communication on social media, accompanied by the ongoing development of both content and personal identity; and (5) the enhancement of personal branding through social media attracts the attention of business stakeholders and brand owners, who leverage influencers’ platforms to promote their products, services, or brands.

The objective of this study is threefold: (1) to identify the components of cost included in the variable cost element, (2) to examine the application of cost analysis based on variable costing for decision-making regarding the acceptance or rejection of special orders, and (3) to assess whether implementing such cost calculations can enhance corporate profitability. This research employs a quantitative descriptive analysis methodology. The primary data utilized comprises production reports for special production orders, which serve as the basis for decision-making regarding the acceptance or rejection of these orders. These data were obtained through interviews and direct observation. According to the cost analysis conducted using variable costing for decision-making purposes, the variable cost associated with cake production amounts to Rp. 358,224,560, whereas the fixed cost totals Rp. 422,398,305. The analysis further reveals that employing variable costing in conjunction with differential cost analysis for evaluating special orders from RM Setia Amurang and Bali Souvenir results in a total profit of Rp. 7,915,068. These findings indicate that accepting special orders under the specified cost conditions can yield financial benefits for the company. Therefore, the management of Tokin Cake Cooking Company is advised to approve special orders at the subscriber-requested cost while carefully considering the resultant revenue and differential costs to maximize profit contribution.

Leprosy is an infectious disease caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium leprae. Based on data from the Ministry of Health new cases of leprosy in Indonesia in 2013 and 2014. there were 16.856 and 16.131 new cases respectively. North Sulawesi ranks sixth among the provinces with the numbers highest Case Detection Rate (CDR) per 100,000 population in Indonesia , which is 14.65 per 100,000 population. Registered patients in the city of Manado in 2013 and 2014 there were 67 and 69 people respectively. Leprosy disability level 2 in the city of Manado is quite high, reaching 10.6%. Disability due to leprosy can be prevented. Leprosy patient behavior plays an important role in the prevention of disability due to the disease itself. This study aimed to describe the behavior of leprosy patients in the prevention of disability due to leprosy. This study is a qualitative descriptive study with cross sectional study design. Data collected by in-depth interview techniques and triangulation with samples of 9 people with leprosy patients using purposive sampling. The results showed that the majority of informants knowledge about leprosy in general still lacking, but knowledge in the prevention of disability through regular treatment is sufficient. The attitude of the informants was good and optimistic with the treatment, showed a positive attitude. Most of the actions of the informants in the prevention of disability as a regular treatment has been good, although still need to be optimized. The behavior of the informants was good overall, but knowledge about leprosy in general needs to be improved further. Patients are advised to more actively seek information about the disease and prevention of disability, as well as the necessity for improved education and health promotion concerning leprosy by the health workers.

Indonesia, a unitary state composed of an archipelago extending from Sabang to Merauke, is characterized by a rich diversity of cultures, ethnic groups, and races. It is also home to numerous historical sites that serve as ancestral relics embodying significant cultural values that require careful maintenance and preservation. Pulutan Village, located within the Pulutan District of Talaud Islands Regency in North Sulawesi Province, spans an area of 10.5 square kilometers. This village features a freshwater spring situated on the shoreline, locally known as Tiwud'di Tamangen. According to indigenous beliefs, Tiwud'di Tamangen is regarded as an ancestral heritage site, warranting ongoing preservation efforts. The residents of Pulutan Village utilize the spring as a source of clean water for daily consumption and attribute to it medicinal properties believed to cure various ailments. However, its transformation into a tourist attraction has introduced constraints on community activities; whereas previously the local inhabitants accessed the spring’s water freely, they are now required to pay an entrance fee. Consequently, the commercialization of Tiwud'di Tamangen presents challenges for the Pulutan community in balancing the maintenance of local wisdom associated with the site alongside the socio-economic benefits and environmental impacts resulting from tourism development.  

Keywords: cultural heritage, freshwater springs, tourism development

The clothing industry experienced a decline in sales during the pandemic but the facts are different from PT Fast Retailing (UNIQLO) which based on research has increased sales in Indonesia during the pandemic, this has something to do with the success of their marketing strategy along with the different brand experiences they created. With this phenomenon, the aim of this research is to analyze the influence of the variables of convenience, user experience, promotion, product recommendation, brand experience, and urge to buy impulsively. This research model was modified from previous research by adding the brand experience variable. The results of the study explain the strongest positive relationship between convenience, product recommendation, and promotion toward brand experience, followed by user experience and promotion toward urge to buy impulsively. In addition, user experience has a significant effect on brand experience and brand experience also has a significant effect on impulse buying. This research was conducted with the number of research subjects 412 respondents who had shopped at UNIQLO through Instagram. Respondents were selected by purposive sampling and snowball sampling, while data collection was carried out using an online questionnaire. The research data were analyzed using the PLS-SEM 3.3.3 method. There are some managerial implications that can be suggested from this research.

Indonesia's tropical climate, characterized by distinct rainy and dry seasons, significantly influences irrigation practices and rain-fed agriculture. These seasonal variations enable farmers to enhance their agricultural productivity by selecting suitable crops tailored to either the rainy or dry periods. In Jirenne Village, located in Lanny Jaya, Papua, the presence of fertile soil contributes to the abundance of natural resources. The villagers predominantly rely on food crops such as sweet potato, sago, and banana as essential components of their subsistence economy. However, the farming community in Jirenne exhibits limited proficiency in the intensive processing of agricultural produce. This limitation is largely attributed to the community’s adherence to traditional customs that dictate agricultural practices, including the belief that planting must conform to established cultural norms. Specifically, the community holds the conviction that crops planted during the dry season are unlikely to thrive, a belief deeply ingrained and resistant to change. Furthermore, mystical beliefs continue to exert significant influence over local agricultural behavior. Despite these challenges, cooperative labor and mutual assistance remain prevalent within the farming community, with villagers actively supporting one another in cultivating available land. 

Keywords: farmers, agriculture, food crops

This study aimed to assess the management of working capital at Meubel Partner Company and to evaluate the company's liquidity status with respect to its working capital. The analysis encompassed data from the years 2018 and 2019. In 2018, liquidity ratios indicated a decline, demonstrating decreases in key measures such as the ratio of current assets to current liabilities, which stood at 2.81; current assets to total assets, at 0.56; and current assets to income, at 1.40. In contrast, the liquidity ratios for 2019 showed a slight reduction compared to the previous year; however, they remained sufficient for the company to meet its short-term obligations. Specifically, in 2019, the ratio of current assets to current liabilities was 1.79, current assets to total assets increased to 0.75, and current assets to income was 1.0. Regarding working capital ratios, 2018 figures revealed a total assets to net working capital ratio of 2.84, a current liabilities to net working capital ratio of 0.56, and a sales to net working capital ratio of 2.82. In 2019, these ratios exhibited an upward trend, with total assets to net working capital rising to 2.97, current liabilities to net working capital increasing to 1.25, and sales to net working capital declining to 2.17.

This study investigates the utilization of Point-of-Sales (POS) Terminals, commonly referred to as EDC machines, which address challenges encountered during customer transactions. Such challenges include concerns about cash security, consumer familiarity with non-cash payment systems, perceived transaction ease, and the advantages of conducting non-cash transactions via POS terminals. The objective of this research is to examine whether significant differences exist between male and female customers' perceptions of BRILink POS Terminal performance, focusing specifically on four dimensions: Security of Operation, Consumer Awareness, Perceived Ease of Use, and Perceived Usefulness. Employing a quantitative research design with comparative analysis, data were collected through questionnaires administered to a sample consisting of 100 respondents, evenly split between 50 male and 50 female customers from Manado. Statistical analysis was conducted using independent samples t-tests to compare mean perception scores. The results reveal no statistically significant differences between male and female customers in their evaluation of the BRILink POS Terminal's performance. Based on these findings, it is recommended that Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) continue enhancing service quality, with particular emphasis on increasing consumer awareness regarding transactions conducted through BRILink's POS Terminal. 

Keywords: Point-of-Sales, Security of Operation, Consumer Awareness, Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, BRILink

This study aims to investigate the composition and population density of insect pests affecting potato plants (Solanum tuberosum L.) in Modoinding, South Minahasa. The research was conducted across several villages in Modoinding, namely Palelon, Makaaroyen, and Lineleyan, employing a survey methodology. Sampling involved a diagonal transect approach, establishing five subplots positioned at the corners and center of each sampling site. Insects were collected by sweeping over the potato crops with insect nets, performing ten double swings per sampling event. Captured specimens were immediately transferred to killing bottles and subsequently preserved in 70% ethanol for identification. Species determination was carried out using the facilities of the Entomology and Plant Pest Laboratory at the Faculty of Agriculture, Universitas Sam Ratulangi (UNSRAT). Results revealed the presence of eight insect pest species associated with potato cultivation: Empoasca sp. (109.03 individuals), Drosophila sp. (37.03), Nesidiocoris sp. (34.11), Lirionyza sp. (10.72), Lygus sp. (4.47), Phthorimaea sp. (2.97), Antractomorpha sp. (1.61), and Epilachna sp. (0.69). The highest mean pest population was observed in Makaaroyen Village (37.99), followed by Palelon Village (22.79), with Lineleyan Village exhibiting the lowest average population (14.49). 

Keywords: Population, Pest, Potato

The public accounting profession primarily serves the function of attestation or legalization. When auditors certify financial information, they issue a report containing conclusions regarding the credibility of management's written assertions. To ensure the production of high-quality audits, auditors are required to perform their work in accordance with established auditing standards, specifically the Standards on Auditing outlined in the Public Accountants Professional Standards (SPAP) or the Auditing Standards applicable to the State Audit Agency (BPK). Various factors can influence the quality of an audit, among which the auditor’s competence and independence are particularly significant. Competence enables auditors to execute their tasks effectively and efficiently, while independence is crucial during the processes of evidence collection and evaluation. The presence of strong competence is insufficient without an adequate level of independence to support objective judgment. This study aims to empirically analyze and demonstrate the influence of auditor competence and independence on audit quality, focusing on Public Accounting Firms (KAP) and the North Sulawesi Representative Office of the BPK. Multiple regression analysis was employed to test the research hypotheses. The partial findings indicate that auditor competence exerts a positive but statistically insignificant effect on audit quality, whereas auditor independence has a positive and statistically significant impact. Furthermore, competence and independence collectively have a positive influence on audit quality. These results suggest that improvements in both auditor competence and independence enhance the overall quality of audits conducted.

Background: Universal Precautions are prevention acts that must be done by all of the health workers to prevent the infection spreading from the patients or vice versa. The purpose of this research is to measure the overview of the implementation of universal precaution in Kolongan Community Health Center. Method: The research method is surveillance descriptive research with total sampling method as the sample collecting method. Result: Accumulatively, there were (9.44%) of all the respondents do not always wash their hand appropriately according to the washing hands procedures and indications. For about (10.57%) do not always wear protective items either in cleaning up medical instruments or doing examination to patients. We found out that (13.33%) do not always decontaminate equipments and devices properly before and after using them. Nevertheless, all of the respondents agreed that there are proper needles and sharps disposals, and all of the respondents always dispose all needles and other sharps promptly to each of their disposals. Also, all of the respondents agreed that there are separated disposals for medical and non medical wastes, and all of the respondents always dispose the wastes properly to the separately disposals. Conclusion: in Kolongan Community Health Center, the overview of the implementation of universal precautions is good. Keywords: Universal Precautions, Infection, Kolongan Community Health Center.

This study examines the management of village funds with a particular focus on the Village Head’s role as the primary authority responsible for financial management and village assets. It highlights that, in determining the village income and expenditure budget, other community components are not involved, and furthermore, the obligation to report the implementation of the Village Budget (APBDes) to the community is not fulfilled. Against this backdrop, the research aims to elucidate the role of the Village Head in managing village funds within the South Essang Subdistrict.

Employing a qualitative research methodology, the investigation centers on the Village Head’s role in the management of village funds, specifically addressing the stages of budgeting, execution, and evaluation. Informants were selected according to criteria aligned with the research objectives. Findings reveal that the planning of the Village Fund Program in South Essang Subdistrict has yet to fully integrate the principles of community participation development, as evidenced by inadequate adherence to participative, responsive, and transparent practices necessary to realize prioritized community programs. While village deliberations (Musrembangdes) guide the planned activities, including physical development and community empowerment, implementation proceeds with insufficient oversight from the village government. This lack of supervision has allowed instances of misconduct among villagers, thereby hampering the effective management of funds related to development and empowerment initiatives. Although evaluations of the village funds were conducted in 2016, the success of development activities remains constrained by operational challenges.

Keywords: Village Head, Village Fund Management

This study aims to examine the extent to which the implementation of restructuring policies impacts organizational effectiveness within the Secretariat of Manado District. Employing a quantitative research design, data were collected from a randomly selected sample of 35 civil servants out of a total population of 186 employees working at the Secretariat. Data collection methods included the administration of questionnaires supplemented by interviews. Analytical techniques utilized in this study consist of frequency distribution, percentage analysis, linear regression, and product-moment correlation.  

Previous studies have revealed that the overall performance of duties and functions within the district secretariat has not reached an optimal level. Insights gathered from interviews with several structural officials and managerial staff suggest that not all planned programs and activities have achieved the outcomes outlined in the strategic planning documents. This observation indicates that the implementation of the restructuring policy may not have been fully effective in enhancing organizational effectiveness.  

The objectives of this research are to understand the relationship between the restructuring policy implementation and organizational effectiveness, as well as to assess the magnitude of the restructuring policy's influence on organizational effectiveness within the Secretariat of Manado District.  

Findings indicate that the implementation of restructuring policies exhibits a functional, positive, and highly significant correlation with the organizational effectiveness of the Secretariat. Furthermore, the application of these restructuring policies has contributed to a substantial improvement in organizational effectiveness. This suggests that the restructuring policies governing district administrative instruments, as stipulated in Government Regulation No. 41 of 2007, have exerted a beneficial impact on the effectiveness of the district secretariat’s operations.  

Keywords: restructuring policy implementation, organizational effectiveness

This study aimed to examine the technologies implemented and the production value associated with aquaculture activities in the waters of Lake Tondano, as well as to identify the factors affecting aquaculture production in the lake. Data collection encompassed both primary and secondary sources. Primary data were obtained through surveys conducted with fish farmers residing around Lake Tondano. Information regarding aquaculture operations was gathered via interviews with fish farmers and direct observations. Secondary data were sourced from various institutions, including the Minahasa Fisheries Office, the Office of the Village Head, and the Fish Farmer Group Administrative Centre. The collected data were analyzed descriptively and presented using tabulations and various diagrammatic models. Fluctuations in aquaculture production value and the number of operational cage net units (KJT) from 2001 to 2014 were analyzed using linear regression and correlation techniques. In 2014, the aquaculture production value of Lake Tondano was estimated at 1,227.3 tons per year, with only 1,203 KJT units in operation. A consistent decline in production value was observed from 2003 to 2014. Statistical analyses revealed an annual decrease of approximately 1.236 tons in aquaculture production and a reduction of 607 operational KJT units over the period from 2001 to 2014. Strong correlations were identified between time (year) and both aquaculture production and the number of operational KJT units. Three principal factors were found to influence the aquaculture production value of Lake Tondano: environmental, technical, and economic factors, with economic factors emerging as the primary determinant. Specifically, the high cost of formulated fish diets coupled with the low market price of the harvested fish constituted major challenges, rendering fish farmers unable to cover investment and operational expenses. Additionally, environmental degradation of Lake Tondano's waters had a significant negative impact on aquaculture operations.  
Keywords: Production, technology, aquaculture, Lake Tondano

Marketing communication constitutes a critical component for organizations striving to achieve their objectives. It is imperative for companies to strategically utilize and maximize the benefits derived from marketing communication efforts. This is particularly true for banks, as financial institutions, where marketing communication plays a pivotal role in driving success, enhancing customer awareness, and fostering customer retention. The present study aims to (1) identify the constituent elements of marketing communication employed by PT Bank SulutGo and (2) determine, from the customers’ perspective, which element most significantly influences their decision to purchase saving products offered by Bank SulutGo. Employing a descriptive research design with qualitative methods, this investigation is grounded in the theoretical frameworks of the marketing communication mix and integrated marketing communication. The study’s informants comprised ten customers holding various types of saving accounts at PT Bank SulutGo. Findings reveal that the marketing communication elements of advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and public relations all impact customers' purchasing decisions. Among these, personal selling emerged as the most influential factor prompting customers to acquire saving products from Bank SulutGo. Consequently, it is recommended that the management of Bank SulutGo prioritize enhancing the quality of personal selling to attract a broader customer base and thereby support the bank’s growth.  
Keywords: marketing communication, bank, integrated marketing communication

This study originates from the initial observation that the procedures involved in the implementation and determination of civil servant transfers within the local government of North Halmahera Regency exhibit a lack of transparency. Consequently, this research aims not only to address issues related to the transparency of civil servant transfers but also to examine how the principle of transparency is applied in the execution of employee transfers at the Regional Personnel Agency (BKD) of North Halmahera Regency. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative approach, the study selected twelve informants based on their level of understanding of the research problem. These informants comprised representatives from the BKD, several related SKPD units, members of the DPRD commission concerned, and members of the press. Data collection methods included observation, documentation review, and interviews. Data processing and analysis were conducted continuously, from the initial collection phase through to data verification, by utilizing interactive techniques.

The findings indicate that (1) information pertaining to the formulation and implementation of public policies, including data on civil servant transfers, is generally adequate, accessible, and timely. However, such information is often classified as "confidential," particularly details regarding the process and criteria for selecting civil servants for transfer. (2) Enhanced transparency of information can improve public understanding and awareness of the processes, procedures, requirements, and rationale underlying civil servant transfers. Among the factors influencing civil servant transfers is the necessity to fill vacant positions. Notably, increased transparency correlates with a modest improvement in public trust in the government. Furthermore, the heightened public trust appears significantly associated with greater satisfaction.

In conclusion, transparency in the context of civil servant transfers positively impacts community knowledge, insight, trust, and participation in regional development. Such participation specifically involves critical engagement whereby the public reports civil servants who should be transferred due to deviations in conduct. The study recommends that the processes and procedures governing civil servant transfers be conducted in a transparent and open manner, grounded in a needs assessment conducted by SKPD units or upon their request, rather than influenced by extraneous factors. Moreover, the establishment of a strategically positioned, neutral partner organization to oversee personnel reform processes within the local government is essential to prevent corrupt practices, collusion, and nepotism (KKN) during the transfer process.

Keywords: Transparency, Employee Transfer

In the study of Kanji characters in the Japanese language, three primary aspects warrant attention: the method of writing, the method of reading, and the associated meanings. Among these, the reading of Kanji presents considerable challenges, largely due to its subdivision into three distinct categories: onyomi and kunyomi, which pertain to the on and kun readings, respectively. The onyomi reading originates from Chinese pronunciations, whereas the kunyomi reading is derived from indigenous Japanese linguistic traditions. Typically, onyomi is applied to compound words composed of two or more Kanji characters combined to yield a novel term with a unique meaning. In contrast, kunyomi generally pertains to individual Kanji characters that function independently, each possessing inherent meaning without necessitating combination with other characters. A crucial element in mastering Kanji reading lies in clearly distinguishing the semantic differences between vocabulary arising from combined Kanji (onyomi) and those represented by standalone characters (kunyomi). This understanding facilitates accurate translation of newly encountered vocabulary during sentence interpretation. Furthermore, it enhances proficiency in utilizing Kanji dictionaries and aids in recognizing unfamiliar terms within translated texts. To discern when Kanji should be read using the onyomi or kunyomi reading, it is essential to focus on several key factors, which will be outlined subsequently.

This study aims to determine whether the ad hoc agency selection process is running as it should and to find out what are the inhibiting factors in the ad hoc agency selection process in Tomohon City. This research was conducted from March to November 2022. The research used a qualitative approach by conducting in-depth interviews with 10 informants. Secondary data was obtained from related agencies, namely through the General Election Commission (GEC) of Tomohon City. Secondary data was also obtained through books obtained from local bookstores and the internet via Google Scholar in the form of books, journal articles and theses related to the topic of this research, namely the selection of ad hoc bodies. The results of the research show that there is still a lack of socialization by the GEC so that the interest of residents to become an ad hoc body is still lacking. One of the obstacles that is often encountered during the selection process is selector constraints, namely the difficulty in getting qualified selectors, honest and able to provide an objective assessment, especially when selection at the level of the Voting Committee (VC) and Voting Organizing Group (VOG), the closeness factor is still very influential when the selection process took place, this is what caused many members of the Tomohon GEC ad hoc body to be dismissed.

Enhancing the quality of public services necessitates civil servants who possess not only adequate quantity but also requisite professional competence and moral integrity, aligning closely with societal demands. Therefore, human resource development within government institutions must focus on advancing professional skills and fostering professional ethics, accompanied by a strong commitment to public service. This study aims to examine the impact of the professionalism of village government officials on the quality of public services in Malalayang One Village, Malalayang District, Manado City.  

The research employed a diagnostic analytical design utilizing a descriptive-quantitative approach combined with an explanatory survey. The selection of quantitative and explanatory descriptive-survey methods was justified by the study’s focus on contemporary social phenomena and the investigation of causal relationships between variables. The population comprised all village officials and service users in Malalayang One Village. Through purposive sampling, a total of 30 respondents were selected, consisting of 15 village government officials and 15 community members who utilize public services.  

Findings from this study reveal a strong positive correlation between the level of professionalism among village officials and the enhancement of public service quality. These results are corroborated by a simple linear regression analysis, yielding the equation Y = 2.062 + 1.040X, and a product moment correlation coefficient (r) of 0.809, indicating a significant relationship between the variables.  

Keywords: Professionalism, Public Service Quality

This study aimed to quantify the abundance and analyze the species distribution of ebony trees (Diospyros spp.) within the Animals Rescue Center of Tasikoki. The research was conducted over a six-month period, from March to September 2015, in Watudambo Village, Kauditan District, North Minahasa Regency. Data collection employed a census approach, whereby all vegetation resembling ebony species within the designated area was systematically observed, beginning from a predetermined starting point and continuing until the entire region had been surveyed. Field observations identified two ebony species: Diospyros maritima and Diospyros ebenum, with total counts of 1,864 and 63 individuals, respectively. Diospyros maritima individuals were categorized into four growth stages: 1,499 seedlings, 249 stakes, 98 poles, and 18 trees. The majority of these growth stages were located in dry, non-flooded areas adjacent to the coastline. Similarly, Diospyros ebenum specimens were classified into three growth stages: 4 seedlings, 54 saplings, and 5 poles, predominantly found in the same dry, non-flooded coastal zones within the Animals Rescue Center of Tasikoki. 

Keywords: Diospyros spp., species distribution, growth stages, Animals Rescue Center of Tasikoki

The purpose of this research was to determine differences in sulforaphane content in sprouts, cauliflower seedlings, mature plants from white flower cabbage, broccoli, cabbage and Chinese cabbage. This research was conducted in Tomohon and analyzed in the Chemistry laboratory of the State Polytechnic of Malang. The research method used was a randomized block design with 4 treatments, namely broccoli, white cauliflower, rock cabbage and Chinese cabbage with 3 repetitions in each growth phase. The results of the analysis of sulforaphane content in the growth phase of sprouts were the highest in broccoli, which was 117.08 ug, higher than white cauliflower (0.72 ug), rock cabbage (16.58 ug) and Chinese cabbage 0.38 ug). Furthermore, in the young plant phase the highest sulforaphane content in broccoli was 0.679 ug compared to white cauliflower (0.018 ug), rock cabbage (0.183 ug), and Chinese cabbage (0.003 ug). Then lastly, the highest sulforaphane content in mature plants was rock cabbage, which was 0.776 ug compared to broccoli (0.148 ug), white cauliflower (0.273 ug), and Chinese cabbage (0.001 ug). So the sulforaphane content in the sprouting phase of broccoli was higher than that of white cauliflower, rock cabbage and cabbage sprouts. Similarly, in young plants and in mature plants, rock cabbage showed higher sulforaphan content.

This study, titled "Connotative Meaning in the Speeches of Donald John Trump," explores the connotative meanings present in the speeches delivered by Donald John Trump. The research addresses two primary questions: first, what types of linguistic forms exhibiting connotative meanings are found in Donald Trump's speeches; and second, what are the functions of these connotative meanings within his discourse. The objective of this investigation is to identify and categorize the various linguistic forms as well as to analyze and elucidate the functions of connotative meaning in Donald John's speeches. Data were collected from several of Trump's speeches, including his Inauguration Speech on January 21, 2021, addresses to the United Nations General Assembly, the 2020 State of the Union annual address, and his Farewell speech delivered from the White House. The theoretical framework underpinning the analysis is based on Geoffrey Leech’s (1981) semantic theory. The study involved identifying and classifying relevant phrases and sentences before conducting a detailed analysis of their connotative meanings. The findings reveal the presence of 40 phrases containing connotative meanings. Among these, 14 phrases serve an informational function, 13 an expressive function, 10 an aesthetic function, 2 a phatic function, and 1 a directive function.  
Keywords: Connotative Meaning, Semantic Analysis, Donald John Trump's Speeches

The increasing challenges associated with prolonging life expectancy warrant careful consideration, particularly given the steadily growing elderly population. Elderly health initiatives aim to maintain and enhance the health and functional capacities of older adults, thereby enabling them to remain productive. In this context, government efforts have focused on organizing sports and health programs for the elderly within community health centers to optimize their quality of life. The present study seeks to investigate the challenges and obstacles encountered in the implementation of elderly sports health programs at community health centers in Manado City. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through in-depth interviews and observations involving key informants, including the heads of health centers and coordinators of sports health programs at these centers. Findings reveal that only four community health centers have prioritized the implementation of such programs, whereas the majority have yet to do so due to various challenges and barriers. It is concluded that to address these challenges, health centers must ensure the availability of well-trained personnel in terms of both quantity and competency, secure adequate funding from operational health support budgets to comprehensively carry out activities, and provide the necessary facilities and infrastructure for program execution. To overcome obstacles, community health centers should conduct outreach efforts to raise awareness among the elderly and their families regarding the benefits of sports health programs, and foster collaborations with community organizations to support program implementation collectively. 

**Keywords:** Sports Health, Elderly, Community Health Center, Challenges, Obstacles

This study, titled "An Error Analysis of Simple Past Tense in Students' Journals: A Case Study in Written English II," aims to identify, categorize, and analyze the types of errors present in the use of the simple past tense within students' journals from a Written English II course. The research seeks to contribute to the enhancement of language acquisition processes and to provide insights that will deepen the understanding of the errors encountered in the application of the simple past tense. Employing a qualitative methodology, the study was conducted through several stages, beginning with a comprehensive review of theoretical frameworks on the simple past tense, as well as an examination of prior related studies. Ellis’s theoretical model was adopted to guide the analysis of students' usage of the simple past tense in their journal entries. Data were collected from Written English II students through a test administered by the instructor, which required them to compose journals. The analysis involved several techniques, including error identification, classification, description, and correction. Findings reveal the presence of three primary types of errors: omission, misinformation, and misordering, which predominantly stem from students’ insufficient mastery of correct English sentence structures. While the students are capable of constructing sentences, they frequently fail to apply the appropriate grammatical patterns accurately.  
Keywords: simple past tense, error analysis, omission, misinformation, misordering.

This study aimed to evaluate the competence of District Officers in delivering administrative services related to land sale and purchase deeds to residents in the Tikala District of Manado City. Employing a qualitative research approach, the study selected ten informants comprising members of the public, community leaders, and government officials within Sub Tikala. The findings indicate that, overall, the officers possess satisfactory technical skills, including knowledge pertinent to the administrative processes and regulatory requirements involved in land sale and purchase deed services. This knowledge facilitates more efficient service delivery to the community. However, a subset of officers demonstrated insufficient understanding of their responsibilities in this domain. Nevertheless, colleagues consistently provided support to mitigate any potential disruption in service provision. In terms of social skills, officers generally exhibited strong capabilities, effectively interpreting others' motives and collaborating with peers in executing land deed administrative duties. Additionally, the officers showed an adequate level of conceptual ability, enabling them to comprehend the organizational complexities inherent in their work.  
Keywords: performance, administration

The incidence of violence among school-age children in Indonesia reached 84% in 2015, according to the Convention on the Regulation of Whaling (ICRW). This study aims to enhance the researcher's capabilities, provide informational data and reference materials for future investigations, and serve as a data source for the Ministry of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection (Ministry PPA). The objective was to assess the attitudes toward and preventive measures against violence among teachers at Christian Elementary School Tabitha 2 in Manado. 

A descriptive qualitative research design was employed. The study population consisted of ten teachers, with eight participating in in-depth interviews and six engaging in focus group discussions (FGDs). Participants ranged in age from 35 to 57 years. Findings revealed that several teachers had provided counseling to both victims and perpetrators of violence. Prevention strategies unanimously supported by the teachers involved religious approaches. 

In conclusion, insights derived from the in-depth interviews and FGDs indicate that the teachers at Christian Elementary School Tabitha 2 in Manado initially inquire about the issues faced by children and subsequently take follow-up actions, including reporting to relevant authorities. Preventive measures primarily incorporate religious guidance and frequent counseling of children. It is recommended that the government play a more proactive role in socializing and raising awareness about violence prevention.

In the context of increasing globalization and intensified competition, organizations must enhance their performance and adaptability to sustain their competitive position. This competitive pressure extends beyond the manufacturing sector to the service industry, with the hotel sector experiencing particularly heightened rivalry. Consequently, Travello Hotel must develop a distinct competitive advantage. To achieve this, the hotel needs to improve operational efficiency by managing activities effectively without compromising service quality provided to customers. The approach employed to optimize activity management and thereby attain efficiency is known as Activity-Based Management (ABM).

This study focuses on the room division of Travello Hotel in Manado. Employing a descriptive research design, it examines all activities within the room division, categorizing them into value-added and non-value-added activities. Non-value-added activities were either eliminated or consolidated with similar value-added activities to reduce non-value-added costs. The research utilized quantitative data, specifically the cost reports from the room division for the year 2012, complemented by qualitative data such as tools and resources available to the hotel.

The findings indicate that implementing Activity-Based Management enables Travello Hotel to minimize non-value-added costs, thereby enhancing operational efficiency without reducing the quality of customer service. As a result, the total expenses in the room division decreased by Rp. 176,226,624.08, from Rp. 3,576,508,933.00 to Rp. 3,400,282,308.92.

Mangroves, as a vital group of coastal plants, provide numerous ecological and societal benefits. These plants typically grow along shorelines and are influenced by tidal fluctuations. This study was conducted in Gamlamo Village, Jailolo Sub-district, West Halmahera Regency, North Maluku Province, with the objective of analyzing the community structure of mangroves and identifying the mangrove species present in this area. The research employed the line transect method, establishing three stations within the study site, each containing two line transects, resulting in a total of six transects. Furthermore, within each transect, five quadrats measuring 10 x 10 cm² were systematically placed. 

The findings revealed the presence of three mangrove species across the three stations: Rhizophora mucronata, Sonneratia alba, and Bruguiera gymnorrhiza. Among these, R. mucronata exhibited the highest density at station 2, with a value of 0.36 individuals per square meter and a relative density of 60%. Additionally, the greatest frequency was recorded at station 2 for R. mucronata, with a frequency of 1 individual per square meter and a relative frequency of 41.67%. The highest dominance was observed at station 1 for S. alba, with a dominance value of 52.89 m² and a relative dominance of 53.31%. The highest Importance Value Index (IVI) was found for R. mucronata at station 2, with a value of 136.57%, followed by B. gymnorrhiza at station 3. Regarding species diversity, the highest diversity index (H') of 1.03 was recorded at station 1, while the lowest index of 0.95 was observed at station 2.

Keywords: Gamlamo Village, Mangrove, Community Structure

This study investigates the attitudes of farmer groups toward the Gernas Kakao program in the Bolaang Mongondow Utara District. Conducted over a three-month period from April to June 2017, the research focused on this specific district. Primary data were collected via interviews with five farmer groups selected through purposive sampling, comprising three groups of advanced farmers and two groups of novice farmers. Each group included six members—namely the chairman, secretary, treasurer, and three additional members—resulting in a total sample of 30 respondents. Secondary data were sourced from the Office of Agriculture and the District Office of Bolaang Mongondow Utara. A descriptive analytical approach was employed to interpret the data. Findings indicate that farmers’ attitudes toward the Gernas Kakao program, across both beginner and advanced groups, were generally positive, with participants strongly agreeing that the program’s activities in intensification, rejuvenation, and rehabilitation contributed to increased cocoa production. Nevertheless, some farmers expressed disagreement with the program, largely due to infrequent participation in counseling and guidance sessions led by extension agents, which led to disparities in knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors compared to more actively involved farmers. Additionally, hesitation to adopt new technologies, stemming from fear of production failure, was particularly observed among beginner farmer groups, who preferred traditional cultivation methods. These results underscore the necessity for extension workers and facilitators to engage in efforts aimed at transforming farmers' mindsets to enhance program acceptance and effectiveness.

A disaster constitutes an event or a series of events that pose a threat to and disrupt the lives of individuals, arising from natural and/or anthropogenic factors, including human activities. Such events result in human casualties, environmental degradation, property damage, and psychological effects. The traumatic experiences stemming from disasters can fundamentally alter the local community's perception of their place of residence where the disaster has occurred. This study employs several analytical techniques, including the Likert scale, descriptive statistics, the Spearman rank correlation test, and the chi-square test. The Likert scale analysis, conducted manually using a specific formula, serves to quantify respondents' opinions, while descriptive analysis summarizes the questionnaire findings. Additionally, the chi-square and Spearman rank correlation tests are utilized to assess the consistency of respondents’ answers in relation to their perceptions, preferences, and emotional responses. The findings indicate that the community in the city of Palu is capable of resilience and adaptation, provided mutual support is sustained; consequently, residents continue to prefer remaining in Palu, equipped with the ability to implement appropriate and effective mitigation measures. 

Keywords: Public perception, Likert scale, Spearman rank test, chi-square test.

In Bolaang Mongondow Regency, locally generated revenue remains relatively low and has not demonstrated significant growth. One of the regional government work units (SKPD) responsible for generating local revenue (PAD) is the Tourism and Culture Office. In 2018, this office failed to meet its revenue targets. The present study seeks to: (1) identify the factors contributing to the shortfall in revenue realization, and (2) evaluate the effectiveness of the office’s revenue performance. A quantitative descriptive research design was employed. Qualitative data, derived from interview explanations, complemented the quantitative data obtained from budget realization reports and ticket inventory records covering the period 2016 to 2018. Data collection involved both interviews and document analysis. Findings indicate that the failure to achieve revenue targets primarily resulted from unrealistically high income targets imposed on the office, despite the limited scope of revenue sources under its management. Regarding performance effectiveness, the results reveal very effective categories in 2016 and 2017, with respective realizations of 113.29% and 102.93%, whereas 2018 fell into the ineffective category, with a realization rate of 69.92%. It is recommended that the Tourism and Culture Office enhance its financial management strategies, focusing particularly on the development of new tourist attractions, to achieve set targets and improve the overall effectiveness of its revenue performance.

Efficiency is important in landing with the aim that the catch as soon as possible reaches the hands of consumers in good quality condition. The research was carried out at the Fish Landing Base, Dumai City, Riau Province, from June 5-25, 2021. The material in the research object was a sondong fishing boat, while the equipment needed was stationery, a stopwatch, a camera, and a laptop. The data collected are basic data, namely unloading time, effective time, wasted time, and supporting data, namely fleet size (GT), number of fish landed (kg), number of unloading personnel (people), and age of activity actors (years). The efficiency of the landing time of the catch using sondong fishing gear at the fish landing base in the city of Dumai is classified into the less efficient category, while the factors that influence fishing productivity are fishing experience, crew, and fishing time.

The issue of border delimitation represents a critical challenge for any nation, particularly for those whose territories share direct (mainland) or indirect (maritime) boundaries with neighboring states. In 2002, Indonesia faced a significant setback when the International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled that the islands of Sipadan and Ligitan belonged to Malaysia. Consequently, Indonesia forfeited sovereignty over these two outer islands adjacent to its neighboring country. As an archipelagic state, Indonesia presently possesses 92 islands bordering countries such as Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Australia, Timor-Leste, and Papua New Guinea. Following the ruling on Sipadan and Ligitan, concerns have arisen regarding the future status of Indonesia’s other outer islands, with fears that they may suffer a similar fate. Among these islands is Miangas, which is administratively part of North Sulawesi and located in close proximity to the territorial waters of the Philippines. To address these apprehensions, both the local government of the Talaud Islands and the central government of the Republic of Indonesia have undertaken development initiatives on Miangas Island. These efforts include the construction of facilities and infrastructure, particularly those related to border security, thereby reinforcing Indonesia’s sovereignty over the island. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology commonly utilized in social sciences such as anthropology, with a focus on phenomenology to explore the meanings embedded within social phenomena, this study seeks to elucidate the significance of development activities in the Indonesia-Philippines border region. Furthermore, it aims to assess whether such development aligns with the inherent characteristics and needs of the Miangas community or is driven primarily by political considerations that overlook local conditions. 

Keywords: Border, Miangas, Development

This study aimed to examine and analyze the effects of the Current Ratio, Debt to Asset Ratio, Inventory Turnover, and Company Size on the profitability of Property and Real Estate companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the period from 2012 to 2016, both individually and collectively. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the population consisted of 46 Property and Real Estate companies registered on the IDX within the specified timeframe. Utilizing purposive sampling, the study selected a sample of 31 companies, resulting in 155 observations. The findings revealed that, individually, the Current Ratio did not exert a significant impact on profitability. Similarly, the Debt to Asset Ratio showed no significant partial effect, and Inventory Turnover also failed to demonstrate a significant influence when assessed separately. While Company Size exhibited a positive relationship with profitability, this effect was not statistically significant. Furthermore, when analyzed simultaneously, the Current Ratio, Debt to Asset Ratio, Inventory Turnover, and Company Size collectively did not significantly affect the profitability of Property and Real Estate companies listed on the IDX for the period 2012 to 2016.

Keywords: Current Ratio (CR), Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR), Inventory Turnover, Company Size, Profitability

Repeat purchase refers to the act of buying the same product or brand that a consumer has previously purchased. Such behavior is often driven by routine and habitual decision-making processes, whereby the need to seek additional information diminishes over time. Various factors, both internal and external, influence consumer repeat purchase behavior. For businesses, particularly within the food industry, cultivating a customer base that consistently repurchases products requires a deliberate process. This study seeks to examine the repeat purchase behavior of consumers at Grill House Mdc and to identify the key factors motivating this behavior among its customers. Employing a qualitative methodology, the research involved conducting in-depth interviews with 20 informants. Data analysis was guided by several indicators, including relationship intimacy and trust, consumer satisfaction, quality of service, product quality, pricing, and consumer needs. Salted eggs are eggs preserved through a marination process. Incorporating ginger extract into the salting solution has been shown to enhance lipase enzyme activity, which can consequently reduce the fat content. Additionally, the inclusion of white turmeric in food products contributes to maintaining freshness and nutritional quality, improving palatability, and extending shelf life. This study employed a completely randomized design (CRD) featuring two factors: the ratio of ginger extract to turmeric extract (100 mL:50 mL, 75 mL:75 mL, and 50 mL:100 mL), and the curing duration (7, 14, and 20 days). The primary objective was to develop salted eggs that are preferred by consumers. The optimal formulation consisted of 100 mL ginger extract combined with 50 mL turmeric extract, cured for 14 days. The chemical composition of the egg yolk under these conditions included water content of 34.18%, fat content of 26.13%, peroxide value of 6.03%, free fatty acids (FFA) at 0.16%, and a pH of 6.1. Sensory evaluation of the egg yolk yielded scores for color (3.84), texture (3.84), ginger flavor (3.84), turmeric flavor (3.16), and overall preference by panelists (4.68). For the egg white, the chemical properties were as follows: water content 82.39%, fat content 0.076%, peroxide value 0.791%, FFA 0.16%, and pH 8.45. Sensory ratings for the egg white were color (3.84), texture (3.84), ginger flavor (3.00), turmeric flavor (3.16), and overall panelist preference (3.84). 

Keywords: ginger, extended curing, salted egg, turmeric.

The enactment of the Regional Autonomy Law, effective since 1999, is fundamentally based on the region's potential, preferences, and democratic aspirations, encompassing the active participation of the local community. One avenue for development and natural resource conservation within this framework is ecotourism. Ecotourism, as a tourism model, is closely aligned with conservation principles and integrates conservation strategies into its development efforts. Consequently, ecotourism serves as an effective and precise means of preserving the integrity and authenticity of local ecosystems. 

This study focuses on the implementation strategies of ecotourism in the city of Manado. Employing qualitative research methods, the investigation incorporates a SWOT analysis to evaluate internal and external factors influencing ecotourism development. Internal factors include strengths and weaknesses: strengths encompass the presence of potential natural tourist attractions, human resource training initiatives, tourism-related events and activities, public awareness regarding tourism, and improved accessibility to tourist sites. Conversely, weaknesses involve limited budgets, a shortage of capital and human resource expertise, inadequate transportation facilities and infrastructure, coastal reclamation issues in Manado Bay, and insufficient government policies or regulations to sustain ecotourism programs.

External factors consist of opportunities and threats. Opportunities arise from advancements in information technology, the growth of hotels and inns, and external investment. Threats include competition from other tourist destinations, negative publicity surrounding Manado city, and the risk of natural disasters.

Based on the SWOT analysis, six strategic recommendations are proposed: enhancing productivity within the tourism sector; increasing promotion and competitiveness; developing the potential of natural tourist attractions while improving access management and information dissemination; fostering cooperation with investors; formulating supportive policies for tourism development; and strengthening human resources through expert recruitment in the tourism sector.

Keywords: ecotourism implementation strategies, Manado city, SWOT analysis.

Generation Z, defined as individuals born between 1995 and 2010, represents the cohort succeeding the millennial generation. As a result, Generation Z has attracted considerable attention from researchers and marketers aiming to identify the defining traits of this group, given their substantial influence on older generations and their role as trendsetters across various industries. 

The present study seeks to examine the impact of price and social media on the consumptive behavior of Generation Z in the context of apparel purchases. Employing a sample of 100 Generation Z university students from the Faculty of Economics and Business at Sam Ratulangi University, Manado, data were gathered using an online questionnaire administered via Google Forms. Utilizing a quantitative research design, the analysis was conducted through Multiple Linear Regression (MLR). The findings indicate that social media exerts a significant influence on the consumptive behavior of Generation Z prior to making apparel purchase decisions. It is recommended that members of Generation Z enhance their financial literacy skills to foster more informed consumption practices.

Keywords: Generation Z, price, social media, consumptive behavior

Working capital holds a critical role in the operation of any enterprise, as it is essential for financing the day-to-day activities of a business. Effective management of working capital is necessary to ensure smooth operational processes and to achieve the anticipated optimal profitability of the company. This study aims to analyze and assess the adequacy of the working capital ratio at PT. HM Sampoerna Tbk. According to Sutrisno (2009), working capital constitutes a vital asset component within a company, without which the organization cannot meet the requirements for conducting its operations. 

The research adopts a descriptive quantitative approach, employing the Working Capital Adequacy Ratio as the analytical tool, which encompasses three specific ratios: Total Assets to Net Working Capital, Current Liabilities to Net Working Capital, and Working Capital Turnover. Secondary data for the analysis were sourced from the financial statements of PT. HM Sampoerna Tbk, specifically the balance sheet and income statement. 

The findings indicate that the Total Assets to Net Working Capital ratio from 2013 to 2016 reflects a satisfactory performance. Similarly, the Current Liabilities to Net Working Capital ratio was deemed adequate in 2013 and 2014; however, it showed a decline in 2015 and 2016, with values of 0.17 and 0.23 respectively. The Working Capital Turnover ratio experienced an increase in 2014 but subsequently declined in 2015 and 2016, suggesting a relatively more effective liquidity ratio during those periods. 

Overall, the working capital management at PT. HM Sampoerna Tbk can be characterized as robust. The analysis of the working capital adequacy ratio offers valuable insights into the company’s ability to manage its working capital effectively. The liquidity position of PT. HM Sampoerna Tbk remains satisfactory, indicating a stable level of working capital adequacy. It is recommended that the company continues to utilize and allocate its working capital efficiently to support coverage of short-term liabilities, thereby optimizing profit generation in each fiscal period.

Keywords: Working Capital, Net Working Capital, Working Capital Ratio

Increment refers to the growth in diameter, basal area, height, volume, or monetary value of a tree or stand over a specified time interval. The primary objective was to characterize the initial growth increment of mahogany stands (Swietenia macrophylla King). Trees were selected as samples using a purposive sampling technique, focusing on individuals whose growth had not been compromised by pest infestation or mechanical damage such as wind breakage. This study seeks to examine the restitution of state financial losses in the context of investigative audits and audits focused on the calculation of such losses. The investigation is conducted from the perspective of auditors representing Indonesia's National Government Internal Audit of North Sulawesi Province. Employing a qualitative research methodology with an exploratory approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews. Key informants were selected via purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria to ensure the acquisition of accurate and precise information. Interview data were transcribed, subsequently analyzed, coded, and organized into thematic categories using content analysis techniques.

The findings reveal several key points: (1) the restitution of state financial losses in investigative audits or audits calculating these losses is not a routine practice among auditors during the execution of their duties; (2) factors influencing the restitution include the good faith or remorse demonstrated by involved parties, the expectation that such restitution may negate or decrease the amount of state financial losses, and the hope for mitigation or abolition of criminal sanctions; (3) although no explicit regulation prohibits the reimbursement of state financial losses prior to the issuance of investigative audit reports or calculation audits, auditors and law enforcement officials generally adhere to the provisions stipulated in Article 4 of Law Number 31 of 1999 concerning the Eradication of Corruption Crimes; (4) the restitution of state financial losses during investigative audits does not impact the auditors’ conclusions nor does it diminish the quantified value of state losses incurred; and (5) such restitution in the audit of the calculation of state financial losses similarly does not influence the audit process or the resulting calculations made by auditors.

This study aimed to (1) characterize the morphometric features of the pearl oyster *Pinctada margaritifera* in the waters of Arakan, Mantehage Bango, and Talengen within North Sulawesi Province, and (2) identify the most suitable site for the potential development of pearl oyster aquaculture. Sampling locations were selected using purposive sampling techniques. Morphometric measurements of the shell included shell length, shell height, hinge length, shell thickness, and shell weight. Additionally, water quality parameters assessed comprised temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, pH, and depth.

In Arakan waters, the shell length of *P. margaritifera* ranged from 44.25 mm to 169.77 mm, with an average of 86.50 mm. In Mantehage Bango waters, shell length ranged from 38.73 mm to 106.09 mm, averaging 80.31 mm, while in Talengen waters, shell length varied between 25.89 mm and 105.34 mm, with a mean of 68.97 mm. The Arakan site was predominantly inhabited by medium-sized *P. margaritifera* individuals (53.78%), suggesting the presence of natural oyster stocks suitable for aquaculture purposes.

Assessment of the environmental suitability for *P. margaritifera* cultivation indicated that Arakan waters achieved a suitability score of 77.7%, classified as suitable (S2). Mantehage Bango waters scored 80%, also denoted as suitable (S2), whereas Talengen waters obtained a score of 68.8%, categorized as conditional suitability (S3).

Background: Adolescents often possess limited knowledge and credible information necessary to navigate the challenges inherent in this developmental stage. This deficiency may place them at a disadvantage, increasing susceptibility to risky behaviors. Adequate understanding of the reproductive system can foster greater responsibility among adolescents and enable them to avoid harmful conduct. Such knowledge enhances their awareness of permissible and impermissible actions relating to reproductive health.

Objective: The present study aims to examine the level of knowledge and sources of information regarding the reproductive system among students at Public High School 1 in Remboken.

Methodology: Employing a descriptive research design and convenience sampling technique, data were collected from 185 participants. Respondents completed a questionnaire utilizing an ordinal scale, and the resulting data were analyzed descriptively.

Results: Findings indicate that, overall, the respondents demonstrated acquisition of reproductive system knowledge, as evidenced by 84 participants. Furthermore, access to reproductive health information was affirmed by 86 respondents. Parental guidance was also significant, with 100 respondents reporting that they received reproductive system information from their parents.

Conclusion: Adolescents have obtained and accessed appropriate information concerning the reproductive system, attributable to the influence of media and parental involvement.

Recommendation: It is imperative to increase the frequency of educational campaigns targeting adolescent reproductive health knowledge to disseminate credible information effectively. Such initiatives are anticipated to enhance adolescents’ awareness and responsible behavior regarding reproductive health.

Utilizing data from the Indonesian Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) spanning 2017 to 2019, the construction sector demonstrated a positive contribution to the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP). However, this sector experienced a decline of 4.52% in the third quarter of 2020. The contraction intensified by the final quarter of 2020, with a recorded decrease of 5.67%. Despite this, the construction sector observed a modest recovery in 2021, growing at rates of 4.42% and 3.84% in the first and second quarters, respectively. Persistent declines in company performance raise concerns regarding potential financial distress, which may ultimately culminate in corporate bankruptcy. Financial ratios serve as critical tools for analyzing financial distress and function as predictive models in this regard. This study aims to examine the influence of several financial ratios—namely, Working Capital to Total Assets (WCTA), Retained Earnings to Total Assets (RETA), Earnings Before Interest and Taxes to Total Assets (EBITTA), and Book Value of Equity to Book Value of Total Debt (BVETD)—on the financial distress status of construction firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange between 2017 and 2021. The findings, derived from multinomial logit regression analysis, indicate that the WCTA ratio significantly predicts financial distress, whereas RETA and EBITTA ratios do not exhibit a statistically significant effect in forecasting financial distress conditions.

This study aims to describe how farmers carry out a strategy of life on three groups of farmer: upper layer, middle layer and peasant farmers to finance their family daily life. This research was conducted in the urban village of Pandu, Sub-District Bunaken, Manado City. Most of them live from farming activities. The research was conducted in November 2015 through to March 2016. The primary data obtained from interviews to three (3) groups. Selection of the sample is purposive stratified sampling. Each group selected five respondents, so a total of 15 respondents. Collection of secondary data derived from the Urban Village Office of Pandu, Manado City. The results showed that the upper and middle groups of farmers tend to apply the accumulation strategy while consolidation strategy was not found. The two groups have incomes that exceed the needs of farming and of the results they could buy a cow, land or other assets. While farmers lower group implement survival strategies. This farmersgroup use their earnings for the daily needs of the family and the other half to farm. Limited income makes farmers can not save even they have to borrow money to supplement the family income either eat or buy school supplies for children.

This study explores the concept of freedom of the press in Indonesia through the theoretical frameworks of McCombs and Shaw's Agenda Setting Theory and Theodore Peterson's Social Responsibility Theory, employing qualitative research methods. The findings indicate that contemporary press freedom in Indonesia is largely situated within the broader context of democratic development. Currently, members of the press experience considerable liberty in seeking, managing, and disseminating news, although such freedom is inevitably accompanied by a corresponding responsibility regarding the content produced. The press remains one of the most influential agents in driving societal change, possessing a potent capacity either to steer society toward negative outcomes or to promote positive advancements. It is imperative that journalists continually enhance their professional skills and demonstrate a sustained commitment to improving the quality of their work. Moreover, freedom of the press in Indonesia is also shaped by the presence of media owners with substantial financial resources, which in turn affects news content. Consequently, journalistic output often reflects certain alignments, and truly independent journalism—characterized by accurate and unbiased reporting free from interference by media proprietors—has yet to be fully realized in Indonesia. 

Keywords: Press, Freedom of the Press

Development planning constitutes the initial and most critical phase in the broader process of development. It serves as the principal determinant of successful developmental outcomes within a country. Effective planning and thorough maturation of the planning process inevitably yield favorable results. Consequently, development planning must engage all stakeholders not merely as passive recipients but as active participants in the implementation of development initiatives. Public participation is essential in this context, acting as a bridge that connects government policies with community interests. Hence, regional planning should adopt a bottom-up or participatory model. Participatory planning seeks to incorporate the interests of the populace and actively involves them—both directly and indirectly—throughout the planning process. However, in practice, planning predominantly remains a top-down approach. This study aims to assess the extent of community participation in development planning within Kecamatan Ibu Selatan, Halmahera Barat District. Employing a descriptive method with a qualitative approach, the research findings derived from interviews indicate that community involvement is currently limited to the expression of ideas, suggestions, and opinions. To enhance community engagement in future development planning, more comprehensive socialization efforts are necessary to encourage greater active participation.  
Keywords: community participation

Television advertising has become a new force capable of influencing the audience to do what the advertisers want, and teenagers are very promising target for producers. This study investigated the influence of television advertising on teenagers purchase decision in Manado. This research aims to analyze (1) what is the impact of television advertising (Brand Preference, Peer Group, and Pester Power) on teenagers purchase decision; (2) which impact of television advertising (Brand Preference, Peer Group, and Pester Power) has the most significant influence on teenagers purchase decision; (3) is there any significant difference between male and female on teenagers purchase decision. Theories supporting the research are advertising and purchase decision. 100 respondents of the questionnaires were distributed to teenagers who live in Manado. The data obtained were analyzed using Multiple Linear Regression and Independent Sample t-test Analysis. The findings reveales that Brand Preference, Peer Group, and Pester Power have significant influence on teenagers purchase decision. Pester Power is the greatest factor that influence teenagers purchase decision and the least significant factor is Peer Group. There is significant difference between male and female for each factors. The result shows that the television advertising has a significant influence on purchase decision of teenagers. Keywords: television advertising, purchase decision, brand preference, peer group, pester power.

Background: Indonesia set targets for clean water usage and sanitation coverage at 68.9% and 63.5%, respectively, in 2015, in alignment with global commitments made at the 2002 Johannesburg Summit. However, research conducted by Jimmy Woodcock in 2011 revealed that only 20% of the Indonesian population had access to clean water. 

Method: This study aimed to describe water usage patterns among adolescents at the Children Development Center ID-127, located in Ranomuut District, Manado City. Employing a quantitative research design, the study surveyed a population of 90 respondents, comprising 41 males and 49 females, all aged between 11 and 15 years. Data were analyzed and presented through distribution tables.

Results: Findings indicate that 46.7% of the adolescents relied on municipal water supply services for their daily water needs. Approximately 65.6% used water filters to obtain drinking water, while 34.4% utilized alternative sources, with all such water being subjected to boiling prior to consumption. The majority consumed water that met physical quality standards, characterized by the absence of color, taste, and odor. Only 18.9% of respondents reported experiencing health complaints after using the water.

Conclusion: Enhancing adolescents’ awareness regarding the importance of clean water through targeted health promotion initiatives and fostering environmental support may contribute to ensuring safe and clean water consumption among this population.

Keywords: community, dengue fever, knowledge, Maen Village
