ABSTRACT This research entitled "Morphophonemic Process in English and Gorontalo Language: a Contrastive Analysis" aims at identifying, analyzing and describing the morphophonemic processes and finding out the similarities and the differences of morphophonemic processes in English and Gorontalo language by using of Crystal's (2008) and Nida's (1949) theory. The English data were collected from several English textbooks. Some of them areA Course in Modern Linguistics(1968) by Hockett,Zeitchrift für Anglistik und Amerikanistik (1969) by Lehnert,Introducing English Linguistics (2009) by Meyer, etc. and the data of Gorontalo language were collected frombooks such asMorfologi dan Sintaksis Bahasa Gorontalo (1988) by Alitu et all.,Kamus Bahasa Gorontalo Indonesia (2001) by Pateda, and Tata Bahasa sederhana Bahasa Gorontalo (2006) by Pateda and Pulubuhu and fivenative speakers at the age of 35-75 years old in Gorontalo. The results of this research shows that in morphophonemic process of English and Gorontalo language have some similarities anddifferences. The similarities are that both languages have kinds of morphophonemic processes. English has seven kinds of morphophonemic processes, they are assimilation, dissimilation, reduction of clusters, loss of consonant phonemes, loss of vowel phonemes, palatalization, and nasalization whereas in Gorontalo language six kinds of them found.The difference is no palatalization found in Gorontalo Language. Other similarities anddifferences are in dissimilation. English has six kinds of dissimilations, they are progressive, regressive, contiguous phonemes, noncontiguous phonemes, point of articulation, and manner of articulation whereas Gorontalo language has only five kinds of dissimilations and doesn't have contiguous phonemes. Keywords: Morphophonemic Process, English and Gorontalo Language, Contrastive Analysis.

This paper aims to examine the influence of the meeting of two cultures, namely the Eastern culture (Javanese) and the West (Europe mainly Dutch), which each have a different social structure. The Ducth culture has affected on rural community of Java. This study is based on the review of secondary data collected from literature. The problem addressed in this paper is, whether socio-political system of a traditional nature is still alive and give benefit to rural communities when the socio-economic development effort conducting at the present time? Based on the framework and Etzioni Tjondronegoro applied to the structure of community and leadership in Java, it can be concluded that: (1) Nepotism loosened in some places/villages in Java. However, in another village, it still preserved. (2) There is a marginalisation occured to the most vulnerable groups. (3) Sodality can still be found at the village level. (4) Congruent type in rural community in Java, which are still alive in certain villages, is a type of Nepotism-Faithful. It can conclude that, the socio-political system of traditional still life in Java and it has a tendency to marginalize the landless communities. For the development community agencies, they needs to consider a vulnerable groups to make sure that benefits of development can distribute equally.

Perfume is a product category often associated with premium pricing that signals quality and attracts consumers. However, as is common with high-value products, such pricing frequently motivates counterfeiters to replicate authentic perfumes. Perfumes are available in a diverse array of fragrances, each possessing distinct characteristics intended to cater to a variety of preferences, moods, and occasions. Additionally, perfume consumption can serve as an expression of specific lifestyles. The perceived value of perfume varies among consumers based on individual perceptions. This study aims to examine the differences in consumers’ perceived quality between counterfeit and original perfumes. Employing a comparative research design, data were collected from a sample of 100 respondents affiliated with the Faculty of Economics and Business at Sam Ratulangi University. Data analysis was conducted using an independent samples t-test via the SPSS software. The findings indicate a statistically significant difference in consumer perceptions, with original perfumes receiving more favorable evaluations than counterfeit alternatives. These results suggest that manufacturers of authentic perfumes should strategically consider the market dynamics in Manado, where consumers demonstrate a preference for genuine products over counterfeits.  
Keywords: consumer perceived quality, counterfeit perfume, original perfume

Sinar Galesong Mandiri Malalayang Manado for the workshop is still not appropriate, because in the calculation of the selling price of the service does not take into account the costs incurred by the company. Selling price of the service, so that the price is relatively cheap, will later increase the motor entry unit and will also increase sales volume.

THE EFFECT OF UTILIZATION OF ACETIC ACID (CH3COOH) SOLUTION IN SHRIMP WASTE MEAL PROCESSING AS A FEED ON CRUDE PROTEIN, CALCIUM AND PHOSPHORUS CONTENT.An experiment was conducted to determine the effect of different level of acetic acid solution in the processing of shrimp waste meal. Shrimp waste material was in the form of leftover meat, skin, head, and other unutilized parts of shrimp. Research was arranged using Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 4 treatments: A0 = distilled water without acetic acid solution, A1 = 5% acetic acid solution, A2 = 10% acetic acid solution, and A3 = 15% acetic acid solution. Each treatment was replicated 4 times. Tukey's test was employed to analyze treatment differences. Variable measured were: crude protein, calcium, and phosphorus content of shrimp waste. Research result showed that acetic acid solution level significantly affect protein, calcium, and phosphorus content of shrimp waste. Crude protein content of A2 was significantly (P < 0.05) higher compared with A0, A1, and A3, but significantly (P < 0.05) reduced calcium and phosphorus content of shrimp waste meal at the higher level. It can be concluded that utilization of 10% acetic acid solution in shrimp waste meal processing gave the best result with protein content of 56,37%, calcium 2,98%, and phosphorus 0,98%. Keywords :Shrimp waste meal, Acetic acid solution, Protein, Calcium, Phosphorus

This research seeks to evaluate the performance of the Tourism Office in the preparation of the Government Agency Performance Accountability Report (GAPAR) for South Minahasa Regency. The study was conducted at the Tourism Office of South Minahasa Regency. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research aims to depict the actual conditions of the subject under investigation, incorporate the perspectives of informants regarding the subject, and relate these insights to existing phenomena to derive pertinent conclusions. Informants were selected through purposive sampling, resulting in a total of seven participants. Data collection methods encompassed observation, interviews, and documentation. To ensure data validity, triangulation techniques were applied to assess credibility. The data analysis process involved data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Findings indicate that, according to performance indicators, several challenges persist in the preparation of GAPAR at the South Minahasa Regional Secretariat. These challenges include ineffective coordination and communication/information processes, limited human resources and equipment, the absence of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for GAPAR preparation within each section, and lack of support from authorized entities responsible for administering rewards and sanctions. Nonetheless, if the performance appraisal process is conducted with consideration of the established indicators, the implementation is expected to proceed effectively without significant hindrances.

Abstract:  
This study aims to examine the implementation of the land certificate policy in the Talaud Islands Regency, which serves as the executor of the KanTah program in the region. The Larasita policy, issued by the National Land Agency of the Republic of Indonesia (BPN RI), seeks to optimize land-related services by providing direct certification services to the community. The research involved six informants and employed a descriptive qualitative methodology, designed to provide a detailed account of social phenomena. Fieldwork was conducted at the Talaud Islands District Land Office from May 14 to 18, 2018. To analyze policy implementation, the study utilized Edward III’s theoretical framework, which identifies four influencing factors: communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure. The findings reveal that the Larasita policy has not been effectively implemented in the Talaud Islands District Land Office. This outcome is attributed to the absence of socialization efforts by implementing agencies towards the community, insufficient human resources comprising only nine civil servants (ASN) and nine contract employees (PTT), a lack of innovative initiatives to enhance land certificate services, and inadequate coordination among the units responsible for policy execution.  

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Land Certificate

The research aims to analyze the leading sectors in the Southeast Minahasa Regency and to analyze the contribution of the leading sectors in the Southeast Minahasa Regency. This study used a quantitative descriptive approach. The data used were secondary data in the form of Gross Regional Domestic Product of Southeast Minahasa Regency and Gross Regional Domestic Product of North Sulawesi Province in the period of 2013-2017, on the basis of Constant Price in 2010. Analysis of the data used in this study, namely quantitative descriptive analysis, including the contribution of economic sectors to the GRDP of Southeast Minahasa Regency, location quotient analysis and shift share analysis. The results of this study indicated the agriculture, forestry and fisheries sector, the mining and quarrying sector, the electricity and gas procurement sector, the construction sector, the transportation and warehousing sector, as well as the real estate sector in Southeast Minahasa Regency, had LQ scores above 1. The agriculture, forestry and fisheries was the sector with the largest contribution to the Southeast Minahasa Regency GRDP in the 2013-2017 period. The role of the leading sector through the calculation of regional shares (Nij) to the Province of North Sulawesi showed positive results. In the proportional shift (Mij) calculation only the agriculture, forestry and fisheries sectors got negative values. In the differential shift calculation (Cij), some sectors in Southeast Minahasa Regency received negative values or did not have competitiveness against similar categories at the provincial level. Those sectors were mining and quarrying, electricity and gas procurement, transportation and warehousing.Keywords: Leading Sector, Location Quotion, Shift Share, Southeast Minahasa Regency

This study seeks to delineate the extent of social interaction within the Sehati Farmer Group located in Kakaskasen Dua Village, Tomohon City, focusing specifically on the dimensions of cooperation, accommodation, and assimilation. The research was conducted over the period from January to May. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in the analysis. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with 10 respondents, including members of the KSB and all participants in the Sehati Farmer Group, employing a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were obtained from BP3K, relevant literature, and prior studies pertinent to the topic. Data collection employed survey techniques and measurement was carried out using a Likert scale. The findings indicate that the overall level of social interaction, assessed through the variables of accommodation, cooperation, and assimilation, reached 84.72%, which is classified as very good. Specifically, the accommodation and assimilation variables scored 85.33% and 89.83% respectively, both falling within the very good category, whereas the cooperation variable scored 77.5%, corresponding to a good classification. These results demonstrate that the Sehati Farmer Group exhibits a very good level of social interaction overall, with cooperation being relatively good. The Likert scale analysis further confirms that social interaction in the Sehati Farmer Group in Kakaskasen Dua Subdistrict, Tomohon City, attains a score of 84.72%, affirming its classification as very good.

This study aimed to evaluate the impact of incorporating purple sweet potatoes (Ipomoea batatas L.) as an extender in ice cream on its organoleptic properties. The materials utilized included fresh milk, purple sweet potatoes, and standard ice cream ingredients. Four treatment groups were established: P0 (1000 ml of milk without purple sweet potatoes), P1 (1000 ml of milk with 150 g of purple sweet potatoes), P2 (1000 ml of milk with 300 g of purple sweet potatoes), and P3 (1000 ml of milk with 450 g of purple sweet potatoes). A completely randomized design was employed, and sensory evaluation was conducted with 35 panelists to assess the organoleptic attributes of the purple sweet potato ice cream. The hedonic scale was used to measure variables such as color, flavor, texture, and taste. Analysis of mean differences was performed using the Duncan’s Multiple Range Test (DMRT). The findings revealed that the treatments had a statistically significant effect on all evaluated organoleptic characteristics (P < 0.01). Based on the sensory evaluation, the addition of 450 g of purple sweet potatoes per 1000 ml of milk is recommended as a suitable formulation for ice cream production. 

Keywords: Ice cream, Purple sweet potato, Organoleptic properties

The research of Talaud morphophonemics is based on structural linguistic study. There are two sub-disciplines of structural linguistics that contributes in developing and analyzing morphophonemics research, which is morphology and phonology. This research is motivated by the renewal of Talaud language structure and aims to describe the process, formulate rules and identify types of assimilation morphophonemics in Talaud language. This research uses descriptive method. Source of the data is taken from the informants who were native speaker of Talaud language. The data collecting techniques was in terms of observing, oral interactive and note taking. While, technique of analysis data started by describing phonemes, then describing morphemes in the form of free and bound morphemeBased on the result of research, three morphophonemics processes have been found namely processes of change, addition, and deletion of phoneme. From the three processes, phonemic changing process always indicates the sound alignment pattern examined in terms of phonemic homorganic form. For example, the replacement of / N / to /m/ /n/, /ῃ/, when matched with the word stem beginning with phonemes /b, p/ /d, t/ /h/, respectively. This research has also successfully identified the type of morphophonemics assimilation. The morphophonemic assimilation of Talaud language can be viewed in terms of assimilation types based on where the process occurs and the nature of assimilation. At least there are three types of assimilation based on the place of occurrence, namely progressive, regressive and reciprocal assimilation. On the other hand, the assimilation based on the nature has two types, namely total and partial assimilation. This process of morphophonemics and particularly assimilation is then described in the chart showing the rules of morphophonemics so that, the language phenomena that occur is easily visible. Key words: Talaud language morphophonemics, processes, rules.

**Abstract**  
This study, titled "Affixation of Verbs in Jane Austen's Novel Northanger Abbey," aims to describe and analyze the inflectional and derivational affixes present in verbs, focusing on their form, function, and meaning. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data were extracted from Jane Austen’s 1983 novel *Northanger Abbey*. The analysis involved identifying, classifying, and interpreting the inflectional and derivational affixes in verbs according to the framework proposed by O'Grady and Dobrovolsky (1997). The findings reveal seven types of verb affixation within the text, specifically the prefixes /de-/, /dis-/, and /re-/, as well as the suffixes /-es/, /-ing/, /-ed/, and /-en/. These affixes serve either inflectional or derivational functions. Among the inflectional affixes, the suffix /-es/ denoting third person singular appears in 11 instances; the suffix /-ing/, indicating the progressive aspect, also occurs 11 times; and the past tense suffix /-ed/ is found in 8 occurrences. The derivational affixes comprise 10 prefixes and 1 suffix. The suffix /-en/, expressing causation or the process of performing an action, appears once; the prefix /de-/, which conveys a lowering or reversing meaning, appears twice; the prefix /dis-/, indicating negation or opposition, is identified in 6 examples; and the prefix /re-/, expressing repetition or return, occurs twice. Theoretically, this research contributes to the understanding of morphological processes, particularly verb affixation. Practically, it enhances readers' comprehension of affixation in the context of *Northanger Abbey* and serves as a valuable resource for students, especially those in the English Department at the Faculty of Humanities, University of Sam Ratulangi, who seek to deepen their knowledge of English verb morphology and support further research in this area.

**Keywords:** Affixation, Verb, Prefix, Suffix, Descriptive Study, *Northanger Abbey*

Dividend policy represents a strategic decision undertaken by a company that requires careful and deliberate consideration. This policy determines the proportion of profits allocated for distribution to shareholders as dividends and the portion retained within the company as retained earnings. Notably, an increase in retained earnings corresponds with a reduction in dividends distributed to shareholders. The process of income allocation presents various challenges. The announcement of dividend distribution serves as a signaling mechanism to shareholders. 

This study investigates the effects of the Current Ratio (CR), Collateralizable Assets (COL), Return on Equity (ROE), and Growth on the Dividend Payout Ratio (DPR) for companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the period from 2005 to 2011. The population comprises companies that have issued dividends and whose financial statements are publicly available on the Stock Exchange. The sample consists of eight manufacturing firms over the specified period. Secondary data were utilized and analyzed using SPSS version 20, employing multiple linear regression as the analytical method.

The findings indicate that collectively, the Current Ratio, Collateralizable Assets, Return on Equity, and Growth do not exert a statistically significant impact on the Dividend Payout Ratio among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Similarly, when examined individually, none of these variables show a significant effect on the Dividend Payout Ratio within the studied sample.

The study recommends that future research expand the scope beyond manufacturing firms, as the current study’s findings may not be generalizable to other sectors due to the limited sample and timeframe. Additionally, subsequent investigations are encouraged to incorporate other variables such as the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER), and to extend the period of analysis to enhance the robustness of results.

The cost associated with raw material inventory represents an economic resource expenditure, quantified in monetary terms, which has been incurred or is anticipated to be incurred. This cost encompasses purchase expenses, storage fees, and losses due to inventory shortages. The objective of this study is threefold: (1) to calculate the Total Inventory Cost (TIC) based on the Raw Material (RM) policy, specifically applying the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) method at Kinamang Fuel Fish throughout the year 2017; (2) to determine the ordering frequency of efficient fish raw materials during the same period; and (3) to establish the appropriate safety stock quantity and reorder point for fish raw materials at Kinamang Fuel Fish in 2017. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative approach and utilizing a case study methodology, the findings indicate that the cost of fish raw material supplies at Kinamang Fuel Fish Restaurant remains suboptimal. This inefficiency is attributed to the ordering decisions being based solely on previous sales estimates without adequately considering the economic implications of purchase and storage costs. Contrastingly, implementation of the EOQ model demonstrates a substantial reduction in raw material inventory costs and facilitates accurate determination of safety stock levels and reorder points. 

Keywords: Inventory Cost, Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Ordering Frequency, Safety Stock, Reorder Point (ROP)

This study seeks to evaluate and compare the quality of liquid smoke products derived from three distinct raw materials: shell, coconut fiber, and corn cobs. The research aims to provide valuable insights into the production of liquid smoke, thereby establishing a foundation for the development of more efficient liquid smoke manufacturing technologies in the future. Liquid smoke is defined as the condensate obtained from the vapor produced through the pyrolysis of wood. Its composition, which includes phenolic compounds, carbonyl groups, and organic acids, plays a crucial role in odor elimination and repellent properties. Consequently, fumigation using liquid smoke presents a potentially simpler and more cost-effective method for plant care.

Employing an experimental design with descriptive analytical techniques, this study utilized raw materials consisting of 90 kg each of shell, coconut coir, and corn cobs. For each treatment, 30 kg of the respective material was subjected to the combustion process to produce liquid smoke. Observations were focused on comparing the raw materials to determine their effectiveness in yielding the desired liquid smoke quality.

The results indicated that the shell yielded liquid smoke at 6.027% with an equipment efficiency of 66.96%. Liquid smoke produced from corn cobs demonstrated a yield of 3.458% and an equipment efficiency of 49.4%, while coconut coir yielded 2.964% with the same equipment efficiency of 49.4%. Moreover, the production times varied across the materials when using 30 kg per batch: shell required 9 hours, coconut coir 6 hours, and corn cobs 7 hours.

Leaders are anticipated to employ an appropriate leadership style, effective communication skills, and a comprehensive understanding of interpersonal and team dynamics to foster a quality work environment for their employees. A leadership style encompasses a leader’s attitudes, expertise, character, and values, which collectively manifest in their behavioral patterns. Employee performance constitutes a critical determinant in enhancing organizational outcomes, as well as shaping employee behaviors and traits. It serves to augment organizational productivity by encompassing the execution of assigned tasks, adherence to deadlines, employee competency, and overall efficiency and effectiveness in task completion. This study aims to examine the impact of leadership style on employee performance at Century Supermarket Tomohon. Utilizing simple linear regression analysis, data were collected from a sample of 30 employees. The findings indicate that leadership style exerts a significant effect on employee performance within the organization. Specifically, it positively influences employees' ability to work effectively and efficiently, fulfill assigned responsibilities, and comprehend their job requirements. Consequently, Century Supermarket Tomohon is encouraged to maintain its current approach to employee management, as it has contributed to enhanced employee performance, which is vital for the company’s overall success.  
Keywords: leadership style, employee performance

Sponge organisms synthesize bioactive compounds that exhibit toxicity as a defensive mechanism. These compounds demonstrate potential antibacterial properties as well as the capacity to absorb ultraviolet (UV) radiation, indicating their prospective use in sunscreen formulations. This study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial efficacy of crude extracts and fractionated compounds derived from sponges against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, as well as to assess their anti-UV activity. Antibacterial activity was determined using the agar diffusion method (Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion), while anti-UV activity was analyzed by subjecting the crude extracts and antibacterial-active fractions to spectrophotometric examination. Four sponge species were extracted and fractionated into aqueous, methanol, and n-hexane fractions. All extracts and fractions were screened for antibacterial activity, revealing inhibitory effects against S. aureus by Plakortis sp. in crude extract (9 mm inhibition zone) and aqueous fraction (8.6 mm), and by Agelas sp. in crude extract (7 mm). In addition, antibacterial activity against E. coli was observed in Plakortis sp. crude extract (12.6 mm) and aqueous fraction (9 mm), Liosina sp. aqueous fraction (7.6 mm), Haliclona sp. aqueous fraction (8 mm), and Agelas sp. crude extract (10.3 mm). Subsequent UV spectrophotometric analysis of crude extracts and aqueous fractions from the four sponge species demonstrated absorption in both UV-B (290–320 nm) and UV-A (320–400 nm) wavelength ranges.  
Keywords: sponges, antibacterial activity, fractionation, ultraviolet absorption

This study investigated the ingestive behavior of the White-bellied Sea Eagle (Haliaeetus leucogaster) within the safeguarded enclosures of the Tasikoki Central Wild Animal Rescue in Minahasa Utara, as part of a conservation strategy supporting translocation efforts. The primary objective was to characterize the feeding patterns of this species, thereby contributing valuable insights to wildlife conservation practices. Employing observational methods and instantaneous sampling techniques, data were collected from 14 individual eagles between 07:00 and 17:00 hours. Key variables included the observation of prey, prey capture, and ingestion behaviors.

Results indicated that the White-bellied Sea Eagle primarily consumed fish but was also observed exhibiting cannibalistic feeding on conspecifics. The type of prey had a significant influence on ingestion behavior, with fish representing the preferred food source. Instances of agonistic interactions were predominantly associated with predation on other eagles. Behavioral observations revealed that these eagles spent approximately 3% of their time scanning prey and their environment, 1% actively capturing fish, and 96% ingesting prey. The species demonstrated heightened sensitivity and preference toward fish compared to conspecific prey.

In summary, this research provides a detailed account of the ingestive behavior of Haliaeetus leucogaster in captivity, offering important reference information for conservation management programs. 

Keywords: White-bellied Sea Eagle (Haliaeetus leucogaster), ingestive behavior, Tasikoki Central Wild Animal Rescue, wildlife conservation.

The defoliation effect of nitrogen fertilizer on the performance of Brachiaria humidicola (Rendle) Schweick cv. Tully was investigated in this study. B. humidicola is recognized for its palatability, weed suppression capability, persistence under intense grazing, and tolerance to dry environmental conditions. Additionally, this species produces the chemical compound brachialactone, a biological nitrification inhibitor that is released into the root rhizosphere automatically following defoliation, thereby enhancing nitrogen use efficiency in the field. The primary objective of this experiment was to examine the influence of defoliation and varying nitrogen fertilizer levels on the growth performance of B. humidicola.

The experiment was conducted at the Balai Pengkajian Teknologi Pertanian (BPTP) experimental station in Pandu, North Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi. The treatments comprised two factors arranged factorially: factor A representing defoliation (a1 = defoliated, a2 = non-defoliated) and factor B representing nitrogen fertilizer application levels (b1 = 0 g, b2 = 40 g, b3 = 80 g, and b4 = 160 g N/plot). The experimental design was a randomized block design with three replications.

Results revealed a significant interaction between defoliation and nitrogen level (a1b1) for total phyllochron, which was higher than other treatment combinations (P < 0.05). Defoliation significantly increased the number of tillers compared to non-defoliation (P < 0.05). Neither the interaction between defoliation and nitrogen nor nitrogen fertilization alone had a significant effect on the shoot/root ratio; however, defoliation alone significantly affected this ratio (P < 0.05).

In conclusion: (1) defoliation enhances the total number of phyllochrons, tiller production, and supports root development in B. humidicola; (2) nitrogen demand is greater for tiller production than for phyllochron development.

Keywords: defoliation, nitrogen, performance, Brachiaria humidicola

The Role of Extensionists in Farmers’ Decision-Making Regarding the Adoption of Technological Innovations on Farms in Sangkub Sub-District, North Bolaang Mongondow District

Extension activities represent a critical governmental initiative aimed at enhancing farmers’ knowledge, skills, and attitudes towards livestock management. Extension workers play a pivotal role in advancing livestock breeding and facilitating the adoption of technological innovations among farmers. This study aims to investigate the influence of extension workers on farmers’ decision-making processes related to the adoption of innovative farming technologies in Sangkub Sub-District, North Bolaang Mongondow Regency. Employing a survey methodology, the research sampled three villages selected through purposive sampling. Subsequently, thirty respondents were randomly chosen from livestock breeder groups. Data collection involved interviews, observations, and documentation. Primary data included respondent demographics, livestock numbers, technologies utilized, and the role of extension workers, whereas secondary data were sourced from the Agriculture Office of North Bolaang Mongondow Regency, the Agricultural and Forestry Extension Agency (BP3K) of Sangkub Sub-District, and the Central Bureau of Statistics of Bolaang Mongondow. The collected data were analyzed using scoring techniques and descriptive statistics. Findings reveal that farmers generally appraise the role of extension workers as motivators, dynamic agents, and facilitators, with this appraisal rated as optimal within the study area. Additionally, the adoption process among cattle breeders in Sangkub Sub-District varied considerably, encompassing individuals unfamiliar with farming technologies, those who have experimented with them, and those who have fully implemented such innovations. The study concludes that extension workers significantly influence farmers’ decisions concerning the adoption of technological innovations in livestock farming within the Sangkub Sub-District.

Keywords: extensionists’ role, adoption process, decision-making

ABSTRACTThe purpose of this research was to evaluate the implementation of the mining safety management system (SMKP) and the mining environmental protection management system (SPPLHP), analyze employee perceptions of the system, and analyze priority strategies for system improvement at PT. Sumber Energi Jaya. (SEJ). This research was conducted from October to December 2020. The research method used is a survey method with questionnaires, interviews, observations, and documentation. Determination of the sample in this study using the purposive sampling method with 50 employees as respondents. The perception data was obtained by using a questionnaire and then tested for validity and reliability with the SPSS 26 program and measured using a Likert scale. The strategy analysis used is SWOT analysis and AHP analysis with the Expert Choice program version 11. The results show that the implementation of SMKP 72% and SPPLHP 80% can be categorized as achievement at the proactive level and measurement of employee perceptions of SMKP and SPPLHP is categorized as high. The priority strategy of SMKP is to optimize company support by allocating a budget for system improvement and SPPLHP's priority strategy is to optimize the management of the mining environment by integrating information, planning, programs, budgets, procedures and structures.

This study seeks to: (1) analyze the potential for beef cattle development through the integration of coconut plantations in Tabaru Subdistrict, West Halmahera Regency; (2) assess fresh forage production from coconut plantation areas in the same region; (3) evaluate the nutritional content of forage within these coconut plantation areas; (4) estimate the potential cattle population and corresponding animal units (AU) in Tabaru Subdistrict; and (5) compare revenue outcomes between integrated and non-integrated farming systems in the area. The research was carried out in Tabaru Subdistrict, West Halmahera Regency, from December 2017 to February 2018. Respondents were selected by simple random sampling, with inclusion criteria requiring household farmers engaged in coco-beef integration, possessing a minimum of one year’s experience in animal husbandry, and having sold cattle. Findings revealed distinct characteristics of the participating households, including an average coconut plantation ownership of 3.8 hectares, an average cattle herd size of 10.2 heads, primary-level education, approximately 12.7 years of livestock breeding experience, and purposes centered on beef production and animal labor. Livestock management practices remained largely traditional, with animals exhibiting disease resistance; however, farmer knowledge regarding animal reproduction was limited. Feed resource conditions were found to be conducive to beef cattle development under the integration system, given the favorable nutritional content of forage and land carrying capacities. Overall, livestock productivity demonstrated significant potential within this integrated farming framework.

This study aimed to assess the outcomes of the evaluation conducted on the staff of the South Minahasa District Office of Transportation following their participation in an educational and technical training program. The evaluation revealed several challenges, indicating discrepancies between expected and achieved results. The utilization of facilities during the implementation of the education and training program remained suboptimal, both from the participants—employees of the South Minahasa Regency Transportation Department—and from the program organizers. Employing a qualitative research design of a descriptive nature, the study collected primary data through interviews and observations, while secondary data were garnered via literature reviews and documentation analysis. Findings suggest that the education and training program did not entirely fulfill its objectives in fostering significant improvements among employees contributing to the advancement of the South Minahasa District Transportation Office. This conclusion is drawn based on the evaluation outcomes, which focused on the four indicators proposed by Daniel Stufflebeam. Consequently, the researchers recommend a greater emphasis on aligning employee placement with the respective education and training programs attended, thereby promoting professional development and enhancing performance in accordance with the specific requirements of each role within the South Minahasa District Transportation Department.

Keywords: Evaluation, Education, Training Programs.

GROWTH RESPONSE OF Brachiaria humidicola cv Tully grass WITH ORGANIC FERTILIZER BOKASHI LAYING CHICKEN. This study aims to determine the growth response i.e stolon length, number of nodes, number of phytomers, and number of tillers of Brachiaria humidicola cv Tully with bokashi organic laying hens fertilizer. The completely randomized design was applied using four treatments and five replications for each treatment. The treatments were assigned level of bokashi. The levels of bokashi that B0 = 0 tons/ha (control), B1 = 2 tons/ha (1.8 kg/plot), B2 = 4 tons/ha (3.6 kg/plot) and B3 = 6 tons/ha (5.4 kg/plot). The variables measured consisted of stolon length, number of nodes, number of phyitomers, number of tillers. The Results of analysis of variance showed that treatment very significantly different (P <0.01) on stolon length, number of phyitomers, number of tillers and significantly different (P <0.05) on the number of nodes. Test of Honest Significance Difference (HSD) showed that B1 (1.8 kg / plot), B2 (3.6 kg / plot), and B3 (5.4 kg / plot) have higher length of stolone, number of phyitomers and number of tillers than B0. B3 and B2 had higher numbers of nodes than B0. It was concluded that the level 1.8 kg/plot organic fertilizer bokashi chicken laying equivalent to 2 tons/ha gave highest B. humidicola cv Tully growth response. Keywords: growth, B. humidicola cv Tully, bokashi laying Chicken

Abstract:  
In the context of globalization, significant changes, enhancements, and advancements across various sectors have become imperative. Pertaining to human resources, there is a pressing need to elevate labor quality and foster the capacity for independent and competitive performance. A critical factor within human resource management that organizations must address is employee motivation, defined as the willingness of employees to dedicate their full efforts to the organization. Motivation assumes growing importance as leadership endeavors to guide subordinates in executing their tasks effectively and aligning their efforts with established organizational objectives. Effective leadership recognizes that employees are inclined to work diligently when they anticipate that their efforts will satisfy both their needs and desires. While employees do not accomplish all tasks individually, collaboration among staff is often essential to complete assignments successfully. Consequently, leaders must actively encourage and stimulate employees’ willingness to work, ensuring that they perform their duties to the best of their abilities and thereby enhance productivity. It is vital to acknowledge that employees are not merely labor units but sentient beings with emotions, needs, desires, and independent thought processes. Organizational performance improvement, encompassing a broad range of internal and external factors, is closely influenced by motivation, which is shaped by elements intrinsic to employees as well as external conditions. This study reveals that motivation has a significant and strong correlation with employee or educator performance. Hence, it is concluded that motivation plays a crucial role as a driving force in enhancing organizational performance.  

Keywords: Role, Motivation, Performance

Activity-Based Costing (ABC) is employed to achieve more precise product cost determination by tracing the activities involved, particularly to support decision-making processes. ABC enables management to identify the elevated costs associated with low-volume products. This study uses Smokie Crab and Grilled Squid from Wisata Bahari Restaurant in Manado as case samples. The research aims to generate a more accurate cost calculation, thereby providing clearer production cost information to the restaurant’s owner, ultimately facilitating improved determination of the cost of goods sold and enhancing competitive positioning. Various methods exist for determining the cost of goods sold, including job order costing (JOC), process costing, and activity-based costing (ABC), alongside approaches for setting selling prices such as normal pricing. Job order costing calculates the cost of goods sold based on specific orders, considering raw materials, labor, and overhead, whereas ABC allocates costs according to the activities performed, assigning total costs to each product based on these activities. A comparison of ABC and JOC calculations for Smokie Crab and Grilled Squid reveals discrepancies in the resulting selling prices. For Smokie Crab, ABC yields more favorable pricing outcomes for Wisata Bahari Restaurant, whereas JOC is preferable for Grilled Squid.  
Keywords: activity-based costing, job order costing, selling price

The aim of this study was to analyze the impact of adoption of Government Regulation No. 46 2013 of Paying Income Tax by Taxpayers at KPP Pratama Manado. The analytical method used is using two different test samples / dependent groups (paired) or Paired Sample T Test. Paired Sample t test course used when the two groups are interconnected. Two paired sample means a sample with the same subject but have two different treatments or measurements of, for example, before and after. Background: The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) stated that stress and depression related to work in 2017/2018 were 595,000 cases with a prevalence rate of 1,800 per 100,000 workers. Work-related stress and depression also contribute 44% of all cases of occupational health disorders and 57% of absences from work due to illness. Job stress can occur to workers in all fields including government employees. This study aims to determine the relationship between risk factorsand work-related stress on civil servants in Regional Financial and Asset Agency of North Sulawesi Province. Method: This research was a quantitative study with cross sectional research design, conducted in 2019, from August to September at the Regional Finance and Assets Agency (BKAD) of North Sulawesi Province. The sample was 118 people determined by the Total Sampling method. Data was collected by respondent completing NIOSH Generic Job Stress Questionnaire. Univariate, bivariate, and multivariate were use to analyze the data using SPSS program. Results: The results showed that there was a relationship between interpersonal conflict, workload, social support and work stress on civil servants in BKAD North Sulawesi Province. Conclusion: This study concluded that interpersonal conflict is the most influential factor in work-related stress on civil servants in BKAD North Sulawesi Province. It is recommended for all civil servants in BKAD North Sulawesi Province to be more aware to the work-related stress factors so that it can be controlled

Fraud constitutes a deliberate act carried out for personal gain or on behalf of others, which results in detriment to specific individuals or institutions. Fraudulent financial statements encompass intentional misrepresentations designed to mislead the users of such reports. These misstatements originate from the manipulation or falsification of accounting records, purposeful omissions or inaccuracies in financial disclosures, and/or the improper application of accounting principles. In Indonesia, incidents of accounting fraud have been observed at the corporate level across both private enterprises and state-owned companies. Notably, on December 6, 2012, Indonesia received a score of 32 on the Corruption Perception Index (CPI), ranking 118th among 176 countries assessed for corruption levels (Transparency International, 2012). An illustrative case occurred in 2001 involving PT Kimia Farma Tbk, a state-owned enterprise that had transitioned into a publicly traded company. Investigations conducted by the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises (BUMN) and Bapepam revealed misstatements in the company's financial statements, resulting in an overstatement of net income by Rp. 32.7 billion for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2001. This figure represented 2.3% of total sales and 24.7% of reported net income. The present study aims to explore the detection of financial statement fraud through the application of five out of eight Beneish ratio indices. According to Beneish’s research, the Days Sales in Receivables Index (DSRI), Gross Margin Index (GMI), Asset Quality Index (AQI), Sales Growth Index (SGI), and Total Accruals to Total Assets Index (TATA) are particularly effective in identifying manipulations within financial reports.

Abstract:  
Rolling represents a dynamic organizational process implemented as a strategy to achieve organizational objectives. This practice aims to alleviate job monotony, enhance employees' knowledge and skills, and boost motivation and morale by assigning officials with relevant expertise to appropriate positions. The present study addresses the research question of how rolling officials influence the quality of public services within the government staffing context of South Minahasa. Employing a quantitative research design, this study investigates the relationship between rolling of officials in South Minahasa district and variables including work experience, knowledge, skills, and employee performance. Data were collected through questionnaires and interviews from a sample of 20 respondents across five selected Regional Work Units (SKPD). The analysis was conducted using linear regression and Pearson product-moment correlation techniques, based on manual calculations of the respective statistical formulas. The findings reveal a positive correlation between rolling officials and the quality of public services, with a correlation coefficient of 0.239. Furthermore, the correlation coefficient specific to the impact of rolling on public service delivery in South Minahasa was 0.306, accompanied by a coefficient of determination of 0.093. These results indicate that the rolling of officials has a significant and positive effect on the quality of public services in South Minahasa district.  

Keywords: influence, rolling, quality, public service

This study seeks to examine (1) the changes in the value of agricultural land before and after its transformation into the Manado-Bitung toll road, and (2) the socio-economic impacts experienced by landowners in Tumaluntung Village. The research was carried out focusing on the construction site of the Manado-Bitung toll road within Tumaluntung Village. Data collection occurred from August to November 2017, with additional fieldwork conducted between May and June 2019. Employing a descriptive research design, findings are presented in tabular form. Sample selection was conducted using purposive sampling techniques. Primary data were gathered through interviews with 15 landowners, while secondary data were sourced from the Tumaluntung village office, scholarly articles accessed via Google Scholar, and theses from various higher education institutions pertinent to the valuation of agricultural land. The study’s findings indicate that (1) the value of agricultural land was higher prior to its conversion into the toll road than after its completion, and (2) the social status of landowners improved, as compensation funds were strategically invested in banking deposits, boarding houses, bakeries, poultry farming, vehicle showrooms, restaurants, and transportation services, thereby enhancing their capacity to meet economic needs.

Leverage constitutes a strategic approach employed by corporations to enhance their earnings by assuming risks associated with debt, fixed assets, or a combination thereof. The utilization of such methods can potentially influence a company's profitability, given the inherent risks involved. It is posited that a higher degree of risk undertaken through leverage should correspond to an increased expected return. This study aims to compare the application of leverage across selected companies and to examine whether a significant difference exists in the profitability of food and beverage firms following the implementation of financial leverage, operating leverage, and total leverage as mechanisms for profit maximization. Employing a quantitative methodology, the research utilizes one-way ANOVA for statistical analysis. The sample comprises six publicly traded companies listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange, all classified within Indonesia’s food and beverage processing industry. The findings reveal that Indofood Sukses Makmur exhibited the highest level of financial leverage, whereas Charoen Pokphand Indonesia demonstrated the greatest operating and total leverage. Although one-way ANOVA was applied to assess financial, operating, and total leverage, no statistically significant differences were detected among the sampled companies. Despite the presence and utilization of leverage, its impact on corporate profitability appears to be insufficiently robust. Therefore, it is recommended that company management optimize leverage strategies to enhance profit maximization. 

Keywords: financial leverage, operating leverage, total leverage, profitability

Background: Adolescence represents a transitional phase characterized by substantial changes in physical, psychological, environmental, and social dimensions, which collectively influence overall human life quality. During this period, adolescents require appropriate outlets to manage the psychological distress arising from these changes. The protective function of schools for adolescents amid the COVID-19 pandemic has diminished, potentially exposing them to various issues, including increased alcohol consumption.  

Aim: This study seeks to examine the quality of life and alcohol consumption patterns among students of SMA Negeri 7 Manado throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.  

Methods: Employing a descriptive cross-sectional design, this research was conducted between September and December 2020. Utilizing stratified random sampling, a total of 93 respondents who satisfied the inclusion and exclusion criteria were selected for analysis.  

Results and Conclusion: Findings indicate that the quality of life among adolescents at SMA Negeri 7 Manado, encompassing both male and female students, predominantly falls within the moderate range. Specifically, males exhibited scores of 66.71% in the physical domain, 52% in the psychological domain, 58.26% in the social domain, and 67.98% in the environmental domain. Female students demonstrated scores of 67.5%, 57.84%, 60.85%, and 67.98% across the respective domains. Additionally, alcohol consumption among these adolescents remained low, with a prevalence of 14%.  

Keywords: quality of life, adolescents, alcohol consumption, COVID-19, pandemic

This study seeks to assess the implementation of two programs: (1) the National Agrarian Program Certification (PRONA) and (2) the Complete Systematic Land Registration (PTSL). Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research was conducted in Kinabuhutan Village, West Likupang Sub-district, North Minahasa District, North Sulawesi Province, from June 2017 to January 2018. The sample comprised 23 respondents involved in PRONA and 21 respondents engaged in PTSL, with participants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected via observation, interviews, and documentation, and subsequently analyzed using descriptive qualitative techniques. The findings indicate that (1) the implementation of land certification through the PRONA program generally adhered to the prescribed procedural stages as stipulated by relevant regulations. Nevertheless, challenges were identified concerning (i) proof of ownership rights, whether derived from sale and purchase, grants, or inheritance, and (ii) land tenure status involving cultivators, which hindered the ability to trace the land's ownership history from the initial holder to the current owner, as well as the demarcation of land boundaries—both of which are essential for certificate management. (2) The execution of the PTSL program also followed the regulated procedural stages. However, certain deficiencies arose, including instances where community members selected for participation could not provide ownership documentation, were absent during land measurement, and lacked physical boundary markers to delineate their property. A common issue affecting the implementation of both programs pertains to the insufficient number of personnel possessing adequate competence as land measurement officers.

Marriage, as a significant lifelong stage in an individual's life from an anthropological perspective, is commonly regarded as one of the phases within the human life cycle, alongside other stages such as infancy, weaning, childhood, adolescence, puberty, post-marital periods, pregnancy, and old age. Transitions between these stages are often marked by rituals or ceremonies, typically involving communal celebrations. The institution of marriage serves various social functions; for instance, the preparation of a wedding ceremony often necessitates collective cooperation, which fosters social cohesion and strengthens communal bonds through mutual assistance. Additionally, marriage has the potential to unite disparate cultures, a process facilitated by the absence of legal restrictions against interethnic marriages within the state.

The Loleba community exemplifies a society characterized by a rich cultural heritage, encompassing diverse dance forms, regional music, local languages, and traditional matrimonial practices. Specifically, the Tobelo traditional wedding ceremony, deeply rooted in the cultural legacy inherited from their ancestors originating from Halmahera, embodies significant social meanings. This ancestral heritage represents a copyrighted cultural knowledge that holds profound value for community life.

The indigenous Tobelo people, long-established in Loleba Village, East Halmahera, continue to uphold the Mohoka tradition within their nuptial customs. This tradition encompasses multiple intrinsic values that metaphorically reflect the everyday experiences of the Tobelo community. The Mohoka cultural and customary practices embody a set of values including religious, cultural, social, personal, and epistemic dimensions. These values collectively contribute to the preservation and transmission of the community’s identity and social fabric.

Keywords: marriage, tradition, ceremony

Government financial reports serve as instruments for communication and accountability between the government and the public. These financial statements are generated through government accounting systems at both the central and local levels, in compliance with Government Regulation Number 8 of 2006 concerning Financial Reporting and Performance of Government Agencies. Prior to submission for audit to the Audit Board of the Republic of Indonesia (BPK RI), the statements are required to undergo a review by the Government Internal Supervisory Apparatus (APIP). The government seeks to enhance public trust in its performance by securing an Unqualified Opinion (Wajar Tanpa Pengecualian, WTP) from BPK RI’s examination of the financial statements. Empirical data reveal that the majority of regional governments have succeeded in obtaining WTP opinions on their Local Government Financial Reports (LKPD) audited by the BPK. However, a notable case is observed in the North Sulawesi Provincial Government, which, despite consecutively receiving seven WTP opinions, continues to encounter findings during BPK’s LKPD audits. This occurs even though the LKPD undergoes prior review by the APIP Regional Inspectorate of North Sulawesi Province. The present study seeks to elucidate the significance of APIP’s role as an internal auditor in reviewing LKPD, drawing on the experiences of APIP personnel engaged in the review process conducted before submission to the BPK. Employing a qualitative methodology with a phenomenological approach, the study’s findings reveal that the internal auditor’s role in the review is predominantly confined to verifying the accuracy of the financial information presented within the North Sulawesi Provincial Government’s LKPD. This role does not extend directly to the oversight of physical work activities in the field, which frequently constitute the basis for audit findings identified by the BPK Representative of North Sulawesi Province.

This research seeks to assess the diversity of nutmeg crops in the Sangihe Island Regency and SITARO District (Siau Island) by examining the characteristics of the fruit, seeds, and nutmeg mace. The study employed direct observational methods conducted within farmers' nutmeg plantation areas. Research locations were selected based on secondary data identifying nutmeg-producing districts and villages, with three observation sites established in each area. At each site, ten nutmeg trees were sampled, and twenty mature fruits per tree were examined. Plant samples were selected based on two criteria: (1) plant age ranging from 15 to 30 years, and (2) the plant’s health and fruit-bearing condition. The parameters observed included: fruit shape, rind color, flesh thickness, individual fruit weight, fruit length, fruit diameter, flesh color, fresh seed weight, seed length, seed diameter, fresh mace weight, and mace color. Findings revealed that the fruit and seed morphology exhibited greater variability in the Sangihe Islands Regency compared to SITARO District. The highest fresh nutmeg fruit weight was recorded at the Talawid site, averaging 57.95 grams, whereas the lowest weight was found at Karatung I, with an average of 35.91 grams. Similarly, the greatest fresh seed weight was observed at Talawid (9.45 grams), and the smallest at Karatung I (6.75 grams). Notably, the mace color consistently appeared as a deep red across samples. 

Keywords: nutmeg plant, fruit diversity, Sangihe, SITARO

The current state of life is undeniably influenced, to a considerable extent, by the existing human resources. It is well recognized that human actions predominantly shape the future; consequently, the decisions and efforts undertaken today profoundly impact the conditions of tomorrow. The rapid advancements in science and technology have significantly accelerated the transmission of information, leading to transformative developments across various sectors. Particularly notable is the enhancement of human resource quality, aimed at cultivating individuals who are skilled, competent, cultured, and ethically grounded, thereby enabling them to effectively navigate future opportunities and challenges.

This study investigates the strategies employed by regional government authorities to improve the quality of human resources in the West District of Manokwari Regency, West Papua Province. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study utilizes SWOT analysis for data evaluation. The analysis of internal factors identifies several strengths, including a highly engaged community, substantial special autonomy funding, and significant local revenue. Conversely, weaknesses are noted in areas such as low educational attainment, insufficient guidance and development of labor productivity, inadequate infrastructure, a scarcity of experts, and limited governmental attention.

With respect to external factors, opportunities arise from technological advancements and the region’s abundant natural resources. However, potential threats are observed in the form of a less open mindset, public affairs interventions, and elevated poverty levels.

Based on the findings of the SWOT analysis, four strategic approaches are proposed: (1) efforts to expand and equitably distribute education and enhance societal productivity; (2) improvement of public services through the development of quality human resources and the implementation of balanced regional development; (3) promotion of increased governmental intervention and public awareness; and (4) exploration and utilization of regional potentials through technology-based initiatives.

Keywords: Local government strategies, human resource quality improvement, SWOT analysis

In contemporary times, the proliferation of Chinese restaurants has been notable. Unlike standard dining establishments, Chinese restaurants embody distinct sociological and cultural characteristics that provide unique experiences for their patrons, which are not typically available in conventional restaurants. In the city of Manado, the three most frequented Chinese restaurants are Afui, New Mie Jakarta, and Samrat Abadi, all situated on Samrat Street. Consumer purchase decision refers to the process by which consumers select a product from multiple alternatives for consumption. Several factors influence consumer decisions within the culinary sector, including price, brand image, cleanliness, service quality, ambiance, and menu design. The objective of this study is to identify the primary criteria influencing consumers' choice of Chinese restaurants in Manado and to determine the most preferred establishment among them. Employing the Analytical Hierarchy Process methodology, data were collected from a sample of 50 respondents. Findings indicate that cleanliness emerges as the most critical factor, followed sequentially by ambiance, service quality, brand image, price, with menu design ranking lowest. Among the alternatives, Samrat Abadi is the most favored restaurant. It is recommended that the establishment maintain its cleanliness standards, while Afui and New Mie Jakarta should focus on enhancing their service quality, increasing promotional activities, and introducing distinctive attributes that differentiate them from their competitors.  
Keywords: consumer purchase decision, Analytical Hierarchy Process

ABSTRACTSThis research entitled "Taboo Words in English and Biak Language: A Contrastive Analysis" is analyzed and described in sociolinguistic field. The objectives of this research are to identify, classify and describe the types and meaning of taboo words and to analyze their differences and similarities. This research used a descriptive method. The data are analyzed using theory of Wardhaugh (1986:230) to find out the types, using Leech's theory (1981:19) to find out the meaning, and were contrasted to find out the differences using Lado's theory (1971:217). The significances of this research are theoretically, this research is expected to give contribution to the development of sociolinguistics especially in terms of taboo words and to practically it can be useful, for young Biak generation who want to learn taboo words in English and for foreign learners who want to study taboo words in Biak language. The result of this research shows that taboo words found in Biak language were classified into eight types, they are, sex, excretion, bodily function, death, animal, religion, and supernatural. The simillarities in English and Biak Language is the use of this word can cause misunderstanding and the differences of English and Biak Language is taboo words in Biak have levels whereas in English there is no level. This shows that the causes of using taboo words are to express the happiness, such as anger, emotion, and surprise, to joke, to insult, and to talk about sex. Keywords : Taboo Words; English and Biak Language; Contrastive Analysis

Widya Kartika University as an educational institution is always committed to providing the best service for its students. Various service systems were formed gradually to address the needs that were growing over time. This development process was not only carried out by the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) unit but also involves students in the process. Therefore, each sub-system could be developed using different development tools. Besides the Academic Information System, there were other sub-systems including Student Activity Recording System, One-Stop Information Service System, SKPI Data Collection System, Moodle-based E-learning System, and several other sub-systems. Lack of system integrity becomes an obstacle in synchronization between these sub-systems. The databases built for each of these sub-systems were also different. Therefore, a portal was created as an intermediary between systems with the Single Sign On (SSO) system by changing the user interface design from the student side. The portal system modeling was made using the Unified Modeling Language (UML) with the Code Igniter framework as the application creation tool. Based on the results of the application, it was found that the making of this portal was effective in overcoming the difficulties of students in using each of the sub-systems that had not previously been integrated. Access becomes faster and easier in the login process because it uses a single user.

This study, entitled "Anxiety and Defense Mechanisms of Alice Howland in Lisa Genova's Novel *Still Alice*," focuses primarily on the protagonist’s anxiety and the corresponding defense mechanisms she employs, despite the presence of fifteen characters in the narrative. The principal objective of this research is to examine the manifestations of Alice’s anxiety and the defense mechanisms depicted within the novel. Methodologically, this study employs a dual approach, integrating both intrinsic and extrinsic analytical frameworks. The analysis of the protagonist’s personality draws upon the theoretical perspectives of Robert Stanton (2007) and Edgard Robert (1964). Furthermore, Freud’s psychoanalytic theory serves as the foundation for exploring Alice’s anxiety and defense mechanisms, complemented by C. George Boeree’s *Personality Theory* (2006). A descriptive research method is utilized, with primary data sourced from the novel itself, supplemented by relevant scholarly articles concerning anxiety and defense mechanisms accessed online. The findings reveal that Alice Howland experiences two forms of anxiety—namely, neurotic and moral anxiety—and employs various defense mechanisms including projection, displacement, turning against the self, rationalization, denial, compensation, and reaction formation.

Keywords: Anxiety, Defense Mechanism, Major Character, Psychoanalysis

These issues hinder the effective implementation of tax policies, causing them to fall short of their full potential. In response to these challenges, the present study seeks to analyze the implementation of policies concerning the management of the Earth and Building Tax within the Manado City Revenue Office. These factors collectively reflect the challenges in policy implementation at the Manado City Revenue Office.

The construction of embankment road structures on soft ground presents several challenges, including stability concerns, settlement, lateral displacement, slope failure, and differential settlement. These issues primarily arise because soft soils typically exhibit low shear strength, high compressibility, and low permeability. Due to the soil’s limited permeability, the consolidation process requires an extended duration. During consolidation, the initial load is borne entirely by pore water pressure, which gradually transfers to the soil’s effective stress, thereby enhancing its strength and load-bearing capacity. Consequently, to prevent excessive settlement and to ensure adequate load capacity, construction on soft soils should ideally commence only after full consolidation has been achieved.

This study focuses on analyzing stability issues associated with embankments on soft soils through the application of bamboo as micropiles. The case study examines marshland improvement in the context of a toll road project in Manado Bitung, North Sulawesi. The primary objectives are to establish graphical relationships between the factor of safety and key soil engineering properties (cohesion, friction angle, and unit weight), as well as to explore the relationship between the factor of safety and the parameter α. The methodological approach includes laboratory-scale experiments employing bamboo micropiles to simulate soil stability, complemented by slope stability analyses conducted using the Rocscience software suite.

The findings indicate that embankments constructed without bamboo micropiles exhibit lower stability compared to those reinforced with bamboo. Swampy terrains characterized by low load-bearing capacity, elevated water content, and very low permeability frequently induce construction difficulties in civil engineering projects. Stability challenges are among the most prevalent issues when dealing with soft soils. The analysis further demonstrates that increases in friction angle (φ) and cohesion (c) correspond to higher safety factors, whereas a decrease in unit weight (γ) results in a reduction of the safety factor. Additionally, an increase in embankment height (h) tends to diminish the safety factor.

Keywords: slope stability, geological processes, landslides, Rocscience software, safety factor

As the chief official of the working area within the district, the sub-district head holds the authority to coordinate development initiatives at the district level. This study aimed to examine the coordination role of the sub-district head in the implementation of development activities in Kauditan District, North Minahasa Regency. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews with ten informants, including the sub-district head, the head of the Economic Development section, two unit office heads, two vertical agency heads, two village heads, one chairman of the Village Consultative Body (BPD), and one chairman of the Community Participation Institution (LPM). The analysis was conducted using the interactive qualitative analysis model proposed by Miles and Huberman. The findings indicate that (1) the sub-district head’s coordination in planning development programs in Kauditan District was executed effectively and satisfactorily; and (2) the coordination concerning the implementation of these programs was also well conducted and fairly effective. Consequently, it can be concluded that the sub-district head’s coordination in development implementation in Kauditan District is performed properly and demonstrates a reasonable level of effectiveness. This coordination fosters harmony, balance, synchronization, and integrated development within the district, thereby ensuring that development programs are carried out in an orderly, smooth, and successful manner. Based on these findings, the study recommends: (1) enhancing the quality of coordination facilities such as meetings, consultation forums, reporting mechanisms, and information/data inquiry processes; and (2) recognizing that effective and optimal coordination can only be achieved through mutual cooperation and harmony between the coordinating authorities and those being coordinated.  
Keywords: coordination, district, development

This study, entitled "Semiotic Analysis of Representamen Signs in Agatha Christie's Novel *Hallowe'en Party*," focuses on the examination of signs within a semiotic framework. Semiotics, as the study of signs, incorporates the concept of Representamen as a fundamental element within Peirce’s triadic model. Representamen signs can be observed in various aspects of daily life. The objective of this research is to identify, categorize, and analyze the Representamen signs presented in the novel. Data were gathered through the author’s detailed explanation of Representamen functioning as conduits of information. The study applies Charles Peirce’s semiotic theory in order to classify these signs. Furthermore, Roland Barthes’ theory on connotation is employed to interpret the data, emphasizing that connotation constitutes new meanings which are shaped by the user’s intentions, cultural background, or societal conventions. The findings indicate that, according to Peirce’s framework, three distinct forms of Representamen—Qualisign, Sinsign, and Legisign—are present in the novel. The Representamen signs convey a wide range of meanings, including but not limited to contemplation, care, confusion, frustration, fear, concern, affection, doubt, murder, guilt, shock, warning, and anger. This study aims to enhance readers’ comprehension of semiotic theory, particularly the role of the Representamen within Peirce’s triadic concept, and its application in literary analysis and everyday contexts.

Keywords: Semiotics, Representamen, Triadic Concept, Novel, *Hallowe'en Party*

Keywords : Product design development, QFD, HoQ

Introduction: Antibiotics are pharmaceutical agents commonly employed to treat bacterial infections. However, the excessive utilization of antibiotics can contribute to environmental pollution if residual waste products are not adequately degraded. Improperly treated antibiotic residues released into the environment pose significant pollution risks. Various sources of antibiotic use, including healthcare facilities such as hospitals, often lack effective waste management systems. Hospitals are required to implement wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) designed to degrade diverse waste materials, thereby preventing adverse environmental impacts upon discharge. Nonetheless, inadequacies in such treatment processes may result in the release of untreated waste, which has the potential to contaminate the surrounding environment. In particular, antibiotics that are not sufficiently degraded may accumulate in sediments, notably in coastal regions. 

Aim: This study aims to provide an overview of the presence of antibiotic residues in the sediments of the coastal area of Manado Bay. 

Method: The research was conducted using a quantitative-descriptive approach. 

Results: The findings revealed the presence of antibiotic residues in the sediment, as evidenced by the detection of bacteria exhibiting resistance to multiple antibiotic agents within the sediment samples collected from the study area. 

Conclusion: The results indicate that antibiotic residues are present in the sediments of the coastal area of Manado Bay.

Keywords: antibiotics, sediment, Manado Bay

Abstract:  
The present study, titled "Kesalahan Gramatikal dalam Abstrak Skripsi dari Lulusan Fakultas Sastra," aims to identify and analyze the types of grammatical errors found in the English abstracts of skripsi authored by graduates of the Faculty of Letters. Data for this research were collected by examining the abstracts of English Department graduates’ skripsi, accessed through the library of the Faculty of Letters at Sam Ratulangi University. A total of thirty abstracts were selected through random sampling, with ten abstracts taken from each of the years 2006, 2007, and 2008, serving as the study’s sample. The analysis employed Elli’s theoretical framework to categorize and interpret the grammatical errors observed in the texts. Findings reveal that students committed three primary categories of errors: omission, which encompasses seven forms (plural ‘-s’, the verb ‘to be’, articles, the suffix ‘-ly’, possessive apostrophe ‘-’s’, the suffix ‘-ing’, and the coordinating conjunction ‘and’); misinformation, including five forms (apostrophe use, past tense verb endings ‘-ed’, the verb ‘to be’, miscellaneous errors, and errors in direct and indirect speech); and misordering, characterized by errors in the use of the verb ‘to be’ and subject-predicate arrangement. The study concludes that grammatical inaccuracies persist in the abstracts analyzed, with misinformation errors occurring most frequently among the graduates’ work. This research contributes to the field of linguistics by expanding understanding of common grammatical challenges faced by Indonesian learners of English.  

Keywords: grammatical errors, error analysis, omission, misinformation, misordering

The development of leasing institutions presents an appealing alternative for entrepreneurs who currently rely on cash transactions for their company’s operational activities. Leasing arrangements enable the generation of funds to finance the acquisition of assets over terms ranging from three to five years or longer. This study focuses on PT Astra Sedaya Finance Manado, recognized as the largest automotive financing company in Indonesia. The primary objective of this research is to evaluate the accountability practices of Astra Sedaya Finance in Manado. Employing a descriptive research method, data were collected and analyzed concerning the types of leases, the systems for recording and reporting leasing transactions, and the advantages and disadvantages associated with the accounting and reporting of such transactions. Subsequently, conclusions were drawn based on these analyses. The findings indicate that leasing transactions encompass various types, classifications, and criteria which influence the applicable accounting system. At PT Astra Sedaya Finance, the accounting and reporting of lease transactions are conducted using a capital lease system, where ownership may be transferred at the conclusion of the lease period. Furthermore, with regard to recording, reporting, and disclosure practices, the accounting treatment of leases at PT Astra Sedaya Finance aligns with the provisions stipulated by the relevant PSAK (Statement of Financial Accounting Standards).  
Keywords: Leasing, Leasing Receivable Accounting, PSAK No. 30

This study, entitled "Derivational Affixes in English and Balantak Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to describe and analyze derivational affixes in terms of their form, function, and meaning across verbs, nouns, adjectives, and adverbs. Additionally, the research explores the relationship between English and Balantak languages, focusing particularly on the most frequently used affixes in both. Employing a descriptive research methodology, data were collected from the New Testament translated into Balantak by Boob et al. (2010) and supplemented by information obtained from native speakers. The collected data were subsequently identified, classified, and analyzed using O'Grady’s framework (1992) to examine derivational affixes according to their morphological form, grammatical function, and semantic content. The findings reveal that both English and Balantak languages possess derivational affixes applicable to verbs, nouns, and adjectives. Notably, English lacks full reduplication, whereas full reduplication is present in Balantak. Furthermore, English derivational processes include both prefixes and suffixes for adverbs, whereas Balantak utilizes only suffixes in this regard. Theoretically, this research contributes concrete insights into the understanding of derivational affixation. Practically, it offers valuable information to readers, particularly students in the English Department at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University, by enhancing their knowledge of derivational affixes and supporting further research developments.

Keywords: derivational affixes, English language, Balantak language, contrastive analysis
