PT. Yosepha operates as a contractor and supplier service company, with an additional business segment focused on the rental of fixed assets to support the company and enhance profitability. The leasing method employed by PT. Yosepha is categorized as an operating lease. An operating lease is characterized as a conventional lease arrangement whereby, upon the termination of the lease period, no option for purchase is granted to the lessee, and the leased heavy equipment remains the property of PT. Yosepha. The leasing transactions undertaken by PT. Yosepha must adhere to the relevant accounting standards, specifically those outlined in Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 30, owing to their significant impact on the company’s financial statements. This study aims to evaluate whether PT. Yosepha's application of lease accounting complies with Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 30 and to examine the consequent effects on its financial reporting. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study’s findings indicate that PT. Yosepha has not fully implemented the prescribed lease accounting practices for operating leases as stipulated by the aforementioned standard. Notably, errors in disclosure and reporting have been observed, leading to financial statements that lack transparency and do not conform to the applicable accounting standards.

Keywords: Operating Lease, Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 30, Financial Statements

Regional tax constitutes a mandatory levy imposed by the regional government on individuals or entities in accordance with applicable legislation, characterized by the absence of direct remuneration and the allocation of proceeds for regional development aimed at maximizing public welfare. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of hotel tax implementation and its contribution to the Locally Generated Revenue (LGR) of Tomohon City. Employing both qualitative and quantitative data, the research utilizes secondary data sources and applies descriptive qualitative analytical methods. The findings indicate that from 2012 to 2016, the hotel tax was highly effective, with the peak effectiveness recorded in 2016 at 134.01%, whereas the lowest effectiveness occurred in 2014 at 27.40%. The contribution of hotel tax to Tomohon’s LGR during the same period demonstrated an overall positive trend with some fluctuations. The highest contribution was observed in 2016, accounting for 67.23%, while the lowest contribution was in 2015 at 4.85%, yielding an average contribution rate of 26.68%. 

Keywords: Effectiveness, Contribution, Hotel Tax, Local Revenue.

Financial performance measurement is the process of recording and assessing the company's achievements in managing finances according to the predetermined goals and standards. This study aims to determine and compare the financial performance of PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk for the 2017-2019 period measured by the economic value added method and profitability ratio. The research method used descriptive qualitative. The method of data analysis used descriptive analysis, done by collecting data, analyzed and then drawn a conclusion. The result showed that the financial performance of PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk in the period 2017-2018 measured by the economic value added method are not good because EVA has negative value (EVA < 0), but in the period 2019 the company's financial performance is in good condition because EVA has positive value (EVA > 0), meanwhile using the overall profitability ratio is quite good, because the percentage of the profitability ratio is positive which means that the company is still able to generate profit. The comparison of the two methods shows that there are differences in the measurement of financial performance because the economic value added takes into account the cost of capital, while the profitability ratio only focuses on assesing the company's ability to create profits without taking into account the cost of capital.

This study aims to examine the impact of advertising on the purchasing decisions of Oppo smartphone products at the Manado IT Center. Employing a quantitative research design, the independent variable was advertising, while the dependent variable was the purchasing decision. The target population comprised Oppo smartphone users in Manado who had purchased Oppo products at the Manado IT Center. Given the unspecified size of this population, it was considered infinite. Probability sampling was utilized, specifically employing incidental sampling techniques, resulting in a sample size of 100 respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, and documentation, with the research instrument utilizing a Likert scale. Instrument validity and reliability were verified through respective tests. Data analysis was conducted using simple linear regression and processed using SPSS version 25. Findings revealed a correlation coefficient of 0.394 between advertising and purchasing decisions, indicating a low relationship. Furthermore, the effect size of advertising on purchasing decisions was calculated to be 0.1555, representing a very low influence. The regression analysis yielded a positive regression coefficient, suggesting that advertising exerts a positive effect on consumers' purchasing decisions.

This study aimed to examine the relationship between incentives and the work motivation of village government officials in Kauditan District, North Minahasa Regency. Employing a quantitative research approach, data were collected from 30 village government officials across four villages within the district. The instruments utilized for data collection included questionnaires, supplemented by interview guides. Hypothesis testing was conducted using simple statistical correlational analysis, specifically Pearson’s product-moment correlation. The findings indicate a significant positive correlation between incentives and the motivation of village government officials, suggesting that their level of work motivation is substantially influenced by the incentives they receive. In particular, higher or more satisfactory incentives correspond to increased motivation in fulfilling their official duties. Based on these results, it is recommended that incentives for village government officials be enhanced, potentially through annual increases in the Village Fund Allocation. Furthermore, district governments should consider allocating separate budgetary provisions for incentives beyond the existing Village Fund Allocation.  
Keywords: Incentives, Work Motivation, Village Government Apparatus

This study aimed to examine the influence of Price, Promotion, and Place on the purchasing decisions of consumers at KFC Mega Mall Manado. The research employed quantitative data analysis, utilizing a questionnaire validity test with a population size of 800 and a sample size of 80 respondents. The analytical methods applied included the F-test, T-test, and Multiple Linear Regression Analysis. Specifically, the T-test was conducted to assess the significance of the relationships between independent variables (Price, Promotion, and Place) and the dependent variable (purchase decision), testing the partial effects of X1, X2, and X3 on Y. Hypotheses were formulated as null (H0) and alternative (H1) to guide this evaluation.

The results indicated that Price (X1) does not significantly influence purchasing decisions, as evidenced by a p-value of 0.585, which exceeds the 0.05 significance threshold. Conversely, Promotion (X2) was found to have a statistically significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a p-value of 0.023, falling below the 0.05 criterion. Moreover, Place (X3) demonstrated a highly significant positive impact on purchasing decisions, supported by a p-value of 0.000, which is less than 0.05. Simultaneous hypothesis testing via the F-test revealed that the combined effect of Price, Promotion, and Place variables exerts a significant and positive influence on the purchasing decisions of KFC Mega Mall Manado customers, as demonstrated by an F-value with a corresponding p-value of 0.000.

Although the livestock sub-sector plays a significant role in the economic growth of North Sulawesi, it has not yet been recognized as a leading commodity within the agro-industry development framework. A primary issue in advancing livestock development is the lack of formulation and implementation of suitable strategies that can effectively maximize existing potentials, thereby enabling the livestock industry to become competitive. This study was carried out through a series of steps: first, conducting a comprehensive review of information sources to identify limitations, key research areas, developmental challenges within the livestock sub-sector, as well as regional and strategic management insights, which informed the formulation of research objectives aimed at practical implementation. Second, a survey of experts was conducted to examine and define the relevant elements and sub-elements associated with the development strategy of the farm estate sector within agro-industry. Third, a system structuring design was developed by reviewing and determining the development of key elements using Interpretative Structural Modeling (ISM). Results from expert evaluations identified four main elements and twelve sub-elements exhibiting strong interactions influencing livestock development in North Sulawesi. These elements were subjected to interaction level analysis using the ISM-VAXO technique. The initial phase involved studying contextual relationships represented in a matrix format (SSIM-VAXO). This approach enabled the classification of all elements into four quadrants based on their Drive Power and Dependence values and established a hierarchical structure by rank and level. Consequently, the study highlighted critical sub-elements for livestock sector development, notably the provision of human resources equipped with appropriate breeding knowledge and skills, and the enhancement of managerial skills through targeted training programs. 

Keywords: livestock, strategy, Interpretative Structural Modeling (ISM)

Antioxidants play a critical role in mitigating oxidative stress. Red dragon fruit (Hylocereus polyrhizus) is recognized as a plant-based source rich in antioxidant flavonoids. Processing red dragon fruit into puree form is an effective method to preserve both its nutritional content and sensory qualities. This study aimed to characterize the antioxidant profile and evaluate the antioxidant activity of red dragon fruit puree subjected to pasteurization at varied temperatures of 65°C, 75°C, and 85°C. An experimental design was employed to assess multiple parameters, including bioactive compound concentrations (total phenols, flavonoids, anthocyanins), antioxidant capacity measured via DPPH and FRAP assays, as well as water and crude fiber content. The results indicated that total phenol content decreased progressively with increasing pasteurization temperatures: 1.15 mg GAE/g at 65°C, 0.94 mg GAE/g at 75°C, and 0.91 mg GAE/g at 85°C, with further reduction noted at 95°C (0.84 mg GAE/g). Similarly, flavonoid content was highest at 65°C (0.71 mg QE/g) and diminished at elevated temperatures (0.70 mg QE/g at both 75°C and 85°C, and 0.56 mg QE/g at 95°C). Anthocyanin levels followed a comparable trend, declining from 51.18% at 65°C to 29.55% at 95°C. Antioxidant activity assessed via the DPPH method revealed IC50 values ascending from 4.18 mg/mL at 65°C up to 112.56 mg/mL at 95°C, signifying reduced activity at higher temperatures. Correspondingly, FRAP assay results demonstrated a decrease in antioxidant capacity from 12.75 mg at 65°C to 9.90 mg at 95°C. Water content remained relatively stable between 65°C and 85°C (approximately 88.66%–89.13%), with a notable decrease at 95°C (83.8%). Crude fiber content exhibited minor reductions with increasing temperature, ranging from 7.7% at 65°C to 6.52% at 95°C. The findings suggest that exposure to elevated pasteurization temperatures leads to a significant diminution of bioactive compounds and antioxidant potential in red dragon fruit puree.

Keywords: Red dragon fruit puree, antioxidant profile, antioxidant activity, pasteurization effects, bioactive compounds

Political participation constitutes a fundamental element of democratic governance, with the deficiency of political engagement among citizens serving as a key indicator of a democratic deficit within a political system. Addressing the challenges associated with the Voter List Problem (DPT), the Constitutional Court, through Decision No. 102/PUU-VII/2009 dated July 6, 2009, mandated that individuals not registered on the voter list are permitted to exercise their voting rights by presenting residency identification documents such as the Resident ID Card (KTP), Family Card (KK), or passport. This provision is further codified in Article 40, paragraph 5 of Law No. 8 of 2012 concerning the elections for the DPR (House of Representatives), DPD (Regional Representative Council), and DPRD (Regional People's Representative Council), stipulating that voters who utilize the KTP or passport are to be included in a Special Voter List (DPK). Despite considerable efforts by the General Elections Commission (KPU) to refine the electoral process, persistent issues related to the accuracy and completeness of the voter lists continue to be observed. The initiatives aimed at updating the voter data have not achieved optimal results, partly due to reports from the electorate concerning the election supervisors’ lack of oversight over the Voter Registration Officers (PPDP) during the designated one-month update period.  
 
Keywords: political participation, democracy, voter list, electoral process

This study seeks to evaluate the profitability and economic feasibility of the Virgin Coconut Oil agro-industry operated by the Grace Farmers Group in Tandurusa Village, Aertembaga Sub-District, Bitung District. The research employs an agro-industrial survey method focusing on the business activities of the Grace Farmers Group in Tandurusa. Data were gathered through structured interviews using a questionnaire, with purposive sampling applied to select members of the Grace Farmers Group as respondents.

Profit analysis was conducted using the formulas TC = TFC + TVC (total cost equals total fixed costs plus total variable costs), TR = Q × P (total revenue equals quantity times price), and π = TR - TC (profit equals total revenue minus total cost). Subsequently, the R/C ratio, defined as total revenue divided by total costs incurred during production, was calculated to assess feasibility: an R/C ratio greater than 1 indicates profitability, equal to 1 denotes a break-even point, and less than 1 signifies unfeasibility. Additionally, the Break Even Point (BEP) analysis was employed to determine whether the Virgin Coconut Oil agro-industry experiences profit or loss.

The results reveal that the total variable costs amount to IDR 81.96 million per year and the total fixed costs to IDR 8.295 million per year. Total revenue was recorded at IDR 249.6 million annually. The BEP was determined to be 61.75 liters, with the corresponding BEP value quantified as IDR 12,343,750 per year, IDR 1,028,645 per month, and IDR 85,720 per two days. The annual profit amounted to IDR 159.345 million. The R/C ratio was calculated at 3, indicating that the Virgin Coconut Oil agro-industry managed by the Grace Farmers Group in Tandurusa Village is profitable and financially viable for development, as it exceeds both the BEP and the R/C ratio threshold of 1.

The study also identifies that fluctuations in raw material prices and availability significantly affect Virgin Coconut Oil production, alongside the level of venture capital investment. Overall, the Virgin Coconut Oil agribusiness presents opportunities to enhance farmers' incomes, generate employment, and contribute positively to the national foreign exchange reserves.

ABSTRACT This research is entitled 'Morphological Process of Nouns in English and Gorontalo Language: a Contrastive Analysis. The objective of the analysis are to identify, and describe the morphological process of nouns in English and Gorontalo language and finding out the similarities and the differences of morphological process of nouns in English and Gorontalo language by using of O'Grady's (1992) theory and contrastive method using Lado (1957) and Whitman (1970). The English data were collected from several English textbooks. Some of them are Morphology: Word Structure in Generative Grammar (1990) by John T. Jensen, and the data of Gorontalo Language from the native speaker's four informants who can speak Gorontalo Language at the age of 20-60 years old in Manado. The result of this research shows that in morphological process of nouns in English and Gorontalo language have some similarities and differences. The similarities are that English and Gorontalo language have affixation as prefix and suffix, reduplication as full of reduplication, compounding as endocentries and excocentries compounding. The difference is that English language has not infix affixation but in Gorontalo language has an infix affixation, reduplication in English has full reduplication with variety of phoneme and in Gorontalo languages have a partial reduplication. Keywords: Morphological Process of Nouns, English and Gorontalo Languages, Contrastive Analysis.

This study examines the impact of government policies on the regional income generated from alcohol aren in North Sulawesi, a commodity with active market trade and consumption behaviors. Government regulations concerning taxation, licensing, and fees significantly influence regional revenue derived from this sector. The research aims to analyze how these policies affect the production of alcohol aren, the associated alcohol and ethanol industries, and consumer demand patterns.

The analysis utilizes time series data from 2013 to 2018, collected from various sources including the Plantation Service, the Central Statistics Agency (BPS), the Trade Regulatory Agency (Deprindag), the World Bank, and industry reports such as those from Casanova and Segaran Sari. A system of simultaneous equations—comprising eleven equations in total (nine structural and two identity equations)—was estimated using the Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS) method implemented through SAS 9.1 software.

Findings indicate that regional income is directly influenced by tax revenues, which are themselves affected by the production of alcoholic beverages (minol). The production of minol is dependent on the output of "captikus" (alcohol aren) and the aggregate industry capacity. Moreover, captikus production responds to the prices of both captikus and minol, while the price of captikus is determined by the demand for minol. Additionally, the price of minol influences captikus production and the demand for alcohol aren. The demand for alcohol aren subsequently affects the demand for minol, which is influenced by minol’s price and supply. Finally, the supply of minol is related to stock levels.

Keywords: Alcohol Aren, Demand and Supply, Production, Quantity Tax, Gross Domestic Regional Product, Simultaneous Equations

The objective of this study is to identify the potential and formulate development strategies for food crop cultivation within the agropolitan region of West Kawangkoan District. Conducted over a three-month period from April to June 2015, this research involved descriptive analysis to assess the food crop potential, while the formulation of development strategies was guided by a SWOT analytical framework. The findings indicate that the agropolitan region in West Kawangkoan District holds significant potential for cultivating maize and peanuts, supported by favorable land conditions and well-developed infrastructure, including buildings, roads, transportation networks, markets, electricity, and telecommunications. Additionally, collaborative partnerships with relevant agencies contribute to the advancement of agropolitan development. Recommended strategic actions include optimizing the use of available resources and farmer expertise in managing maize and peanut crops, enhancing productivity through the adoption of appropriate technologies, and expanding the processing industry to satisfy consumer demand. Furthermore, establishing robust cooperation with government entities is essential for effective mentoring and monitoring of the distribution channels for seeds, fertilizers, and agricultural machinery, ensuring their timely provision from manufacturers to intermediaries and ultimately to farmers. Strengthening synergies between farmers and processing as well as animal feed industries is also vital for advancing the agropolitan region. The selection of this region was informed by a SWOT analysis, positioning it within the first cell of the second quadrant, indicative of an aggressive growth strategy. This approach is expected to stimulate the development of food crops, particularly maize and peanuts, in the West Kawangkoan District.

Keywords: Food Crops, Agropolitan Region, Development Strategy, SWOT Analysis

The present study aimed to examine the level of interest among the Tuminting Village community regarding the development of quail farming as a strategy to enhance family economic stability in the context of the New Normal. Additionally, the research sought to provide an overview of the community’s basic knowledge concerning the potential expansion of quail farming utilizing simple technological methods. The variables assessed included educational attainment, occupational engagement and income levels within the community, the degree of interest in quail farming, and the comprehension of village officials about quail cultivation. Data were analyzed through percentage calculations and visually represented using bar charts, while observational findings were described qualitatively based on direct interactions with community members. Results indicated that approximately 32.02% of the population expressed interest in advancing quail farming during the Covid-19 New Normal period. The basic understanding of quail farming among community members was measured at 51.09%. In contrast, over 56.25% of village officials demonstrated limited understanding of quail farming practices; nevertheless, they exhibited strong support for the development of quail cultivation, with a support rate of approximately 84.75%. In conclusion, despite a substantial proportion of participants lacking comprehensive knowledge, there remains a pronounced interest and willingness to engage in quail farming as a means to bolster the family economy amid the New Normal Covid-19 era.

Keywords: community interest, village officials, quail farming, New Normal Covid-19

This study seeks to evaluate the biophysical potential of the Kali Tahapan Telu Waterfall region. The research was conducted in August 2020 at the Kali Tahapan Telu Waterfall, located in Kali Village, Pineleng District, North Sulawesi. Employing a survey methodology, primary data were gathered through interviews with stakeholders involved in the management of the natural tourism site, complemented by direct observations of the waterfall and its environs. These observations focused on aspects such as tourist attractions, accessibility, accommodation, facilities, and tourism support infrastructure. Secondary data were sourced from existing literature and relevant institutional agencies. Data analysis was performed using a scoring technique.

Findings indicate that the natural tourism site exhibits considerable biophysical potential, characterized by the biotic and physical environmental attributes that render it suitable for tourism development. Specifically, the area is home to two faunal species endemic to North Sulawesi and four floristic species distinctive to the region. Furthermore, the site offers multiple appealing vantage points, both outwardly from the tourist area and internally between its various sections. The biophysical potential, as assessed through the scoring method, was categorized as moderate.

Enhancement of this biophysical potential may be achieved by introducing additional endemic plant species within and around the tourist area, thereby elevating its attractiveness through increased biodiversity and conservation emphasis. Such initiatives would also serve educational purposes by highlighting local natural resources. Additionally, infrastructure improvements—such as the construction of viewing platforms or gazebos reflecting local architectural styles, alongside aesthetically pleasing landscape designs—could augment the scenic value and overall visitor experience.

Regarding agricultural land use, the presence of community-managed agricultural plots featuring regionally characteristic crops such as cloves, coconut, palm, and nutmeg contributes indirectly to the touristic appeal, especially when integrated with complementary landscape designs that frame and enhance the natural scenery. Directly linked to community empowerment, the development of agricultural products into marketable souvenirs represents an untapped opportunity that could stimulate local economic growth. Moreover, involving local communities in augmenting the area's attractions—particularly through the promotion of regional cultural heritage—further supports sustainable tourism development.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate organic strawberry agribusiness in the East Bolaang Mongondow Regency by evaluating the dimensions of agribusiness players, the dimensions of agribusiness activity and the dimensions of behavior of organic strawberry agribusiness. The method used in this study was the survey method. The selection of the location of the study was done intentionally by determining the highland area in the East Bolaang Regency that cultivated strawberries. The area was the village of Mooat, Guaan Village, and New Bongkudai Village. This research begins in May to August 2018. The types of data used in this study were primary and secondary data. Data were analyzed using income analysis, added value, and were evaluated with an evaluation structure design adopted from the modified Hammond Evaluation Structure into agribusiness. The results of the study showed that agribusiness players consisting of key players had not made strawberries as commercial commodities while the tourism business of D'Mooat had made strawberries as a commercial commodity. The agricultural input activities were in the form of the use of the workforce of the community around the tourist area and the provision of production facilities, both purchased and made by themselves. The agricultural production activities had not fully utilized organic materials with an average production of 1,080 kg / year and the revenues of Rp.128,505,250/year for the area of 2,000 m2. The agricultural industry activities provided added value around of Rp. 57,000 / kg for strawberries and the average profit of Rp. 52,870 / kg through processing strawberries into strawberry juice, smoothie strawberry juice and dragon berry juice. Agricultural marketing activities were take place only in the tourist attractions area. The agricultural service activities were in the form of credit from Bank (BRI) while coordination with related agencies has not been established. The production technique behavior was good; the agribusiness management behavior was still in traditional way, whereas the agribusiness system behavior have not yet.

This study aims to determine the potential and opportunities for developing crystal guava farming and to analyze the financial feasibility of crystal guava farming in Warisa Village, Talawaan Sub-district, North Minahasa Regency. The study was conducted from July to October 2020. The selection of respondents was carried out by purposive sampling method. The research used primary data and secondary data. Primary data obtained from interviews, based on a questionnaire to one guava crystal farmer. Secondary data were obtained from the Head of Village Office, the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) and the Agriculture Office of North Minahasa Regency. The results showed that the potential of natural resources, namely the availability of land for the development of crystal guava cultivation is still quite extensive and the use of existing land can still be maximized. Warisa Village fulfills the growing requirements for the development of guava plants because it is located at an altitude of ± 1-500 meters above sea level (masl), has a temperature of around 26.9-33,710 C in the daytime, rainfall is 1,993 mm year, type of soil is loose and fertile. PRODUCTION PERFORMANCE OF GROWING PIGS FED RATION CONTAINING CAKALANG FISH WASTE PRODUCT. The study aims to determine the extent of the effect of using fish waste flour as a partial substitute for concentrates in feed on the appearance of grower phase pig production to finiser. Swines are very potential to be developed in North Sulawesi because they have the attributes and capabilities of fast growth rates, high number of litter size, good ration efficiency, and a high percentage of carcass. Cakalang fish waste is one of the feed ingredients that are potentially used as animal feed ingredients because it is easy to be obtained and its price is relatively cheap. Cakalang fish waste can be processed into fish meal and can be used for animal feed mixtures including swines, poultry and fishery. This research was carried out on the farm belongs to Mr. Cloudio Lumowa, starting with the pre-trial for the 2 weeks and data collection for the 10 weeks, starting on June 14 to August 26, 2017. Research was using 20 heads of gilt and boar with a range body weight of 53-63kg. The research design used was Randomized Block Design (RCBD) involving 4 treatments and 5 replications at each treatment. The treatments of feeding were including R0 = ration without cakalang fish waste flour, R1 = ration + 2% cakalang fish waste flour, R2 = ration + 4% cakalang fish waste flour, and R3 = ration + 6% cakalang fish waste flour. The results of the research showed that the use of cakalang fish waste flour with a level of 2%, 4%, and 6% had a significant effect (P< 0.05) on swine weight gain and feed effciciency, but did not affect significantly feed consumption. Based on the results of the study and discussion of all variables, it can be concluded that the use of cakalang fish waste flour as a partial replacement of concentrate up to 6% in grower to finisher produced the same ration consumption, a good body weight gain and feed efficiency.Keywords: cakalang fish waste, production, grower

Abstract: This research aims at examining the effectiveness of settling the objection of waste retribution which is based on the time accomplished, coordination within relevant technical institutions and the capability of human resources at Local Revenue Office of Manado City. This study used qualitative research and the data were collected through interviews, direct observing and documentation. The informants were obtained based on the consideration of the researcher, i.e. they are deemed able to provide objectives and accurate information in accordance with the research problem. The informants from the civil servants of the Local Revenue Office of Manado City were 3 persons and 5 persons from the compulsory of cleanliness retribution so the total number of all informants was 8 persons. The results of this study show that those involved in a compulsory retribution were generally satisfied with the service but they did not feel satisfied with the follow-up of results of the report's objection. Thus it is suggested that in order to improve the performance of employees required upgrading the capacity in terms of employees' active participation in education and functional training on local taxes and retribution, the working motivation of employees and compensation. Keywords: effectiveness of settling the objection, waste retribution

This study seeks to evaluate the value of coconut flour at PT. Tropica Cocoprima. The research was conducted at PT. Tropica Cocoprima and its supply chain stakeholders located in Lelema Village, Tumpaan Subdistrict, South Minahasa Regency, along Jalan Trans Sulawesi. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in this investigation. Data collection was performed through interviews employing questionnaires designed to address issues pertinent to the research objectives. The sampling technique employed was purposive sampling, with the focal firm, PT. Tropica Cocoprima, included alongside five raw material suppliers and two coconut farmers selected from each supplier, totaling ten farmers. The analysis was carried out using value chain methodology, incorporating cost and margin assessments. Findings indicate that multiple actors participate in the value creation process of the coconut flour value chain at PT. Tropica Cocoprima, including coconut farmers and suppliers who provide raw materials to the firm. Each participant in the value chain earns a margin reflective of their respective efforts. The cumulative value added through the involvement of one, two, and three actors amounted to Rp. 195,000,000. Specifically, PT. Tropica Cocoprima achieved a margin of Rp. 12,277,822, suppliers obtained Rp. 6,675,000, and coconut farmers gained Rp. 100,102,700.

This study aimed to find out the right extraction method to produce ketapang leaf extract with best phytochemical content and best inhibition ability against ice-ice causing bacteria. The experiment was conducted at the Laboratory of Fish Health, Environmental and Toxicology, from April to June, 2021. The experiment was designed according to a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 5 treatments and 3 replications. The three main treatments were, treatment A: extraction of ketapang leaves Terminalia catappa L. with 95% ethanol (extract A), treatment B: extraction of ketapang leaves T. catappa L. with 40°C water (extract B), and treatment C, extraction of ketapang leaves T. catappa L. with distilled water (extract C). In the inhibition ability test, each extract obtained from the three main treatments was compared with two controls namely treatment D: positive control (Kanamicyn) and treatment E: negative control (aquadest). The phytochemical content data was analyzed descriptively, while the bacterial inhibition zone diameter data was statistically analyzed with Anova and LSD. The phytochemical analysis result showed that, the extract A contains alkaloids, flavonoids, triterpenoids and tannins, while extract B and extract C contain alkaloid, saponin and tannin. The inhibition ability test showed that extract A gave the strongest inhibition (14.87 mm) against the ice-ice causing bacteria, and was significantly different from that of extract B (5.23 mm) and C (2.47 mm). The inhibition ability of extract B was significantly different from that of extract C. The inhibition ability of the three ketapang leaf extracts (A, B and C) against the ice-ice causing bacteria was much weaker and significantly different from that of Kanamicyn (positive control).

Abstract: Digital marketing encompasses the promotion of products or services through various digital technologies, primarily via the internet, as well as through mobile phones, display advertising, and other digital platforms. It represents a strategic approach employed by companies to enhance their business visibility and brand recognition online. This study aims to examine the extent to which digital marketing is utilized by Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and to assess its impact on their operations. To achieve these objectives, data were collected from ten respondents through qualitative methods, specifically in-depth interviews, utilizing purposive sampling. The findings indicate that digital marketing exerts a positive influence on MSME owners and plays a crucial role in the promotion and sale of their products. Additionally, digital marketing facilitates customer reach in a cost-effective and measurable manner. Its advantages include ease of use, significant utility, and particular benefits for novices in the field. It is recommended that MSME proprietors invest in enhancing their knowledge and skills related to digital marketing to further leverage its potential.  
Keywords: digital marketing, MSMEs, utilization

ABSTRACTPIG FARM ANALYSIS OF KASEWEAN COMPANY AT KAKASKASEN II OF TOMOHON MUNICIPALITY. The objective of this study were to find cost production, benefit and break even point of pig farming in Kasewean enterprise located in Tomohon city. The Results of the study showed that, Kasewean enterprise had breakeven Point on pig farming at 103 103 heads, and the income level was Rp. 178.509.314/period of production. Value of the breakeven point could be seen through the value Margin Of Safety (MOS) of 67.62%, meaning that if the rate of production decreased by 67.63%, the pig farm is still in state of breakeven point, then the MOS value can be explained by Return Of Invesment (ROI). ROI obtained a value of 1.51. This means that the use of capital (cost of production) on a pig farm "Kasawean" in Tomohon already at efficient scale or provide the level of profit. Conclusions were (1) The average cost of production of pig farming in Kasewean company Tomohon was 1.136.863/head/production period consisted of a fixed cost of Rp. 278.093 of a fixed cost and Rp. 858.770/heads/production period of variable cost with the value of ROI was 1.51 which means the use of capital (cost of production) of pig farm on the"Kasewean" company in Tomohon already efficient, (2) Pig farm on the "kasewean" company obtained significant profit because the everage income was Rp. 580.932/head/production period and the average monthly profit was Rp. 15.539.943. and (3) Animal farm on "Kasewean" company has reached the value above breakeven point of 103.92 on production volume of 103 units or heads with turnover level of Rp. 178.509.314/production periodKey Words : Pig farming, benefit, cost, breakeven point

Good village financial management is an important aspect in the success of village development and community welfare. Moreover, each year the funds allocated to each village have increased. Good village financial management is management that is in accordance with guidelines set by the government, which is contained in Permendagri Number 113 of 2014 concerning Village Financial Management. The purpose of this study is to analyze the adequacy of village financial management, especially in the process of expenditure administration organized by the Ongkaw Tiga Village Government. In this study, the type of data used is qualitative data, while for data sources using primary data, and the analytical method used is descriptive analysis method. Based on the results of the study, it was concluded that in the preparation of the RAB, filing employee expenditure, filing SPP on goods and services spending, filing SPP capital expenditure almost everything done by the Ongkaw Tiga village government can be said to be not complied with. After the evaluation, the factors that influence the non-compliance of the village government in carrying out the procedures for submitting village expenditures are the lack of knowledge and understanding of the village apparatus from the Village Head to the Implementing Officer on the rules imposed so that there are many errors in the preparation or preparation of these documents.

This study investigates the influence of training on the competencies of Agricultural Extension Workers, as well as the impact of the organizational environment on these competencies. Additionally, it examines how training and organizational environment affect the performance of Agricultural Extension Workers, considering work competence as an intervening variable. Employing an exploratory research design with a quantitative approach, the study was conducted at the North Sulawesi Provincial Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Department. Given the limited population size, the entire population of 18 individuals was sampled. Data were collected and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods, specifically path analysis with t-tests for hypothesis testing. The findings indicate that training has a significant positive effect on the work competence of Agricultural Extension Workers. Similarly, the organizational environment significantly influences their work competence. Furthermore, work competence exerts a significant impact on the performance of these workers. Both training and the organizational environment were found to have significant direct effects on performance, as well as indirect effects mediated through work competence. Overall, the study reveals increases in both the direct and indirect influences among the variables under investigation.

In accordance with PSAK 24, recognition and measurement of short term employee benefits are recorded at the expense at the time the employee is payable while the post-employment benefits expense is recognized and measured based on contributions paid by the company. PT Vandika Abadi also provides post-employment benefits that are benefits to its employees, employee benefits are payments and services that protect and supplement salaries.Keywords: PSAK 24, Short-term Employee Benefit, Post Employment Benefit

This study aims to analyze the relevance of the report on the realization of the use of school operational assistance funds, the obstacles that hinder and the efforts to overcome the obstacles to financial management in North Halmahera Regency. This research method is exploratory qualitative research. The term "expectation gap" in auditing refers to the disparity between auditors' perceptions of their responsibilities and the expectations held by users of financial statements regarding the auditors' actual duties. This study aimed to investigate the differences in perceptions between accounting students and management students concerning the implementation of audit procedures that result in an unqualified opinion, particularly in relation to auditor responsibility and independence. Employing a quantitative research design, the study population comprised eighth-semester students enrolled in the Accounting and Management Departments of the undergraduate (S1) program. A purposive sampling technique was utilized to select respondents. A total of 60 questionnaires were distributed and all were deemed valid for analysis. Hypothesis testing was conducted using the Independent Sample T-Test, facilitated by the SPSS software version 23.0. The findings from the Independent Sample T-Test indicated that (1) there exists a significant difference in perceptions between accounting and management students regarding auditor responsibility, and (2) a significant difference also exists between the two groups concerning auditor independence.

Keywords: Unqualified Opinion Implementation, Expectation Gap, Students, Auditor Responsibility, Auditor Independence.

This study seeks to examine the extent of parental participation in the administration of Kinilow GMIM Primary School Education in Tomohon City. The theoretical framework employed is Epstein's (2001) model, which delineates parental involvement into six distinct categories: parenting, communication, volunteering, learning at home, decision-making, and collaboration with the community. Participation is conceptualized as the engagement of an individual or group in activities, encompassing mental, emotional, and physical dimensions, whereby individuals utilize their full capacities, including initiative-taking, to support the achievement of goals and assume responsibility for their involvement. Specifically, participation entails the psychological and emotional engagement of individuals within group contexts.

This investigation adopts a qualitative research design aimed at providing a systematic, factual, and accurate description of the issues and characteristics pertinent to the population under study. Data collection methods include: (1) interviews, defined as oral question-and-answer sessions intended to elicit descriptive accounts of lived experiences; (2) observations, employed to gather empirical data concerning parental involvement in the delivery of educational services; and (3) documentation, which involves the examination and recording of existing documents relevant to the study.

The findings reveal several challenges, notably the necessity for synergistic parenting efforts between the school and families, ensuring a supportive environment conducive to children's task completion. Additionally, effective communication between parents and children fosters a sense of recognition and openness, thereby strengthening relational transparency. Furthermore, the remaining four dimensions of parental involvement must complement one another to facilitate productive cooperation between parents and the school, ultimately enhancing child development.

Keywords: Parental Participation, Educational Administration, Community Engagement, Qualitative Research

In industrial operations, heavy metals are extensively utilized to enhance and manufacture products. The use of heavy metals as catalysts, products, and by-products has resulted in the contamination of coastal areas around Bitung Municipality with heavy metal pollutants. The present study aimed to assess the impact of industrial heavy metal activities on the socio-economic conditions of farmers and the surrounding communities, as indicated by biological assessment methods, in the coastal regions of Bitung Municipality. Research was conducted from May 1999 to January 2000, involving eleven sampling sites distributed throughout the coastal areas of Bitung Municipality. Samples were collected biweekly at each site and subsequently analyzed in the laboratory. A socio-economic survey of farmers was administered following the determination of heavy metal concentrations in the samples. The findings revealed that biodiversity indices for benthic fauna ranged between 0.33 and 2.79. In most locations from Station 2 to Station 11, plankton diversity indices varied from 1.12 to 3.14, with approximately 48 plankton species observed during the study period. Shell diversity indices ranged from 0 to 1.79, while fish diversity indices varied from 0 to 2.43, with many indices exceeding the value of 2. In conclusion, the results indicate that industrial activities surrounding the coastal areas of Bitung Municipality have introduced heavy metal contamination into the bodies of various marine organisms, including benthic fauna, plankton, fish, and shell species, with variability observed across the eleven sampling sites.

Abstract:  
The effective organization of government bodies is essential to ensure high-quality work performance and to foster professional operations, thereby enhancing the authority and efficiency of public sector institutions. Competitiveness is predominantly demonstrated through proficiency in technical tasks, including the mastery of modern technologies, which are currently indispensable for each organization aiming to improve productivity and public sector competence. This study aims to examine the role of the head of government organizations in the development of subdistricts within Southeast Minahasa Regency, Ratahan. Employing qualitative research methods, this investigation explores the natural conditions and current status of the organizational environment as critical instruments for assessment. The findings reveal that the leadership role of the government head in village development is well-executed, fulfilling fundamental tasks and functions as the primary leader in Ratahan. Notably, improvements in employee work quality have been observed, particularly through the enforcement of stricter disciplinary measures aimed at cultivating a workforce that is both professional and high-performing. Furthermore, the leader actively promotes technical competency by encouraging employees to enhance and update their skills continuously. Specific initiatives include training programs focused on computer operations and other technological tools. Nonetheless, certain limitations and challenges persist, which have prevented the village government organization from achieving optimal performance.  

Keywords: Role of the Head of Government Organization, Subdistrict Development, Public Sector Leadership, Technical Competency, Qualitative Research

Positioning constitutes a crucial element in marketing planning and the formulation of business strategies. Product positioning refers to the process by which marketers identify the most effective means of communicating their products’ attributes to targeted customers, taking into account consumer needs, competitive dynamics, available communication channels, and strategically developed key messages. Indonesia’s population growth rate was estimated at one percent in 2013. Nutritional experts and pediatricians recommend that infants consume either breast milk or formula, with infant formula serving as a substitute for breastfeeding. The infant formula market features numerous competing brands. This study aims to identify and illustrate the brand positioning of various infant formula brands available in the Manado market through the application of perceptual mapping, incorporating multidimensional scaling and correspondence analysis methods. A sample of 100 respondents was employed for data collection. The brands examined include SGM, Lactogen, Nutrilon, Enfagrow, S26, and Nan. Price and quality were selected as the primary attributes for assessing the brands. Findings from perceptual mapping reveal that demographic factors such as age and occupation are correlated with brand perception. Variations in age and occupational status may lead to differing preferences and perceptions regarding infant formula brands.  
Keywords: consumer perception, perceived price, perceived quality.

THE DEVELOPMENT POTENTIAL OF LAYER POULTRY IN WEST HALMAHERA REGENCY.The objective of this study was to analyse the potential and constraints and strategic priority of laying hen development. Respondents were chosen purposively involving farmers, policy makers and related stakeholders. Breeders weregenerally in their productive age with medium education levels, the breeders who were not been trained and the breeders who had no breeding experience. Majority of breeders had the profession as farmers. The ownership status of the farm business belongs to both group and private, and most of them made their livestock business as a sideline to add their income. Management of cultivation wasnot done properly so that the population fluctuated, and productivity was very low. The main strength was business capital support from local government and egg marketing was relatively easy. The main weakness was the lack of information. The main opportunity was the government policy supporting the livestock industry in conducive situation and the biggest threat was the price of feed tending to fluctuate. The alternative strategy achieved were increasing the market share to achieve market leader position through local government policy, improving the quality of human resources through mentoring and assistance to increase productivity, providing livestock production facilities, especially feed in the area by utilizing available local raw materials, and establishing cooperation through partnership between farmers and the private company. Based on QSPM analysis, the priority of strategy chosen was to establish cooperation through partnership between breeder and private sector / Animal Husbandry Company with the highest total TAS value of 5,353. Keywords: layerdevelopment strategy, West Halmahera regency potential.

This study seeks to elucidate the supply chain of coconut wood-based furniture, with a specific focus on the Technical Education Training Center (Kaaten BLPT) located in Tomohon City. The research was conducted over a three-month period, from September to November 2017. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized. Primary data were collected through direct field observations and in-depth interviews involving three respondents: one coconut farmer and two employees of the Technical Education Training Center (BLPT). Secondary data were derived from company documentation. The findings reveal that the supply chain for coconut wood furniture at BLPT Kaaten encompasses four principal components: suppliers, producers, expedition services, and end consumers. Specifically, (a) suppliers of coconut wood raw materials are distributed across multiple regions including Lemoh, Tanawangko, Airmadidi, Kembes, Tenggari, Kaima, Bitung, Lolak, and Belang; (b) BLPT Kaaten is responsible for procurement, production, sales, and shipping activities; (c) expedition services facilitate the transportation of products from Bitung port to destinations outside Sulawesi, including Java Island and international export locations; and (d) the final consumers. Among the three key processes identified in the implementation of supply chain management, two—namely the flow of goods and the flow of information—are effectively managed. These well-coordinated flows have contributed to the sustained operation of coconut wood furniture production.

ABSTRACT This research is entitled "Taxonomy of Food and Beverage in English and Tondano Language (A Contrastive Analysis)". The objectives of this research are to identify, classify and describe the taxonomy of food and beverage, the way food and beverage are made and the basic ingredients of food and beverage in English and Tondano Language and to find out the similarities and differences in both languages. The data of food and beverage in English were collected from the text books, articles, and the website, while in Tondano Language were collected from informants and also by taking picture of foods and beverages in some wedding party, sorrow ceremony, restaurant, and traditional market. The data about foods in English and Tondano language that have been collected then identified, classified, and analyzed by using the theory of Frisch in Hickerson and the theory of Foley. Then, the data of both languages were contrasted by using Lado's theory. The results of this research showed that in English and Tondano language, there are similarities in the food categories namely solid foods and beverages in English, and in Tondano language namely solid foods, and beverages. In English there are six kinds of solid food, such as meat, bread, fruits, vegetables, fish and sea food, but in Tondano language has five kinds of solid food, such as meat, fruits, vegetables, fish and rice. English and Tondano language has the same kinds of drinks, such as alcoholic and non-alcoholic drink. The way of food and beverage in English are made: namely baking, grilling, sauteing, boiling, steaming, blending and squeeze, while in Tondano language it is tapan/panggang "grilling", tinumis/tumis "sauteing", ginoreng/goreng "frying", pinera/woku "frying/grilling", kinukus/kukus "steaming", tinunu/bakar "baking", and rinubus/rebus "boiling". Food and beverage based on the basic ingredients in English are meat, fish, wheat, flour, fruits, vegetables, milk, coffee, and herbal plants, while in Tondano language are daging "meat", ikan "fish", sayur-sayuran "vegetables", buah-buahan "fruits", susu "milk", tepung "flour", umbi-umbian "tubers", beras "rice", kopi "coffee", pohon "tree" dan daun "leaf".Keywords: Taxonomy of Food and Beverage, English and Tondano Language, Contrastive Analysis

The objective of this study was to investigate and analyze the behavior of Satpol PP members, as local government officials in Manado City, in the execution of their duties and functions. A qualitative research approach was employed, with data collection conducted through interviews, observations, and documentation. The informants consisted of seven civil service members of Satpol PP, two voluntary members, one temporary member, and five community members, totaling fifteen participants. Findings indicate that Satpol PP personnel exhibited a lack of discipline in task performance, particularly regarding attendance, which was limited to participation during morning and evening briefings, notably among civil servants. The primary motivation for civil service staff was financial remuneration, whereas voluntary members were motivated solely by their status as full-time civil servants. Many personnel lacked proficiency in basic tasks, functions, and relevant legal frameworks, with some having been employed without undergoing proper selection procedures. Consequently, their conduct in the field often manifested as arrogance, emotional instability, and susceptibility to bribery. The predominance of high school-level educational attainment and limited access to training resulted in insufficient knowledge and skills pertinent to their assigned responsibilities. Based on these findings, it can be concluded that the behavior of personnel within the Manado City Civil Service Police Unit does not consistently align with statutory regulations concerning their duties and functions, nor with community expectations of police civil servants as protectors and social security agents. Deviations from performance standards and societal expectations were influenced by deficiencies in officers’ competence, personal integrity, and the work environment. Additionally, an unfavorable working atmosphere, coupled with inconsistent and unsustainable disciplinary enforcement, further impacted personnel attitudes and behaviors. To foster appropriate conduct, enhancing knowledge, attitude, and discipline is critical in shaping the behavior of agency personnel.

Keywords: work behavior, motivation, task performance, Satpol PP

This study investigates the species composition and population density of Bactrocera fruit flies in a red chili cultivation area located in Kakaskasen II Village, Tomohon Utara Subdistrict, Tomohon City, with respect to varying catch times. Employing a Randomized Block Design (RBD), the research incorporated three distinct catch time treatments: Treatment A (06:00–12:00), Treatment B (12:01–18:00), and Treatment C (19:01–05:00). Fruit fly specimens were identified at the species level. Population data were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test if significant differences among treatments were detected. The findings revealed seven species of fruit flies captured using Steiner traps baited with methyl eugenol during four consecutive observation periods in the chili field. These species included Bactrocera dorsalis (Hendel), Bactrocera umbrosa (Fabricius), Bactrocera papayae (Drew & Hancock), Bactrocera synnephes (Hendel), Bactrocera carambolae (Drew & Hancock), Bactrocera facialis (Coquillett), and an unidentified Bactrocera species. The highest fruit fly populations were recorded during the catch intervals of 06:00–12:00 and 12:01–18:00. 

Keywords: Bactrocera species, methyl eugenol, catch time, fruit fly population

ABSTRACT Ongole cross bread has important role in the economical needs of people in Tompaso Barat. In addition as beef cattle, household farmers also use it as a working cattle, source of fertilize and investment. In addition to farmer's income and the acceleration growth of cattle population, in the year of 2011, District West Tompaso Barat did an artificial insemination program. The problem was whether this program is beneficial for the farmer or not. The aim at this research is to analyze the profit of farmers using artificial insemination program. This research was conducted using survey method involving about 169 farmers raising Ongole crossbred cattle at West Tompaso District applying artificial insemination. The data were analyzed by profit analysis. Result showed that the total income received from the total sale of the beef cattle using artificial insemination were IDR 490,950,000.- with the total cost of IDR 468,945,750. The profit of the household farmers was the balance between the total income and the total cost getting IDR 21,504,250. The average income of the respondent was about IDR 716,808. Therefore, it can be concluded that the household farmers raising Ongole crossbred cattle get more profit when they used artificial insemination. Based on this research it can be suggested that the beef cattle management should be maintained on the bases of agribusiness. Keywords: Profit, Ongole crossbred cattle, Artificial Insemination

The objective of the study was to develop the cellulose Nata/dietary fiber production from coconut water using bacterium, Acetobacter xylinum, as health product containing natural fibers. The study used Complete Randomized Design with treatments of different concentration of inoculum Acetobacter xylinum, each of which had 3 replications. The treatments were liquid inoculum of Acetobacter xylinum: A = 5 %/1000 ml (5 % of liquid inocula were added into 1000 ml of coconut water), B = 7.5 %/1000 ml (7.5 % of liquid inocula were added into 1000 ml of coconut water), C = 10 %/1000 ml (10 % of liquid inocula were added into 1000 ml of coconut water), D = 12.5 %/1000 ml (12.5 % of liquid inocula were added into 1000 ml of coconut water), and E = 15 %/1000 ml (15 % of liquid inocula were added into 1000 ml of coconut water). This study concluded that 1) the liquid inocula of Acetobacter xylinum could result in cellulose nata; 2) the highest quality of the cellulose nata/dietary fiber from the use of liquid inocula of Acetobacter xylinum) was found in treatment E for pellicle weight, 1009.3 gr, layer thickness, 1.50 cm, rendement, 90.82 %, and water content, 79.71 %, and fiber level, 1.31 %, for treatment D and E, respectively. Keywords: cellulose nata, coconut wastewater, Acetobacter xylinum bacterium

This study investigates the side effects of a porang flour solution supplemented with 3% (w/v) Aluminum Sulfate on Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) levels, serving as a biomarker for liver function in Wistar rats. The experiment was carried out in a controlled laboratory setting employing a completely randomized design with three replications. The treatment involved the administration of a porang flour solution containing Aluminum Sulfate into which 3 grams of porang flour were incorporated. Prior to treatment, the rats were induced with gastric ulcers through the application of 12.5% acetic acid for three consecutive days. Subsequently, the porang flour solution was administered orally via a sonde over a period of 21 days. The parameters assessed included locomotor activity, morphological features, body weight (growth), and AST levels (U/L) measured at intervals of 7, 14, and 21 days following treatment. Statistical analysis was conducted using Statistica 6, with significance determined at a 95% confidence level. Findings revealed that rats subjected to porang flour treatment exhibited significantly lower body weight but remained healthy, exhibiting high levels of agility and movement, suggesting the potential of the porang flour combined with Aluminum Sulfate as an alternative dietary supplement. Notably, AST levels declined after 21 days of treatment. Morphological observations, coupled with the reduction in AST levels, indicated that the gastric ulcers induced by 12.5% acetic acid in Wistar rats were effectively healed after 21 days of administering a 2 mL porang flour solution via sonde.

The diversity observed among farm animals originates from a protracted process involving domestication, which encompasses migration, selective breeding, adaptation, and various natural phenomena. The preservation of this diversity necessitates conservation efforts grounded in demographic profiling, comprehensive documentation of production environments, and the implementation of robust data management systems. Within this context, molecular biology-based data assume critical importance, particularly due to the identification of numerous livestock breeds prevalent today, notably in equine and poultry species. Reliance on production records or morphological traits alone proves inadequate for elucidating species hierarchies in horses and chickens, especially within population genetic studies frequently conducted in livestock research. Molecular investigations facilitate a deeper comprehension of genetic variation in these species. It is widely accepted that chicken domestication resulted from multiple distinct events, predominantly involving the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), with possible contributions from Gallus sonneratii and Gallus lafayettii. Equine domestication, conversely, occurred across extensive regions of the Eurasian steppe, wherein mares likely underwent domestication on numerous occasions, whereas a limited number of stallions were responsible for the genetic composition of domestic horses.  

Keywords: Genetic Diversity, Horses, Chickens, Domestication, Livestock Genetic Database

The present study, entitled "Compliment Utterances in the Film *Me Before You* by Jojo Moyes: A Pragmatic Analysis," aims to identify, categorize, and examine the functions of compliment utterances within the film. Employing a descriptive research method, the data were collected from dialogues among the characters. Subsequently, these utterances were classified and analyzed according to Holmes's (1986) theoretical framework. The findings reveal five distinct types of compliment utterances and their respective functions as utilized by the characters. First, compliments related to ability comprise seven utterances, functioning to express solidarity and genuine admiration for actual skills. Second, possession-based compliments include ten utterances that serve to convey appreciation for tangible possessions deserving recognition. Third, physical appearance compliments consist of eight utterances, intended to express attraction and admiration in a sincere manner that fosters positive interpersonal communication without irony or mockery. Fourth, personality compliments account for twenty-two utterances, which aim to express solidarity, admiration, and appreciation for an individual’s behavior, character, or nature, thereby enhancing self-confidence. Lastly, compliments concerning quality include three utterances that function to acknowledge and appreciate both positive and negative qualities or actions, thus motivating the recipient. 

Keywords: Compliment utterances, *Me Before You*, Pragmatic analysis

The Regional Employment Board has not effectively managed its human resources, necessitating enhancement in the quality of personnel to improve the professional performance of its staff, particularly in the domain of management skills development. The population for this study comprised all officers or employees within Sub Tobelo, North Halmahera, totaling 25 civil servants. This research employed a quantitative methodology, selected due to the study's focus on examining the actual and factual relationships or influences between variables. Using product moment correlation and simple regression analyses, the hypothesis—that education and training have a significant impact on the organizational performance of the Regional Employment Board of North Halmahera—was tested at the 1% significance level. The findings demonstrate a substantial influence of education and training on organizational performance, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.894, indicating that approximately 89.4% of the variance in organizational performance can be attributed to education and training. Furthermore, the data reveal a strong, significant, and contributive relationship between education and training and organizational performance. These results underscore the critical role of education and training in enhancing the effectiveness of the Regional Employment Board's operations.  

Keywords: education and training, organizational performance

This research seeks to examine the impact of service quality on customer satisfaction. Employing a quantitative research design, the study utilized an accidental sampling technique, whereby respondents were selected based on convenience; individuals encountered by the researcher who met the primary criterion of being buyers or consumers were included as participants. Data collection was conducted using a Likert scale, and subsequent data analysis was performed with SPSS version 25 for Windows. The findings reveal that service quality exerts a positive influence on customer satisfaction, as evidenced by a positive correlation between these two variables. Specifically, the partial T-test analysis yielded a coefficient of 0.451 for the service quality variable, indicating a significant positive effect. Furthermore, the coefficient of determination (R²) demonstrated that service quality accounts for 28.9% of the variance in customer satisfaction, with the remaining variation attributed to factors beyond the scope of this study. Regression analysis confirmed the statistical significance of this relationship, with a significance value (p-value) of 0.000. Consequently, improvements in service quality are likely to enhance customer satisfaction.

The aim of the present research was to evaluate the daily growth ratio, food conversion ratio and mortality of grouper (Epinephelus tauvina) and rabbit fish (Siganus canaliculatus) in floating net with polyculture system. This experiment was done at the coastal area of Tomini Bay in the North Sulawesi Province. The observations were done every two weeks for three months from August - November 2014. Twenty five groupers (62.41 grams in ABWo) and twenty five rabbit fish (52.2 grams in ABWo) were used for polyculture experiment, while fifty groupers (56.71 grams in ABWo) for monoculture. The results indicated that the daily individual growth of Epinephelus tauvina on polyculture was 1.29%, with food conversion ratio 6.1, while it on monoculture was 1,18%, with food conversion ratio 6.4. The daily individual growth of Siganus canaliculatus on polyculture was 0,8%, with food conversion ratio 3.8. Mortality for all species studied were 0%. The present research showed that the polyculture system was better than monoculture system. The future studies suggest that the polyculture system in the floating net may be developed and applied as a mariculture model in the North Sulawesi Province for prosperous life of fisherman. Keywords: Epinephelus tauvina, Siganus canaliculatus, polyculture system, floating net, prosperous life, fisherman.

This study examines two key variables: bureaucratic culture and the effectiveness of apparatus services. The primary objective is to assess the impact of bureaucratic culture on the effectiveness of service delivery by apparatus members. Bureaucratic culture was operationalized through six distinct indicators, while the effectiveness of apparatus services was evaluated across three dimensions. The research was conducted within the National Unity and Political Protection Agency of Manado City. Employing a quantitative methodology, data were gathered via questionnaires administered to a sample of 41 employees from the agency. Data analysis was performed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and simple linear regression in SPSS for iOS. The Spearman correlation coefficient between bureaucratic culture and service effectiveness was found to be +0.467, indicating a statistically significant and positive association between these variables. Furthermore, the simple linear regression analysis yielded a significance value of 0.001 for the bureaucratic culture variable, which is below the threshold of 0.05, thereby confirming a significant effect of bureaucratic culture on service effectiveness. In conclusion, the findings demonstrate a significant, positive, and unidirectional relationship between bureaucratic culture and the effectiveness of apparatus services. This implies that bureaucratic culture substantially influences service effectiveness within the National Unity and Political Protection Agency of Manado City.  

Keywords: Bureaucratic Culture, Effectiveness of Apparatus Services.

The study recommends continued efforts to preserve and enhance these positive aspects within the community organization to facilitate the successful realization of its objectives.

Calcareous sponges constitute the rarest class among marine sponges, accounting for merely 4% of the sponge species currently documented worldwide. Although demosponges have been reported in abundance from multiple sites across Indonesia, only 40 species of calcareous sponges have been identified within the country over the past two centuries. This disparity underscores not only the rarity of calcareous sponges but also highlights a considerable gap in the understanding of Leucetta sponges in the Indonesian region. The present study aimed to elucidate the biological characteristics of a calcareous sponge belonging to the genus Leucetta, collected from the Sangihe Islands, Indonesia. Morphological examination was performed utilizing a modified acid digestion technique, with the resultant data subsequently compared to existing records for Leucetta species. The sponge specimen displayed triactine spicules, a diagnostic feature of the genus Leucetta. Furthermore, a comprehensive literature review was conducted to compile an inventory of Indonesian Leucetta species. Historical records indicate that 40 calcareous sponge species have been reported in Indonesia from 1890 to 2023. Notably, Leucetta avocado is recognized as an indigenous species to Palau; however, this species, along with closely related taxa, has also been documented in other regions. Consequently, it is hypothesized that the current presence of L. avocado in the Sangihe Islands and Bali results from a combination of factors including the Indonesian Throughflow, sexual reproduction, and possible stepping stone dispersal events. This study contributes novel insights into the biology and distribution of L. avocado within Indonesia.

Title: Analysis of the Effect of Feed Concentrate Type on Amino Acid Consumption in Laying Hens

Abstract:  
Laying hens require a balanced intake of various nutrients, particularly proteins that provide essential amino acids of adequate quality. Currently, multiple types of commercial concentrates for laying hens are produced by different manufacturers, with protein quality varying according to the composition of essential amino acids present in these feeds. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of different commercial concentrate types on amino acid consumption in laying hens. The research was conducted on a laying hen farm in Matali Village, East Kotamobagu District, Kotamobagu Municipality. A total of 240 Silver Strain laying hens, aged 78 weeks, were utilized. The experimental design was a completely randomized design (CRD) comprising three treatment groups with eight replications each. The treatments involved the administration of three commercial concentrates: Concentrate A (RA), Concentrate B (RB), and Concentrate C (RC). Laboratory analyses revealed that Concentrate C (RC) contained approximately 80% higher levels of key essential amino acids—including arginine, lysine, histidine, leucine, isoleucine, valine, threonine, and phenylalanine—than Concentrates A and B. These results suggest that Concentrate C provides a superior and more balanced amino acid profile both qualitatively and quantitatively compared to RA and RB. Consequently, the enhanced amino acid composition in RC was associated with increased feed consumption in laying hens relative to the other concentrates.  

Keywords: Laying hens, amino acids, commercial concentrate

The budget serves as a fundamental framework for the existence of a state and functions as a directive for future actions. The local government budgeting process should act as a standard for attaining the anticipated performance outcomes, thereby necessitating that regional budget planning clearly delineate specific performance objectives. The formulation of a well-constructed budget facilitates the acquisition of pertinent information vital for decision-making. Local governments bear the responsibility for managing local finances, and in the administration of regional financial management, the regional head possesses overarching authority and is obligated to operate in accordance with established regulations. Ensuring that the management of local finances is conducted in an orderly manner and in compliance with applicable legislation is essential.

This study aims to examine the procedures involved in budget preparation and assess the financial performance within Sonder District of Minahasa Regency. The data collection method employed is qualitative descriptive analysis, which involves detailing the processes related to budget preparation and financial performance of the local government in Sonder subdistrict. The findings indicate that the budgeting process in Sonder District commences with the formulation of the Local Government Work Plan (RKPD), followed by the General Budget Policy and Provisional Budget Ceiling (KUA/PPAS), progressing to the Working Budget Plan of Local Government Work Unit (RKA-SKPD), and culminating in the presentation of the Budget Implementation Document of the Regional Work Unit (DPA-SKPD).

The budgeting and financial performance of the local government in Sonder District are demonstrated to be relatively effective. This effectiveness is attributed to the adoption of the Planning, Programming, and Budgeting System (PPBS) approach in the budgeting process. Although some delays were noted in budget preparation, overall implementation remains well-managed and controlled. These outcomes are reflected in the careful preparation of the budget and the strategic long-term planning established for the district.

Keywords: Budget Preparation Process, Financial Performance
