This study seeks to conduct a comparative analysis of revenues derived from the Land and Building Title Transfer Duty (BPHTB) by contrasting valuations based on the Property Tax Selling Value of Tax Objects (NJOP PBB) with those derived from the Land Value Zone (ZNT) Map. Additionally, the research aims to assess the potential percentage increase in BPHTB revenue when utilizing the Land Value Zone Map within the Central Tomohon District of Tomohon City. The investigation was undertaken over a two-month period, from March to April 2020, within the Central Tomohon District, Tomohon City, North Sulawesi Province. Secondary data sources were employed, including local revenue records from property tax collections in 2018. Complementary data encompassed the 2018 Tomohon City ZNT map, the 2019 List of Tax Assessment Associations (DHKP) for Central Tomohon District, the administrative map of Central Tomohon District, and the 2019 fees associated with the Acquisition of Land and Building Rights. Utilizing a descriptive quantitative methodology, the data were analyzed and interpreted through statistical techniques. A saturated sampling approach was adopted, encompassing the entire population of 74 tax objects subject to BPHTB in Central Tomohon District. The findings reveal a significant disparity between BPHTB revenues calculated via NJOP and those based on the ZNT map, with the latter yielding higher revenue values. In light of these results, it is recommended that the Tomohon City Government promptly enhance the application of the ZNT map as a tool for determining market values to augment the potential revenue from BPHTB within Tomohon City.

Accurate, sensitive, and valid methodologies for detecting metal contamination are essential for the effective control and monitoring of metal pollution, which poses significant threats to marine ecosystems, disrupts sustainable living environments, and endangers human health. This necessity arises from the escalating discharge of hazardous wastewater substances—referred to as B3 in Indonesia—into the marine environment, a trend driven by increasing industrialization across various sectors. Notably, these B3 wastes are currently classified as "environmentally safe" according to the Indonesian Wastewater Quality Standards (IWQS), despite their potential risks. Research has identified the bioaccumulation of metals within marine organisms’ tissues, a process closely linked to the activity of metal-binding proteins known as metallothioneins. These proteins, characterized as specific non-enzymatic molecules, have been recognized as playing a crucial role in metal metabolism. While the IWQS provides regulatory guidelines, it is not rigidly fixed and may be revised or enhanced in response to evolving circumstances and advancements in technology. Importantly, the establishment of IWQS aims not only to safeguard ecosystems but also to protect the broader living environment, including human populations who are integral to environmental stewardship. Consequently, the development and implementation of sensitive, precise, and reliable techniques for quantifying pollution levels are imperative to complement and potentially refine the IWQS framework. In this context, the measurement of metallothionein levels emerges as a promising approach. Moreover, this method can be employed to identify hazardous and toxic substances (B3), thereby augmenting existing toxicity assessments and other protocols incorporated within the IWQS.

Lake Tondano constitutes a critical natural resource for the population of North Sulawesi, particularly for residents of the Minahasa Residency and the City of Manado. The lake fulfills several essential functions, including the provision of potable water, irrigation for agriculture, and the generation of hydroelectric power. Unfortunately, over the past five years, Lake Tondano has undergone considerable environmental stress, manifested by a pronounced proliferation of aquatic vegetation, alongside issues related to sediment accumulation and a decline in water volume. 

In response to these challenges, the Center for Environmental Studies at Sam Ratulangi University, in collaboration with the UCE-CEPI, has initiated an integrated research project centered on the Tondano Watershed. This study, entitled "The Abundance of Aquatic Plants in Lake Tondano," forms part of the aforementioned collaborative endeavor. The primary aim of the research was to ascertain and analyze the distribution patterns and abundance of aquatic plant species within Lake Tondano. It is anticipated that the results will establish foundational data critical for addressing problems related to eutrophication.

To achieve these objectives, vegetation analysis was conducted employing a systematic strip sampling methodology. Subsequent analyses involved the calculation of important value indices, as well as richness, diversity, and evenness indices. The results revealed the following: firstly, water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) was identified as the predominant aquatic plant species; secondly, according to the Richness Index, the Tolour area exhibited the highest species richness among the regions surrounding Lake Tondano; and thirdly, the aquatic vegetation in the Tasuka and Ranomerut areas was exclusively dominated by water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes).

Background: In response to the Covid-19 pandemic, the government has established various policies aimed at mitigating the transmission of the virus. Nevertheless, these interventions have not achieved optimal effectiveness, as evidenced by the continued presence of individuals who violate established health protocols, subsequently contributing to a rise in Covid-19 cases. This study aims to examine public perceptions regarding the implementation of government-issued policies for Covid-19 prevention within Tikala District, Manado City.

Methods: An observational cross-sectional study was conducted in August 2020 in Tikala District, Manado City. The study population comprised 100 heads of households who fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The primary variable of interest was the public’s perception of government policy implementation related to Covid-19 preventive measures. Data were analyzed using univariate statistical methods, and findings were presented in both tabular and narrative formats.

Results: Findings reveal that only 10% of respondents perceived that the government had effectively implemented policies intended to prevent Covid-19. Among the various policy measures, public dissemination of information concerning Covid-19 received the lowest approval rating. Furthermore, government oversight pertaining to mask usage, body temperature monitoring, and the verification of health documentation issued by healthcare institutions was perceived to be approximately 11%. These results suggest that governmental efforts in policy enforcement for Covid-19 prevention remain suboptimal.

Conclusion: The study concludes that government initiatives to prevent Covid-19, particularly in the domains of public communication and regulatory supervision, have not been adequately executed. It is therefore imperative that intensified and collaborative efforts in socialization and monitoring be undertaken by governmental authorities in conjunction with all regional stakeholders to effectively curb the escalation of Covid-19 cases.

This study, entitled *Commissive Acts in the Novel The Stars Shine Down by Sidney Sheldon*, employs Austin’s (1962) theory of speech acts as a foundational framework. Austin categorizes utterances based on their illocutionary force into five types: verdictives, executives, commissives, behabitives, and expositives. Among these, commissive acts are characterized by the speaker’s commitment to future actions. The present research aims to identify, classify, and analyze commissive acts within the novel *The Stars Shine Down* by Sidney Sheldon.

A descriptive research method was utilized for data collection, whereby instances of commissive acts were extracted directly from the novel. These acts were subsequently identified and classified according to the various types of commissives delineated by Austin’s theory. Furthermore, the meanings conveyed by these commissive acts were analyzed within the pragmatic context of the novel.

The findings reveal several distinct categories and their corresponding meanings, including: promises (such as completing the tower, transferring ownership of the building, and arranging a meeting with Marthin); engagements (including focusing on tasks, seeking intelligent individuals, assigning names, listening attentively, attending to a sick father, selecting a hotel location, and purchasing tickets); offerings (like reading messages, lending money, and providing advice); agreements (evident in descriptions of Lara as an “iron butterfly,” her superiority over competitors, and the depiction of Venice as a beautiful city); intentions (expressed through statements); guarantees (such as guarding her father, completing the building, and ensuring Lara’s success); mean tos (plans to travel to New York); and declarations (including assigning new workers, sending Bert to London, and canceling meetings).

It is anticipated that this study will contribute to deeper understanding of pragmatic functions, particularly commissive acts, thus offering valuable insights for readers and students engaged in the study of pragmatics through literary texts such as *The Stars Shine Down* by Sidney Sheldon.

**Keywords:** Commissive Acts, *The Stars Shine Down*, Pragmatic Analysis

Cymbopogon citratus Stapf, commonly known as lemongrass, is widely recognized as a traditional culinary ingredient distinguished by its unique and refreshing aroma. The present study aimed to quantify the phytochemical constituents of lemongrass leaves and to evaluate the effects of their extracts on the photooxidation of linoleic acid and ascorbic acid within a model system. Sequential extraction of lemongrass leaves was performed using hexane followed by methanol. The photooxidation system for linoleic acid comprised a 0.03 M solution in ethanol containing 0.017 mM erythrosine as a photosensitizer, with the reaction mixture subjected to illumination under 4000 lux fluorescent light for up to five hours. Meanwhile, ascorbic acid at a concentration of 200 μg/mL in phosphate buffer solution (pH 7.5), containing 0.0068 mM erythrosine, was exposed to illumination for twenty minutes. Phytochemical analyses were conducted by measuring total phenolic and flavonoid contents. The extent of linoleic acid photooxidation was assessed by determining peroxide values, whereas ascorbic acid degradation was monitored spectrophotometrically at 265 nm. Results indicated that the hexane extract exhibited a higher total phenolic content compared to the methanol extract. At a concentration of 1500 ppm, the hexane extract demonstrated a superior singlet oxygen quenching effect on linoleic acid photooxidation relative to the methanol extract, as evidenced by peroxide values of 3.57 and 3.72 meq/kg, respectively, after five hours of illumination. Similarly, the hexane extract at 100 ppm more effectively inhibited ascorbic acid photooxidation compared to the methanol extract, with ascorbic acid levels of 185.44 mg/kg versus 76.67 mg/kg following five hours of exposure. In conclusion, the hexane extract of lemongrass leaves contains phenolic compounds exhibiting notable singlet oxygen quenching activity.

This study investigates the performance of the rice commodity supply chain, focusing on its efficacy and efficiency in market competition and demand fulfillment. Specifically, the research examines the supply chain in Rasi Village, Southeast Minahasa Regency. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, the study sampled ten rice farmer groups. The research considers two main variables: supply chain performance and rice commodities. To mitigate uncertainties within the supply chain, strategic management approaches are deemed necessary to enhance overall efficiency. Findings indicate that, although the rice supply chain operates with a moderate level of effectiveness, it lacks full efficiency, primarily due to suboptimal organization and limited availability of key raw materials, particularly fertilizers. The present study aimed to evaluate the impact of substituting rice bran with coffee husk meal in the diets of growing pigs on dry matter and crude fiber digestibility. The experiment was conducted over a period of 60 days, involving 20 castrated male pigs of the Duroc × Spotted Poland China crossbreed, aged between 2.5 and 3.0 months, with an average body weight ranging from 30.1 to 40.0 kg. The experimental diets were formulated as follows: R0 contained 25% rice bran and 0% coffee husk meal (control); R1 included 18.75% rice bran and 6.25% coffee husk meal (25% substitution); R2 consisted of 12.5% rice bran and 12.5% coffee husk meal (50% substitution); R3 comprised 6.25% rice bran and 18.75% coffee husk meal (75% substitution); and R4 involved 0% rice bran and 25% coffee husk meal (100% substitution). A Completely Randomized Block Design (CRBD) with five treatments and four replications was employed for statistical analysis using ANOVA. Treatment differences were further assessed through orthogonal contrast tests, with significance declared at P < 0.05. The parameters measured included digestibility of dry matter and crude fiber. Results indicated a statistically significant increase (P < 0.05) in crude fiber digestibility corresponding with the elevated levels of rice bran substitution by coffee husk meal. Conversely, no significant effect (P > 0.05) on dry matter digestibility was observed across the treatments. In conclusion, replacing rice bran with coffee husk meal up to 100% in the diet of growing pigs enhances crude fiber digestibility without adversely affecting dry matter digestibility.

Keywords: growing pigs, rice bran, coffee husk meal, dry matter digestibility, crude fiber digestibility

This study aims to analyze the suitability of the accountability of social aid expenditures in the Manado City Government with applicable regulations, to analyze the obstacles faced in the implementation of social aid expenditure accountability and the efforts made by the Manado City Government to increase the accountability of social aid expenditures. This study uses a qualitative method with an exploratory case study approach. Data were obtained through in-depth interviews, documentation studies and observation.The results of the study indicate that the accountability of social aid expenditures in the Manado City Government has been implemented based on the regulations set by the government, although in its management there are still some obstacles. These constraints are human resource competence, compliance, sanctions, coordination, monitoring and regulation. Of the seven processes for managing social aid expenditures, the accountability and reporting processes are the processes that often experience problems, namely human resource competence, compliance, coordination and monitoring. Meanwhile, efforts that have been made to increase the accountability of social aid expenditures are by conducting socialization and requesting accountability reports to recipients of social assistance.Furthermore, there are several things that are recommended to increase the accountability of social aid expenditures to the Manado City Government, namely: it is necessary to pay attention to the balance of the use of human resources between the number of staff needed (quantity) and the expertise (competence) possessed; strict sanctions must be regulated in regulations and actually implemented; it is necessary to have an initiative from the manager in this case the related SKPD to study the regulations that become a reference on the main tasks and functions in the management of social aid expenditures; coordination between fellow social aid managers needs to be carried out; the manager is obliged to assist the recipient in preparing the accountability report; in addition to sending letters and making calls, requests for accountability reports need to be followed up by picking up directly from the recipient; managers need to provide an accountability report format, because in addition to assisting recipients in making accountability reports, they also facilitate auditors in conducting audits.

This study seeks to identify marketing patterns and quantify margins, profits, marketing costs, as well as the farmers' share in Sinisir Village, Modoinding Sub-district, Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted over the period from June to August 2018. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in this investigation. Primary data were gathered through interviews guided by a predetermined questionnaire administered to 14 respondents, comprising 10 farmers from Sinisir Village, one collecting trader from Tompaso Baru Dua Village, two retailers from Tompaso Baru Dua Village and Karombasan Village, and one large trader from Sinisir Village, Modoinding District. Secondary data were acquired from the Sinisir Village Office of Modoinding District, local bookstores, and online sources, including books and theses from other universities retrieved via Google search. The findings revealed four distinct marketing channels in Sinisir Village, Modoinding District: (I) Farmers to Consumers; (II) Farmers to Retailers to Consumers; (III) Farmers to Collector Traders to Retailers to Consumers; and (IV) Farmers to Wholesalers. Among these, the carrot marketing channel with the highest cost, margin, and marketing profit was Channel II, amounting to Rp 5,429 per kilogram, Rp 6,000 per kilogram, and Rp 571 per kilogram, respectively. Furthermore, the greatest farmers’ share was observed in Channel I, reaching 100 percent.

ABSTRACT  
This study, entitled "Mood in English and Tontemboan Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify, classify, analyze, and compare the moods present in both English and Tontemboan. The English language data were sourced from books and websites, while data for the Tontemboan language were collected through interviews with several native speakers residing in Kopiwangker, Langowan district. The researcher employed Frank’s (1972) theoretical framework to identify and classify the types and functions of mood and utilized Lado’s (1957) theory for conducting the contrastive analysis between the two languages. A descriptive research method was applied throughout the study. The findings reveal that both languages exhibit three types of mood—imperative, subjunctive, and indicative—each serving distinct functions. Specifically, the imperative mood is used to express commands or requests; the subjunctive mood conveys unreality, wishes, and conjectures; and the indicative mood is employed in all other contexts not covered by the imperative or subjunctive moods. Notable differences between the two languages include the presence of regular and irregular verb forms in English, as well as the use of the auxiliary verb "to be" to mark singular and plural distinctions, whereas Tontemboan does not exhibit verb form variations based on number.  

Keywords: Mood, English, Tontemboan Language, Contrastive Analysis

Currently, coffee shops have become increasingly prevalent throughout Indonesia, with numerous brands operating in the market. Among these, Starbucks remains a prominent competitor alongside both domestic and international coffee chains. Competitors such as St. Ali, an international coffee shop, as well as The Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, J.CO Donut & Coffee, Excelso, MOKKA Coffee Cabana, MAXX Coffee, Kopi Luwak, and Yellow Truck, offer beverages at more affordable price points, thereby attracting a significant portion of the Indonesian consumer base. This study aims to investigate whether there exists a significant difference between male and female customers regarding their repurchase intentions, as influenced by brand trust and brand commitment towards Starbucks in Manado. Employing a quantitative research approach, this study utilizes an independent sample t-test to analyze data collected from a sample of 100 Starbucks customers in Manado. The findings indicate no statistically significant difference between male and female customers in terms of repurchase intention based on brand trust and brand commitment. Based on these results, it is recommended that Starbucks in Manado consider implementing special promotional offers targeted separately at male and female customers on different days, as well as expanding their presence by opening additional branches to enhance customer accessibility.

Keywords: brand trust, brand commitment, independent sample t-test

The consumption expenditure patterns of household farmers who are beneficiaries of capital assistance for cattle production in the Western Tompaso District of Minahasa Regency were examined in this study. Household farmers represent economic units involved in both production and consumption decision-making processes. The capital assistance provided for livestock production is utilized by these farmers not only for productive purposes but also to support household consumption with the aim of maximizing household utility or satisfaction. This research seeks to analyze the consumption expenditure behavior of farmer households receiving production capital assistance for livestock.

A descriptive and quantitative approach was employed in this investigation. Participants consisted of household farmers who had received capital assistance and subsequently sold cattle. The consumption expenditure patterns of these beneficiary households were categorized into food and non-food consumption. Furthermore, food consumption expenditure was subdivided into purchased and non-purchased food items.

Findings indicate that within the three categories of consumption expenditure, the largest portion of purchased food expenditure was allocated to fish products, accounting for 28.69 percent. In contrast, the highest non-purchased food expenditure pertained to food seasonings, representing 29.94 percent. Lastly, among non-food consumption expenditures, the greatest allocation was observed in clothing, footwear, and headgear, which comprised 27.83 percent.

Keywords: consumption expenditure, household farmers, capital assistance, livestock production

Abstract:  
Human resources constitute a critical determinant of organizational effectiveness. This study aimed to assess the extent to which the competence of apparatus personnel influences the effectiveness of administrative offices within the Health Office of North Minahasa Regency. Employing quantitative research methods, the study involved 40 respondents, comprising all employees and officials at the Health Office of North Minahasa Regency. Data were collected through questionnaires supplemented by structured interviews guided by a predefined interview protocol. Hypothesis testing was conducted via simple linear regression analysis and Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient. The findings indicate that (1) the regression coefficient for personnel competence on administrative office effectiveness is positive and statistically significant, and (2) the correlation coefficient and coefficient of determination demonstrate a significant relationship between personnel competence and office administration effectiveness. Consequently, this study concludes that personnel competence is positively and significantly associated with the effectiveness of administrative offices. Based on these results, it is recommended that the development of personnel competence be prioritized as a strategic measure to enhance administrative office effectiveness.  

Keywords: Competence, Human Resources, Administrative Effectiveness, Office Administration

Determination of Nitrogen Retention and Metabolizable Energy of Banana Peel (Musa paradisiaca) Fermented with Rhizopus oligosporus in Broiler Diets

Banana peels, a commonly generated agricultural byproduct, represent a promising feed resource due to their abundance and nutrient profile suitable for livestock. This study aimed to evaluate protein intake, nitrogen retention (RN), and nitrogen-corrected metabolizable energy (AMEn) in broiler diets incorporating either unfermented or Rhizopus oligosporus-fermented plantain peel flour. The experiment utilized twenty Arbor Acres CP 707 broilers, aged five weeks, assigned to two treatment groups (n=10 per group) in a Student’s t-test design. One group received diets containing unfermented plantain peel flour, while the other was fed diets supplemented with plantain peel flour fermented with Rhizopus oligosporus. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences (P < 0.05) between the treatments for protein intake, nitrogen retention, and metabolizable energy. Specifically, protein intake improved from 63.59% in the unfermented group to 71.87% in the fermented group. Correspondingly, nitrogen retention and metabolizable energy values increased from 2336.6 kcal/kg to 2732.4 kcal/kg in broilers receiving fermented peel-based diets. These findings indicate that incorporating Rhizopus oligosporus-fermented plantain peel into broiler rations enhances protein utilization, nitrogen retention, and metabolizable energy, thereby suggesting its potential as an effective feed ingredient.

Keywords: plantain peel, fermentation, Rhizopus oligosporus, broiler chickens

This study aims to (1). Knowing the content and quality of Rahayu's tofu and tempe factory liquidwaste in Uner Village, Kawangkoan Sub-district, Minahasa Regency, and (2). The significance of economic sectors within a region is intrinsically linked to the functions and policies of the governing body responsible for managing the local economy. Government initiatives aimed at regional economic development fundamentally seek to achieve the overall welfare of the community, aligning with the collective aspirations and desires of its members. This research aimed to analyze the contribution of individual economic sectors to the economy of South Minahasa Regency. The study was conducted from September to November 2019 and utilized secondary data comprising time series of the Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP) for South Minahasa Regency and North Sulawesi Province from 2014 to 2018. These data were sourced from official publications available on the websites of Statistics Indonesia for both South Minahasa Regency and North Sulawesi Province. The documentation method was employed for data collection and analysis. Findings revealed that the Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries sector holds a crucial role in the current and prospective economic landscape of South Minahasa Regency. Nevertheless, this sector's impact is closely intertwined with the contributions of other economic sectors, which collectively shape the region’s economy.

Keywords: economic sectors, role, South Minahasa, regional economy

Abstract

This study, entitled "Conjunction in the Album Survival by Bob Marley and The Wailers," examines the use of conjunctions within the lyrical content of the 1979 album Survival. Conjunctions are linguistic elements that link words, phrases, and clauses, thereby clarifying the relationships among the connected components. The primary objectives of this research are to describe, identify, and analyze the various forms, functions, and semantic roles of conjunctions present in the songs. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the data identification and classification adhere to the frameworks established by Payne (2011) and Algeo (2006) regarding conjunction forms and functions. Furthermore, the semantic analysis of conjunction meanings is grounded in the theoretical perspectives of Hartford (2004) and ABA English (2014). Findings reveal the presence of coordinate conjunctions such as "and," "but," and "for"; complex coordinate conjunctions including "and then"; and subordinate conjunctions like "'cause," "before," "when," "as," "so," "than," "that," "who," "which," "what," "if," and "no matter." Coordinate conjunctions primarily function to connect words, phrases, clauses, and sentences, while subordinate conjunctions serve to link clauses specifically. The meanings conveyed by these conjunctions align with recognized categories such as addition, temporal relation, contrast, result, and purpose. Data were collected through a combination of library research and fieldwork focused on the lyrics of the album Survival. This study aims to provide a foundation for future research conducted by students of English linguistics and others interested in the grammatical aspect of conjunctions.

Keywords: Album Survival, Bob Marley and The Wailers, conjunctions, forms, functions, meanings

The Covid-19 pandemic represents a novel and severe global health crisis. Theoretically, the transmission of infectious diseases is frequently exacerbated by densely populated environments. This premise prompts an investigation into the applicability of density theory within Manado City, which serves as both the capital and primary gateway of North Sulawesi Province, characterized by its largest population in the region. Population density constitutes a critical metric for understanding the spatial configuration of urban areas. Consequently, the formulation of an optimal urban spatial structure is imperative for effective pandemic response and management. This study aims to examine the relationship between both static and dynamic density indicators and the spatial distribution of Covid-19 cases in Manado City. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates an origin-destination preference survey to identify population movement patterns—representing dynamic density—and utilizes Pearson correlation analysis as the principal statistical tool. Findings indicate that static density, measured as population density on built-up land, does not exhibit a significant correlation with the spatial distribution of Covid-19 infections in Manado City. In contrast, the city’s spatial structure, which tends toward a mono-polycentric configuration as inferred from dynamic density indicators, demonstrates a significant correlation with the distribution of cases. Specifically, trips associated with work, recreation, and healthcare access show statistically significant positive correlations with increases in Covid-19 cases during the initial wave of the pandemic. Based on these insights, this study recommends adopting a polycentric urban spatial model as an effective strategy to mitigate pandemic-related challenges.  

Keywords: Static Density, Dynamic Density, Covid-19, Pearson Correlation

ABSTRACT: Organizations consistently aim to maximize employee productivity to ensure the achievement of corporate goals aligned with established targets. However, numerous challenges arise due to the diverse thoughts, emotions, statuses, desires, and backgrounds that employees bring to the workplace. In this context, transformational leadership assumes a critical role by providing individualized consideration and intellectual stimulation, while possessing charisma and a nuanced understanding of both intrinsic and extrinsic motivational factors influencing employees. Such leadership is instrumental in enhancing work productivity. This study aims to examine the impact of transformational leadership and motivation on employee productivity, drawing upon Bass and Avolio's transformational leadership theory, Frederick Herzberg's motivation theory, and Sedarmayanti’s theory of work productivity. Employing a quantitative descriptive methodology, the research utilizes multiple linear regression and correlation analyses. The derived regression equation is expressed as Y = 2.237 + 0.246X₁ + 0.720X₂. These findings suggest that in the absence of transformational leadership and motivation, employee productivity attains a baseline score of 2.237. An incremental one-unit increase in transformational leadership corresponds to a 0.246 increase in employee productivity, while a similar increase in motivation corresponds to a 0.720 increase. The F-test yielded a value of 46.873, exceeding the critical value of 3.25 at a significance level of 0.000 (p < 0.05), leading to the rejection of the null hypothesis (Ho) and acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (Ha). These results confirm that both transformational leadership and motivation significantly affect employee productivity.

Keywords: Transformational Leadership, Motivation, Work Productivity

Keywords: Perceived Information Security, Consumer Trust, E-commerce

In the domain of traffic engineering, numerous methodologies exist for quantifying queues and delays, notably queuing theory and shockwave analysis. This study aims to compare these two approaches to identify the most suitable characteristics for examining queue dynamics and associated delays. The research utilizes primary data collected manually from the Megamas Area to perform analyses based on both shockwave theory and queuing theory.

The findings can be summarized as follows: (1) Shockwave analysis at the exit gateway counter, grounded in Greenshields’ fundamental diagram, reveals that queue length, the total duration from counter opening to the final vehicle joining the queue, and the overall time from counter opening to the restoration of normal conditions all exhibit a linear increase relative to the duration of incidence. Conversely, the delay experienced demonstrates an exponential growth pattern. (2) Analysis through queuing theory indicates that the existing counters generally maintain the capacity to serve incoming vehicles, as evidenced by an average utilization factor (ρ) less than one, though certain time intervals exhibit ρ values exceeding one, suggesting temporary overcapacity. The service level at all counters is strongly contingent upon factors such as the operating speed and accuracy of the counter personnel, availability of change funds, and the preparedness of drivers with respect to requisite payments including retribution fees and admission tickets. (3) From a practical standpoint, queuing theory offers a more straightforward framework for analyzing queue conditions at the counters compared to shockwave analysis. The latter is more appropriate for macroscopic evaluations involving traffic parameters like volume, speed, density, and roadway capacity, particularly when assessing the impact of obstructions on traffic flow via shockwave characterization. Given the spatial constraints on queuing length at the Megamas vehicle exit gateway—where excessive queue lengths extending to the intersection between segments A and B detrimentally affect speeds on both segments—queuing theory presents itself as a more effective and efficient analytical tool in this context.

Keywords: shockwave analysis, queuing theory, queue length

Abstract: Housing constitutes one of the fundamental human needs, alongside sustenance and clothing. Shelter serves not only as a residence but also as a daily gathering place for family members. The research population comprises individuals who have purchased or currently reside in this estate, with a sample size of 100 respondents. Employing a quantitative research design, primary data were collected through the distribution of structured questionnaires. To achieve regional capability and autonomy while reinforcing the structure of regional revenue, it is essential to continuously enhance the contribution of locally generated income within the state expenditure budget. This contribution serves as a critical indicator of regional capacity and reflects the degree of regional independence. Market retribution constitutes a significant source of regional revenue in addition to other financial resources, playing a strategic role in financing regional development. Accordingly, this study investigates strategies to increase market retribution in Youtefa Market as a key source of local revenue in Jayapura City, employing an interactive analysis model alongside SWOT analysis.

This research adopts a qualitative methodology, utilizing SWOT analytical techniques to evaluate internal and external factors. Internal analysis identifies strengths and weaknesses. Strengths include the authority granted by the City Government, human resource training initiatives, established procedures for retribution collection, provision of facilities for traders, and the clear mandate of the Youtefa Market organization. Conversely, weaknesses encompass low levels of formal education, limited financial capacity to meet budgetary requirements, insufficient competence in social empathy, lack of functional education, and deficiencies in supervision and law enforcement.

External factor analysis reveals opportunities and threats. Opportunities consist of a solid legal foundation for managing market retribution, robust economic growth, rising community income, and improvements in public education. Threats involve multiple stakeholders influencing retribution rate determinations, weak enforcement of regulations, inadequate infrastructure and facilities, and limited government responsiveness regarding market payments.

Based on the SWOT analysis, ten strategic recommendations have been formulated to enhance market retribution at Youtefa Market. 

Keywords: Strategy, Market Retribution, Regional Original Income.

The present study, titled "Deixis in the Film Enola Holmes by Harry Bradbeer," explores the phenomenon of deixis as a linguistic and pragmatic concept. Deixis is categorized into five distinct types: person deixis (encompassing first person, second person, and third person), place deixis, time deixis, discourse deixis, and social deixis. Derived from the Greek term *deiktikos*, meaning "pointing," deixis is a key subject within the field of pragmatics. This research aims to identify and classify the various types of deixis present in the film Enola Holmes, directed by Harry Bradbeer, as well as to analyze their respective functions within the narrative. Employing a descriptive methodology, the study systematically identifies, classifies, and analyzes deixis instances according to Levinson’s theoretical framework. The findings reveal the presence of all five deixis types: person deixis including first person pronouns (I, me, mine, our, we, us, my), second person pronouns (your, yours, you), and third person pronouns (he, him, they, them); place deixis such as here, there, this train, and this house; time deixis exemplified by terms like ago, tomorrow, next time, later, and now; discourse deixis including the use of this; and social deixis comprising terms like madam, master, sir, uncle, brother, and mother. Furthermore, the study elucidates the specific communicative functions fulfilled by each type of deixis within the film. It is anticipated that this research will contribute to the educational resources available to students and other readers interested in the pragmatic aspects of language, particularly in regard to deixis.

Keywords: Film, Pragmatics, Deixis

Transportation services play a crucial role in facilitating individuals' daily activities. The emergence of GO-JEK in Manado has become a significant phenomenon, particularly due to the widespread use of its online-based transportation service, notably the Go-Ride feature. This study aims to examine both the service quality and pricing of the Go-Ride feature within the GO-JEK application in Manado. Employing a descriptive research design with a quantitative approach, the Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) technique was utilized as the assessment instrument. The research involved a sample of 100 respondents who had prior experience using the Go-Ride feature in Manado. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using convenience sampling. Findings related to service quality indicate that the driving skills of Go-Ride drivers are highly valued by customers; PT. GO-JEK demonstrated strong performance in this aspect, situating this attribute in Quadrant 2 of the IPA matrix. Conversely, the service quality attribute concerning the completeness of Go-Ride drivers received the lowest average scores in both importance and performance. Regarding price, affordability emerged as the attribute with the highest levels of importance and performance. In contrast, attributes such as the price comparability of the Go-Ride feature with other facilities and its cheaper cost relative to other public transportation options were positioned in Quadrant 3, reflecting lower average scores.  
Keywords: Importance-Performance Analysis, service quality, pricing, Go-Ride, GO-JEK.

ABSTRACT: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is defined as brain damage resulting from an external physical force, which may lead to temporary or permanent impairments, functional disabilities, or psychosocial maladjustments.1 The incidence of TBI is approximately twice as high in males compared to females, with a reported ratio of 2.5:1; furthermore, mortality rates among males are three to four times greater than those observed in females.1,2 The frequency of TBI demonstrates a bimodal distribution, with peak incidence occurring in individuals aged 15 to 24 years and again in those aged 65 years and older. Motor vehicle accidents and violent incidents are more prevalent causes of TBI in younger populations, whereas falls predominate as a causative factor among the elderly.3,4 TBI severity is commonly classified into mild, moderate, and severe categories based on the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), whereby injuries with GCS scores of 13–15 are classified as mild, scores of 9–12 as moderate, and scores of 3–8 as severe.5,6 Hemiparesis, characterized by weakness or partial paralysis affecting one side of the body, typically arises from brain damage contralateral to the affected side, often secondary to cerebral vascular accident (CVA) or other brain injuries. Individuals with TBI may experience impairments in mobility and self-care attributable to isolated motor weakness or coordination deficits involving either the upper or lower extremities.7 Dysarthria, a collection of motor speech disorders resulting from central or peripheral nervous system injury, affects between 10% and 65% of patients with acquired brain injury, with prevalence influenced by the type, severity, and duration of the injury. This condition manifests as weakness, paralysis, or incoordination of the muscles responsible for speech, thereby compromising articulation, respiration, resonance, and phonation. Rehabilitation encompasses four functional domains: physical, cognitive, affective, and social. Consequently, rehabilitation services necessitate the involvement of multidisciplinary teams to guide treatment planning and to address these domains comprehensively.8 Herein, we present the rehabilitation process of a young male patient exhibiting left hemiparesis and dysarthria secondary to traumatic brain injury.

The present study aimed to investigate the impact of varying doses of garlic (Allium sativum) on the nonspecific immune response and growth performance of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Experimental subjects were Nile tilapia measuring 8 to 15 cm in length, with an average individual weight of 10.4 g. Prior to experimentation, the fish were acclimated for two weeks in fiber tanks. Subsequently, the fish were transferred into glass aquaria (50 cm × 30 cm × 30 cm) at a stocking density of 15 fish per aquarium, each equipped with an aeration system. Five dietary treatments were administered, consisting of garlic supplementation at levels of 0 g/kg (Treatment A), 10 g/kg (Treatment B), 20 g/kg (Treatment C), 30 g/kg (Treatment D), and 40 g/kg (Treatment E). The fish were fed the experimental diets twice daily, at 08:00 and 17:00, with feed amounts corresponding to 5% of body weight per day.

At the conclusion of the feeding trial, immune parameters—specifically total leukocyte count (TLC) and phagocytic activity—along with growth metrics, were assessed. Statistical analysis utilizing ANOVA was conducted to determine the effects of the treatments on immune response and growth, followed by Duncan's multiple range test to identify significant differences among groups. Results revealed that after four weeks, TLC in fish receiving garlic-supplemented diets was significantly higher (p < 0.01) compared to the control group. The highest TLC was recorded in Treatment C (15.413 × 10^7 cells mL^-1), followed by Treatments B (15.39 × 10^7 cells mL^-1), D (13.920 × 10^7 cells mL^-1), E (13.582 × 10^7 cells mL^-1), and A (12.195 × 10^7 cells mL^-1). Statistically significant differences in TLC were observed between Treatment C and the control, as well as among other treatment groups. Similarly, phagocytic activity was markedly elevated (p < 0.01) in Treatment C in comparison to the control, with the activity ranking from highest to lowest as C, B, D, E, and A. Growth performance was also significantly enhanced in Treatment C relative to the control and other treatments. 

In summary, dietary inclusion of garlic at 20 g/kg effectively improves the nonspecific immune response and growth of Nile tilapia. 

Keywords: Garlic, Immune response, Total leukocyte count, Phagocytic activity, Growth

In order to enhance the performance of Satpol PP, it is essential to establish institutional frameworks capable of fostering peaceful, orderly, and well-regulated regional environments. The organizational structure of Satpol PP must take into account not only population density but also the workload, responsibilities, and safety risks faced by civil service police officers. Consequently, the importance of the roles and functions of daily freelance workers within Satpol PP, particularly in the realms of security and law enforcement, is anticipated to intensify. This is evidenced by their work capabilities, motivation, and the disciplinary conduct exhibited—factors that are often observed by the community in the execution of their duties.

The present study aims to examine and analyze the impact of work ability, work motivation, and work discipline on the performance of daily freelance workers at the Satpol PP Office in Manado City. Utilizing a survey research design with quantitative sampling, primary data were collected via questionnaires administered to a sample of 82 daily freelance workers. Responses were measured using a Likert scale and analyzed through SPSS version 21.

Findings, significant at the 0.01 level, reveal that collectively, work ability, motivation, and discipline exert a positive influence on the performance of daily freelance workers, as demonstrated by the F-test results. Furthermore, t-test analysis indicates that work ability independently has a positive and significant effect on the performance of these freelancers.

Based on the data analysis, it is concluded that while work ability significantly enhances performance, work motivation and discipline exhibit positive but statistically insignificant effects. The combined explanatory power of work ability, motivation, and discipline on variations in daily freelance worker performance is limited. Accordingly, it is recommended that the Regional Office of Satpol PP in Manado place greater emphasis on improving these factors by fostering supportive work environments and encouraging collaboration among colleagues, with the aim of enhancing the overall performance of daily freelance workers.

Keywords: Work Ability, Work Motivation, Work Discipline

This study seeks to examine the professionalism of officials involved in the distribution of prosperous rice in the Eastern Malalayang Village. Conducted in May 2017, the research employed a qualitative methodology, which is appropriate for investigating phenomena in their natural contexts. The researchers served as the primary instruments for data collection, utilizing triangulation techniques to ensure data validity, while inductive methods guided the data analysis process. The qualitative findings emphasize the interpretation of emerging meanings rather than quantification. 

The study’s participants numbered twelve, comprising one urban village head, three neighborhood heads, seven distribution unit implementers, and seven residents. The results indicate that the professionalism of the officials, as assessed through dimensions of creativity, innovation, and responsiveness, was considered moderately satisfactory. However, when evaluated based on overall competency, the officials could not be classified as fully professional. Analysis further revealed deficiencies in administrative accuracy, with issues such as misaligned data collection targets arising largely from inadequate coordination and cooperation among urban village administrators. 

In light of these findings, several recommendations are proposed: (1) government authorities should adopt a more critical stance toward addressing public complaints related to beneficiary households within the village administration; (2) annual data collection activities should be conducted to reflect the dynamic nature of poverty, which may fluctuate over time; (3) the provision of complaint and suggestion boxes in each village should be prioritized to accommodate individuals who may feel reluctant or apprehensive about voicing concerns directly; and (4) enhanced socialization efforts are necessary to improve communication and understanding between the community and village officials regarding the distribution process of prosperous rice.

Keywords: Professionalism, Apparatus, Distribution, Prosperous Rice, Eastern Malalayang Village

The lathe machine is a machine tool designed to rotate a workpiece to facilitate cutting operations. The lathe cutting process involves a chisel, which moves parallel to the rotating axis of the workpiece. This machining operation generates heat as a byproduct. To mitigate this thermal effect, lathe machines are equipped with a direct-contact liquid cooling system that cools both the chisel and the workpiece. 

The present study investigates the influence of varying cooling liquid flow rates on the heat produced during the cutting process of a cylindrical workpiece. This research has two primary objectives: firstly, to quantify the heat generated by the cutting operation; and secondly, to identify the optimal cooling liquid flow rate for effectively cooling the chisel and workpiece. 

Experimental procedures involved three different flow rate settings, controlled by adjusting the opening angles of a ball valve regulating the cooling liquid: 30°, 60°, and 90°. The results indicate that the application of the cooling liquid significantly reduces the temperature generated by the cutting process. Notably, the valve opening at 90° demonstrated the most effective cooling performance, whereas reductions in temperature at valve openings of 30° and 60° were comparatively less significant.

Keywords: effect of cooling liquid flow rates, heat generation, cutting process, cylindrical workpiece

Nowadays, education has a significant meaning. Education supports and has a function of enhancing human quality. The business owners have seen this as an opportunity to build private schools. Having built these schools, they need to know the right strategy to meet its customers' satisfactions. The purpose of this study was to determine the influence of marketing mix such as product, price, promotion, place, people, physical evidence, and process for student satisfaction. The place of research is in Tomohon Caritas Catholic High School. The population is 284 students and the sample taken is as many as 100 samples. The analytical method used is the Multiple Regression, while validity and reliability tests are also used. This research can be categorized into quantitative descriptive research. The result shows that as for the t-test, the variables product, price, place people and physical evidence, individually as well as partially is significant influence toward students' satisfactions of Charity Catholic high school students in Tomohon. On the other hand, the variables promotion and the process, individually as well as partially, is not significantly influence toward students' satisfactions of Charity Catholic high school students in Tomohon. The management of Charity Catholic high school needs to improve and focus its marketing strategies on marketing mix strategy with respect to the education quality of the school, in detail such as teachers' attentions and learning process. Keywords: services marketing mix, student satisfaction

This study seeks to evaluate the quality of public health services provided to the elderly at the Duono Health Center in Ibu Tabaru District, West Halmahera Regency. Employing a qualitative descriptive research design, the investigation utilized both primary and secondary data to inform the analysis. The assessment was based on several indicators, including service timeliness, courtesy and friendliness during service delivery, ease of access to services, and overall consumer comfort. Findings reveal that the quality of services at the Duono Health Center remains suboptimal. This situation is evidenced by insufficient facilities and infrastructure that do not correspond to the volume of patient visits, as well as inadequately maintained amenities that fail to ensure comfort for the elderly clientele. Additionally, certain service personnel do not adhere to scheduled service hours. The center faces a shortage and imbalance of medical staff, including doctors, midwives, and nurses. Furthermore, some healthcare providers demonstrate a lack of punctuality, insufficient friendliness, and an inability to create a comfortable service environment. To enhance the effectiveness of elderly public health services at the Duono Health Center, targeted improvements are necessary.  
 
Keywords: Quality, Health Services, Elderly Population

Abstract: Intussusception refers to the telescoping of one segment of the bowel into an adjacent segment. While this condition can manifest at any age, it predominantly affects children between three months and two years old. In pediatric cases, intussusception is generally idiopathic, with presumed etiologies including uncoordinated intestinal peristalsis and lymphoid hyperplasia, potentially triggered by gastrointestinal infections. Clinically, affected individuals present with intermittent abdominal pain, vomiting, and characteristic red currant jelly stools. Diagnostic confirmation is achieved through imaging modalities such as contrast enema, ultrasonography, and computed tomography. Prior to surgical intervention, it is essential to stabilize the patient's condition. Overall, the prognosis of intussusception is favorable when diagnosis and treatment occur promptly. Surgical management is reserved for cases complicated by adverse outcomes or when reduction via enema proves unsuccessful.

Keywords: intussusception; bowel invagination

This study seeks to examine the dynamics of the Sarongsong Youth farmer group in Tumatangtang One Village, South Tomohon Sub-District. Employing a case study approach, data were collected from both primary and secondary sources over the period from February to April 2016. Primary data were gathered through structured interviews utilizing a predetermined questionnaire, while secondary data were obtained from the Neighborhood Office, District Office, and the local Office of Agricultural Extension, Fisheries, and Forestry (BP3K). The entire membership of the Sarongsong Youth farmer group in Tumatangtang One Village served as the respondent population for this investigation. The research variables encompassed eight factors related to farmer group dynamics: the group’s objectives, organizational structure, functional roles, coaching functions, cohesiveness, group atmosphere, external pressures on the group, and overall group effectiveness. Descriptive analysis was applied to the collected data, and findings were presented in tabular form as percentages. The results indicate that the Sarongsong Youth farmer group in Tumatangtang One Village generally exhibits positive dynamic characteristics. However, group pressure was identified as a comparatively weaker sub-factor within these dynamics. To enhance the group’s functionality, it is recommended that particular attention be given to strengthening this aspect. Additionally, implementing an award system to recognize members who significantly contribute to other farmer groups may serve as an effective motivational strategy.

Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has garnered considerable attention and has been extensively investigated; despite the progression to end-stage renal failure, patients often maintain a prolonged lifespan with a relatively good quality of life, although the prevalence of the condition continues to increase annually. A notable complication associated with CKD is uremia, a clinical and laboratory syndrome affecting multiple organs. In uremia, platelet function is impaired, prostacyclin production in blood vessels is elevated, and elevated blood urea levels act as potential vasodilators and antagonists of platelet aggregation. 

Methods: This study employed an analytical observational cross-sectional design. The sample comprised patients diagnosed with CKD at the Hospital Clinic of Nephrology-Hypertension Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou Manado from December to February 2014. Inclusion criteria encompassed patients under 80 years of age who had undergone diagnosis through physical examination and laboratory investigations conducted by medical professionals. Data collected included urea and creatinine levels, complete blood count, and platelet aggregation assays performed at Prokita Laboratory Manado. Statistical analyses involved the use of the Shapiro-Wilk test and Pearson’s correlation test.

Results: A total of 20 CKD patients were included in the study. Analysis revealed a significant correlation between urea-creatinine levels and platelet aggregation in response to trace ADP 5 µM (P = 0.004), whereas no significant correlation was observed with aggregation responses at trace ADP 10 µM (P = 0.399).

Conclusion: Among patients with chronic kidney disease, urea-creatinine levels were significantly associated with platelet aggregation at trace ADP 5 µM concentration, while no such association was detected at trace ADP 10 µM. 

Keywords: Chronic kidney disease, platelet aggregation.

Abstract: The rural government continues to organize the national tax system, which embodies a sense of justice and thorough awareness by imposing taxes on various taxable objects regardless of size, thereby encompassing all segments of society. Fundamentally, tax payments collected from the population are intended to promote the welfare of the people—that is, taxes are collected from the people for the benefit of the people. National development has resulted in rapid progress across multiple sectors of life, alongside increasing public infrastructure and facilities. This study aims to examine the leadership role of the village chief in enhancing public awareness regarding the payment of property taxes. Through the implementation of national income tax policies, economic growth can be regulated, and equitable income distribution can be achieved. The research employs a qualitative descriptive-explorative method. Primary data sources consist of 12 village government officials and 13 taxpayers, totaling 25 participants as informants. The study population comprises all community members residing within the Tolotoyon rural government’s jurisdiction. Efforts by government task forces, acting as tax administrators, include motivating, socializing, coaching, and counseling the public on the significance of taxation for state interests and community development, including both infrastructure and superstructure. Despite these initiatives, awareness and tax payment responsibilities among the Tolotoyon rural population remain insufficient. To encourage tax compliance, administrative procedures should be effectively managed, with intensified socialization, counseling, and guidance provided to taxpayers to facilitate timely payments.  

Keywords: Village head leadership, Rural taxation, Taxpayer awareness

The process of job placement involves determining whether an employee is assigned to a specific position within an organization. Employee performance plays a critical role in enabling businesses and individuals to achieve their objectives. This study seeks to examine the influence of job placement on the performance of employees at PT. FIFGROUP Cabang Manado. Employing a quantitative associative research design, data were collected through a survey method. The population comprised all employees of PT. FIFGROUP Cabang Manado, from which a sample of 85 respondents was selected using the Slovin formula. The analysis was conducted using simple linear regression and correlation techniques with SPSS version 23.0. The findings revealed a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.282, indicating a weak relationship between job placement and employee performance. Furthermore, the coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.079, suggesting that 7.9% of the variance in employee performance could be explained by job placement, while the remaining 92.1% was attributable to factors outside the scope of this research. One contributing factor to the limited effect of job placement on performance is the organizational policy at PT. FIFGROUP Cabang Manado, which does not mandate alignment between employees’ educational backgrounds and their assigned positions. To enhance employee performance, it is recommended that job placement practices better correspond to individuals’ educational qualifications. 

Keywords: Job Placement, Employee Performance

This study examines the responses of cattle farmers to the adoption of artificial insemination (AI) technology in Tondegesan Dua Village, Kawangkoan District, Minahasa Regency. The government has promoted advancements in science and technology within the cattle farming sector to enhance productivity and thereby increase the livestock population. The primary objectives of this research were to assess the farmers’ attitudes toward AI technology adoption and to evaluate their knowledge and motivation concerning AI in the specified village. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized, with data collection conducted through observations and structured interviews. The study population comprised 42 farmers, including those participating in AI activities and those not yet involved but familiar with the technology. From this population, a purposive sample of 30 farmers was selected for analysis. Measurement of research indicators employed a Likert scale, and statistical testing was conducted to explore the relationship between farmer responses and AI adoption. Findings reveal that farmers generally exhibited a moderately positive attitude toward AI technology. In conclusion, the responses of farmers toward artificial insemination were considered to be fairly favorable. 

Keywords: farmer motivation, artificial insemination technology, Tondegesan Dua Village

This study aimed to identify the optimal honey concentration for sperm dilution to enhance sperm motility, fertilization rates, and egg hatchability in goldfish (Cyprinus carpio). A Completely Randomized Design (CRD) was employed, consisting of four treatments with three replications each. The treatments were as follows: A (0 mL honey per 100 mL physiological NaCl), B (0.2 mL honey per 99.8 mL physiological NaCl), C (0.4 mL honey per 99.6 mL physiological NaCl), and D (0.6 mL honey per 99.4 mL physiological NaCl). Sperm dilution was carried out in twelve plastic cups, while fertilization and hatching procedures were conducted using twelve brass plates. Sperm motility was assessed immediately after dilution, fertilization rates were evaluated 12 hours post-fertilization, and egg hatchability was recorded after 72 hours. Results demonstrated that the addition of honey significantly improved sperm motility, fertilization success, and hatchability of goldfish eggs. Among the concentrations tested, 0.6 mL honey per 100 mL physiological NaCl produced the most favorable outcomes, yielding average sperm motility, fertilization, and hatchability rates of 80.00%, 84.00%, and 82.33%, respectively.

Keywords: honey, sperm motility, fertilization, egg hatchability, Cyprinus carpio L.

South Bolaang Mongondow is one of the regencies located in North Selawesi Province which is one of the regencies that is growing rapidly. Along with the increase in population, inadequate infrastructure, facilities and public utilities have resulted in many people in this district living in places that do not meet the standards, which are slums. Slum areas in South Bolaang Mongondow Regency according to the 2016 South Bolaang Mongondow Regency slum decree, there are 23 villages that are included in slum areas, these slums have three classifications, namely, heavy slums, medium slums and light slums. Based on this classification, it is combined with land status and other considerations so that a priority scale for handling slum settlements can be drawn up and how the pattern of handling slum settlements in Bolaang Mongondow Selatan Regency can be. The method used is a multi-criteria analysis method with 9 indicators, namely building conditions, environmental road conditions, environmental drainage conditions, drinking water supply conditions, wastewater management conditions, waste management conditions, fire protection conditions and land status and other considerations. Based on the results of the study, it was found that 16 villages would be treated with a rejuvenation pattern, 1 village would be resettled and 6 villages would be treated with a restoration pattern.Keyword : Slums, Slum Level, Priority Scale, slum settlement pattern

Abstract:  
Public Health Centers maintain a diverse inventory of medications to meet the treatment needs of their patients. The availability and management of these drugs constitute a critical component of the center’s operations. Consequently, the implementation of an efficient and effective drug data management system is essential to enhance institutional performance. To address this need, the authors developed a web-based drug inventory application designed specifically for Public Health Centers. This application facilitates comprehensive management of drug data, including the recording of drug inflow and outflow. Although the system currently supports a single user in the role of administrator, provisions have been made to accommodate additional personnel as required. Key functionalities of the application include the entry of incoming and outgoing drug data, the addition of new drug records, and the ability to view detailed information on existing pharmaceutical stock, encompassing supply and demand metrics. The application was developed using web technologies such as HTML, CSS, PHP, and BOOTSTRAP for templating, with MySQL serving as the database backend. The overall functionality was evaluated through black box and beta testing methodologies, ensuring the reliability of the implemented features. The successful deployment of this application is anticipated to streamline workflow processes, thereby increasing operational efficiency and effectiveness within the Public Health Center.  

Keywords: Application, Inventory, Public Health Center Stock, Web-based System.

Abstract:  
Butterflies, insects classified within the order Lepidoptera, are characterized by possessing two pairs of wings covered with scales and a scaly body. The richness of butterfly species may decline as a consequence of intensified deforestation and the conversion of forested land, which adversely impacts the availability and diversity of larval host plants as well as adult nectar sources. This study aimed to assess the diversity of butterfly species along with their larval and adult feeding plants within the protected forests of Mount Tampusu and Mount Mahawu. The research employed the transect count method to collect data. Findings revealed the presence of five butterfly families comprising a total of 37 species across both sites, with 26 species recorded in the Mount Tampusu protected forest and 23 species in the Mount Mahawu protected forest. Analysis via the Shannon-Wiener diversity index yielded a value of H' = 2.74, while the evenness index was calculated as E = 2.74 / ln(37) = 0.76. Larval host plants identified in the Mount Tampusu protected forest included species from the genus Ficus, whereas in Mount Mahawu, Glochidion and Alpinia species served as larval food sources. Adult butterflies in the Mount Tampusu protected forest were observed feeding on Crassocephalum crepidioides, Lantana camara, Lindernia crustacea, and Mikania cordata, while in Mount Mahawu, forage plants comprised Bidens pilosa, Crassocephalum crepidioides, Hyptis capitata, Impatiens species, Sida acuta, and Vernonia species.  
Keywords: Butterflies; host plants; feeding plants; Mount Tampusu; Mount Mahawu protected forests

Local revenue (Pendapatan Asli Daerah, PAD) serves as a crucial indicator reflecting the autonomy of local governments in managing their regional finances. To enhance local revenue, it is imperative for local authorities to prioritize the identification and utilization of income-generating sources within their jurisdictions, particularly those with potential for taxation and levies. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and contribution of the Hotel Tax to the Original Revenue in Manado City. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research analyzes the effectiveness levels and contribution of hotel tax realization data in Manado from 2013 to 2019. The findings indicate a general increase in the effectiveness of the Hotel Tax over the period from 2013 to 2017, with the highest effectiveness recorded in 2017 at 127.51%, categorized as very effective. Conversely, the contribution of the Hotel Tax to the overall local revenue during 2013 to 2017 remained relatively low. A decline in effectiveness was observed in 2019, dropping to 94.81%, and the lowest effectiveness was noted in 2015 at 6.28%, attributed primarily to insufficient taxpayer awareness regarding tax obligations. There was, however, an upward trend in contribution during 2018–2019, with percentages of 10.39% and 10.29%, respectively. These findings underscore the necessity for increased taxpayer education through socialization efforts or seminars. Additionally, imposing penalties on taxpayers who delay payments may be warranted to enhance compliance and optimize revenue collection.

The objective of this research is to assess the current carbon stock within the Bron Forest Research Station located in Warembungan Village, Minahasa Regency, and to evaluate its capacity for atmospheric carbon sequestration. The investigation was conducted over a three-month period at the Bron Forest Research Station. Data collection involved measurements taken from fifteen systematically arranged observation plots. The parameters recorded included diameter at breast height (DBH), bole height, and the biomass of litter and understory vegetation.

The findings indicate that the total biomass of Bron Forest Research Station amounts to 49,821.84 tonnes, equivalent to 996.44 tonnes per hectare. This biomass corresponds to a carbon stock of 23,416.27 tonnes, or 468.33 tonnes per hectare. Up to the time of measurement, the station has sequestered approximately 85,859.65 tonnes of carbon dioxide, translating to 1,717.19 tonnes per hectare. Provided that the forest remains largely undisturbed, it is projected that the biomass will increase by 4.66 tonnes per hectare annually, equating to 232.90 tonnes per year across the entire 50-hectare area. This growth in biomass is associated with an annual increment in carbon stock of 1.72 tonnes per hectare, or 86.17 tonnes for the whole site. Consequently, the potential for additional atmospheric carbon dioxide sequestration is estimated at 6.32 tonnes per hectare per year, amounting to 315.97 tonnes annually for the entire forest area.

Keywords: biomass, carbon sequestration, carbon dioxide sequestration

Architect or urban designer's major task is to create the best possible outdoor environment to the people's activities. Environmental-friendly technology appreciation in the context of urban architecture may be interpreted as the application of materials covering buildings envelop and ground surface. Soft and hard materials covering park space, roofing and envelop wall, play important role determining convective and radiant temperature of its environment. Outdoor thermal comfort that influenced by ambiance temperature, is therefore depends on utilization of surface material.This paper contains the intention of thermal performance of outdoor environment in a tropical and humid environment with a case of the city of Manado, Indonesia. One hour steps of temperature measurement at the surface of hard materials for ground covering (asphalt and concrete block) without solar shading in a hot season were done. Air temperature of outdoor space was also recorded. This is to know the effect of using different types of materials on outdoor environment. Some of calculations were also realized in order to make comparison with the results from measurement and to know the quantity of outdoor comfort level of the environment. This study recommend of principles of thermal properties of materials for ground covering of a tropical environment.
