This study aims to evaluate the performance of the Village Head of Tolok in the implementation of village development initiatives. The research was conducted from April to June 2017, employing a qualitative methodology that provides a descriptive account of factual data obtained from the field, closely aligned with the research focus. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized, involving ten informants who possess relevant insights into the contextual conditions of the study area. These informants comprised the Village Head (1 person), Village Secretary (1 person), three security officers, and five community members. 

Findings indicate that the Village Head’s performance in executing development activities can be assessed through various dimensions, including work quantity, quality, job knowledge, creativity, collaboration, initiative, reliability, and personal characteristics. Overall, the performance was found to be satisfactory, as evidenced by several successful development programs.

Based on the results, the study proposes the following recommendations to address identified challenges: (1) To ensure the effective realization of all village development plans and programs, particularly in tiered village structures, it is essential that the Village Head not only finalizes and implements development programs but also actively engages in direct socialization with the community. This engagement aims to promote active community participation in development processes, thereby raising awareness of the significance of such involvement. (2) To enhance community awareness and participation in village development activities, it is advisable for the Village Head and village officials to investigate and comprehend the community’s urgent needs during the planning and implementation phases of development programs.

Keywords: Village Head Performance, Village Development, Community Participation

Abstract: Manado city is experiencing a rapid economic development, it can be seen from the minimum wage which is the third largest in Indonesia and the largest in Sulawesi Island. This condition attracts some new retailers to do market expansion in Manado City, two of the latest entrance are Giant Ekstra and Transmart Carrefour. Their brand awareness is not as good as other retailers, meaning people in Manado are still evaluating whether these stores suit their shopping preference or not. Previous research found that store image has a positive effect on store loyalty through store satisfaction which may lead to more spending of money in the stores. The result of this research may later be used as a strategy for both stores. A casual type of research is adapted which uses primary data obtained through questionnaires and uses Ordinal Regression Analysis. The population is the people in Manado who already have shopping experience in both stores with 200 respondents as the sample size. The results turns out that Store Image does not significantly affects Consumer Spending. For recommendations, the retailers in Manado better give more effort in upgrading their pricing system and product quality control rather than upgrading their store image.Keywords: Store Image, Consumer Spending, Consumer Behavior, Retail

Indonesia is characterized by a diverse array of cultures and peoples distributed throughout its regions. Each region possesses unique characteristics that distinguish it from other areas, necessitating that local utilities and cultural expressions reflect these specific traits. The extensive cultural diversity in Indonesia has fostered the development of varied cultural forms across different regions, as culture fundamentally serves as both a beneficial resource and a distinctive identity that differentiates one territorial culture from another. Among the enduring cultural elements is the traditional house, which holds significant importance as a vernacular dwelling that supports family life.

This study employs a qualitative descriptive methodology aimed at thoroughly depicting the attributes of individuals, conditions, phenomena, or the frequency and interrelations of symptoms within society. The research posits that traditional houses embody a creative cultural expression characterized by unique features, exemplified by the Minahasa traditional house. This house type represents the legacy of ancient ancestors, reflecting the creativity of the Minahasa community. Notably, the customary houses in Woloan Village, Tomohon Barat District, Tomohon City, have evolved into a source of income generation, particularly benefiting local potters. These houses are frequently ordered beyond the local region, with consumer demands influencing size but without altering the fundamental traditional Minahasa architectural standards. The widespread appreciation for these houses, especially from those outside the Minahasa region, underscores the significance of this cultural heritage and its role in showcasing the craftsmanship of the local people.

Keywords: traditional house, cultural significance, Minahasa, vernacular architecture

This study examines the internal control system pertaining to fixed assets, designed to support management in overseeing and monitoring costs incurred from the acquisition of fixed assets through to the disposal of property, plant, and equipment. The system also facilitates the addition or extension of the useful life of fixed assets, thereby enhancing the operational effectiveness and productive capacity of the company’s fixed assets. Furthermore, it aims to safeguard assets and ensure the accuracy and reliability of fixed asset data within the company. The objective of this research is to evaluate the implementation of the internal control structure of fixed assets at PT Lumbung Berkat Indonesia, a construction company. A descriptive analytical approach was employed, utilizing qualitative data drawn from secondary sources. The findings indicate that the internal control system at PT Lumbung Berkat Indonesia remains ineffective. This ineffectiveness is evidenced by inadequate segregation of duties between the finance and accounting departments, the lack of an audit committee, and the absence of routine testing and measurement of fixed assets. Although decisions related to fixed assets require authorization from the President Director, the company does not perform physical inspections or reconcile asset records with actual fixed assets. Additionally, the company does not track capital expenditures and revenue associated with fixed assets. The straight-line depreciation method is consistently applied annually; however, the company’s fixed asset register is outdated, as it only includes assets such as buildings and vehicles related to projects while excluding office vehicles and inventory.  

Keywords: Internal Control, Fixed Assets.

THE INFLUENCE CHICKEN MANURE BOKASHI ON VEGETATIVE GROWTH OF BROWN MIDRIB SORGHUM (BMR) UNDER SHADE. The aim of this experiment was to study the effects of application of chicken manure bokashi on the vegetative growth of Brown Midrib (BMR) sorghum. Completely Randomized Design (CRD) has been used according to Steel and Torrie (1995). The treatments were level of chicken manure bokashi as follows B1= 0 gram; B2= 200 gram; B3= 400 gram and B4= 800 gram/polybag, with 7 replications to form 28 numbers of observations. The variables measured were plant height, leaf number and length of leaf. Analysis of Variance showed that treatments effected significanly different (P<0.05) on plant height, leaf number and length of leaf. Result of Tuckey Simultenaus Test showed that between treatment B3 and B4 were not significant different (P>0.05) on all variable measured, but both treatments gave a good performance of all variable measured significantly (P<0,05) better than treatments B2 and B1. Based on this research result it can be concluded that utilization of chicken manure bokashi up to 400 gram/polybag could provide nutrients requirement to support vegetative growth of sorghum BMR in term of height of plant, leaf number and length of leaf. Keywords: Bokashi, chicken manure, growth, BMR sorghum, shaded.

The implementation of regional autonomy in managing own-source revenue is anticipated to serve as a financial buffer supporting regional development activities. Among the various types of local taxes, the Manado Government particularly focuses on the Restaurant and Entertainment Tax. This study aims to assess both the effectiveness and the contribution of revenues derived from these taxes as sources of local income for the city of Manado. Employing a descriptive quantitative approach, the analysis examines target figures alongside actual revenues from the Restaurant and Entertainment Taxes spanning the years 2010 to 2014, utilizing effectiveness and contribution ratios as evaluative metrics. Findings indicate that the effectiveness of the Restaurant Tax was classified as highly effective in 2010, 2012, 2013, and 2014, while in 2011, it was deemed effective. Similarly, the Entertainment Tax demonstrated a highly effective status in 2010, 2012, and 2013, with effectiveness categorized as effective in both 2011 and 2014. Despite these results, the contribution of Restaurant and Entertainment Taxes to the city’s revenue over the five-year period is considered suboptimal, falling within the criteria of very poor contributions. Consequently, it is recommended that the Manado city government enhance tax collection oversight and control pertaining to these taxes to augment their contribution to local revenue.  
 
Keywords: restaurant tax, entertainment tax, regional revenue, effectiveness

This study addresses the persistent challenges encountered in the supervision conducted by subdistrict heads (Camat) concerning the implementation of village budgets (APB-Desa). The primary aim is to examine the supervisory practices employed by the Camat in overseeing the execution of APB-Desa within the subdistricts of North Minahasa Regency, specifically Kauditan. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the study involved nine informants, including the head of research/secretary of the district, village chiefs, caretakers, and administrators from BPD and LPM. Data were gathered through structured interviews guided by predetermined questions, and the analysis was performed using the interactive model proposed by Miles and Huberman. Findings reveal that direct supervision by the village head regarding APB implementation remains suboptimal. This is evidenced by insufficient involvement in village government activities during APB preparation, inadequate evaluation of draft local regulations prior to submission to the Regent, limited direct monitoring of APB execution within villages, and insufficient on-site verification following reports of irregularities. Conversely, indirect supervision is more effectively conducted by village heads through periodic (quarterly) written reporting on APB progress and implementation, oral reporting during coordination meetings at the village and subdistrict levels, and evaluation of semesterly realization reports, which are subsequently submitted to the Regent.  
 
Keywords: Supervision, Camat, Village Budget (APB-Desa).

ABSTRACT This research is entitled "Lexical Relations and Meaning Properties in The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel Movie Script". The objectives of this research are to describe the types of lexical relations and meaning properties and to analyze which type of lexical relations and meaning properties that occur the most in the movie script. This research uses a descriptive method. There are three steps to finish this research, the first step is preparation. In this step, the writer watches the movie to find out the data. The second step is data collection. The writer collects the words that include in lexical relations and meaning properties and compares them with the movie script. The third step is data analysis. The writer describes and classifies the types of lexical relations according to Palmer's (1976:57-81) theory and meaning properties according to Leech's (1981:29) theory, then the writer uses formula to get the types that occur the most in the movie script. The results of this research show that there are 72 data include in lexical relations and 107 data include in meaning properties. All of the words according to Palmer's (1976:57-81) and Leech's (1981:29) theory are found in this movie. The lexical relations and meaning properties found in the movie script of The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel are 3 data or 5 % of hyponym, 11 data or 19 % of synonym, 23 data or 39 % of antonym, 20 data or 34 % of polysemy, 2 data or 3,3 % of homonym, 103 data or 96 % of meaningfulness, 0 data or 0% of anomaly, 0 data or 0 % of contradictory, 4 data or 3,5% of ambiguity, and 0 data or 0 % of redundancy. It also shows that the types that occur the most are antonym and meaningfulness. The findings of this research support the theory of Palmer and Leech. Keywords : Lexical Relations, Meaning Properties, Movie: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel; Palmer, Leech.

The performance of the Village Government apparatus can be understood as the outcome of their work or the extent to which they achieve the targets and objectives set by the Village Government institutions. Among these objectives is the attainment of transparent and accountable management of village finances, which can be facilitated through the implementation of the Village Financial System (Siskeudes). This study aimed to examine and empirically verify the influence of competence, motivation, and compensation on the performance of Village Government apparatus involved in Siskeudes-based village financial management within Remboken District, Minahasa Regency. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the study adopted an explanatory survey design with a cross-sectional approach. The population comprised all Village Government apparatus serving as Village Financial Management Authority Holders (PKPKD) and Village Financial Management Implementers (PPKD) across 11 villages in the Remboken District. Saturation sampling, or census method, was utilized to select the sample, consisting of 73 respondents representing the entire population. Data collection was conducted via a structured questionnaire. Hypothesis testing was performed using multiple linear regression analysis at a 5% significance level, encompassing the F-test, t-test, and determination coefficient assessments. The results revealed that competence, motivation, and compensation exerted significant effects—both individually and collectively—on the performance of Village Government apparatus engaged in Siskeudes-based financial management in Remboken District. The findings of this study may serve as a valuable benchmark for Village Government institutions to evaluate their apparatus’ performance. Furthermore, the results provide a basis for developing and implementing various programs and policies aimed at enhancing competence, motivation, and compensation, thereby fostering improvements in performance.

Stand-up comedy constitutes a form of entertainment that exemplifies both artistic expression and linguistic proficiency. As a solitary performer on stage, without the aid of props or supporting partners, a comedian is afforded the liberty to articulate any utterance with the intent of eliciting laughter from the audience. Consequently, the linguistic dimension emerges as a fundamental component of this art form, manifesting primarily through utterances. Grounded in the theoretical premise that language simultaneously expresses and embodies cultural identity, this study addresses the question: how do language and culture interrelate within the utterances of comedians? The present research seeks to examine both the content and the manner in which comedians convey their utterances during stand-up performances, with the objective of elucidating the intimate connection between language and culture. Data were obtained from video recordings of the champion comedians featured in the fourth season of Indonesian Stand-Up Comedy. Employing a qualitative methodological framework encompassing data collection, analysis, presentation, and interpretation, the findings indicate that the content of the comedians’ utterances reflects their distinct cultural identities, including elements of ethnicity and community, which are intertwined with social issues pertinent to their lives. Furthermore, the analysis reveals notable variations among the three comedians in their phonetic articulation, lexical choices, syntactic constructions, and utilization of comedic gimmicks. These differences in content underscore the influence of their respective cultural and social backgrounds. Overall, stand-up comedy serves as a lens through which the intricate relationship between language and culture is vividly demonstrated. 

Keywords: comedian, culture, language, linguistic identity, stand-up comedy

The present study focuses on the design and fabrication of a soybean planting implement, taking into account critical factors such as planting conditions, seed quantity per planting hole, inter-seed spacing, seed viability at the time of planting, and operational efficiency. The intended objective is to develop a planting device suitable for use by both farmers and academic researchers, thereby contributing to governmental initiatives aimed at enhancing national soybean production. The design and manufacturing processes were conducted within the Agriculture Technology Laboratory, while field testing and performance evaluation occurred at the Unsrat experimental village in Wailan, North Tomohon District. The study spanned from April 8 to May 20, 2019, during which the tool was constructed; subsequent planting trials were performed on May 22, 2019, employing the device towed by a hand tractor, followed by a three-week observation period of soybean growth. The soybean cultivar utilized was the Dega 1 variety, identified as the superior cultivar according to the 2017 research and development data. Results obtained post-planting and observation indicated a field efficiency of 81.57%, with 61.59% of seeds germinating and 38.41% failing to grow. The overall germination rate exhibited a strong correlation with the tool's operational performance; however, limitations were noted in the metering mechanism, where a gap between the hopper and metering component led to seed damage and reduced successful germination. 

Keywords: Soybean planting implement, seed spacing, Dega 1 variety, seed germination percentage, field efficiency, metering mechanism

The purpose of this study is to examine and analyze the effect of auditor competence and independence on audit quality as moderated by auditor ethics and professional commitment. The population of this study is the BPKP Auditor Representative of Papua Province with census sampling as the sampling method. Data collection was carried out by direct survey. Hypothesis testing was tested empirically using Moderated Regression Analysis. The results of the study have proven that the competence and independence of auditors has a positive and significant effect on audit quality at BPKP Representatives of Papua Province. It is evidenced by the regression coefficient, which shows that the increase follows competence or independence of auditors increases, as well as the increase of audit quality. The results of this study also show that the interaction or influence of auditor ethics does not moderate the effect of auditor competence on audit quality at BPKP Representatives of Papua Province. Moreover, the interaction of professional commitment does not moderate the effect of auditor independence on audit quality. It is believed that the factor caused the phenomena is that the auditors of BPKP Representative of Papua Province have good values or fundamental principles of ethics as well as professional commitment. The values that have been held so far are relatively relevant or have a lot in common with the auditors' ethics and professional commitment.

Research on the Vegetative Growth Response of Halut Local Rice to inundation has been carried out. This study aims to examine the morphological response of local rice plants in North Halmahera to flooding during the growth phase.This research was carried out using polybags in the greenhouse of the Agriculture Service of North Halmahera Regency using a completely randomized basic design experiment consisting of 2 factors, the first factor was variety and the second factor was the provision of inundation stress. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance (ANOVA). The characters observed in this study included plant height, number of leaves, root length, and speed of stem elongation.The results showed that the treatment factors had significant differences when experiencing 10 days of inundation stress which was found in the observation character of the number of leaves. Meanwhile, the treatment factor, the variety factor, and the interaction between the treatment factor and the variety showed a very significant difference when experiencing a 20-day inundation on the observation of the number of leaves. The character of plant height, root length, and speed of stem elongation showed no significant effect on treatment factors, varietal factors, and interactions between treatment factors and varieties.The morphological response of Halut rice varieties to flooding was that only the number of leaves was significantly influenced by flooding factors compared to other parameters (plant height, root length, and stem elongation speed). Based on the agronomic character of the number of leaves, the singing variety is more resistant/tolerant to flooding.Keywords: Inundation, Morphological Response, North Halmahera Local Rice

Permendagri No. 113 defines the Village Budget as encompassing all rights and obligations that can be quantified in terms of monetary value and goods, which are associated with the execution of the village’s rights and duties. Budget control comprises a comprehensive set of activities, including the planning, implementation, administration, reporting, and accountability related to the village budget. The Alokasi Dana Desa (Village Fund Allocation), commonly referred to as "ADD," represents the balancing fund derived from the regional government budget (APBD) after deducting the special allocation fund. Effective budgeting necessitates oversight by the community, ensuring that it remains transparent, accountable, and comprehensible to all segments of the village population.

This study aims to: (1) examine the role of the community in the process of controlling the Village Budget (ADD) in Desa Kuma Selatan, Kecamatan Essang Selatan; and (2) provide an account of the utilization of the Village Budget in relation to village development. A qualitative research methodology was employed, with data analysis conducted following the approach outlined by Miles and Huberman (2001). The findings indicate that the community’s involvement in the village budget control process falls significantly short of expectations. This insufficiency is primarily attributed to the community’s limited understanding of the control mechanisms. The controlling process is designed to prevent financial leakage, inappropriate implementation, and the misuse of authority.

In practice, village budget control aligns with the principle of supervision and is thereby divided into two categories: internal and external control. Internal control is exercised through project implementation by the Public Works Department (Dinas PU), which acts as the decision-making authority for developmental activities. Additionally, internal control involves the Village head, who possesses both the authority and responsibility to oversee the implementation of the ADD within the village. Conversely, external control is entrusted to the community, which plays a critical role in the oversight process.

Keywords: community role, budget control, supervision, Alokasi Dana Desa (ADD).

Background: Young adult is a population of productive age who has a very important role. During the Covid-19 pandemic, the government imposed restrictions on community activities that caused stress on young adults. The purpose of this study was to description the stress and body image in young adults in Bahu Village, Malalayang District, Manado City, during the Covid19 pandemic. Methods: This study is a descriptive study, carried out in February - July 2021 in Bahu Village, Malalayang District, Manado City. The sampling method used simple random sampling by taking a sample of 78 respondents. This study uses a questionnaire instrument where the assessment indicator uses the Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10) to measure stress, while to measure body image using the Body Shape Questionnaire-16 (BSQ-16). The data analysis method used is univariate data analysis. Results: The results showed that the stress variable showed that the young adults in Bahu Village, Malalayang District, Manado City who experienced stress as many as 52 people (66.7%), while 26 people (33.3%) did not experience stress. The results of the study of the body image variables showed that 45 people (57.7%) had a negative body image and 33 people (2.3%) had a positive body image. Conclusion: That can be conclude that the most of the young adults in Bahu Village, Malalayang District, Manado City during the Covid-19 pandemic experienced stress and had a negative body image.Based on this, respondents need to control the stress conditions experienced and for respondentswith negative body image it is necessary to respect themselves more and be grateful for theappearance they already have.

Abstract. This research aims to test the influence of such independent variables as the organizational commitment, Accounting Internal Control, The Role Of Internal Audit, Education, and the quality of training to such dependent variables as the reliability of the financial report of local government. This research uses a quantitative approach, using primary data through questionnaires. The respondents in this study were the employees who processes the financial administration and those who make financial report at the Local Working Unit (SKPD) in North Halmahera Regency Government. The population used for this research is a group of financial staff which is about 298 people in each of the SKPD, and the samples taken are 75 respondents. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis and the data were tested by using SPSS program version 22. The results of a multiple linear regression analysis shows that partially, the organizational commitment, accounting internal control, the role of internal audit, education, and the quality of training give positive impacts and significant effects to the reliability of the financial report of local government. This study investigated the effects of incorporating palm sugar into drinking water on the growth performance, feed intake, and feed efficiency of growing pigs from the grower to finisher phases. Evaluating production parameters such as weight gain, feed consumption, and feed efficiency is essential for assessing pig production potential. Conducted over a ten-week period—comprising two weeks of preliminary data collection followed by an eight-week experimental phase—this research aimed to determine the influence of varying concentrations of palm sugar on the productivity of pigs during growth. The experiment involved sixteen mixed-gender pigs, aged 12 to 14 weeks, crossbred between Yorkshire and Landrace breeds. A randomized block design was employed, with four treatment levels of palm sugar supplementation in drinking water (0%, 2%, 4%, and 6%) assigned across four weight-based replication groups. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed a statistically significant effect (P < 0.05) of palm sugar on weight gain, which ranged from 0.57 to 0.65 kg. However, differences in feed consumption (2.56 to 2.64 kg) and feed efficiency (0.22 to 0.25) were not statistically significant (P > 0.05). Notably, water intake varied significantly (6.57 to 8.91 liters; P < 0.05) among treatment groups. These findings suggest that supplementing drinking water with palm sugar during the grower-to-finisher stages promotes favorable growth performance in pigs, despite unchanged feed consumption levels and feed efficiency metrics.  

**Keywords:** grower, finisher, palm sugar

This research investigates the hedonistic lifestyle among students of the Faculty of Economics and Business at Sam Ratulangi University, Manado, and its long-term detrimental effects. The study highlights that individuals who seek immediate and effortless results without embracing the necessary processes may contribute to a decline in mutual respect and moral integrity, issues often reflected in the unethical conduct and negligent leadership within society. Specifically, problems observed among some students include pronounced consumerist behaviors, diminished academic motivation, and engagement in behaviors such as premarital sexual activities, alcohol consumption, and participation in the LGBT community, which are perceived as influenced by improper guidance. Additionally, these factors contribute to extended durations for degree completion, frequently exceeding five years.

The primary objective of this study is to analyze the prevalence and characteristics of hedonistic lifestyles among students in the aforementioned faculty. Employing qualitative research methods, data were collected through observation and interviews with eleven student informants from the Faculty of Economics and Business at Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. Data analysis involved reduction, presentation, and verification processes to derive meaningful conclusions.

Findings reveal that female students’ hedonistic behaviors tend to evolve with the influence of new social circles encountered during their academic tenure. Notably, there is an increased emphasis on outward appearances, including hairstyles, clothing choices, accessories, and the acquisition of branded products, reflecting peer group norms. Furthermore, the study identifies a significant shift in local cultural values, religious adherence, and social customs attributable to the influence of popular culture, leading to more liberal social associations and a diminished academic seriousness among youth.

Keywords: Lifestyle, Hedonism, Students

This study, entitled "Derivational Affixes of English and Pamona Language: A Contrastive Analysis," fulfills the requirements for the Sarjana Sastra degree at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University. The primary objectives of this research are to identify and classify the types, functions, and meanings of derivational affixes in both English and the Pamona language, as well as to analyze their similarities and differences. Theoretical frameworks by Fromkin et al. (2014) and Katamba (1993) guided the analysis, while Lado's (1971) contrastive analysis theory was employed to compare the two languages. Employing a descriptive research method, data for English derivational affixes were derived from the speeches of Barack Obama and Donald Trump, whereas data for the Pamona language were collected from three native speakers residing in Tentena Village, Central Sulawesi.

The findings reveal that derivational affixes in English are comprised of prefixes and suffixes, while the Pamona language features prefixes, infixes, suffixes, and confixes. In both languages, the primary function of derivational affixes is either to alter or maintain the grammatical class of the root word. Both English and Pamona share prefixes that serve as distinct word-forming devices, producing new lexemes with meanings different from their base forms. Notable differences include the presence of infixation in Pamona, which is absent in English. Additionally, English derivational prefixes can convey negative meanings, a feature not observed in Pamona prefixes. Furthermore, English lacks derivational affixes that facilitate reduplication, a mechanism found in Pamona. Concerning adverb formation, English adverbs are exclusively derived from adjectives, whereas in Pamona, adverbs can originate from both noun and adjective bases.

Keywords: Derivational Affixes, English, Pamona Language, Contrastive Analysis

Title: The Impact of Feed Prices and Labor Wages on Profitability in Cattle Farming: A Case Study in Wineru Village, East Likupang Sub-District, North Minahasa Regency

Abstract:
The advancement of beef cattle farming plays a significant role in fostering economic development by enhancing farmers' income, supplying animal-based food products, providing raw materials for various industries, and generating employment opportunities, particularly in regions identified as centers of beef cattle production. However, challenges such as the availability of adequate feed and skilled labor persist among farmers. This study aims to analyze the profitability of beef cattle farming and assess the effects of feed prices and labor wages on farm profit margins. Employing a survey methodology, primary data were collected with samples selected through purposive sampling—specifically targeting farmers possessing a minimum of two cattle and who had not engaged in cattle sales. Descriptive statistical techniques and profit function analysis, utilizing output unit pricing, were applied to examine the data. Findings reveal that the total number of cattle owned was 83 heads, of which 43 had been sold. The primary feedstock comprised corn waste and field grass, with an average consumption of 12.125 kg per head per day. Labor allocation analysis indicated that the majority of working hours were dedicated to cattle movement, constituting 48% for owned cattle and 35.84% for sold cattle. The average profit derived from beef cattle farming was positive, amounting to Rp 2,692,830. Furthermore, both feed prices and labor wages were found to have a statistically significant impact on farm profitability. 

Keywords: cattle farming, feed prices, labor wages, profitability

Employee intention to leave constitutes a significant challenge faced by organizations across various sectors. A high level of intention to leave within an organization can adversely impact its reputation and overall performance, as it is closely linked to turnover rates. The banking sector, exemplified by institutions such as PT. BRI Unit Sam Ratulangi Manado, is particularly susceptible to this issue due to the demanding nature of its work system, which requires extensive working hours, strict discipline, and professionalism from employees. Numerous factors may influence an employee's decision to leave an organization, making it essential to identify these determinants in order to develop effective strategies for mitigating this concern. 

This study aims to examine the factors influencing employees’ intention to leave at PT. BRI Unit Sam Ratulangi Manado. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews conducted with ten informants from the office. The findings reveal four primary factors significantly affecting employees’ intention to leave: family reasons, job-related stress, salary, and opportunities for career advancement. Based on these results, it is recommended that the management of Bank Rakyat Indonesia prioritize enhancing employee satisfaction across multiple dimensions to decrease and proactively address the intention to leave among their workforce.

Keywords: job satisfaction, intention to leave

EFFECT OF SUBSTITUTION OF FISH MEAL WITH MAGGOT (Hermetia Illucens) MEAL ON CALCIUM (Ca) AND PHOSPHORUS (P) DIGESTIBILITY OF BROILER CHICKEN. As an animal feed, maggot from black soldier fly (Hermetia Illucens) has high calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) content. Yet, little is known about the digestibility of calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) in the diet containing maggot. The present study was designed to determine the effect of substitution of fish meal with maggot (Hermetia illucens) meal in the diets on (Ca) and phosphorus (P) digestibility of broiler chicken. Twenty day old chicks (DOC) CP 707 broiler chicken of about 1300-1500 g body weight were assigned to each dietary treatment which was replicated four times in a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) arrangment. The experimental diet consisted of 5 treatments and 4 replications, formulated as follow: R0 = 100% fish meal + 0% maggot meal; R1 = 75% fish meal + 25% maggot meal; R2 = 50% fish meal + 50% maggot meal; R3 = 25% fish meal + 75% maggot meal; and R4 = 0% fish meal + 100% maggot meal. Calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) digestibility were calculated using total collection method. Parameters measured were calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) digestibility. Differences were considered significant at P < 0.05. Tukey test (HSD) was employed to further analyze among treatment diferences. The results showed that calcium (Ca) digestibility was significantly (P < 0,05) increased as the level of maggot (Hermetia Illucens) meal in the diets increased; whereas the digestibility of phosphorus (P) was not significantly (P > 0,05) affected by the treatments. It can be concluded utilization of maggot (Hermetia illucens) meal up to 100% replaced fish meal or 15% in the diet, inreased calcium (Ca) digestibility and did not affect phosphorus (P) digestibility of broiler chicken. Key words: Fish meal, Maggot (Hermetia Illucens) meal, Calcium and Phosphours digestibility

Keywords: cash, certificate, uncollectible accounts, assets, profitability.

Land constitutes a critical element in human life, thereby underscoring the significance of legal certainty and protection for landowners. Systematic Land Registration (PTSL) serves as an effective mechanism to expedite land registration processes, ultimately enhancing legal certainty, safeguarding ownership rights, and promoting societal welfare. In 2019, Tambelang village was identified as one of the locations implementing PTSL, yet it exhibited low performance in cluster 1, which pertains to the issuance of land certificates. This study aims to analyze the factors contributing to the low achievement in cluster 1 and to formulate strategies to elevate cluster 1 outcomes by improving conditions in clusters 2 and 3, as well as by updating cluster 4 data. Employing a mixed-method approach, the research integrates qualitative analysis to investigate the underlying causes of the deficient cluster 1 performance, alongside quantitative methods utilizing SWOT analysis to propose strategic enhancements for certificate production and data updating. Data collection involved both primary and secondary sources, with purposive sampling guiding in-depth interviews and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs). The findings indicate that suboptimal socialization efforts, insufficient juridical staffing, a registration fee of Rp. 350,000, limited community awareness regarding the benefits of certification, and land parcel disputes collectively contribute to the underperformance in cluster 1. Based on these insights, recommended strategies include: (1) for improving cluster 1 outcomes from cluster 2, facilitating amicable resolution of boundary and ownership issues by leveraging village government support and providing venues such as the General Meeting Hall; (2) for transitioning cluster 3 to cluster 1, implementing cross-subsidies to alleviate administrative costs, fostering collaboration between Regional Government and the National Land Agency (BPN) to fund certificate administration, and harnessing technological advancements to engage individuals located outside the immediate area; and (3) for updating cluster 4 data, enhancing the roles of physical officers and village officials in educating the public on the significance of land plotting, alongside augmenting archival capacity by increasing staffing.  
 
**Keywords:** Strategy, Land, Land Registration, Legal Certainty

The central government holds the authority and responsibility to administer governmental systems and provide social services to society. To effectively discharge these responsibilities, it requires a system that facilitates the execution of its functions. The Accounting Institution System represents one such governmental mechanism, designed to regulate the flow of goods, services, and funds essential for the fulfillment of governmental duties. This study aims to evaluate the conformity of the management system procedures and regulations of the Supreme Audit Institution (SAI), examine the reconciliation process, and assess the utilization of information systems associated with the Accounting Institution System within BKKBN SULUT. Employing a descriptive comparative analytical approach, the study seeks to fundamentally identify causal factors by analyzing the elements contributing to the occurrence or manifestation of specific phenomena. The findings indicate that the organizational structure delineates the division of responsibilities and authority, particularly concerning the SAI components comprising the SAK and SIMAK-BMN. However, the implementation of the SAI within BKKBN SULUT has not been fully aligned with prevailing regulations. While both internal and external reconciliation processes have generally been conducted following established procedures, occasional technical errors have been encountered. In contrast, the information systems related to the SAI have been implemented adequately and maintain a well-organized structure.

The present study examines the effectiveness of digital newspaper communication, specifically tribuanmanado.co.id, among students from the Department of Social and Political Sciences at the University of Sam Ratulangi. The evolution of information technology from traditional print to digital formats—commonly referred to as online media—has intensified competition within the newspaper industry, compelling publishers to adopt strategies that sustain reader engagement and facilitate convenient access to desired information. Tribun Manado, a prominent regional newspaper in North Sulawesi, has transitioned from conventional print to a digital platform (tribunmanado.co.id) to expedite and enhance the dissemination of news to the public. The local community in North Sulawesi is well-acquainted with Tribun Manado’s publications, which are characterized by balanced reporting and clear presentation. Given that a significant portion of the North Sulawesi population remains unfamiliar with digital newspapers or online media, this research endeavors to assess the effectiveness of tribunmanado.co.id in meeting the informational needs of its audience.

The focus on students is justified by their active engagement with online media, contrasted with their relatively infrequent usage of print newspapers as sources of information. The study specifically targets students from the Department of Communications within the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences at the University of Sam Ratulangi, based on the assumption that they possess adequate knowledge and awareness regarding digital newspapers. Through qualitative analysis of interview data, the findings indicate that digital newspaper tribunmanado.co.id serves as an effective information source for students who utilize the internet. Furthermore, the practical benefits and efficiency associated with internet services contribute significantly to students’ recognition of the ease of accessing digital news via tribunmanado.co.id.

His iconic character, the "consulting detective" Sherlock Holmes, continues to enjoy worldwide popularity to this day. Conan Doyle authored a total of sixty stories depicting Sherlock Holmes's adventures, primarily published during the Victorian era. This study, titled "Moral Values in Three Short Stories by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle," seeks to identify, categorize, and analyze the moral values conveyed through the characters’ dialogues and the narrator’s descriptions, as well as to examine the connection between these moral values and Victorian era ethics. The research data were gathered by concentrating on the dialogues and narrative elements within three selected short stories: *A Scandal in Bohemia*, *A Case of Identity*, and *The Five Orange Pips*. To analyze the moral values present in these stories, the study employs Wellek and Warren’s (1949) theory on the function of literature, which draws from Horace’s concept of *Dulce et Utile*, emphasizing the dual purpose of literature to educate and entertain readers. Furthermore, to assess the relevance of these moral values to the Victorian era, the research applies Wellek and Warren’s (1956) literary and sociological framework, which posits that literary works should authentically reflect the realities of life. The findings indicate that the three short stories encompass three key moral values: mutual assistance, concern for others, and respect. Regarding their relevance, the investigation reveals that the Victorian era upheld six core values, two of which correspond closely with the moral values identified in the stories. Specifically, mutual assistance and concern align with the Victorian sense of duty and responsibility toward the less fortunate, while the moral value of respect corresponds with the era’s emphasis on honoring others.

Keywords: Moral Values, Victorian Era, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle

The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of supplementing fish meal protected with tannin extracts derived from Acacia leucophloea, Acacia catechu, and Samanea saman on the performance of goats. The experiment was conducted using a Completely Randomized Design comprising four treatments with four replicates each. A total of sixteen male local goats were assigned to the following treatments: P0 (basal feed combined with corn-urea and non-protected fish meal containing tannin extract), P1 (basal feed with corn-urea and fish meal protected with tannin extract from Acacia leucophloea), P2 (basal feed with corn-urea and fish meal protected with tannin extract from Acacia catechu), and P3 (basal feed with corn-urea and fish meal protected with tannin extract from Samanea saman). The basal diet consisted of a mixture of native grass and Leucaena in a 60:40 ratio. The results demonstrated that all treatments significantly enhanced goat performance, with the supplementation of fish meal protected by tannin extract from Acacia leucophloea yielding the most favorable outcomes (dry matter intake of 719.88 g/animal/day; nitrogen retention of 10.46 g/animal/day; average daily gain of 52.94 g/animal/day; and feed efficiency of 0.070). Similarly, fish meal protected with tannin extract from Acacia catechu also showed substantial improvements (dry matter intake of 719.88 g/animal/day; nitrogen retention of 10.03 g/animal/day; average daily gain of 51.47 g/animal/day; and feed efficiency of 0.072). 

**Keywords:** supplementation, fish meal, protection, tannin extract, goat performance

This study aims to examine the application of participatory approaches in rural development within Tawaang Village, Tenga District, South Minahasa Regency. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research investigates the extent to which participatory methods are integrated across various phases of village development, including planning, program implementation, monitoring, and evaluation. The study’s informants comprise eight individuals: the head dea, the head of BPD, the head of LPM, community leaders, and villagers of Tawaang. Data collection was conducted through guided interviews, and data were analyzed utilizing the interactive model framework proposed by Miles and Huberman.

The findings indicate that: (1) the participatory approach during the planning phase is implemented satisfactorily through village musrembang activities; (2) participatory methods are more effectively employed during program implementation compared to other stages; (3) monitoring of program implementation embodies a moderately good participatory approach; and (4) the program evaluation phase also reflects a reasonably well-adopted participatory practice.

Based on these outcomes, the study proposes several recommendations: (1) inclusive representation of all community groups should be ensured during village musrembang meetings; (2) villagers, particularly community leaders and representatives from various groups, ought to be actively engaged in designing program implementation; (3) findings derived from community monitoring activities should be earnestly considered by the village government; and (4) evaluation meetings for village development programs should involve all stakeholders within the village community.

Keywords: Participatory Approach, Rural Development.

This study addresses the challenges faced by villages in overcoming obstacles to achieve shared developmental objectives. Such constraints manifest in varying levels of community participation and in the effectiveness of development planning, which ultimately impact the enhancement of the quality of human resources. Consequently, the research centers on examining community participation in development planning within Igo Village, situated in the North Loloda Sub-district of North Halmahera District. The primary research questions investigate the nature of community participation, the strategies employed to enhance it, and the outcomes attained in relation to development planning in Igo Village.

Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, this study draws on the specific context of Igo Village. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentary analysis. The analytical process involved systematically collecting, reducing, and presenting data, followed by drawing informed conclusions.

Findings indicate that the participatory approach to development planning in Igo Village is initiated by the government, which communicates the objectives of development projects, motivates the community, disseminates pertinent information, and evaluates the extent of public involvement. Despite these efforts, the level of community participation remains suboptimal, as evidenced by the final evaluation of development planning, which falls below the maximum achievement category. This deficiency is attributed to the community’s insufficient engagement in the planning process. The study underscores that improvements in community participation are closely linked to the government’s continuous role in encouraging and motivating residents to engage actively in the village’s development planning initiatives.

Keywords: Participation, Development Planning, Community Engagement

ABSTRACT This research has a title " Kalimat Imperatif dalam Bahasa Inggris dan Bahasa Saluan" and focuses on the types, functions, similarities, and differences of imperative sentences on English and Saluan language. The research questions are: what are the types and functions, and what are the similarities and differences of imperative sentences in English and Saluan language. The data in English were collected from some English grammar books and data in Saluan language were taken from ten informants who know well about Saluan language using the interview method. After collecting the data, the writer identified and classified the imperative sentences in English and Saluan language. Then the data were analysed using contrastive analysis method, which means that the writer contrasted the data between English and Saluan language to find out the similarities, and differences. There are two types of imperative sentences in English and Saluan language, namely positive and negative imperative sentences. In terms of function, the imperative sentences both in English and Saluan Language have function as command, wish, invitation, instruction and warning. Though the imperative sentences in English and Saluan language have similarities, these languages show differences in terms of the use of words which are related to the socio-cultural aspects. Keywords: Imperative sentence, English Saluan language, Contrastive analysis.

The golden snail (Pomacea canaliculata L.), commonly referred to as the mulberry snail, is recognized as a significant pest affecting rice cultivation in North Sulawesi, including the City of Tomohon. This pest predominantly targets young rice plants, with damage intensity ranging from 10% to 100%, contingent upon the population density present in each cultivated area. The snail inflicts harm by scraping and consuming plant tissues. To address the challenges faced by farmers, this study investigated the population of golden snails using bait and trap methods on lowland rice plants (Oryza sativa L.). The objective was to evaluate the impact of papaya leaf baits and water-filled trench traps on reducing golden snail populations. The research was conducted in Taratara 1 Village, West Tomohon District, Tomohon City, over a period of approximately four months from March to May 2020. Employing a quantitative descriptive approach, field experiments were performed using two separate lowland rice plots designated for bait and trap treatments. Observations were recorded at 21, 28, and 35 days after planting. Findings indicated that the mean population density was 24.8 individuals/m² in the papaya leaf bait treatment and 31.4 individuals/m² in the water trench trap treatment. Notably, the snail population declined in both treatments from 21 to 35 days post-planting. It was also observed that plant age influenced snail prevalence, with younger plants more susceptible due to the tender structure of their stems and leaves, facilitating easier feeding by the pest. Both bait and trap methods yielded positive outcomes; thus, further studies are recommended to explore the combined application of these techniques on a larger scale, potentially integrating them with other environmentally sustainable pest management strategies.

The calculation of the cost of goods manufactured plays a crucial role in setting the price of a product. This study aims to examine the differences between the company’s method of calculating production costs and the full costing method, as well as to compare the selling price determined by the company with that derived from the cost-plus pricing approach. Employing a descriptive quantitative research design and a comparative analytical approach, the study reveals that the company’s reported production costs are lower than those calculated using the full costing method. Specifically, the discrepancy in production costs between the company’s calculation and the full costing method amounts to Rp. 10,133. This variation arises because the company’s factory overhead cost calculations exclude certain expenses—such as maintenance and repair of production equipment and the depreciation of production assets. Furthermore, the selling price of the product, determined with a 40% markup by the company, differs by Rp. 2,083 when compared to the price established via the cost-plus pricing method. This difference is attributed to the company’s omission of non-production costs in pricing decisions and its failure to apply the full costing method when calculating production costs.

Banana chips represent a type of fried snack that is widely prepared due to the simplicity of their production process. They are commonly made by housewives, small-scale fried food cottage industries, and restaurant proprietors alike. The production of Goroho banana chips traditionally relies on a conventional frying method, which involves repeatedly using poured frying oil until a noticeable change in the oil’s color occurs. This study aimed to evaluate the safety of repeatedly reused frying oil in the preparation of banana chips while maintaining the product’s nutritive value, appealing taste and aroma, attractive color, and ensuring that the quality of the used frying oil remains satisfactory.

A Completely Randomized Design (CRD) was employed as the experimental framework, encompassing seven different frying intensities. The quality parameters assessed in the frying oil included Free Fatty Acids (FFA) and peroxide value, whereas the banana chip samples underwent organoleptic evaluation and proximate analysis, including measurements of moisture, ash, fat, crude fiber, protein, and carbohydrate contents. 

Results indicated that the lowest FFA concentration (0.16%) was observed in the control treatment, whereas the highest concentration (0.58%) was detected after the ninth frying cycle. Similarly, the maximum peroxide value (22.10 meq/kg) was recorded following the twelfth frying cycle. Proximate analysis of the banana chips revealed average compositions of 3.57% moisture, 1.49% ash, 39.44% fat, 0.74% crude fiber, 4.48% protein, and 52.02% carbohydrates. Organoleptic assessment demonstrated that panelists’ preference scores ranged from "like" (5) to "very like" (6) predominantly during the first frying intensity treatment.

Keywords: frying intensity, free fatty acids (FFA), peroxide value

Rante Lembang, V.W., W. Tilaar, and T.M. Frans (2015) investigated the ecological potential, dispersion patterns, and utilization practices of natural fiber plants within the Limited Production Forest (LPF) of Sinonsayang Mount, North Sulawesi Province. In this region, bast fiber plants are distributed across both primary and secondary forest areas, including the LPF, yet comprehensive data regarding their ecological status, spatial distribution, and usage remain insufficient. The present study aimed to address these gaps by characterizing the ecological potential, spatial dispersion, and patterns of utilization of natural fibers in the LPF of Sinonsayang Mount.

The research was conducted over a two-month period within an approximately 500-acre area historically employed by local communities for dryland farming and characterized by shrub overgrowth. A randomized inventory method was implemented, utilizing simple random sampling to establish plots for data collection. Field surveys identified five natural fiber species: bamboo, pandanus, cotton, agave, and rosella. Among these, bamboo exhibited the highest population density, ranging between 19 and 21 individuals per hectare, whereas rosella possessed the lowest density, estimated between 0.08 and 0.09 individuals per hectare. 

Quantitative analyses revealed that bamboo fibers had a frequency value of 0.73 and accounted for 95.66% of the population, in contrast to rosella, which demonstrated minimal presence with a frequency value of 0.02 and a relative abundance of 0.04%. The dispersion pattern of bamboo was determined to be random across the study area, while pandanus, cotton, agave, and rosella fibers exhibited clustered distributions. 

Regarding utilization, three of the five identified fiber types—bamboo, pandanus, and cotton—were actively employed by the local population. Bamboo fibers were predominantly utilized for both subsistence and commercial purposes within village and district markets. The community's exploitation of bamboo encompassed eleven distinct applications, including construction of house walls and garden shelters, fencing, staircases, livestock enclosures, poultry nesting sites, ethanol refining apparatus, furnace construction, cooking tools for fish and pies, rice winnowing devices, bamboo shoot harvesting, and structures known as lalandangan. In contrast, pandanus and cotton fibers were primarily used on a limited scale for personal consumption, serving as raw materials in the production of mats, pillows, and lamp fuses.

Keywords: natural fibers, ecological potential, dispersion patterns, utilization patterns, Limited Production Forest, Sinonsayang Mount, North Sulawesi

Obesity constitutes a significant public health challenge, rendering its prevention and treatment a priority within the healthcare sector. Interventions targeting obesity primarily focus on weight reduction. Among adults aged over 18 years, overweight and obesity represent a major nutritional concern. The prevalence of obesity is notably higher among women, reaching 26.9%. A 2013 study conducted at the Wawonasa Public Health Centre revealed that 41.6% of respondents were classified as obese based on nutritional status assessments.

This study aims to examine the efforts undertaken to reduce weight among productive-age women at the Wawonasa Public Health Centre, Singkil Manado. Employing a qualitative research design, the study was carried out from November 2013 to January 2014 at the aforementioned health center. Purposive sampling was utilized to select 10 informants, each of whom participated in in-depth interviews. Data were analyzed through content analysis, and the validity of findings was ensured using triangulation techniques involving both data sources and methods.

Findings indicate that productive-age women at the Wawonasa Public Health Centre are aware of the consequences of obesity and engage in various weight reduction strategies, including physical exercise, reducing food portion size and meal frequency, using dietary products, fasting, and smoking. However, participants reported facing several obstacles in their weight loss endeavors, such as adherence to inappropriate diet programs, difficulties in controlling appetite, and lack of spousal support.

Keywords: Obesity, Productive-age Women, Weight Reduction Efforts

This study aimed to identify the symptoms and quantify the infestation intensity of aphids (Chaetosiphon sp.) on strawberry plants cultivated in Rurukan Village, Tomohon. The research was carried out over a four-month period from February to May 2014. The methodology employed included surveys, direct observations of aphid populations, and purposive sampling of strawberry plants. Field data collection took place within strawberry cultivation areas, while laboratory analyses were conducted at the Entomology and Plant Pest Laboratory, Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University. Observations of infestation intensity were performed on subplots measuring 2 meters by 1 meter along beds extending up to 12 meters in length. Two subplots per bed were examined, with each subplot comprising 20 plants. The findings revealed that Chaetosiphon sp. aphids adversely affect strawberry plants during both the vegetative and generative growth phases. Specifically, infestation in the vegetative phase resulted in stunted plant growth, whereas attacks during the generative phase inhibited flower and fruit development. The average infestation intensity demonstrated a progressive increase on a weekly basis, reaching its peak in the sixth week, with 46.0% of plants affected during the initial observation and 55.0% during the subsequent assessment.

Keywords: Symptoms, infestation intensity, Chaetosiphon sp., strawberry aphids

AbstractThe research is entitled "Obedience in the Film The Book of Daniel Produced by Pure Flix Entertaiment". The focus of this research is obedience in the film the Book of Daniel, which is reflected in the character of Daniel. The aims of this research are to identify, classify and analyze the theme in the Film the Book of Daniel through the characters. The writer uses the theory of Grace (2009) to analyze the major theme in the Film The Book of Daniel through the character and plot, and Martin (1995) as theory of religious film as a hagiopic genre, which tells the life of someone as a hero of religion. This research seeks to examine the income level of the palm sugar home industry in Kaayuran Atas Village, located in the South Langowan District. The study was carried out in February 2021. Data collection involved obtaining primary data through direct interviews with respondents using structured questionnaires. Additionally, secondary data were acquired from relevant agencies associated with the research topic, including physical data pertaining to Kaayuran Atas Village and other pertinent information. The findings reveal that the palm sugar home industry’s average monthly income in Kaayuran Atas Village amounted to IDR 5,839,166. When compared against the production costs, which averaged IDR 5,885,469 per month, the industry incurred a deficit of IDR 46,303 monthly, indicating a loss. However, this calculation includes family labor costs averaging IDR 3,600,000 per month. Excluding these labor costs, total production expenses reduce to IDR 2,209,000, thereby resulting in a net income of IDR 3,319,000 for the palm sugar home industry. Consequently, when family labor costs are excluded, the industry does not experience losses. Moreover, the managers of the palm sugar home industry engage in supplementary activities, such as gardening, which contribute to their overall livelihood.

This study addresses a fundamental issue: to what extent does the implementation of the Village Budget Policy (APBDes) influence the success of development in Lovra Kusu Village, Kao District, North Halmahera? Accordingly, the research aims to ascertain the impact of APBDes policy implementation on rural development outcomes in Lovra Kusu Village.

Employing a quantitative methodology, this study utilizes descriptive and explanatory approaches. Data were collected through questionnaires administered to 50 respondents, supplemented by observational and documentary evidence. The data were subsequently analyzed using product-moment correlation and simple linear regression techniques.

The analysis reveals that both the implementation of APBDes and the rural development achievements in Lovra Kusu Village fall within a “medium” category, indicating moderate success. This outcome suggests that the current policy implementation of APBDes has not reached an optimal level, thereby limiting its potential contribution to rural development success. The suboptimal results are attributed primarily to insufficient resources, particularly concerning the quantity and quality of human resources involved in APBDes policy execution.

In conclusion, the study finds that the implementation of the APBDes policy exerts a positive and statistically significant effect on rural development success in Lovra Kusu Village, Kao District, North Halmahera. To enhance the efficacy of APBDes policy implementation, it is recommended that the North Halmahera district government augment both the number and competency of village officials responsible for managing rural finances, through targeted professional and technical training programs.

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Village Budget (APBDes), Rural Development

The 2014 data on respiratory tract disorders (ISPA) in North Sulawesi Province indicate that Kotamobagu City reported the highest number of cases, totaling 15,367. This was followed by Sangihe with 9,984 cases, Manado City with 4,500 cases, Bolaang Mongondow Utara Regency with 3,153 cases, Minahasa Tenggara Regency with 1,532 cases, and Minahasa Utara Regency with 376 cases. Further data obtained from the Sanitary Department of Manado City in 2014 show monthly case distributions as follows: February with 153 cases, March 1,189 cases, April 679 cases, May 1,349 cases, June 685 cases, July 79 cases, September 216 cases, October 199 cases, November 99 cases, and December 442 cases.

Previous studies have established a connection between dust exposure and the incidence of ISPA. For instance, research conducted by Dinda Anggun in Palembang (2013) demonstrated that 48.6% (34 out of 70) of individuals were affected by ISPA related to dust exposure. Similarly, Yusnabeti et al. (2009) found that 43 out of 98 furniture industry workers in rural West Kern Cilebut experienced ISPA as a result of dust exposure. Additionally, a study by Khairiah et al. (2012) in North Sumatra reported that 19 out of 56 individuals exhibited respiratory disorders associated with dust concentration.

This study employed a cross-sectional analytic survey design to investigate the relationship between dust exposure and respiratory disorders in the community located in Kairagi 1 Environment 3, Manado City. Chi-square testing yielded a correlation value of 0.006 (p < 0.05), indicating a statistically significant association between dust exposure and the incidence of respiratory disorders in the studied community.

The findings revealed that dust exposure levels were categorized into medium (38.6%) and light (61.4%). Among the respondents, 45 individuals (64.3%) reported experiencing respiratory tract disorders (ISPA), while 25 individuals (35.7%) did not report such conditions in Kairagi Village Environment 3, Manado City. The results affirm the existence of a significant relationship between dust exposure and respiratory disorder events within this population.

Keywords: dust exposure, respiratory disorders incidence

Paddy rice represents the primary staple food in Indonesia, with more than half of the population relying on rice derived from paddy plants for sustenance. Approximately 1.75 billion of the three billion inhabitants in Asia, including 210 million Indonesians, depend on rice as their main caloric source. This study aims to determine the population density and infestation intensity of the paddy bug, Leptocorisa acuta, on paddy plants across the districts of North Tombatu, East Tombatu, and Pasan in the Southeast Minahasa Regency. The research is intended to provide comprehensive data regarding the distribution and infestation levels of L. acuta in various locations, as well as to inform control strategies. Findings indicate that L. acuta is widely distributed throughout the paddy fields in all three districts. The highest population density was recorded in East Tombatu (33.9 individuals per ten double sweeps), followed by Pasan (24.1 individuals per ten double sweeps), while North Tombatu exhibited the lowest density (9.2 individuals per ten double sweeps). Elevated populations of the paddy bug are attributed to environmental conditions and local farming practices associated with paddy cultivation. Given the considerable infestation intensity observed, the presence of this pest poses a significant threat to paddy production. 

Keywords: paddy plants, population density, infestation intensity, paddy bug pest (Leptocorisa acuta Thunb.)

This study aimed to examine the impact of information technology on organizational effectiveness within the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives (DPRD) of the Sula Islands Regency, North Maluku Province. Employing a quantitative approach, the research operationalized information technology through indicators such as computer hardware, software, information and communication networks, and databases. Organizational effectiveness was assessed using variables including production output, efficiency, flexibility, and organizational adaptability. The sample comprised 35 respondents selected via simple random sampling, consisting of 25 Secretariat employees and 10 DPRD members. Data collection was conducted through questionnaires supplemented by guided interviews. Inferential statistical methods, specifically linear regression analysis and Pearson product-moment correlation, were utilized for data analysis. The findings revealed: (1) a positive and statistically significant regression coefficient between information technology and organizational effectiveness; (2) a strong and significant correlation coefficient and coefficient of determination indicating the relationship between information technology and organizational effectiveness. Consequently, the study concluded that information technology exerts a positive and significant influence on organizational effectiveness. Based on these conclusions, the study recommends: (1) enhancing both the quantity and quality of information technology infrastructure within the Secretariat of DPRD Sula Islands Regency, with particular emphasis on hardware, software, communication networks, and database systems; (2) improving employees’ competencies in information technology applications through targeted training programs; and (3) equipping DPRD members with knowledge and skills in information technology to facilitate more effective task execution.

Keywords: Information Technology, Organizational Effectiveness.

This research focuses on Bank Indonesia as the subject of study, specifically examining its role within the banking sector. The organization seeks to optimize employee performance through the implementation of a compensation system that incorporates both rewards and punishments with considerable rigor. The primary objective of this study is to assess the effect of rewards and punishments on the performance of employees at the Bank Indonesia Branch in Manado. Employing multiple regression analysis, data were collected from a sample comprising 40 employees of the same branch. The findings indicate that both rewards and punishments have a statistically significant impact on employee performance, both simultaneously and individually. Employees reportedly perceive the rewards granted by the organization as a form of recognition, which in turn enhances their motivation and encourages improved work performance. Similarly, punishments are interpreted positively by employees, who regard them as valuable learning experiences that serve as motivation to achieve better outcomes. It is recommended that the Human Resource department of Bank Indonesia Manado Branch DAOP 8 sustain their effective performance management by increasing the provision of rewards to further elevate employee performance, while also fostering a constructive perception of punishments among employees. 

Keywords: reward, punishment, employee performance

Customer loyalty constitutes a critical factor for the success of a company, as it positively influences corporate profitability through both cost reduction and additional revenue generation. Loyalty offers numerous benefits to organizations, including customer retention and favorable recommendations to peers regarding brand purchases. This prevailing significance of customer loyalty underpins the business sector’s keen interest in the concept. The present study seeks to examine the influence of the dimensions of trust, commitment, communication, and complaint handling on customer loyalty at Otomoto Manado. An associative analytical approach was employed, utilizing Multiple Linear Regression Analysis along with tests for Classical Assumptions. The study population comprised 276 Otomoto customers who had experienced service or made purchases at least twice, from which a sample of 75 respondents was selected. The findings indicate that, collectively, trust, commitment, communication, and complaint handling significantly impact customer loyalty. Individually, trust, commitment, and complaint handling exert a positive effect on customer loyalty, whereas communication does not demonstrate a positive influence. It is recommended that the management of Otomoto Manado undertake further initiatives to enhance customer loyalty to bolster their competitive position within the market. 

Keywords: trust, commitment, communication, complaint handling, customer loyalty

This study focuses on the implementation of good governance within the staffing process of the Regional Staffing Agency in the recruitment sector of Manado City. Employing qualitative research methods, the study seeks to explore and elucidate the underlying realities of the staffing procedures in the Manado Regional Staffing Agency. Findings indicate that communication throughout the staffing process is both effective and transparent. While transparency and accountability in recruitment are commendable, the study identifies areas requiring improvement to enhance the overall quality of the workforce.

Keywords: Implementation, Good Governance, Regional Staffing Agency

The present study focused on assessing the condition of mangrove communities on Batanta Island and Salawati Island, located within the Raja Ampat District of West Papua Province. The methodology employed was developed by the Indonesian Institute of Sciences Research Center for Oceanography (P2O LIPI). To determine mangrove canopy coverage percentages, hemispherical photography was utilized, and subsequent data analysis was conducted using ImageJ software integrated with Excel for tabulation purposes. The findings revealed a decline in mangrove canopy coverage from 85.73% in 2017 to 84.14% in 2018. However, since the initial observations in 2015, no statistically significant changes in mangrove coverage were observed. On average, coverage increased by 3.45%, rising from 75.09% in 2015 to 78.54% in 2016, followed by a further increase of 7.20% in 2017 (85.73%). These data suggest that fluctuations in mangrove coverage are minimal, leading to the conclusion that the mangrove ecosystems within the study area have not undergone significant degradation and exhibit a robust growth rate. Furthermore, the average tree density was recorded at 1,254.3 trees per hectare during the 2016-2018 period, representing an approximate 16.5% increase since 2015. The study identified five mangrove species (Rhizophora mucronata, Rhizophora apiculata, Bruguiera gymnorrhiza, Sonneratia alba, and Xylocarpus granatum) distributed across eight observation stations. Overall, these results indicate that the mangrove ecosystems at the research sites remain stable and provide a conducive habitat supporting the associated biotic communities.
