Job satisfaction constitutes an affective or emotional response to various facets of an individual's job, indicating that it is a multifaceted construct rather than a singular concept. An individual may experience satisfaction with certain aspects of their job while simultaneously harboring dissatisfaction toward others. It can be defined as a worker's positive attitude toward their employment, which emerges from an evaluative process regarding the work environment. This evaluation is often grounded in the recognition of attaining significant values inherent in the job. Employees who are satisfied tend to prefer their work circumstances over unfavorable conditions.

The present study aims to examine the influence of Work-Life Balance and Emotional Intelligence on Work Satisfaction among employees at Hotel Sintesa Peninsula Manado. Employing multiple linear regression analysis, the research investigates these relationships quantitatively. The findings from the hypothesis testing reveal that, collectively, Work-Life Balance and Emotional Intelligence exert a significant impact on Work Satisfaction at Hotel Sintesa Peninsula Manado. However, when examined independently, Work-Life Balance does not demonstrate a significant effect on Work Satisfaction.

Consequently, it is recommended that Hotel Sintesa Peninsula Manado focus on sustaining and enhancing the emotional intelligence of its employees, as this may foster greater job satisfaction and, in turn, contribute to improved employee performance.

Keywords: Work-Life Balance, Emotional Intelligence, Work Satisfaction

The street lighting tax is one of the district / city taxes imposed on the use of electricity provided that street lighting is available in the area, whose accounts are paid by the regional government. Street lighting tax is one of the potential sources of regional income that can be influenced by certain factors. Therefore, this study aims to determine the potential and tax effectiveness of street lighting in the Regional Revenue Office of the City of Manado. The analytical method used is qualitative descriptive analysis. The data sources used in this study are secondary data, namely data originating from the Regional Revenue Office of the City of Manado. The results of the study indicate that the potential for street lighting tax in Manado City is less effective, and the tax effectiveness of street lighting from 2013-2017 is very effective. In 2013 the highest effectiveness of street lighting tax was 105.82 with very effective criteria, and in 2016 the lowest effectiveness of street lighting tax was 100.87 with very effective criteria. This means that tax on street lighting is very efficient and good, because the realization of street lighting tax revenues in the city of Manado reaches its real revenue potential.Keywords: Potential, Effectiveness.

Financial statements constitute a fundamental aspect for enterprises of all sizes, encompassing both large corporations and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). In Indonesia, data from the Ministry of Cooperatives and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises indicate that as of 2013, there were a total of 57,900,787 business units, of which SMEs comprised the overwhelming majority at 57,895,721 units (99.99%), while large enterprises accounted for only 5,066 units (0.01%). Although SME growth is primarily reflected in numerical terms, their financial development remains comparatively underdeveloped. This financial lag is exemplified by UD Mitra Pelita, a business entity that has yet to prepare formal financial statements. The present study aims to examine the financial management practices of UD Mitra Pelita, exploring their perceptions regarding the advantages and disadvantages associated with the preparation of financial statements, as well as identifying the factors contributing to the owner’s failure or reluctance to compile such reports. Employing a descriptive research methodology with a case study approach, the findings demonstrate that the financial management practices at UD Mitra Pelita mirror those of SMEs in general, characterized by the absence of prepared financial reports. This deficiency generates numerous challenges in the conduct of their business operations. Moreover, the factors impeding the preparation of financial statements at UD Mitra Pelita are largely consistent with those observed across SMEs broadly. Nonetheless, these identified factors do not preclude UD Mitra Pelita from implementing financial reporting practices, which offer substantial benefits for their business activities.

Keywords: Financial Reports, Benefits, Challenges, Influencing Factors

This research endeavors to assess the management of the Village Fund in Kalasey Dua Village, located in Mandolang Sub-district, Minahasa Regency. The study was carried out between May 2018 and January 2019. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized for this investigation. Primary data were obtained through interviews conducted with two members of the Village Consultation Board (Badan Permusyawaratan Desa, BPD), three village officials, and 50 selected community members. The selected community members were individuals over the age of 21 who had resided in the village for more than ten years, resulting in a total of 55 respondents. The interviews with community members were analyzed using a Likert Scale. Secondary data comprised archives and reports from the Kalasey Dua Village office, including Village Monographs, Village Fund Management Data, and other related documents. Additional secondary information was gathered from books available at local bookstores as well as scholarly articles and theses accessed via internet searches, primarily through Google Scholar. Descriptive analysis was employed to examine the collected data. The findings reveal that the Village Fund in Kalasey Dua Village has been effectively managed by local authorities in accordance with established procedures, supported by the availability of relevant documentation. Furthermore, the management process adheres to fundamental principles such as fairness, addressing community needs, respecting village authority, encouraging participation, fostering self-management and village-based resources, recognizing village typology, and ensuring transparency and accountability. Community members have reportedly experienced tangible benefits from the Village Fund, which has contributed to infrastructural development (including roads, culverts, and solar-powered street lighting) and the empowerment of rural communities through technical guidance in the management of Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDES), including those beyond the local area.

The present study investigated the impact of Acalypha indica leaf extract on the immune response of Nile tilapia, with the objective of identifying the optimal extract concentration that enhances total leukocyte count and phagocytic activity. Leaves were separated from stems, thoroughly washed, air-dried at ambient temperature, and subsequently ground into powder. Extraction was performed via maceration, wherein 40 grams of leaf powder were soaked in 200 mL of ethanol for a total of 72 hours, with intermittent stirring. The resultant extract was filtered through Whatman filter paper and concentrated by evaporation at room temperature over several days. 

Experimental diets incorporated varying concentrations of the concentrated extract: 0 g/kg (Control, Treatment A), 10 g/kg (Treatment B), 20 g/kg (Treatment C), 30 g/kg (Treatment D), and 40 g/kg (Treatment E). These diets were administered to Nile tilapia juveniles over a 30-day period at a dosage corresponding to 3% of body weight per day, divided into two feedings at 09:00 and 16:00 hours. Post-treatment, blood samples were collected from the caudal vein using 1 mL syringes pre-treated with 10% EDTA as an anticoagulant. Total leukocyte counts were determined by mixing 50 µL of blood with Turk’s solution (1:10 blood to Turk’s ratio) followed by 5 minutes of incubation. Phagocytic activity was assessed by combining 50 µL of blood with 50 µL of baker’s yeast cells as a stimulant and incubating for 20 minutes. Subsequently, blood smears were prepared, stained with Giemsa, and examined under a light microscope.

The findings demonstrated a statistically significant increase (p < 0.01) in both total leukocyte counts and phagocytic activity following administration of A. indica leaf extract. Notably, the most pronounced immunostimulatory effects were observed at extract concentrations ranging from 20 to 30 g/kg of feed after 30 days of treatment.

This study investigates the impact of family income on the consumption of pork and its substitutes in Ranotana Weru Village, located in Wanea District. Both primary and secondary data were collected through a survey method. Purposive sampling was employed to select the study participants. To analyze the data, a multiple regression model was applied, specified as follows: C = b0 + b1x1 + b2x2 + b3x3. The resulting regression equation obtained was C = 59.44 + 1.38(x1) + 0.018(x2) + 4.97(x3), with an R² value of 0.95. The intercept value of 59.44 suggests that, in the absence of changes in pork prices, substitute prices, and family income, the average pork consumption per person remains at 59.44 grams. The regression coefficient for the price of pork (1.38) indicates that for every increase of Rp 1,000 in pork price, pork consumption decreases by 1.38 grams per capita. Additionally, the coefficient for the price of substitutes (0.018) reveals that a Rp 1,000 increase in the price of substitute goods results in a 0.018-gram increase in consumption of those substitutes. The coefficient for family income (4.97) implies that a Rp 1,000 rise in income corresponds to an increase of 4.97 grams in pork consumption. The coefficient of determination (R² = 0.95) signifies that 95% of the variation in pork and substitute consumption can be explained by family income, while the remaining 5% is attributable to other factors not captured in the model. Statistical testing confirms the significant influence of family income on the consumption of pork and its substitutes in Ranotana Weru Village, as evidenced by a t-value of 0.786, which is less than the critical t-value of 2.000. 

**Keywords:** Family income, pork consumption, substitute goods

The concentration of 60% ethanol yield of total 0,171 carotenoids, 2,693 color intensity and color stability to light ranges from 0,602 to 0,657. Sensory testing of the extraction of red fruit as a natural dyes to the flavor, aroma, and color that preferred by the panelists is treated with 70% concentration of ethanol.

ABSTRACT The research is entitled Discourse Analysis of Martin Luther King Jr.'s speech, "I Have a Dream" (Addressed to the March on Washington). It is an attempt to analyzeand explain the discourse analysis norms. The objective of this research is to identify, classify, and analyze the discourse analysis norms in Martin Luther King Jr's Speech. The writer conducts this research by using descriptive method. In collecting data, the speech and its history were taken from the book American speech and other relevant source from internet as a source data. The data analysis was based on by Juez (2008:20) and supportedby De Beaugrande and Dressler (1986:8) and Aarts and Aarts (1982: 4).These discourse analysis norms were applied in the Martin Luther King Jr's Speech. The theory consists of seven norms, they are: cohesion (pronoun, substitusion, ellipsis, conjuction, and lexical), coherence (mark coherence and unmark coherence), intentionality, acceptability, informatifity, situationality, and intertextuality. The result of this research shows that in the cohesion norm, there are 131 pronouns, 52 subtitusion, 1 ellipsis, 90 conjuction and 16 lexical. In coherence norm, there are 46 mark coherence and there is no unmark coherence. There are also others norms like intentionality, acceptability, informatifity, situationality, and intertextuality. This speech contains the seven norms sugested by Juez (2008:20). Keywords : Discourse Analysis, Speech, Martin L.King Jr., Norms.

Retirement is a universal experience for employees, necessitating adequate preparedness to effectively navigate the subsequent phase of life. Notably, employees' orientations toward gender roles, which inherently differ in characteristics, contribute to variations in retirement readiness. This study investigates the significance of differences in retirement readiness between male and female civil servants at BKPSDM Talaud. The sample comprised 100 respondents, equally divided between males and females, selected through random sampling. Data were collected using a Likert scale designed to measure pension readiness, based on theoretical frameworks proposed by Sutarto and Ismulcokro. Statistical analysis was conducted employing the t-test to evaluate gender-based differences. The findings revealed a significance value of 0.001 (p < 0.05), indicating a notable difference in retirement readiness between male and female employees at BKPSDM Talaud. Both male and female employees receiving adequate compensation demonstrated the ability to maintain financial stability and adjust effectively to retirement. It is imperative that employees, particularly those nearing retirement, prepare comprehensively by addressing both external factors—such as financial management, physical health, engagement in post-retirement activities, and environmental conditions—and internal factors encompassing mental and psychological well-being.  

Keywords: retirement readiness, compensation, gender

This research aims to determine the participation of the community in the development of Mapalus culture during the Covid 19 Pandemic in Desa Picuan Satu Kecamatan Motoling Timur, Kabupaten Minahasa Selatan. The research uses descriptive design qualitative analysis. Data collection techniques used are observation, interview, and documentation. To see how community participation in Mapalus cultural development during the covid 19 pandemic in Desa Picuan Satu. Researchers use 4 indicators, namely: family, consensus deliberation, cooperation, unity and unity. Based on the results of the research shows that the culture of "Mapalus" formed and applicable in Desa Picuan Satu is very useful, especially in increasing the level of community economy. However, in its implementation, it is not necessarily obeyed by all members of the community, especially among teenagers and civil servants (civil servants). They are only seen participating in certain activities. As for members of the community who are truly obedient and uphold Mapalus culture remain active and participate in various activities. This indicates the participation of the community in the development of Mapalus culture, but not all residents of Desa Picuan Satu adhere to and uphold the culture of "Mapalus". Nevertheless, the government of Desa Picuan Satu maintains and maintains balance so that there are no divisions and differences in perception in the community. Keywords: Participation, Community, Mapalus, Pandemic Covid 19

The fishermen community is a community found in North Sulawesi, especially in the coastal area of Sario-Malalayang, Manado. With different cultural backgrounds, ethnicities, this group has its own uniqueness, especially in language. This research succeeded is finding expressions in the fishermen community in the coastal area of Sario-Malalayang. These expressions consist of forms of words, phrases, and clauses in accordance with the lingual forms of theory from Widdowson (1997: 3). The results of the study found a number of lingual forms in affixed words, which had a similar prefix as in the words ba-daseng, ba-kintu, ba-tono, ba-saoh, ba-pake. In addition, the majority of phrases contained in the results of the study are predominantly dominated by noun phrases, such as in the lips phrases of napo, puru loe, coolies, ikang itching, mulu sosoroka, gargantang tubir.This research also succeeded in exploring and discovering cultural meanings. The meanings in the form of words, such as 'badaseng', 'sunga', then the form of a phrase, like 'puru loe', 'mulu sosoroka', then sentence expressions in the form of expressions like 'udang deng katang so kurang sama', 'kase wora mar jang talapas', 'karja cuma sampe di kuli aer', etc. The expressions encountered generally contain various cultural meanings, namely advice, satire, ridicule, seduction, warning, insults, and despair. Based on the conclusion, the researcher suggests to the next researcher, to be more comprehensive related to the use of Manado Malay language expression in different background and contexts in order to get a whole description about expressions system of Manado Malay language, especially in the fishermen community in North Sulawesi.Keywords: fishermen community, language and culture

The purpose of this study are to know about strategys to development tourism object Danau Linouw to increasing local revenue of Tomohon City. This study use descriptive qualitative method. The sampling technique is taken based on the consideration that the existing population is not known exactly in number so using accidental sampling. The variables in this study consisted of the development of tourist attraction and the increase of local revenue (PAD). Data collection techniques consist of interviews, observation, questionnaires, documentation. Data analysis techniques use SWOT analysis and development strategy. The result of the research shows that the development strategy of Lake Linouw Tourism Object in increasing Tomohon District Revenue (PAD) based on SWOT analysis has been done, located in Quadrant I position or strategy through Horizontal Integration, which is located between external opportunity and internal strength. This is a major strategy for developing tourism by maintaining strength and optimizing opportunities while improving weaknesses and anticipating existing threats in an effort to increase the number of tourist arrivals that can increase local revenue (PAD) of Tomohon City. To increase the original revenue of Tomohon City, it is hoped that the Government and Private sector, especially Lake Linouw Tourism Manager, need to plan a marketing strategy so that tourists who visit will continue to grow. Improving facilities and infrastructure related to access road to Lake Linouw attraction which is considered less extensive to be passed by visitors who use motor vehicles.

ABSTRACT:  
Leadership behavior varies fundamentally among individuals and is commonly referred to as leadership style. The success of an organization is greatly influenced by the leader’s role and the particular style of leadership they employ. This study investigates the extent to which leadership styles affect the work motivation of civil servants employed at the Department of Energy and Mineral Resources in North Sulawesi. A quantitative research approach was utilized, with the population comprising civil servants at the aforementioned department. A sample of 20 respondents was selected systematically. Data were gathered through the administration of questionnaires. The analysis procedures included linear regression analysis and the product-moment correlation coefficient.  

The findings reveal that the regression coefficient for leadership style (X) in relation to work motivation (Y) is statistically significant and positive. Additionally, both the correlation and determination coefficients fall within the moderate category. These results indicate that leadership style exerts a positive influence on the motivation of civil servants, thereby highlighting leadership style as a critical determinant of employee work motivation.  

Based on these conclusions, several recommendations are proposed: (1) leaders should foster effective communication between employees and management; (2) greater attention should be directed by leaders toward employees demonstrating high job performance; and (3) the implementation of participatory leadership styles is encouraged to promote harmonious cooperation, enhance employee loyalty, and increase participation.  

Keywords: leadership styles, work motivation

This research seeks to evaluate the financial performance of PT Indonesia Prima Property Tbk, located in Central Jakarta, through an analysis of financial ratios over the period from 2016 to 2018. The financial ratios examined in this study include the Current Ratio (CR), Quick Ratio (QR), Total Asset Turnover (TAT), Net Profit Margin (NPM), Gross Profit Margin (GPM), and Debt to Total Assets (DtAT). The primary data utilized consist of the company's financial statements for the years 2016 through 2018. 

The results indicate that the liquidity position, as measured by the Current Ratio, was 2.78%, 4.28%, and 0.80% for 2016, 2017, and 2018, respectively. Correspondingly, the Quick Ratio values were recorded as 2.38%, 3.83%, and 0.72% during the same period. The activity ratio, reflected by the Total Asset Turnover, showed a declining trend with values of 0.56%, 0.43%, and 0.03%, which can be attributed to relatively low levels of inventory sales. Regarding profitability, the Net Profit Margin rose incrementally from 0.02% in 2016 to 0.06% in 2018, while the Gross Profit Margin declined from 0.49% to 0.37% over the three years. Lastly, the solvency ratio, as indicated by the Debt to Total Assets ratio, demonstrated fluctuations with percentages of 0.03%, 0.02%, and 0.09%, reflecting a capital structure supported by equity funding in a stable solvency condition.

The collection of surface water tax (hereafter referred to as APER) must fundamentally adhere to the procedures prescribed by the relevant Regional Regulations. Surface water tax constitutes one of the various categories of local taxes that contribute to Regional Original Income (PAD) and serve as a crucial financial resource for government operations and regional development aimed at enhancing community welfare. The collection process for this tax is conducted directly at the Regional Revenue Service Branch (CPPD) of West Java Province, specifically within West Java Regency. This process is implemented in collaboration with the One Stop Integrated Service and Capital Licensing Service (DPMPTSP) and the Water Resources Management Agency (PSDA). 

The operational sequence encompasses several stages, including the issuance of the Water Taking Permit (SIPPA) for new taxpayers, registration and data collection, submission of the Water Acquisition Value (NPA) to Dispenda, reporting and preparation of the Regional Tax Return (SPPD), tax assessment, provisioning of the tax, distribution of the Regional Tax Assessment Letter (SKPD) to the company for billing, followed by payment transactions by the taxpayers. 

Based on the study’s findings, it is recommended that the Regional Revenue Service Unit of West Java Regency Padalarang enhance guidance and provide comprehensive counseling to taxpayers. This outreach should be conducted both directly and indirectly, particularly targeting those who utilize and extract surface water, ensuring such practices do not cause environmental harm.

Keywords: Surface Water Tax Collection Process

Switching behavior refers to the act of consumers discontinuing the use of a product or service in favor of a competitor’s offering. This study aims to examine customer responses to banking services within the context of intense competition among banks. Specifically, the research investigates the switching behavior of customers between Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) and Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) in the cities of Manado and Bitung. Employing a quantitative research design, primary data were collected through questionnaires, and an independent sample t-test was utilized to determine whether significant differences exist in consumer switching behavior across five indicators: price, reputation, distance, advertisement, and service quality. The study population comprised all customers of BNI and BRI in Manado and Bitung, both developing urban centers in North Sulawesi province. A total of 200 respondents participated, with 100 customers from each bank. The findings revealed that, for three of the indicators, no significant differences in switching behavior were observed between the two banks. Based on these outcomes, it is recommended that BNI enhance its service delivery, particularly in rural areas surrounding Manado and Bitung.  
Keywords: consumer switching behavior, independent sample t-test

Keywords: informal sector, employment, motorcycle taxi

The interrelation between language and culture is profound and inseparable. Indonesia, known for its diverse customs, includes the Galela ethnic group in Kokota Jaya, North Halmahera, North Maluku province, which possesses a rich heritage of ancestral traditions. Among these traditions is a courtship ceremony intended to propose marriage, reflecting the cultural values upheld within the community. This event encompasses various linguistic and lexical expressions imbued with cultural significance, alongside meaningful verbal and nonverbal communicative behaviors. This study addresses the necessity of comprehensively understanding the meanings conveyed through both verbal and nonverbal expressions during the ceremonial courtship process. The primary objective of this research is to identify and analyze the cultural meanings embedded in the forms of verbal and nonverbal expressions utilized in the Galela ethnic marriage proposal ceremony in Kokota Jaya. The findings indicate the presence of distinct linguistic and lexical elements within the courtship ceremony, as well as culturally significant verbal and nonverbal expressions. It is therefore recommended that further, more detailed examinations of the marriage proposal ceremonies be conducted. Moreover, it is imperative for the Galela community, particularly the younger generation in Kokota Jaya, to actively engage in learning and preserving the regional language as a vital cultural heritage.  
Keywords: Expression, Culture, Galela Ethnic Group

ABSTRACT  
Acalypha indica L., commonly known as the cooperleaf herb, is traditionally utilized for medicinal purposes. The leaves of this plant are specifically employed to reduce blood glucose levels. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of ethanol extracts of cooperleaf herb leaves on the blood glucose levels in male Wistar strain white mice induced with sucrose. Fifteen male Wistar mice were randomly assigned to five treatment groups: a negative control group, a positive control group, and three experimental groups receiving ethanol leaf extract doses of 3.15 g/kg, 6.3 g/kg, and 12.6 g/kg body weight, respectively. Blood glucose measurements were taken following sucrose administration at 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes post-treatment. Data were analyzed using One-Way ANOVA followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test to determine differences among treatment groups. The findings indicate that ethanol extracts of cooperleaf herb leaves at doses of 3.15 g/kg, 6.3 g/kg, and 12.6 g/kg body weight significantly reduced blood glucose levels in male Wistar mice.

Background: Patient waiting time constitutes a critical component in evaluating the quality of medical services from the patient’s perspective. This waiting time encompasses the duration patients spend from registration through to receiving healthcare services and obtaining medications at the pharmacy. The present study aims to investigate the factors influencing patient waiting times during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

Methods: Employing a qualitative research design with a case study approach, this study was conducted between July and September 2020 at the Outpatient Unit of Bhayangkara Hospital in Manado. Seven informants were purposively selected using the snowball sampling technique. The variables examined included administration, medical records, human resources (HR), and hospital infrastructure. Data were collected via in-depth interviews and direct field observations. Interview recordings were transcribed and subjected to content analysis.

Results: Findings revealed that the average patient waiting time at the Bhayangkara Manado Hospital outpatient unit during the COVID-19 pandemic complied with the hospital’s minimum service standard of under 60 minutes. Contrary to expectations, the administrative process did not adversely affect waiting times amidst the pandemic; in fact, it expedited due to a reduction in patient volume. Conversely, delays were attributed to factors related to medical records, human resources, and hospital infrastructure amid the pandemic conditions.

Conclusion: In summary, patient waiting times at the outpatient unit of Bhayangkara Hospital Manado remain within the hospital’s prescribed minimum service standards. The determinants influencing these waiting periods include administrative procedures, human resource availability, management of medical records, and hospital infrastructure.

This study addresses the issue that the physical appearance and the author do not adequately support the facilities in the service units of the branch offices (UPC), resulting in employee-related deficiencies such as unsatisfactory service and employee unfriendliness, which are frequently encountered problems. Moreover, each component of the marketing mix individually exerts a significant influence on consumer decisions. Therefore, PT Pegadaian should continuously maintain and enhance its marketing mix strategies across all dimensions—including product, price, place, promotion, people, process, and physical appearance—to positively affect consumer decision-making.  

Keywords: marketing mix, consumer decision

The implementation of employee education and training programs has not been optimized, largely due to limitations concerning teaching staff or trainers involved in the instructional process. In light of this issue, the present study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of the employee training program at the Office of Manpower and Transmigration of North Maluku Province. Employing a qualitative research design, the study aims to provide an in-depth explanation of the phenomenon through comprehensive data collection, emphasizing the significance of data depth and detail. Data were gathered using multiple techniques, including interviews, direct observation, and documentation.

Findings indicate that the employee training program has yet to achieve full effectiveness. Employees exhibiting enthusiasm and willingness to participate demonstrated positive responses, whereas those perceiving the training merely as a mandatory work obligation exhibited negative reactions. Regarding the learning dimension, the program was effective in enhancing conceptual understanding, job-related knowledge, fostering interpersonal work relationships, and facilitating the utilization of workplace resources. Behavioral dimension analysis revealed the program's efficacy in promoting changes in attitudes toward subordinates, improving communication, interpersonal conduct, and mutual assistance. Furthermore, the organizational results dimension reflected the program’s positive impact on relationships with supervisors, colleagues, and work partners, as well as in accelerating the realization of the organization’s vision and mission, alongside fostering responsibility and work motivation.

Keywords: effectiveness; training program; employees

The expansion of urban areas has been indirectly driven by population growth, leading to the conversion of green open spaces into built environments to accommodate the increasing demand for services and infrastructure. This transformation has contributed to elevated air temperatures, diminished groundwater and urban air quality, as well as heightened noise pollution. The strategic organization of urban green open spaces can mitigate these developmental impacts and address the ecological disturbances caused by human activities within the City of Manado. To achieve ecological equilibrium in Manado, it is imperative to adopt a green open space development strategy that considers both spatial requirements and oxygen demand. This study seeks to quantify the necessary green open space area for Manado City based on its oxygen-supplying capacity. Data analysis was conducted by evaluating green open space requirements in accordance with area-based regulations outlined in Law Number 26 Year 2007, alongside oxygen demand calculations utilizing the Gerakis formula (1974) as modified by Wisesa (1998). Findings indicate that Manado City requires a total of 2,953.45 hectares of green open space. To fulfill the oxygen provision function of these spaces, it is recommended that each individual plants three trees within an area of 25 square meters. 

Keywords: green open space, oxygen demand, Manado City

WATER HOLDING CAPACITY AND COOKING LOSS OF DRIED AND VACUUM PACKAGE BEEF MEAT. Fresh meat is categorized into perishable physical and chemical material product due to high nutrient composition as the main media of growing microorganism. This meat damage could be handled by drying and vacuum package method. The objective of this study was to evaluate effect of drying time period and storage time period on water holding capacity and cooking loss of vacuum package beef meat. Treatment was conducted using completely randomized design divided into two factors with three replications in each combination of the factors. Factor A, as main plot of drying time period was divided into 12 hours (A1), 16 hours (A2) and 20 hours (A3). Factor B as sub plot of storage time period in room temperature of 270 C was divided into 00 C (B0), 120 C (B1), 240 C (B2), and 360 C (B3). Results showed that treatments affected significantly quality of beef meat. There was no interaction effect on water holding capacity and cooking loss of vacuum package beef meat. Beef meat being dried during 16 hours with temperature of 60 0C using vacuum package and stored at room temperature of 270 C during 36 days produced normal standard of water holding capacity and cooking loss of meat. Key words: water-holding capacity, cooking loss, vacuum package.

This study aims to: (1) analyze the financial performance of PT. Tropica Cocoprima from 2012 to 2014 by utilizing Return on Investment (ROI) through the Dupont system approach, and (2) compare the ROI of PT. Tropica Cocoprima across the years 2012 to 2014. The research was conducted at PT. Tropica Cocoprima, located at City Hall No. 12, Manado, over a two-month period from September to October 2016. Secondary data were obtained directly from the company, specifically financial statements including income statements and balance sheets for the years 2012, 2013, and 2014. Key financial data extracted for ROI calculation encompassed cost of goods sold, cost of sales, administrative expenses, taxes, sales, cash, bank balances, accounts receivable, inventory, and fixed assets. 

Quantitative analysis was employed, focusing on the computation of ROI using the Dupont system, which provides a comprehensive evaluation of the company’s effectiveness in generating returns on invested capital by decomposing ROI into activity and profitability ratios. The study aimed to interpret numerical data to draw conclusions regarding PT. Tropica Cocoprima’s financial performance during the specified period.

Findings from the Dupont analysis indicate that for the years 2012 to 2014, the financial performance of PT. Tropica Cocoprima, as measured by ROI, remained relatively stable, albeit with some fluctuations. The variations in ROI were largely attributable to fluctuations in the Net Profit Margin (NPM), which declined significantly due to reductions in net income. This decrease in net income was primarily driven by rising total costs, especially an increase in costs of sales linked to substantial raw material purchase expenses. Conversely, the Total Asset Turnover (TATO) ratio exhibited favorable trends, improving throughout the study period.

Furthermore, the Dupont system analysis revealed that the ROI percentage for 2013 surpassed that of 2012 and 2014, with the 2012 ROI percentage also exceeding that of 2014. These results highlight temporal differences in the company's financial efficiency and profitability over the three years examined.

Abstract Background : Menstrual cup is an internal device for menstrual flow and is claimed to be an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional menstrual sanitation protection. Women's knowledge about environmentally friendly menstrual cups is important for every woman's attention in the concept of menstrual hygiene and helps in realizing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in 2030. However, inappropriate knowledge makes menstrual cups less desirable. Aim : this study aimed to analyze the relationship between knowledge and interest in the use of menstrual cups. Methods : the method was a cross sectional approach. The sample in this study was 88 nursing students at the National University of Jakarta through accidental sampling technique. The variables analyzed were the level of knowledge and interest of female students. The research instrument used was a knowledge and interest questionnaire. Data were analyzed with Mann Whitney with p=0,05 . Results : Respondents in this study had a good level of knowledge (54.6%) and had no interest in the use of menstrual cups (78.4%). Based on the results of the Mann Whitney test, the P value obtained is P = 0.120 > 0.05 . Conclusion : There was no relationship between knowledge about menstrual cups and interest in using menstrual cups. Keywords : Menstrual Cup; Interest; Knowledge

Traditional Becak transportation can still be found in several regions, particularly in Makassar City. However, in recent years, the number of Becak has gradually declined due to the emergence of more modern and faster vehicles that have rendered Becak increasingly obsolete. Becak drivers rely solely on physical exertion to earn their livelihood. Paddling the Becak is a demanding activity, performed daily from morning until afternoon, and sometimes continuing into the evening. Despite the difficulty, the drivers recognize that this occupation is their primary means of supporting their families. Meeting their basic needs is challenging for some drivers, especially when their earnings do not align with their requirements, necessitating a careful distinction between needs and desires. The majority of Becak drivers in Makassar originate from various regions within South Sulawesi province, such as Jeneponto, Gowa, Maros, and Pangkep, rather than the city itself. One reason many individuals choose Becak driving is the ongoing demand for this mode of transportation. Additionally, the occupation does not require a high level of education or formal academic qualifications. 

Keywords: Becak, transportation, informal sector.

ABSTRACT This research entitled 'Prinsip-prinsip Kesopanan dalam Film The Help Karya Tate Taylor : Suatu Analisis Pragmatik' focuses on maxim related to the politeness principles. The aims of this research is to identify, classify and analyze the politeness principles and their function in The Help movie.This research used a descriptive method. The data collected from conversation among characters, then classify and analyze them according to the concept of Leech (1983). The result shows that there are six maxims of politeness and their function applied by the characters in their dialogues. First, tact maxim consist of 17 utterances functioning to minimizes cost to other and maximizes benefit to the other. Second, generosity maxim consist of 11 utterances functioning to minimizes benefit to self and maximizes cost to self. Third, approbation maxim consist of 21 utterances functioning to minimizes dispraise of other and maximizes praise of other. Fourth, modesty maxim consist of 9 utterances functioning to minimizes praise of self and maximizes dispraise of self. Fifth, agreement maxim consist of 10 utterances functioning to maximizes agreement between self and other and minimizes disagreement between self and other. Sixth, sympathy maxim consist of 9 utterances functioning to minimizes antipathy between self and other and maximizes sympathy between self and other. It is expected that this research will help students and readers in learning pragmatic aspects, especially about politeness principles. Keywords : Politeness Principles, Maxims, Pragmatic Analysis, The Help Movie

The Bogani Nani Wartabone National Park serves as a conservation habitat for diverse flora and fauna, including the endemic Maleo bird (Macrocephalon maleo) of Sulawesi Island. This study aimed to investigate the egg-laying behavior of the Maleo bird, examining parameters such as egg hole temperature, hole depth, visitation frequency at egg-laying sites, and potential predation threats in the vicinity. Research was conducted through direct observation within the natural nesting areas of the Maleo bird. Data collected were analyzed descriptively to elucidate the behavioral patterns and environmental conditions at the nesting sites.

Findings revealed that pre-laying activities encompassed digging of the egg-laying holes, actual egg deposition, covering the holes, and excavation of decoy holes. Post-laying behaviors included periods of resting and foraging near the nesting sites, followed by flight into the forested areas. The entire egg-laying process lasted between one and three hours, commencing with the selection of suitable nesting areas, hole excavation, and culminating with egg deposition. Measured average depths of the nesting holes were 41.8 ± 14.28 cm, with temperatures ranging from 27°C to 34°C.

The frequency of egg-laying was higher near Tower I compared to Tower II. The area surrounding Tower I featured dense tree vegetation, providing shelter and protection from predators as well as open, scrub-free ground facilitating easier excavation of nesting holes. Conversely, Tower II was characterized by the growth of scrubs such as Saccharum spontaneum and Imperata cylindrical, which impeded secure nesting and complicated the digging process. Observational data recorded 28 Maleo pairs and one unpaired male through visual observations, alongside an additional nine pairs identified by auditory cues, amounting to 37 pairs in total—comprising 37 females and 38 males. During the observation period, a total of 42 eggs were recorded, of which 40 successfully hatched using an artificial incubator at the study site, while two eggs were found damaged.

Keywords: Egg-laying behavior, Maleo bird (Macrocephalon maleo).

ABSTRACT This study aims to determine the population and percentage of S. coarctata attacks on rice plants in Kakas Subdistrict, Minahasa Regency. This research is expected to provide information about the level of damage caused by attacks and pest populations of S. coarctata so that farmers can control soil-borne pests in Kakas District Minahasa Regency. This research uses observational research (survey) conducted in Kakas Subdistrict in two villages (Tontimomor and Kalawiran). From each village as a location of observation, three observation plots were determined. Light traps use modern white electric car lights, which are spread diagonally, the trapping is adjusted to the battery life of 8 hours, the installation is done at 10 pm and the observation is done at 6 am, the sampling is 4 repetitions, with intervals 1 week time for rice plants aged 22-68 days after planting. In Kalawiran village there is 8,5 tails and Tontimomor village, there is 7,6 tails, and then the population of Black Bug lowest observed on IV, in Kalawiran village 3.1 tails and Tontimomor village is 2,3 tails. Based on data analysis, at first, second, third, fourth observation, highest attack on second observed in 38 days after planting, in Kalawiran village 23,79% and Tontimomor village 12,54%. Keywords: population, percentage, S. coarctata

This study seeks to identify the factors that contribute to school dropout among children of farmers and non-farmers, as well as to examine whether these factors differ between the two groups. A descriptive analytical approach was employed in this research, which was conducted from April to June 2017. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized, with primary data being collected through structured interviews based on a predefined questionnaire administered to a total of 28 respondents. The sampling strategy applied was purposive sampling, targeting children of farmers and non-farmers alongside their parents.

The findings reveal that the causes of school dropout among children from both farmer and non-farmer households can be categorized into internal and external factors. Internal factors include the children's own volition and a lack of interest in school, while external factors comprise the parents' economic constraints, which limit their ability to finance education, and the influence of the social environment, particularly exposure to peers who have previously dropped out. At the parental level, no significant differences were observed between farmers and non-farmers regarding reasons for their children's dropout. However, at the children's level, the reasons for discontinuing education differ: children of non-farmers predominantly attribute dropout to internal motivations, whereas children of farmers primarily cite external influences stemming from their social environment.

The objective of this study was to determine the minimum concentration of extract in inhibiting motile motile aeromonad septicaemia. The material used was the stems and leaves of the plant P. grandiflora as much as 10 g. The crushed simplicia was then macerated with aquades with a ratio of 1:10, then filtered with filter paper and, put in an Erlenmeyer, and evaporated in an incubator at temperature of 30°C. The sensitivity test was performed by placing a paper disc containing extract on the agar medium that had been scratched with bacterial colonies. Clear zone formed around the paper disc was compared with standard classification table for clarifying the inhibition level. The results showed that stem and leaf extract had inhibition zone against Aeromonas hydrophila bacteria that caused motile aeromonad septicaemia. The best result was obtain at concentration of extract 3.25 mg / L) with an average diameter of 22.67 mm and for leaf extract had a moderate to strong zone for all treatments. These proved that stem and leaf extract of P. grandiflora plant had antibacterial activity and can be used as control of MAS disease caused by A. hydrophila bacteria. Keywords: Portulaca grandiflora plant, motile aeromonad septicemia, minimum inbibition concentration

This study aims to examine and analyze the impact of mutations on the workforce and the development of human resources in the western region of Maluku. The research employs an associative method grounded in positivist philosophy, targeting a specific population or sample. The sampling technique utilized is accidental sampling, focusing on personnel within the civil service and human resource development sectors in Southwest Maluku, with a total sample size of 33 respondents. Data analysis involves simple regression and simple correlation techniques. The correlation analysis revealed an r value of 0.848, indicating a strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship between the variables. Furthermore, the simple regression equation obtained was y = 8.667 + 0.722x, signifying a positive association between the variables examined. The coefficient of determination (R²) was found to be 0.72, suggesting that 72% of the variance in workforce motivation can be explained by the mutation variable, while the remaining 28% is attributed to other factors. An F-test yielded a calculated value of 79.379, which exceeds the critical F-value of 2.60 at the 0.05 significance level (F_calculated > F_table). Consequently, the null hypothesis was rejected and the alternative hypothesis accepted, confirming a significant influence of mutations within the workforce environment on human resource development in the western region of Maluku.

Keywords: Mutation, Workforce, Civil Service Apparatus

This study seeks to examine and analyze the impact of recruitment on the implementation of public services within the Population and Civil Registration Office of North Halmahera Regency. A quantitative research methodology was employed to conduct the investigation. Data collection was primarily carried out through the administration of questionnaires, supplemented by interviews with respondents. The study population consisted of all 36 employees working in the Population and Civil Registration Office of North Halmahera Regency. The data analysis involved hypothesis testing using frequency distribution tables, Pearson product-moment correlation, and simple linear regression techniques. Findings reveal that a majority of respondents (66.66%) rated the recruitment process of the State Civil Apparatus as "high." Conversely, 12 respondents (33.33%) categorized recruitment as "medium," and no respondents rated it as "low." Regarding the public service variable, 52.77% of respondents classified the quality of public services as "high," while 47.22% rated it as "medium," with no respondents indicating a "low" category. These results suggest a generally positive perception among employees concerning both recruitment practices and the implementation of public services in the office studied.

Keywords: Recruitment of State Civil Apparatus, Public Services

The aim of this study was to analyze the level of inequality in regencies / cities in North Sulawesi Province and to analyze the factors that influenced regional disparities that occur in regencies / cities in North Sulawesi Province. Research used secondary data. Data were collected and obtained from the Central Statistics Agency of North Sulawesi Province and related Government Agencies for the period of 2013 to 2017 in the form of GRDP, population, economic potential, and various other secondary data. The data obtained were grouped and processed using the MS Excel application. Method of data analysis was the Williamson Index Method, which was a method of measuring regional inequality. The results showed that North Sulawesi Province experienced low inequality in 2013 to 2016 and high inequality in 2017 with a value of 0.55. Factors affecting North Sulawesi's regional inequality were the concentration of regional economic activity, investment allocation, low levels of mobility and production factors between regions, differences in the demographic conditions of the region and less smooth of trade in land, sea and air transportation. The Williamson Index in 2013-2014 was worth of 0.48, in 2015 it was worth of 0.47, in 2016 it was worth of 0.48 and in 2017 it was worth of 0.55. This showed that the inequality in North Sulawesi from 2013 to 2016 was low but in 2017 was high.Keywords: Regional Inequality, Index Williamson

The objectives of this study was to synthesized 4,6-diallyl-2-methoxyphenol (DMP) from allyl eugenol by Claisen rearrangement. The reaction was carried out at temperature 170-200oC and the reaction time was 30 minutes. The synthesis of DMP by heating at 170-200oC for a certain period of time appears to be a fairly good and simple method. The synthesis compounds were elucidated by infrared (IR), nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR), and mass spectrometry (MS) techniques. Antioxidant activity evaluated the based on the heating of coconut oil. At higher temperatures of reaction the yield will be higher and at the reaction time 30 minutes will produce will produce higher yield which was 59,19%. The gas chromatographic analysis showed that the purity of DMP was 96,45% The structure of 4,6-diallyl-2-methoxyphenol was identified by IR spectrometry which shows strong absorption at 3527 cm-1 indicating hydroxyl group from the phenolic compound and 1H NMR spectra showed that the number of protons of aromatic ring was two hydrogen while the mass spectrometry showed the molecular ion peak at m/z 204 as base peak and absence of peak at (M-41)+ as the indicator of ally eugenol. The addition of DMP at concentration 200 ppm in coconut oil exhibited excellent inhibition of oxidation reaction more than BHT as control positive. The result concluded that 4,6-diallyl-2-methoxyphenol had antioxidant activity on heating of coconut oil at 80oC for 30 day.

This research investigates the impact of occupational health and safety measures on the performance of employees within the Department of Social Outreach and Local Development (SLD) and Community Relations (CR) at PT Freeport Indonesia. Employee personal safety is defined as the protection from injuries resulting from workplace accidents. Occupational hazards in the work environment may include risks such as fire, electrical shock, cuts, bruises, sprains, fractures, organ damage, and impairments to vision and hearing. The primary objective of this study is to examine the effect of occupational health and safety on employee performance in the SLD/CR departments at PT Freeport Indonesia. Employing a descriptive quantitative research design, the study uses simple linear regression analysis facilitated by the SPSS software. The analysis involves two variables: the independent variable (X) representing occupational health and safety, and the dependent variable (Y) representing employee performance. The study population encompasses all employees working at the Regional Office V Pawnshop Manado. The regression analysis yielded the equation Y = 19.835 + 0.461X, indicating that occupational health and safety practices significantly influence employee performance within the SLD/CR departments. This conclusion is supported by an F-statistic of 12.089, which exceeds the critical F-value of 4.00 at a significance level of 0.001 (p < 0.05). Thus, the findings demonstrate that occupational health and safety have a statistically significant and positive effect on employee performance.  

Keywords: Occupational Health, Safety, Employee Performance

This study was conducted to examine the antagonistic activity of probiotic bacteria isolated from the digestive tract of fish (Oxyeleotris marmorata). Fish having an average weight of 500 grams were obtained from fish ponds in Tetey Village, North Minahasa Regency. Fish were dissected, the intestine was separated from the other internal organs. The intestine was then weighed as much as 1 gram, cut into small pieces and then crushed using a mortar until smooth. The results of the scour were transferred to a test tube and 9 mL of NaCl solution was added, then centrifuged at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes for 2 times. The supernatant was diluted to obtain a concentration of 10-2 to 10-3. The dilution was spread onto MRS media and incubated for 24-48 hours at 28oC. Growing colonies were cultured on MRS agar, purified and propagated. The pure isolate obtained were then subjected to Gram Stain, biochemical tests and antagonistic tests. The results of the study found that the characteristics of the bacteria were round shape, milky white in color, rod-shaped and Gram positive, and biochemically identified as Lactobacillus sp. These bacteria had strong antagonistic activity against A. hydrophila which was indicated by the presence of a clear zone with a diameter of 26.88 mm around the probiotic disc.

Language serves as a vital instrument of communication, facilitating the transmission of information. Additionally, language functions as an auditory alert system mutually recognized and employed by members of specific communities to collaborate, communicate, and establish group identity. The present study is grounded in the concept of kinship, which is closely linked to cultural practices within certain communities, such as those in Sangihe, where particular terms are used to address family members within the community. This cultural phenomenon has attracted scholarly interest regarding the use and significance of kinship terminology in society. 

The primary objectives of this research are to identify kinship terms used among the Sangihe people and to elucidate the meanings of these kinship terms as reflections of Sangihe culture. A descriptive qualitative methodology was adopted to conduct this investigation. To address the first research question, Burling’s theory (1970) was employed, while the second question was explored using theoretical frameworks proposed by Spradley (1979) and Casson (1981).

Data collection in the field incorporated the SBCL method (refer to method capable) alongside the administration of questionnaires based on Sudaryanto’s (1993) guidelines. Furthermore, interview techniques recommended by Spradley (1997) were utilized, including general inquiries, specific questions, sample questions, experience-based questions, and queries regarding native language or dialect usage. The responses were systematically recorded for subsequent analysis.

For data analysis, the study employed conceptual expression analysis aimed at comprehensively identifying and interpreting the collected data. This approach, grounded in the linguistic theory of cultural anthropology, enabled the uncovering of the cultural meanings embedded within the kinship terminology prevalent among the Sangihe society.

The halua kenari is a distinctive product originating from North Sulawesi, particularly in the regions of Minahasa and Siau. The processes of fat and oil oxidation contribute to unfavorable changes in taste and flavor, as well as the deterioration of nutritional and functional properties. Beyond its chemical composition, the degradation of halua kenari is further exacerbated by improper handling and packaging during transportation, distribution, and storage by both consumers and vendors. This study aims to predict the shelf life of halua kenari produced by small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the Sitaro Archipelago district using an accelerated shelf life testing (ASLT) model based on the Arrhenius equation, as well as to develop a corresponding shelf life model for these products. The research was conducted in two phases: the first involved the determination of quality characteristics of halua kenari through chemical analyses and organoleptic evaluations; the second assessed shelf life utilizing the ASLT model. Samples were stored at elevated temperatures to accelerate quality deterioration, and the resulting data were extrapolated using the Arrhenius mathematical model. Findings indicate that processing characteristics, storage temperature, and conditions significantly influence the quality degradation and shelf life of halua kenari. Specifically, halua kenari products with low fat and oil content (designated A1) stored at 30°C exhibited a shelf life of 106 days. In contrast, high fat and oil variants stored under the same conditions demonstrated markedly shorter shelf lives, with samples A2, A3, and A4 lasting 18, 23, and 17 days, respectively.  

Keywords: halua kenari, shelf life, Arrhenius model, water content, free fatty acids (FFA)

The food and beverage industry, along with its associated advancements, is widely recognized by individuals across the globe. This study aims to examine the impact of customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, and brand commitment on word-of-mouth communication. To fulfill these objectives, a causal research design was employed, utilizing multiple regression analysis as the primary analytical technique. The target population comprised consumers in Manado who have previously experienced Wall’s Ice Cream, with a sample size of 120 respondents. The findings indicate that customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, and brand commitment collectively exert a significant influence on the word-of-mouth promotion of Wall’s Ice Cream in Manado. Furthermore, these factors significantly affect the variations observed in word-of-mouth communication for the brand. Based on these results, it is recommended that management prioritize the enhancement of customer satisfaction, loyalty, and brand commitment to effectively promote positive word-of-mouth and consider additional variables that might also impact word-of-mouth regarding the company’s ice cream products.

Keywords: customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, brand commitment, word of mouth.

In the domain of state financial management, the occurrence of fraud remains an inherent risk. According to data compiled by the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) as of December 31, 2018, and corroborated by reports from Indonesia Corruption Watch (ICW), there were 454 documented instances of misappropriation and embezzlement of the state budget within government institutions during 2018. These fraudulent activities resulted in financial losses amounting to Rp 5.8 trillion for the state. Given the substantial prevalence of fraud cases, the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) is anticipated to enhance its capacity to detect fraud effectively in order to mitigate ongoing corrupt practices. This study investigates the influence of moral reasoning, work experience, workload, and personality type on auditors’ fraud detection capabilities. The research sample consisted of 54 auditors from the Provincial Representatives of the Supreme Audit Agency of the Republic of Indonesia (BPK RI) in North Sulawesi and Gorontalo. Hypotheses were tested through multiple linear regression analysis. The findings indicate that moral reasoning significantly impacts auditors’ ability to detect fraud, as does work experience and workload, thereby supporting the first three hypotheses of the study.

The Effect of Planting Space On Productivity of Indigofera (Indigofera zollingeriana) in Full Sun Area. The purpose of this research was determines the productivity of Indigofera zollingeriana with three different planting space. This experiment was conducted using Completely Randomized Design (CRD). The treatment consisted of three planting space, (1) 1.0 m x 0.5 m, (2) 1.0 m x 1.0 m, and (3) 1.0 m x 1.5 m, each treatment had six replications. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance and HSD test. The variables measured were fresh and dried stem weight, fresh and dried leaf weight. The results showed that planting space were significant different (P<0.01) on fresh and dried stem weight, fresh and dried leaf weight. HSD test showed that planting space 1.0 m x 1.5 m were significant (P<0.01) have higher stem fresh weight, stem dry matter weight, fresh leaf weight and leaf dry matter weight than planting space 1.0 m x 1.0 m and 1.0 m x 0.5 m. It can be concluded that planting space 1.0 m x 1.5 m have the highest productivity that were highest stem freshweight, stem dry matter weight, leaf freshweight and leaf dry matter weight.Key words: Indigofera zollingeriana, planting space, productivity

This study evaluates the effectiveness of the extension program implemented in the cattle farming sector within Sinonsayang District, South Minahasa Regency. Sinonsayang District, encompassing 13 villages and covering an area of 12,960 hectares, is predominantly inhabited by communities engaged in farming and ranching activities. The largest concentration of cattle, totaling 296 heads, is primarily located in three villages: Blongko, Ongkaw II, and Ongkaw III. The primary research question addresses the extent to which the extension program, conducted by BP3K, has succeeded in enhancing the educational level of cattle farmers in Sinonsayang District. The objective was to systematically assess the implementation and impact of extension activities across the district. The study employed a survey methodology from January to February 2014, focusing on the three villages with the highest cattle populations. Data were collected from a purposively sampled group of 30 respondents—farmers and ranchers—selected based on specific characteristics relevant to the population. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized during the two-month data collection period. Findings reveal that BP3K’s extension services were limited in reach, failing to engage a substantial proportion of cattle breeders. Consequently, this lack of widespread extension outreach correlated with diminished motivation among farmers to increase their cattle numbers. These results indicate that the extension program was neither effectively nor successfully implemented in the study area. 

Keywords: Extension Program Evaluation, Livestock Management, Cattle Farming, Agricultural Outreach

This study aims to identify the physical conditions in the rural urban fringe area and analyze the development pattern of fringe settlements in the rural urban fringe area. EFFECTS OF ADDITIVES ADDITION (ENZYMES AND ORGANIC ACIDS) WITH HIGH AND LOW PROTEIN IN RICE BRAN BASE RATION ON RABBIT'S PERFORMANCE. A research evaluating the effectiveness of enzymes and organic acids in the rice bran-based with different protein content on the production performance of weaning rabbits. This research was conducted in March to May 2014 at the Livestock Research Center Ciawi. One hundred and twenty rabbits Rex and Reza of 900 -1400g body weight. The design used was factorial (2x4) based on Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 5 replications. Combinations treatment consisted of factors, namely the level of protein factor A: A1 = 14% protein and A2 = 18% protein and factor B the addition of additives (enzymes + Organic Acids) consisting of: B1 = Ration Basal; B2 = Ration Basal + Feed Enzymes; B3 = Feed Enzymes and propionic acid; B4 = Feed Enzymes and butyric acid. Variables measured were Feed Consumption, Daily Body Weight Gain, and Feed Conversion. Feed consumption in this research were 74.95 to 86.59 g/ head/ day. Analysis of variance showed that there were no significant effects of treatments on feed consumption (P> 0.05). Daily body weight gain of rabbits ranged from 11.73 to 16.74 g/head/day. There was a significant effect of treatment interaction on average daily body weight gain (P <0.05). Tukey test showed that Average Daily Gain (ADG) of rabbits fed A2B3 16.74 g/ head/day (18% protein with the addition of enzyme and propionic acid) was significantly higher than the rabbits fed A1B3 11.73 g/head/day (14 % protein with the addition of enzymes and organic acids). The feed conversion in this research is about 4.93 to 6.60 g/head/day. There were significant difference among treatment on feed conversion (P> 0.05). It can be concluded that there is no need of additive supplement when the ration has fulfilled nutrient requirement on 14 % and 18 % protein. Keywords: Rabbit, Rice Bran, Enzymes, Organic Acids

The aim of this research was to count the total leukocytes and phagocytosis activity of goldfish seeds treated with probiotics. The test fish used were goldfish seeds measuring 5-8 cm. 500 fish will be taken from the Tateli Fish Cultivation and Development Center (BP3I). This study used a completely randomized design (CRD) with 5 treatments, where each treatment had 3 replications. The treatments used were probiotic bacteria from the intestines of goldfish with different concentrations. The treatments tested consisted of: A: without the addition of probiotics, B: addition of probiotics 1x106 cfu / mL, C: addition of probiotics 1x107 cfu / mL, D: addition of probiotics 1x108 cfu / mL, E: addition of probiotics 1x109 cfu / mL. Each concentration of bacteria that has been prepared is then sprayed on the commercial feed evenly using a sprayer and then dried to room temperature. After drying the feed was coated with 2% egg yolk and dried again at room temperature. Fish are stocked in an aquarium measuring 60x40x40cm3 with a density of 20 fish / aquarium. Each aquarium is equipped with an aerator and a water pump for recirculation. The fish were then given feed that had been added with probiotics at the same dose and frequency of administration as in the acclimatization process. The treatment is given for 6 weeks. At the end of the treatment feeding, fish samples were taken from each experimental unit to measure immune parameters, namely total leukocytes and phagocytic activity. Based on the results of research using the probiotic Lactobacillus sp. which originated from the intestines of goldfish and added to the feed had a significant effect on increasing total leukocytes and phagocytosis activity and the optimal concenration was 1x107 - 1x108 cfu / mL with a duration of 6 weeks of administration

Background: Work fatigue is characterized by a sensation of tiredness accompanied by a reduction in alertness. Although fatigue encompasses various physiological states, all lead to diminished work capacity and lowered resistance to occupational demands. Notably, workplace fatigue accounts for 50% or more of occupational accidents. This study seeks to examine the relationship among workload, job stress, and sleep quality with work fatigue among nurses employed at The Regional General Hospital of Bitung City and Budi Mulia Hospital Bitung City.

Method: Employing a cross-sectional design, this research involved nurses from the Intensive Care Unit, Emergency Room, and Inpatient Room of the aforementioned hospitals in Bitung, North Sulawesi Province. Data were collected through the administration of structured questionnaires.

Results: The findings revealed significant correlations between work fatigue and workload (p = 0.000), job stress (p = 0.000), as well as sleep quality (p = 0.002). Furthermore, multivariate analysis identified job stress as the variable most strongly associated with work fatigue (β = 0.370).

Conclusion: The present study concludes that workload, job stress, and sleep quality are significantly correlated with work fatigue among nurses in the studied hospitals, with job stress emerging as the predominant factor influencing fatigue.

The internal environment constitutes a critical factor influencing organizational operations and activities. This study addresses two primary issues: the prevailing environmental conditions and the level of employee performance within organizations. Specifically, the research aims to examine the impact of the organizational environment on employee performance in the Tuminting district of Manado city. Employing a quantitative methodology, the study utilizes both descriptive and explanatory approaches. The population comprises all 32 employees of the Tuminting district office. Data were gathered through questionnaires and field surveys conducted via observational techniques. Analytical procedures included simple correlation and regression analyses. The findings indicate that respondents generally perceive the organizational environment at the Tuminting district office to be moderate to high. Conversely, employee performance levels tend to range from low to moderate. The regression analysis reveals a positive and statistically significant relationship between the work environment and employee performance, corroborated by a meaningful correlation coefficient of determination. Consequently, it can be concluded that the organizational environment in the Tuminting district office positively and significantly affects employee performance. Based on these results, it is recommended that organizational leaders, particularly those in Tuminting district, foster conducive working conditions and actively enhance employee morale. Furthermore, local government initiatives should focus on implementing concrete measures to improve the organizational work environment.  

Keywords: Organizational environment, Employee performance

Planning and budgeting constitute an integral component of government financial management processes. Ensuring integrity with respect to the scheduling of the planning and budgeting of the Anggaran Pendapatan dan Belanja Daerah (APBD), as well as maintaining the coherence among linked planning documents, is essential. Furthermore, it is necessary to provide effective and efficient local government solutions to address the constraints encountered in the planning and budgeting of the prior fiscal year’s APBD, to facilitate its implementation in the subsequent fiscal year. The Badan Keuangan Kabupaten Kepulauan Sangihe functions as a governmental agency responsible for managing local governance affairs based on the principles of autonomy and supportive roles in the domains of income, asset, and financial management. This enables the effective operation of regional government financial management systems. The objective of this study was to assess whether the planning and budgeting process for the APBD within the Badan Keuangan Kabupaten Sangihe for the fiscal year 2015 complied with the provisions stipulated in Permendagri Nomor 13 Tahun 2006. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study’s findings revealed that out of fourteen procedural steps, one step demonstrated discrepancies related to timing and function in accordance with Permendagri Nomor 13 Tahun 2006. 

Keywords: Planning, Budgeting, Regional Expenditure

Background: Hospitals in Indonesia generate substantial volumes of wastewater, which may contain infectious agents, pathogenic microorganisms, and hazardous chemicals posing risks to both public health and the surrounding environment. Previous investigations have identified antibiotics as constituents of hospital wastewater, and the majority of microorganisms isolated from such wastewater have demonstrated resistance to frequently administered antibiotics.

Objective: This study seeks to assess antibiotic contamination within the wastewater system of RSUP Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou Manado by performing bacterial isolation and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

Methods: A descriptive quantitative research design was employed. Wastewater samples were collected from both inlet and outlet points of the treatment system. Bacterial isolation and identification procedures were conducted in accordance with Bergey's Manual of Determinative Bacteriology. Antibiotic susceptibility was evaluated using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method with clindamycin as the test antibiotic. Interpretation of results adhered to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines.

Results: The bacterial genera identified included Bacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., Escherichia spp., and Staphylococcus spp. With the exception of Bacillus spp., which could not be conclusively interpreted, the isolates exhibited resistance to clindamycin.

Conclusion: The findings indicate the presence of antibiotic contamination in the wastewater at RSUP Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou Manado, as evidenced by the clindamycin resistance observed in Streptococcus spp., Escherichia spp., and Staphylococcus spp. isolates.

Keywords: hospital wastewater, bacterial identification, antibiotic susceptibility testing

This study, entitled "Nouns in English and Tetun Language: A Contrastive Analysis," has been conducted to fulfill the academic requirements for the completion of the English Department program at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University. The primary objectives of this research are to classify and describe the various types of nouns present in both English and Tetun languages. While studies on English nouns are widely accessible and commonly found in grammar books and online resources, research focusing on nouns in the Tetun language remains comparatively scarce. Consequently, this investigation aims to enhance understanding of Tetun nouns through a comparative analysis with their English counterparts. The theoretical framework employed in this study draws upon the concepts advanced by Frank (1972) and Lado (1979). Data analysis involves the classification and description of nouns into categories such as proper nouns, concrete and abstract nouns, countable and uncountable nouns, and collective nouns. The findings indicate that English and Tetun nouns share similar categories based on semantic criteria. However, a notable distinction arises concerning countable nouns: in English, plurality is typically marked by the addition of an -s suffix, whereas in Tetun, numerical indicators specify countability without morphological changes to the noun. This study reveals both convergences and divergences in noun classification between the two languages. It is recommended that readers interested in further exploring the Tetun language either consult this research or pursue additional studies in this area.

Keywords: Nouns, English, Tetun Language
