The allocation of village funds constitutes a portion of the residual funds received by districts or cities, with a mandated minimum of 10% of these residual funds—calculated from the net budget revenue and expenditure excluding special allocation funds—designated for village-level use. The primary objectives of the Village Fund Allocation (ADD) include enhancing the administrative capacity of village governments to effectively deliver government services and promote community development in alignment with their respective authorities; strengthening the ability of village associations and individual villages to engage in participatory planning, implementation, and oversight of development initiatives tailored to local potentials; improving income distribution, employment prospects, and entrepreneurial opportunities for both rural and urban populations; and fostering the growth of mutual aid within non-governmental societal groups.

This study aims to assess the effectiveness of the fund allocation process within villages located in the East Motoling District of South Minahasa Regency. Data were collected through direct field observations, structured interviews, and comprehensive documentation review. Findings from the evaluation indicate that the fund allocation in East Motoling District operates ineffectively due to several discrepancies. Notably, the formulation of village fund utilization plans often excludes community involvement, leading to misinformation among residents regarding the precise purposes of the fund allocation. Furthermore, portions of the budget have been diverted toward personal and group interests, such as funding outdated technical guidance projects, rather than prioritizing broader community development initiatives. Additionally, inadequate supervision by district government authorities contributes to the suboptimal management and utilization of village funds.

Keywords: Effectiveness Evaluation, Village Fund Allocation, Community Development, Participatory Governance

This study was conducted with the objective of enhancing English vocabulary acquisition among second-grade students at SD GMIM 7 Manado through the application of the Total Physical Response (TPR) method. The research aims to elucidate the process of TPR implementation and to evaluate the improvement in students' vocabulary following its use. Employing Classroom Action Research (CAR) as the methodological framework, data were gathered through a sequence of pre-tests, instructional treatments, and post-tests. The analysis involved simple statistical comparison of scores obtained from the pre- and post-tests. Findings indicate that the TPR method effectively facilitates the enhancement of students’ English vocabulary, as evidenced by an increase in average scores from 65 in the pre-test to 92 in the post-test. This represents a 42% improvement in students’ performance subsequent to TPR implementation. Consequently, the results substantiate the efficacy of the Total Physical Response approach in vocabulary development within the elementary school context.

Keywords: Classroom Action Research, Vocabulary Development, Total Physical Response, Elementary Education.

This study investigates the disciplinary policies applied to civil servants within the Secretariat and staffing agencies of Ternate City, conducted as part of the requirements for the completion of a college degree thesis. The disciplinary framework, governed by Government Regulation No. 53 of 2010 concerning civil servant disciplinary rules, has been implemented in governmental institutions at both the organizational and regional levels. However, despite these regulations, instances of civil servant misconduct, including authority abuse, continue to be observed. Such behaviors have been found to negatively impact civil servant performance, thereby reducing the overall effectiveness of government organizations.

The primary objective of this research is to examine the influence of civil servant disciplinary policies on the effectiveness of government operations in Ternate City. The findings of this study are anticipated to offer theoretical contributions, particularly enriching the literature on public administration and social sciences. Practically, the results aim to inform policymakers—especially those within the Ternate City government and associated stakeholders—by providing insights to address practical challenges related to civil servant management. Enhancing work discipline among civil servants is expected to yield beneficial effects on improving organizational effectiveness within governmental bodies.

The study concludes that, while the Secretariat and staffing agencies in Ternate City exhibit a reasonable level of effectiveness, it remains suboptimal. Statistical analysis reveals a significant and contributory relationship between employee discipline and governmental effectiveness within these agencies. Based on these findings, it is recommended that measures be taken to raise awareness regarding disciplinary adherence, strengthen supervisory mechanisms, and implement robust functional monitoring within the government. Furthermore, activating and enhancing functional training programs is advised to improve the quality of human resources, thus optimizing employee work discipline and bolstering institutional effectiveness.

This study aims to quantify the water requirements of cucumber plants cultivated in a mixture of soil and wood charcoal within polyester containers and to investigate the impact of wood-based growing media on cucumber growth. The experimental design employed a completely randomized layout comprising three soil-to-charcoal ratio treatments alongside a control treatment without charcoal. Specifically, treatment A consisted of a soil-to-charcoal ratio of 4:1, treatment B of 3:2, treatment C of 2:2, and treatment K as the control with soil only. Each treatment was replicated four times, resulting in a total of sixteen experimental units. Analysis of variance revealed significant differences in the volume of irrigation water applied during cucumber growth across treatments, with mean values recorded as follows: treatment A (4:1) at 10,035.33 ml, treatment B (3:2) at 10,698.33 ml, treatment C (2:2) at 11,060 ml, and the control treatment K at 8,716.67 ml. Conversely, no statistically significant differences were observed concerning plant growth parameters or fruit yield among the treatments. The findings suggest that incorporating wood charcoal into the growing medium influences water consumption patterns and affects cucumber development.

Government Accounting Standards (SAP) serve as guidelines for the preparation and presentation of financial statements within government entities, aiming to promote transparency and accountability at both central and regional levels. These standards are codified in Government Regulation No. 71 of 2010. This study seeks to assess the implementation of PSAP No. 02, which pertains to the presentation of the budget realization report, as prepared by the Secretariat Office of the Manado City Regional House of Representatives (DPRD), evaluating its conformity with Government Regulation No. 71 of 2010 on government accounting standards. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, the research utilized interviews and document analysis as data collection techniques. The findings reveal that the Manado City DPRD Secretariat Office has incorporated expenditure categories, surplus/deficit, and the remaining budget financing (either excess or shortfall) within a single reporting period. However, revenue accounts are not reflected since the Secretariat functions solely as a user of Regional Original Income (PAD). Additionally, accounts related to transfers, financing receipts, financing expenditures, and net financing are excluded due to the Secretariat’s lack of financing and transfer activities. This approach aligns with SAP requirements concerning the content of the Budget Realization Report, as the Manado City DPRD Secretariat applies accounting categories strictly based on operational necessity.

This study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of education and training programs for civil servants in enhancing the performance of personnel within the Regional Employment Board (BKD) of Ternate City. Specifically, it aims to ascertain whether such educational and training initiatives contribute significantly to improving apparatus performance in this context. Employing a qualitative research methodology, data were collected through interviews with ten informants, comprising both structural officials and staff members engaged in operational roles at BKD Ternate. The data analysis was conducted using the interactive qualitative analysis model developed by Miles and Huberman.

Findings indicate that (1) civil servant training programs—encompassing structural/leadership, technical, and functional training—effectively enhance competencies related to knowledge, skills, and attitudes; (2) these training programs also positively influence personality development, ethical standards, moral values, and cognitive dynamism among personnel; and (3) the training confers practical benefits by improving task execution efficiency, timely completion of duties, resource management, responsiveness to evolving work demands, decision-making capabilities, and problem-solving in operational contexts.

Based on these results, it can be concluded that the education and training of civil servants play a critical role in advancing the performance of personnel at the Regional Employment Board in Ternate. This suggests a positive correlation between the extent and quality of training undertaken and the enhancement of apparatus performance.

In light of the findings, several recommendations are proposed: (1) the improvement and expansion of both structural and technical/functional training programs are imperative, particularly given the currently limited budget allocation (APBD) for such initiatives, which remains insufficient; (2) training programs should be aligned with the specific needs and responsibilities corresponding to various organizational levels, grounded in thorough analyses at organizational, job/position, and individual levels, adhering to the principles of organizational development.

**Keywords:** civil servant training, apparatus performance

This study seeks to identify the potential types of parasitoids affecting the egg parasitoid *S. nubila* on Salibabu Island, located within the Talaud Islands. The investigation was carried out over a four-month period, from October 2014 to January 2015, at coconut plantations managed by local farmers on Salibabu Island. Employing a survey methodology, research was conducted across four districts: Salibabu, Kalongan, Lirung, and Moronge. Within each district, three sampling sites were systematically selected. Sampling followed a diagonal pattern, with each site subdivided into five sub-locations. Egg samples were collected from a circular area with a 0.5-meter diameter, and observations were divided into four cardinal sectors: North, East, South, and West. Sampling was performed six times, at intervals of twice per month.

The results indicated that parasitization of the egg samples was exclusively attributed to a single parasitoid species, subsequently identified as *Leefmansia bicolor*. The parasitization rates of eggs by *L. bicolor* varied across districts, with the highest average percentage recorded in the Lirung district at 26.54%, followed by Moronge (17.68%), Kalongan (13.03%), and Salibabu (4.20%). Additionally, analysis based on wind direction revealed that the Eastern sector exhibited the highest average parasitization rate (32.35%), with progressively lower rates observed in the Western (13.39%), Southern (10.25%), and Northern (5.45%) sectors.

Keywords: parasitization, *Sexava nubila*, *Leefmansia bicolor*, Salibabu, Talaud Islands

In English grammar, verbs are categorized into two primary subclasses: lexical verbs and auxiliary verbs. Auxiliary verbs, functioning as helping verbs, serve a grammatical role in constructing verb phrases and enhancing their semantic content. This study aims to describe and analyze the auxiliary verbs present in the albums *Overexposed* and *V* by Maroon 5. The objective is to classify and identify the forms, meanings, and functions of auxiliary verbs utilized within the lyrical content of these albums. Employing a descriptive research method, the data comprising auxiliary verbs were extracted from the album lyrics and examined using Hudson’s theoretical framework. Findings indicate that the auxiliary verbs identified in both albums fall into two categories: primary auxiliary verbs (such as am, is, are, was, were) and modal auxiliary verbs (including can, could, may, might, will, would, should). Notably, auxiliaries such as must, shall, be to, used to, need, be supposed to, and dare were not observed in either album. Regarding semantic analysis, primary auxiliary verbs do not convey independent meanings, whereas modal auxiliary verbs possess distinct meanings contingent upon context. Specifically, can and could express ability or inability in their negative forms; may denotes possibility; will conveys willingness, situational representation, promise, or agreement; would signifies willingness; and should indicates obligation.

Keywords: auxiliary verb, Overexposed, V

The Quality of Work Life (QWL) concept represents a management system designed to harness and align the potential of human resources by simultaneously addressing the needs of both organizational members and the institution in a continuous manner. This study aims to examine the impact of Quality of Work Life on employee performance at PT. Flammable Bank Headquarters. Employing a quantitative research methodology, the primary variables investigated include Quality of Work Life (X) and Employee Performance (Y). The study population comprised 150 employees of PT. Bank of North Sulawesi. Applying Slovin’s formula with a 10% margin of error, a sample size of 60 individuals was determined. Data were collected via questionnaires and analyzed through simple linear regression and correlation techniques, yielding statistically significant results. Hypothesis testing was conducted using the t-test, with the criterion for rejecting the null hypothesis (H₀) set as t_calculated > t_critical, and for accepting the alternative hypothesis (H₁) as t_calculated < t_critical. The computed t-value was 5.3454. Given a two-tailed test at a 5% significance level and degrees of freedom (df) equal to n-2, the critical t-value was found to be 1.67. Since the calculated t-value exceeds the critical value (5.3454 > 1.67), the null hypothesis is rejected. These findings indicate a significant positive effect of Quality of Work Life on employee performance at PT. Bank of North Sulawesi.  

Keywords: Quality of Work Life, Employee Performance

This study aimed to characterize the physical dimensions and related properties of cocoa beans from two clone varieties, 45 and Sulawesi 01. Specifically, measurements were taken of bean length, width, and thickness, as well as the average arithmetic and geometric diameters, sphericity, porosity, bulk density (density of kamba), angle of repose, and angle of friction. An experimental approach was employed, and the resulting data were analyzed descriptively. Findings indicated that, on average, the Klon 45 variety exhibited a length of 27.25 mm, width of 14.35 mm, thickness of 7.25 mm, arithmetic diameter of 16.28 mm, geometric diameter of 14.03 mm, and sphericity of 0.52. In contrast, the Sulawesi 01 variety showed a length of 20.44 mm, width of 12.29 mm, thickness of 7.52 mm, arithmetic diameter of 13.46 mm, geometric diameter of 12.32 mm, and sphericity of 0.60. The porosity of clone 45 was measured at 30.62%, with a bulk density of 0.44 g/ml, and a hundred-seed weight of 95.39 g. In comparison, the Sulawesi 01 variety demonstrated a porosity of 29.62%, bulk density of 0.51 g/ml, and a hundred-seed weight of 144.72 g. Regarding flow properties, the angle of repose for clone 45 was 29.96º at a moisture content of 9.19%, whereas for Sulawesi 01 it was 23.07º at 7.57% moisture content. This study aimed to identify the presence of Aeromonas species in a tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) culture pond located in Matungkas Village, Dimembe District, North Minahasa Regency. The bacterial identification procedures were conducted at the Fish Quarantine Center’s Laboratory for Quality and Safety Control of Fishery Products in Manado. The research was carried out over the period from February to June 2021. Ten fish samples exhibiting clinical symptoms indicative of bacterial infection—such as pallid body surface, erythematous spots, and ulcerations—were collected from three different ponds. From these samples, a total of 19 bacterial isolates were obtained for further analysis. Identification was performed through a series of bacteriological assays including Gram staining and various biochemical tests: motility, oxidase, oxidative-fermentative metabolism, and tolerance to incubation temperature, pH variations, and NaCl concentration, in addition to testing on Rimler-Shotts selective medium. Among the 19 isolates derived from the 10 samples, seven were confirmed as Aeromonas hydrophila (designated N1.4.1, N2.1.1, N2.1.2, N2.2.1, N2.3.2, N3.3.1, and N3.3.2), whereas the remaining twelve isolates tested negative for this species. The isolates identified as A. hydrophila exhibited characteristic features including creamy coloration, Gram-negative staining, oxidase positivity, motility, and fermentative metabolism. They demonstrated tolerance to incubation temperatures of 4 °C and 37 °C, but not at 50 °C. Regarding pH tolerance, these isolates did not survive at pH 3, but tolerated pH levels of 5, 9, and 11. Similarly, they exhibited positive growth at NaCl concentrations of 0.5% and 3%, but not at 5%. Additionally, the isolates tested positive on Rimler-Shotts medium. The findings indicate that all sampled ponds in Matungkas Village were contaminated with Aeromonas hydrophila.

An effective approach to fostering national economic growth is through the development of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). This study aims to examine the application of financial reporting practices at CV. M'ars Studio, specifically focusing on the preparation of the statement of financial position (balance sheet) at the end of the period, the income statement for the period, and the notes to financial statements, all in accordance with the EMKM SAK ETAP standards. The study’s subject is the implementation of EMKM Financial Accounting Standards at CV. M'ars Studio. Employing a qualitative research design, the methodology is primarily descriptive and involves the collection of primary data through interviews with the company’s owners and administrators, as well as direct observations conducted at the studio. Additionally, secondary data were gathered through library research and documentary analysis of materials possessed by CV. M'ars Studio. Findings reveal that several IFRS elements tailored for MSMEs have yet to be adopted by the company. While the balance sheet remains relatively simple, its preparation is reasonably adequate; similarly, the income statement largely complies with the relevant standards, indicating satisfactory implementation. However, the notes to the financial statements have not been prepared. A significant challenge identified in applying the SAK EMKM relates to insufficient dissemination of information concerning the specific IFRS requirements applicable to MSMEs.

Abstract:  
The Hajj constitutes a compulsory religious duty for Muslims who possess the physical and financial capacity to undertake it at least once in their lifetime. This pilgrimage is conducted annually in Makkah Al-Mukarramah, Saudi Arabia, on the 10th of Dzulhijjah. Organizing and restructuring the Hajj administration is a complex endeavor that seeks to meet the satisfaction of all stakeholders involved. This study employed a qualitative research methodology, focusing on the Hajj Management Office at the Regional Office of the Ministry of Religion in North Sulawesi Province, pilgrims from the 2013 to 2015 seasons, and various Islamic organizations. Data were collected through interviews with 15 informants, comprising four staff members from the Regional Office of the Ministry of Religion (SISKOHAT), two representatives from BPS-BPIH, six pilgrims from the 2013–2015 period, and three religious leaders or community figures. The primary objective of this research was to examine the management quality of the Hajj organization in North Sulawesi Province, which was found to be suboptimal. Consequently, the study emphasizes the necessity to enhance management roles and improve public understanding related to pilgrimage administration and services. The findings indicate a need for increased socialization efforts, infrastructure development, and professional capacity building among personnel engaged in Hajj organization.  
Keywords: Management; Hajj Organization; Pilgrimage Administration; North Sulawesi.

Abstract:  
The Regional Market Company of Tomohon City functions as an institution responsible for public service, specifically catering to marketers operating within Tomohon's traditional market. This organization is tasked with revitalizing the traditional market to enhance its competitiveness against modern retail outlets, with the broader objective of fostering economic growth through economic empowerment. The ultimate goal is to develop the Tomohon market into a professional, beneficial, and autonomous entity. The impact of these efforts is evident in the achievements attained by the Tomohon market, as perceived by the local community. Employee professionalism is a critical factor readily assessed through the quality of public services delivered. Conversely, substandard public service often indicates a lack of professionalism and low employee performance.  

This study aims to examine the professionalism of employees within the Regional Market Company of Tomohon City in delivering public services to marketers. Employing a qualitative research approach, primary data were gathered via in-depth interviews with fifteen informants, including the President Director, General Manager, division heads, staff members, and marketers. Secondary data comprised relevant organizational documents such as decrees, primary tasks and functions, organizational charts, service procedures, work reports, and other materials pertinent to employee professionalism and public service. Data analysis involved categorization and reduction techniques.  

Findings indicate that while employees have contributed to public service delivery, there remains a significant need for improvement in their professionalism. Notably, employees demonstrate limited creativity, innovation, and responsibility in their daily tasks. Moreover, they exhibit inflexibility and a tendency to await instructions rather than acting proactively. It is recommended that technical training be enhanced to optimize service provision for marketers. Furthermore, fostering employee innovation aligned with advancements in modern technology and reinforcing accountability is essential to elevate the quality of public services. Additionally, mechanisms should be established to effectively incorporate marketers' aspirations and address their grievances.  

Keywords: Professionalism, Creativity, Innovation, Responsiveness

Abstract:  
In various industries in Manado, the personal characteristics of leaders play a crucial role in defining their leadership functions. This study aims to identify the factors influencing workers’ perceptions of leadership roles within different industries in Manado, including PT Astra Isuzu International Manado (automobile distribution), Multimart (retail), Girsafotocopy and Print (printing services), and WarungBendito (restaurant). The research employs a causal research design, characterized by its quantitative methodology and structured approach, focusing on explaining cause-and-effect relationships among variables. Conducted in Manado, North Sulawesi, during the first semester of 2018, this investigation utilizes primary data collected through questionnaires administered to a sample of 230 respondents, thus classifying it as field research. Statistical analyses indicate that neither task assignment nor personal characteristics have a significant impact on the leadership roles of managers in the examined industries. This finding suggests that the manner in which leaders delegate tasks does not influence their personal character, whether positive or negative. Organizations throughout Manado should consider these results carefully, as possessing commendable leadership qualities is essential for strengthening the relationship between leaders and employees, which in turn fosters a more conducive work environment.  

Keywords: effective leadership, task assignment, personal characteristics, professional characteristics, attitude

The objective of this research is to identify product flow, financial flow, information flow. And analyze the level of marketing efficiency in the coconut supply chain. The research was carried out from June to August 2021. The data collected were primary data obtained from farmers and traders using questionnaires, internet secondary data, and the Sangkub Satu Village Office. Sampling using purposive sampling method as many as 24 people from 52 farmers, and snowball sampling method as many as 24 farmers and 3 traders. The research result showed that (1). Coconut supply chain in the channel Farmers-Collectors-Factory based on product flow flowing from upstream to downstream where farmers process coconut into copra and sell copra to traders, traders sell copra to factories, financial flows flow from downstream to upstream where factories buy copra with a transaction via banks to traders and traders buy copra with transactions directly to farmers, the first flow of information on the direction of the factory informs copra quality and price to traders, traders informs copra prices to farmers. The second flow of information is the two farmers to inform the copra quality to trader and the trader will inform the factory the amount of copra to the factory. (2). The level of marketing efficiency in the coconut supply chain is seen from marketing margins, costs and profits, farmers and traders who have been efficient.

Eating habits encompass behaviors related to food, including meal frequency, dietary patterns, food distribution within the family, and food selection criteria. The present research aimed to elucidate the dietary patterns of residents within the Allandrew Malalayang I environment, specifically in the XI Manado city urban community. This study employed a descriptive design utilizing a survey methodology. The target population comprised 480 individuals aged 25 to 55 years residing in the Permai housing area of Allandrew XI. From this population, a sample of 90 respondents was selected using systematic and random sampling techniques. Data collection was conducted through structured interviews based on a pre-prepared questionnaire. The findings revealed consumption rates for various food items as follows: rice (55%), bread (38.9%), soybean (78.9%), tofu (97.8%), fish (55.6%), chicken meat (34.4%), pork (65.5%), vegetables (70%), fruits (28.9%), fried bananas (46%), crepes (50%), malabar (47.8%), tea (52.2%), coffee (37%), and milk (18.9%). In conclusion, the study determined that the staple foods most frequently consumed were rice and bread; vegetable protein sources primarily included tempeh and tofu; animal protein sources consisted of fish, chicken, and pork; and commonly consumed vegetables, fruits, and side dishes included items such as fried bananas, martabak, and malabar. Beverages commonly consumed comprised tea, coffee, and milk.  
Keywords: Eating Habits

This study employed a descriptive research design to examine the perceptions of community leaders and cattle breeders regarding the performance of extension workers in enhancing the beef cattle farming business in Sangkub District, North Bolaang Mongondow Regency. Purposive sampling was utilized to select 30 respondents, comprising village officials, community leaders, and farmers from the villages of Sangkub 1, Tombolango, Busisingo, Pangkusa, and Sidodadi. The variables were measured according to the Likert Scale framework, assigning scores based on each respondent's answers.

The findings revealed that community leaders uniformly regarded the communication role of extension workers as highly effective, with 100% of respondents deeming it beneficial. Regarding the content of counseling sessions, 93% of respondents perceived the information as useful, while 7% remained uncertain. In terms of counseling methods, 63% of respondents found them to be effective, whereas 37% expressed doubts. Notably, all respondents (100%) considered the counseling aids to be ineffective. Concerning the target group of the counseling, 93% rated it favorably, and 3% were uncertain. Moreover, the timing and location of counseling activities were rated positively by all respondents. Lastly, the benefits of extension workers’ efforts in enhancing the beef cattle farming business were affirmed by 100% of the participants.

Correlation analysis using the Spearman rank-order model indicated a statistically significant relationship between the perceptions of community leaders and village officials and the performance of extension workers in advancing the beef cattle farming enterprise. These results underscore the critical role that extension workers play as perceived by key stakeholders within the community.

The regional head elections for the Governor and Vice Governor of North Maluku were characterized by significant conflict involving supporters competing for political power. These conflicts arose principally due to overlapping interests among factions vying to control the leadership of North Maluku. Empirical observations from the field reveal several key stages during which conflict intensified. 

Firstly, tensions emerged at the candidate registration phase, where applicants failed to meet established eligibility criteria, specifically the requirement of securing at least 15% of the vote share and corresponding seat support. Secondly, during the campaign period, disputes further escalated, notably due to protests from one candidate pair and their campaign team regarding the election schedule, some of which coincided with Ramadan and Eid observances. Nevertheless, the dissemination of information about subsequent campaign phases was generally accepted by all parties. 

Thirdly, the stages of vote counting and tabulation witnessed the most overt and prolonged confrontations. This was largely attributable to political elites prioritizing their individual interests over negotiation and conflict resolution, resulting in a zero-sum approach that disregarded procedural fairness and facilitated various tactics aimed at securing electoral victory. Ultimately, the 2007 gubernatorial election conflicts concluded only after the Supreme Court (Mahkamah Agung) issued a definitive ruling on the winner, while the Constitutional Court (Mahkamah Konstitusi) dismissed jurisdictional disputes submitted by the North Maluku Provincial Election Commission (KPUD). 

The genesis of these election conflicts can be attributed to the strategic maneuvers of political elites who acted as patrons for their respective supporter groups. To mitigate the risk of violent power struggles, political elites aiming to assume office must adopt approaches that prevent such conflict dynamics.

Keywords: political elite, supporters, conflict

This study seeks to identify issues related to the accountability of activities at the Regional Employment Board (BKD) of North Sulawesi. It also aims to establish a mutual understanding between the Inspectorate auditors and BKD North Sulawesi concerning the accountability of expenditures on food and beverages, ensuring alignment with the programs and activities outlined in the DPA SKPD. Such alignment is intended to prevent errors during the documentation process of accountability related to activity implementation. The research focuses on the Regional Employment Board of North Sulawesi Province and the North Sulawesi Provincial Inspectorate. The sample comprises twelve individuals selected from various roles, including the Treasurer of Expenditures at BKD North Sulawesi and DKP North Sulawesi, the Head of the Planning and Finance Subdivision at both BKD and DKP, BKD staff involved in treasury and verification functions, as well as auditors and officials responsible for Functional Implementation Supervisory Affairs of Regional Government (P2UPD) within the North Sulawesi Provincial Inspectorate. Primary data were collected through interviews conducted with these participants. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study’s findings reveal discrepancies in the understanding of accountability practices related to food and beverage budget expenditures between BKD North Sulawesi personnel and Inspectorate auditors. Additionally, challenges were identified concerning communication and insufficient comprehension of the relevant regulations.

In the contemporary context of globalization, the business sector is experiencing rapid growth, particularly within the culinary industry. The proliferation of enterprises in this domain has led to an increase in businesses offering similar products or services, thereby intensifying competitive dynamics. In light of the identified issues and research questions, the objectives of this study are articulated as follows: (1) to examine the impact of the physical environment of Sarina Kawangkoan Coffee House on consumer emotions, and (2) to investigate the influence of the social environment of the same establishment on consumer emotions. This study employs an explanatory research design, which aims to describe and elucidate the relationship between two variables—the independent and dependent variables—by analyzing the nature and extent of their interaction. Multiple linear regression analysis was utilized as the primary technique for data evaluation. The study’s findings reveal that (1) the physical environment does not exert a statistically significant effect on customer emotions at Rumah Kopi Sarina Kawangkoan; (2) the social environment similarly lacks a significant influence on customer emotions at this location; however, (3) when considered together, the physical and social environments significantly affect customer emotions at Rumah Kopi Sarina Kawangkoan.  
Keywords: service environment, customer emotions

Abstract The Covid-19 pandemic has caused many restrictions on almost all routine services, including restrictions on maternal and neonatal health services. The purpose of this study was to determine the relationship between the health literacy of pregnant women and preparation for childbirth during the Covid-19 pandemic at the Tuminting Health Center in Manado City. Statistical test showed p value = 0.026. The conclusion is that there is a relationship between the health literacy of pregnant women and preparation for delivery at the Tuminting Health Center in Manado City

White copra refers to the dried fruit flesh obtained through a drying process utilizing a drying apparatus, which enhances the quality of the copra by reducing its moisture content and ensuring cleanliness. This material is produced via two distinct methods: oven drying and solar dryer dome drying. The present study aims to compare the income generated from the white copra business employing these two drying techniques at JR Agro Indonesia. The data analysis involved the use of the High and Low Points method, income analysis, and the calculation of the revenue-to-cost (R/C) ratio. Findings indicate that the total production cost associated with oven drying amounted to Rp. 184,561,202, whereas the cost for solar dryer dome drying was slightly higher at Rp. 189,991,500. Both methods yielded identical total revenues of Rp. 240,000,000. Consequently, the net income derived from oven processing was Rp. 55,438,798, compared to Rp. 50,008,500 from the solar dryer dome method. The comparison reveals a difference in income between the two drying processes. Furthermore, the cost efficiency analysis produced R/C ratios of 1.30 for oven processing and 1.26 for solar dryer dome processing, indicating that both methods are economically viable and cost-efficient since the ratios exceed unity.

Abstract:  
The global mortality rate among neonates with congenital anomalies remains substantially high within the first four weeks postpartum each year. This study sought to characterize the demographic and clinical profiles of patients with congenital anomalies associated with postoperative mortality at the Pediatric Surgery Department of Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou Hospital, Manado, Indonesia. Employing a descriptive and retrospective design, the study analyzed 98 cases from 2019 to 2021. The primary outcome of interest was postoperative mortality, while sex, gestational age, birth weight, and length of hospital stay were examined as potential risk factors. Data were subjected to univariate analysis. Findings indicated a postoperative mortality rate of 27.6%, with an approximately equal distribution of sex (male 51%, female 49%). The majority of patients were term infants (77.5%) compared to preterm (22.5%). Similarly, 77.5% of neonates had a birth weight ≥2500 g, while 22.5% were classified as low birth weight (<2500 g). Most hospitalizations (82.7%) involved stays shorter than two weeks. The spectrum of congenital anomalies treated surgically included anorectal malformations (41.7%), Hirschsprung disease (15.1%), lateral inguinal hernias (11.3%), undescended testis (4.1%), ileojejunal atresia (4.1%), invagination (4.1%), esophageal atresia (5.1%), diaphragm hernia (3.1%), duodenal atresia (3.1%), mechanical bowel obstruction (3.1%), omphalocele (2.1%), gastroschisis (2.1%), and biliary atresia (1%). In summary, over the past two years, the pediatric surgical management of congenital anomalies exhibited an overall postoperative mortality rate of 27.6%, with no significant sex predominance. The majority of patients were term neonates of normal birth weight, presenting with relatively brief hospital stays.  

Keywords: congenital anomalies; postoperative mortality; pediatric surgery; neonatal outcomes

The concept of performance management has been incorporated into a government agency’s performance accountability system, characterized by a systematic and continuous process. The implementation of this system within government agencies encompasses performance planning, measurement, reporting, and evaluation, with the objective of enhancing accountability for governmental performance. This study examines the performance management practices of the West Halmahera District Secretariat in relation to the Government Agency Performance Accountability System (SAKIP), employing the theoretical framework of the Performance Management Cycle. Utilizing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews with seven purposively selected informants and relevant documentary sources. Analysis was conducted through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing or data verification. Findings reveal that although the West Halmahera District Secretariat has adopted the performance management framework, each phase remains suboptimal. Specifically, performance planning documents exhibited low quality, performance measurements were misaligned with targets, performance reporting was delayed, and internal evaluations were inadequately executed. Consequently, the overall performance accountability of the Secretariat has not met satisfactory standards. To address these challenges, the study suggests strategies including enhancing the quality of performance planning documents, providing technical training and guidance to improve human resource capabilities, and conducting more frequent internal evaluations to promptly address recommendations arising from work program assessments. 

Keywords: Performance Management, SAKIP

The Covid-19 pandemic has severely impacted Indonesia's economy, with the tourism sector being particularly affected. Marketing research within the tourism and hospitality industries offers valuable insights into individuals' motivations for visiting specific destinations, choosing particular accommodations, or purchasing related products, thereby aiding the recovery of these sectors. This study seeks to explore the factors that motivate individuals to stay at five-star hotels in Bali and to examine whether Social Media Influencers (SMIs) exert a moderating influence on the intention to stay at such establishments. Employing a non-probability sampling strategy with purposive sampling as the technique, data were collected from a sample of 100 respondents. The analysis was conducted using path analysis via the SEM-PLS application. The findings indicate that both attitude toward the brand and brand image do not significantly influence the intention to stay at a five-star hotel. In contrast, brand trust was found to have a significant positive effect on this intention. Regarding the moderating role of SMIs, the results reveal that SMIs do not moderate the relationship between brand evaluation variables (brand trust, brand image, and attitude toward the brand) and the intention to stay at the hotel. However, SMIs were identified as having a significant direct effect on the intention to stay at the hotel when considered as an independent variable.

This study aimed to investigate the composition and diversity of macrobenthic organisms inhabiting aggregations of Septifer bilocularis shellfish in the coastal waters of Tiwoho, North Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi. Macrobenthos samples were collected using a PVC core sampler at three distinct aggregation sites: small aggregation (AK), medium-large aggregation (ABT), and large edge aggregation (ABP). Sampling was conducted four times across the different shellfish aggregations. The collected data were analyzed through the Diversity Index (H), Dominance Index (D), and Evenness Index (E). Results revealed the presence of 25 macrobenthic taxa across all septifer bilocularis aggregations, representing 11 taxonomic classes, including Gastropoda, Bivalvia, Malacostraca, Florideophyceae, Ulvophyceae, Ophiuroidea, Clitellata, Maxillopoda, Globothalamea, Tubothalamea, and Phaeophyceae. The diversity index values ranged from 1.60 to 1.70, indicating moderate species diversity within each aggregation. Evenness indices varied slightly, with values of 0.069, 0.066, and 0.064 for the small (AK), medium-large (ABT), and large edge (ABP) aggregations, respectively, suggesting low uniformity among macrobenthic communities within the aggregations. The dominance index across all sites ranged between 0.27 and 0.36, signifying the absence of any single species dominance in the macrobenthic populations associated with the different shellfish aggregations.

Keywords: Diversity, Macrobenthos, Septifer bilocularis, Tiwoho

ABSTRACT Information on agricultural machinery and equipment is required for the development of agricultural technology in Indonesia. Although Indonesia is known as an agricultural country, its agricultural technology is considered less developed compared to many other non-agricultural countries. One reason behind this is the dissemination of information regarding agricultural machinery and equipment still believed asunstructured and fragmented. Advancement in information and communication technology has made easiness for people in accessing information. Android operating system is gaining more and more popularity and its userin Indonesia is growingfast. This research aims to develop an Android based practical learning application on agricultural machinery and equipment. This research was carried out during the month of April 2015 to June 2015 and the resulted application was successfully installed in Android as a 1.8 Mb APK file format. The application was tested on CPU emulator and Andromax smartphone followed by a survey to 16 respondents using questionnaire having 10 questions in it (5 questions for application and 5 other questions for content of application). The respondents, who marked each question with 1=very disagree; 2=disagree; 3=neutral; 4=agree; 5=very agree, consist of 10 university students, 3 university lecturers, 1 representing farmer, 1 consultant in agricultural machinery and equipment, and 1 representingcommon people. Results of the test conclude that this Android application can be implemented as information media to improve awareness of public and university students regarding agricultural machinery and equipment in a quicker and a more efficient way. The application can also help disseminating information regarding agricultural machinery and equipment in a more variety way in order to support the development of agricultural technology in Indonesia.

Agroforestry is a land-use system that integrates forestry crops (woody perennials) with agricultural crops, livestock, or fisheries within a single land unit. To date, there has been no documented information regarding agroforestry patterns in Togid Village, Tutuyan District, East Bolaang Mongondow Regency. This study aims to elucidate the agroforestry patterns practiced in Togid Village, Tutuyan District, East Bolaang Mongondow Regency, as observed in February 2021. The research employed field surveys, interviews, and data collection methods. Respondents were selected through purposive sampling based on criteria identifying farmers who implement agroforestry systems in their gardens. The collected data were analyzed descriptively and presented in tabular format. Findings reveal two primary agroforestry patterns utilized by the farmers: the agrisilvicultural pattern and the agrosilvopasture-fishery pattern. Among the 14 respondents, nine distinct combinations of plant, animal, and fish components were identified across their garden plots. Specifically, one garden plot was managed using the agrosilvopasture-fishery pattern, while the remaining 13 employed the agrisilvicultural pattern. In gardens incorporating woody plants, food crops were present in eight plots, spice plants in nine, ornamental plants in three, fodder sources for caged livestock in four, and fish in one garden. The presence of agroforestry systems within Togid Village contributes substantially to the local community, yielding significant economic and ecological benefits.

Keywords: Agroforestry patterns, Togid Village

Agrosilvopasture, a component of agroforestry systems, presents a viable land management strategy to address challenges such as food availability, limited land ownership, and declining soil fertility. This system integrates woody perennial plants with seasonal agricultural crops and concurrently incorporates livestock grazing on the same parcel of land. Sumarayar Village, situated in East Langowan District, Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi Province, predominantly comprises farmers, many of whom also engage in livestock herding. This study aims to examine the patterns of agrosilvopasture practiced in Sumarayar Village and to evaluate the associated benefits and limitations of these practices. Employing a survey methodology that includes interviews and direct field observations, findings reveal that in Sumarayar Village, annual woody plants are cultivated along land boundaries and serve as barriers for food crops. The implementation of agrosilvopasture yields enhanced productivity by enabling the simultaneous presence of trees, crops, and livestock on a single land unit, thereby increasing income. However, a notable challenge lies in the difficulty of accurately measuring productivity, as agricultural economists often rely on conventional farming models that do not account for the diverse species of trees and shrubs with unclear economic valuations inherent in agroforestry systems.

Keywords: Agrosilvopasture, Sumarayar Village, East Langowan District

Murabaha is a sale and purchase contract wherein the selling price of goods is determined by adding an agreed profit margin to the cost price, which the seller is obliged to disclose to the buyer. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the internal control system implemented at BRI Syariah KC Manado, specifically assessing its adherence to the COSO (Committee of Sponsoring Organizations) framework principles. Employing a descriptive analytical approach, the research compares data obtained through observations, interviews, and document analysis with relevant theoretical constructs. Data were collected via interviews, direct observation, and review of documentation. The findings indicate that the internal control mechanisms for Murabaha financing at BRI Syariah KC Manado encompass management-established policies, the organizational structure, standardized forms and documents utilized in Murabaha transactions, proper recording of legitimate financing activities, and ongoing monitoring procedures. Overall, the internal control system demonstrates satisfactory functionality; however, certain deficiencies were identified that may impede optimal implementation. Notably, the occurrence of employees performing multiple roles contravenes COSO principles, which emphasize the need for employee competence and specialization. Consequently, it is recommended that BRI Syariah KC Manado enhance personnel qualifications to strengthen internal control efficacy. In conclusion, the internal control system at BRI Syariah KC Manado can be regarded as generally consistent with COSO principles.  
 
Keywords: COSO, Murabaha financing, internal control system

Hepatitis B is a viral disease characterized by inflammation primarily affecting organs such as the liver. The transmission rate of Hepatitis B exceeds that of the HIV virus. This study aimed to examine the demographic characteristics and medication usage patterns among Hepatitis B patients at a Government Hospital in Manado. Employing a descriptive research design, data were retrospectively collected over a two-year period, from January 2011 to December 2012. A total of 70 patient medical records diagnosed with Hepatitis B were included in the analysis. Findings revealed that the highest proportion of patients belonged to the 46-65 age group, accounting for 44.3% (31 patients). Males represented the majority of the sample with 67.1% (47 patients). Regarding treatment duration, the most common was a single-day course, observed in 30% (21 patients) of cases. Therapeutically, treatment modalities were classified into two main categories: single-agent therapy with Hepamax, comprising 38.6% (27 patients), and combination therapy involving Hepamax and Curcuma, representing 12.9% (9 patients). All administered treatments were delivered exclusively via the oral route.  

**Keywords:** Hepatitis B, Hepatitis B medication, Single-agent therapy, Combination therapy

Professional judgment constitutes an essential component of financial statement audits, primarily because auditing standards offer auditors limited detailed guidance or specific criteria regarding methods, techniques, or approaches to be employed. Although auditors are expected to exercise judgment through deliberate and reasoned analysis, there exists the potential for them to deviate from such systematic processes, instead relying on heuristic shortcuts in their decision-making. This study seeks to investigate the presence of cognitive biases within auditors’ judgments and to identify the heuristics that contribute to these biases. Employing a qualitative research methodology grounded in ethnomethodology, data were gathered through in-depth semi-structured interviews conducted with 15 auditors occupying various roles—including partners, managers, seniors, and juniors—within a public accounting firm. Utilizing the heuristic-bias framework as an analytical lens, and applying a systematic process encompassing data condensation, data display, as well as conclusion drawing and verification, the study uncovers five distinct types of biases that auditors may exhibit: jumping to conclusions, groupthink, representativeness, availability, and anchoring biases. The findings yield practical implications for auditors, professional accounting bodies, public accounting firms, and academic institutions by offering insights that can inform the development of strategies aimed at enhancing auditors’ awareness of potential systematic errors introduced by heuristic-based judgment processes.

This study seeks to examine the impact of brand image on consumers' purchasing interest in Oriflame products within Manado City. Employing a quantitative research design, the investigation targets residents of Manado City who have previously purchased and used Oriflame products as its population. The sampling method applied is non-probability sampling. Due to the unknown total population size, the sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula, as adapted from Isac Michael’s theory, resulting in a sample of 100 respondents. To assess instrument validity, the Product Moment Correlation technique was utilized, while reliability was measured using the Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient. Regression analysis and hypothesis testing revealed a statistically significant positive effect of brand image on purchasing interest, indicated by a significance value of 0.000. This implies that improvements in brand image are associated with increased purchasing interest. The adjusted R-squared value of 0.382 suggests that 38.2% of the variability in purchasing interest can be explained by brand image, whereas the remaining 61.8% is attributable to factors beyond the scope of this model. In conclusion, the findings demonstrate that brand image positively influences consumer buying interest in Oriflame products in Manado City.

Observation show that K treatment with a concentration of (0 %) is known not to show an average mortality, compared to treatment C (50 %) it is known that the average mortality in each replication is 56,25 %, on treatment B (60 %) it is known that the average mortality in each replication is 67,5 %, and on treatment A (70 %) it is known that the average mortality in each replication is 86,25 %. Waste can be categorized into two types based on its material composition: organic waste, originating from animal, plant, and human sources, and inorganic waste, which consists of materials such as metal, glass, styrofoam, plastic, and rubber. Among the various forms of coastal pollution, inorganic waste poses a significant environmental challenge. However, there remains a paucity of data regarding inorganic waste within mangrove ecosystems, particularly in Lesah Village, Tagulandang Subdistrict, Sitaro Regency. This study seeks to elucidate the spatial distribution of inorganic waste by type and to characterize this waste in terms of its quantity, size, and weight. Employing the line transect method across three distinct sampling stations, the investigation identified several categories of marine debris, including plastic, rubber, metal, and glass. The debris was further classified into two size-based categories: mega-debris and macro-debris. Among these, plastic materials were the most prevalent, with 161 items recorded over an area of 23.329 m² (equivalent to 69,099 items per hectare), totaling 1,357.75 grams per hectare in weight and 1,938.93 centimeters per hectare in size. Rubber debris was less abundant, with 5 items per 23.329 m² (2,146 items per hectare), weighing 159.309 grams per hectare and measuring 59.871 centimeters per hectare. Glass debris comprised 4 items per 23.329 m² (1,717 items per hectare), with a weight of 402.159 grams per hectare and a size of 31.030 centimeters per hectare. Metal debris was recorded as the least common, with 3 items per 23.329 m² (1,288 items per hectare), a total weight of 67.622 grams per hectare, and a total size of 19.528 centimeters per hectare. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the composition and distribution of inorganic waste within the mangrove ecosystem of Desa Lesah.

Keywords: Inorganic waste, Mangrove ecosystem, Desa Lesah

The Bugis tribe possesses a fundamental value or philosophy known as Siri' (shame), commonly referred to as Siri' na pesse'. This cultural principle profoundly influences various aspects of social life in South Sulawesi and, on a hierarchical level, significantly shapes the character and mentality of its people. The institution of marriage is particularly imbued with the Siri' culture, as it is regarded as a crucial occasion for families to demonstrate their dignity. This phenomenon is evident among the Bugis community in Bitung City, where the values of Siri' continue to be upheld despite modernization. Notably, the tradition of Panai' money remains a central and ideal prerequisite for marriage within the Bugis tribe. Initially, Panai' money functioned as a token of appreciation toward women; however, it has evolved into a symbol of social prestige linked to the concept of Siri'. The social status and stratification of women correspondingly determine the monetary value of the customary payment, with higher status commanding higher amounts. Consequently, Panai' money, once a cultural expression, has at times become a source of tension and anxiety. Instances of marriage cancellations occur due to disagreements over the Panai' money amount, as brides frequently insist on a specific sum. Failure to meet these demands often leads to the rejection of the marriage proposal, prompting some couples to elope, a practice known as Silariang.  
Keywords: marriage, tradition, Panai' money

THE EFFECT OF PARTLY SUBSTITUTION OF DIET WITH WHITE CHINESE CABBAGE (Brasscia pekinensia L) WASTE PRODUCT ON BIOLOGICAL PERFORMANCE OF BROILER CHICKEN The present study was conducted to characterize the effect of white Chinese cabbage (Brasscia pekinensia L) waste product as an alternative feed source for broiler chicken. The experiment was conducted at Faculty of Animal Husbandry's experimetal station for 21 days using 60 MB-202 broiler chicken. The experiment was started at 21 days of age and terminated at 42 days of age. Birds were allocated to 20 experimental battery cage, 3 birds in each cage. Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 5 treatments and 4 replications was employed to analyze experimental data. Treatment diets were formulated as follow: R0 = 100% basal diet and 0% white Chinese cabbage waste product; R1 = 95% basal diet and 5% white Chinese cabbage waste product; R2 = 90% basal diet and 10% white Chinese cabbage waste product; R3 = 85% basal diet and 15% white Chinese cabbage waste product; and R4 = 80% basal diet and 20% white Chinese cabbage waste product. Parameters measured were: 1) daily feed consumption; 2) daily gain; and 3) feed conversion ratio (FCR). The results of the study during which feed consumption (138,09-141,57g), weight gain (64,95-68,53g), and feed conversion (2,07-2,12). The results showed that partly substitution (up to 20%) of basal diet with white Chinese cabbage waste product gave non significant (P > 0.05) effect on feed consumption, daily gain, and feed conversion ratio (FCR) of broiler chicken. It can be concluded that white Chinese cabbage waste product can be used up to 20% feed gives good results on broiler performance. Key Words: Substitution, white Chinese cabbage waste product, broiler performance

The rapid expansion of settlements in the Luwuk and North Luwuk Subdistricts has significantly affected the physical characteristics of the land, thereby increasing the demand for residential land. This study aims to evaluate the carrying capacity of residential areas through the application of the building coverage concept and to examine settlement development directions based on the residential carrying capacity in these subdistricts. Employing a descriptive quantitative methodology, the research utilizes a spatial analysis approach facilitated by Geographic Information System (GIS) technology. Data analysis is conducted in accordance with the technical guidelines outlined in the Minister of Public Works Regulation No. 20/PRT/M/2007, which addresses physical, environmental, economic, and socio-cultural factors in spatial planning. The analytical procedures incorporate overlay and scoring techniques to assign values to various parameters. Findings indicate that the carrying capacity assessment supports the establishment of protected zones grounded in environmental physical conditions. Specifically, in Luwuk District, settlement development directions for Class 1 correspond to 20.16 hectares with a 48% land cover ratio, while in North Luwuk District, the figures are 176.60 hectares with a 42% cover ratio. For Class 2, Luwuk District comprises 92.13 hectares at a 19% land cover ratio, and North Luwuk District encompasses 3,588.01 hectares at a 50% cover ratio. Class 3 areas measure 168.10 hectares with a 20% land cover ratio in Luwuk, and 1,866.62 hectares with the same cover ratio in North Luwuk. Lastly, Class 4 areas include 5,080.15 hectares with a 0% land cover ratio in Luwuk, and 23,355.84 hectares with a 0% cover ratio in North Luwuk District.

Broilers were became consumer preference significantly at the Pinasungkulan Market, meaning that there was difference of consumer preference on broiler attributes. Sequences of broiler attribute from the highest consideration to the lowest consideration were meat color, skin color, meat smell, skin tenderness and meat weight. The banking sector plays a crucial role in the economic development of a nation. A greater number of financial institutions within a country typically correlates with an improved economic performance. This improvement is largely attributed to individuals with surplus funds being able to deposit their savings in banks, while those in need of capital for business initiation or expansion can obtain loans directly from nearby banking institutions that comply with specified requirements. The present study aims to examine the impact of the Muslim population, financing, and profit-sharing mechanisms on the nominal amount of savings within Islamic banking in Indonesia. Data were collected through surveys and subjected to analysis employing multiple linear regression techniques using SPSS version 21. The research utilized secondary data obtained from internet sources and annual financial reports of several Islamic banks in Indonesia, including PT Bank BRI Syariah, Bank Syariah Bukopin, Bank Syariah Mandiri, Bank Panin Syariah, and PT Bank Muamalat Indonesia, spanning the period from 2009 to 2013. The findings indicate that the Muslim population (X1) does not have a statistically significant effect on the nominal amount of savings (Y). In contrast, financing (X2) demonstrates a significant positive effect on the nominal amount of savings (Y). Moreover, profit-sharing results (X3) exhibit no significant influence on the nominal amount of savings (Y). 

Keywords: Muslim population impact, financing, profit-sharing, nominal savings amount, Islamic banking

The Buntudatu Pine Forest, located in Mengkendek District, Tana Toraja Regency, serves as a limited production forest designated for open nature tourism and is managed by the Buntudatu Village-Owned Enterprise (BUMDes). This site accommodates various activities, including recreation, camping, and relaxation. The objective of this study was to describe and evaluate the potential for tourism development within the Buntudatu Pine Forest, drawing upon visitor observations and perceptions. The study focused on key variables such as the attractiveness, accessibility, and infrastructure of the tourism site. Data were collected through direct observation and the distribution of questionnaires to 36 visitors present at the site. The collected data were analyzed using the Objects of Natural Tourist Attraction (ODTWA) assessment framework and the Likert scale. Findings revealed that, according to the ODTWA evaluation, the tourism potential of the Buntudatu Pine Forest received an attractiveness score of 750, placing it in the medium category; accessibility was rated with a score of 450, categorized as high; and infrastructure facilities scored 300, also in the high category. Additionally, visitor perceptions indicated that attractiveness was considered good, with a score of 72.66%; accessibility was likewise rated good, with 68.69%; facilities were deemed good, achieving 66.66%; and tourist activities were rated very good, attaining a perfect score of 100%.

Background: Physical activity is bodily movement produced by skeletal muscles and requires energy expenditure and is the fourth leading risk factor for global death. The Health Belief Model is a health behavior change theory and psychological model that is used to predict health behavior by focusing on individual perceptions and beliefs about an illness. The purpose of this research is to analyze how the implementation of physical activity based on the health belief model by health workers at Puskesmas Bahu Manado. Methods: This research was conducted using qualitative methods at Puskesmas Bahu Manado from July to August 2020, using a purposive sampling technique. The target population is all employees at Puskesmas Bahu Manado and the reachable population is representatives of the staff at Puskesmas Bahu who are informants. There were 6 informants in this study who were based on the principles of appropriateness (approppiateness) and adequacy (adequacy). The research instruments used were interview guides, notebooks, voice recorders, and cameras. Data collection was carried out by in-depth interviews and direct observation. Data analysis using content analysis. Results: The results of in-depth interviews and document observations based on the health belief model show that health workers believe that people will be motivated to take actions that will improve their health because they know the risk of diseases that negatively affect their health. Conclusion: The implementation of physical activity based on Perceived Suspectibility, Perceived Severity, Perceived Benefits, Perceived Barriers, Cues To Action and Self Efficacy by health personnel at Puskesmas Bahu has been implemented.

The current teaching and learning processes within the Agricultural Engineering Study Program at Sam Ratulangi University remain predominantly conventional. Interaction between students and lecturers is restricted to physical classroom meetings with limited availability. Consequently, the absence of such meetings impedes the continuity of the learning process. Furthermore, if a lecturer is unable to attend class for any reason, the delivery of course materials is disrupted. These factors contribute to an inefficient learning environment due to constraints related to time and location. To address these challenges, the implementation of an electronic learning system (e-learning) utilizing the Moodle Learning Management System (LMS) is proposed as a viable solution. E-learning is intended to supplement the existing conventional instructional methods within the Agricultural Engineering Study Program at Sam Ratulangi University. This study aimed to analyze and design a suitable e-learning application tailored to the needs of the program. Findings indicate that the developed system’s functionalities adequately meet the requirements necessary to support the e-learning process. Survey results from lecturers and students reveal that over 80% of respondents consider the system highly beneficial for enhancing learning activities, while more than 84% express interest in adopting the e-learning platform.

This study aims to evaluate the implementation of Smart City policies in Manado City. The research was carried out in January-July 2021. The data used were primary and secondary data. Primary data were obtained through in-depth interviews with informants who have a direct role in the implementation of the Manado Smart City policy. Secondary data were obtained through the study of documents and archives related to the implementation of Smart City Policies. The research variables used were taken from the results of the final evaluation of 96 programs included in the 6 dimensions of the Smart City of Manado City. The analytical method used was interactive data analysis through 4 stages, namely data collection, data reduction, data display and conclusions. For the analysis stage, it was focused on the final evaluation of the achievements of the Smart City program in Manado City. The results showed that the compliance of the implementor in implementing the Smart City program was not completely in accordance with the objectives of the Smart City Masterplan. The six dimensions of Smart City owned by Manado City contained 96 activity programs spread across various OPDs. Out of this 96 activities, there were 28 of them that had not been realized, and there were 35 others that had not been successfully implemented according to the indicators of success. Communication was an inhibiting factor in the implementation of the Smart City policy in Manado City, while resources, disposition and bureaucratic structure were the driving factors.

North Sulawesi province is known as one of the biggest coconut production in Indonesia. South Minahasa Regency is the biggest coconut production in the North Sulawesi Province. District of Tenga is one of major coconut production in South Minahasa Regency. Therefore, effort should be conducted in order to maintain the coconut production in District of Tenga. One effort to maintain coconut production in District of Tenga is to cultivate coconut varieties which can result high yield. High yield production of coconut can be resulted through plant breeding. In plant breeding, variation is parameter of selection that can be used to evaluate population performance of breeding material. The variation of coconut in District of Tenga has not been investigated. In order to support selection program to produce good quality of coconut varieties it is important to assess coconut population in District of Tenga. Research was conducted by collecting samples at four villages namely Tawaang, Tawaang Barat, Radey and Malinow representing in District of Tenga. Sample was collected using purposive sampling. Twenty-five sampels of coconut tree were collected at each village. Samples of coconut tree were collected using purposive sampling followed by marking of each sample. Characters observed were number of fruit per tree, number of fruit per bunch, fruit weight per bunch, fruit weight without husk per bunch, fruit weight without water per bunch, coconut shell weight per bunch and fresh fruit meat (white flesh) weight per bunch. This study aims to enhance food security by developing products through the utilization of local raw materials, independent of material type. Specifically, purse—a local ingredient rich in carbohydrates, proteins, and fats—was processed into flour due to its considerable potential for diverse product development, including its application in bread production. Conventional bread typically relies on wheat flour owing to its gluten content; however, purse flour lacks gluten and was explored as a substitute in this research. The primary objectives were to evaluate the impact of varying concentrations of purse flour on dough expansion, porosity, and overall bread quality, as well as to assess consumer acceptance and conduct chemical analyses of bread containing purse flour.

A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed in this study, with each treatment replicated three times. The treatments consisted of substituting wheat flour with purse flour at levels of 0% (control), 30%, 50%, and 70%. Parameters measured included dough expansion, porosity, moisture content, ash content, protein, fat, carbohydrate composition, and organoleptic properties through sensory evaluation.

Findings indicated that sample A, containing 70% wheat flour and 30% purse flour, exhibited a dough expansion of 2.8 cm, porosity of 31%, moisture content of 31.85%, ash content of 1.26%, fat content of 4.39%, protein content of 7.02%, and carbohydrate content of 54.57%. This formulation also achieved the highest organoleptic scores for color (3.55), odor (3.50), flavor (3.50), and texture (3.40), thus being the most favored by panelists. The substitution of wheat flour with higher concentrations of purse flour significantly influenced dough expansion, porosity, bread quality, and consumer preference. Additionally, chemical analyses revealed decreasing trends in moisture, fat, protein, carbohydrate, and ash contents with increasing levels of purse flour.

Keywords: Bread, Gluten, Purse Flour, Wheat Flour.

This study investigated the drying characteristics of corn using a hybrid dryer powered by both solar and biomass energy sources. The primary aim was to analyze variations in temperature, relative humidity, moisture content, and drying rate throughout the drying process. Employing an experimental design complemented by descriptive analysis, the research evaluated the performance of the drying system under different heat sources. Results indicated that during solar drying, the air temperature within the drying chamber was influenced by the intensity of solar radiation, with material temperature varying according to rack position. When biomass energy was utilized as the heat source, material temperature similarly fluctuated by rack location, with the highest temperatures recorded on the bottom shelf, followed by the middle and upper shelves. Relative humidity (RH) within the drying chamber changed throughout the process; specifically, the average RH during biomass heating was relatively low at 51.5%, compared to an external RH of 83.2%. In contrast, solar drying yielded an average internal RH of 66.1%, while the ambient RH averaged 84.9%. Moisture content of the corn decreased from an initial 38.6% to 6.7% (wet basis) by the end of drying. Additionally, drying rates varied by rack position, with the bottom shelf exhibiting the highest rates ranging from 0.61 to 2.68% per hour, followed by the middle shelf (0.45 to 1.72% per hour), and the top shelf showing the lowest rates (0.25 to 0.67% per hour).

Keywords: maize, solar drying, biomass energy.

This study seeks to examine the transformations in the local wisdom of Mapalus Tani within the Rurukan Satu Subdistrict of East Tomohon District. The research was conducted over a three-month period, from February to April 2019. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with various sources and informants/respondents, utilizing structured interview guides and direct questioning. A snowball sampling technique was employed to identify participants. The findings indicate that all informants reported alterations in the values, norms, and organizational structure of Mapalus Tani, although a few respondents maintained that no significant changes had occurred. Specifically, modifications in values included the discontinuation of certain customs such as ma'tambor, pontuong, and pre-garden rituals, as well as shifts in behavioral practices during garden-related activities. Regarding norms, one notable change was the elimination of the traditional labor exchange system whereby labor was reciprocated with energy; this system has been partially replaced by monetary compensation. Additionally, adherence to customary rules has become less stringent than in the past. Organizationally, the leadership of Mapalus Tani has evolved, with the traditional leader, referred to as the tumutuuz, no longer serving as the head responsible for customs and rituals. Changes were also observed in the materials used, as traditional forest ropes employed in Mapalus Tani activities have been supplanted by plastic ropes. Despite these numerous changes, Mapalus Tani continues to exist and function, actively engaging in its customary activities. Furthermore, membership in Mapalus Tani provides community members with assistance in alleviating the financial burdens associated with land management.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the implementation of the Ayo Nabung Sampah program in maintaining environmental cleanliness within the Maesa Subdistrict of Bitung City. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research is guided by Sondang Siagian’s (2000) theory of effectiveness. The informants consist of individuals directly involved in the execution of the Ayo Nabung Sampah program in Maesa Subdistrict. Data collection was conducted through interviews and document analysis, followed by data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions from the analyzed data. The findings indicate that the Ayo Nabung Sampah program is functioning with a relatively high degree of effectiveness. This is evidenced by the clarity of its objectives, the strategies employed to achieve its goals, the analytical processes involved, the consistency of policy formulation, thorough planning, appropriate program preparation, and the availability of necessary infrastructure. Nevertheless, two indicators were identified as suboptimal. First, the goal achievement strategy, which primarily involves socialization and promotion activities, has not been fully effective, as these efforts have failed to sufficiently alter societal mindsets and behaviors. Consequently, this insufficiency has led to a lack of understanding among community members and external stakeholders regarding the program’s objectives. Second, infrastructural availability in Kekenturan Satu Urban Village remains inadequate. 

Keywords: Effectiveness, Ayo Nabung Sampah program

Water Sensitive Urban Design (WSUD) is a multidisciplinary approach to the integration of water cycle management into urban planning and design. It is an internationally recognised concept that offers an alternative to traditional development practices of stormwater management. Water Sensitive Urban Design (WSUD) is an integrated management of stormwater. using a holistic approach to the planning and design of urban development that aims to minimize negative impacts on the natural water cycle and protect the health of aquatic ecosystems. The WSUD objectives can be achieved by implementing the integration of various Best Planning Practices (BPPs) and Best Management Practices (BMPs). BPPs involve site analysis, land capability assessment and land use planning for enhancing the capability of stormwater management, while BMPs involve managing stormwater quantity and quality with the application of structural and non-structural measures. Non-structural BMPs include development policy, environmental consideration at project site, education programs and law enforcement, while structural BMPs are stormwater treatment measures which are used to achieved the multiple objectives of stormwater management (Lloyd et. Al., 2002).This literature review paper presents the philosophy of Water Sensitive Urban Design (WSUD), its implementation through the integration of BPPs and BMPs. The paper also explains the application of structural and non-structural WSUD measures. Key words : WSUD, stormwater management, urban stormwater, urban drainage system
