The electronic invoice (e-Invoice) is a digital tax invoice issued by the Directorate General of Taxes with the objective of minimizing fraudulent activities, such as the manipulation or fabrication of tax invoices, which can adversely impact the value-added tax (VAT) liability. The phased implementation of the Electronic Tax Invoice system, as mandated by Regulation PER-16/PJ/2014 of the Director General of Taxes, commenced on July 1, 2014, with subsequent stages occurring on July 1, 2015, and concluding on July 1, 2016. This study aims to evaluate the application of the e-Invoice system in invoice issuance and to examine the use of the VAT Period SPT reporting procedure at CV. Wastu Citra Pratama. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative methodology, the findings indicate that CV. Wastu Citra Pratama has utilized the e-Invoice system since July 2014. The process of generating tax invoices via the e-Invoice platform has been effectively implemented. Nevertheless, the company occasionally encounters challenges related primarily to internet connectivity issues, which impede successful invoice uploads; however, these obstacles have been manageable with increased vigilance. Regarding the application of the e-Invoice system in VAT Period SPT reporting, the procedures remain consistent with those prior to e-Invoice implementation, with the exception that invoicing is now conducted through the electronic system. The company continues to employ e-filing for tax return submissions, although delays in reporting VAT tax returns persist. 

Keywords: electronic invoice, VAT Period SPT, PER-16/PJ/2014

Title: The Role of Extension Workers in Supporting the Joint Venture Pig Business Group "Singkatuhang": A Case Study in Buha Village, Mapanget Subdistrict

This study was conducted from April to August 2019 in Buha Village, Mapanget Subdistrict, Manado City. The primary objective was to examine the role of extension workers, specifically animal husbandry instructors, in facilitating and transforming the behavior—encompassing knowledge, skills, and attitudes—of farmers involved in the joint venture pig business group "Singkatuhang" (a term from the Bantik ethnic language meaning brotherhood). The focus was on enhancing farmers’ ability to implement effective pig-rearing management systems. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through observations and interviews, followed by descriptive analysis. Primary data concerning group activities and pig breeding operations were gathered from the leader and members of the "Singkatuhang" group as well as the head of the extension workers. Secondary data regarding the regional context and extension institutions were sourced from the Buha Village Office and the Manado City Office of Agriculture, Marine, and Fisheries. Behavioral variables were measured using an ordinal scale, while group profitability was assessed via a ratio scale. The findings indicate that the involvement of extension workers has positively influenced farmers' behavioral changes and moderately enhanced their income within the "Singkatuhang" joint venture pig business group, when compared to the 2019 minimum wage standards in North Sulawesi Province.

One way to reduce various problems due to the use of synthetic insecticides is to develop effective and environmentally friendly means of control by using insecticides derived from plants (plant-based insecticides). The aim of this study was to study the storage duration of B. asiatica beetroot (seed) extracts stored at 100C (refrigerator) against mortality of C. paconana pests. The study was conducted at the Center for the Protection and Testing of Food Crops and Horticulture in North Sulawesi Province, for 6 (six) months from November 2018 to May 2019. Using a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 7 (Seven) treatment and 5 (Five) replications . The treatment is the storage time of bitung fruit (seed) extract (0 days, 6 days, 12 days, 18 days, 24 days, 30 days and 36 days). The results showed that the feeding activity and the motion activity of C. pavonana larvae after application with the extract of B. asiatica greatly decreased and eventually died. The results showed a relationship between the fast and long days of storage of B. asiatica extracts and mortality of C. pavonana larvae, the faster the application of B. asiatica extracts, the higher the mortality rate of test insects. B. asiatica extracts stored at 100C (refrigerator) for up to 36 days show mortality above 50%, this proves that the application of extracts stored at 100C (refrigerator) is effective in controlling C. pavonana larvae test insects.

Despite relevant laws and regulations being in force for years, it has been argued that Indonesian legal system is not sufficient to protect consumers on e-commerce transactions. This article seeks to prove this premise by demonstrating insufficiency of Indonesian Consumer Law and Electronic Information and Transaction Law as well as other relevant regulations in addressing e-commerce issues on consumer protection.The Indonesian legal system does not adequately protect e-commerce consumers particularly because of three main factors. Firstly, the absence of the personal data protection law has been considered as to be a significant issue of security measures on electronic commerce transactions. Background: Market sanitation encompasses the oversight of activities related to maintaining cleanliness and sanitary conditions within the market environment, particularly to prevent the spread of diseases. According to the Indonesian Minister of Health Regulation No. 519/Menkes/SK/VI/2008, insufficient attention to market sanitation can facilitate the proliferation of bacteria or vectors, thereby increasing the risk of disease transmission. This study aims to describe the environmental conditions of the Winenet Traditional Market in Bitung City during the year 2019.

Method: A descriptive survey research design employing observational techniques was utilized to assess the environmental conditions at Winenet Market, Bitung City. Data collection occurred between September and November 2019 through direct researcher observation using a checklist. The instruments included observation sheets, documentation tools, and paperwork facilitating univariate analysis. Variables examined comprised market infrastructure, waste management, drainage systems, toilet facilities, access to clean water, food sales sanitation, disease and vector control strategies, and handwashing facilities. The frequency distribution for each variable was computed to provide a comprehensive descriptive overview.

Results: The market sanitation assessment was based on a checklist aligned with the Minister of Health Decree No. 519 of 2008. Each of the 45 questions received a score of 1 for affirmative responses and 0 for negative responses. The final sanitation scores were categorized as follows: ≥36 affirmative responses (≥80%) indicated a “well” rating; 29–35 affirmative responses (65%–79%) reflected a “good enough” rating; and ≤28 affirmative responses (≤64%) were classified as “less good.” The overall assessment for the Winenet Market environment yielded a score of 72.25%, corresponding to the "good enough" category.

Conclusion: The findings indicate that the overall environmental sanitation condition of the Winenet Traditional Market in Bitung City is moderately satisfactory, with an aggregate score suggesting a "good enough" level of compliance with recommended sanitation standards.

This study investigates the effects of fermenting banana peel var. Raja (Musa paradisiaca) with Rhizopus oligosporus on changes in dry matter content, organic matter, and crude protein. Conducted over a three-week period, the experiment employed a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) comprising nine treatment groups, each replicated three times. The treatments varied according to inoculum dose (0.2%, 0.4%, and 0.6%) and fermentation duration (48, 96, and 144 hours), designated as follows: P1 (0.2% inoculum, 48 hours), P2 (0.4%, 48 hours), P3 (0.6%, 48 hours), P4 (0.2%, 96 hours), P5 (0.4%, 96 hours), P6 (0.6%, 96 hours), P7 (0.2%, 144 hours), P8 (0.4%, 144 hours), and P9 (0.6%, 144 hours). Analysis of variance revealed that both inoculum dosage and fermentation time significantly influenced (P < 0.05) the dry matter content, organic matter, and crude protein levels. The findings indicate that bioconversion of banana peel var. Raja with Rhizopus oligosporus results in an increased percentage change in dry matter and crude protein, alongside a reduction in organic matter content. Notably, treatment P5 (0.4% inoculum dose with 96 hours of fermentation) achieved a 6.55% increase in dry matter, a 3.97% decrease in organic matter, and a substantial 60.91% increase in crude protein content.  
  
**Keywords:** Bioconversion, Banana Peel var. Raja, Rhizopus oligosporus

Probiotic from carp intestines and its effects on increasing growth performance and feed efficiency had been investigated. Fish used were carp fingerlings weighing 2.33 g in average. The fish were taken from the Tatelu Freshwater Aquaculture Fisheries Center. Probiotics used were isolated from the intestines of carp. Before running the experiment, the fish were acclimatized for 10 days under laboratory conditions. During acclimatization the fish were fed commercial pellets without the addition of probiotics. The dose of feeding was 5% /bw/day, 2 times a day at 09:00 am and 16:00 pm. Furthermore, fish are stocked in 15 aquariums each measuring 60x40x40cm3 with a density of 20 fish/aquarium. Each aquarium was equipped with aeration and water pumps for recirculation. Uneaten feed and feces were removed through siphoning. Water exchange was done every 2-3 days. After acclimatization, the fish were fed with pellet supplemented with probiotic at concentration of A: without addition of probiotic; B: 1 x 106 cfu /mL; C: 1 x 107 cfu / mL; D: 1 x 108 cfu / mL; E: 1 x 109 cfu/mL. The fish were fed twice a day with feeding dose of 5% /bw/ day, for 21 days. Data collected consisted of daily growth rates, growth rates, feed efficiency and feed conversion ratio. The results of research showed that the addition of probiotics in feed had a very significant effect on growth, feed efficiency, and feed conversion ratio (P <0.01) with the best results achieved in administering probiotics as much as 1 x 108 cfu / mL. In conclusion, probiotic bacteria originating from the intestines of carp can be used to improve the growth performance of the fish itself.

This study, guided by Chairman Eyverson Ruauw and committee members Charles R. Ngangi and Martha M. Sendow, aims to evaluate the labor productivity of sweet potato farming in Lenganeng Village, Northern Tabukan Sub-district. Employing a case study methodology, the research focuses on sweet potato cultivation within the specified locality. Data were collected through direct interviews with farmer groups and individual farmers, selected via simple random sampling, yielding a total of 16 respondents. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive techniques. Findings indicate that the labor productivity of sweet potato farming in Lenganeng Village was 79.72 kg per laborer, 57.66 kg per working day, and 35.89 kg per hour of labor (HOK). The study concludes that involving a greater number of workers simultaneously on the farm is more efficient than employing fewer workers over a longer number of days, as evidenced by higher average productivity figures associated with increased labor input compared to extended working days.

The operational activities of banks inherently involve risks that are intrinsically linked to their role as financial intermediation institutions. This necessitates the evaluation of the banks' health status to enhance public confidence. This study aims to assess the health level of PT. Bank SulutGo by examining the RGEC (Risk, Governance, Earnings, Capital) components over the period of 2014 to 2016. Employing an ex-post facto research design, the study retrospectively analyzes past events to identify the underlying factors influencing the bank’s condition.

Findings from the data analysis indicate that Bank SulutGo’s risk profile, measured through two key credit risk indicators—Non-Performing Loans (NPL) ratio and Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR)—remained within healthy thresholds throughout 2014 to 2016. Regarding Good Corporate Governance (GCG), the bank achieved a composite score of 3 in 2014-2015, reflecting a satisfactory implementation of governance practices, with an improvement to a composite score of 2 in 2016, indicating further enhancement. 

The bank’s earnings, evaluated using the Return on Assets (ROA), Return on Equity (ROE), Net Interest Margin (NIM), and Operating Expenses to Operating Income (BOPO) ratios, consistently demonstrated a sound financial condition over the three-year period. The average values of these indicators suggest that Bank SulutGo effectively managed its operational performance. Additionally, the capital adequacy of Bank SulutGo, assessed against the minimum standard of 8% established by Bank Indonesia, was maintained at a healthy level from 2014 to 2016, indicative of robust capital management.

Keywords: Bank, Health Assessment, RGEC Method

Buzz marketing encompasses strategic promotional techniques designed to capture the attention of consumers and key influencers, thereby amplifying the marketing message to a degree that discussions about a brand, product, or service become engaging, intriguing, and newsworthy. This study aims to investigate the role of buzz marketing in the development of start-up culinary businesses in Manado. To achieve this objective, the researcher conducted a qualitative inquiry, employing in-depth interviews with 10 purposively selected respondents. The findings reveal that buzz marketing significantly contributes to the growth of start-up culinary enterprises, generating a positive impact on their business performance. All participants emphasized that buzz marketing proved highly effective and beneficial for product promotion within the culinary sector. Through the use of buzz marketing, culinary business owners are able to promote their offerings with ease, leveraging a cost-effective approach that yields substantial impact. It is recommended that start-up culinary ventures continue to utilize buzz marketing strategies to accelerate product recognition and market growth, while simultaneously striving to enhance and sustain these efforts.  

Keywords: buzz marketing, start-up business, culinary business

Human Resource Management holds critical significance within the hospitality sector. One such establishment operating in Manado City is the Ibis Hotel, where the issue of employee retention warrants particular attention. Employee retention refers to the ability of an organization to maintain the appropriate personnel in suitable positions. The present study seeks to examine the challenges associated with employee retention at Ibis Hotel Manado. Specifically, it aims to identify the factors influencing employee retention and to ascertain which of these factors exert the greatest impact. Employing a descriptive quantitative approach, this research targets the employees of Ibis Hotel Manado as its population and sample, utilizing a saturated sampling technique to gather data from respondents. The findings reveal that four principal factors affect employee retention at Ibis Hotel Manado. These include the talent management factor—encompassing training and development, perceived organizational support, organizational justice, job autonomy, career development, commitment, performance appraisal, and employee empowerment; the workload factor—comprising job satisfaction, work environment, leadership, organizational culture, and work-life balance; the social interaction factor—consisting of demographics, mentoring, and compensation; and the psychological well-being factor—which includes reward, job stress, and job security. 

Keywords: employee retention, factor analysis, talent management, workload, psychological well-being, job security.

This study, entitled "Conjunction in English and Tagulandang Languages: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to examine and compare the conjunctions found in both languages in terms of their form, function, and meaning, with the goal of identifying their similarities and differences. The research addresses the following questions: What are the forms, functions, and meanings of conjunctions in English and Tagulandang, and what similarities and differences exist between them? Employing a descriptive research method, the data on conjunctions were collected from both English and Tagulandang sources. Analysis was conducted based on the theoretical frameworks proposed by Aarts and Aarts (1982), Nesfield (1957), John and Yates (1982), and Lado (1972). Data gathering involved both library research and fieldwork; English conjunction data were sourced from grammatical and linguistic literature, as well as online resources, while Tagulandang data were obtained through informants. The findings reveal that the conjunctions in English and Tagulandang exhibit both similarities and differences in terms of form and function. Notably, English includes complex conjunctions, whereas such structures are absent in the Tagulandang language. Regarding meaning, conjunctions in both languages display corresponding features. 

Keywords: Conjunction, English, Tagulandang Language, Contrastive Analysis

This study aimed to examine the role of the Camat in empowering communities within the Rainis subdistrict of the Talaud Islands district. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research focused on several key aspects: the encouragement of public participation by subdistrict governments in development planning; the guidance provided to work units responsible for implementing community development programs; and the supervision of these activities within the district. Data were collected through interviews with ten informants, including two subdistrict government officials, two village heads, two members of Orang LMP, two community leaders, and two villagers. The gathered data were analyzed using qualitative descriptive techniques, following the interactive model of Miles and Huberman.

The findings indicate that: (1) the Camat's efforts to foster public participation in development planning forums have been moderately successful; (2) their guidance to government work units and community organizations has been fairly effective; and (3) their supervisory role in overseeing program implementation conducted by governmental and civil society entities has also been reasonably well executed. Based on these conclusions, the study recommends: (1) enhancing efforts to actively mobilize community involvement in development planning at both village and subdistrict levels; (2) improving the effectiveness of coordination meetings and consultation forums aimed at guiding work units engaged in community empowerment activities; and (3) strengthening the monitoring and reporting systems to ensure regular and systematic evaluation of program implementation within the district.

Keywords: community empowerment, role of the Camat, development planning, qualitative descriptive study.

Abstract:  
The Electronic Licensing and Investment Information Services system (SPIPISE) represents an innovative advancement in public service aimed at enhancing both licensing and non-licensing procedures. This electronic system facilitates investor access to licensing processes that are streamlined, cost-effective, efficient, and predictable. Additionally, SPIPISE provides significant convenience for officials at the Capital Investment Coordinating Agency (BKPM) and the One-Stop Integrated Service (PTSP) by enabling validation and data retrieval during the processing of investment applications submitted to either authority. The system comprises three primary modules: capital investment information, capital investment itself, and supporting services. The implementation of SPIPISE is analyzed through the lens of Edward III’s four implementation theory dimensions, namely communication, resources, attitudes, and bureaucratic structure. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, this study involved in-depth interviews with ten informants, observational techniques, and the collection of supplementary documentation, including interview guidelines, recording equipment, and note-taking materials. The findings indicate that, overall, the implementation of the Electronic Licensing and Investment Information Services system has not been optimal.

Keywords: Implementation, Licensing, Investment Information Service

The data used are primary data obtained through interviews with 60 respondents who have bought fruit in October 2016. The sampling method is to use accidental sampling method. Analysis of the data used consisted of a questionnaire test, classic assumption test, descriptive analysis, regression test, determination test, F test and t test. These results indicate the test results of multiple regression analysis is positive and significant F-test value <0.05, which means simultaneously independent variables affect the dependent variable. The results of t test analysis of individual consumer variables, environmental influences and marketing strategies significant value <0.05 means that the independent variable (the individual consumer, environmental influences, and marketing strategies) partially influence on purchasing decisions. Thus the individual consumer factors, environmental influences and marketing strategy and a significant positive influence in decisions on buying fruit.Keywords: consumer, purchasing decisions, fruit, Freshmart, Tikala, Manado

ABSTRACT This research entitled "Interrogative Sentences in English and Loloda Language" is an attempt to analyze and describe English and Loloda Language focus on interrogative sentences in relation to their forms and functions in both languages.The data of English language are collected from several books, internet, and some theories that related to this research, whereas the data of Loloda language are collected by interviewing from some informants who know well about this language by using contrastive analysis approach. He said that contrastive analysis is a way to compare language elements in term of form, meaning, and distribution, in finding the differences and the similarities of both languages. The result of this research shows that English and Loloda language have similarities and differences. The similarities of two languages are found in form of interrogative sentences such as who, why, what, where, when, how (in English); nango, okia, moruoka, kiaka, idoa, sokonoke ( in Loloda) and function of question word of both languages. The differences between two languages are found, such as placing of question words, using "who" , taq questions and structure of sentence. Accounts receivable typically constitute the majority of a company’s current assets as well as the largest portion of its total assets. Accordingly, effective accounting practices and management of accounts receivable are essential. This study aims to examine the management, recording, and analysis of accounts receivable at PDAM Kabupaten Minahasa Utara. The research focuses on PDAM Kabupaten Minahasa Utara as the object of the study. A descriptive research method was employed, which involves drawing comparisons and analyzing research outcomes without extending to broader generalizations. Secondary data, specifically the financial reports of PDAM Kabupaten Minahasa Utara from 2013 to 2015, were utilized as the primary data source. The findings indicate that PDAM Kabupaten Minahasa Utara has implemented the Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards for Entities Without Public Accountability (SAK ETAP) in its accounting management and record-keeping processes. However, certain provisions of SAK ETAP have not been fully adhered to, resulting in a significant amount of bad debts. Furthermore, analysis of the Receivable Turnover (RTO) and Average Collection Period (ACP) ratios reveals that the turnover and collection of receivables do not meet the company’s targets.

Keywords: Accounts Receivable, Receivable Turnover, Receivables Collection, SAK ETAP

Abstract

Background: COVID-19, a communicable disease characterized by gastrointestinal manifestations, exhibits high morbidity and mortality rates due to its rapid transmission. Preventive measures include adherence to health protocols, notably hand hygiene practices. 

Objective: This study aims to assess the variation in vigilance behavior regarding COVID-19 transmission before and after the implementation of a 6-step hand washing health education program among members of the Aisyiyah community during the New Normal period.

Methods: Employing a quasi-experimental design with a time series approach, this research was conducted in August 2020 involving a total sample of 31 individuals residing in the Aisyiyah area.

Results: Bivariate analysis demonstrated statistically significant differences in COVID-19 transmission vigilance behaviors pre- and post-intervention, with a p-value of 0.000. Specifically, comparisons of handwashing behavior before and immediately after, as well as one month following the health education, revealed significant changes (p-values = 0.000). These differences were substantiated through Cochran’s Q test followed by Post Hoc McNemar tests to determine significance across the three time points.

Conclusion: The provision of targeted health education significantly influences individual handwashing behavior, underscoring the necessity for repeated observations to sustain these positive behavioral changes.

Keywords: COVID-19; hand hygiene; health education

This thesis investigates the introduction and expansion of Islam in the sub-region of Tombatu. The research employs methodologies traditionally utilized in historical studies, encompassing four key stages: heuristic investigation, critical analysis, interpretation, and historiography. The study aims to elucidate the process through which Islam arrived and developed among the population, as well as its socio-cultural impact on the Tombatu community between 1952 and 2010. 

Based on the findings, it can be concluded that the entry of Islam into sub-Tombatu is intrinsically linked to the broader dissemination of Islam throughout Indonesia. The influence of Islamic teachings in Tombatu originated from various regions across Indonesia, including Bolaang Mongondow, Gorontalo, Sanger Talaud, Maluku, South Sulawesi, Makassar, and Tondano—home to descendants of freedom fighters exiled to North Sulawesi. Additionally, the propagation of Islam was facilitated by Arabian traders from Java and Kalimantan who, while primarily engaging in commerce, also attracted the local population through traditional medicine practices, storytelling, and religious lectures. 

Over time, the development of Islam in Tombatu was further reinforced through intermarriage and cultural exchanges between Muslims and indigenous inhabitants, fostering a gradual but sustained religious transformation within the community.

Keywords: Development, religion, society.

The purpose of this research is to analyze the marketing of corn in each marketing channel in the village of Dimembe, Dimembe Subdistrict, North Minahasa Regency. The data used in this study are primary and secondary data. Primary data was obtained from interviews with 15 farmers while secondary data from the Village Office, North Minahasa Statistics Agency and the North Sulawesi Provincial Statistics Agency. The sampling method used the snowball sampling method. Data analysis methods are analysis of Marketing Channel, Marketing Agency, Marketing Margin and Marketing Costs. The results showed that there were three types of marketing channels, namely the first marketing channel: Farmers to Consumers; second marketing channel 2 from Farmers toRetailers then to Consumers; and the third marketing channel from Farmers to Collector Traders then arrived at the Consumer. Marketing margin on marketing channel I is Rp 213.33 / kg, on marketing channel II is Rp 1,500.00 / kg, and on marketing channel III is Rp 2,500.00 / kg. The highest share received by farmers is in the marketing channel I at 93.90%. While the lowest share received by farmers is in marketing channel III, which is equal to 58.33%. Thus it can be concluded that the longer the marketing channel, the greater the marketing margin and vice versa. This study investigates the calculation and reporting processes of Income Tax Article 21 for permanent employees at the Regional Finance and Asset Management Board (BPK-AD) of Manado City. It further compares these practices with the stipulations outlined in the Minister of Finance Regulation No. 101/PMK.010/2016 and the Regulation of the Director General of Taxation No. PER-31/PJ/2012. Notably, Non-Taxable Income (Penghasilan Tidak Kena Pajak, PTKP) functions as a deductible component in the calculation of Income Tax Article 21. The recent increase in PTKP results in a reduced tax burden, which, for individual taxpayers, can approach zero. Employing a qualitative research methodology, data were collected through interviews and document observations, subsequently described and presented to accurately reflect the prevailing circumstances. The findings reveal that the calculation of Income Tax Article 21 for individual taxpayers by BPK-AD Manado City deviates from the provisions of Law Number 36 Year 2008, as the figures incorporated include excess values, thereby inflating the Income Tax Article 21 amount. Conversely, the determination of PTKP aligns with Minister of Finance Regulation No. 101/PMK.010/2016. Regarding tax reporting, while the submission of Employee Income Tax (PPh 21) through e-filing occurs by the statutory deadline at the end of April, it does not fully comply with applicable tax regulations. 

Keywords: Income Tax Article 21, Calculation, Reporting, Non-Taxable Income (PTKP)

Background: Despite long-standing implementation of albendazole treatment programs, intestinal helminth infections remain a significant public health concern both in Indonesia and globally. Beyond pharmacological efficacy, various non-pharmacological factors may influence the success of albendazole therapy for intestinal worms. This study aimed to identify and examine such non-pharmacological determinants affecting albendazole treatment outcomes.

Methods: A systematic review was conducted by retrieving relevant scholarly articles from multiple databases including PubMed, Science Direct, Wiley Online Library, and Google Scholar. The search employed combinations of keywords such as "worms," "helminthiases," "soil transmitted helminthes," "albendazole," "drug adherence," "drug compliance," "nutrition," "nutritional," "age," "gender," "sex," "environment," and "sanitation." An initial pool of 6,322 articles was identified between February and March 2021. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, articles were screened by title, abstract, and full text, resulting in the inclusion of four studies eligible for in-depth analysis.

Results: The electronic search yielded 592 articles from databases (PubMed, Wiley Online Library, Science Direct) and an additional 5,730 articles from Google Scholar. After rigorous screening, four studies were selected, comprising one conducted in Asia and three in Africa. The identified non-pharmacological factors encompassed medication adherence (one study), nutritional status (one study), combined influence of age and sex (one study), and environmental conditions (two studies).

Conclusion: This systematic review highlights four key non-pharmacological factors influencing the effectiveness of albendazole treatment for intestinal helminths: patient adherence to medication, nutritional status, demographic variables (age and gender), and environmental context. These findings underscore the importance of addressing these factors to enhance treatment outcomes, and further research is warranted to elucidate the relationships among compliance, nutrition, demographic characteristics, and environmental influences.

Abstract: 

In recent years, the demand for orthodontic treatment has risen concurrently with increasing public awareness regarding the significance of dental and oral health. However, orthodontic interventions can occasionally give rise to complications involving periodontal tissues. Specifically, orthodontic appliances bonded to tooth surfaces often complicate plaque control, particularly in marginal regions, thereby promoting inflammation and gingival enlargement. Factors such as elevated tensile strength and limited tissue resilience may also contribute to the development of gingival overgrowth. This case report details the management of gingival enlargement in a patient undergoing fixed orthodontic therapy. An 18-year-old female patient in good systemic health presented with localized gingival overgrowth in the anterior mandibular region. Surgical treatment was conducted employing conventional techniques aimed at eliminating the gingival pocket to facilitate improved plaque control. The use of a scalpel proved highly effective in excising excessive gingival tissue. Follow-up at two weeks postoperatively demonstrated satisfactory tissue repair. Orthodontic treatment was able to continue without interruption three months following the surgical intervention. Emphasis on oral hygiene education and patient motivation was deemed crucial to prevent recurrence. Furthermore, a multidisciplinary approach involving collaboration between orthodontists and periodontists was identified as essential for optimizing treatment outcomes.

Keywords: gingival overgrowth; gingivectomy; orthodontic appliance

ABSTRACT  
Tahuna, situated on Sangihe Island, is home to a diverse array of avian species unique to the region. Along the coastline of Tahuna Bay, three distinct land cover types are present: built-up areas, coastal forests, and mangrove forests. Variations in these habitats correspond to differences in bird species diversity, as each habitat type supports specific bird communities that serve as observation points. This study was carried out at six sites employing the point count method, with the objective of comparing avian species diversity and community composition across built-up areas, coastal forests, and mangrove forests within Tahuna Bay. Field data were analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques and subsequently presented in tabular and graphical formats. Analyses included assessments of species richness, diversity indices, community similarity, abundance, and population density. The findings reveal a total of 27 bird species representing 15 families across Tahuna Bay. The highest species richness was recorded in the mangrove habitat, an area characterized by minimal human disturbance, with 15 species from 10 families, whereas the built-up zones, primarily commercial areas, exhibited the lowest species richness, comprising 5 species from 5 families. The Eurasian Tree Sparrow (Passer montanus) exhibited the greatest density in Tahuna Bay, with a value of 7.67 individuals per hectare. Overall, Tahuna Bay demonstrated a moderate species diversity index (H' = 2.28) and an evenness index across observation points of 0.69. Notably, natural habitats, specifically coastal forests and mangroves, displayed a high community similarity index (IS = 73%), in contrast to the built-up area, which presented the lowest community similarity index (IS = 25%).  
Keywords: Avian Species Diversity, Tahuna Bay, Habitat Variation, Community Similarity

This study seeks to enhance the understanding of the determinants influencing the transition of youth labor, specifically children of farmers, from the agricultural sector to non-agricultural sectors. The research was carried out in Treman Village, Kauditan District, North Minahasa Regency, over the period from January to June 2018. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in this investigation. The sample comprised 18 children of farmers, representing the XVIII Jaga group, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using descriptive qualitative methods, supported by tabular presentations and basic quantitative calculations.

Findings reveal two primary categories of factors driving the labor shift among farmers' children from agriculture to non-agricultural sectors. The first category, identified as push factors, includes: (1) the conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural uses, such as the development of buildings and roads, which reduces the availability of agricultural work and land; and (2) a lack of knowledge and willingness to engage in agricultural work. The second category, termed pull factors, encompasses: (1) comparatively higher wages or salaries offered by non-agricultural sectors relative to those in agriculture; (2) farmers’ children's perceptions of employment within agricultural versus non-agricultural sectors. These perceptions comprise four perspectives: (a) employment aligning with their educational background, which tends to be related to non-agricultural fields; (b) greater social recognition and elevated status associated with non-agricultural work; (c) a desire to gain experience in non-agricultural professions; and (d) superior working conditions in non-agricultural sectors compared to agricultural employment; and (3) the broader availability and diversity of business and employment opportunities in the non-agricultural sector compared to agriculture.

Abstract:  
Organizations, whether public or private, are established with specific objectives, and their success is determined by the achievement of these goals. Attaining success necessitates a solid foundation of competence, which serves to enhance organizational performance. Competence, rooted in a robust background of skills and knowledge, is essential for improving employee performance and is a critical component in all human resource processes. Given the increasing complexities faced by organizations, this study aims to elucidate the significance of competence in influencing employee performance.

This study employs a qualitative research methodology, which examines phenomena in their natural settings, with the researcher acting as the primary instrument of data collection. The sampling method used is purposive sampling, selecting data sources based on specific research objectives (Sugiono, 2009). Informants in this study include representatives from the Civil Service Bureau and the Public Finance Department of Sam Ratulangi University in Manado.

Findings indicate that work-related competence within the General Affairs and Finance Departments of Sam Ratulangi University remains inadequate, primarily due to limited opportunities for employees to engage in educational and training programs. Employee performance is generally categorized as moderate to low, underscoring the necessity for internal organizational policies aimed at performance improvement. Notably, formal education appears to have a limited impact on enhancing employee performance, whereas training and practical work experience play a more substantial role in promoting performance improvements within the financial and general administration sectors of the university.

Keywords: Competence, Employee Performance

ABSTRACT

This study, entitled "Error Analysis in the Use of Past Tense by Students of SMA Negeri 2 Manado," aims to identify, classify, and analyze the various types of errors committed by senior high school students in their use of the past tense. The investigation seeks to contribute to the readers’ understanding of error analysis, with a particular focus on the application of the simple past tense. Employing a descriptive research methodology, this study utilizes Ellis’s theoretical framework to elucidate the process of analyzing past tense usage among students at SMA Negeri 2 Manado. Data were collected from 48 students enrolled in classes XI MIA 2 and XI MIA 4 through instructional sessions and several assessment instruments, including fill-in-the-blank, true/false, and essay tests centered on simple past tense material. The findings reveal three principal categories of errors: omission, misinformation, and misordering. Specifically, omission errors pertain to the neglect of verb endings (-ed, -d), auxiliary verbs such as "did" and "not," regular and irregular verbs, and the verb "to be." Misinformation errors involve incorrect usage of regular and irregular verbs, the past forms of irregular verbs, "to be," and "to do." Misordering errors concern the sequence of verbs, objects, subjects, and time complements. 

Keywords: simple past tense, error analysis, omission, misinformation, misordering.

The purpose of this study was to determine the composition of nematocysts in the body tissue of the coral fungia, C. vaugani. The location for the collection of C. vaugani colonies was on the coral reefs of the Malalayang coastal area, Manado. This research was carried out in September - December 2020. The observation of nematocysts of C. vaugani was carried out using an Olympus CX41 microscope with a magnification of x100 objective lens which connected to a computer monitor equipped with an optical view 7 application at the Fish Health Environment and Toxicology Laboratory, Faculty of Fisheries and Marine Science, UNSRAT. The present results showed that C. vaugani had a composition of nematocysts, namely type I microbasic p-mastigophore (MpM-I) of 40.00%, small type II microbasic p-mastigophore (sMpM-II) of 31.11%, small holotrichous isorhizas (sHI) of 24.44 %, large type II microbasic p-mastigophore (lMpM-II) of 2.22%, and large holotrichous isorhizas (IHI) of 2.22%. sMpM-II is the most dominant nematocyst type of C. vaugani and this type of nematocyst is thought to be used by coral for aggression and killing prey or predator if there is disturbance from the surrounding aquatic environment where the coral lives. Further research is recommended to study the types and morphology of nematocyst from various species of coral fungia, including C. vaugani to understand the differences in their types and dimension of the nematocyst. Keywords: Composition, Cycloseris vaugani, Fungia, Manado, nematosit

Fishing households exemplify pre-prosperous families within the community. Historically, fishermen and their families have been perceived as poor, engaged primarily as farm laborers and craftsmen. The poverty experienced by fishermen is a multifaceted issue, largely stemming from their limited access to natural resources. Contributing factors such as low educational attainment, inadequate skills, lack of capital, and limited accessibility have increasingly marginalized this group. In this context, the fisherman's wife plays a crucial role in addressing and alleviating poverty as part of efforts to enhance household welfare. The fishing community in Kima Bajo village provides concrete evidence of the dual role assumed by wives in such communities. Beyond fulfilling traditional responsibilities as homemakers, these women often engage in supplementary economic activities due to the irregular and insufficient income of their husbands. For instance, many fisherwomen participate in crab harvesting by using nets and subsequently selling their catch in nearby markets. Additionally, some undertake various income-generating occupations such as laundry services, cake sales, and operating food stalls or canteens. These endeavors significantly contribute to meeting family needs. Among the wives of fishermen in Kima Bajo, side businesses such as stall vending, cake sales, canteen operations, fuel sales, laundry and ironing services, and the manufacturing of crab capture equipment (IGI) are prevalent. Consequently, these supplementary incomes help compensate for the insufficient earnings of their husbands.

Keywords: fishermen, housewives, roles

Abstract  
Numerous large corporations initially experienced rapid growth but subsequently ceased operations or failed abruptly. One identified cause of such business failures is the occurrence of human errors in the execution of management functions. This study aims to examine the role of management functions in the utilization of natural resources, specifically steam power, at PT. Pertamina Geothermal Energy Area Lahendong, Kota Tomohon. In accordance with the research objectives and problem formulation, this study employs a qualitative descriptive methodology. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation. Findings from interviews with several employees at PT. Pertamina Geothermal Energy Area Lahendong reveal that the management of natural resources, viewed through the lens of planning processes, adheres well to established operational guidelines, including strategies for implementation, spatial design, and personnel recruitment. Furthermore, the organizing function demonstrated effectiveness, as all personnel perform duties aligned with their respective roles, supported by clear division of labor, resulting in minimal operational obstacles. The management also enforces strict discipline concerning punctuality and adherence to working hours, with violations subject to sanctions up to termination. However, the study also uncovers incidents of managerial abuse of power, evidenced by the dismissal of numerous employees based on unjustifiable grounds.  
Keywords: management, natural resources management, organizational function

This study aims to assess community participation in the planning of the National Program for Rural Community Empowerment (PNPM-MP) in Tawa Village, Central Bacan District, South Halmahera. The overarching goal of the PNPM-MP is to enhance the livelihoods and employment opportunities of impoverished populations in rural areas. To analyze public participation in program planning, the researchers utilized the theoretical framework proposed by Ericson (as cited in Slamet, 1994: 89), which categorizes community participation in development into three stages: planning, implementation, and utilization.

Employing a qualitative methodology, the study involved six key informants, with the researcher serving as the primary instrument of data collection. Findings indicate that community engagement in the planning phase of PNPM-MP in Tawa Village was suboptimal; only a segment of the population contributed ideas, suggestions, or input during the formulation of development programs. During the implementation phase, male community members demonstrated a more active role by contributing labor, ideas, and material resources, whereas women predominantly managed household responsibilities. However, participation in the utilization stage of the program was inadequately fostered, resulting in improper or insufficient continuation of program benefits by the community.

To fulfill the general objectives of the PNPM-MP effectively, it is imperative that village authorities improve dissemination of program information and actively encourage public involvement during the planning phase. Both men and women, as target groups of the PNPM-MP, are expected to engage actively in the program’s implementation. Given that the central aim of PNPM-MP is to improve the welfare of local residents, the village government must also promote greater community awareness concerning the maintenance of development outcomes. Establishing a dedicated maintenance team to oversee the sustainability of PNPM-MP projects in Tawa Village is recommended to ensure long-term program success.

Keywords: Community Participation, National Program for Rural Community Empowerment (PNPM-MP).

Abstract: Full dental prosthesis rehabilitation on flat mandibular ridge has been a difficult case for clinicians for a long time. A huge resorption of mandibular ridge results in inadequate retention, and tounge muscle pressure, as well as lip and cheek muscles, causing a decrease in denture's stability and retention. Neutral zone is a potential area or position where lips and cheek on one side, and tounge on the other side have balance pressure. We reported a 60-year-old male patient with chief complaints of difficulty in mastication, and loose upper and lower dentures. He also complained of denture moving during swallowing and speaking. In case management, the aim was to acquire optimum stability of the denture and arrangement of the mandibular teeth in full dental prosthesis guided by using the neutral zone. Preliminary impression was done by using alginate, then, horizontal and vertical jaw relation was recorded by using bite rim. Suction method impression technique was used to acquire functional impression. Lower denture teeth arrangement adapted the result of neutral zone impression. Acrylic denture was being contoured to adjust the natural anatomy of the oral cavity. In conclusion, the patient got a new full denture with maximum retention and stability while speaking as well as masticating. This article discussed about making of full dental prosthesis with pressure point on neutral zone impression technique on flat mandibular ridge caused by huge resorption.Keywords: flat mandibular ridge; denture stability; neutral zone; impression technique

Abstract

The execution of the duties and responsibilities of a village chief within the government framework constitutes a significant aspect of governmental efforts aimed at enhancing community welfare. This study seeks to elucidate the implementation of these functions. The village chief plays a crucial role in fostering and advancing a self-help mutual aid society to ensure the realization of development initiatives outlined in the Village Budget. As the village leader, the village chief serves as both the organizer and the accountable agent in governance and community development, bearing responsibility for encouraging and nurturing communal cooperation.

Given the significance of the village chief’s role, this research examines "The Role of the Village Head in Stimulating Community Participation in the Salibabu Village District, Salibabu Talaud Islands." Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study focuses on how the village chief’s role influences community involvement in rural development. The study’s respondents comprised ten individuals, including local officials and residents of the Salibabu District.

The analysis is guided by theoretical frameworks centered on three key indicators: first, the village head as a motivator stimulating community engagement in village development; second, as a facilitator enhancing participation in rural development; and third, as a mobilizer driving community involvement in developmental activities. Findings indicate that while the village head’s roles as motivator, facilitator, and mobilizer are generally well-executed, it remains imperative for the village chief to effectively perform these functions to ensure robust public participation in development programs. Moreover, the success of the village chief is closely intertwined with the active involvement of the community he leads.

Keywords: village head role, community participation promotion, rural development

Title: The Impact of Immersion in Avocado Seed Tannin Extract Solution on the Internal Quality of Chicken Eggs

Abstract:  
This study aimed to evaluate the effects of immersing chicken eggs in a tannin extract solution derived from avocado seeds on their internal quality. One-day-old chicken eggs, avocado seeds, and distilled water were utilized as primary materials. The experimental treatments comprised eight groups: R1) untreated eggs stored for 14 days; R2) untreated eggs stored for 21 days; R3) eggs immersed in 10% tannin extract and stored for 14 days; R4) eggs immersed in 10% tannin extract and stored for 21 days; R5) eggs immersed in 20% tannin extract and stored for 14 days; R6) eggs immersed in 20% tannin extract and stored for 21 days; R7) eggs immersed in 30% tannin extract and stored for 14 days; and R8) eggs immersed in 30% tannin extract and stored for 21 days. The eggs were immersed in the tannin extract solution for one day prior to storage at room temperature for observation periods of 14 and 21 days. Variables assessed included the albumin index (IPT), yolk index (IKT), Haugh units (HU), and percentage of egg weight loss. A completely randomized design with four replications per treatment was employed, and data were analyzed via analysis of variance (ANOVA). Post hoc comparisons were conducted using Duncan’s Multiple Range Test. Results indicated significant differences (P < 0.05) in all measured variables between the 14-day and 21-day storage durations for both immersed and non-immersed eggs. Additionally, immersion in the tannin extract solution significantly affected egg quality compared to untreated controls (P < 0.05). However, no statistically significant differences (P > 0.05) were observed among the various tannin extract concentrations of 10%, 20%, and 30% for either storage period. In conclusion, immersion of eggs in avocado seed tannin extract concentrations ranging from 10% to 30% effectively maintained acceptable internal egg quality for up to 14 days of storage.  

Keywords: chicken eggs, avocado seed tannin extract, internal egg quality, egg storage

Local government assets constitute a significant component of the regional government balance sheet, wherein the asset information presented in the balance sheet report reflects the economic wealth possessed by local governments. Analyzing local government assets is essential for gaining a deeper understanding of the wealth and economic potential inherent within local governments, thereby enabling the public to make informed evaluations. Asset accounting pertains to the economic resources controlled and owned by local governments. The asset accounting systems and procedures serve as vital instruments for managing assets within Regional Work Units. This study aimed to examine the systems and procedures of asset accounting implemented by the Regional One-Stop Service and Investment Office in North Sulawesi Province. Employing a descriptive analytical method, the research findings reveal that the asset accounting systems and procedures are applied in compliance with the Regulation of the Minister of Home Affairs No. 17 of 2007. It is recommended that the asset accounting systems and procedures at the One-Stop Investment and Integrated Service Office of North Sulawesi be maintained in accordance with regulatory standards, with continued efforts in technical guidance and socialization to enhance human resource quality.  

Keywords: systems, procedures, assets, accounting, analysis

ABSTRACT:  
The ethical code of conduct for librarians aims to uphold their professional prestige and moral integrity, thereby enhancing both the quality of services provided to society and the standards of the profession. Consequently, librarians must adhere to principles grounded in aptitude, normative behavior, and courteousness when performing their duties, reflecting the core values of their ethical framework. This study investigates the relationship between librarians’ ethical conduct and their performance in the fields of library management, documentation, and archiving within North Sulawesi. The research encompasses all 32 librarians serving in the region as respondents. The findings reveal a significant and strong correlation between librarians' ethics of conduct and their professional performance in the provincial library board, archives, and documentation centers. This is evidenced by a t-test statistic of 73, which substantially exceeds the critical t-value of 2.042, and is further supported by a correlation coefficient (r) of 0.7, indicating a strong, statistically significant relationship according to the Guilford scale. Additionally, the coefficient of determination (R²) was calculated at 0.49, signifying that 49% of the variance in librarians’ performance can be explained by their adherence to ethical conduct, while the remaining 51% can be attributed to other variables not examined in this study.  

Keywords: librarian ethics, ethical conduct, professional performance, library management, documentation, archives, North Sulawesi

Abstract: The aims of this study are to know the role of organizational communication in the improvement of service quality in the West Bolang Itang District, the impact of organizational communication satisfaction, and the factors supporting the communication services organization in the process. The method used in this study put more emphasis on qualitative research methods. The instruments used in this study were a list of questions with emphasis on the various lists of questions that have been circulated to the informant in a structured or unstructured. The data collection techniques were observation and interviews. The observation was conducted in a participatory manner, in which researchers directed the targeted research communities. The analytical techniques used in this study were more emphasis on qualitative analysis. From this study it can be concluded that a) the role of organizational communication in the organization's service process can be applied through the relationship between superiors and subordinates, to maximize the timeliness of the work, affecting the attitude of openness subordinates in performing duties, affecting the administrative service, increasing the level of professionalism through education, and maximize the implementation of the discipline, b) good organizational communication satisfaction can affect the quality of service that can be seen from the procedure of service satisfaction, satisfaction in meeting the requirements of the various forms of service, satisfaction in the provision of cost of service, and satisfaction with services completion time, c) factors that supports communication between other organizations through service accountability, transparency of service, knowledge and skill factors and factors of discipline in conducting the service. The present study investigates the impact of replacing fish meal with black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) maggot meal in broiler rations on carcass and abdominal lipid percentages. In recent years, black soldier fly maggot meal has been explored as a viable alternative protein source in poultry diets, substituting traditional fish meal. This research was conducted over a six-month period at the Department of Animal Science, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. A total of eighty day-old broiler chicks of the CP 707 strain were distributed into 20 cages, following a Completely Randomized Design comprising five treatment groups with four replications each. The treatment groups were as follows: R0 (100% fish meal, 0% maggot meal), R1 (75% fish meal + 25% maggot meal; 3.75% maggot meal in the ration), R2 (50% fish meal + 50% maggot meal; 7.5% maggot meal in the ration), R3 (25% fish meal + 75% maggot meal; 11.25% maggot meal in the ration), and R4 (100% maggot meal; 15% maggot meal in the ration). The primary variables measured were carcass and abdominal lipid percentages. Observed carcass and abdominal lipid percentages ranged from 68.47% to 73.17% and 3.08% to 4.38%, respectively. Statistical analysis using analysis of variance revealed significant treatment effects (P < 0.01) on both carcass and abdominal lipid contents. Subsequent Tukey’s post hoc testing indicated that the R4 treatment group (100% substitution with maggot meal corresponding to 15% of the ration) exhibited significantly lower carcass percentages compared to R0, R1, and R2, although no significant differences were found among R0, R1, R2, and R3. Additionally, carcass percentages in R3 did not differ significantly from those in R4. Regarding abdominal lipid percentages, R4 was significantly higher than R0, but there were no significant differences among R1, R2, R3, and R4. Based on these findings, it is concluded that fish meal in broiler rations can be effectively replaced by maggot meal up to 75% substitution (equivalent to 11.25% maggot meal in the diet) without adverse effects on carcass and abdominal lipid percentages.  

**Keywords:** fish meal, maggot meal, carcass percentage, abdominal lipids, broiler

ABSTRACT

This study investigates the acquisition of English vocabulary among 4- to 5-year-old children through the use of picture visualization at TK Gmim Bukit Zaitun. The research addresses two primary questions: to what extent English vocabulary mastery is achieved via picture visualization, and which specific vocabulary items are acquired through this method at the institution. The objectives of the study include identifying and categorizing the levels of English vocabulary mastery attained through picture visualization, as well as analyzing and describing the vocabulary learned using this approach. 

The research sample comprised 17 students, and data were collected through interviews. A qualitative research methodology, supplemented by basic statistical analysis, was employed to respond to the research questions. The theoretical framework guiding the study is based on Tabors and Snow’s concepts of telegraphic and formulaic speech, alongside productive language development. 

Findings from the interviews reveal that English vocabulary acquisition occurs in two stages—telegraphic/formulaic speech and productive language—across various lexical categories: parts of the body (70% telegraphic, 30% productive language), fruits (59% telegraphic, 41% productive language), family members (71% telegraphic, 29% productive language), numerals (53% telegraphic, 47% productive language), and colors (59% telegraphic, 41% productive language). The English vocabulary acquired through picture visualization includes the following items: parts of the body (head, eye, ear, nose, mouth, hand, foot), fruits (apple, strawberry, grapes, banana, lemon, pineapple), family members (grandfather, grandmother, father, mother, uncle, aunt, brother, sister, baby), numerals (one through ten), and colors (red, pink, brown, white, orange, green, blue, black, gray, yellow, purple).

Based on these results, it is recommended that educators at TK Gmim Bukit Zaitun enhance students’ motivation to learn English by employing engaging picture visualization techniques and providing increased opportunities for vocabulary pronunciation practice. Furthermore, the study suggests that future research should focus on English language acquisition in preschool, kindergarten, or elementary school settings.

Keywords: Language Acquisition, Picture Visualization, Children, Kindergarten (TK)

Abstract: 

The organization of public services by officers is frequently criticized by society, particularly regarding the speed of service delivery, the timeliness of completion, errors in service outcomes, and other related issues. These challenges are attributed to deficiencies in officer professionalism and bureaucratic inefficiencies. This study aims to examine the professionalism of officers within the public service organization at the Malalayang Subdistrict Office in Manado. Employing a qualitative methodology, the research involved purposive sampling of 28 civil servants (PNS) working in the subdistrict office. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using the qualitative interactive model proposed by Miles and Huberman.

The findings reveal that: (1) the officers’ professionalism in organizing public services is generally adequate when assessed from the perspective of knowledge competence, which aligns with their formal education and relevance to the public service sector; (2) professionalism is comparatively weak with respect to expertise competence and creativity, as evidenced by training and education pertinent to their public service roles; and (3) the officers demonstrate satisfactory professionalism in terms of attitude competence in the provision of public services.

Based on these conclusions, the study recommends: (1) the provision of education and training that are relevant to technical and functional skills for officers; and (2) careful assignment of officers to tasks within the public service sector to enhance and develop greater professionalism.

Keywords: officer professionalism, public services, civil servants, qualitative study.

The present study aimed to evaluate and compare the effects of black rice extract and red rice extract on the lipid profiles of Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus). A randomized experimental design with a pre-test and post-test framework was employed. Each experimental group comprised six rats. The treatment groups were divided into four categories: black rice extract administered once daily (Group A) and thrice daily (Group B), as well as red rice extract administered once daily (Group C) and thrice daily (Group D). The control groups included a placebo group (Group E) and a standard treatment group (Group F), which received Lovastatin. Baseline, pre-treatment, and post-treatment data (denoted as P1, P2, and P3, respectively) were collected via random phlebotomy from one rat per group. Lipid profile measurements were analyzed within each group using paired pre-post testing, while intergroup differences were evaluated using analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by post hoc tests. The findings indicate that administration of black rice extract resulted in significant reductions in total cholesterol, triglycerides, and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) levels, alongside an increase in high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels in Wistar rats. Conversely, red rice extract contributed to decreases in total cholesterol, triglycerides, and LDL levels. Lovastatin treatment effectively lowered LDL concentrations. Furthermore, the efficacy of black rice extract in reducing total cholesterol and triglycerides was comparable to that observed with red rice extract.  

Keywords: black rice, efficacy, red rice, lipid profile

Abstract:  
Oral biofilms comprising diverse microorganisms are implicated in the etiology of various oral infections and inflammatory conditions. Extracts derived from the peel of rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum L.) contain bioactive compounds with demonstrated antibacterial properties. Given that nanoparticles possess enhanced antimicrobial efficacy due to their reduced size, this study aimed to evaluate and compare the antibacterial effectiveness of rambutan peel extracts (RPEs) formulated as microparticles and nanoparticles against oral bacterial species, specifically Streptococcus mutans and Staphylococcus aureus. Employing a laboratory-based experimental design with a post-test-only approach, RPEs were prepared in microparticle form at concentrations of 62.5 mg/mL and 250 mg/mL, as well as in nanoparticle form at 26.5 mg/mL. Particle size characterization revealed average sizes of 2489 nm for microparticles and 7.491 nm for nanoparticles. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis identified oleic acid, hexadecanoic acid, and decanoic acid as principal constituents in both particle types, with a greater proportion of oleic acid detected within the nanoparticle formulation. Antibacterial activity assessed via the disc diffusion method indicated a statistically significant increase in inhibition zones corresponding to nanoparticle RPEs (16.25 ± 1.529 mm) relative to microparticles at 62.5 mg/mL (12.83 ± 1.532 mm). Moreover, the inhibitory effect intensified concomitantly with higher RPE concentrations, attributed to an augmented presence of bioactive chemical components. Statistical analyses using ANOVA and subsequent post-hoc Tukey HSD tests confirmed significant differences (p < 0.05) in antimicrobial efficacy between nanoparticle RPEs and microparticles at 62.5 mg/mL against both S. mutans and S. aureus. In summary, the findings demonstrate that rambutan peel extracts formulated as nanoparticles exhibit superior antibacterial activity, with greater inhibitory effects observed against Staphylococcus aureus compared to Streptococcus mutans.

Keywords: nanoparticles; rambutan peel; Nephelium lappaceum L.; antibacterial activity; Streptococcus mutans; Staphylococcus aureus

This SIMDA financial application has been integrated starting from the budgeting function, regional financial administration functions, to the accounting and reporting functions.The type of data used in this study is, Qualitative Data is data obtained from the technique of gathering through a Questionnaire.This data collection was carried out on 48 Regional Work Units in the Minahasa Regency. The results of this study indicate that competency, motivation and organizational commitment have a significantly positive and partially significant impact on performance of financial management.

This study was motivated by preliminary observations indicating that the implementation of the Raskin program in Sawang Bendar Village was characterized by inefficiency, lack of targeting, and inappropriate allocation quantities. Accordingly, the primary objective of this research was to examine the implementation process of the Raskin program and identify the challenges encountered during its execution.

To address these research questions, a qualitative descriptive methodology was employed. Data were gathered through observation, interviews, and document analysis. The study involved ten informants, comprising four representatives from the Tahuna District Government, four officials from the Sawang Bendar Village Government, and two individuals from the RTS-PM. The collected data were analyzed using interactive techniques.

Findings revealed that the implementation of the Raskin program in Sawang Bendar Subdistrict, Tahuna, was generally conducted adequately and demonstrated a reasonable degree of effectiveness. However, two specific aspects—namely, the availability of resources and the organizational structure responsible for implementation—were identified as suboptimal and hindered full achievement of program objectives. Furthermore, several factors impeded the program’s execution, including: (a) adverse weather conditions affecting distribution operations, (b) low motivation and engagement among personnel directly responsible for distribution, and (c) delays in the disbursement of operational funds at the district level.

Based on these findings, several recommendations are proposed to address the identified issues: (1) enhancing internal coordination through the establishment of supervisory teams assigned to each level of the implementation hierarchy, and (2) encouraging village heads (Lurahs) to provide consistent guidance aimed at enforcing work discipline among members of the Raskin program’s distribution team, specifically the RTS-PM personnel.

Keywords: Raskin program implementation, rice subsidy distribution, program obstacles, qualitative descriptive study
