The study aims to examine the benefits of the Trans Yamdena Road as the main distribution channel for agricultural products, and to determine the distribution path of agricultural products before the opening of the Trans Yamdena Road in Wertamrian District, West Southeast Maluku Regency. The type of research data was qualitative. The data used in the study were secondary and primary ones. The secondary data were collected from the related sources according to the research objectives, and primary data were obtained directly from informants, which included farmers in Wertamrian District, the apparatus West Southeast Maluku Regency regional government, and Omele traditional market traders. Data were analyzed using Miles and Huberman models, and were tested by using triangulation methods. The results showed the benefits of the Trans Yamdena Road were ease of accessibility, creating business opportunities, transportation time and cost efficiency, expediting transportation and distribution processes of agricultural commodities, creating economic business opportunities and price stability, determining the location of economic center development, becoming the main supply channel for agricultural commodities. The study concluded that the benefits of the Trans Yamdena Road on the distribution channel of agricultural commodities in Wertamrian District were as supporting infrastructure for agricultural economic businesses, the main channel of distribution of agricultural commodities, and smoothing the supply chain. The distribution channel of agricultural commodities before the operation of the Trans Yamdena Road was the eastern sea lane, and the land area to the south of Yamdena Island.the Trans Yamdena Road is the eastern sea lane, and the land area to the south of Yamdena Island.Keywords: Benefits, Trans Yamdena Road, Social and Economy

ABSTRACT  
Clove (Syzygium aromaticum L.), commonly referred to as cloves in English, represents a fragrant dried flower bud belonging to the Myrtaceae family. Indigenous to Indonesia, clove is predominantly utilized as a principal component in the production of Indonesian clove cigarettes. Pest infestation constitutes a significant limiting factor in enhancing clove productivity. The present study investigates the impact of lanta (Excoecaria agallocha L.) fruit extracts on the larval infestation of Hexamitodera semivelutina in clove plants and seeks to identify the optimal concentration of lanta fruit extract for effectively managing H. semivelutina larval attacks. The research was conducted in Rerer Village, Kombi District, Minahasa Regency, from October to December 2019, employing a purposive sampling technique that involved the deliberate selection of study sites and subjects. The experimental design comprised five treatment groups, each replicated four times, with each treatment consisting of five clove trees harboring a single active H. semivelutina larva, thus totaling 100 sampled trees. Materials utilized included lanta fruit, blenders, filters, plastic containers, injection apparatus, knives or cutters, and photographic equipment. Results demonstrated that the application of a 20% concentration of lanta fruit extract (treatment D) yielded the highest larval mortality rate of 100%, followed by 15% concentration (treatment C) at 75%, 10% concentration (treatment B) at 55%, and the lowest efficacy observed at 5% concentration (treatment A) with 35% mortality.  
Keywords: Excoecaria agallocha, Hexamitodera semivelutina, clove

ABSTRACT  
The community of Worat-Worat Village continues to incorporate plants into various aspects of daily life, including their use as medicinal resources, household tools, materials for wickerwork, clothing, food, shelter, and components of traditional ceremonies. Among the traditional ceremonies preserved in Worat-Worat Village are the traditional eating ceremony (Orom Sasadu) and wedding ceremonies. This study aims to identify the plant and animal species involved in these traditional ceremonies and to elucidate their respective uses within the context of Worat-Worat Village, Sahu District, West Halmahera Regency. The research methodology comprised interviews and field observations. Informants were selected using purposive sampling, targeting individuals with specific knowledge and roles, such as traditional leaders, village authorities, and community members. Findings reveal that a total of eighteen plant species—including rice, sugar palm, betel, areca nut, forest banana, gofasa, sago, cempaka, yellow bamboo, stone bamboo, talang bamboo, balsam tree, durian, melinjo, rattan, kayu besi, coconut, and langsat—and four animal species—wild boar, deer, dusky megapode (gosong kelam), and rice snail—are utilized during traditional ceremonies. The applications of these plants encompass various parts such as stems, bark, leaves, fruits, and sap. Animal-derived materials include rice snail shells employed as lime, dusky megapode eggs consumed as food, wild boar meat as sustenance, and deer skin used in the manufacture of tifa drums. These results highlight the extensive diversity and multifunctionality of biological resources integrated into the cultural practices of Worat-Worat Village.  

Keywords: Ethnobiology, traditional ceremony, Worat-Worat Village

This study aims to examine the influence of environmental and individual characteristics of job activities on employee performance. Data were collected through interviews with company representatives and the distribution of questionnaires to 32 employees. The analysis employed both simple correlation and multiple linear regression methods. The findings indicate that the combined effect of environmental and individual job characteristics significantly impacts employee performance. However, the work environment exerts a stronger partial influence on employee performance compared to individual characteristics.

Correlation analysis revealed a significant relationship between individual characteristics (X1), work environment (X2), and employee performance (Y). The t-test results showed a calculated t-value of 4.221 and 0.592, both exceeding the critical t-value of 1.611 at a significance level below 0.05. The correlation coefficient (R) was 0.743, indicating a strong association between the independent variables (environmental and individual characteristics of activity) and the dependent variable (employee performance), as this value approaches 1. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.552, suggesting that 55.2% of the variance in employee performance can be explained by environmental and individual characteristics, while the remaining 44.8% is attributable to other variables not included in this study.

In conclusion, the results demonstrate that both environmental and individual characteristics of job activities significantly influence employee performance at PT. Taspen (Persero) Manado Branch Office.

Keywords: Individual Characteristics, Work Environment, Employee Performance

Abstract The skripsi which is entitled "Bahasa Kiasan dalam Puisi-Puisi Karya William Butler Yeats" aims at identifying and analyzing the types of figurative language that has been used by William Butler Yeats in his poems. The data were collected from the collections of The Wild Swans at Coole amongst many collections of William Butler Yeats' poems and are analyzed descriptively by focusing on figurative language. The data are analyzed by using the intrinsic approach referring to Laurence Perrine's theory concerning the types of figurative language. The two purpose of literature are to entertain and educate its readers, by analyzing the figurative language containded in the William Butler Yeats poems, it will help the writer to understand the meaning of poem better and then it can provides the readers with the entertaining and educating experiences they need. The result of this skripsi shows that William Butler Yeats uses the figurative language to convey and clarify his purpose through his poem. There are seven types of figurative language found in William Butler Yeats' poems. They are metaphor, simile, personification, synecdoche, symbol, overstatement, and irony. It was found that metaphors dominate the whole usage of figurative language in his poems. Keywords: Figurative Language, William Butler Yeats' Poems, Intrinsic approach.

This literature study aims to determine the application of the principle of sustainable development as an effort to prevent environmental damage in the field of mining in terms of Law No. 4 of 2009. Data collection methods used in this literature study, as the material for analysising, using the following methods: (1 ) Research specifications. The type of legal research conducted in answering the problems is normative legal research with the consideration that the starting point of analysis research on the application of sustainable development principles to the laws and regulations of the field of mineral and coal mining. Normative legal research is a literature assessment, so the research used secondary data. (2) Research Data. Materials in this research are taken from secondary data consisting of: (a) Primary legal materials, namely binding legal materials and consist of: (i) the Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Year 1945; (ii) Law No. 4 of 2009 on Mineral and Coal Additions and (iii) Law No. 32 of 2009 on Environmental Protection and Management. (b) Secondary legal substances, ie legal materials that provide explanations of primary legal materials, such as the Draft Law, the opinions of legal experts. (c) Tertiary legal substances, which provide guidance as well as explanations of the primary and secondary legal materials which include such as the Law Dictionary, Indonesian Dictionary, and English Dictionary. (3) Data collection techniques. Collecting data from the writing of this research is done through literature research, a series of efforts to obtain data and facts by way of reading, reviewing, clarifying, identifying and understanding about legal materials in the form of laws and regulations as well as books, literature books, articles, journals, and other sources of relevance to the research problem. The research results show that the company's responsibility in the management of natural resources and the environment is linked to the principle of sustainable development differentiated between social responsibility and absolute responsibility. Social responsibility includes corporate social responsibility programs (CSR). While the absolute responsibility emphasizes that the company should manage the natural resources properly and can be absolutely required accountability in case of damage to the environment. In such a management, coordination and partnership with related parties should be carried out in order to achieve integration and synchronization between economic, social, and environmental. Corporate social and environmental responsibilities should apply some principles of sustainable development, namely: Principles of intergenerational justice, principles of intragenerational justice, principles of early prevention, principles of biodiversity protection, Principles of internalization of environmental costs. Principle, sustainable development as an effort to prevent environmental damage in the field of mining in view of Law No. 4 of 2009 on Mineral and Coal Mining has been implied in several articles in this law. Sustainability in mining does not mean that the activity can be done continuously. In Article 2 and 3 of the Constitution Act of Minerba, it states that there are alignments to the national interest and the principles of sustainability and environmental insight (eco-vision).

The purpose of this study is to analyze the factors influencing consumer decisions when purchasing staple goods in either traditional or modern markets within the city of Manado. This research utilizes both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with respondents, employing a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were obtained from the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) of Manado City. Sampling was conducted using the Accidental Sampling technique, whereby respondents were selected incidentally based on their willingness to participate when encountered by the researcher at the study locations. The respondents comprised consumers who had recently purchased basic commodities and consented to be interviewed. A total of 40 respondents were surveyed, with 20 from the Pinasungkulan traditional market and 20 from the Freshmart supermarket in Manado. The analysis of internal factors—specifically consumer characteristics such as age, education, occupation, income, number of dependents, and types of basic goods purchased—revealed that consumers perceive greater satisfaction, comfort, and fulfillment of their needs in both market types. Regarding external factors related to market conditions, the findings indicated a consumer preference for modern markets, attributed to assurances of product quality, customer service, competitive pricing, and convenient location and accessibility. Additionally, psychological factors emerged, with 12 respondents (30%) reporting increased comfort while shopping in modern markets.  
Keywords: Consumer Behavior, Basic Necessities, Traditional Markets, Modern Markets

This study aims to determine the role of the agricultural sector to the economy of South Bolaang Mongondow Regency and its development in the period of 5 years ie in 2010 until 2014 and also to know the agricultural sector is the base or non-base sector. The data used is secondary data. This secondary data is obtained from the relevant agencies namely the Central Bureau of Statistics of North Sulawesi Province. The data is then analyzed using contribution formulas, growth formula and Location Quotient (LQ) analysis. The results showed that the agricultural sector is the largest contributor to the economy of Bolaang Mongondow Selatan Regency. This can be seen from the calculation of contribution and development of agricultural sector contribution to South Bolaang Mongondow Regency PDRB from 2010 to 2014. Based on the results of research also known that the development of agriculture sector to PDRB shows an increase that is from 2010-2014 with the largest increase occurred in 2013 with growth reached 5.82%, this can be interpreted that the productivity of agricultural sector in South Bolaang Mongondow Regency is good. From the analysis result using LQ, it can be seen that agriculture sector is base sector in South Bolaang Mongondow Regency, it means the role of agricultural sector in Bolaang Mongondow Selatan Regency is bigger.

This study aimed to examine the responses of students from the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences (FISPOL) at Sam Ratulangi University (UNSRAT) regarding their participation in online learning to date. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, the investigation utilized both primary and secondary data. Data collection methods included observation, interviews, and document analysis. The theoretical framework was grounded in Steven M. Caffee's theory, as presented in Jalaludin Rakhmat's (1999) work, which identifies three dimensions of individual response: cognitive, affective, and psychomotor. Findings indicate that students' responses to online learning varied individually, encompassing both positive and negative reactions. Advantages reported included the convenience of studying from home and cost savings. Conversely, challenges such as network connectivity issues hindered students' ability to fully grasp lecture material. It is recommended that students persist in fulfilling their academic responsibilities, show appreciation for lecturers’ efforts in delivering instruction, and adapt to evolving technological advancements characteristic of Indonesia’s progression into Industry 4.0. 

Keywords: Response, Cognitive, Affective, Psychomotor, Online Learning

The analysis and discussion from this research found that there is significant difference between online and offline store measured by price and promotional schemes. And there is no significant difference between online and offline store measured by availability of brand and product, standardization of product and family or social experience. A Financial Analysis of the CV. Rindrilly Swine Farm in Tontalete Village, Kema District, North Minahasa Regency

Established in the year 2000, CV. Rindrilly Swine Farm was the subject of this study, which aimed to assess its financial viability. Employing a case study approach, the research collected primary data through direct interviews with the farm owner, utilizing structured questionnaires. Secondary data were sourced from the North Minahasa Regency’s Central Statistics Agency (Badan Pusat Statistik, BPS) and other pertinent research publications. The study applied both descriptive analysis and investment criteria evaluation to determine financial feasibility.

Findings indicate that the swine farm is financially viable based on the investment appraisal criteria. The break-even point (BEP) was calculated at 288 pigs per production cycle, with a corresponding BEP value of IDR 807,437,525 per production period. This threshold was surpassed, as the farm sold 1,500 pigs per six-month production cycle, resulting in an annual revenue of IDR 8,869,000,000. Furthermore, the Net Benefit-Cost ratio (Net B/C) and Gross Benefit-Cost ratio (Gross B/C) were found to be 1.18 and 1.26, respectively. The Net Present Value (NPV) amounted to IDR 764,420,240, while the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) was 22.18%, exceeding prevailing bank interest rates. These financial metrics collectively affirm the economic feasibility of CV. Rindrilly Swine Farm’s operations.

This study seeks to evaluate the suitability of locations for waste landfill sites in Kota Kotamobagu, alongside examining community responses to such sites. Additionally, it aims to identify the factors constraining land suitability for waste landfill development in this region. The research was carried out over a three-month period, from February to March 2017, focusing on areas designated for the establishment of the Kotamobagu Municipal landfill site, as indicated in the Kota Kotamobagu RTRW document. Employing an observational research design, the collected data were analyzed using a quantitative descriptive approach. The findings revealed that within the designated landfill development zones, one candidate site in West Mongkonai Village met the criteria for potential suitability, according to the standards outlined in SNI 03-3241-1994. Community attitudes varied by location; residents surrounding the Small Poyowa landfill development or expansion generally displayed acceptance of the landfill's presence, whereas those in West Mongkonai largely opposed the establishment of a landfill site in their area. The factors limiting land suitability for landfill placement in Kota Kotamobagu were categorized into two primary constraints: firstly, social factors, involving community opposition to landfill sites near their residences; and secondly, physical factors, including land permeability, rainfall intensity, and proximity to agricultural zones.

This study seeks to evaluate the implementation of the self-help housing stimulant program aimed at providing livable houses in Tolok Satu Village, Tompaso District, Minahasa Regency. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, the research focuses on portraying the data gathered regarding the execution of the self-help housing stimulant assistance program in facilitating adequate housing. Both primary and secondary data sources are utilized in this investigation. Data collection methods include observation, interviews, and document analysis, followed by a systematic approach to data handling encompassing data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The theoretical framework underpinning this study comprises six key dimensions: policy standards and objectives, resource availability, inter-organizational relationships, characteristics of implementing agents, socio-political and economic contexts, as well as the attitudes of program implementers.

Findings reveal that the implementation of the self-help housing stimulant program in providing decent homes within Tolok Satu Village has not been executed optimally. Specifically, regarding the standard criteria for target beneficiaries, the program’s recruitment has been insufficient due to community unpreparedness to effectively receive the assistance. Moreover, the financial resources allocated for the program proved inadequate. The socialization efforts conducted by field facilitators (TFL) were limited to an initial introduction phase, lacking subsequent engagement, which resulted in beneficiaries’ inadequate understanding of the BSPS program’s operational mechanisms. Additionally, the attitudes of the implementers, particularly the TFLs, demonstrated a lack of decisiveness in conveying program information to recipients. Although the program mandates group-based implementation, in practice, beneficiaries tended to construct houses individually.

Keywords: Program Implementation, Assistance Program, BSPS, Decent Housing

Even though there are many issues surrounding dividend policy, dividend remains one of the main goals for investors to achieve. The aim of this study is to find out determinants of dividend policy in Indonesia. Most of the samples in observed period have varieties of dividend policies. Data for this study was collected from 258 business entities in the period between 2009 and 2012. For hypotheses testing, a binary logistic regression and factor analysis were used. The result from binary logistic regression showed that share price, earnings per share and current ratio are significant factors for dividend policy, while debt to equity ratio and corporate tax are insignificant. The insignificance of debt and tax was probably due to current ratio affected by accounting adjustments. Even though debt and tax are insignificant, they could not be ignored. Using factor analysis, it is confirmed that, most companies in this study have a similar objective through dividend policy, which is to maximize their share value in the stock market by considering profitability and liquidity on cash availability and also debt and tax. Dividends as a form of "trust value" offered by companies to their shareholders stimulate the trust of investors or shareholders and resulting the increase of share price.

To support the national water security program, which ensures the provision of raw water for households, urban areas, and industries, as well as to mitigate flood-related damages in Bolaang Mongondow Regency—particularly within Lolak Subdistrict—the construction of the Lolak Dam has been undertaken. While the dam offers numerous benefits, it also presents potential challenges, notably the risk of structural failure. Such failure risks generally arise from hydrological and hydraulic factors, water seepage, and structural deficiencies.

This study conducts a comprehensive analysis of the potential causes of dam failure, focusing on hydrological and hydraulic influences, seepage phenomena, and structural integrity. The investigation includes an assessment of foundation repair effectiveness using the grouting method, evaluation of dam stability against deformation, and computation of safety factors under eight distinct scenarios. Furthermore, the stability concerning seepage and the critical velocity within both the dam body and foundation are examined under conditions before and after soil improvement interventions.

The stability evaluations were performed employing PLAXIS 8.5 software. Input parameters for the model included gamma unsaturated (gunsat), gamma saturated (gsat), modulus of elasticity (E), cohesion (C), permeability (k), Poisson’s ratio (ν), and shear angle (φ), all tailored to align with the dam’s design specifications. These results were then compared with established safety criteria and allowable safety factor thresholds.

Keywords: Dam, Lolak Dam, Dam Stability, Soil Improvement.

The contemporary development of Indonesia's business sector reflects a promising trajectory, as evidenced by the emergence of diverse business entities operating in both small- and large-scale goods and services markets. Among these enterprises, wedding organizer service providers play a significant role. To enhance consumer satisfaction, such companies must deliver optimal service quality. This study focuses on the application of the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) methodology to identify factors contributing to the low customer satisfaction levels experienced by wedding organizer service providers. The primary objective is to ascertain the critical determinants underlying customer dissatisfaction and to propose actionable recommendations for improving service performance within this industry. The analysis employs the SERVQUAL framework, encompassing key service quality dimensions: tangibles, reliability, empathy, responsiveness, and assurance. Findings derived from 14 measured variables indicate that three principal factors contribute to diminished customer satisfaction: delayed responsiveness to consumer complaints, inadequate provision of information tailored to customer requirements (specifically, the absence of a comprehensive service list), and the unavailability of appealing event photobooths, including a lack of photographers stationed at photobooth locations. Based on these findings, five improvement measures are recommended for wedding organizer service providers: the acquisition of enhanced communication equipment, task assignment aligned with staff expertise, meticulous scheduling practices, more comprehensive information dissemination, and greater attention to event concept and theme customization in accordance with consumer preferences.

Keywords: Wedding Organizer, SERVQUAL, Consumer Satisfaction, Root Cause Analysis.

In societal life, conflicts are both inevitable and understandable due to the diverse interests held by individuals and groups. When the interests of one individual or group clash with those of another, conflict arises. Such conflicts are inseparable from social existence, as they represent phenomena intrinsic to social interactions. While conflicts cannot be entirely eradicated, they can be managed and minimized to prevent threats to the stability and wellbeing of society, the nation, and the state. Integration consistently emerges as a hopeful and effective means to resolve problems stemming from social conflicts.

The subdistrict of Sahu Timur provides a pertinent case, characterized by the arrival and settlement of Homesteaders alongside other settlers. This area exhibits a complex social fabric marked by religious and ethnic diversity. Notably, several Trans villagers are dispersed throughout the Eastern Sahu subdistrict, each group maintaining distinct cultural identities affiliated with their ethnic backgrounds. This intricate social composition renders the community vulnerable to conflict, especially in the interactions between indigenous populations of West Halmahera Regency and the incoming settlers. Despite occasional tensions, the communities coexist, and the integration process in Eastern Sahu proceeds relatively well, with conflict episodes not significantly disrupting communal harmony.

The Trans village community perceives several factors as impediments to rapid social integration. Prominent among these are differences in religion, ethnicity, language, and divergent viewpoints during communal discussions. Moreover, expatriate communities often maintain their own cultural practices regardless of the dominant local culture. In such contexts, proactive intervention by governmental authorities or local village officials is necessary to foster harmonious coexistence among diverse cultures and to prevent conflicts arising from these differences.

Keywords: integration, social fabric, conflict

ABSTRACT This skripsi entitled suffix ing in journal "English Teaching Forum" : a Syntactical Analysis. The -Ing form is neutral with respect to time; the time that is intended often depends on the tense or the meaning of the main verb. The suffix -ing is often used loosely instead of the perfect form of the gerund object of verbs. The suffix -ing of a verb can be used as a present participle, Frank (1972: 315). This research aims at identifying, classifying, and analyzing, the suffix -ing used in journal "English Teaching Forum" in terms of forms and functions. The data of the suffix -ing were collected from journal article chapter 1-5 based on Arts and Arts's (1982: 167), Lado's (2008: 24-62), Quirk. et al's., (1972: 242: 246) and Phillips's (2000: 117)'s theories. In analyzing the data in terms of forms and function, the concept of Arts and Arts (1982: 167), were used. The method of this research is descriptive qualitative method. The results of this research show that the suffix -ing used in the sentences of the journal "English Teaching Forum are various namely : suffix -ing as present continuous tense (3 data), past continuous tense (1data), gerund (9 data), reduced clause (6 data), -ing form as adjective (25 data) and -ing form as clauses that have an explicit subject and non explicit subject (21 data ). Furthermore the -ing forms have three functions: as verb, noun and as adjective. The study results show that the Ing form functioning as adjective is the most used in the journal articles mentioned. Key Words: The suffix -ing, Journal : English Teaching Forum

Calamansi (Citrofortunella microcarpa), commonly known as lemonfish or lemon cui in the Minahasa region, is a citrus fruit capable of yielding up to four harvests annually, producing approximately 40 to 42 kilograms per harvest. Each Calamansi fruit contains approximately 12 calories and comprises minimal fat, 1.2 grams of dietary fiber, 37 milligrams of potassium, 7.3 milligrams of vitamin C, 54.4 milligrams of vitamin A, 8.4 milligrams of calcium, and 15.5% water content. This study investigates the potential of Calamansi to be processed into confectionery products, specifically candies. The objective was to assess panelists' preferences regarding the color, aroma, taste, and texture of Calamansi candies, alongside evaluating the chemical properties of the candies, including moisture content, ash content, reducing sugar, and total acid levels.

The research employed a completely randomized design (CRD) consisting of four treatment groups based on varying sucrose-to-glucose ratios: A (80% sucrose: 20% glucose), B (70% sucrose: 30% glucose), C (60% sucrose: 40% glucose), and D (50% sucrose: 50% glucose). Each treatment was evaluated by a panel of 25 individuals. The treatment identified as most preferred was subject to further chemical quality analyses. Results indicated that treatment C, with a composition of 60% sucrose and 40% glucose, was favored by panelists due to its bright yellow color, citrus aroma and flavor, and relatively firm texture. Chemical analysis of the preferred Calamansi candy revealed a moisture content of 1.80%, ash content of 0.15%, reducing sugar concentration of 68.03%, and total acid content of 2.28%.

The problem with the restaurant business after the Covid-19 pandemic era is how consumers intend to buy in the business. This is related to the change in consumer lifestyles to become digital-based, as well as the desire for quality food products. This needs to be anticipated by companies engaged in the food and beverage industry. This study examines the relationship between online reviews and food quality on purchase intention with a study on BBQ Mega Mas, Manado Restaurant. This study uses a research with a quantitative approach which will be conducted in March-April 2021. The research location is the BBQ Mega Mas Restaurant in Manado. The research population is restaurant visitors with a total sample of 100 respondents. Data retrieval is done online using a Google Form which is shared via online social media. Data analysis used hypothesis testing and multiple linear regression analysis. Research respondents are dominated by women, young, college educated, university students, with an income of less than three million rupiah per month. The study found that simultaneously online reviews and food quality had a positive and significant effect on purchase intention. Furthermore, partially purchase intention is also positively and significantly influenced by online reviews and also the quality of the food of consumers who visit the Manado BBQ Restaurant. The research suggestion is that further research is needed on other factors outside of this research model that affect the purchase intention of restaurant consumers in Manado City. Keywords: online review, food quality, purchase intention, restaurant

Background: Adolescence, defined as the age range between 10 and 19 years, is characterized by rapid growth and developmental changes. High school students, who belong to this youth demographic, primarily focus on academic attainment. The onset of the COVID-19 pandemic necessitated a transition to home-based learning, which has the potential to influence adolescents' quality of life. Quality of life refers to individuals’ subjective evaluation of their overall well-being within the contexts of culture, behavior, and value systems, encompassing factors such as living standards, personal expectations, sources of enjoyment, and self-assessment of life circumstances. This study seeks to examine the quality of life and academic performance of students at SMA Negeri 9 Manado during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods: Employing a descriptive research design, data were collected from 95 adolescent participants with documented academic achievements. Results: Findings indicate that most adolescents reported moderate levels of quality of life. Furthermore, students achieving higher academic averages (scores ranging from 90.6 to 100) demonstrated superior quality of life across physical, psychological, social, and environmental health domains compared to peers with lower academic scores (74.6 to 90.5). Conclusion: Students at SMA Negeri 9 Manado exhibit commendable academic performance alongside a moderate quality of life. The data suggest a positive association between higher academic achievement and enhanced quality of life among these adolescents.  
Keywords: Adolescents, quality of life, academic achievement

National development has historically aimed, and continues to aim, to enhance the well-being and prosperity of society. Article IV of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia explicitly articulates development as a primary objective of the nation. This study addresses the research question: What role does the Tobaru customary community play in sustaining rural development in the North Head District of West Halmahera Regency? Consequently, the focus of the investigation is to elucidate the contributions of the Tobaru indigenous community in maintaining rural development within this district. Geographically, the North Head District is situated on the western part of Halmahera Island, encompassing an area approximately 1,234.5 square kilometers, extending from east to west. Analysis of the collected data indicates that the Tobaru community's role in supporting indigenous rural development in the North Head District has not been realized to its fullest potential. Based on the findings, several recommendations are proposed to enhance the effectiveness of the Tobaru community’s participation in sustaining rural development, particularly within the North Head District.

Keywords: Tobaru indigenous role, rural development

Abstract Banggai Regency is one of the regencies in Central Sulawesi Province that has a natural beauty and diverse natural resources, including local foodstuffs, one of them is proud cassava (Dioscorea sp.). Sweet potato (Dioscorea sp) or often called uwi is one of the many species of the genus Dioscoreaceae. Dioscoreaceae has potential as a food source because it contains a high amount of carbohydrates. Sweet potato processing is a form of flour that is more resistant to storage, easy to mix, and is more practical and easy to use for advanced processing such as making semprong cakes. The semprong cake is one of the traditional pastries and is loved by the people of Indonesia. The main ingredients for making this semprong cake are wheat flour, coconut milk, eggs, sugar and cinnamon as flavoring ingredients. This study aims to determine the most appropriate proportion of proud sweet potato flour and wheat flour, based on organoleptic testing of semprong cakes and knowing the chemical characteristics of semprong cakes. This study used a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with Treatments A (100% Banggai Sweet Potato Flour), B (75% Banggai Sweet Potato Flour: 25% Wheat Flour), C (50% Proud Cassava Flour: 50% Wheat Flour), D (D) 25% Banggai Sweet Potato Flour: 75% Flour) and E (100% Flour). The preferred organoleptic test for the semprong cake in terms of color, taste, aroma and texture is the D treatment (75% wheat flour: 25% proud yam flour). The results of the chemical analysis of semprong cakes for water content ranged between 1.78% - 2.99%, ash content 1.37% - 2.10%, fat content 22.74% - 23.60%, protein content 7.20 % - 7.62%, and carbohydrate content 65.18 - 65.67%. Keywords : Semprong Cake, Banggai Yam Flour and Wheat Flour

Fisheries should be a sustainable economic activity in order to maintain its services in the future. Sustainable marine fisheries resources exploitation requires a utilization rate lower than the resources availability. Therefore, the exploitation rate should not achieve the recovery ability of the resources in any particular period. In fishing activities, for instance, there is a guideline not to catch fish over the Total Allowable Catch (TAC), 80% of the MSY value. The exploitation rate of the anchovy (Stolephorus sp.) in Dodinga Bay was still low. It could result from small-scaled traditional fishermen and low fishing distance from the shore. Their income was also low due to high operational cost and fluctuation in fish price. To improve the fishermen prosperity, it is necessary to raise the fishing productivity and the efficiency of production input utilization on the boat lift net. This study focused on understanding the anchovy fishing season of the boat lift net in Dodinga Bay to analyze the yearly fishing seasons for the last five years. Results concluded that the fishing season of the anchovy (Stolephorus sp.) in Dodinga Bay could be separated into two phases, March to June and October to November, but the former was more extensive and lager in scale than the later.

ABSTRACT:  
This study aims to examine the influence of organizational culture on the performance of commanding apparatuses. Organizational culture constitutes a unified system of meanings shared by members, which distinguishes one organization from others. Performance refers to the degree of success in achieving predetermined objectives, where success is defined by the attainment of desired outcomes. Respondents, who are commanding apparatus members, were assessed to evaluate performance improvement, as individual achievements within the organization significantly impact overall organizational performance. Consequently, performance evaluation is considered a critical component of human resource management within organizations.

The research employed a quantitative observational methodology to investigate the problem formulated as: "To what extent does organizational culture influence the performance of commanding apparatuses in Tompaso District?" Using product-moment correlation and simple regression analysis, the hypothesis stating that "organizational culture significantly influences the performance of commanding apparatuses in Tompaso District, Minahasa Regency" was tested at a 1% significance level. The results indicate that organizational culture is a dominant factor affecting the performance of commanding apparatuses in this district. This is reflected by the coefficient of determination (R²) value of 0.894, implying that 89.4% of the variation in commanding apparatus performance can be explained by changes in organizational culture. Additionally, 10.6% of the performance variation is attributed to other factors.

Data analysis suggests a significant and contributive relationship between organizational culture and the performance of commanding apparatuses. Thus, organizational culture plays a critical and empirical role in shaping performance outcomes.  

Keywords: organizational culture, commanding apparatus performance

Marriage extends beyond the fulfillment of biological needs and human desires, representing an intrinsic or innate bond between a man and a woman. More accurately, marriage constitutes a social and legal covenant between individuals, establishing kinship as a recognized institution within local cultures that formalizes intimate or sexual relationships. The marriage ceremony serves to solemnize vows exchanged by two individuals, thereby inaugurating a legally, religiously, customarily, and statutorily recognized marital bond. The realization of marriage inevitably involves a series of procedural stages, each of which is shaped and influenced by the prevailing cultural context. Culture plays a decisive role by structuring social systems, thereby exerting influence over marital practices.

In the community of Pusian Village, Dumoga District, Bolaang Mongondow Regency, a traditional matrimonial custom known as the Mogama' tradition is practiced. This tradition entails a ceremonial event whereby the groom’s family formally receives the bride or daughter-in-law at the groom’s residence. The Mogama' tradition unfolds in several distinct stages: the initial stage involves preparatory deliberations between both families concerning the timing of the event, notifications to governmental and customary institutions, and the setting of a date for the ceremony. Subsequently, the second stage, referred to as Tompangkoi In Gama, marks the commencement of the bride’s retrieval. The third stage, known as Pinomama'an, consists of a communal betel nut consumption ritual. The ceremony concludes with the fourth stage, Ba Dati, characterized by the symbolic shaking of hands.

Keywords: ceremony, marriage, Mogama' tradition

Vester J. Worung. 13031108059. Physical Land Suitability Assessment for Clove Cultivation in Tenga Village, Tenga District. Supervised by Dr. Ir. Jody M. Mawara, M.Si (Chair) and Dr. Ir. Lientje Th. Karamoy, M.Si (Member).

This study aims to assess the degree of land suitability for clove cultivation within Tenga Village, identifying the limiting factors that affect plant growth, and mapping the spatial distribution of suitability classes for clove plantations in the study area. The findings are intended to provide valuable information for local farmers and the regional government regarding land characteristics and suitability, thereby facilitating more effective planning of land use for clove agriculture.

A descriptive survey method was employed, incorporating direct field observations of soil depth, soil drainage, erosion levels, flood hazards, surface rock presence, slope gradient, rainfall, air humidity, and temperature. Climatic data were obtained from the Meteorology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG). Soil texture was assessed in situ through tactile evaluation along with measurements of soil permeability. The collection of land characteristic data was conducted using a land unit approach.

Results indicate that the actual land suitability classes for clove cultivation in Tenga Village are as follows: Class S1 (very suitable) on land units V1 (LaIIKl), V3 (LaIKl), and V4 (LaIIIKl), encompassing an area of 1,450 hectares (31.73%); Class S3 (marginally suitable) on land unit V5 (LaIVKl) covering 720 hectares (15.75%); and Class N (not suitable) on land units V2 (LaVKl), V6 (LaVIKl), and V7 (LaVKl), which together occupy 2,400 hectares (52.52%). The principal limiting factor affecting suitability, particularly within the not suitable class, is erosion hazard (eh), with slope gradient identified as the predominant contributor.

Attention to the limiting factors in land units V2, V6, and V7 is critical; these areas exhibit erosion risks primarily due to steep slopes. However, with the implementation of soil conservation measures such as the construction of bench terraces, individual terraces, cultivation of ground cover crops to mitigate direct rain impact and surface runoff, three potential land suitability classes emerge: (1) Class S1 (very suitable) on units V1, V3, and V4 covering 1,450 hectares (31.73%), (2) Class S2eh (moderately suitable with erosion hazard) on unit V5 covering 720 hectares (15.75%), and (3) Class S3eh (marginally suitable with erosion hazard) on units V2, V6, and V7 occupying 2,400 hectares (52.52%).

This research underscores the importance of aligning clove plantation site selection with land suitability classifications, prioritizing areas classified as very suitable and marginal where slope-induced limitations can be mitigated through appropriate soil management practices.

Keywords: Land suitability, physical land characteristics, clove cultivation

ABSTRACT The research was arranged in a randomized block design (RBD), with 10 treatments and 3 replications. The results of this experiment documented 12 species of insect pests attacking soybean plants. Soybean pest populations were relatively low, except for Aphis glycine that was quite high. The lowest virus attacks found on compost of 5 tons per ha with 43 plants infected per treatment, the highest virus attack showed on combination of 5 tons compost per ha + inorganic fertilizer + mulch, in which there were 274 infected plants per treatment. Jackfruit leaves have been traditionally utilized for their medicinal properties, particularly in the treatment of skin conditions such as wounds. This study aims to evaluate the quality and wound-healing efficacy of ointments formulated with ethanolic extracts of jackfruit leaves at concentrations of 5%, 10%, and 15%. Employing a laboratory experimental design, the ethanolic extract was obtained through maceration. Subsequently, ointments containing 5%, 10%, and 15% concentrations of the extract were prepared. The formulations underwent evaluation via organoleptic, homogeneity, and pH tests to assess their quality. The wound-healing activity was assessed using five groups of rabbits, each with a 1.5 cm open wound: three treatment groups receiving the different extract concentrations, a positive control group treated with Betadine ointment, and a negative control group receiving a base ointment. Observations were conducted over a seven-day period. Statistical analysis was performed using One-Way ANOVA, followed by the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test. The findings indicate that all three concentrations produced ointments meeting quality criteria and demonstrated efficacy in promoting open wound healing in rabbits, with the 15% extract ointment exhibiting the highest therapeutic effectiveness.

Keywords: ethanolic extract of jackfruit leaves, ointment, wound healing, rabbit model

In Indonesia, individuals frequently allocate their leisure time to socializing, visiting shopping centers, patronizing entertainment venues, or relaxing at preferred coffee shops. Traditionally, Indonesian coffee shops are characterized as modest, small-scale establishments offering a typical menu featuring tubruk coffee accompanied by bread. These coffee shops possess distinctive attributes, providing an environment conducive to active social interaction among patrons. An illustrative example is the Billy Samrat Coffee House, a longstanding establishment operating for approximately 40 years in South Titiwungan, Manado City, which remains a popular destination attracting a diverse clientele from various professional, social, and educational backgrounds.

Contemporary observations reveal that coffee shops have transcended their conventional role as venues for interpersonal discourse, particularly among students. While historically these establishments functioned as hubs for debating and exchanging ideas, the advent and proliferation of information technology have considerably transformed their social utility. Presently, coffee shops increasingly serve as communal spaces where individuals congregate primarily to utilize Wi-Fi services. This shift is evident as many students now engage less in direct verbal interaction and more in digital connectivity, facilitated through activities such as online gaming and social media engagement.

Keywords: behavior, student, coffee shop

The color of a product is often a key factor influencing consumer preferences, particularly in relation to its perceived attractiveness. For certain products, such as city cars, color significantly affects perceptions of elegance, price, and design, which can, in turn, impact purchase intentions. This study aims to examine whether a significant difference exists between male and female consumers in Manado regarding their purchase intentions related to the color of city cars. Employing a comparative research design, the study utilizes a quantitative approach and applies an independent samples t-test for data analysis. The research population comprises individuals in Manado who either intend to purchase or already own a city car. A total of 100 respondents were selected, with an equal gender distribution of 50 males and 50 females. The findings indicate that there is no statistically significant difference between male and female purchase intentions concerning the color of city cars. Furthermore, consumers in Manado appear to place minimal importance on color when deciding to purchase a city car, often prioritizing factors such as price affordability, attractive design, fuel economy, and flexibility. Based on these outcomes, it is recommended that city car manufacturers allocate less emphasis on color variation during production. 

Keywords: purchase intention, color

The energy and protein digestibility of broiler chickens fed diets incorporating maggot meal (Hermetia illucens) as a substitute for fish meal was investigated in this study. Maggot meal derived from the black soldier fly is characterized by its high protein and lipid content, yet limited data exist regarding the digestibility of energy and protein in diets containing this ingredient. This research aimed to evaluate the effects of progressively replacing fish meal with maggot meal on the digestibility parameters in broiler chickens.

A total of twenty chicks were allocated to each dietary treatment, with four replications arranged in a completely randomized design (CRD). The dietary treatments were formulated as follows: R0 (control) consisted of 100% fish meal at 15% inclusion with no maggot meal; R1 contained 75% fish meal (11.25% in the diet) and 25% maggot meal (3.75% in the diet); R2 combined 50% fish meal (7.5%) with 50% maggot meal (7.5%); R3 included 25% fish meal (3.75%) alongside 75% maggot meal (11.25%); and R4 comprised 100% maggot meal (15%) with no fish meal. The key response variables assessed were the digestibility of energy and protein, determined via the internal lignin indicator method.

Data were analyzed using ANOVA appropriate for the CRD, with significance declared at P < 0.05. The findings revealed that dry matter, energy, and protein digestibility were significantly enhanced (P < 0.05) in the R1 treatment compared to R0, R2, R3, and R4. No significant differences (P > 0.05) were observed among treatments R0, R2, R3, and R4. These results suggest that maggot meal can effectively replace fish meal up to 25% inclusion (equivalent to 11.25% in the total diet) to optimize digestibility. Nevertheless, maggot meal can be utilized to fully substitute fish meal in broiler diets without adversely affecting the digestibility of dry matter, energy, or protein.

Keywords: fish meal, maggot meal, Hermetia illucens, energy digestibility, protein digestibility

The management of village finances encompasses a comprehensive set of activities, including planning, implementation, reporting, and accountability. Effective administration of village financial resources must adhere to established regulations and principles, alongside the competencies of the personnel responsible for their execution. This study aims to assess the compliance of financial management practices in Inobonto Two Village with the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation No. 113 of 2014, focusing on the stages of planning, implementation, and accountability. Employing a qualitative descriptive research approach, the investigation revealed that the financial management procedures in Inobonto Two Village, Bolaang Mongondow Subdistrict, have not been fully aligned with the stipulated regulatory framework. Specifically, transparency concerning the village’s budgetary income and expenditure remains insufficient in both financial planning and execution phases. Furthermore, the village has yet to implement the Village Financial System (SISKEUDES) for managing its finances. Accordingly, it is recommended that future financial management activities incorporate the use of SISKEUDES to enhance compliance and transparency in subsequent fiscal years.

ABSTRACT

This study, entitled "Euphemism in English and Tontemboan Language (Makela'i Dialect): A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify, classify, analyze, and compare euphemisms in English and the Tontemboan language, specifically the Makela'i dialect. Employing a descriptive research method, the English data were gathered from sources such as euphemism and sociolinguistic books, journals, websites, and several undergraduate theses (skripsi). Meanwhile, data for the Tontemboan language were obtained through interviews with native speakers residing in Manembo village, South Langowan Sub District, as well as from library materials and previous studies. The analysis draws upon the theoretical frameworks of Wardhaugh (1986) and Fromkin and Rodman (1997) to examine euphemistic usage, while Lado’s theory (1971) is utilized to contrast the two languages, thereby illuminating their similarities and differences. The findings reveal that both English and Tontemboan (Makela'i dialect) share certain euphemistic expressions with comparable meanings and employ euphemisms to render conversations more polite. However, differences were also observed; euphemisms in English predominantly appear in interrogative sentences, whereas in the Tontemboan language, euphemisms are employed in both interrogative and declarative statements.

Keywords: Euphemism, English, Tontemboan Language (Makela'i Dialect), Contrastive Analysis

Consumers frequently evaluate product quality based on available information. Such information may pertain directly to specific product attributes or may be extrinsic, encompassing factors like buyers’ perceptions of price, retail outlet, and brand name. Examples of intrinsic product attributes include volume, ingredients, and country of origin. This study aims primarily to examine the impact of brand equity on the price premium of the Apple iPhone and to determine which component of brand equity most significantly influences this price premium. The theoretical framework underpinning this investigation includes concepts of brand equity and price premium. The research population comprises Apple iPhone consumers, with a sample size of 100 respondents analyzed using a Multiple Regression Analysis model. Findings indicate that (1) all independent variables exhibit a strong and positive correlation with the price premium, (2) perceived quality, brand awareness, brand associations, and uniqueness significantly affect the price premium, whereas brand loyalty does not demonstrate a significant effect, and (3) uniqueness emerges as the most influential factor explaining variations in the Apple iPhone’s price premium. Based on these results, it is recommended that consumers in Manado reconsider their purchasing decisions regarding the Apple iPhone, while the company should focus on strengthening customer relationships in Manado to boost brand loyalty.  

Keywords: brand equity, price premium

This research was conducted to determine the bacterial pathogen affecting cultured eel elvers (Anguilla marmorata). Specimens were collected from the Tatelu Freshwater Aquaculture Center, specifically juvenile elvers exhibiting clinical signs consistent with bacterial infection. These symptoms included hemorrhaging on the chest, abdomen, and fin bases; reduced motility; general weakness; impaired balance; diminished appetite; lesions on the dorsal fin, chest, and tail; and loss of the characteristic slippery, shiny body surface. Three elvers, each measuring between 4 and 6 cm and weighing approximately 0.2 g, were selected for analysis. The head kidney was targeted for bacterial isolation. Each specimen was processed in duplicate; isolates were cultured on Tryptic Soy Agar (TSA) medium. The first set of isolates underwent identification at the Tatelu Health Laboratory of Freshwater Aquaculture, while the second set was analyzed at the North Sulawesi Provincial Health Laboratory. Bacterial identification involved morphological examination of colonies via Gram staining and a series of biochemical assays, including oxidase, catalase, Triple Sugar Iron Agar (TSIA), hydrogen sulfide production, motility, oxidative/fermentative (O/F) metabolism, and Simmons Citrate Agar (SCA) tests. Additionally, water quality parameters—temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, and ammonia concentration—were monitored. The findings revealed that the cultured elvers at the Tatelu Freshwater Aquaculture Center were infected by Aeromonas hydrophila. 

Keywords: elver, bacterial identification, Aeromonas hydrophila, Tatelu Freshwater Aquaculture Center

This study, entitled "Deixis in the Film Me Before You by Alison Owen," explores the five recognized types of deixis: person deixis (encompassing first, second, and third persons), place deixis, time deixis, discourse deixis, and social deixis. The primary aims of this research are to identify and categorize the various forms of deixis present and to examine their usage within the film Me Before You, directed by Alison Owen. The deixis data were extracted from the dialogues and sentences featured in the movie. Employing a descriptive research methodology grounded in Levinson’s theoretical framework, the analysis reveals the presence of all five deixis types throughout the film. Specifically, person deixis is manifested through first-person pronouns such as "I," "me," "my," and "our"; second-person references including "you" and "your"; and third-person forms like "we," "he," and "his." Place deixis is identified in terms such as "home," "here," "castle," and "kitchen." Time deixis includes expressions like "now," "when," "week," "today," and "tomorrow." Discourse deixis is illustrated by demonstratives such as "that" and "this." Finally, social deixis relates to distinctions in social hierarchy among characters, evident through terms denoting social classes—low, middle, and high—exemplified by designations including "pretty waitress," "premier badges holders," "madame," and "head of maintenance."  
Keywords: Deixis, Film Me Before You, Pragmatic Analysis

This study investigates the effect of complete feeding regimens based on corn forage on the digestibility of crude fiber and nitrogen-free extract (NFE) in Fries Holland (FH) dairy cows. Fourteen FH dairy cows, aged between 7 and 8 years and weighing 300 to 400 kg, were utilized in this experimental study. The experimental design involved two treatment groups with seven replications each, analyzed using a t-test assuming unequal variances. The two dietary treatments were as follows: Ra, comprising 70% corn forage and 30% concentrate; and Rb, consisting of 35% corn forage, 35% king grass, and 30% concentrate. The parameters measured included consumption and digestibility of crude fiber and NFE. Statistical analysis indicated no significant difference (P>0.05) in crude fiber intake between treatments Ra (2.07 kg/head/day) and Rb (2.10 kg/head/day), nor in NFE intake between Ra (3.36 kg/head/day) and Rb (3.46 kg/head/day). However, crude fiber digestibility was significantly higher (P<0.01) in treatment Rb (78.15%) compared to Ra (70.31%), whereas NFE digestibility did not differ significantly (P>0.05) between Ra (87.97%) and Rb (90.28%). These findings suggest that a diet composed of 30% concentrate, 35% corn forage, and 35% king grass enhances crude fiber digestibility more effectively than a diet consisting of 70% corn forage and 30% concentrate in FH dairy cows.

Keywords: digestibility, crude fiber, nitrogen-free extract, Fries Holland dairy cows

Keywords: raw water, treatment procedure, station hygiene and sanitation, bacteriological characteristics

Title: Cohesion in George W. Bush’s Speech Script: An Analysis of the "Address to the Nation 9-11"

Abstract:  
This study aims to identify, categorize, and analyze the five primary cohesive devices present in George W. Bush’s "Address to the Nation 9-11." Employing a descriptive research methodology, data were collected from the speech text and its historical context, sourced primarily from the American Speech Miller Center website and other relevant internet resources. The analysis framework is grounded in the theoretical perspectives of Halliday and Hasan (1976), supplemented by insights from De Beaugrande and Dressler (1986:8) and Brown and Yule (1983:191). The investigation focuses on five general categories of cohesive devices: pronouns (including personal, possessive, demonstrative, and interrogative forms), substitution, ellipsis, conjunctions (divided into adversative, temporal, coordinating, correlative, subordinating, and causal types), and lexical cohesion (encompassing repetition, synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy, equivalence, and correlation). The findings reveal that the speech contains a total of 76 pronouns, distributed as 48 personal pronouns, 16 demonstrative pronouns, and 12 interrogative pronouns, with no possessive pronouns observed. Additionally, the speech employs 2 instances of substitution, 49 conjunctions—comprising 43 coordinating conjunctions, 4 adversative, 3 causal, and 2 temporal conjunctions—with no occurrences of correlative or subordinating conjunctions. The lexical cohesion devices amount to 15 instances, while ellipsis was not identified in the text. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of cohesion mechanisms within political discourse, specifically within the context of a significant historical address.

Keywords: Discourse Analysis, Cohesion, Speech, George W. Bush

According to Article 36 of the 2008 tax regulation, all individuals who meet the criteria for being subject to taxation are obligated to pay income tax. The diverse nature of employee work arrangements and the wage systems in place can introduce complexities in the accounting processes related to income tax implementation. Additionally, discrepancies may arise when a company’s tax calculations deviate from the mandated tax regulations. Should a company report tax calculations lower than those prescribed by regulations, it may be subject to penalties imposed by the tax authorities. 

This study aims to examine the accuracy of the calculation and deduction of Income Tax Article 21 for permanent employees at Pancaran Kasih Hospital in Manado, assessing whether these procedures comply with existing tax regulations. The objective is to minimize potential errors in future tax implementations. Employing a quantitative descriptive methodology, the study involves collecting company data, conducting observations and interviews, and performing comparative analyses between the company’s calculation results and those obtained by the researcher. The data examined include the salary payments for permanent employees and the corresponding calculations and deductions of Income Tax Article 21 at Pancaran Kasih Hospital, Manado, for the year 2016.

The findings indicate that the calculation and deduction processes for Income Tax Article 21 concerning permanent employees do not fully conform to the requirements stipulated in Article 36 of the 2008 tax regulation and PMK No. 101/PMK.010/2016.

Keywords: Income Tax Article 21, Tax Regulation, Permanent Employees

This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying concentrations of the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana on the mortality of Plutella xylostella larvae infesting cabbage plants under laboratory conditions. A Completely Randomized Design (CRD) was employed, comprising four treatments: a control group (Treatment A) receiving sterile distilled water, and three experimental groups treated with B. bassiana spore suspensions at concentrations of 10^6 (Treatment B), 10^7 (Treatment C), and 10^8 spores per milliliter (Treatment D). Each treatment was replicated four times, with each replicate consisting of twenty third-instar larvae collected from pesticide-free cabbage plants in Tomohon. Data obtained were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA), and in cases where significant differences were observed, means were further compared using the Least Significant Difference (LSD) test. The findings indicated that B. bassiana effectively induced mortality in P. xylostella larvae, with the highest average mortality rate recorded at the 10^6 spores/ml concentration (65.00%), while treatments at 10^7 and 10^8 spores/ml yielded mortality rates of 58.75% and 55.00%, respectively. 

Keywords: Beauveria bassiana, Plutella xylostella, entomopathogen

Background: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a significant public health concern. In Central Sulawesi province, the cure and treatment success rates for pulmonary TB from 2009 to 2012 ranged between 87% and 88%, thereby surpassing the national target threshold of 85%. This study aimed to examine the relationship between TB patients’ knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors, and their therapeutic outcomes. 

Methods: Employing a descriptive analytical design with a cross-sectional approach, this study involved 49 pulmonary TB patients residing in nine villages across two sub-districts within the Biak Public Health Center’s jurisdiction in Luwuk Utara, Banggai Regency. Data collection was conducted using a structured questionnaire, and the resulting data were analyzed through correlation tests utilizing SPSS software.

Results: The findings revealed a statistically significant correlation between patients’ knowledge regarding pulmonary TB and their therapeutic outcomes (p < 0.05; r = 0.374). In contrast, no significant associations were observed between patients’ attitudes or behaviors and the results of therapy.

Conclusion: The present study concludes that patients’ knowledge about pulmonary TB is positively correlated with treatment outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of community education initiatives aimed at enhancing public understanding of TB to improve therapeutic efficacy.

This study, entitled *Complements in the Book of Ezekiel: A Syntactic Analysis*, employs the New International Version (NIV) of the biblical text. It addresses two primary research questions: (1) What types of complements are present in the Book of Ezekiel? and (2) What are their syntactic positions within sentences in the book? The research adopts a descriptive methodology comprising three distinct stages. The first stage involves preparation, during which the researcher thoroughly read the Book of Ezekiel alongside relevant secondary literature. The second stage encompasses data collection, where complements are identified, gathered, and categorized. The final stage, data analysis, entails determining the subjects, predicates, as well as the types and positions of complements within sentences. The theoretical framework for this analysis is based on Forlini et al. (1987), who define complements as words or groups of words that complete the meaning of a sentence predicate. They classify complements into five categories: direct object, indirect object, objective complement, predicate nominative, and predicate adjective. Although the Book of Ezekiel comprises 48 chapters, this study focuses exclusively on the first 24 chapters. Within these chapters, 494 sentences containing complements were examined. The findings reveal that: (1) all five categories of complements are represented in the text; and (2) the syntactic positioning of complements varies systematically. Specifically, direct objects appear after predicates, following indirect objects, preceding objective complements, and in conjunction with predicate nominatives, predicate adjectives, as well as combinations involving indirect objects and objective complements or predicate nominatives. Indirect objects are situated between predicates and direct objects, and may co-occur with objective complements or predicate nominatives. Objective complements are located subsequent to direct objects and can appear alongside indirect objects. Predicate nominatives occur after linking verbs, and may co-occur with direct objects, indirect objects, or predicate adjectives. Similarly, predicate adjectives follow linking verbs and frequently appear in conjunction with direct objects, indirect objects, or predicate nominatives.  
Keywords: complement, adjective complement, predicate nominative

This study was initiated based on the findings of a preliminary survey indicating that the organizational performance of the Department of Population and Civil Registration in Southeast Minahasa Regency has not yet reached an optimal level. This suboptimal performance is presumed to be associated with the relatively low quality of public services provided. Consequently, this research aims to examine and measure the impact of organizational performance on public service quality within the said department. A descriptive and quantitative methodology was employed to address the research problem. Purposive sampling was used to select 36 employees/service personnel as respondents, who were subsequently given questionnaires. The collected data were analyzed using regression and product-moment correlation techniques.

The results revealed that, overall, both public service quality and organizational performance variables in the Department of Population and Civil Registration of Southeast Minahasa Regency fall into the ‘high’ category. Nevertheless, two dimensions of public service quality—empathy and tangible evidence—have not yet achieved their optimal levels. This shortcoming is attributed to relatively weak supervisory practices by leadership. The analysis further demonstrated a significant positive relationship between public service quality and organizational performance, with both variables exhibiting a linear functional pattern and mutual contribution. Improvements in public service quality are therefore expected to enhance organizational performance, particularly within the Department of Population and Civil Registration of Southeast Minahasa Regency.

In conclusion, the empirical evidence supports the proposed research hypotheses and validates the theoretical framework employed. It is recommended that local government authorities strengthen supervisory mechanisms and implement training programs aimed at enhancing both public service quality and organizational performance.

Keywords: public service quality, organizational performance

This study, entitled "Taboo Words in English and Buru Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify and classify taboo words in both English and the Buru language, as well as to examine the differences between these two languages. Employing a descriptive research method, the study was conducted in three phases. Initially, the researcher reviewed relevant literature, including books and journal articles related to taboo words. Data for the English language were gathered from English-language texts, while data pertaining to taboo words in the Buru language were obtained through interviews with native speakers from Basalale Village, Waelata sub-district. The informants, aged between 30 and 60 years, were selected based on their native proficiency, clear pronunciation, and maintained linguistic competence. The collected data from both languages were subsequently classified, analyzed, and interpreted according to Wardhaugh’s (1986) theoretical framework, and the comparative analysis was conducted utilizing Lado’s (1975) contrastive theory. Based on Wardhaugh’s classification, six categories of taboo words were identified in English: sex, bodily functions, animals, excretion, death, and religion. In contrast, the Buru language exhibited eight categories, encompassing the aforementioned six as well as additional categories of curses and address terms. 

Keywords: taboo words, English, Buru language, contrastive analysis, sociolinguistics

The purpose of this study was to identify chydoridae using conservative way, while the observations of the life cycle was done through a microscope to determine the egg production per parent and length of life. Individual chydoridae acclimatized to reach 10 generations (1 month), and 10 females were isolated for the production of seedlings. Based on literatures review, chydoridae used was derived from subfamily Aloninae (Alona spp.); while studies on the life cycle found: the egg size of chydoridae 150.2 ± 22.4 μm, and neonates have an average size of 291.82 ± 3.06 μm, and reached adult size after 2.3 ± 0.5 days, with an average size of 441.22 ± 10.2 μm. Time of embryonic development occured for 1-2 days. On the entire life cycle, only 2 eggs could be produced per individual. Based on this study, the number of eggs produced by the female during its lifetime ranges between 30-60 eggs. Similarly, the length of life of this organism on average 47.2 ± 11.7 days, with the longest lifespan was achieved 60 days. It was found also the maximum size was 1,037 ± 8.5 mm; while the average size of an organism's body was 800.42 ± 56.3 μm.Keywords: chydoridae, identification, life cycle, Alona spp

The Covid-19 pandemic has significantly affected the Rural Banks (Bank Perkreditan Rakyat, or BPR) sector in South Kalimantan Province. This study focuses on a case study of BPR Kota Baru, a BPR institution operating within the same region. According to the financial reports released by the Financial Services Authority (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, or OJK), BPR Kota Baru has demonstrated one of the strongest Return on Assets (ROA) performances, with the ROA ratio exhibiting consistent growth throughout the pandemic period. The primary objective of this research is to evaluate the extent of BPR Kota Baru’s ROA performance in comparison to that of other BPRs in South Kalimantan Province, specifically before and during the Covid-19 pandemic, emphasizing their ability to maintain positive ROA values. The analysis utilizes data derived from the financial statements of conventional BPRs, available through the OJK’s website. Employing a comparative research methodology, the findings indicate that as of September 2020, BPR Kota Baru achieved an ROA of 6.74%, surpassing the average ROA of 4.80% reported by other BPRs. Furthermore, regarding asset management and the efficiency of operational costs relative to operating income (BOPO), the management of BPR Kota Baru successfully enhanced profitability amidst the challenges posed by the Covid-19 pandemic, as reflected in the financial statements published in September 2020.
