Mustard (Brassica juncea L.) is a horticultural crop valued for its provision of essential vitamins and minerals. Consequently, enhancing mustard cultivation is imperative. One approach to improve cultivation involves selecting an optimal growing medium to support vegetable crop development, particularly in contexts with limited land availability. This research aimed to investigate the impact of varying growing media compositions on the growth and yield of mustard greens. The experiment was conducted using a completely randomized design encompassing four treatments: A) soil alone; B) soil combined with manure in a 1:1 ratio; C) soil, manure, and compost mixed equally in a 1:1:1 ratio; and D) soil, manure, and sand combined equally in a 1:1:1 ratio. Each treatment was replicated four times, resulting in a total of sixteen experimental units. Observations included plant height and leaf number, measured at two and four weeks post-transplanting, as well as the fresh biomass of mustard greens at harvest. Data were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by a Least Significant Difference (LSD) test at the 5% significance level when treatment effects were significant. Findings revealed that the inclusion of manure in the planting medium markedly enhanced the growth and yield of mustard greens. Among the treatments, the soil-manure-compost mixture (1:1:1) was identified as the most favorable medium for mustard cultivation.

THE EFFECTS OF AFFERING KING GRASS (Pennisetum Purpupoides) AND CORN STOVER ON PERFORMANCE OF ONGOLE CROSSBREED COWS A research evaluating the effects of affering king grass (Pennisetum purpupoides) and corn stover as feed ingredients on performance of ongole crossbreed cows has been conducled. Two years old, of fifteen ongole crossbreed cows with ± 200 kg body weight were used in this experiment. Completely Randomized Design with 5 treatments and 3 replications was used. The treatments were R1 = 100% king grass, R2 = 75% king grass + 25% corn stover, R3 = 50% king grass + 50% corn stover, R4 = 25% king grass + 75% corn stover and R5 = 100% corn stover. Variables measured were dry matter consumption (DMC), average daily gain (ADG) and feed conversion (FC). The average of DMC, ADG and FC were 4,64-5,97 kg/tail/day, 0,36-0,55 kg/tail/day and 10,89-13,44 respectively. The results showed that there were significant effects (P<0,05) on DMC and ADG, however, there was no significant effect (P>0,05) on FC. Tukey test showed that DMC of cows fed R1 were significantly (P<0,05) lower compared to R5, however, there was no significant (P>0,05) difference among cows fed R3, R4 and R5. ADG of cows fed R1 was not significantly (P>0,05) different compared to R2, R3 and R4, while, cows fed R1 and R2 were Significantly (P<0,05) lower compared to R5. Based on the results on DMC, ADG and FC it can be concluded that to increase performance of crossbreed cows the portion of king grass can be affered up to 50%, on the other hand corn stover is more than 50% in the ration. Key words : Kinggrass (Pennisetum purpupoides), corn stover, performance ongole crossbreed cows.

This study examines the potential of Angkak as a binding compoundin the process of making chicken sausages that are rejected as curingingredients. These physical tests include water binding capacity, pH andcooking losses. The design was carried out in a completely randomizeddesign (CRD) 4 x 4, as a treatment using the angkak level, ie without angkak0%, angkak 0.5%, angkak 1% and angkak 1.5% with replications 4 timesfollowed by BNJ test. The data obtained were analyzed using the SPSSversion 24 program. The results of the diversity analysis showed that therewere significant differences between treatments (P <0.05). This differenceis followed by the BNT test, indicating that the higher the concentration ofAngkak added, the binding capacity of the water will increase (41.38 -42.57). The results of the variance analysis for the pH value of sausages(6.24 - 5.83), showed that there was a significant effect (P <0.05) on thelevel of angkak administration which was then followed by the LSD test.Significant influence also applies to variable cooking losses (P <0.05),cooking shrinkage values 17.74 -12.67. The results of this study can beconcluded that at the level of 0.5% it can affect the physical properties ofwater binding capacity, pH and cooking losses of rejected chicken sausages.Keywords: Sausage, Angkak, Cooking Shrinkage, Water Binding Capacity, pH

This research aimed to investigate the feasibility of utilizing rice husk, corn cob, and corn skin for the production of bio-briquettes as sustainable alternatives to conventional kerosene and gas fuels. The study focused on analyzing the calorific value and ash content of rice husk, corn cob, corn skin, and the combustion characteristics of the resulting bio-briquettes. An experimental approach was employed to assess the quality of the bio-briquettes both in laboratory and field settings. Initially, charcoal was produced from rice husk and corn skin using a charcoal furnace, and the yield (rendement) was calculated. The charcoal quality was evaluated through measurements of calorific value and ash content. Bio-briquette quality was assessed by varying particle sizes (15 mesh, 20 mesh, 25 mesh, 30 mesh) and applying pressure via compression using a hydraulic pump exerting 5000 kg/m².

Raw materials, specifically rice husk and corn skin, were sourced from North Minahasa Regency. Key variables monitored during the experimentation included the charcoal production process parameters such as yield percentage, duration of charring (minutes), maximum charcoal temperature (°C), and laboratory-determined calorific value (cal/g) and ash content (%), with analyses conducted at the Research and Industrial Standardization Board laboratory in Manado. The bio-briquette performance was gauged primarily by measuring water boiling time.

Results indicated that the longest water boiling duration was observed with the 15 mesh size bio-briquettes, recorded at 27 minutes. The highest temperature under the cooking vessel, reaching 383°C, was achieved with the 30 mesh size bio-briquettes, which also exhibited the longest burn-out time of 562 minutes. Furthermore, the lowest residual ash content following combustion, at 12.48%, was obtained from the 15 mesh treatment. These findings demonstrate that agricultural residues such as rice husk and corn skin can be effectively transformed into environmentally sustainable bio-briquettes, with the 15 mesh particle size delivering optimal performance in terms of boiling time and minimal ash residue, while the 30 mesh size maximized combustion temperature and prolonged burn duration.

**Keywords:** bio-briquettes, rice husk, corn skin

Research on groundwater for various purposes, i.e. for drinking water, for agriculture water, hotels water, industrial water, or water for needs of the city has been investigated by many researchers, until nowadays it's been a lot of countries that have successfully empower groundwater, such as the State of Japan in the city of Kumamoto. Groundwater research in this paper was conducted in the Kecamatan Modoinding with the objective to investigate the potential of groundwater for horticultural crops. Implementation research shows that the average climate data, which includes temperature 27.60C, air humidity was about 99.83%, evaporation was about 2.19mm, wind speed was about 4.46km/day, the sun shines was about 40.13% and an average rainfall depth of 206.6mm, the existence of two mountains, four streams that are intermittent and perennial characteristics, two lakes and groundwater wells located within the study location, all the indicators are variables and parameters that can be used to determine the groundwater potential of the fields. The results show there is a potential of groundwater in the Kecamatan Modoinding with relatively large volume can be used for vegetable crops in the summer, however more research needs to be done to empower the groundwater at a low cost. Key words: Groundwater potential, exploration and exploitation, horticultural crops.

ABSTRACT: Local taxes constitute a significant source of revenue for regional governments, anticipated to support the implementation of local autonomy by enabling them to effectively organize and manage their financial affairs. In addition to government subsidies and assistance, local tax revenues are expected to finance local governance and developmental activities. Specifically, Manado City, recognized as a tourism destination, exhibits a growing number of hotels ranging from luxury establishments to budget accommodations, which represent tourism businesses capable of generating substantial hotel tax revenue. The increasing development within Manado City suggests that hotel tax possesses considerable potential as an optimal source of local revenue. This study employed a descriptive quantitative approach, utilizing secondary data in the form of time series covering hotel tax revenues from 2010 to 2014. The findings indicate that, based on the hotel tax targets set by the Manado City government, hotel tax revenue contributed significantly during the 2010 to 2014 period, totaling IDR 66,946,272,913. On average, hotel tax revenue accounted for approximately 7.58% of Manado's local government revenue (PAD) annually. Consequently, hotel tax in Manado City represents a substantial and valuable contributor to the city’s original local revenue.  
Keywords: Hotel Tax, Local Revenue

Abstract:  
Motherhood, encompassing pregnancy, childbirth, and child-rearing, necessitates that women avail themselves of maternity leave. This study aims to examine the impact of maternity leave and career development on employee performance at the BNI branch in Manado. Employing a qualitative research design, data were collected through interviews with female employees at BNI Manado who had taken maternity leave. A purposive sampling technique was utilized to select participants. Constructs related to maternity leave, career development, and employee performance were derived from extant literature to explore their interrelationships. Findings indicate that 40% of the participants experienced challenges and discomfort while balancing work responsibilities and motherhood concurrently, whereas 60% reported no such difficulties. The study concludes that maternity leave at BNI Manado does not adversely affect employee performance, as the employees who took maternity leave possess substantial professional skills and maternal experience. It is recommended that BNI Manado continue to foster objectivity and enhance support mechanisms for employees availing maternity leave.  

Keywords: maternity leave, employee performance, career development

Today, woman in Indonesia their role as a housewife has been divided with role as an employee to meet the family needs because of unfavorable economic conditions. However having to simultaneously act for two roles is not easy. This situation will result in a very significant achievement for business establishments, which is affected their performance in the office. This study aimed to determine the influence of role as a housewife and role as an employee to the employee performance as a civil servant in the level of government Tomohon. This research used quantitative method. The analytical method used was multiple linear regression analysis. The data used in this research is primary data obtain through the questionnaire. The population observed is the married woman in the level of government Tomohon with sample as many as 100 respondents. Result of the analysis showed that both role as a housewife and role as an employee has a significant influence to the Employee Performance as a civil servant in the level of government Tomohon. The Tomohon city government's still consider the dual role of career woman and still maintain the performance of employees especially career women who have a family in order to keep balance between their work in the office with their obligations at home as a housewife, and with regard to their discipline in work. Keywords: role as a housewife, role as an employee, employee performance

ABSTRACT The title of this study is "The Use of Phrasal Verbs by the Students of SMA Negeri 2 Manado". The main object of this study is the use of phrasal verbs by the XI grade students of SMA Negeri 2 Manado (Mathematics and Natural Sciences class). The method that has been applied by the writer in this research is descriptive method which has been done in several stages: preparation was made by reading the theory about phrasal verbs and goingto the school to get a picture of the English curriculum. Data collection was taken from 40 students of SMA Negeri 2 Manado, by giving them tests containing phrasal verbs. They are multiple choice, fill in the blank and true or false. The indentified data were analyzed by using simple statistic and qualitative method based on Furchon (1982). The result of the test is described by using some tables. The result of the analysis shows that the student's difficulty in using phrasal verbs is high; that is only 36.8% of the students have right answer while 63.2% have wrong answer. The difficulty is caused by the misunderstanding of the meaning of phrasal verbs. Some of the students do not understand what the phrasal verbs are and how to use phrasal verbs in a sentences due to the minimum teaching of phrasal verbs in SMA Negeri 2 Manado. Key words : phrasal verb, students, misunderstanding, use, presentage

The synthesis of Islamic beliefs with indigenous cultural practices creates a distinctive character in local religious expressions, particularly in the ways religious rituals diverge from orthodox forms. Local communities perceive religion or faith primarily as a guiding framework for achieving security both in this life and the afterlife. Deviations or misinterpretations of religious teachings are not unprecedented within these communities; however, local proselytism remains unrecognized and is often met with passive acceptance. Importantly, such divergences do not result in discord among religious groups. For instance, the indigenous religion known as Islam Masade, practiced in the Sangihe region—especially within Lenganeng Village—continues to persist and maintain a respected status among the people.

Despite ongoing theological debates surrounding the pejorative labeling of Muslims by followers of Islam Tua, these disputes have yet to be resolved. Adherents of Islam Masade believe that their oral traditions and the transmission of teachings, inherited verbally from ancestors, constitute a doctrinal legacy that must be preserved. This oral heritage constitutes a fundamental aspect of Islam Masade’s uniqueness. The community’s adherence to religious truths integrated into daily life, alongside active participation in communal activities, has enabled the religion to endure peacefully without engendering conflicts commonly observed in other regions.

Efforts by governmental authorities to realign Islam Masade teachings with mainstream Islamic doctrine have proven ineffective, largely because the customs and practices of Islam Masade are deeply embedded within the social fabric. Nevertheless, a cooperative relationship has been established between practitioners of Islam Masade and Islamic mass organizations in the Kecamatan Tabukan Utara area.

Keywords: religious teachings, faith, discipleship

Title: Infestation of Ticks on Cattle in Tolok Village, Tompaso District, Minahasa

Abstract:  
Ticks represent one of the most prevalent ectoparasites affecting livestock, with the capacity to substantially diminish both the quality and quantity of animal products. The consequences of tick infestations encompass local dermal damage, anemia, paralysis induced by tick-borne toxins, and the transmission of various diseases. This study was undertaken over a one-month period in Tolok Village, Minahasa District, with the objective of determining the prevalence of tick infestation in cattle, as well as examining infestation preferences relative to specific body regions, sex, and age categories. Employing a survey methodology, tick specimens were collected during daylight hours, preserved in 70% ethanol, and subsequently quantified within the laboratory of the Faculty of Animal Science at Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. The findings revealed a 100% infestation prevalence among the 53 cattle examined, indicating that all subjects were harboring ticks. Analysis of infestation distribution across body parts indicated the highest mean tick burden in the crotch region (6.70 ticks), followed by the neck (5.55 ticks), abdomen (4.44 ticks), back (3.40 ticks), head (1.75 ticks), and legs (1.11 ticks). When categorized by sex, females exhibited a greater average tick load (32.05 ticks) compared to males (20.65 ticks). Regarding age, calves demonstrated a slightly higher infestation level (average of 27 ticks) relative to adult cattle (26.15 ticks). These results suggest that tick infestation intensity varies according to anatomical location, sex, and age, with calves showing a marginally higher susceptibility than mature cattle.

Keywords: Tick infestation, Cattle, Ectoparasites, Prevalence, Minahasa

Merantau for the sake of education is also considered, as an effort to prove the quality of self as an independent adult and responsible in making decisions. And to actively adjust to the new environment, an overseas student from Jakarta uses various actions to adapt. Adaptation is a key concept in looking at human relationships with the environment. Culture shock is a picture of the profound and negative responses of depression, frustration and disorientation experienced by individuals living in one new environment. The purpose of this research is to find out the adaptation strategy of overseas students from Jakarta at the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences, Sam Ratulangi University Manado. This research uses qualitative descriptive method, because qualitative method as research procedure that produces descriptive data in the form of written or oral words directly. Informants in this study there are 7 overseas students from Jakarta at the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. Data collection techniques used are data collection techniques used, namely observation, interview, and documentation. And data analysis techniques include data reduction, data display, conclusion and verifikas. The results showed that overseas students from Jakarta can adapt by adjusting to such as living independently, by living away from parents or family, by learning new things such as washing dishes and washing their own clothes. Learn to use Manado language in the learning and teaching process, and follow several campus organizations to be able to mingle and get along with other students. Obstacles obstacles in adapting are faced by having an open attitude and accepting all the differences that exist. Keywords : Adaptation, Overseas, Students

Creative employees play a crucial role in meeting the increasingly demanding requirements of the modern work environment. It is essential for managers to empower their employees, thereby fostering confidence in performing tasks creatively. Through managerial empowerment, employees experience psychological empowerment, which in turn enhances their motivation and leads to innovative outcomes for the organization. This study aims to examine both the combined and individual effects of the dimensions of impact, choice, competence, and meaning on employee creativity. Employing a quantitative research design, multiple linear regression analysis was conducted with a sample of 75 employees from the BNI Main Branch Office in Manado. The findings indicate that impact, choice, competence, and meaning have significant simultaneous and partial effects on employee creativity. Consequently, this research recommends that managers at BNI Main Branch Office Manado actively empower and motivate employees by granting them autonomy in selecting work methods, assigning employees to divisions aligned with their competencies, and recruiting individuals driven by genuine passion for their work. Proper implementation of psychological empowerment has the potential to enhance creativity, productivity, and overall employee satisfaction.  

Keywords: creativity, empowerment, psychological empowerment

A survey conducted on Indonesian health data revealed that adolescent knowledge regarding reproductive health remains inadequate; specifically, only 33% of female adolescents and 37% of male adolescents recognized the increased likelihood of pregnancy resulting from sexual intercourse. Overall, adolescent understanding of reproductive health is comparatively low. This study employed a pre-experimental design utilizing a one-group pretest-posttest approach. The research population consisted of 45 students from class X at State Senior High School 7 Manado, selected through purposive sampling. Prior to the implementation of reproductive health education, participants’ knowledge levels were categorized as follows: 7 respondents (15.5%) demonstrated a good level of knowledge, 23 respondents (51.1%) were classified as sufficient, and 15 respondents (33.3%) were categorized as poor. Following the educational intervention, these figures shifted, with 25 respondents (55.6%) achieving a good level, 17 respondents (37.8%) sufficient, and only 3 respondents (6.7%) poor. Quantitatively, the mean knowledge score increased from 63.11% before the intervention to 79.00% afterward. Statistical analysis using a paired t-test yielded a p-value of 0.000, indicating a statistically significant improvement at p < 0.05. Consequently, the findings demonstrate that reproductive health education significantly enhances adolescent knowledge among students at State Senior High School 7 Manado. 

Keywords: health education, reproductive health, adolescent knowledge

Southeast Minahasa has growing tourism potential, however, several tourism objects need attention, such as the marine tourism area. Cooperation between the government, the private sector and the community is urgently needed. The purpose of this research is to identify the potential of marine tourism areas in Southeast Minahasa Regency, to map the zoning of marine tourism areas in Southeast Minahasa Regency. The research was conducted using secondary data analysis methods obtained in several related institutions and equipped with survey methods then assisted by field observations, data analysis including potential objects was carried out by observation and identification. Potential objects are obtained from the tourism object assessment criteria and the assessed assessment technique, then the total score found is classified as applying the interval class method in the low, medium and high categories. The results showed that Lakban Beach was included in a high combined potential. Lumintang Beach, Bentenan Beach, Punten Island and Naga Island (Dakokayu) belong to the mixed potential class. Meanwhile, Baling-Baling Island, Hais Beach and Pasir Panjang Beach are included in the low combined potential class. There are three marine tourism zones, namely the coastal zone, the sea level zone, the underwater zone, the distributionzone for the location of marine tourism areas which are implemented in the form of a Geographical Information System in the form of a thematic map. Keywords: Potential, Maritime Tourism, Zoning.

The organization or forum functions as a collective entity in which individuals convene and collaborate in a rational and systematic manner, aiming to utilize the organization’s resources efficiently and effectively to achieve predetermined objectives. Cooperation typically occurs through interaction patterns among individuals or groups both within and external to the organization. These interaction patterns conform to established rules, norms, beliefs, and values that govern the organization. Over time, such interaction patterns develop into habitual behaviors or a shared organizational culture that regulates member conduct. 

The Student Forum of Tidore Islands City (FOMAKATI) represents a regional social organization based in Manado City, comprising students originating from Tidore Islands City who pursue education in Manado. This forum serves as a platform to facilitate interaction among these students during their academic tenure in Manado. FOMAKATI consists of members with diverse backgrounds, which occasionally gives rise to conflicts. Such conflicts in FOMAKATI primarily manifest through communication breakdowns and factionalism during deliberations, particularly concerning the rotation of the chairmanship. The division of factions, as identified by stewards and members, is rooted in group egocentrism linked to organizational affiliations within Cipayung, resulting in competition for key leadership positions within FOMAKATI.

Conflict resolution within FOMAKATI is conducted through trustee-organized meetings aimed at addressing and resolving disputes. 

Keywords: interaction, FOMAKATI

The Pension Fund is a legal entity that manages and operates a program that promises retirement benefits. Implementation of cash procurement and pension fund payment at PT. Pos Indonesia Branch Manado can be done easily and does not take a long time because it uses a good system and procedures, and can illustrate how the implementation of internal controls on the procurement of cash and pension payments. The research method used in this thesis research is descriptive method whose purpose every data collected is analyzed and then drawn a conclusion and research type used is qualitative descriptive. The results obtained that the system and procedures of cash procurement and payment of pension funds at PT. Pos Indonesia Branch Manado runs well, in accordance with established standards, and is supported by the Fund Distribution system. Implementation of internal controls on the system and procedures of cash procurement and payment of pension funds at PT. Pos Indonesia Branch Manado has been run well because it is implemented in accordance with standard operating policy guidelines procedures and policies of directors.Keywords: System and Procedure, Cash Procurement, Pension Fund Payment.

In Indonesia, diverse cashless payment systems have been integrated into various applications, including online commerce, financial technology, and online transportation services. Nevertheless, providers of online transportation continue to accept cash payments despite the prevalence of cashless alternatives. As these providers strive to enhance customer satisfaction, it is imperative that they also anticipate the potential shift of customers from cash to cashless payment methods. This consideration is essential for the strategic planning of online transportation services. Accordingly, the present study aims to identify the factors influencing customer satisfaction in the context of using the OVO payment method for online transportation. Employing a quantitative approach, data were collected from 146 respondents and analyzed using SMART PLS 3.0. The results indicate that the switching load significantly affects the intention of young online transportation users in Jakarta to switch to the OVO payment method. However, the switching load does not have a significant impact on the satisfaction levels of these young users with the OVO payment system. Additionally, the study reveals that the intention to switch to the OVO payment method significantly influences user satisfaction among online transportation users in Jakarta. These findings suggest that the desire to switch plays a crucial role in determining user satisfaction and should be taken into account by service providers. In particular, providers might consider incorporating attractive elements that facilitate switching, such as offering more competitive promotional programs compared to rivals.

This study aimed to investigate the effects of cattle dung on the growth and biomass of silkworms. The experimental trial was carried out at the Freshwater Aquaculture Center (BPBAT) in Tatelu Village, Dimembe Subdistrict, North Minahasa Regency, North Sulawesi Province, approximately 35 kilometers from Manado city. The growth media utilized consisted of pig manure, chicken manure, cattle dung, and fine sediment, each supplemented with EM4. A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed, involving four treatment groups: Treatment A comprised 500 g each of pig manure, chicken manure, cattle dung, and fine sediment; Treatment B consisted of 600 g pig manure, 400 g chicken manure, 500 g cattle dung, and 500 g fine sediment; Treatment C contained 700 g pig manure, 300 g chicken manure, 500 g cattle dung, and 500 g fine sediment; while Treatment K (control) used 2000 g of fine sediment only. Each treatment was replicated three times. Throughout the experiment, water quality parameters, including temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), nitrate, and nitrite concentrations, were monitored. The findings demonstrated a highly significant impact of the treatments on silkworm growth, although no significant differences were observed in silkworm biomass. The greatest growth, measured at 38 g, was recorded in Treatment A, which also yielded the highest biomass at 1.5 g/cm³. Water quality parameters during the study ranged from 24.3 to 25.4 °C for temperature, 7.1 to 7.3 for pH, 2.7 to 5.7 ppm for DO, 1.1 to 1.4 ppm for nitrate, and 0.011 to 0.201 ppm for nitrite.  
Keywords: cattle dung, growth, biomass, Tubifex sp., aquaculture

This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of songs in enhancing vocabulary mastery among second-grade students at SMP Negeri 3 Merauke, as well as to examine whether the use of songs can increase students' interest in developing their vocabulary skills. The research subjects comprised 30 second-grade students from SMP Negeri 3 Merauke. Employing a qualitative descriptive research design, the study utilized a pretest-posttest approach. Data collection instruments included a vocabulary test and a questionnaire. The vocabulary test, consisting of multiple-choice items, was administered to assess students' progress in English vocabulary mastery. Meanwhile, the questionnaire, composed of five items, was employed to gauge students' attitudes toward the use of songs in English vocabulary instruction. Results indicated a significant improvement in vocabulary mastery, as evidenced by an increase in test scores from 40.66% on the pretest to 87.83% on the posttest. Furthermore, the questionnaire responses revealed that the majority of students perceived songs as a motivating factor that heightened their interest in learning English vocabulary. These findings suggest that incorporating songs into vocabulary teaching can effectively enhance both mastery and student engagement in the learning process.  
Keywords: songs, vocabulary development, vocabulary mastery

Taxation serves as a primary source of revenue for governments worldwide. The existence and implementation of tax systems are crucial to the functioning of the state and its governance. In both developed and developing countries, a portion of the potential state revenue derived from taxes has been allocated to advancing innovation, technology, business enterprises, and national industries. Through taxation, governments are also able to implement policies aimed at stabilizing inflation rates, thereby maintaining price stability. 

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of tax collection methods, specifically the use of forced letters and warning letters, and to assess the extent of their contribution to tax revenue collection at the Pratama Manado Tax Office. The data analysis reveals a significant difference in effectiveness, indicating that the efficacy of tax collection through warning and forced letters was greater in 2011 compared to 2012. Several factors influence the collection of taxes through these methods, including taxpayer negligence in settling tax debts, failure to acknowledge tax liabilities, and the inability of taxpayers to fulfill their tax obligations.

Moreover, the calculations demonstrate that tax collection via warning letters in 2011 and 2012 was less effective relative to collection through forced letters, which proved to be highly effective. Additionally, the contribution of warning letters toward reducing outstanding tax arrears was relatively low when compared to the more substantial impact of forced letters.

Sago baruk (Arenga microcarpa) serves as a carbohydrate-rich food source. This study aims to determine the optimal formulation and preferred analogue for the production of composite rice flour, by evaluating the physicochemical properties of the composite analog flour and obtaining rice starch with increased resistance and enhanced nutritional value. The research procedure involved the extraction of starch from baruk sago, followed by the modification of this starch through Heat Moisture Treatment (HMT). Subsequently, composite flours were prepared by blending the modified sago starch with varying proportions of wheat bulbs purse flour and red bean flour, alongside the manufacture of rice analogues.

A completely randomized design (CRD) was implemented, consisting of seven treatment groups with three replications each. The formulations were as follows: P1 (100% natural sago starch, serving as control), P2 (100% HMT-modified sago starch), P3 (90% HMT-modified sago starch + 5% wheat bulbs purse flour + 5% red bean flour), P4 (80% HMT-modified sago starch + 10% wheat bulbs purse flour + 10% red bean flour), P5 (70% HMT-modified sago starch + 15% wheat bulbs purse flour + 15% red bean flour), P6 (60% HMT-modified sago starch + 20% wheat bulbs purse flour + 20% red bean flour), and P7 (50% HMT-modified sago starch + 25% wheat bulbs purse flour + 25% red bean flour).

To identify the most suitable and consumer-preferred formulation, organoleptic evaluations were conducted assessing flavor, aroma, color, and texture. These sensory assessments were complemented by physical analyses, including texture measurement, colorimetry, gelatinization temperature, Kamba density, and the weight of 100 grains. Chemical analyses were also performed to ascertain moisture content, ash content, protein, fat, starch, amylose, amylopectin concentrations, and in vitro starch digestibility of the treatment with the highest consumer acceptance.

The findings indicated that formulation P6—comprising 60% HMT-modified sago starch, 20% wheat bulbs purse flour, and 20% red bean flour—was the most preferred by consumers. Physical characterization revealed a texture of 2 mm/g.det, a Kamba density of 0.497 g/ml, a 100-grain weight of 4.480 g, color values of L* 36.56, a* 8.56, b* 16.22, and a gelatinization temperature of 65°C with a gelatinization time of 31 minutes. Chemical analysis of this formulation demonstrated a moisture content of 14.10%, ash content of 0.93%, protein content of 5.83%, fat content of 0.20%, starch content of 73.00%, amylose concentration of 20.66%, amylopectin concentration of 52.34%, and an in vitro starch digestibility of 8.68%.

Keywords: rice analogue, sago baruk, starch.

Abstract: 

Regional retributions are levies imposed by local governments that differ from taxes and are based on the government's capacity to provide public services. Among these local government levies is the traditional market retribution, which represents a fee for the use of facilities in traditional or simple markets, such as stalls or shops, managed or provided by the local government for the benefit of specific communities or entities. The government of Ternate City, located in North Maluku Province, is currently prioritizing the development of the goods and services sector. As part of this initiative, the city government has undertaken efforts to enhance the trade and services sector by constructing traditional markets, including the Bahari Berkesan Traditional Hygienic Market. However, recurring conflicts have been observed between market officials and traders, primarily due to unauthorized trading outside designated areas, which disrupts market organization and leads to congestion. Additionally, infrastructure issues related to the comfort and convenience of both traders and buyers have been resolved slowly. This study employs a qualitative research methodology to gain an in-depth understanding of the implementation of the Bahari Berkesan Traditional Hygienic Market retribution policy in Ternate City. Data were collected from nine informants. The findings reveal that key factors influencing the implementation of this policy include communication, available resources, attitudes, and the bureaucratic structure. 

Keywords: Policy implementation, retribution

Marketing strategies are continually refined and enhanced to increase the likelihood of organizational success. Effective marketing is intrinsically linked to the quality of products and the pricing strategies implemented. A diverse product range combined with affordable pricing confers a competitive advantage to businesses operating within the trade sector, as it encourages consumers to engage in repeat purchases. This research aims to examine the impact of product completeness and pricing on consumer repurchase behavior at Freshmart Bahu Manado. Employing a quantitative research design, data were collected from a sample of 60 respondents and subsequently analyzed using multiple regression analysis. The findings indicate a significant effect of both product completeness and pricing on consumer repurchase intentions, as evidenced by the multiple regression and correlation coefficient results. Consequently, the hypothesis asserting that product attributes and pricing influence consumer repurchase behavior is supported. In conclusion, higher product quality and competitive pricing levels correspond to increased consumer repurchase rates, whereas inferior product quality and higher prices are associated with reduced repurchase frequency.  
Keywords: Product Attributes, Pricing, Consumer Repurchase Behavior

This thesis, entitled "The Personal Pronouns of English and Klabra Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify, classify, and analyze the personal pronouns in English and Klabra with respect to their form, function, and meaning. Beyond mere identification and categorization, the research seeks to compare and contrast the similarities and differences between the personal pronouns of English and Klabra, drawing upon Marcella Frank’s theoretical framework (1972:29). The study employs two theoretical perspectives on personal pronouns, namely those proposed by Frank (1972:29) and Bloomfield (1933). Data pertaining to English personal pronouns were sourced from English textbooks and various linguistic publications, while information regarding the Klabra language was collected from native informants via telephone interviews. English, a member of the Germanic branch of the Indo-European language family, contrasts with Klabra, which belongs to the Austronesian language family. The findings indicate that personal pronouns in both English and Klabra can be classified into first, second, and third person categories. The analysis reveals both convergences and divergences; for instance, both languages utilize personal pronouns similarly in their grammatical functions as subjects and objects, and both position pronouns before the verb and after the noun within sentences. However, notable differences exist, such as the English second-person pronoun "you," which serves as both singular and plural, whereas Klabra distinguishes between singular and plural second-person pronouns with "nin" and "nan," respectively.

Keywords: Personal pronouns, Contrastive analysis, English, Klabra language, Function, Meaning

This study discusses the Income Tax Article 23 withholding treatment of a series of transactions conducted by the Freight forwarding . the authors conducted an analysis of the suitability of the practice of withholding tax by Act No. 36 of 2008. Background: Coronaviruses constitute a group of viruses responsible for diseases in both animals and humans, including Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). In humans, infection with these viruses may result in respiratory illnesses varying from mild symptoms such as flu, cough, and common cold to more severe conditions like Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS). The objective of this study was to examine the behavioral responses of coastal communities regarding the prevention of COVID-19 transmission. 

Methods: This descriptive study was carried out between August and December 2020 in Desa Atep Oki, Kecamatan Lembean Timur, involving 80 respondents. The variables assessed included knowledge, attitude, and behavior related to COVID-19 prevention. Data collection instruments comprised questionnaires, photographic documentation, and writing tools. Univariate analysis was used to examine the data.

ABSTRACT ANALYSIS OF INTEGRATED FARMING SYSTEM BETWEEN BEEF CATTLE AND RICE PADDY IN FARMERS GROUP OF KEONG MAS AT SANGKUB DISTRICT, NORTHBOLAANG MONGONDOW REGENCY (CASE STUDY). Integrated farming system of beef cattle and rice paddy is a combination of beef cattle fattening and rice paddy managed by "Keong Mas" Farmers Group. Cost-Volume-Profit (CVP) analysis serves as an essential managerial instrument for profit planning within organizations. This analytical approach facilitates the determination of revenue objectives and the estimation of costs necessary to achieve desired profit levels. The CVP framework encompasses several key elements, such as the contribution margin, break-even point, margin of safety, operating leverage, shutdown point, and profit target analysis. The present study aims to evaluate the profit planning of PT. Air Manado through the application of Cost-Volume-Profit analysis. Employing a descriptive research methodology, the study assesses the financial performance of Cousin Coffee & Eatery in the year 2022. Findings indicate that the establishment successfully covered its fixed costs and generated a profit, reflected by a contribution margin of Rp333,976,953, equivalent to 77%. The break-even sales volume was identified as Rp429,773,456, corresponding to a break-even revenue of Rp31,969,264. Furthermore, the margin of safety—indicating the allowable decrease in sales before incurring losses—was calculated at Rp397,804,192, or 92.56%. Operating leverage was determined to be 1.08, suggesting the sensitivity of operating income to sales fluctuations. The shutdown point, representing the minimum sales level required to cover cash costs, was also Rp31,969,264, implying that sales must exceed this threshold to avoid cessation of operations. To achieve a 50% increase in profit, amounting to Rp309,360,620, Cousin Coffee & Eatery must augment sales to Rp429,773,456. It is projected that variable costs will increase proportionally with the rise in production volume, while fixed costs are assumed to remain constant.

This study is prompted by challenges identified in the archival management at the Bank Perkreditan Rakyat (BPR) office of Prisma Dana Manado, where inefficiencies in work time utilization have led to task accumulation, compounded by limited human resources. The primary objective is to examine the extent to which archival management impacts employee work efficiency at PT. BPR Prisma Dana Manado. Among the issues encountered is the inadequate maintenance of records, evidenced by files being stacked in cabinets, resulting in easy deterioration and difficulty in retrieval when needed, thereby impeding office operations. Consequently, effective and systematic archival management is essential to facilitate prompt and efficient access to records by employees. Organizational arrangement is a critical factor that must be implemented within the office environment to enhance productivity and operational efficiency.

This research employs a descriptive quantitative approach, utilizing a questionnaire administered to a sample of 50 respondents. The instruments were evaluated for validity and reliability prior to data collection. Data analysis involved both descriptive and inferential statistics, including simple correlation coefficient and regression analysis, conducted with SPSS for Windows version 24.0. The findings reveal a significant relationship between archival management and work efficiency. Specifically, the analysis demonstrates that archival management exerts a positive influence on employee work efficiency at PT. BPR Prisma Dana Manado, with an explanatory power of 21.3%. This supports the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis. Based on these results, it is recommended that improvements be made to the filing system to further enhance work efficiency.

Keywords: archival management, work efficiency

The objective of this study was to investigate the physicochemical changes of snake fruit (Salacca spp.) stored at ambient temperature and coated with wax emulsion. The experiment was conducted over a period of approximately four months within an agricultural technology laboratory. A completely randomized factorial design was employed, examining the effects of different wax emulsion mixing ratios and storage durations. The treatments consisted of three wax emulsion formulations: A1 (wax to air ratio of 1:2), A2 (wax to water ratio of 1:4), and A3 (wax to water ratio of 1:6), alongside four storage time intervals: B1 (0 days), B2 (3 days), B3 (6 days), and B4 (9 days), all maintained at room temperature. Physicochemical analyses included measurements of texture, weight, brightness, sucrose content, acidity, and moisture content.

Results indicated that the poorest texture after nine days of storage occurred in fruit treated with the 1:4 wax emulsion ratio (5.21 kg), whereas the highest texture value was observed in the 1:2 ratio treatment (6.34 kg). The greatest weight retention was achieved in the 1:4 ratio group (67.67%), while the lowest was found in the 1:6 ratio (51%). Brightness was highest in the 1:6 treatment (29.88%) and lowest in the 1:4 treatment (29.35%). Sucrose concentration peaked in the 1:2 ratio treatment (14.16%) and was lowest in the 1:4 ratio (13.33%). Acidity was greatest in the 1:4 ratio group (12.33%) and least in the 1:2 ratio (11.8%). Moisture content was highest in the 1:4 ratio (43.33%) and lowest in the 1:6 ratio (43.01%).

In conclusion, snake fruit coated with a wax emulsion at a ratio of 1:4 and stored for nine days at ambient temperature exhibited the most favorable quality attributes.

Keywords: snake fruit, storage, waxing, physicochemical properties

Nutmeg (Myristica fragrans Houtt), an indigenous Indonesian plant, holds significant potential as a commodity for both domestic and international trade. Historically recognized as a valuable spice, nutmeg also serves as a critical source of essential oils utilized across diverse industries, including food, pharmaceuticals, perfumery, and cosmetics (Rukmana, 2004). A notable characteristic of the nutmeg plant is its comprehensive utility, as nearly all parts of the fruit—comprising the aril (the red covering surrounding the seed), the nutmeg seed, and the mace—are employed for various purposes. This study aims to investigate the drying characteristics of nutmeg seeds using rack-type dryers, focusing on parameters such as temperature variation, relative humidity, material weight, airflow rate, air volume flow, moisture content of the material, drying time, and drying rate. Employing a descriptive methodology, the drying process was conducted at temperatures below 55°C and repeated three times until the moisture content reached 8–10% wet basis. Observations revealed that the external relative humidity of the dryer ranged between 83.28% and 89.50%, while the internal relative humidity varied from 86.58% to 97.91%. Throughout the drying period, the moisture content of the nutmeg seeds decreased significantly from an initial 38.75% to an average final value of 18.05%, with specific moisture contents recorded as 6.54%, 8.28%, and 9.70% on the first, second, and third shelves, respectively, over a 12-hour observation period.

Title: Semen Quality of Limousin and Simmental Bulls Maintained in Different Pen Configurations at the Lembang Artificial Insemination Institution

Abstract:  
This study investigates the impact of pen housing configurations on the semen quality of Limousin and Simmental bulls maintained at the Lembang Artificial Insemination Institution in West Java. Bulls were housed intensively in animal houses and pens designed to protect them from environmental stressors such as sunlight, rain, high wind speeds, and predators. The objective was to compare semen quality parameters between bulls kept individually in single pens (SB) and those housed in pairs within double pens (DB). Both primary and secondary reproductive data were collected for Limousin and Simmental bulls and analyzed using the t-test statistical method.

The findings revealed that the average semen volume in bulls housed singly (SB) was 9.54 ± 2.19 mL per ejaculation, which was significantly higher by 7.67% compared to bulls housed in pairs (DB), which had an average volume of 8.86 ± 1.79 mL per ejaculation. Sperm motility percentages did not differ significantly between the SB group (70.10 ± 2.37%) and the DB group (71.00 ± 2.67%). Additionally, the average sperm mass movement score was significantly greater in the SB group (1.94 ± 0.24), reflecting a 5.43% increase in vigor compared to the DB group (1.84 ± 0.37). The mean semen pH values for bulls in SB (6.66 ± 0.11) and DB (6.64 ± 0.10) conditions showed no significant difference.

Correlation analysis of reproductive parameters across both pen types and breeds indicated no significant relationships among the measured variables, with correlation coefficients ranging from -0.29 to 0.18. In conclusion, semen quality in Limousin and Simmental bulls housed individually was superior to that of bulls maintained in pairs. Furthermore, reproductive traits were independent of one another regardless of pen configuration.

Keywords: Pen Type, Semen Quality, Simmental Bull, Limousin Bull

This thesis, entitled "Anxiety in the Novel *Thirteen Reasons Why* by Jay Asher," constitutes a partial fulfillment of the requirements for obtaining the Sarjana degree at the Faculty of Humanities, Manado. The study aims to identify and analyze the manifestations of anxiety and its impact on the characters within Jay Asher’s *Thirteen Reasons Why*. Characterization, including the identification of different types of anxiety, is systematically examined. Methodologically, this research employs a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic approaches. The intrinsic approach encompasses the literary elements of the novel, while the extrinsic approach involves psychological concepts related to anxiety and its various categories. The theoretical framework is primarily based on Freud’s psychological theory of anxiety as referenced in Minderop (2010), supplemented by theoretical insights from Davison, Neale, and Kring (2012), and further informed by Roberts’ (1983) paradigm. The study utilizes descriptive analytical methods. Findings indicate that the characters Clay Jensen, Hannah Baker, and Mr. Porter exhibit anxiety. Specifically, Clay Jensen experiences objective anxiety and is diagnosed with phobia disorder, panic disorder, and generalized anxiety disorder. Hannah Baker is also identified as having objective anxiety, categorized under panic disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder, while Mr. Porter displays objective anxiety. The consequences of anxiety are observed as recklessness in Clay Jensen, and depression in both Hannah Baker and Mr. Porter. Notably, Hannah Baker’s depression culminates in her suicide, which significantly impacts the narrative as a major event.  

Keywords: Literature, Anxiety, Psychological Analysis, *Thirteen Reasons Why*

The purpose of this study is to examine and compare the added value and profitability of processing salak fruit into dodol salak, differentiated by the type of harvest. The research was carried out over a three-month period from April to June 2018 at UD Mandiri, located in Pangu I Village, Ratahan District, Southeast Minahasa. Primary data were collected through interviews with the business owner using structured questionnaires. The analysis of added value employed the formula NTp = Na - (Bb + Bp + Bbp), while profit analysis utilized the formula π = TR - TC. The findings indicate that the added value generated from the dodol salak business during the large harvest (panen raya) amounted to Rp. 19,399,652.78, compared to Rp. 18,649,652.78 during the medium harvest (panen sedang), and Rp. 17,749,652.78 during the small harvest (panen kecil). Correspondingly, the profits from the dodol salak business were Rp. 8,499,652.78 for the large harvest, Rp. 7,749,652.78 for the medium harvest, and Rp. 6,849,652.78 for the small harvest. The added value during the large harvest was 9.30% higher than that observed in the small harvest and 4.02% greater than in the medium harvest. Regarding profitability, the large harvest yielded profits that were 24.09% greater than those of the small harvest and 9.68% higher than those of the medium harvest.

Piracy represents a detrimental consequence of technological advancement, with its negative effects felt globally, including in Indonesia. Despite these adverse impacts, numerous individuals engage in piracy activities, disregarding the ethical implications of their actions in pursuit of personal gain. This study aims to elucidate the perceptions and attitudes of consumers towards optical disc and online piracy in Manado, focusing specifically on university students from five institutions: De La Salle University, Nusantara University, Politeknik University, Pembangunan Indonesia University, and Sam Ratulangi University. Employing a qualitative research methodology within a case study framework, the investigation provides a descriptive analysis of the piracy phenomenon. The research sample comprises 14 university students from Manado who participate in piracy activities. The findings reveal that although these students recognize piracy as illegal and unethical, the advantages offered by pirated products—such as lower cost, easy accessibility, and widespread availability—lead them to prefer these goods over original products, thereby overlooking the moral and legal considerations. The persistence of piracy under current conditions suggests its continued existence in the future. Accordingly, this study recommends that governmental bodies and relevant organizations implement effective measures, including enhanced law enforcement, improved information dissemination, advanced security technologies, and educational programs, to combat piracy. 

Keywords: consumer perceptions, attitudes, piracy, online.

**Abstract**  
This study investigates the digestibility of local and imported feeds in Indonesian child racehorses, aiming to evaluate their capacity to utilize different feed sources. Nutrient digestibility serves as a critical indicator of feed ingredient quality and its suitability for equine consumption. Using a t-test statistical analysis, data were collected through interviews and direct observations at racehorse breeding facilities. The local feed components examined included corn, rice bran, fish meal, soybean, mung beans, and coconut cake, whereas the imported feed comprised Sustaina. Measurements involved quantifying the intake of forage and concentrates and subsequent fecal output (g/head/day). A total of 12 fecal samples were obtained from 8 horses fed local feed and 4 horses fed imported feed. The primary variables assessed were energy digestibility and protein digestibility. Findings revealed that digestible energy values were 85.92% for local feed and 87.58% for imported feed, while protein digestibility was 75.86% and 86.89%, respectively. Statistical analysis indicated no significant difference (P > 0.05) in the energy digestibility between local and imported feeds; however, protein digestibility was significantly higher (P < 0.01) in horses consuming imported feed compared to those on local feed. These results suggest that imported feeds provide superior protein digestibility relative to local feedstuffs.  

**Keywords:** Equine nutrition, local feed, imported feed, nutrient digestibility, racehorses

The potential of a tourist attraction plays a significant role in shaping an individual’s motivation and purpose for travel. Tourist attractions constitute the primary factors influencing tourists' decisions to select specific destinations, especially as tourism has become an essential aspect of contemporary life. Various motivations drive tourists to choose destinations, including personal interests, novelty, popularity, aesthetic appeal, therapeutic benefits, and personal fulfillment. In the context of religious tourism particularly, visitors typically possess a clear intention and motivation, which enables them to derive meaningful experiences from their visits. This study aims to examine and elucidate the potential of religious tourism sites, specifically focusing on the Prayer Hill in Tomohon City. The motivations for tourists visiting this site include photography, relaxation, as well as devotional practices such as praying and worship. Effective governance, strategic management, and proper organization and positioning of the Prayer Hill site significantly contribute to enhancing the visitors’ spiritual renewal and the overall effectiveness of religious tourism at this location. Moreover, the distinctive features and iconic status of the Prayer Hill in Tomohon City render it a preferred and prominent destination for religious tourism, surpassing other similar attractions. 

Keywords: potential, tourism objects, religious tourism

ABSTRACTThe purpose of this study was to analyze the landslide prone areas in Sub Watershed of Tondano in order to obtain the vulnerability information and dissemination in the form of map by using the Geographic Information Systems. The study was conducted by using a Descriptive Method which consisted of a survey and map overlay, while the identification of areas prone to landslides using the scoring method. Parameters measured were soil type , slope , elevation , land use and rainfall . The results showed that the spread of landslide-prone areas in the Sub Watershed of Tondano consisted of five classes of landslide susceptibility, namely (1) No class landslide prone area of 993.12 ha, or 23.64%, spread over an area of 137.42 ha districts Eris, Kakas of 1.31 ha and 854.39 ha area of East Tondano; (2) The low vulnerability class area of 207.59 ha, or 4.94%, spread over an area of 144.10 ha district of Eris, Kakas area of 0.29 ha and 63.20 ha area of East Tondano; (3) Moderate impact class area of 894.19 ha, or 21.28% spread over an area of 503.06 ha district of Eris, Kakas area of 114.97 ha and 276.16 ha area of East Tondano; (4) High vulnerability class area of 469.23 ha, or 11.17% spread over an area of 256.27 ha district of Eris, Kakas area of 48.03 ha and 164.93 ha area of East Tondano; (5) Highest area of 1637.23 ha or 38.97% spread over area of 455.60 ha district of Eris, Kakas area of 45.46 ha and 1136.17 ha area of East Tondano.Key Words : Mapping, Landslide, Sub Watershed of Tondano, GIS (Geographic Information System)

Tourism development serves as a strategic approach to enhancing the local economy while simultaneously supporting governmental policies. From a social perspective, tourism activities broaden employment opportunities not only through the construction and enhancement of facilities and infrastructure but also via various business sectors that are either directly or indirectly connected to tourism. Economically, tourism can generate substantial job creation and business opportunities. The increasing number of visitors to Batu Pinagut Beach exemplifies the growth of tourism in the area. This expansion has led to multifaceted impacts—both positive and negative—on the environmental, economic, social, and cultural conditions of the local communities, particularly those residing in North Boroko. It is important to emphasize that tourism development should not be conducted for the sole benefit of the tourist industry; rather, it must be grounded in the principle of "tourism for the community," prioritizing the public interest and addressing community needs. With community-based tourism development, residents have experienced an improvement in their income levels, which is reflected in the transition from traditional wooden homes to more permanent structures with solid walls and enhanced household amenities. Furthermore, the increase in revenue has positively influenced educational opportunities, enabling parents who previously lacked financial means to support their children's schooling to now afford higher levels of education.

Keywords: tourism, impact, community

The source of the Regional Original Revenue is local tax, one of which is parking tax. In this study, it was described how the practice of parking tax collection, parking tax collection function, contribution and participation in increasing the original regional income of Bitung City, while the research method used was using a qualitative descriptive approach. One source of funds that comes from regional capacity itself is Regional Original Revenue. From the results of this study indicate that the contribution of Parking Tax to support the Original Revenue of Bitung City in 2015-2017 tends to decrease. In 2015 where parking tax had the highest contribution of 152.89% and the low contribution can be seen in 2017 which was 89.17%. The decrease in the contribution of parking tax was due to several causes, namely in fulfilling the taxation regulations that apply to taxpayers lacking a good understanding so that taxpayers have the awareness to pay their due taxes, found several new parking spaces and it is known that they have not been registered as regional taxpayers In addition, there is income from a parking lot whose income cannot be estimated so that the parking lot does not pay the due tax.Keywords : Collection, Parking Tax and Local Revenue

Griya Paniki Indah (GPI) housing represents one of the largest residential complexes in North Sulawesi, comprising over 7,000 housing units. This extensive settlement has fostered a conducive environment for the proliferation of online food vending enterprises aimed at fulfilling the culinary needs of its residents. The present Community Service Program (PKM) targets the enhancement of these online food sellers, predominantly micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), whose numbers have been steadily increasing. However, consumer dissatisfaction frequently arises, primarily due to discrepancies between product quality and its online descriptions, delivery times exceeding one hour, and inconsistent product standards. Recognizing the economic productivity of this online food seller cohort, the program seeks to mitigate customer dissatisfaction by implementing comprehensive training designed to impart knowledge and understanding of quality management principles. These principles encompass key attributes such as performance, features, reliability, conformance, durability, serviceability, aesthetics, and consumer perception. Furthermore, the initiative promotes strategies for holistic quality enhancement through the adoption of Total Quality Management (TQM) components, including customer focus, quality obsession, long-term commitment, teamwork, continuous system improvement, education and training, unity of purpose, as well as employee involvement and empowerment.

Title: Growth Performance of Grower-Finisher Pigs Fed Diets Incorporating Coffee Pulp Flour as Partial Substitute for Fine Bran

Abstract:  
This study investigates the potential of utilizing coffee fruit skin, an underexploited by-product with a crude fiber content of 33.60%, as a partial replacement for fine bran in swine diets. North Sulawesi’s Bolaang Mongondow region, a prominent coffee-producing area with a plantation size of 4,097.7 hectares yielding 2,135.46 tons of raw coffee material, generates substantial amounts of coffee pulp as a by-product following the separation of coffee fruit from leaves and stems. Annually, approximately 1,288.22 tons of coffee fruit are processed, yielding around 448.45 tons of coffee fruit skin.

This 66-day experimental study, including a 14-day preliminary phase, aimed to evaluate the effects of substituting fine bran with coffee pulp flour on the production performance of grower to finisher pigs. Sixteen pigs (male and female), aged 12 to 16 weeks of Yorkshire and Landrace descent, were assigned to four treatment groups arranged in a randomized block design. The treatments comprised graded substitution levels of coffee pulp flour at 0%, 25%, 50%, and 75% replacing fine bran. Body weight variations served as replications for statistical analysis.

Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed that replacing fine bran with coffee husk powder significantly influenced weight gain (P < 0.05), whereas feed intake showed no statistically significant differences among treatment groups (P > 0.05). Feed conversion efficiency was also significantly affected by the inclusion of coffee pulp flour. These findings indicate that incorporating coffee pulp as a partial substitute for fine bran in grower-finisher pig diets can promote favorable growth performance and enhance feed utilization efficiency.

Keywords: grower phase, finisher phase, coffee pulp flour, swine nutrition, feed substitution

This study aims to examine the growth of credit disbursed by Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) within the agricultural sector, to analyze the trends in credit financing for both agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, and to assess the occurrence of non-performing loans (NPLs) at BRI. The research was conducted at PT. Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, specifically focusing on the Tondano branch in Minahasa District. The investigation concentrated on selected BRI units responsible for lending to the agricultural sector, namely the Langowan, Kawangkoan, Tondano, and Sonder branches. Data were analyzed employing both quantitative and qualitative descriptive methods and subsequently presented in tabular form. The findings reveal a consistent year-on-year increase in financing plans and credit disbursement by the Tondano BRI branch to the agricultural sector in Minahasa. This is evidenced by financing achievements exceeding the predetermined targets. Furthermore, there was a notable rise in both agricultural and non-agricultural financing through BRI credit schemes such as KUR Mikro and KKP-E between 2011 and 2013. However, challenges in credit repayment were identified, with the NPL rate for the non-agricultural sector reaching 50%, contrasted with a 20% NPL rate in the agricultural sector. These issues are attributed primarily to borrowers' inability to fulfill their debt obligations.

This study seeks to evaluate the effectiveness of land and building tax collection in Kamanga Dua Village, located within the Tompaso Subdistrict. Employing a descriptive-qualitative research design, the investigation utilizes both primary and secondary data sources. Data collection was conducted through interviews and direct field observations. Subsequently, the gathered data were analyzed using percentage analysis techniques to assess the efficacy of tax collection, while interview data were subjected to interactive analysis methods.

The findings indicate that (1) the collection of land and building taxes in Kamanga Dua Village, Tompaso Subdistrict, Minahasa District, is categorized as "not yet effective," with an average annual achievement equating to 100 percent against a target set at 30.15 million rupiah per year. (2) The inefficiency in tax collection observed in 2017 is attributed to several factors, including the administrative transition of tax management from the central government to district/city authorities. This shift resulted in limited time for tax officials to effectively disseminate relevant information to taxpayers. Additionally, there exists a perception that tax revenues are not fully allocated toward regional development, accompanied by suspicions of misuse by certain parties.

To improve the attainment of tax revenue targets in Kamanga Dua Village, it is recommended that tax collection officers be equipped with enhanced skills through specialized training programs facilitated by government authorities. Furthermore, to optimize revenue outcomes and meet established goals, village officials should actively disseminate up-to-date information to taxpayers regarding any modifications to tax collection policies.

Keywords: Effectiveness, Land and Building Tax Collection

Electronic banking (e-Banking) is a digital payment system that facilitates a variety of financial transactions for clients of banks and other financial institutions via their official websites. The adoption of e-Banking has become prevalent across both developed and developing nations globally. In Indonesia, the number of e-Banking users has experienced substantial growth, rising from 13.6 million in 2012 to 50.3 million in 2016. This study aims to examine the differences in e-Banking services between Bank Central Asia and Bank Mandiri within the city of Manado. Employing a quantitative research design, this investigation utilizes an independent sample t-test on a sample comprising 100 customers from each bank. The findings indicate a significant difference in e-Banking services delivered through Banking Mobile Applications—including Mobile Banking, Internet Banking, and SMS Banking—between the two banks. Conversely, no significant difference was observed in Automated Teller Machine (ATM) services between Bank Central Asia and Bank Mandiri in Manado. Based on these outcomes, it is recommended that Bank Mandiri further enhance its e-Banking application system to improve and sustain customer satisfaction.  
Keywords: electronic banking, banking mobile application, mobile banking, internet banking, SMS banking, automated teller machine

Background: Cryptococcal meningitis is an opportunistic infection commonly affecting patients with AIDS. Accurate diagnosis is critical for initiating standardized antifungal treatment, yet it remains challenging. The Lateral Flow Assay (LFA) is a straightforward antigen detection method currently under development, whereas India ink staining is the conventional microscopic technique for identifying the pathogen in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) but requires a skilled examiner. 

Objective: This study aimed to evaluate whether LFA could detect a greater number of cryptococcal meningitis cases compared to India ink staining at R.D. Kandou Hospital in Manado.

Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted using CSF samples from hospitalized AIDS patients with intracranial opportunistic infections who underwent CSF examination. The diagnostic outcomes of CSF LFA and India ink staining were compared on a per-patient basis, alongside an assessment of their clinical characteristics. 

Results: Six eligible patients were identified, among whom two tested positive for cryptococcal meningitis. All subjects were male, aged between 31 and 40 years. Headache was reported in five patients, and altered consciousness was also noted. Routine CSF analysis revealed mean protein concentrations of 30 g/dL and 145 g/dL in LFA/India ink positive and negative cases, respectively. Concordance between tests was observed: all samples positive by India ink were also positive by LFA; similarly, samples negative by India ink were negative by LFA.

Conclusion: In this cohort, CSF LFA did not demonstrate superiority over India ink staining for the detection of cryptococcal meningitis. Nonetheless, LFA presents an operational advantage in settings lacking skilled personnel capable of performing India ink examinations.

Keywords: Cryptococcal meningitis, Lateral Flow Assay, India ink staining

This study aims to determine the effect of Non-Performing Loans, Loan to Deposit Ratios, Return On Assets, and Capital Adequacy Ratios on the Prediction of Potential Financial Distress in State-Owned Banks in Indonesia for the 2014-2021 Period partially or simultaneously. The data in this study are 32 data, namely 8 years of time series data and 4 state-owned banks. The data analysis used in this research is multiple regressions. The results of the study show that (1) Non-Performing Loans (NPL) have an effect on the prediction of potential financial distress in state-owned banks in Indonesia for the period 2014-2021. (2) Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR) has no effect on the prediction of potential financial distress at state-owned banks in Indonesia for the period 2014-2021. (3) Return on Assets (ROA) has an effect on the prediction of potential financial distress at state-owned banks in Indonesia for the 2014-2021 periods. (4) Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) affects the prediction of potential financial distress in state-owned banks in Indonesia for the period 2014-2021. (5) Non-Performing Loans (NPL), Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), Return On Assets (ROA), and Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) simultaneously affect the prediction of potential financial distress in BUMN Banks in Indonesia for the period 2014-2021 with a value of the coefficient of determination is 97.68%. As for the ability of other variables in explaining the prediction of potential financial distress of 2.32% which is thought to be the market ratio variable, the efficiency ratio (BOPO), and corporate banking investment.

Ensuring the provision of adequate drinking water to villagers constitutes a fundamental component of governmental efforts to fulfill one of humanity’s essential needs. The intrinsic and fundamental demand for water continues to rise in tandem with population growth, lifestyle improvements, and economic advancement. The PAMSIMAS program represents a cornerstone initiative by the government aimed at delivering clean water and sanitation services to rural and suburban communities through participatory, community-based strategies. Initiated in 2008, the program has successfully expanded access to potable water and sanitation in these areas. Moreover, it contributes to fostering the adoption of hygienic practices and the promotion of a clean and healthy lifestyle among the population.

Effectiveness in this context is defined as the extent to which the program's targets—pertaining to quantity, quality, and timeliness—have been achieved, with higher percentages indicating greater effectiveness. This study adopts a descriptive qualitative methodology, selected to elucidate the current conditions of the subject matter by interpreting empirical data collected via observations, interviews, and document analysis.

Program monitoring, entailing the supervision and evaluation of activities to ensure alignment with objectives, has been identified as inadequately implemented within the PAMSIMAS framework at the village government level, which serves as the supervisory entity. Notably, discrepancies exist between program objectives and actual water availability, as supply volumes remain insufficient to meet community demand. Efforts by village authorities to disseminate information about the program have been conducted through socialization initiatives within the community.

Coordination and supervision by village governments in collaboration with PAMSIMAS management have been undertaken; however, it is recommended that program targets be broadened to more effectively address community needs. Continuous socialization efforts are necessary to maintain engagement, alongside enhanced community oversight of program management to improve accountability and outcomes.

Keywords: Program Implementation, Monitoring, Socialization, Target Achievement, Water Supply.

ABSTRACT This research entitled Phonological Variation of Black American English in the Songs of Alicia Keys, and focuses on Alicia Keys's fifth album, 'The Diary of Alicia Keys'. Black American English is a unique English varieties that growing in the black Americans society, it have a different grammar and pronounce. This research is conducted by using a descriptive method. In collecting data, the first thing that the writer do is taking the lyrics from internet. Then, identifies those words that contains this variation. In analyzing data, the writer uses the theory of Rickford (1999) about phonological features of African American Vernacular English. The result of this research shows that there are some variations of African American Vernacular English in the songs of Alicia Keys, especially in the album 'The Diary of Alicia Keys'. Such as: Reduction of word final consonants clusters, especially those ending in t and the ed suffix pronounced as /t/, Deletion of word-final single consonant, Realization of final ng /ŋ/ as n /n/, Realization of voiceless th /θ/ as t, Realization of voiced /ð/ as d, Deletion or vocalization of l after a vowel, Deletion or vocalization of r after a vowel, Deletion of initial d and g in certain tense-aspect auxiliaries, Deletion of unstressed initial, Monophthongal pronunciation of ay, and ey, Most of the songs that sings by a black people have a different variation because their daily activities. The writer hopes that this study would give more knowledge to the readers in understanding the phonological variations of the Black American English, in the Faculty of Humanity, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. Keywords: The Phonological Variations, Black American English/African American Vernacular English

This study seeks to ascertain the extent to which the income of employees at Mas Gendon’s tofu factory contributes to their household earnings. The research was carried out in North Karombasan Village, located in the North District of Manado City. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized for this investigation. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with the factory’s owners and workers via structured questionnaires, whereas secondary data were gathered from monograph records and online resources. The sample consisted of five respondents, selected using a census approach to include the entire population. The variables examined in this study included respondent characteristics, family members’ income, motivations for employment, and the distribution of workers’ time. Analytical techniques involved assessments of family income and its corresponding contributions. Findings indicate that workers at Mas Gendon’s tofu factory earn a monthly wage of IDR 2,000,000, supplemented by housing and meal provisions. Workers allocate approximately 1.8 hours per day to domestic tasks, 16 hours to productive activities, and 6.2 hours to other activities. The income generated by the workers accounts for 76.92% of the total family income, a proportion deemed very substantial according to contribution criteria (i.e., exceeding 50%). Conversely, income from other family members represents 23.08% and is classified within the moderate contribution category.
