Background: On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) officially declared the coronavirus outbreak a global pandemic. This declaration impacted countries worldwide, including Indonesia, leading to restrictions on activities outside the home, particularly limiting physical activity. Body image, knowledge, and attitudes have been identified as factors influencing physical activity levels. This study aimed to examine the associations between body image, knowledge, and attitudes and the level of physical activity among students of the Faculty of Public Health, Sam Ratulangi University (FKM UNSRAT) during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Methods: Employing a quantitative research design, this study utilized survey methods alongside associative (correlational) analysis techniques. A purposive sampling strategy was adopted to select participants. The research was conducted in January 2021 among FKM UNSRAT students with an interest in Occupational Health and Safety (K3). The sample comprised 60 students drawn from the overall population. Physical activity was designated as the dependent variable, while body image, knowledge, and attitudes served as independent variables. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using univariate and bivariate methods, with the chi-square test applied for statistical analysis. Findings were presented both in tabular and narrative formats.

Results: The findings revealed that 92% of students with a satisfactory body image engaged in sufficient physical activity. Furthermore, 85% of students possessing good knowledge levels and 80% demonstrating positive attitudes reported adequate physical activity levels. Bivariate analysis indicated statistically significant correlations between body image, knowledge, attitudes, and the level of physical activity among FKM UNSRAT students during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Conclusion: This study concludes that body image, knowledge, and attitudes are significantly correlated with physical activity levels among students at FKM UNSRAT during the COVID-19 pandemic.

This study investigates the potential of pangi seed extract (Pangium edule Reinw) as a natural preservative alternative for broiler meat by examining its impact on shelf life and durability. The experimental materials included fresh broiler meat, pangi seeds (Pangium edule Reinw), water, distilled water (aquadest), and nutrient agar (NA) media. Employing a completely randomized design with a split-plot arrangement (3x4), the treatments consisted of varying concentrations of pangi seed extract—A0: 0 mL, A1: 3 mL, A2: 6 mL, and A3: 9 mL—alongside different observation times—B0: 0 hours, B1: 6 hours, and B2: 12 hours—at a controlled room temperature of 27 °C. Each treatment was replicated three times. Statistical analysis revealed that both the concentration of pangi seed extract and storage duration significantly influenced (P < 0.05) the total microbial counts, while no significant effects (P > 0.05) were observed on the moisture content and pH levels of the broiler meat. The findings indicate that injecting 9 mL of pangi seed extract into broiler meat effectively preserves its quality for up to 12 hours at room temperature. 

Keywords: Broiler meat, Pangi seed extract, Preservation.

This search aimed to determine the shelf life of seaweed seedlings that are packaged using banana and sponge fronds in Styrofoam, determine the best seaweed packaging media in preventing damage or disease when seedlings are planted. The study was conducted for 5 weeks, from January to February 2020. Observation of seaweed seedlings was conducted at the Laboratory of Fish Health, Environment and Toxicology, Faculty of Fisheries and Marine Sciences and planting tests were carried out in Arakan Village, Tatapaan District. South Minahasa Regency.The research method was carried out in the form of: packing Kappaphycus alvarezii seaweed, observing seaweed seeds and planting test. The experiment was designed according to a factorial completely randomized 3 x 3 design so that there were two factors tested in this experiment, namely the packaging medium factor and the shelf life. The packaging medium factor (A), consists of the level ie, (a1) control / without medium, (a2) banana fronds, (a3) sponge; while the shelf life factor (B), consists of three levels namely, (b1) 24 hours, (b2) 36 hours and (b3) 48 hours with three treatments and three replications so that the total number is 27 units of experiment with the number of seeds needed as much as 108 kg. The treatments taken are A: control, B: Packaging seaweed seeds with the addition of banana midrib, C: Packaging seaweed seeds with the addition of a sponge. The data obtained were analyzed ANOVA statistics for factorial RAL using the JMP (SAS-institute) statistical program. The results of the analysis of the variance showed that differences in treatment (the combination between the storage medium and the shelf life) had a very significant effect on differences in the texture and color of seaweed ("P" <0.0001). However, the effect of the storage medium factor on the texture of seaweed did not change significantly at the time of the change in the shelf life factor level ("P" = 0.1664).

Supervision constitutes a fundamental function of management within organizations, defined as the process of monitoring and assessing activities. In the workplace, established regulations must be adhered to by all personnel. The absence of supervision within organizational activities leads to a decline in work discipline, consequently impeding other operations and obstructing the achievement of organizational objectives. Companies, including Sintesa Peninsula Hotel Manado, aim to deliver satisfactory service to customers; therefore, the hotel must ensure the provision of optimal and valuable services. To achieve this, employees are required to exhibit diligence and commitment in their tasks, especially given that hotel operations are closely tied to punctuality. Poor service delivery results in customer dissatisfaction. This study employed a quantitative research method to examine the influence of supervision on employee work discipline at Sintesa Peninsula Hotel Manado. The findings reveal that supervision positively impacts employee work discipline, affirming its significant role in the operational effectiveness of the hotel. 

Keywords: Supervision, Work Discipline

Background: Diarrhea is characterized by the passage of three or more loose or liquid stools per day, or by an increase in stool frequency beyond an individual's normal pattern. Research Objective: This study aimed to examine the association between hand-washing behavior and the incidence of diarrhea among students at Manado Advent Sario Elementary School. Methods: Employing a cross-sectional survey design, the study population consisted of all active sixth-grade students present and attending classes at the time of data collection. Purposive random sampling was utilized to select a sample of 31 children. Results: Findings revealed that 31 children (90.3%) demonstrated proper hand-washing behavior using soap, whereas 4 children (9.7%) exhibited inadequate hand-washing practices. In terms of diarrhea incidence within the past six months, 9 children (29%) experienced at least one episode, while 22 children (71%) reported no such occurrences. Conclusion: Statistical analysis indicated a significant relationship between hand-washing behavior with soap and the occurrence of diarrhea among primary school children at Manado Advent Sario Elementary School (p = 0.03). This underscores the importance of hand hygiene in reducing diarrheal incidence in this population.  
Keywords: hand-washing with soap, diarrhea incidence, school children

This study, conducted by Maria Esria Lumban Gaol, Dra. Theresia M. C. Lasut, M.Hum, and Dra. Hetty Pelealu, S.H., M.Hum, is entitled "Negative Sentences in the Song Lyrics of the Album No.6 Collaboration Project by Ed Sheeran." The primary aims of this research are to identify, classify, and analyze the various forms of negative sentences present in the song lyrics, as well as to elucidate their grammatical functions and categories. Employing a descriptive methodological approach, the study draws upon the theoretical frameworks proposed by Aarts and Aarts (1982) and Thomson and Martinet (1968: 107) to guide the data analysis. The dataset consists of song lyrics extracted from Ed Sheeran’s 2019 album No.6 Collaboration Project. The findings reveal a total of 130 negative sentences within the lyrics, which are categorized into three principal forms: negative sentences constructed with the word "not" (49 instances), negative sentences utilizing the periphrastic "do" (45 instances), and negative sentences employing negative expressions (36 instances). Notably, negative sentences formed with "not" in conjunction with modal verbs such as dare, need, and used, as well as those involving negative expressions like none, hardly, and hardly ever, were not observed in the analyzed data. Regarding grammatical functions, negative sentences serve as Subject (Su), Predicator (P), Direct Object (DO), Adverbial (A), and Complement. In terms of syntactic categories, these sentences encompass Noun Phrases (NP), Verb Phrases (VP), Adjective Phrases (Adj. P), and Prepositional Phrases (Prep. P).

Keywords: Negative Sentences, Descriptive Analysis, Grammatical Functions, Syntactic Categories, No.6 Collaboration Project (2019)

This study investigates biogas production derived from the combined use of cow and pig feces. The research was conducted at the Bailang Abattoir in Manado, North Sulawesi. The materials utilized included cow feces, pig feces, and water, mixed in a ratio where cow feces constituted two buckets, pig feces one bucket, and water three buckets, corresponding to a 1:1 ratio. The experimental apparatus comprised a horizontal-type digester, measuring instruments, a thermometer, a pH indicator, a biogas stove, hoses, barrels, and buckets. Descriptive analysis was employed to analyze the collected data. Key variables monitored throughout the study included biogas volume, temperature, pH levels, and the practical application of the produced biogas. Over the 31-day experimental period, a total biogas volume of 122,266,262 m³ was generated. The average recorded temperatures were 31ºC during morning measurements and 30ºC in the afternoon, with a consistent pH value of 7 observed throughout. Biogas quality testing was performed twice, initially on day 15 and subsequently on day 31. The generated biogas was effectively utilized for cooking, requiring approximately 24 minutes to complete the cooking process. In conclusion, the combination of cow and pig feces maintained at a temperature of 30–31ºC and a neutral pH of 7 yielded a biogas volume of 122,266,262 cm³, capable of sustaining cooking activities for 24 minutes.  

Keywords: biogas, cow feces, pig feces

ABSTRACT ANALYSIS OF SAFETY MARGIN ON "MERRYLAND" QUAIL POULTRY FARM AT KALI VILLAGE PINELENG DISTRICT OF MINAHASA REGENCY. Government goods/services procurement is the mechanism of government spending that absorbs the most budget. According to LKPP, every year the procurement of goods/services absorbs a budget of around 40% of the APBN and APBD. Due to the large budget in the procurement of goods/services so the possibility of deviation is very large. One of the Government's efforts to prevent fraud is to implement a new type of audit, the probity audit of goods/services procurement. But seeing the current conditions that there are still many cases of corruption in the procurement of goods / services even though a probity audit has been applied, it indicates that the probity audit carried out does not meet the expected objectives. This study aimed to find out what are the problems in implementing a probity audit and the steps that must be taken to overcome the problems that arise in the conduct of a probity audit. This study uses a qualitative method with a case study approach to the Regional Inspectorate of North Sulawesi Province. The Regional Inspectorate of North Sulawesi Province was chosen because it has conducted a probity audit from 2015 to 2019. The informants in this study were functional officials (Auditors and P2UPD) who carried out probity audits, starting from the level of Team Members, Team Leaders and Technical Controllers. The results of the study found that there were still many problems in implementing the probity audit by the Regional Inspectorate of North Sulawesi Province. Problems exist at each stage of the probity audit, starting from the preparation stage to the follow-up stages of the results of the audit, among others there are no internal policies related to the implementation of the audit probity, in house training has not been carried out optimally, the implementation of the audit probity is not real time and is only carried out once a year, there is still a lack of auditors who are competent in goods / services audits, audits do not have enough time, physical audits and market price comparisons are not carried out and correction action to the problem found of probity audits is not carried out.

PT. Sapta Sari Tama is a national enterprise specializing in the distribution of pharmaceuticals. Due to the extensive variety of products and the frequent movement of goods in and out of inventory, potential issues may arise, including discrepancies between the physical stock in the warehouse and the quantities recorded in inventory records, as well as risks of loss or theft. Consequently, effective internal control over the inventory and warehousing processes is essential to prevent fraudulent activities in operational tasks. This study aims to evaluate the adequacy of internal controls pertaining to the inventory and warehousing cycles at PT. Sapta Sari Tama. Employing a qualitative research approach, the study is presented descriptively. Data collection was conducted through direct surveys at PT. Sapta Sari Tama and interviews with various company informants. Keywords: Analysis, Internal Control, Inventory, Warehousing, PSAK No. 14

This study examines the influence of perceived price and perceived quality on consumer purchase intention, both individually and collectively. Cupcakes represent a consumer choice that caters to diverse flavor preferences through the use of high-quality ingredients. Ensuring product excellence is crucial for maintaining favorable consumer perceptions and attracting potential customers, as purchasing decisions are largely influenced by product type and taste. Therefore, it is imperative for pastry entrepreneurs and companies to continuously enhance the quality of their offerings.

Employing a quantitative research approach, this investigation utilized multiple linear regression analysis to analyze primary data collected via questionnaires. The study population comprised consumers of SHMILY Cupcakes in Manado, with a sample size of 100 respondents. The results indicate that perceived price and perceived quality jointly exert a significant impact on consumer purchase intention. However, when considered separately, perceived quality demonstrates a more substantial effect on purchase intention than perceived price. Consequently, it is recommended that SHMILY Cupcakes’ management prioritize product quality over pricing strategies, given its stronger influence on consumer purchasing decisions.

Keywords: perceived price, perceived quality, consumer purchase intention.

The placebo effect has recently attracted considerable attention among marketing researchers seeking to enhance their understanding of the influence of various psychological constructs on consumer behavior. It is well established that manipulating marketing variables—such as price, packaging, and distribution channels—can substantially affect consumer beliefs and expectations, thereby altering their perceptions of a product. This study aims to provide a clearer and more comprehensive understanding of the placebo effect in relation to pricing from the consumer’s perspective. Employing a qualitative research design with a case study approach, the investigation offers descriptive insights into the phenomenon. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and document analysis, with participants selected randomly from diverse occupational backgrounds to capture spontaneous perspectives on the placebo effect. The findings reveal multiple viewpoints regarding the placebo effect on pricing; however, the central conclusion emphasizes that the placebo effect fundamentally shapes consumers’ assessment of product quality. The influence of psychological factors should not be underestimated, as the mindset may impact abilities and skills. Regardless of the validity of this claim, it is ethically imperative to compensate customers fairly—paying what a product is truly worth rather than the minimum possible.  
Keywords: placebo effect, product perception, price

This study aimed to evaluate the anti-inflammatory effects of the ethanol extract derived from the skin of Mahkota Dewa fruit on foot edema in male white rats induced by a 5% solution of egg white. Additionally, the study sought to identify the most effective dose of this ethanol extract in reducing the volume of foot edema in the test subjects. A total of 15 male white rats were used and randomly assigned to five groups: a negative control group receiving aquadest, a positive control group receiving sodium diclofenac, and three treatment groups administered ethanol extract of Mahkota Dewa skin fruit at doses of 140 mg/200 g body weight (BW), 280 mg/200 g BW, and 420 mg/200 g BW, respectively. Following oral administration, foot edema was induced by injection of a 5% egg white solution. The volume of the rats' foot edema was measured hourly over a 7-hour period. The results indicated that the ethanol extract exerted anti-inflammatory effects at doses of 140 mg/200 g BW (16.91%), 280 mg/200 g BW (18.87%), and 420 mg/200 g BW (19.09%). Among these, the dose of 420 mg/200 g BW showed the greatest efficacy in reducing foot edema volume. 

Keywords: anti-inflammatory, edema, Phaleria macrocarpa Boerl

This research seeks to examine the behavioral patterns of mobile vegetable traders amid the Covid-19 pandemic in Sea Dua Village, Pineleng District, Minahasa Regency. The study was conducted between October and December 2021, with its geographical focus limited to Sea Dua Village, Pineleng District, Minahasa Regency. Sampling was performed using an accidental sampling method, identifying a total of ten mobile vegetable traders utilizing motorbikes, whose trade activities were confined to the Sea Dua Village area. The primary data collected for this study pertained directly to the traders' behaviors during the pandemic period. Data collection involved direct interviews based on a structured questionnaire developed in accordance with the research objectives. Findings indicate that the traders’ knowledge regarding the pandemic scored 68.75%, categorizing it as good; their attitudes during the pandemic achieved a 75% score, also within the good category; however, their behavioral actions received a 55% score, which falls into the poor category.

This study seeks to determine the yard farmland area owned by farmers' families used for cultivating vegetables and spices, as well as to ascertain the monthly expenditure incurred by these families on the consumption of vegetables and spices. The research was conducted over a three-month period, spanning from the initial preparation phase through to the completion of the final research report, with activities taking place from September to November 2017. Both primary and secondary data sources were utilized in this investigation. Primary data were collected from respondents via surveys, documentation, and interviews, employing a pre-designed questionnaire. A purposive sampling technique was applied, selecting 30 respondents in total, comprising 15 farming families engaged in vegetable and spice cultivation and 15 farming families who did not cultivate these crops. The gathered data were subsequently analyzed descriptively and presented in both narrative and tabular formats. The analysis revealed that the yard farmland area possessed by families cultivating vegetables and spices predominantly ranged between 100 m² and 120 m², whereas farming families not engaged in such cultivation typically owned yard areas between 121 m² and 140 m². Regarding monthly vegetable consumption costs, both cultivating and non-cultivating farming families exhibited average expenses ranging from Rp 330,000 to Rp 599,000. Similarly, for spice consumption, the average monthly costs for both groups were found to be between Rp 289,000 and Rp 576,000.

This study, entitled "The Terms of Food in English and Patani Language: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to identify, classify, analyze, and describe food-related terminology in both English and the Patani language. Data in English were gathered from theses and online sources, while Patani language data were elicited from native informants. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, the analysis of food categories followed the theoretical framework proposed by Frisch in Hickerson. Subsequently, a contrastive analysis was conducted using Robert Lado’s theory to examine similarities and differences between the two languages. Furthermore, the study utilized Givon’s (1994) and Leech’s (1971) theories for data analysis, complemented by Lado’s (1957) framework for language comparison. The findings reveal that food terms in both English and Patani can be categorized into two primary groups: solid food and oil-based food. Specifically, solid food in English includes fruits, vegetables, bread, meat, fish and seafood, as well as processed food, while the Patani language categorizes food into liquid and solid forms. In English, food terminology primarily comprises words and phrases with denotative meanings. Conversely, in Patani society, numerous celebrations are associated with specific food terms expressed through words, phrases, and clauses, which carry both denotative and connotative meanings.

Keywords: Food Terminology in English and Patani, Contrastive Analysis

The solar dryer employing an alternative heat energy source represents an environmentally sustainable drying technology. This study aimed to evaluate the quality parameters of dried chili, including moisture content, color characteristics, vitamin C concentration, total mold count in chili powder, and overall yield. The findings indicated that the moisture content of dried Red chili and Local Chili processed using the solar dryer with heat energy replacement were 7.3% wb and 6.24% wb, requiring drying durations of 10 and 8 hours, respectively. In contrast, the moisture content of the same samples subjected to conventional drying methods was higher, at 11.89% wb and 8.63% wb, with considerably longer drying times of 71 and 41 hours, respectively. Additionally, colorimetric analysis revealed that dried Red chili, Local Chili, and their powders processed via the solar dryer exhibited higher L*, a*, and b* values compared to those dried using conventional methods. The vitamin C content in the powders obtained through the solar drying method was also significantly elevated, measured at 54.33 mg/100 g for Red chili powder and 27.73 mg/100 g for Local Chili powder, compared to 36.33 mg/100 g and 8.60 mg/100 g, respectively, in samples dried conventionally. Total mold counts were highest in conventionally dried Red chili powder and Local Chili powder, registering 6.46 × 10² colonies/g and 2.06 × 10² colonies/g, respectively. Conversely, Local Chili powder dried by the solar dryer exhibited no detectable mold presence, while Red chili powder showed a substantially lower mold count of 1.1 × 10² colonies/g. The drying yield of Red chili and Local Chili ranged from 24.97% to 32.17%, with yields from the solar dryer surpassing those obtained via conventional drying methods. 

Keywords: Quality, Chili powder, Solar dryer

A brand encompasses a name, term, design, symbol, or any distinguishing feature that differentiates one seller's product from those of competitors. To effectively introduce a product to the market, a company must establish a strong brand to enhance consumers' attitudes towards sportswear. In order to support advertising efforts, particularly in conveying information and capturing public attention, companies often rely on brand awareness and brand trust. The present study aims to examine the influence of brand awareness and brand trust on consumers' attitudes towards sportswear brand extensions. Employing a quantitative methodology, data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple regression techniques. The study population comprised members of The Hill Fitness Center at Swissbell Hotel Manado, with a sample size of 60 respondents. Findings indicate that, when considered simultaneously, brand awareness and brand trust significantly impact brand extension attitudes. However, in partial analyses, only brand awareness demonstrated a significant effect on consumers' brand extension attitudes, whereas brand trust did not exhibit a significant independent influence. Consequently, brand awareness emerges as a more appropriate variable for measuring consumers' attitudes towards sportswear brand extensions. Nonetheless, the analysis did not provide definitive evidence supporting the individual effects of brand awareness and brand trust on consumers' brand extension attitudes.  

Keywords: brand awareness, brand trust, consumer brand extension attitude

A budget is essential for forecasting future activities and resource allocation, typically covering a specific timeframe, often one year. An effective budget facilitates informed decision-making by providing relevant information. Consequently, efficient budget allocation is crucial to balancing diverse demands and achieving targeted objectives. This study aimed to examine the impact of implementing performance-based budgeting on the performance of work units within the Sangihe Regency government islands. The research methodology involved surveying Echelon II and Echelon III personnel through questionnaires distributed to 60 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using simple linear regression, with hypothesis testing performed using a statistical t-test, facilitated by SPSS Version 2.0 for Windows. The regression analysis produced the equation Y = 5.134 + 0.748X, where the coefficient for performance-based budgeting (X) was positive (0.748), indicating a direct positive effect on the performance variable (Y) related to education. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 57.3%, suggesting that performance-based budgeting accounts for 57.3% of the variance in educational performance within the Sangihe Regency government, while the remaining 43.7% is attributed to other factors not addressed in this study, such as financial reporting information systems.

The Inspectorate, as a supervisory institution, bears the responsibility of reviewing the drafting of the RKA SKPD. In executing its supervisory functions, a phenomenon often encountered is the expectation gap—a disparity between stakeholders' expectations and the actual performance demonstrated by the APIP. Frequently, stakeholders' demands exceed the defined roles and responsibilities of the APIP. This study aims to examine the expectation gap between APIP and its stakeholders (auditees) concerning APIP’s role and independence in overseeing the preparation of the regional budget within the Government of North Sulawesi Province. Employing a qualitative methodology, the research was conducted across five SKPDs within the Government of North Sulawesi province. Informants included APIP officials from the North Sulawesi Inspectorate with more than five years of experience and auditees responsible for drafting the RKA. Findings indicate that no expectation gap exists regarding the APIP’s role; however, perceptions relating to limitations in APIP’s responsibilities warrant further evaluation, particularly in areas requiring enhancement such as human resource quality, regulatory comprehension, and skill development. Regarding independence, although no expectation gap was observed concerning APIP’s perceived independence, an expectation gap was identified with respect to the influence of organizational structure and the APIP’s consultative role. 

Keywords: Expectation Gap, APIP Role, APIP Independence, Supervision of Regional Budget Preparation

The market, as a community economic institution, fundamentally represents social relations, reflecting the intrinsic integration of economic activity within social life. Traditional markets continue to serve as crucial trading centers for basic commodities, primarily facilitating the marketing of agricultural, livestock, and fishery products. In this context, traditional markets function to minimize the distance between producers and consumers, thereby effectively meeting everyday subsistence needs. Bersehati Market, one of the largest traditional markets in Manado city, operates continuously for 24 hours daily, without holidays, supporting a vibrant and ongoing commercial environment. 

Vegetables, characterized by their perishable nature, necessitate specialized handling that demands rapid distribution by vegetable traders to consumers, thereby shortening the marketing chain as much as possible. Given this perishable commodity’s requirements, the existence of a robust network among vegetable traders is essential to ensure access to marketing opportunities, distribution channels, and real-time information on product availability. The social networks that emerge within the community of vegetable traders at Bersehati Market play a pivotal role in facilitating the smooth operation of vegetable trading activities, significantly enhancing the efficiency of distribution and marketing processes.

This study employs a qualitative descriptive methodology aimed at providing systematic and factual descriptions of the objects under investigation. The research emphasizes the importance of maintaining good social relations and adherence to prevailing social norms within trade practices, fostering a sense of social solidarity among traders. Economic behaviors observed are closely linked to the sustainability of capital, with marketing activities often influenced by underlying social relationships and network dynamics.

Keywords: social capital, vegetable traders, marketing

ABSTRACT This study aims to determine the effect of interactions between the number of branches and the number of fruit on the production of watermelon plants. The study was carried out in Kalasey 2 Village, Mandolang District, Kab. Minahasa which runs from May to July 2019. This research uses a Randomized Block Design (RBD) consisting of 2 factors. Factor A Number of branches, 1 branch (A1) and 2 branches (A2). Factor B Number of fruits, 1 fruit in 1 branch (B1) 2 fruits in 1 branch (B2) 3 fruits in 1 branch (B3). Thus obtained 6 combinations of treatments A1B1, A1B2, A1B3, A2B1, A2B2, A2B3, the treatment was repeated three times. Observed in this study were fruit weight, fruit diameter, fruit length, and carried out at harvest. The results showed that there was an interaction between the number of branches and the number of fruit on the length and weight of watermelon fruit. Watermelon plants that have 2 branches and 1 fruit (A2B1) produce the heaviest fruit that is 4.63 kg, and the longest fruit that is 27 cm. Then the treatment of 1 fruit (B1) produces the widest fruit diameter that is 56cm. Through this research it is recommended to farmers to get a large fruit size and length and weight, then in 1 plant only retained 1 or 2 watermelons. Keywords : Watermelon, Pruning

Skipjack (Katsuwonus pelamis) is a leading economic activity in the fisheries sector of the North Sulawesi, commonly captured by pole and line fishing gear. To improve the fishing efficiency with the gear, it is indispensible to know the distribution of fishing ground and fishing seasons. This study was aimed describing the pole and line fishing gear and its fishing process, mapping the position of skipjack fishing ground landed in Belang Coastal Fishing Port, and predicting the skipjack fishing season, by using a descriptive method. Primary data gained by interviews and direct measurement techniques to know the position of fishing ground during fishing operation, supported by secondary data. Findings demonstrate that all tested porous media—sand (T1), clay (T2), and the clay plus activated charcoal dust mixture (T3)—are effective as environmental sanitation instruments for treating the organic matter-laden liquid waste of the Indofood instant noodle production process.

This study aims to delineate the wetland potential within Ratahan District through the application of Geographic Information System (GIS) technology. Employing a descriptive methodology, the research integrates field surveys with map overlay techniques. Data collection involved the analysis of satellite imagery and direct physical observations supported by georeferenced coordinates obtained at five distinct points within the study area. The cartographic processes were conducted over a two-month period (February to March) at the Remote Sensing and GIS Laboratory, Department of Soil Science, Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University.

The findings revealed that the wetland potential in Ratahan District encompasses a total area of 6,216.73 hectares, which is stratified by slope classes. Areas with slopes ranging from 0 to 8% cover approximately 5,850 hectares, including 4,467.00 hectares of land currently utilized for smallholder plantations, 448.00 hectares of shrubland, 444.00 hectares of moorland, and 451.00 hectares of existing wetland use. Potential paddy fields are predominantly located in the villages of Maulit, Poniki, Rasi, Wioi, Ratahan, Pangu, Tosiraya, Vice Mayor, and Vice Mayor Pasan. Conversely, wetlands on slopes exceeding 8% occupy 366.73 hectares, consisting of 191.81 hectares employed as smallholder plantations and 174.92 hectares under current wetland use, primarily distributed in Kalatin and Lowu villages.

Keywords: Wetland, Geographic Information System, Land Use, Ratahan District

Arther Manueke conducted a study on employment absorption within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both agribusiness and non-agribusiness sectors, focusing on the Village Kakaskasen Two, North Tomohon Sub-District. The research was supervised by Chairperson Jen Tatuh, with Lorraine W.Th. Sondak and Agnes E. Loho serving as committee members. MSMEs play a critical role in regional economic enhancement, as sectoral expansion not only fosters business development but also promotes employment growth, thereby contributing to a reduction in local unemployment rates.

This investigation took place from April to June 2014 and utilized both primary and secondary data sources. Primary data were collected through structured interviews based on a pre-prepared questionnaire, while secondary data were obtained from relevant authorities, including the Village Kakaskasen Two administrative office and the Tomohon Department of Cooperatives. The data were analyzed descriptively using labor coefficient methods and presented in tabular formats.

Over the course of the two years prior to the study, the number of SME business units in Kakaskasen Two sub-district notably increased, with records indicating 82 units in 2012 and 209 units in 2013. Findings reveal that, within agribusiness MSMEs, catering enterprises accounted for the lowest employment figures but demonstrated relatively high productivity levels. In contrast, restaurant businesses exhibited the highest labor productivity coefficients but commanded a minimal workforce. Among non-agribusiness MSMEs, sound system rental services displayed the highest labor coefficient; despite this, their productivity was low. Meanwhile, businesses such as hotels, cottages, and boarding houses showed lower labor productivity coefficients, yet their overall productivity remained substantial.

In summary, agribusiness MSMEs exhibited greater employment absorption compared to their non-agribusiness counterparts, whereas productivity was higher within non-agribusiness sectors. Special attention is warranted for catering and hospitality-related businesses—specifically hotels, cottages, and boarding houses—since they generate significant revenue with relatively limited labor input.

Taxation constitutes a financial resource for the State, with individual taxpayers serving as a principal source through which the government secures funds necessary for national development. Among taxpayers who provide independent personal services, tax compliance occurs voluntarily, as no external parties compel their tax payments; such taxpayers possess tax identification numbers by their own volition. This phenomenon presents a compelling context for examining the factors that motivate individuals to fulfill their tax obligations. Accordingly, this study investigates the effects of tax payment awareness, knowledge and understanding of tax regulations, and service quality on the willingness of individual taxpayers to pay taxes. The population under study comprises individual taxpayers engaged in independent personal services registered with the Office of Counseling and Consultation Services Tax in Tomohon, with a sample size of 77 respondents. Hypothesis testing employed the t-test to assess the partial influence of independent variables on the dependent variable, while the F-test was utilized to evaluate their simultaneous impact. The findings reveal that tax payment awareness and service quality exert a significant partial influence on the willingness of individual taxpayers in Tomohon City to pay taxes. Conversely, knowledge and understanding of tax laws do not significantly affect taxpayers' willingness. Collectively, tax payment awareness, knowledge and understanding of tax laws, and service quality significantly influence the willingness of individual taxpayers to comply with tax obligations in Tomohon City.

This study investigates the development of wheat flour biscuits incorporated with locally sourced starches as a strategy to enhance food security. Both wheat flour and starches predominantly contain amylose and amylopectin, albeit in varying proportions. The starches utilized in this research include tacca tuber starch, cassava tuber starch, sago starch, and corn starch, each exhibiting distinct amylose and amylopectin compositions. Variations in these components significantly influence the texture, sensory attributes, and gelatinization temperature of the final product. The objective of the study was to assess the physical characteristics resulting from the blending of wheat flour with the aforementioned starches and to evaluate the role of these starch blends in shaping the sensory properties of biscuits. Employing a Completely Randomized Design (CRD), treatments consisted of flour-starch blends mixed at a 1:1 ratio, with each treatment replicated three times. Data analysis revealed that the TTPT treatment scored highest in aroma preference, the TTPS treatment exhibited the most favored color, while the TTPJ treatment achieved the highest ratings for taste and crispness. Biscuits prepared with the TTPS composite flour demonstrated a broad range of preference levels, whereas the TTPJ composite flour biscuits attained the highest crispness rating, which correlated with their measured hardness. Additionally, each composite flour exhibited distinct solubility and water absorption properties, highlighting their diverse functional characteristics.

The objective of this study was to identify diseases afflicting tilapia and to assess the quality of the water surrounding the floating net cages. The research employed both in situ and ex situ methodologies. Sampling was conducted in Pematang Limau Village, while disease diagnosis took place at the PUSKESWAN Laboratory, and water chemistry analyses were performed at the Health and Calibration Laboratory in Palangka Raya. Fish samples were collected to observe clinical symptoms for disease identification, focusing on both parasitic and bacterial infections. Additionally, physical and chemical water quality parameters were examined. Based on diagnostic observations conducted in the field and laboratory analyses, it was determined that the tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) cultured in floating net cages in Pematang Limau Village did not suffer from any specific diseases, as symptoms were limited to bleeding and the formation of lumps on the skin and the lateral side of the mouths of some specimens. Laboratory testing revealed no presence of bacterial pathogens; however, parasitic infections were detected at mild levels, involving four types of ectoparasites commonly affecting tilapia. Water quality assessment indicated generally favorable conditions, although biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and chemical oxygen demand (COD) values suggested the presence of slight water pollution.

This study addresses the critical issue of public service quality amid ongoing bureaucratic reforms in Indonesia, with a specific focus on Bahu Village, Malalayang District, Manado. The primary research question centers on identifying the factors that influence the quality of public services at the Village Office of Bahu. The objective of this investigation is to elucidate the determinants associated with the performance of public service employees in the village.

Public service is conceptualized as a facilitative process involving assistance delivered through interpersonal sensitivity and relationships, aimed at achieving client satisfaction and successful outcomes. The variables examined include Organizational Structure (X1), Apparatus Capability (X2), and Service Systems (X3). Public Satisfaction (Y) is defined as the emotional response—either positive or negative—arising from the comparison between perceived service performance and service expectations.

A qualitative methodological approach was employed, utilizing data collected via surveys, interviews, and questionnaires administered to 95 households. The data analysis involved Multiple Linear Regression, Correlation Coefficient, Coefficient of Determination, and hypothesis testing using both F-tests for simultaneous effects and t-tests for individual variable significance, conducted at a significance level of α = 0.1.

The regression analysis yielded the equation Y = 11.232 + 0.298X1 + 0.138X2 + 0.122X3. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 46.7%, and the correlation coefficient (R) was 21.9%, indicating that organizational structure, apparatus capability, and service system variables collectively exert a measurable influence on community satisfaction. The simultaneous hypothesis test produced an F-value of 8.482, exceeding the critical F-value of 3.10, while partial tests for each independent variable resulted in t-values of 4.268, 1.860, and 1.712, respectively, all surpassing the threshold t-value of 1.66. Consequently, the hypotheses were accepted.

In conclusion, the findings suggest that the quality of public service, as determined by organizational structure, personnel competence, and service systems, significantly affects community satisfaction. It is therefore recommended that the leadership of the Bahu Village Office and relevant governmental bodies prioritize the enhancement of these factors to improve public satisfaction levels in the village.

Keywords: Quality of public services, organizational structure, apparatus capability, service system, community satisfaction

This research seeks to quantify the incidence of Brontispa longissima (Gestro) infestations on two coconut (Cocos nucifera L.) varieties, namely Genjah Raja and Dalam Bido. The findings are intended to enhance public understanding concerning the proportion of pest attacks by B. longissima on coconut palms, thereby facilitating more effective pest management strategies. The study was conducted within the coconut plantation of the Palma Research Institute (Balit Palma) located in the Mapanget District, North Minahasa Regency, over the period from March to July 2021. Employing a survey methodology through direct field observations, the investigation focused on experimental plots at the Mapanget research site. Each coconut variety was cultivated on approximately 0.2 hectares, subdivided into five diagonally distributed observation sub-plots. Parameters assessed included pest attack symptoms, identification of affected plants, attacked fronds, and classification of attack severity. The results revealed that the pest attack rate by B. longissima was 20% in the Dalam Bido variety and 12.5% in the Genjah Raja variety. The present study aimed to evaluate the impact of incorporating yellow pumpkin flour (Cucurbita moschata) into the diets of laying hens on internal egg quality parameters, specifically the egg white index, yolk index, and yolk coloration. A total of 100 laying hens, each 42 weeks old, were utilized in this experiment conducted at the Animal Product Technology Laboratory, Faculty of Animal Husbandry, Sam Ratulangi University. The experimental design employed was a completely randomized design comprising five treatment groups with five replications per treatment. The treatments consisted of replacing part of the basal ration with yellow pumpkin flour at varying inclusion levels: R0 (control) with 0%, R1 with 2%, R2 with 4%, R3 with 6%, and R4 with 8% yellow pumpkin flour. The measured variables included egg white index, yolk index, and yolk color. Statistical analysis indicated that supplementation of the basal ration with yellow pumpkin flour at levels of 2%, 4%, 6%, and 8% did not produce significant differences (P > 0.05) in the evaluated egg quality traits. Consequently, it can be concluded that the inclusion of up to 8% yellow pumpkin flour derived from pumpkin waste in the diets of laying hens does not adversely affect the egg white index, yolk index, or yolk color. 

Keywords: Yellow pumpkin waste, egg quality, laying hens

This study seeks to investigate the reasons behind the failure to achieve the anticipated outcomes in the implementation of the Population Document Service System policy through the Es Ma Ma (Community Service Expedition) application. The research was conducted at the Office of Population and Civil Registration in Bitung City, employing a qualitative descriptive research design. Data for this study were gathered from both primary and secondary sources. Primary data were collected through in-depth interviews with key informants and additional supporting informants in the field. Secondary data comprised processed or officially published information obtained from mass media reports, documentation, and archives of relevant institutions. Six informants participated in the study, including the Head of the Population and Civil Registration Office of Bitung City, two operators of the ES MAMA Program Manager, and three community members responsible for managing population document files. The findings reveal that the failure to meet policy objectives can be attributed to three main factors: first, the implementing organization’s infrastructure was not specifically designed to support this program; second, implementers perceived the program’s services as merely part of routine operations; and third, there was a limited frequency and intensity of information dissemination to the community.

ABSTRACT Sweetened dried citrus peel is a product from citrus peel as an effort to give value to citrus' by-products and food diversification as a new food product. Results showed that moisture content of sweetened dried citrus peel were ranged from 10-84% - 15,34% and they were significantly different among treatments. The temperature used during drying process in this research was 700C The highest moisture content was in treatment A (4 h drying), whilst the lowest was in treatment D (7 h drying). The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of incorporating cakalang (Skipjack tuna) fish oil waste (STO) into the diets of MB 402 laying hens on egg weight, yolk weight, and yolk coloration. A total of 100 MB 402 laying hens, aged 36 weeks, were randomly assigned to five treatment groups with five replications each, wherein each cage housed four hens. The dietary treatments comprised a basal ration without STO (R0), and basal rations supplemented with 1% (R1), 2% (R2), 3% (R3), or 4% (R4) STO. The measured parameters included egg weight, yolk weight, and yolk color. The experimental design employed was a Completely Randomized Design (CRD). Results indicated that dietary inclusion of cakalang fish oil waste up to 4% did not significantly (P > 0.05) influence egg weight, yolk weight, or yolk color in MB 402 laying hens. Consequently, it is concluded that supplementation of skipjack fish oil waste at levels up to 4% does not adversely affect the internal quality of eggs.

Keywords: Cakalang (Skipjack tuna) fish oil waste, MB 402 laying hens, internal egg quality.

This study examines the use of negative sentences in the song lyrics of Meghan Trainor. Titled "Negative Sentences in Meghan Trainor’s Song Lyrics," the research aims to identify, classify, and analyze the various forms of negative sentences present, as well as to determine which forms are most frequently employed. Employing a descriptive research methodology, data were extracted from the lyrics of Meghan Trainor’s 2015 album, *Title*. The analysis was conducted utilizing the theoretical frameworks proposed by Aarts and Aarts (1982) alongside Thomson and Martinet (1986). Findings reveal a total of 63 negative sentences within the lyrics. These negative sentences are categorized into two primary types: those formed using the word *not* (48 instances) and those constructed with negative expressions (15 instances). Notably, negative sentences featuring *not* with the verbs *dare*, *need*, and *used*, as well as negative sentences containing expressions such as *none*, *hardly*, and *hardly ever*, were absent from the corpus. The predominant form identified in Meghan Trainor’s lyrics is the negative sentence formed with *not*, accounting for the majority of the data. 

Keywords: Negative Sentences, Meghan Trainor, Song Lyrics, Descriptive Analysis

Abstract:  
Online shopping has emerged as a prevalent mode of purchasing, offering greater convenience as well as significant savings in time and energy. Consumers are presented with a wide array of options for acquiring products through online platforms. This mode of shopping enables buyers to fulfill diverse needs without the necessity of face-to-face interaction with sellers. The objective of this study is to identify which online store is favored most by consumers and to examine the criteria that exert the greatest influence on their preferences. Employing the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), this research evaluates various online retailers according to the following criteria: Trust, Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, Website Attractiveness, Perceived Enjoyment, and Perceived Riskiness. The study was conducted in Manado City during the period of September to October 2016, involving 100 respondents who had previously made purchases from three selected online shops. Participants were selected through purposive sampling. Findings indicate that Trust constitutes the most critical criterion with a weight of 0.429, followed by Perceived Ease of Use (0.248), Perceived Usefulness (0.177), Website Attractiveness (0.095), Perceived Enjoyment (0.071), and Perceived Riskiness (0.043). Furthermore, Lazada emerged as the most preferred online retailer among respondents, with Bukalapak and Tokopedia ranking second and third, respectively.  
Keywords: consumer purchase intention, online shopping, analytical hierarchy process

Sumampow Meify conducted an analysis of the carrot marketing margin within the Maramis Farmer's Group located in Rurukan Village, East Tomohon Subdistrict, under the guidance of C. Talumingan and co-advisors Benu O.L.S. and Ellen Tangkere. The primary objective of this research was to determine the extent of marketing margins and the proportion of farmer share across various marketing channels in the urban area of Maramis Rurukan.

Data collection was performed through structured interviews utilizing a questionnaire. The sample included 20 farmers selected via purposive sampling to target specific respondents, alongside 3 traders and 3 retailers identified through snowball sampling techniques. Descriptive analytical methods were employed to elucidate the existing marketing channels, followed by an examination of marketing margins and the distribution of farmer shares.

The study revealed the following marketing channel model in urban Rurukan: Farmers → Collecting Traders → Retailers → Consumers. Findings indicated that traders realized a marketing margin of Rp 7,000, representing 56.75% of the margin, which arises from the price difference between the carrot sales price at the collectors and that at the farmer level. This margin compensates traders for costs such as labor, transportation, and other expenses. Middlemen’s profit amounted to Rp 2,250, or 18.24%. At the retail level, the margin was reported to be Rp 6,583 (53.37%), calculated based on the difference between retail selling prices and collector prices. Ultimately, carrots were sold to the final consumer at a price of Rp 12,333 per kilogram.

The research concluded that farmers received a share equivalent to 20.27% within the current marketing channels. This relatively low farmer share was attributed to the absence of institutional frameworks that could support collective marketing efforts, resulting in individual marketing actors capitalizing on advantages during the carrot marketing process. The study quantified the cumulative marketing margin from producers to consumers at Rp 13,583 — comprising Rp 7,000 between traders and retailers and Rp 6,583 between retailers and consumers.

Given these findings, the study underscores the necessity of empowering farmers by enhancing their bargaining positions to increase their share of the marketing margin. Strengthening farmers' market leverage could lead to more equitable distribution of profits within the carrot supply chain.

Gender equality and justice constitute one of the eight global objectives established by the countries participating in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The issue of Gender Equality and Justice (KKG) has gained significant prominence and has become a collective commitment among nations worldwide, including Indonesia, thereby obligating all countries to uphold these pledges. Consequently, the empowerment of women has been prioritized as a national agenda, necessitating the collaborative support of various stakeholders. The persistent gender disparities in Indonesia are reflected in the socio-economic conditions affecting women. A notable factor contributing to this inequality is the relatively low level of gender awareness among the State Civil Apparatus (ASN), which has hindered the advancement of women into leadership and decision-making roles compared to their male counterparts. The prevailing patriarchal culture further undermines women’s status. This situation is partly attributed to the inadequate implementation of gender-conscious programs within the ASN. Thus, enhancing the role of gender awareness among ASN personnel is critical for promoting equitable public service delivery without gender-based discrimination. Moreover, achieving gender equality in human resource management, particularly in ASN recruitment and system reforms, is essential to address these disparities effectively.

Keywords: gender, women, State Civil Apparatus

Abstract:  
In the contemporary fast-paced era, transportation plays a vital role in facilitating individuals' daily activities. As a full-service airline, Batik Air must prioritize the quality of its service offerings. This study aims to assess the significance and performance of Batik Air’s in-flight services. The variables examined include cabin ambience, in-flight meal service, in-flight entertainment, and cabin crew service. The population under study comprises all Batik Air customers in Manado, with a sample of 100 customers who have experienced Batik Air’s in-flight services. The Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) method was employed to analyze the data. The IPA results indicate that factors such as flavorful food, high-quality ingredients, and a calm cabin ambience are located in Quadrant I. Elements including hygienic food, aromatic cabin atmosphere, air temperature, attractive appearance of flight attendants, their patience and understanding, accurate information provision, polite behavior, and friendly service are positioned in Quadrant II. Items such as well-read magazines, reasonable meal portions, visually appealing food, engaging cabin decoration, attractive TV screens, pleasant music, and diverse TV programming fall into Quadrant III. Lastly, ease of use of TV facilities and appropriate lighting are categorized in Quadrant IV.  
Keywords: Airline industry, Batik Air, In-flight service, Importance-Performance Analysis.

This study aims to investigate the motivations and approaches employed by female entrepreneurs in Manado who engage in entrepreneurship as a supplementary activity. This inquiry is particularly relevant given the prevailing male dominance within the Indonesian labor market and the documented instances of female students successfully managing businesses while maintaining active academic commitments. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative methodology, the study utilizes triangulation techniques to enhance data validity. Findings indicate that the strategies employed by these part-time entrepreneurs do not significantly differ from those adopted by full-time entrepreneurs. The participants demonstrated awareness of their entrepreneurial endeavors, engaging in prior planning and typically initiating their ventures using personal savings as seed capital. Regarding time management, most participants acknowledged their primary occupational responsibilities, consequently allocating less time to their entrepreneurial activities. The primary motivations identified for pursuing entrepreneurship included personal interest (hobby), supplementing income, desire for autonomy, and the availability of personal resources. For female workers and students possessing business ideas or seeking additional income, engaging in entrepreneurship as a side activity may represent a viable option.  

Keywords: entrepreneurship, supplementary activity, female entrepreneurs, student entrepreneurs.

The present study seeks to establish the optimal formulation of pumpkin pulp and chicken meat to produce meatballs of superior quality and to assess panelists’ preferences concerning flavor, aroma, texture, color, and overall appearance of the resulting chicken-pumpkin meatball mixtures. The purpose of this research is to provide insights into the quality attributes of chicken meatballs enriched with pumpkin pulp and to promote such products as diversified, nutrient-dense food options. Employing a completely randomized design (CRD), the study tested four treatment groups: Treatment A consisting of 20% pumpkin puree and 80% chicken meat, Treatment B comprising 30% pumpkin puree and 70% chicken meat, Treatment C containing 40% pumpkin puree and 60% chicken meat, and Treatment D with equal proportions of 50% pumpkin puree and 50% chicken meat. Organoleptic evaluations indicated that the formulation with 20% pumpkin pulp and 80% chicken meat was most preferred by panelists in terms of aroma and flavor. In contrast, the formulation with 30% pumpkin pulp and 70% chicken meat was favored for texture, while the 50% pumpkin and 50% chicken mixture was preferred in terms of color. Chemical analysis of the preferred treatment (20% pumpkin pulp, 80% chicken meat) revealed the following composition: moisture content of 72.29%, ash content of 1.63%, fat content of 1.63%, protein content of 13.36%, and carbohydrate content of 11.62%. These findings suggest that incorporating pumpkin pulp at a 20% level can enhance certain sensory attributes and maintain desirable chemical qualities in chicken meatballs.

**Keywords:** pumpkin, puree, chicken meatballs

Background: Early initiation of breastfeeding (EI) plays a crucial role in reducing infant mortality, particularly in island settings. This study aimed to investigate the factors influencing the early initiation of breastfeeding within the jurisdiction of the Dapalan Health Center in the Tampan'amma sub-district of Kepulauan Talaud Regency.

Methods: Employing a quantitative, analytical observational approach with a cross-sectional design, this research was conducted from March to May 2020 in the working area of the Dapalan Public Health Center, Tampan'amma District. The study population comprised all mothers (N=56) who had spontaneous vaginal deliveries between January and December 2019. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire, and analyses included both bivariate and multivariate statistical methods.

Results: The findings indicated significant associations between EI and maternal knowledge (p = 0.001 < 0.05), maternal motivation (p = 0.040 < 0.05), and health worker support (p = 0.000 < 0.05). In contrast, family support did not show a significant relationship with EI (p = 0.938 > 0.05). Among the variables examined, support from health workers emerged as the most influential factor in the early initiation of breastfeeding.

Conclusion: The study concludes that maternal knowledge, motivation, and health worker support are significantly associated with early initiation of breastfeeding, underscoring the importance of these factors in interventions aimed at promoting optimal breastfeeding practices.

The issue of bureaucracy, which is prevalent across all local governments, significantly impedes the implementation of Good Governance. This challenge arises primarily because Good Governance has not yet been institutionalized within local governments, neither in terms of structural and cultural aspects nor through supportive nomenclature programs. Furthermore, the absence of skilled human resources with adequate expertise in their respective fields contributes to the inefficiency of local government bureaucracy. Consequently, it can be asserted that, to date, the implementation of Good Governance at the local government level remains largely rhetorical. This circumstance motivated the researcher to examine the enforcement of Good Governance policies at the Secretariat Office of Bitung City.

The objectives of this study are twofold: (1) to analyze and elucidate the implementation of transparency at the Secretariat Office in Bitung City, and (2) to analyze and describe the application of accountability principles within the same institution. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology, data were gathered through direct interviews and field observations. Informants were selected through purposive sampling, a method aimed at describing social phenomena related to specific social issues based on deliberate criteria. The research participants comprised seven employees from the Secretariat Office in Bitung City, including five structural employees (echelon II, III, and IV) and two non-structural employees, chosen due to their deeper familiarity with the issues under investigation.

The study’s findings indicate that the principle of transparency is implemented to a satisfactory degree at the Secretariat Office in Bitung City. Based on these results, it is recommended that efforts to enhance transparency and accountability be intensified to achieve an optimal realization of Good Governance, in alignment with the expectations of both the organization and the community of Bitung City.

Keywords: Transparency, Accountability, Implementation of Good Governance

This study aimed to examine the effect of probiotic Effective Microorganism-4 (EM4) on the growth rate of the natural feed population of Daphnia magna and to determine the right dose to obtain the highest growth. This research was conducted at the Aquaculture Technology Laboratory, Faculty of Fisheries and Marine Sciences, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. The time of the study was carried out from April to May 2021. The experimental design used was designed according to a 4 x 4 factorial experimental design in Completely Randomized (CRD). The first factor was the dose of EM4 with 3 levels, namely 0.75 mL, 1 mL and 1.25 mL with 1 control, then the second factor is the time difference (weeks) I, II, III, and IV. The results of the study using the Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) using the JMP application showed 1. The dose difference in the density of daphnia on the culture medium was not significantly affected by the difference between the culture medium and chicken manure (value 'Prob>F)' = 0.1411), 2. The difference in density of daphnia on culture medium was very significant by differences in culture time (Value 'Prob>F' = 0.0003), 3. Interaction, The effect of culture medium factors (EM-4) dose and chicken manure on the density of daphnia changed significantly at the time of the change in the level of the time factor (weeks) (Value 'Prob>F' = 0.0439). Further contrast tests showed that the density of daphnia at week-I was significantly different from the density of daphnia at week-II, week-III, and week-IV and the density of daphnia at week-II, week-III and week-IV were not significantly different.

**Students’ Perception of YouTube Utilization in Vocabulary Enhancement**

**Theresia Katiandagho¹, Golda J. Tulung², Garryn C. Ranuntu³**

**Abstract**

This study, entitled "Students’ Perception of the Use of YouTube to Enhance Vocabulary," aims to identify, categorize, and elucidate the methods employed by English students in using YouTube to improve their vocabulary skills. Additionally, it seeks to analyze and describe students’ perceptions regarding this utilization. Employing a descriptive quantitative approach, data were gathered through questionnaires and interviews. The sample consisted of 30 students from the 2017 cohort of the English Department at the Faculty of Humanities. Responses were collected via an online questionnaire administered through Google Forms, and follow-up interviews were conducted via WhatsApp. The collected data were quantitatively analyzed using percentage calculations. The theoretical framework guiding this study includes Freeman and Anderson (2011: 250) for language learning processes and Nelson-Smith’s theory (2008: 32) to assess university students’ perceptions of YouTube as a vocabulary development tool. The findings reveal that the majority of respondents hold positive attitudes toward using YouTube for vocabulary acquisition, recognizing it as both an instructional resource and an enhancer of the learning experience. Consequently, it can be concluded that students in the English Department at the Faculty of Humanities, Sam Ratulangi University, perceive YouTube as a beneficial educational medium.

**Keywords:** university students’ perception, learning media, YouTube, vocabulary

The success of an enterprise is fundamentally contingent upon the competency of corporate management in effectively operating the company. Among the critical responsibilities of a manager is decision-making. In the execution of organizational activities, management frequently encounters multiple alternatives or courses of action. Selecting the most appropriate alternative necessitates access to accurate cost information. This study aimed to evaluate the production cost calculation methods employed by the company and to analyze relevant costs associated with the acceptance or rejection of a special order. Employing a descriptive research approach, the study found that CV. Manguni Perkasa does not utilize relevant cost analysis when determining production costs. Although the special order price of Rp 183.6 million initially appears disadvantageous compared to the normal selling price of Rp 216 million for the stilt houses, further analysis using relevant cost calculations—separating variable costs from full production costs—indicates that accepting the special order is justifiable. This conclusion is based on the observation that the sales price of the special order exceeds the variable costs incurred in producing the stilt houses.

This study aims to advance scholarship in the domain of state administration, with a particular focus on local government policies pertaining to the development of educational facilities and infrastructure. Additionally, it seeks to provide substantive information and input to the local government of Jayawijaya Regency to enhance the quality of education through infrastructural development. The research participants included eleven key informants: the Regent (Bupati), the Deputy Regent, the Chairman of Commission C of the Regional House of Representatives (DPRD), the Head of the Education Office, the Head of Education and Educational Facilities, and six school principals. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and a review of relevant literature. The analysis employed a qualitative approach utilizing the interactive model framework proposed by Miles and Huberman. Findings indicate that the local government, as the primary policy formulator and implementer at the regional level, holds the responsibility to improve educational quality through infrastructure development in Jayawijaya Regency. However, the existing educational facilities and infrastructure require substantial financial investment to meet adequate educational service standards, particularly for elementary, junior high, and vocational high schools. The study underscores the critical importance of not only physical infrastructure but also complementary components such as educational support facilities and qualified educators, which collectively facilitate the teaching and learning processes, thereby optimizing educational quality. Furthermore, the enhancement of education service quality is significantly influenced by the dedication and commitment of visionary school principals, the effectiveness of quality management systems employed, and the efforts of education administrators and school organizers to deliver high-quality education.  

Keywords: Local Government Policy, Educational Facilities, Educational Infrastructure.

The Directorate General of Taxation, representing the Government, enacted Government Regulation (PP) Number 46 of 2013 concerning taxation for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). To support small and medium economic activities, the government implements a tax policy whereby MSME taxpayers are subject to a 1% tax rate levied on gross sales turnover not exceeding Rp 4.8 billion annually. This study seeks to analyze the change in the number of taxpayers prior to and following the enforcement of PP No. 46 of 2013, as well as to evaluate the revenue generated from Income Tax Article 4 Paragraph (2) within the jurisdiction of the KPP Pratama Luwuk office. Employing a descriptive qualitative research approach, the findings reveal a decline in taxpayer growth by 2.43% subsequent to the regulation’s implementation. Additionally, the average revenue collected under Income Tax Article 4 Paragraph (2) from MSMEs over a forty-two-month period post-implementation was recorded at 2.58%, categorized as Very Low. Moving forward, it is imperative that the government, particularly KPP Pratama Luwuk, enhances its proactive efforts in identifying potential tax revenues, sustains effective management of tax income, and undertakes a thorough evaluation of PP No. 46/2013 as part of future policy assessments.

Keywords: Government Regulation No. 46 of 2013, income tax, tax revenue.

The "Dinas Komunikasi dan Informatika" of Kota Manado is a governmental agency specializing in communication and informatics. Within the administrative framework of Kota Manado, this institution is responsible for implementing the E-Government system. E-Government refers to the deployment of electronic-based systems aimed at enhancing the quality of public services in a manner that is both effective and efficient. The integration of technology through E-Government fosters improved interactions between the government and its stakeholders, including citizens, entrepreneurs, and other entities. The primary objective of E-Government is to elevate the quality of public services utilizing information technology, thereby facilitating transparent, accountable governance and effectively responding to evolving demands. E-Government encompasses three types of relationships: Government to Citizen (G2C), Government to Business (G2B), and Government to Government (G2G). The "Dinas Komunikasi dan Informatika Kota Manado" has incorporated these three relational models, developing a total of thirteen applications to support the E-Government framework within Kota Manado. This study aims to encourage the continuous enhancement and innovation of existing applications by the agency, alongside regular updates to maintain system efficacy. Additionally, it emphasizes the necessity for proactive dissemination of information about these applications to the public, not only through social media platforms but also via direct outreach to each district within Kota Manado.

Keywords: E-Government, Public Service, Information Technology

The contemporary business landscape is characterized by intensifying competition among companies, particularly in the management of business units. This competitive environment is evidenced by the emergence of firms that offer high-quality products at competitive prices. In order to address this heightened market competition, one common strategy employed by companies is the implementation of strategic pricing. Through this approach, firms attempt to establish prices that are competitive within the market, thereby maximizing product sales. Appropriate and well-controlled pricing can create a positive cascading effect, fostering long-term customer relationships and consequently increasing sales volume.

This study adopts a descriptive quantitative methodology, utilizing correlation analysis and simple regression techniques to examine the relationships between variables and to assess their impacts. The primary objective of the research is to determine the extent to which pricing influences the sales growth of PT. ROBCAGA in Talaud.

The findings of the study indicate that price exhibits a significant and positive correlation with the increase in sales at PT. ROBCAGA Talaud. The correlation coefficient obtained (r = 0.685) suggests a strong positive relationship. Furthermore, the coefficient of determination reveals that price accounts for 46.5% of the variance in sales growth, while the remaining 53.5% is attributable to other factors not examined in this study.

Keywords: sales growth, pricing strategy, sales volume
