P. blanchardii is recognized as a principal insect pest affecting date palms. Both adult and nymph stages of this insect feed on nitrogen and essential macroelements present in leaves. Severe infestations by P. blanchardii result in significant damage, manifested by a reduction in photosynthetic activity. The pest’s attacks induce the formation of an excessively dense leaf surface on date palms, which subsequently disrupts vital physiological processes such as transpiration, respiration, and photosynthesis. These disruptions lead to leaf wilting, inhibited growth, diminished yields in mature trees, and mortality in young trees. This study was conducted between November 2019 and February 2020 within the Greenhouse facility at Balit Palma Manado, North Sulawesi. The experimental design employed was a randomized complete block design (RCBD) encompassing seven treatments, corresponding to different date palm varieties, each replicated three times. Data collection followed a quantitative descriptive approach, relying on primary data gathered through direct field observations of P. blanchardii infestations on palm leaves. Key variables monitored included the symptoms of P. blanchardii pest attacks on date palm leaves, infestation levels on 5 and 10 leaflets, and the extent of attack across seven date palm varieties per tree. The findings indicated that the highest infestation rate was observed in the Fard variety, with a 55.41% attack incidence, whereas the Barhee variety exhibited the lowest attack rate at 9.32%. These results underscore the necessity for continued research on P. blanchardii infestations and the development of pest management strategies, particularly through the utilization of natural enemies, to control this pest on date palms in Indonesia.

Keywords: P. blanchardii, pest infestation, date palm varieties, pest management

This study investigates the concentrations of nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe), alongside histopathological assessments of marine fish from the waters surrounding Obi Island, employed as bioindicators of environmental pollution. Additionally, water quality parameters were evaluated through both in-situ and ex-situ measurements. The variables measured included temperature, turbidity, salinity, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), nitrate, orthophosphate, ammonia, as well as iron and nickel concentrations. Findings revealed temperature values ranging from 26.48 ℃ to 27.99 ℃, which fall below established quality standards, indicating comparatively low temperatures. Turbidity measurements between 12 m and 13 m likewise did not meet quality standards. Salinity levels varied from 31.01 ppt to 32.13 ppt, also below the accepted threshold. The pH values ranged from 8.6 to 8.7, reflecting alkaline conditions. Concentrations of ammonia (0.4 mg/L to 0.7 mg/L), nitrate (0.009 mg/L to 0.012 mg/L), and orthophosphate (0.016 mg/L to 0.019 mg/L) exceeded the recommended quality limits. Dissolved oxygen concentrations (3.68 mg/L to 3.77 mg/L) were recorded below the standards. The measured levels of iron (0.6 mg/L to 0.9 mg/L) and nickel (0.06 mg/L to 0.09 mg/L) also surpassed the permissible quality thresholds. Histopathological examination revealed hepatic alterations including hemorrhage, vascular degeneration, vacuolar degeneration, and necrosis. Muscular tissues exhibited edema, degeneration of muscle fibers, muscle bundle atrophy, vacuolar degeneration, hemorrhage, lymphocytic infiltration, and necrosis. Intestinal tissue showed infiltration by lymphocytes and melanomacrophages, along with necrotic changes. Furthermore, ovarian tissue from P. tayenus specimens demonstrated oocyte necrosis. These results underscore the potential for bioaccumulation of heavy metals in fish tissues and highlight the necessity for ongoing monitoring to mitigate heavy metal pollution in the marine environment of Obi Island.

ABSTRACT Semiotics is a study about signs and everything related with it; it also related with other signs, the sender and the recipient. System of significance exist (and therefore called code) if there possibility of generating function of signs that have been agreed by the community. The code is a set of rules or conventions (agreements) together in which signs can be combined, thus enabling the message can be communicated from one to another, In this research, the writer takes the codes used by touring in motorcycle touring activity as the object of research. In this categogy, codes are used in motorcycle touring activity for communication. The problem in this research, forms of codes used by YVCI or Yamaha Vixion Club Indonesia as a club of motorcycle and the mean of the codes are the aim of this research. The popularity of Japanese cuisine has been rising in Indonesia, with its flavors notably aligning well with the Indonesian palate. Among the most favored Japanese desserts in the country is Sumoboo, a well-established franchise. Conversely, Sumikko, a local brand operating exclusively in Manado, presents an alternative option. This study aims to investigate customer perceptions of Japanese dessert shops. Employing a descriptive research design with a qualitative approach, the study sampled 15 customers of both Sumoboo and Sumikko. Data collection utilized purposive and snowball sampling techniques through customer interviews. The primary findings reveal that the top three factors influencing customer perception are quality, value, and financial risk. Notably, residents of Manado exhibit distinct perceptions regarding Japanese desserts. Although the attributes of perceived quality, perceived value, and perceived risk are important to customers, their influence was found to be statistically insignificant in this context. This research aspires to provide a foundation for future studies exploring additional attributes affecting customer perception in similar dessert businesses, with the goal of enhancing profitability and competitive advantage.  

Keywords: customer perception, perceived quality, perceived value, perceived risk, dessert shop

This study seeks to investigate (1) the influence of demographic and geographical factors on the effectiveness of Village Fund management during the pandemic in Southeast Minahasa Regency, and (2) the extent to which the effectiveness of the Village Fund is reflected through its allocation and the performance of villages in enhancing the local economy. Employing a Multiple Linear Regression analytical approach, data were gathered through interviews, observational guides, and document analysis. The dataset comprised working papers used to calculate village funds and APBDes budget positions relating to income, expenditure, and financing. 

The findings indicate that (1) individually, there exists a significant and positive correlation between population ratio, poor population ratio, and area ratio with Village Fund management effectiveness in Southeast Minahasa Regency; conversely, the Geographical Difficulty Index (IKG) does not exhibit a statistically significant effect when assessed independently; (2) collectively, the population ratio, poor population ratio, area ratio, and IKG jointly exert a significant impact on Village Fund management, with the population ratio demonstrating the greatest influence, particularly in the domain of rural community development and empowerment; (3) 97.17% of the variation in the effectiveness of Village Fund management can be attributed to changes in the aforementioned four independent variables; (4) the overall quality of Village Fund management in Southeast Minahasa Regency is classified as very effective; and (5) notwithstanding the existence of 47 villages designated as developed based on an independent village index, there remains room for improvement in the effectiveness of Village Fund management throughout the regency.

In light of these results, the study recommends that future village government policies focus on enhancing the management and allocation of Village Funds and the meticulous recording of Village Assets, while simultaneously reinforcing the institutional roles of village government bodies. Furthermore, promoting transparency in village budget management across various sectors is crucial to ensure that the distribution of Village Funds aligns with established plans.

ABSTRACT  
This study, entitled "Tanda Ikon Dalam Komik One Punch Man Karya One: Suatu Analisis Semiotik," concentrates on the examination of icons present within the comic *One Punch Man*. The primary objectives are to identify the various types and forms of icons depicted in the comic and to interpret the meanings conveyed in each individual frame. The research employs the theoretical frameworks of McCloud and Zoest for the classification and identification of icon types and forms, while Berger’s theory is utilized to analyze the semantic content of each frame. The methodology adopted is descriptive in nature. Each icon identified in the comic is systematically categorized into four distinct forms: human icons, animal icons, object icons, and onomatopoeic icons; as well as three types of icons: typological, diagrammatic, and metaphoric. Subsequently, the frames are analyzed through the lens of Berger’s theory. The findings reveal the presence of 42 human icons, 7 animal icons, 24 object icons, and 7 onomatopoeic icons. Regarding icon types, typological icons appear in 18 frames, diagrammatic icons in 30 frames, and metaphoric icons in 30 frames. Furthermore, the study concludes that the meanings embedded in each frame of the *One Punch Man* comic are distinct and varied.  

Keywords: Icon, Comic, One Punch Man, Semiotic Analysis

Abstract

This study investigates the relationship between household income and the consumption of meat and eggs in the Suluun Tareran District, located within the South Minahasa Regency. The population of Suluun Tareran primarily comprises farming households, with a minority engaged in civil service, private employment, and business activities. The consumption patterns of meat and eggs among the community are predominantly influenced by household income levels. An increase in income corresponds with a higher demand for these animal protein sources. The central research question addresses whether household income significantly influences meat and egg consumption in the district. The objective of this study was to assess the quantity of meat and egg consumption at the household level and to determine the effect of income on these consumption levels within the Suluun Tareran community.

The research was conducted with a sample of 74 households over a two-month period utilizing survey methods for data collection. The gathered data were analyzed through simple regression analysis to ascertain the impact of income on meat and egg consumption. Findings revealed that the average monthly household income was Rp 2,558,050. Despite this income level, consumption averages for meat and eggs have not yet attained the recommended targets of 7.7 kg and 4.1 kg per capita annually, respectively, as suggested by Widyakarya (2004) for adequate nutritional intake. The analysis confirms that household income exerts a significant effect on the consumption of meat and eggs in the Suluun Tareran District.

Keywords: meat and egg consumption, household income, Suluun Tareran District

The existence of agricultural extension agents in Sidodadi Village is important because of the lack of knowledge and public awareness of the importance of this extension. The ability of farmers to obtain agricultural information and technology is a reflection of the confidence in the extension activities. Therefore, it is necessary to examine how the farmers' perceptions of the performance of field agricultural extension agents.The objective of this research is to determine farmers' perceptions of the performance of field agricultural instructors in Sidodadi Village, Sangkub Sub District, Bolaang Mongondow Utara Regency. This research was conducted from December 2019 to February 2020. The data used in this study are primary data and secondary data. Primary data were obtained through direct interviews with 30 respondents using a questionnaire measured using a Likert scale. Secondary data obtained from books, journals, BPS (Central Statistics Agency), Village Offices and BPP (Agricultural Extension Center).Based on the results of the research, it can be concluded that the farmers' perceptions of the performance of the agricultural extension agents in Sidodadi Village are overall good. This is evidenced by the results of the interpretation of the value of farmers' perceptions on the performance of the extension workers, which was 84 percent.Keywords: Farmers' Perception, Agricultural Instructor Performance

This study explores the way in which intellectual capital characteristics contribute towards a competitive advantage to public sector firms, particularlyState Owned Enterprises (SOEs) in Indonesia. The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationship between the intellectual capital and performance of public sector firms. Another purpose was to find out the difference of SOEs and non SOEs listed on Indonesian Stock Exchange regarding the effect of intellectual capital on financial performance The motivation based on the opinion that public sector in Indonesia had a bad performance compares to private sector. In government context human capital include competence, level of knowledge and integrity. Structural capital consist of culture and system or bureaucracy. Customer capital pertaining services to public. The sample consist of 36 firms were listed in Indonesia Stock Exchange, 18 SOEs and 18 non SOEs. Data were drawn for three years, 2010-2012. It was an empirical study using multiple regression model and independent sample t test for the data analysis. The paper tests elements of VAICTM and financial company's performance. The findings show that: as partial, the components of intellectual capital (VAICTM), physical capital have a significantly influences to firms performance, but human capital and structural capital have no significantly influences to firms performance.

ABSTRACT

This study seeks to (1) identify and characterize the protagonist of Oey Kim Tiang's novel *San Pek Eng Tay*, and (2) elucidate the moral message conveyed by the author through this character. Employing a descriptive-analytic methodology, the research is conducted in two primary phases. The first phase involves a psychological analysis of the main character, Eng Tay, utilizing character theory grounded in the Hippocratic and Galenic frameworks. The second phase examines the moral message by analyzing the attitudes, behaviors, and moral order presented in the novel, following the conceptualization proposed by Sugiarti (2018). A descriptive approach, as defined by Keraf (1981, cited in Breyvi), is employed to depict the subject matter objectively. Data collection encompasses all dialogues attributed to the main character, constituting the population for this study, to facilitate identification, classification, and comprehensive description in alignment with the research objectives. Findings derived from the literary psychological analysis reveal that the protagonist embodies strength and perseverance, notably in the pursuit of rights and responsibilities. Specifically, the character demonstrates resilience and steadfastness, exemplified by Ciok Eng Tay’s unwavering commitment to her obligations as a woman. The moral message imparted by *San Pek Eng Tay* underscores the necessity of persistent effort in the pursuit of virtuous goals, resonating with the Indonesian proverb, "Effort will not betray results," thereby advocating against premature surrender. 

Keywords: Main Character, Character Analysis, Moral Message, Novel

The demographic cohort known as Baby Boomers, positioned between the Silent Generation and Generation X, is variably defined by differing birth year ranges. Demographers and scholars commonly identify the onset of this cohort between the early to mid-1940s, with its conclusion occurring between 1960 and 1964. Historically, Baby Boomers have been recognized as the wealthiest, most active, and physically fit generation relative to preceding cohorts, and they were among the first to anticipate societal progress over time. 

This study employed a qualitative research design, specifically in-depth interviews, to explore Baby Boomers’ acceptance of cashless payment systems. Data were collected from ten purposively selected informants belonging to this cohort. Analysis of the collected information revealed a generally positive reception towards cashless payment methods among Baby Boomers. Despite encountering some challenges, participants expressed favorable attitudes and acknowledged the advantages of adopting cashless transactions as a contemporary payment trend. 

The findings indicate that Baby Boomers are willing to embrace cashless payments and do not exhibit resistance towards this system. It is recommended that educational initiatives be implemented to enhance Baby Boomers’ familiarity and comfort with cashless technology, thereby facilitating greater adoption. 

Keywords: Baby Boomers, Cashless Payment

This study questioned the two main problems, namely: How does the process of implementation of the bureaucratic functions in the administration of local government and any constraint faced by the government in implementing the functions of bureaucracy. This study therefore aims to: (1) describe the implementation of the bureaucratic functions in the regional administration, especially in the northern Loloda districts on North Halmahera regency; (2) to identify obstacles or barriers faced by local governments in implementing bureaucratic functions, specialy on northern Loloda district of North Halmahera regency. This study used a descriptive-analytic method. The data and information collected by the technique of questionnaires distributed to 80 respondents and equipped with observation and documentation techniques then analyzed with descriptive analysis technique equipped with a secondary data analysis. Based on the analysis of data, it is known that: (1) the implementation of the public service has been running pretty good, although there are three indicators of public service functions that have not been optimally realized, such as discipline, responsibility and ability of service personnel. (2) there are three factors that are considered as constraint / barrier in the implementation of the bureaucratic functions of particular public service functions, namely: self-discipline, responsibility, and capacity / service personnel in providing services to the public. It can be concluded that the indicator function of public services such as discipline, responsibility and ability to care workers need to get the government's attention, for a fixed the public service for a better future. Keywords: bureaucracy function implementation, the regional administration

Title: Dry Matter Intake and the Digestibility of Calcium and Phosphorus in Local and Imported Feeds for Indonesian Racer Foals

Abstract:  
This study aimed to evaluate the consumption and digestibility of calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) in both local and imported feeds provided to racer foals in Indonesia. The research was conducted over a 30-day period in Pinabetengan Village, Tompaso District, during which feed intake and fecal samples were collected for analysis. Seventeen foals participated in the study and were divided into two groups: nine foals received local feed, while eight foals were fed imported feed. The primary variables measured were the digestibility coefficients of calcium and phosphorus. Statistical analysis was performed using the independent samples t-test assuming unequal variances. The results demonstrated that the digestibility of calcium in the imported feed group (mean ± SD: 1.22 ± 0.82) was significantly greater (p < 0.05) than that observed in the local feed group. Similarly, phosphorus digestibility was higher in foals consuming imported feed (0.68 ± 0.56) compared to those on local feed. These findings indicate that imported feed exhibits superior digestibility of calcium and phosphorus relative to local feed in racer foals.  

Keywords: Racer foal, local feed, imported feed, calcium digestibility, phosphorus digestibility

Accounts receivables represent a current asset held by a company, arising from credit sales transactions. Nevertheless, the presence of such receivables inherently entails the risk of incurring bad debts. At PT Multi Pilar Indah Jaya (Distributor of PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk) in Gunungsitoli, ineffective management control over receivables has led to the occurrence of bad debts. This study aims to examine the methods employed to control accounts receivable in order to minimize bad debts at PT Multi Pilar Indah Jaya. Employing a descriptive qualitative research design, the study involves analyzing receivables data and providing a comprehensive account of the findings. Primary data were collected through interviews and observations conducted at the company. An analysis of receivables over the period 2019 to 2021 revealed an increase in bad debts, attributed to the adverse effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, which compromised the effectiveness of receivables management systems. Consequently, the study suggests the necessity of government intervention by refraining from implementing Large-Scale Social Restrictions (PSBB). Following the government’s decision not to enforce PSBB and subsequent improvements in management practices, a decrease in bad debts was observed. 

Keywords: accounts receivable management, bad debts, COVID-19, government policy

The research objective is to examine the impact of the stock ownership structure to company value, which is divided in to 4 (four) classification that will be tested as follows : (1) stock ownership < 25%, (2) stock ownership between 25% - 50%, (3) stock ownership between 51% - 75%, and (4) stock ownership >75%. From this four classification that will be tested, there are only 2 (two) classification that is fit with the test because those two classification have the uniformity that fulfilled the condition to be tested as follows, there are (1) stock ownership between 25% - 50% and (2) stock ownership between 51% - 75%. This research uses regression analysis methodology to find out the relationship between independent variable and dependent variable with 3 (three) control variable as follows : total assets, total debts and total capital. Result of the research : (1) Stock ownership between 25% - 50% have a significant effect to the company value if uses one of the control variable such as total asset or total debts or total capital. (2) Stock ownership between 51% - 75% do not have effect to the compnay value, with or without the control variablesKeywords: stock ownership structure, company value, banking

An experiment was conducted to examine the effectiveness of Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb and Curcuma Zedoaria rox flours added in ration on performances of broilers. Fifty-four CP-707® strain broilers were used in the experiment at animal house of Animal Husbandry Faculty, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado and they were placed into cages (60cm x 45cm x 45cm), three birds per cage. Randomized completely design were used in this experiment, with three treatments and six replications. The three treatments were R0 (ration without Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb and Curcuma Zedoaria rox flours), R1 (Ration with 2% of Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb flour) and R2 (Ration with 2% of Curcuma Zedoaria rox flour). It was found that, there were no significant different (P>0.05) between treatments on feed consumption, body growth and feed conversion ratio of broilers. Feed consumptions were 111,69gram/bird/day (R0), 118,98gram/bird/day (R1), and 124,34gram/bird/day (R2); Body growths were 53,09gram/bird/day (R0), 54,84gram/birdr/day (R1), 57,59gram/bird/day (R2); Feed conversion ratios were 2,20gram/bird/day (R0), 2,18gram/bird/day (R1), and 2,16gram/bird/day (R2) respectively. It was concluded that, the performances of broilers given ration with addition of 2% of Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb and Curcuma Zedoaria rox flours were same as the performances of broiler given ration without Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb and Curcuma Zedoaria rox flours Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb and Curcuma Zedoaria rox flours. Key words: Broilers, Curcuma Xanthorrhiza roxb, Curcuma Zedoaria rox, flour.

The COVID-19 pandemic, which initially emerged in Wuhan, has profoundly impacted not only the city itself but also the global community. This unprecedented health crisis has compelled numerous major institutions and financial entities to revise their projections regarding the global economic outlook. In Indonesia, the rapid transmission of the coronavirus has precipitated multifaceted crises, with the economic sector being particularly affected. Within this sector, the audit process has experienced significant disruption. Traditionally conducted through in-person, on-site examinations to assess a company's financial status and performance over an annual period, audits have been compelled to transition to remote or online modalities in response to the COVID-19 restrictions. Consequently, internal auditors, who serve as both examiners and overseers of financial statements, are required to perform their duties with enhanced effectiveness.

This study seeks to empirically investigate the influence of Work From Home (WFH) arrangements and auditor independence on the quality of internal audits conducted by the inspectorate personnel responsible for regional financial oversight. Employing a quantitative research design, primary data were collected via structured questionnaires distributed to internal supervisory officers affiliated with the Inspectorate of Manado City. The sample comprised 50 respondents actively engaged in inspection activities. Data were subjected to multiple linear regression analysis, facilitated by SPSS software version 22.

The findings reveal that: (1) the implementation of Work From Home practices exerts a significant positive impact on the quality of internal audits performed by the inspectorate staff overseeing regional financial supervision in Manado City; and (2) auditor independence similarly has a significant positive effect on internal audit quality within the same context.

This study aims to elucidate the effectiveness of village administration in Molobog Village, located within the Motomgkad District of East Bolaang Mongondow. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study involved nine informants: one village head, four village officials, and four community members. Data were collected through guided interviews, and analysis was conducted using the interactive model developed by Miles and Huberman.

The findings of this investigation reveal several key conclusions. First, the implementation of government programs and administrative activities in Molobog Village is notably effective. The village administration demonstrates commendable performance in fulfilling assigned tasks, supported by employees' competencies and adherence to established governmental regulations and administrative guidelines. Second, the efficiency in utilizing organizational resources—particularly human capital and financial expenditures—exhibits a high degree of punctuality in meeting program objectives. This efficiency is largely attributed to innovative practices introduced by the village administration. Third, the village government shows substantial adaptability and flexibility in addressing evolving tasks and emerging challenges. The apparatus's capacity to adjust to the working environment and organizational dynamics fosters positive working relationships among officials and between the government and the local community, thereby enhancing the quality of public service delivery.

Keywords: Effectiveness, village administration implementation

The present study investigated the impact of partially substituting the basal diet with sweet potato vines (Ipomoea batatas) meal on the energy and protein digestibility in finishing pigs. Pork serves as a significant source of animal protein, and sweet potato vines, typically regarded as an agricultural by-product, have potential as a feed ingredient for swine. This experiment involved five castrated male pigs of the 'Duroc X Spotted Poland China' breed, aged between 3.5 and 4.0 months, with an initial average body weight of 50 kg (±2.5 kg). The animals were assigned to five dietary treatments as follows: R0 (100% basal diet without sweet potato vines meal), R1 (92.5% basal diet with 7.5% sweet potato vines meal), R2 (85% basal diet with 15% sweet potato vines meal), R3 (77.5% basal diet with 22.5% sweet potato vines meal), and R4 (70% basal diet with 30% sweet potato vines meal). The primary parameters assessed were the digestibility of energy and protein. The results revealed no statistically significant differences (P > 0.05) across treatments regarding these digestibility measures. These findings suggest that incorporating sweet potato vines meal up to a 30% replacement level in the basal diet does not adversely influence the digestibility of energy and protein in finishing pigs. Consequently, it is concluded that sweet potato vines meal can be utilized as a partial substitute in pig diets without negatively affecting nutrient utilization.  

Keywords: Sweet potato vines, energy digestibility, protein digestibility, finishing pigs

Recent advancements in Information and Communication Technology have introduced novel marketing channels that facilitate communication and interactivity for companies, while simultaneously transforming their business operations and marketing practices. Mobile marketing, particularly through text-based advertising delivered via Instant Messaging Services, has emerged as a prevalent medium for engaging both prospective and existing customers. This study seeks to evaluate the impact of mobile marketing on consumer attitudes among mobile phone users, specifically targeting students of Sam Ratulangi University. Additionally, it examines how entertainment, informativeness, and credibility influence consumer attitudes toward mobile marketing. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire, and multiple regression analysis was employed to test the hypotheses and assess the relationships between the dependent and independent variables. The findings indicate that entertainment and credibility significantly affect consumer attitudes toward mobile marketing, whereas informativeness does not demonstrate a significant influence. The study suggests that companies utilizing mobile marketing strategies should gain a deeper understanding of consumer demographic characteristics to design more effective mobile marketing programs.  

Keywords: mobile marketing, entertainment, informativeness, credibility, consumer attitude

The budget holds a critical function within both governmental and private sector organizations. It serves as a directive framework guiding the actions implemented by government entities. Comprising planned expenditures and financing transfers measured in Rupiah, the budget is systematically organized according to specific classifications over a designated period. Effective budget preparation requires advance planning to ensure that organizational programs and activities meet their intended objectives. This study aims to examine the budget formulation process, assess the effectiveness of budget utilization as a mechanism for controlling direct expenditures, and identify the factors contributing to budget absorption discrepancies within the North Sulawesi Provincial Legal Bureau during the period from 2015 to 2017. Employing descriptive analytical methods, the study reveals that budget preparation adheres to relevant regulatory standards. Furthermore, the overall effectiveness of budget utilization from 2015 to 2017 is categorized as effective. Specifically, in 2015, the effectiveness of direct expenditure budget utilization was recorded at 96.33%, representing the lowest absorption rate within the examined timeframe. In 2016, this effectiveness increased to 99.76%, while in 2017, it remained high at 99.70%. Budget absorption mismatches were attributed primarily to budget savings resulting from residual expenditure values and discrepancies between market prices and those initially budgeted by the Sulawesi Provincial Legal Bureau.  

Keywords: Budget, Effectiveness, Direct Expenditure

Abstract: 

Human resource development programs are implemented across various urban and rural areas to benefit local populations. However, the effectiveness of government policy implementation in these regions remains uncertain, which subsequently influences the outcomes achieved. This study aims to evaluate the government’s role in executing human resource development policies within the Tewaan sub-district villages of Bitung city. Employing a qualitative research approach, the study also incorporates percentage-based analytical techniques utilizing the formula P = F / N × 100. Data were collected from 14 respondents, comprising six village office staff members and eight community leaders, through questionnaires complemented by interviews. The analysis indicates a highly positive and significant governmental role in policy implementation, demonstrating strong and directed efforts to enhance living standards. Consequently, the study concludes that the government has successfully implemented a high-quality human resource development policy in the Tewaan villages, aligned with community expectations and needs. Indonesia experiences natural disasters with considerable frequency, which often lead to diverse forms of damage, losses, and health-related complications. Insufficient knowledge concerning disaster preparedness can significantly influence an individual's attitudes and behaviors in response to such events. In this context, medical students—who are future healthcare professionals—require specialized expertise to effectively contribute to health services during natural disasters. This study aims to describe the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding natural disaster preparedness among students enrolled in the Medical Education Study Program at the Faculty of Medicine, Sam Ratulangi University. Employing a descriptive, cross-sectional design, the study utilized simple random sampling to select participants. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered via Google Forms. A total of 116 students participated in the research. Findings revealed that a majority of the respondents demonstrated high knowledge (61.2%) of disaster preparedness, exhibited positive attitudes (63.8%), and were capable of implementing appropriate preparedness actions (71.6%). Consequently, it is concluded that the Medical Education students at the Faculty of Medicine, Sam Ratulangi University possess substantial knowledge, favorable attitudes, and effective practices related to natural disaster preparedness.  

**Keywords:** Disaster preparedness, knowledge, attitude, practice

Abstract:  
The dissemination and provision of information to the public regarding the performance of labor and social services in the Banggai Archipelago transmigration area remain suboptimal, particularly in the management of data and information related to empowerment and social assistance. This limitation is primarily attributable to the scarce resources available to policy implementers, both in terms of quality and quantity, which consequently affect the effectiveness of policy implementation. Furthermore, inadequacies in public knowledge and understanding of governance, especially concerning empowerment and social assistance, diminish the impact of information delivery. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach to depict the realities encountered in the field, utilizing data collection methods such as observation, interviews, literature review, and documentation. The findings indicate that public information disclosure can be evaluated across three dimensions: ease of access to information, accuracy and sufficiency of information, and the extent of information disclosure. Among these dimensions, the ease of obtaining information was found to be insufficiently met, largely due to low human resource capacity and suboptimal utilization within the implementing agency. The study concludes that while the implementation of public disclosure policy has been initiated, it has not been fully optimized, primarily owing to inadequacies in human resource utilization. It is recommended that the government enhance human resource capabilities through formal education and training initiatives.

Keywords: public disclosure policy implementation, empowerment, social assistance

This study examines the application of conceptual accountability management within village financial affairs, aiming to elucidate the role of government in facilitating the transition toward or the consolidation of improved institutional frameworks for the benefit of local citizens. The investigation arises from concerns regarding the management of fund allocations by the Village Budget Committee, which, although administered with a degree of fairness, contravenes legal regulations. Consequently, the findings of this research are anticipated to provide valuable insights not only for Talaud Regency but also for Damau District, particularly in enhancing the accountability mechanisms governing village financial administration.

The research was conducted in Peret Village, located in Damau District. The study population comprised local residents and members of village committees, who were deemed competent representatives for the survey units involved in managing village financial allocations. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the study integrates both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, with a particular emphasis on contextual analysis through ethnographic techniques such as direct participant observation and interviews. These methods were designed to capture a diverse range of judgments and perceptions.

Findings from the research indicate that effective planning and implementation of village fund allocation substantively contribute to the establishment of improved accountability management within local government structures. Despite the relative success achieved in implementing such accountability frameworks, the management processes have not yet been thoroughly and properly administered. Consequently, there remains a need for enhanced regulation and further guidance for involved personnel. Additionally, the study identifies inefficiencies and a lack of prioritization concerning both organizational apparatus and human resource reforms, highlighting the necessity for sustained support from local government entities.

Keywords: Village Financial Allocations, Performance, Evaluation

This study, entitled "Forms and Functions of Conjunctions in the Novel *A Stolen Life* by Jaycee Dugard," aims to identify, classify, and analyze the conjunctions present within the text from both formal and functional perspectives. In terms of form, conjunctions are categorized into three types: coordinative, subordinative, and correlative conjunctions. Functionally, coordination conjunctions (coordinators) serve to link sentences, clauses, and phrases, whereas subordinating conjunctions (subordinators) introduce subordinate clauses that function as constituents within sentences or phrases. Employing a descriptive research design based on the conceptual framework of Aarts and Aarts (1982), this study reveals that the coordinate conjunctions identified within the novel include: *and*, *but*, *or*, and *for*. The subordinate conjunctions identified comprise: *if*, *while*, *because*, *unless*, *that*, *before*, *whether*, *since*, *yet*, *until*, *as*, *than*, *so*, *although*, *however*, *whenever*, *as soon as*, *as if*, *as well as*, and *such as*. Additionally, the correlative conjunctions found are *whether…or* and *either…or*. The conjunctions function primarily as connectors between two words, between two phrases within a single sentence, between clauses, between clauses and phrases, and vice versa. 

Keywords: Forms and Functions, Conjunctions, *A Stolen Life*

The enactment of Law Number 6 of 2014 concerning Villages aims to enhance opportunities for villages to independently govern and implement equitable development. This legislation aspires to empower village administrations to autonomously manage governmental affairs and various natural resources, including financial assets and village property. The present service initiative is designed to equip village officials with a comprehensive understanding of the village financial management cycle, encompassing the stages of planning and budgeting, execution and administration, as well as reporting and accountability. The primary objective of this service is to facilitate the preparation of the Village Budget Implementation Realization Report (APB Village) and the Accountability Report for the Village Budget Implementation Realization. To accomplish these goals, the program employs a combination of lectures and technical training: lectures serve to impart foundational knowledge on village financial management, while technical training focuses on the practical preparation of financial realization and accountability reports. The service implementation commenced with a preliminary survey to identify village-specific challenges related to fund management. Subsequently, consultations were held with village leaders to foster collaboration, followed by the development of training materials tailored for presentation to the village government.

The Food and Beverage industry currently constitutes the largest share within the SME sector, including in Manado. Presently, businesses within this sector face unprecedented competitive challenges, as they must not only contend with one another but also endure the repercussions of the global Covid-19 pandemic, which has significantly impacted Indonesia and, more specifically, Manado. This study aims to identify the key determinants influencing the survival of SMEs during the Covid-19 pandemic. Metaphor, as a form of figurative language, involves the identification of one entity with another, often disparate, entity. Its use enables speakers or writers to provide clearer descriptions through processes of comparison or contrast. This study acknowledges the pervasive presence of music as an auditory phenomenon embedded in various aspects of human experience. The primary objective is to examine the forms and meanings of metaphors present in the lyrics of Adele’s songs, with the intent of encouraging readers, particularly students of the English Department, to utilize song lyrics as a pedagogical tool for studying meaning. Employing a descriptive research method, data collection focused on identifying metaphorical expressions in the form of words, phrases, or nouns. The findings indicate that the metaphors found in the song lyrics can be classified into four categories: metaphor nominative subjective, metaphor nominative objective, metaphor predicative, and metaphor sentence. These metaphorical elements were analyzed according to Lakoff’s theoretical framework, which distinguishes between the tenor—the underlying concept or principal subject—and the source—the borrowed idea or entity to which the tenor is compared. The results demonstrate that each metaphor carries a specific meaning contingent upon its contextual usage and that these meanings correspond clearly to particular tenor and source relationships.

Keywords: metaphoric meaning, target and source, semantic analysis

In the current era of globalization, intense competition has become a significant driving force in marketing, particularly experiencing rapid growth annually within the technology sector. Smartphones, as an advanced form of mobile technology, have integrated deeply into modern lifestyles, offering functionalities that surpass those of traditional mobile phones. Consumer consumption trends in the smartphone market are largely influenced by brand segmentation. Notably, consumers tend to favor products associated with a positive brand image or well-established brands. This study aims to investigate the effects of brand image, brand personality, and brand awareness on the purchase intentions of consumers regarding Apple smartphones. Employing a multiple regression analysis approach, data were gathered through questionnaires distributed to a sample of 100 students from the Faculty of Economics and Business at Sam Ratulangi University in Manado. The findings indicate that brand image, brand personality, and brand awareness all significantly impact consumers’ purchase intentions toward Apple smartphones. Among these variables, brand awareness emerged as the most influential factor affecting consumer purchase intention, surpassing the effects of brand image and brand personality.  
 
Keywords: consumer behavior, brand image, brand personality, brand awareness, purchase intention

This study aims to analyze the nutmeg plantation subsector within North Sulawesi Province. The research was conducted over a three-month period, from August to October 2015, encompassing activities from initial preparation to the finalization of results. The investigation was carried out in North Sulawesi Province, utilizing secondary data sources. Specifically, data were obtained from regional records of North Sulawesi to assess nutmeg production, with sampling focused on two primary nutmeg-producing areas: Sitaro Islands Regency and North Minahasa Regency. The data analysis employed Location Quotient (LQ) and Shift Share analytical methods. The findings indicate that the LQ value for the nutmeg commodity in North Minahasa Regency from 2010 to 2014 exceeds 1. Additionally, the Proportional Shift is negative while the Differential Shift is positive, placing North Minahasa Regency within Group II, characterized as a growing (developing) category. Similarly, the nutmeg LQ value for Sitaro Islands Regency during the same period is also greater than 1. Based on the Proportional and Differential Shift values, nutmeg in North Minahasa Regency is classified within Group II, signifying a developing sector.

This study aims to investigate the determinants affecting the information value of local government financial reporting, where information value is defined by its reliability and timeliness. This research aimed to investigate the influence of 6-benzylaminopurine (BAP) on the growth and morphogenesis of Kulo Chrysanthemum using shoot and node explants in vitro. The study was carried out from July to March 2021 at the Network Culture Laboratory of the Agriculture and Fisheries Service in Tomohon City. A factorial completely randomized design (CRD) was employed, incorporating two factors: explant type (shoot and node) and BAP concentration (0 mg/L, 0.5 mg/L, 1 mg/L, and 1.5 mg/L), resulting in eight treatment combinations. Each treatment was replicated five times, producing a total of 40 experimental units, with each unit consisting of a single explant. The findings indicated that the interaction between explant type and BAP concentration did not significantly affect plantlet height, shoot number, leaf number, time to root formation (days after planting; DAP), or time to shoot formation (DAP). Additionally, explant type alone exhibited no significant impact on these parameters. Conversely, BAP concentration significantly influenced plantlet height, shoot number, leaf number, and root formation time (DAP), while it did not have a significant effect on shoot formation time (DAP).

The present study investigates the impact of incorporating palm sugar (Arenga pinnata Merr) into the drinking water of grower pigs on slaughter weight, carcass weight, carcass length, and carcass yield. A total of sixteen grower pigs were utilized as experimental subjects. The measured variables included slaughter weight, carcass weight, carcass length, and carcass percentage. The experimental design was a randomized block design comprising four initial weight groups and four different treatment levels of palm sugar in drinking water: R0 (0% palm sugar solution), R1 (2% palm sugar solution), R2 (4% palm sugar solution), and R3 (6% palm sugar solution). Statistical analysis revealed that supplementation with 2% palm sugar significantly increased slaughter weight (P<0.05), whereas higher concentrations did not produce statistically significant effects. The least significant difference (LSD) test confirmed that pigs receiving 2% palm sugar in their drinking water exhibited a significantly greater slaughter weight compared to the control group. However, no significant differences were observed in carcass length, carcass weight, or carcass percentage across treatments. In conclusion, administering 2% palm sugar solution—equivalent to 140 grams—in drinking water effectively enhances slaughter weight (97.67 kg) in grower pigs without adversely affecting carcass quality parameters. 

Keywords: pig, palm sugar, carcass quality

In 2014, the province of North Sulawesi implemented a cigarette tax, a regulatory levy specifically intended to address public health concerns. North Sulawesi is recognized as one of the prominent regions for nutmeg production in Indonesia. Nutmeg is composed of four distinct parts: flesh, seed, mace, and skin. However, the flesh portion is typically discarded due to its relatively low market value compared to the seed and mace. Consequently, it is necessary to develop innovative and creative applications for nutmeg flesh, such as transforming it into an effervescent product. Effervescence refers to a form characterized by the generation of gas bubbles (CO2) resulting from a chemical reaction, specifically between citric acid and sodium bicarbonate. This study aims to evaluate the physical, chemical, and sensory properties of nutmeg flesh effervescent formulations with varying concentrations of citric acid and sodium bicarbonate. Four distinct formulations were prepared, each differing in the concentrations of the two reactive components. The findings indicate that the variations in citric acid and sodium bicarbonate concentrations significantly influenced parameters including dissolution time, moisture content, total acidity, and taste of the nutmeg flesh effervescent. Dissolution time ranged from approximately 1 minute 36 seconds to 2 minutes 2 seconds, moisture content varied between 7.15% and 8.13%, and total acidity ranged from 0.0031% to 0.0120%. Sensory evaluation revealed that formulation C achieved the highest acceptability score and was regarded as nearly delightful by the panelists.

In the context of expanding business opportunities, the food and soft drink industry represents a highly promising sector that continues to experience significant growth. Stereodesserts is a premium brand specializing in the production of homemade desserts, originating from Bandung, that utilizes high-quality ingredients and aligns with environmentally sustainable practices through its support of the green campaign. A key competitive advantage for Stereodesserts lies in its packaging design. Consequently, this study aims to investigate the significance and effectiveness of the packaging design employed by Stereodesserts.

This research pursues two primary objectives: (1) to elucidate the importance of Stereodesserts’ packaging design, and (2) to evaluate the performance of the packaging. Investors have recently become more knowledgeable about investments aimed at securing their future financial benefits. Over time, they have recognized that certain events can significantly influence stock price performance, raising concerns about whether such events might impact the value of their holdings, particularly those within the LQ-45 index. Among these events, presidential elections are considered a macroeconomic factor that affects multiple aspects of the country’s economy, including investment activities. This study aims to examine the extent to which stock prices exhibit significant changes in response to presidential elections and to determine whether this event influences the prices of stocks in the LQ-45 index. Employing Time Series Analysis, the Paired Sample t-Test, and purposive sampling, the research sample comprises all stocks listed in the LQ-45 on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The findings reveal a correlation between stock prices and presidential elections, with a statistically significant change in stock prices observed following the election. Consequently, it is concluded that presidential elections constitute a factor affecting stock price performance. Investors are advised to exercise increased caution when processing such information during stock transactions to enhance investment decision-making.  

Keywords: stock price, presidential election, event study

The novel *My Sister’s Keeper* by Jodie Picoult, regarded as one of her significant works, serves as the focal point of this study. This research, entitled "Anna Fitzgerald's Conflicts in the Novel *My Sister’s Keeper* by Jodie Picoult," aims to examine the internal and external conflicts experienced by the protagonist, Anna Fitzgerald, as well as to explore the causes and consequences of these conflicts on her character. Buehler’s theory of conflict styles (1998) was employed to analyze Anna Fitzgerald’s internal and physical conflicts within the narrative. Additionally, the theoretical framework proposed by Wellek and Warren (1964) was utilized to elucidate the relationship between literature and psychological concepts by investigating the origins and ramifications of Anna’s conflicts as portrayed by Picoult in the novel. Data collection focused on identifying Anna’s inner and physical conflicts alongside their causes and effects. These data were subsequently analyzed through intrinsic and extrinsic approaches: the intrinsic approach was applied to investigate the plot and character development of Anna Fitzgerald, while the extrinsic approach was used to examine the psychological dimensions of the causes and effects impacting her. Findings indicate that Anna Fitzgerald, as the central character, confronts both internal and physical conflicts that profoundly influence her life. These conflicts principally stem from her sister’s illness, resulting in various physical, psychological, and behavioral consequences for Anna.

This study, entitled "Prepositions in English and the Talaud Language in the Book of Isaiah: A Contrastive Analysis," aims to examine and compare the forms and meanings of prepositions in both languages as they appear in the Book of Isaiah, focusing specifically on their syntactic structures. The research addresses two primary questions: what are the forms and meanings of prepositions in English and Talaud, respectively, within the context of the Book of Isaiah, and what similarities and differences exist between them? The objectives of this investigation are to identify and classify the various forms and meanings of prepositions in English and Talaud, and subsequently to analyze their points of convergence and divergence.

Employing a descriptive research methodology, this study draws upon theoretical frameworks provided by Crystal (1999), Aarts and Aarts (1982), Harman (1992), and Lado (1972). Data collection was conducted through a combination of library research and fieldwork. English data were sourced from the English Bible, linguistic literature, and online resources, while Talaud data were obtained from the Talaud Bible and native speakers serving as informants. 

The findings reveal both similarities and differences between English and Talaud prepositions in terms of form and meaning. Concerning form, English exhibits both single-word and multi-word prepositional constructions; in contrast, Talaud data indicate the presence of only single-word prepositions. Regarding meaning, there are notable correspondences between the two languages. 

Theoretically, this research contributes to the body of knowledge on prepositional usage by providing a comparative reference that highlights both commonalities and distinctions between English and the Talaud language, with implications for the advancement of syntactic studies. Practically, it aims to assist students studying English and related fields by enhancing their understanding of prepositional forms and meanings across these languages.

Keywords: Preposition, English, Talaud Language, Contrastive Analysis

Mustard is an agricultural commodity that attracts considerable interest from the community, thereby possessing substantial commercial potential and economic value. The application of organic fertilizers has been demonstrated to enhance various soil properties, including physical, chemical, and biological characteristics. This study utilized weed biomass as the primary raw material for the production of both organic and inorganic fertilizers. The objectives were to evaluate the effects of inorganic and organic fertilizers, as well as their individual impacts, on the growth and yield of mustard plants, and to identify an optimal fertilization dosage for mustard cultivation. The research was conducted from August to October 2018 at the experimental garden of the Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University, Walian Village, Tomohon City, and at the Mapanget Balitpalma Laboratory. A factorial completely randomized design was employed, with two factors: (A) fertilizer treatments comprising A0 (0 kg Phonska/ha and 0 kg Urea/ha) and A1 (200 kg Phonska/ha and 100 kg Urea/ha), and (B) organic weed fertilizer levels including B1 (15 tons weed/ha), B2 (20 tons weed/ha), B3 (25 tons weed/ha), and B4 (30 tons weed/ha). Each of the eight treatment combinations was replicated three times, resulting in a total of 24 experimental units. The findings revealed a significant interaction between inorganic and organic fertilizers on the wet weight of the mustard plants, particularly at the A1B1 treatment level (200 kg Phonska/ha, 100 kg Urea/ha, and 15 tons/ha organic weed fertilizer). Overall, the application of both inorganic and organic fertilizers derived from weeds effectively enhanced the wet biomass of mustard plants. Based on the results, the recommended fertilization regimen for mustard production consists of 200 kg Phonska/ha, 100 kg Urea/ha, and 15 tons/ha organic weed fertilizer.

Keywords: Mustard, Inorganic Fertilizer, Organic Fertilizer, Weed

This study focuses on Papua, the easternmost island of Indonesia, which retains numerous privileges and traditional values largely unaffected by globalization. The indigenous customs and beliefs continue to be actively preserved and upheld. Among these traditions is the stone-burning ritual practiced by the Dani tribal community, symbolizing unity and the sacredness of social life. This ritual is prominently observed during significant events such as the conclusion of customary warfare, bride price ceremonies, reconciliation with natural spirits, and Christian celebrations like Christmas and Easter.

Papuan traditional ceremonies encompass various rituals conducted to commemorate important cultural occasions, including traditional feasts, births, deaths, marriages, harvest thanksgiving, and other significant events. The stone-burning ritual, inherited from ancestral practices, historically functioned as a form of offering and an expression of communal joy and sorrow during pivotal moments. Furthermore, this ritual serves to consolidate collective spiritual strength, invoking the presence of clan protective spirits. These spirits act as guides and aides to individual souls, assisting them in fulfilling their obligations to the clan and the broader community.

Keywords: tradition, ritual, stone burning

The delivery of public services by government officials to the community represents a manifestation of state functions, whereby the apparatus operates as public servants dedicated to serving the state and its citizens. Among the public services managed by the district government is the processing of sale and purchase deeds. Despite these services, public complaints persist regarding the performance of civil servants within the organization, citing delays, inefficiencies, and complexities, particularly in the facilitation of sale and purchase deeds. Additionally, concerns have been raised regarding levies that occasionally deviate from established regulations.

This study aims to investigate and elucidate the quality of sale and purchase deed services at the District Office of Kema, North Minahasa Regency. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study gathered data from ten informants comprising government officials at the village level, community leaders, and residents within North Minahasa Regency, Kema District. Data analysis involved systematic procedures including data reduction, presentation, and verification to draw substantiated conclusions.

Findings indicate that the quality of sale and purchase deed services at the District Office of Kema is generally satisfactory. The service requirements for processing deeds are aligned strictly with regulatory provisions, with no extraneous demands that might unnecessarily complicate transactions. When applicants submit all requisite documents, the processing of deeds occurs promptly and within the stipulated timeframe. The certificates issued by the district government provide legal certainty to service recipients, as the authorities exercise meticulous scrutiny to verify the validity of all supporting documents. Any invalid documentation results in the immediate cessation of the deed processing procedure.

Furthermore, the fees associated with obtaining a sale and purchase deed are regulated in accordance with prevailing legislation, and no additional charges are levied beyond the prescribed costs. These procedures and associated fees are transparently communicated to the public through posted tables in the service waiting area, ensuring awareness of all conditions involved in the process. The district government administers these services without discrimination, upholding equal rights for all community members to access the service.

In cases where delays occur in processing sale and purchase deeds, the government is forthcoming in clarifying the specific obstacles responsible for such delays. Overall, the study concludes that the District Office of Kema demonstrates a commendable standard of service quality in the management of sale and purchase deeds.

**Keywords:** Sale and Purchase Deed, Service Quality, Public Service, District Government, North Minahasa Regency

This study is prompted by a series of findings concerning the management and reporting of School Operational Assistance (BOS) funds, alongside issues faced by the Manado City Government, specifically delays in reporting detailed BOS fund assets. Such delays significantly influence the balance sheet values within the Regional Government Financial Statements. Consequently, this research aims to examine the reporting mechanisms for BOS funds within the Education and Culture Office of Manado City. The study's objectives are confined to three focal points: understanding the reporting process of BOS fund assets by the Manado City Education and Culture Office, identifying the factors that contribute to delays in reporting these assets—critical determinants of balance sheet values—and exploring the strategies implemented by the Manado City Government to address these reporting challenges.

Employing a qualitative research methodology with a case study design, data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. Participants included individuals responsible for receiving and processing BOS fund reports from the Manado City Regional Finance and Assets Agency, the Manado City BOS Management Team, and the School BOS Management Teams. The findings reveal that the BOS fund reporting process, including asset-specific reporting, complies with the relevant regulations. However, challenges identified include limitations in human resources, account mismatches, and issues of non-compliance. To mitigate these obstacles, the Manado City Government has undertaken measures such as providing mentorship and support to operator personnel, reclassifying accounts following reconciliation efforts, and enforcing sanctions where necessary.

NDF AND ADF DIGESTIBILITY OF COMPLETE FEED OF CORN FORAGE IN FH CATTLE. The purpose of this study was to determine the consumption and digestibility of NDF and ADF based on corn forage based feed in FH cattle. The experimental material used was 14 FH dairy cows, aged 7-8 years with weights between 300 - 400 kg, treatment feed, consisting of: Ra = 30% concentrate feed + 70% corn forage and treatment Rb = 30% concentrate + 35% corn forage + 35% king grass. The research method was a biological experiment, with a statistical analysis of the two-sample T test with unequal variation (t-test two sample assuming unequal varience). The results of the T test analysis showed that the NDF consumption of Rb treatment was not significantly different (P> 0.05) compared to Ra, whereas the consumption of ADF, as well as the digestibility of NDF and ADF treatment of Rb was significantly different (P <0.01) with Ra treatment. It can be concluded that the digestibility of NDF and ADF complete feed consisting of concentrate, corn forage and king grass is better, compared to complete feed consisting of concentrate and corn forage. Keywords: Consumption, digestibility, NDF, ADF, complete feed, FH cattle.

Over the past decade, agricultural development has predominantly aligned with commodity development, primarily aimed at fulfilling domestic food requirements. In the context of globalization, it is imperative for the government to actively facilitate and encourage communities to engage in productive activities, including the advancement of the creative food industry. This industry is distinguished not only by its ability to meet quantitative and qualitative standards but also by its capacity to generate marketable value through product excellence and economic added value. The collaboration among various stakeholders has stimulated the enhancement of creative food product output by leveraging technology, information, innovative ideas, creativity, and skills emerging from the community, encompassing both individual farmers and industrial groups within South Minahasa Regency.

This research aims to: (1) identify the types and characteristics of coconut-based food industries in South Minahasa Regency; (2) calculate the economic added value derived from the development of these industries; and (3) determine appropriate methods, strategies, and models for advancing coconut-based food industry development in the region. The study employs a mixed methodological approach, including a descriptive analysis, economic added value computation based on the framework of Coster and Schaffer (1982), and a SWOT analysis to formulate effective developmental strategies and models tailored to South Minahasa.

Findings indicate the existence of three primary categories of creative food industries utilizing coconut as raw material in South Minahasa Regency: culinary products, medicinal applications, and research and development initiatives. These industries have demonstrably contributed significant economic added value at both the micro level—benefiting farmers and industrial groups—and the macro level, fostering broader economic growth within the community. The implementation of methods, strategies, and models that align with the local potential and characteristics has proven essential to this success.

Keywords: agricultural development, creative food industry, coconut raw materials, economic added value, South Minahasa Regency

**Abstract**

This study investigates the challenges in implementing Good Governance in the Village of Sea, which have not been adequately addressed in accordance with Law No. 8 of 1999 concerning the implementation of good governance. The researchers employed a qualitative methodology, gathering data through a series of stages including observation, in-depth interviews, and document analysis. Data collection was guided by a structured interview protocol, with ten informants participating in the interview process. 

Following data collection, the researchers conducted a multi-phase analysis. Initially, data obtained from observations and interviews were organized, transcribed, and edited as necessary. Subsequently, the data underwent reduction by selecting and refining relevant information, summarizing key points while discarding extraneous material. The third phase involved presenting and simplifying the processed data to facilitate the drawing of conclusions. Finally, conclusions were verified by cross-referencing the data and incorporating discussions with colleagues and supervisory faculty to ensure validity and to analyze causal relationships.

The findings revealed that the implementation of Good Governance has not been optimally realized, as anticipated by Law No. 8 of 1999 and the theoretical framework proposed by Inu Kencana (1994). The study concludes that several principles of Good Governance remain inadequately fulfilled. Public participation in the management processes of KTP (Identity Card) and KK (Family Card) issuance is notably insufficient. Although law enforcement activities are functioning adequately, the establishment of village regulations (PERDES) is advisable to improve governance. Transparency requires enhancement, particularly regarding financial disclosure to the community. 

Government responsiveness is deficient, evidenced by delays in updating beneficiary data for social assistance programs such as rice provision. Updates to the Village Government Work Plan (RKP Desa) and village profiles must reflect current conditions as of 2016. Additionally, the government’s communication with the community, including the availability of information boards and outreach efforts for KK and ID card services, remains limited. While consensus-building processes are effectively conducted, issues concerning equitable access to services for vulnerable populations persist, potentially undermining targeted assistance efforts. Furthermore, the effectiveness and efficiency of governance cannot be rated positively due to these identified shortcomings.

On a positive note, accountability mechanisms are functioning well, as demonstrated by routine financial reporting to the district government and proactive community notification about upcoming programs. This research aims to contribute to the sociological theory of governance and to provide practical recommendations for improving the effectiveness and efficiency of Good Governance implementation at the village level.

**Keywords:** Good Governance, Village Governance, Public Participation, Transparency, Accountability

Among the numerous languages spoken throughout Indonesia, several are nearing extinction and warrant urgent scholarly attention. Bolangese, the focus of this study, represents one such language, with its speaker population estimated to number fewer than one thousand individuals. This research investigates morphological typology, specifically examining the processes, rules, and categories of word formation within Bolangese. The primary objectives of the study are to identify and explicate the mechanisms of word formation, establish the governing rules, and classify the various types of word formation present.

Employing a qualitative methodology, this study utilizes descriptive linguistic methods to analyze linguistic phenomena observed in the Bolangese language. The dataset comprises written Bolangese materials in the form of scripts, which were gathered through observation, bibliographic research, and collaboration with informants. Data analysis was conducted utilizing distributional methods, incorporating the binary opposition technique as delineated by Subroto (2007). The identification of word formation processes and rules draws upon Kridalaksana’s (1989) theoretical framework, while Keraf’s (1980) concepts underpin the analysis of language typology.

Findings indicate that affixation in Bolangese encompasses affixes that produce verbs, nouns, adjectives, adverbs, and imperatives. Meanwhile, reduplication processes generate verbs, nouns, adjectives, and adverbs; however, no evidence of reduplication forming imperatives was found. The rules governing word formation in Bolangese are categorized into inflectional and derivational types. In total, the language features 44 distinct word formation types, comprising 36 affixational and 8 reduplicative forms. Consequently, Bolangese can be characterized as a language typified by affixation and reduplication processes. The study recommends further research into Bolangese typology to explore additional forms of word formation, including compound words, abbreviations, and metanalysis.

Keywords: Bolangese, Typology, Word Formation

This study seeks to identify the different models of distribution channels and staple food marketing, as well as to evaluate the performance of each distribution and marketing channel for staple foods to consumers in the Talaud Islands District. Primary data were collected through direct field observations and in-depth interviews, employing a pre-designed questionnaire administered to food marketing and distribution institutions. Respondent selection was carried out using a purposive sampling technique alongside snowball sampling to identify key informants within various marketing agencies. 

The findings indicate that the distribution of milled rice in the Talaud Islands District follows a single model involving multiple marketing agents, specifically village traders, wholesalers, and retailers based in Manado and Lirung town within the Talaud Islands. In contrast, the distribution of packaged rice from Surabaya involves a network comprising local distributors in Manado, wholesalers in Manado city, and retailers located in Lirung town. 

Furthermore, the study revealed that the total marketing margin for the milled rice distribution channel in the Talaud Islands amounts to Rp 2,500 per kilogram, with total marketing costs of Rp 413 per kilogram. For packaged rice, the total marketing margin across distribution channels reaches Rp 3,500 per kilogram, accompanied by marketing costs of Rp 454 per kilogram. The farmer's share of the revenue from milled rice marketing in Talaud Islands stands at 73.68%, based on a farm-gate price of Rp 7,000 per kilogram and a consumer price of Rp 9,500 per kilogram. The cost-efficiency ratio is significantly higher for village trader marketing agencies compared to those operating in Manado and Lirung city retailers. Notably, the lowest cost-benefit ratio was observed among large wholesalers in the Manado marketing agencies.

The buying decision stage refers to the phase in which consumers determine whether to purchase a specific product. This study aims to examine the simultaneous impact of brand image and perceived quality on consumer buying decisions. The research population comprises individuals residing in Manado who use Samsung mobile phones, with a sample size of 100 respondents. Employing a quantitative approach, data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Multiple Regression Analysis. The findings indicate that both brand image and perceived quality exert a significant simultaneous influence on consumer buying decisions. However, when considered individually, brand image has a statistically significant effect, whereas perceived quality does not. Given these results, the brand image variable is recommended as a more effective predictor of consumer buying behavior. Future research is encouraged to incorporate additional variables that may affect buying decisions and to expand the respondent base beyond Manado to include comparative analyses with neighboring cities.  
Keywords: brand image, perceived quality, buying decision

UTILIZATION OF BOKASHI FESES COW ON PRODUCTIVITY RATOON OF KAWALI SORGHUM VARIETY. This study aims to determine the effect of bokashi cow feces on the productivity of ratoon sorghum variety of kawali. This research was implemented in Wusa village at districts Talawaan. The design used was completely randomized design (CRD), which consists of 4 treatments and 5 replications to obtain 20 units of trial. The treatment consists of P0= without fertilization, P1= 4 kg of fertilization, P2= 8 kg of fertilization, P3= 12 kg of fertilization. The measured variables are number of tillers, plant height, and panicle weight. Result of the analysis showed that treatment with 12 kg/plot provides highly significant effect (P <0.01) of the number of tillers, plant height, and panicle weight compared with other treatments, ie 8 and 4 kg/plot. The HSD test indicated that treatment number of tillers showed that between treatment P3, P0, P1, and P2 showed highly significant. In the treatments of advanced test HSD indicated also that plant height between P3, P0, P1, and P2 showed highly significant. In the treatment of panicle weight of advanced test of HSD showed that between treatment P3 and P0, treatment of P3 and P1 is very different, but the treatment of P3 and P2 showed no significant difference. Based on this research it can be concluded that cattle feces bokashi as the organic fertilizer up to 12 kg produced the best effect on number of tillers, plant height, and panicle weight. Keywords: Bokashi, productivity, ratoon, sorghum, kawali

Electromagnetic waves directly influence the generation and spatial distribution of temperature in food items subjected to microwave heating. When using a domestic microwave oven operating at a single frequency of 2.45 GHz, the temporal heat distribution within sweet potatoes exhibits varied patterns. Microwave heating processes primarily depend on the dielectric properties of the food material. This study aims to simulate the heat distribution within sweet potatoes of different geometric shapes and sizes when exposed to microwave radiation. Specifically, spherical and cylindrical sample geometries were examined. The finite element method was employed to model the heat distribution within the microwave oven, supporting the analysis. The results indicate that both the shape and size of the sweet potato significantly affect the resulting heat distribution. This effect arises from the substantial penetration depth of microwaves in the sweet potato, such that the absorption of microwave energy depends on the sample’s thickness and geometry. Simulation results reveal that heating does not initiate at the surface and progress inward; rather, the highest temperature increase occurs near the sample's center, where microwave energy conversion to heat predominates, subsequently spreading outward to the surface after microwave penetration depth is reached. Comparatively, the spherical samples exhibit a more rapid temperature increase than cylindrical samples. For instance, a spherical sweet potato with a radius of 42 mm required approximately 60 seconds to reach 100°C, demonstrating an almost uniform heat distribution throughout the sample.
