This study, entitled *Commissive Acts in the Novel Herzog by Saul Bellow*, investigates the nature of commissive speech acts within the framework of pragmatics. Communication is often regarded as a complex process involving various challenges. According to Leech (1983), speech situations can be analyzed through five components, one of which is the speech act. Speech acts represent fundamental units of communication. Austin (1962) categorizes speech acts into three types: locutionary, illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts. He further classifies illocutionary acts based on their intended functions, including verdictives, executives, commissives, behabitives, and expositives. Commissive acts specifically involve commitments made by the speaker concerning future actions, such as promises. This research aims to identify, categorize, and analyze commissive acts as they appear in Saul Bellow’s *Herzog*. The data collected are examined using Austin’s theoretical framework and analyzed through a descriptive methodology. The findings reveal various types and functions of commissive acts according to Austin’s classification. Among these, the commissive acts identified include persuasion, offering, engagement, planning, betting, agreeing, opposing, espousing, guaranteeing, promising, and swearing. Notably, offering is the most frequently occurring commissive function within the novel. 

Keywords: Commissive acts, Pragmatic analysis, Novel *Herzog*

ABSTRACT The educational system across the world has immensely been affected due to outbreak of Covid-19. In the absence of traditional classroom teaching, online learning has emerged as closest substitute for offline teaching. Against such a backdrop, it is pertinent to examine the students' perception about online learning system adopted at the university level during the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic. This research aims to identify the students' perceptions on the ease of use and usefulness of online learning based on Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and to analyze the factors influencing students' perceptions towards English online learning especially in EFL context. For the present study, the descriptive approach with survei method has been adopted and responses from 97 students of English Department of Sam Ratulangi University were collected through online questionnaire and structured interviews. Purposive sampling was used to obtain the sample and ten students were interviewed to seek more information about their experiences during the learning process. The findings of the study reveal students' positive perception towards online learning and thus acceptance of the new learning system. It has also empirically demonstrated the significance of online learning in the time of Covid-19 crisis. There were several factors that influence the students' perception, which were the perceiver, the object, and the situation. The participants agreed that online learning has emerged as a new way of enhancing the learning process and may further improve the learning output.Keywords: students' perception, online learning, English learning, Covid-19

Indonesia employs a democratic system of governance. One challenge arising from the implementation of this democratic system is the direct election of regional heads. Religion has often served as a means through which various groups pursue their objectives. This study aims to analyze the consequences of internal conflict within the Evangelical Christian Church in 2013. The findings reveal that social conflict emerged within the Evangelical Christian Church following the gubernatorial election in North Maluku in 2013. Notably, this conflict was explicitly and clearly instigated by BPHS. Furthermore, the reform movement of GMIH was initiated by elements among regional heads who were defeated in the direct election for governor in North Maluku. These actors exploited their constituents to undermine the unity of GMIH. This research recommends that church organizations, including pastors and church committees, should refrain from direct involvement in practical political activities or serving as political committees. Pastors holding structural positions are advised against engaging in practical politics, such as managing political parties or candidacies for legislative councils, KPU, or executive regional offices including regent, vice-regent, governor, or vice-governor. Additionally, local government authorities, exemplified by the North Halmahera Regent and the Local Citizen Council Delegation (DPRD), must respond promptly to monitor conflicts within the church and seek appropriate solutions.  
 
Keywords: Social Conflict, Governor’s Election, Democracy

Title: The Role of Interpersonal Communication between Guardians and Student Teachers at New Village Ternate Vocational School Tjokroaminoto

Abstract:  
The development of educational institutions is significantly influenced by students’ academic knowledge, discipline, and respect towards their teachers. Motivational levels among students are also closely linked to the nature of interactions and relational dynamics fostered by teachers within the school environment. Observational research indicates that not all educational settings possess teachers capable of effectively motivating their students, a shortfall largely attributed to insufficient interpersonal communication between teachers and their assigned guardians or homeroom teachers. Interpersonal communication serves as a critical factor in achieving educational objectives during the learning process. It entails the exchange and reception of messages between sender and receiver, which may occur either directly—where parties communicate face-to-face without intermediaries—or indirectly, mediated by certain communication tools. This study employed qualitative research methods grounded in symbolic interaction theory to investigate the interpersonal communication between homeroom teachers and their students at New Village Ternate Vocational School Tjokroaminoto. The findings reveal varying degrees of effectiveness in these communications, identifying both successful and suboptimal interactions. It is recommended that interpersonal communication between homeroom teachers and students be enhanced and more intensively practiced to prevent relational fatigue, thereby supporting both academic learning and student character development.

Keywords: Interpersonal Communication, Homeroom Teacher, Student Motivation, Vocational Education, Symbolic Interaction Theory

ABSTRACT The research aims to assess the response to the growth and production of onion against of liquid organic fertilizer from cow biourie in some concentrations and to get the best concentration for the growth and production of red onion. The research was conducted atfield experimental in Pandu, North Minahasa regency from May to July 2014. The experiment was designed using a randomized block design. The treatment was concentration of cow biourine namely 0% (B1) 10%, (B2) 20%, (B3) 30%, (B4) 40% and (B5) 50%. Each treatment was replicated three times. Characters observed were plant height, number of leaves, tuber diameter, number of tuber, fresh weight of tuber with leaves and dry weight of tuber. Data was analyzed using analysis of variance. The result showed that the biourine concentration had significant effect on plant height, number of leaves, tuber diameter, number of tuber, fresh weight of tuber with leaves and dry weight of tuber. Treatment of B1, B2, B3 and B4 concentration were not significant difference at plant height. However, those four treatments were significantly different compared to B0 and B5. The fives treatment differed with the control on characters of number of leaves, number of tuber andfresh weight of tuber with leaves. On character of tuber dry weight, B2 treatment was significant difference compared to control whereas the other treatments were not significantly differed. On character of tuber diameter, three treatments were significant difference compared to the control namely B2, B4 and B5. Keywords : Allium ascalonicum L, biourine cow, fertilizer, growth and production

This study aims to examine the impact of education/training, motivation, and competence on employee performance. Employing a descriptive research design, the investigation targeted the entire population of civil servants at the Local Revenue Office of North Sulawesi Province. A proportional sampling method was applied to select 150 civil servants, comprising 50 individuals from the headquarters and 100 from the Local Technical Implementation Unit (UPTD). Data were analyzed using multiple regression analysis to test the proposed hypotheses. The findings reveal that education/training significantly influences employee performance at a significance level of α = 0.05. Specifically, employee performance is predicted to increase by 0.263 units for each one-unit enhancement in education/training, assuming motivation and competence remain constant. The effect of employee motivation on performance was observed to be impeded due to inadequate coordination with relevant technical institutions. Consequently, the study recommends strengthening coordination among related institutions and relevant authorities, both vertically and horizontally across departments and sub-departments within the organization. Furthermore, it advocates for the advancement of human resource management through the implementation of technical training in local tax management and other training programs aligned with the employees’ fundamental duties and functions, aiming to ultimately enhance overall work effectiveness.

Keywords: education/training, motivation, competence, employee performance

The rapid advancements in technology compel professionals across various industries to adapt to the evolving technological landscape, with those in the broadcasting sector facing particular challenges. The proliferation of online platforms enabling access to a diverse array of video content has prompted broadcasting industry stakeholders to enhance the quality of their television programs in order to remain competitive against digital media. Among the television programming genres that have garnered significant public favor are comedy-based shows. This study aims to examine the impact of humor in television programming on brand awareness, focusing specifically on the case of the TV show Opera Van Java. Employing primary data collected via questionnaires, the research utilizes multiple linear regression analysis to evaluate responses from a sample of 209 viewers located in Manado. The findings indicate that dimensions of happiness, content quality, and message delivery significantly influence brand awareness. Despite Opera Van Java's status as a highly successful television program, it is imperative for the producers to preserve the originality of their content, continuously foster creativity in content development to engage viewers effectively, and place greater emphasis on the strategies employed in message delivery.  
Keywords: brand awareness, happiness, content quality, message delivery

This objective is to determine internal and external factors related to the productivity of chili farming and to find out the role of farmer groups in chili productivity in Raanan Baru village. This research was conducted from December 2019 to February 2020. Data collection methods were carried out by means of observation and questionnaires to farmer groups in Raanan Baru village which consisted of 30 members. In this study of chili farming, and to determine the factors related to the productivity of chili farming, seen from the crosstabulation test using SPSS v25 between each member characteristic (internal factors) and external factors with chili productivity, the descriptive method is used to determine the role of farmer groups on the productivity. Based on the results of research, internal and external factors related to the productivity of chili farming and the role of farmer groups on chili productivity. Factors related to farm productivity of members of the Cita Imbaya farmer group are age, level of education, farming status, intensity of exposure to counseling, and land tenure status. External factors for farmers in the form of business climate and business plan are also related to the productivity of members of the Cita Imbaya farmer group. The role of farmer groups that most members perceive is the role of farmer groups as a vehicle for cooperation and the role of farmer groups as farm production units.

Introduction: Chronic disease is one of the health problems in Indonesia which continues to increase and has not been successfully reduced. Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a chronic disease which has been a major cause of death and global burden of disease. The prevalence of CHD in North Sulawesi is 1.8%, exceeding the national prevalence, making North Sulawesi the fourth highest province in Indonesia. The management of CHD aims to prevent recurrent coronary events and complications by modifying risk factors. Holistic approach is needed to identify the risk factors that cause CHD. Family medicine is a medical specialty that provides health care with a holistic approach at first-level health facilities. Program Rujuk Balik (PRB), as one of the leading programs, is optimized to improve the quality of health services for the participants of BPJS Kesehatan and to facilitate access to health services for participants who have chronic diseases. The catastrophic costs can be minimized through holistic management of CHD by family physicians maximizing the function of PRB. Objective: To determine the overview of the management of PRB participants with CHD by family physicians in Manado City. Methods: This research is a descriptive study with a cross-sectional design. Results: It was found that all respondents were in the good category at managing the participants of PRB with CHD (100%). Conclusion: The management of the participants of PRB with CHD by family physicians in Manado City has been well. Keywords: program rujuk balik, coronary heart disease, family physicians.

Statement of Government Accounting Standards (PSAP) 07 is the accounting standard for property, plant and equipment including recognition, determination of carrying amount, accounting treatment of revaluation and impairment of carrying value of property and equipment. This study aims to determine the suitability of the application of accounting depreciation of fixed asset based on PSAP 07 at the Public Works Department of North Sulawesi Province. The data used is the report of depreciation in fiscal year 2016. The method used is descriptive analysis method. The results of the research indicate that the Public Works Agency in the application of fixed asset depreciation, the determination of depreciation value, the useful life of the asset, the use of depreciation method and the determination of the book value of the asset is in accordance with PSAP 07, however in the implementation of recording into reporting depreciation of fixed assets, has not implemented it independently but is done by the Regional Financial Management and Asset Board (BPKAD) of North Sulawesi Province somehow it is not in accordance with the assumption of entity independence in Government Regulation Number 71 of 2010 on Government Accounting Standards. It is expected that the Public Works Department of North Sulawesi Province may apply accounting for depreciation in accordance into applicable regulations.Keywords : PSAP 07, Depreciation of Fixed Asset, Implementation of Depreciation

Analysis of Cattle Farmers' Perceptions Regarding the Role of Extension Agents in Sangkub District, North Bolaang Mongondow Regency

Sangkub District in North Bolaang Mongondow Regency is home to approximately 596 cattle farmers, of whom 210 are organized into 21 farmer groups. Among these groups, seven remain actively engaged in farming operations, while the remainder have become inactive. Factors contributing to this inactivity may include insufficient capital, mismanagement of farm operations, or a lack of awareness concerning the economic value of cattle farming. This study aims to elucidate cattle farmers' perceptions of the role played by extension agents within Sangkub District, North Bolaang Mongondow Regency. Employing a descriptive research design, the study systematically captured and analyzed key phenomena related to the variables of interest. Purposeful sampling was used to select participants from farmer groups, resulting in a final sample of 30 cattle farmers residing in the villages of Tombolango Induk, Busisingo, and Sangkub II. Data collection utilized Likert scale measurements to quantify responses across various indicators. The findings reveal that farmers’ perceptions of extension agents’ roles are predominantly positive: 96.67% rated extension agents as facilitators positively, with 3.33% rating them very positively; as mediators, 83.33% deemed their role fair, while 3.33% rated it positively; as motivators, 83.33% assessed the role as fair, complemented by 16.67% who rated it very positively; as educators, 93.33% considered their contribution good, with 6.67% very good; and as communicators, 100% rated the role as good. Overall, 93.33% of respondents evaluated the role of extension agents in cattle farming as good, while 6.67% rated it very good. 

Keywords: Perception, Cattle Farmers, Extension Agents, North Bolaang Mongondow Regency

ABSTRACT This research, aimed at determining alternative marketing strategies especially the marketing mix for home industry of palm sugar in Tomohon. The method of analysis used are the SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) and SPACE (Stategic Position and Action Evaluation). The results show that the home industry of palm sugar has strengths: product quality is good, as well as the availability of labors and natural resources, and capital required is relatively small. While weakness its are the packaging process of products produced still wears banana leaves and seems unattractive, not having brand and product labels, the promotions which is still not optimal, as well as long distribution channels and price information that are still lacking. Opportunities that need to be explored in home industries of palm sugar in Tomohon consist of technological developments, the opening of export markets, partnership with food companies and changes in population. While threats encountered are changes of the consumer tastes and the emergence of similar products from other regions. The marketing position of palm sugar in home industries Tomohon is located in quadrant I. The strategy adopted in the marketing of this home industries has opportunity and strength in such a way that it can take advantage of existing opportunities. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 40% of maternal mortality in developing countries is associated with anemia during pregnancy. The Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) serves as a critical indicator of the effectiveness of healthcare systems within a country. The occurrence of anemia in pregnancy is influenced by adequate levels of vitamin C and sufficient iron intake. This study aimed to examine the relationship between the consumption of protein, B vitamins, folic acid, and iron, and the incidence of anemia among pregnant women in their second and third trimesters at the Amurang Health Center in East Amurang. Employing a cross-sectional analytical design, the study was conducted among pregnant women in their second and third trimesters attending the health center. Data collection involved the use of a Semi-Quantitative Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) alongside laboratory blood assessments utilizing the cyanmethemoglobin method. Statistical analyses were performed using the chi-square test. The findings revealed a statistically significant association between protein intake and anemia incidence (χ² test, p=0.000). Similarly, significant relationships were observed between anemia and the consumption of vitamin C (p=0.000), folic acid (p=0.000), and iron (p=0.000), all with p-values below the 0.05 significance threshold. These results underscore the importance of adequate nutritional intake in reducing anemia among pregnant women in this population.

ABSTRACT Pineapples are a fruit that grows on bushes with the scientific name Ananas comosus. They are native to Brazil (South America) and have been domesticated there since before Columbus' advent. In the 16th century, Spaniards brought pineapples to the Philippines and the Malaysian Peninsula, then into Indonesia in the 17th century. This study aims to know the insects associated to monocultured and polycultured pineapples (A. comosus) and to know the dominant insects among said plants. This study is expected to inform about significant insects, both as pests as well as natural enemies, so it can be managed in pineapple planting systems and used in pineapple pest control. This study was done in the pineapple plantation village of Lobong and Mongkunai, regency of BolaangMongondow. Laboratory observations were done in the Weeds and Entomology laboratory of the Agriculture Faculty, University of Sam Ratulangi. Observation of insects on plant pineapples were calculated using the trap sinks. Insect observations showed that there are 6 insect orders founded to monocultured and polycultured pineapple plants, namely: Coleoptera Orders, Orthoptera Orders, Diptera Orders, Hymenoptera Orders, Collembola Orders and Lepidoptera Orders. Dominant insects in the monocultured and polycultured pineapple plantations are firstly from the Hymenoptera Order (Family of Formicidae), next from the Orthoptera Order (Family of Acrididae), third from the Coleoptera Order (Family of Scolytidae) and fourth from the Diptera Order (Familiy of Drosophilidae). Key words : Pineapple Plant (Ananas comosus), Inventory of insects, Monocultured And Polycultured.

Management Information Systems (MIS) are commonly understood as frameworks designed to convert data into information for use by organizations or specific stakeholders requiring such information. This study addresses the issue formulated as follows: "How is the management of the National Land Management Information System (SIMTANAS) optimized to support the effective execution of land-related tasks at the Ternate City Land Office?" The primary objective of this research was to examine the management of SIMTANAS and its role in facilitating the efficient performance of land administration duties within the Ternate Land Office.

The findings indicate that while the implementation of SIMTANAS’s eight core principles at the Ternate Land Office has generally been satisfactory, it remains suboptimal. Certain criteria, specifically relevance, timeliness, and consistency, have not been fully met. Regarding the effectiveness of land-related task execution, results suggest that, although the overall process functions as intended, optimal outcomes have yet to be achieved. Key performance indicators such as initiative, creativity, responsibility, job satisfaction, and the quality and quantity of work have not reached expected standards.

SIMTANAS contributes notably to the effectiveness of land task execution at the Ternate Land Office; however, its impact is constrained by the underperformance of certain principles, particularly those concerning relevance, timeliness, and consistency. To enhance SIMTANAS’s functionality, it is recommended that efforts focus on advancing these specific principles. Furthermore, improving the effectiveness of land task implementation necessitates accelerating employee capabilities in initiative, creativity, responsibility, job satisfaction, and work quality and quantity, especially within the Ternate Land Office.

Additionally, to augment SIMTANAS’s support for land task efficiency, there is a need to improve system infrastructure and provide comprehensive training to staff involved in electronic systems and field operations. Addressing these areas will likely result in improved adherence to SIMTANAS principles and greater overall operational effectiveness in land management.

**Keywords:** National Land Systems

Urban waterfronts, inherently complex bioregions and historically significant socio-economic hubs, present substantial challenges for planning agencies attempting to anticipate and respond to developmental trends and dynamics. In their pursuit of competitiveness, cities engage in urban practices aimed at attracting investments and resources by rediscovering urban traditions and cultural elements that are fundamental to constructing a compelling urban identity. The tertiary sector, including urban tourism, is being actively promoted in strategically positioned and aesthetically appealing locations through the revitalization of city centers and waterfront areas.

Comprehending the principal challenges and issues associated with urban waterfront redevelopment is essential for planning sustainable futures for these areas. This article delineates the challenges and concerns intrinsic to urban waterfront redevelopment, which are closely linked to the historical planning of the adjacent urban regions, while also highlighting the abundant opportunities that can be harnessed as integral aspects of a city’s future growth trajectory. Although sustainable urban waterfront redevelopment strategies vary across different localities, case studies reveal that the key challenges and issues encountered share notable similarities.

This study compares four urban waterfront redevelopment plans situated in Toronto Central Waterfront, Dalian Waterfront, Zanzibar’s Stone Town, and Jakarta’s Waterfront to examine the scope of planning efforts, identify challenges distinctive to waterfront redevelopment, and analyze the approaches employed to achieve sustainable waterfront design. The objective of this comparative review is to identify exemplary implementations of theoretical frameworks, focusing on envisioned futures for waterfronts, planning methodologies, and the nature of institutional and cross-sectoral cooperation. The cases were selected to reflect variations in geographical context and cultural background, as well as differing approaches and waterfront characteristics. Zanzibar and Jakarta, both situated in developing countries, exemplify distinct challenges, particularly those involving urban poverty as a central concern. In contrast, Toronto and Dalian, located in more developed settings (Canada and China respectively), provide insights into both the differences and similarities relative to the developing-world contexts.

Findings indicate that urban waterfronts constitute environments where urban planning must continuously negotiate tensions among three critical pillars: economy, society, and ecology. Evidence from the case studies underscores that major challenges in urban waterfront redevelopment require sustainable solutions facilitated by multi-sectoral and multi-scale institutional collaboration. Key issues encompass economic diversification, preservation of social identity, flexible land use enabled by urban policies, resolution of conflicting interests, enhancement of local institutional capacities, and effective planning systems and implementation mechanisms.

Keywords: urban waterfront, sustainability, urban redevelopment, sustainable spatial planning

RETENTION OF N, Ca and P in GOAT GIVEN FINE BRAN THAT OUTOCLAVED WITH DIFFERENT LEVEL. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of autoclaved fine bran use at different levels on the retention of nitrogen (N), calcium (Ca) and phosphorus (P) in goats. This study used four goats at age of 7-8 months old with body weight of 8-10 kg. Basic feed used was Brachiaria mutica grass, which added with autoclaved fine bran at different levels, as follows: R0 = Brachiaria mutica grass R1 = Brachiaria mutica grass+ 10% autoclaved fine bran R2 = Brachiaria mutica grass+ 20% autoclaved fine bran R1 = Brachiaria mutica grass+ 30% autoclaved fine bran This study used an experimental method based on the 4 x 4 Latin square design, where livestock served as row and experimental method as a line, followed by Duncan's multiple range test analysis. Results of analysis of variance showed that the treatment effect is highly significant (p <0.01) on dry matter intake, consumption and retention of N, consumption and retention of Ca and P. With Duncan's multiple range test showed that the treatment R3 was higher (p <0.01) than treatments of R2, R1 and R0 on consumption and retention of N, Ca and P. From these results, it can be concluded that the use of autoclaved fine bran up to 30% can improve the retention of N, Ca and P in goats. Keywords: Fine bran, Autoclave, Retention, Goat

The Effects of Palm Juice Vinegar on the Organoleptic Properties of Muscovy Duck Meat (Cairina moschata)

Duck farming continues to develop in North Sulawesi, where most operations are conducted using traditional methods. The predominant duck species cultivated in this region is the Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata). Specific culinary treatments are often employed during the cooking process to mitigate the undesirable odor and tough texture commonly associated with duck meat. Palm juice vinegar, which contains acetic acid, is known to influence various food products, including duck meat, when incorporated. This study aimed to assess the organoleptic qualities of Muscovy duck breast meat subjected to immersion in palm juice vinegar. Samples of duck breast meat were immersed in the vinegar and stored for periods of 4, 8, and 12 days. Employing a completely randomized design, the study involved four treatment groups and 40 untrained panelists serving as replicates. The evaluated parameters included color, aroma, flavor, and tenderness of the meat. Statistical analysis was performed using analysis of variance (ANOVA), followed by Duncan’s Multiple Range Test (DMRT) to identify significant differences among treatments. The findings revealed that immersion in palm juice vinegar significantly affected (P<0.01) the organoleptic characteristics of Muscovy duck meat across all storage durations. Subsequent DMRT analysis indicated that the meat treated with vinegar for 12 days was rated most favorably by the panelists. 

Keywords: organoleptic evaluation, duck meat, palm juice vinegar

Masengi, G. conducted a feasibility study on the El-Shadai Restaurant business located within the culinary tourism area of Wakeke Manado. Under the supervision of Celcius Talumingan as chairman, with Grace A. J. Rumagit and Melissa L.G. Tarore serving as members, the research aimed to comprehensively examine the business activity profile and monthly profit generated by the establishment. The primary objective was to determine whether the El-Shadai Restaurant business is viable and sustainable in the specified culinary tourism region.

This study employed primary data collected through direct interviews with the business owner, utilizing a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were obtained from relevant governmental institutions, specifically the Sub-district Office of Wenang Utara. The analysis was conducted using a descriptive approach, wherein the collected data were systematically presented in tabular form. Subsequently, profit analysis was performed alongside the calculation of the Return on Cost (R/C) ratio to assess the business's feasibility.

The findings reveal that the El-Shadai Restaurant generates a monthly profit of Rp. 13,829,942. Additionally, the calculated R/C ratio was 1.33, indicating that the business is financially feasible. This ratio signifies that for every Rp. 1 expended on production costs, the restaurant yields a return of Rp. 1.33 in revenue. Consequently, the total income exceeds the total production expenses, confirming that the business continues to generate a profit on a monthly basis.

Banks function as financial intermediaries by facilitating the transfer of funds from parties with surplus capital to those requiring financial resources, as well as ensuring the efficient processing of payment transactions. This study primarily aims to examine the simultaneous effect of the CAMEL model on bank earnings and to determine the most influential individual CAMEL component on profitability among publicly listed banks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the period 2008 to 2010. The research adopts a causal-comparative design and employs Multiple Linear Regression analysis. Secondary data utilized in this investigation were sourced from relevant research journals concerning CAMEL ratios, including the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Asset Quality (AQ), Operating Expense to Operating Income (OEOI), Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), and financial statements of 15 banking institutions listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange within the specified timeframe. Hypothesis testing reveals that CAR, Asset Quality, OEOI, and LDR collectively and individually exert a significant impact on profitability. Nonetheless, it is recommended that both banking managers and researchers incorporate additional indicators to more accurately assess the overall health and performance of banks.  

Keywords: CAMEL model, profitability

The present study aimed to evaluate the impact of substituting rice bran with coffee husk meal on the energy and protein digestibility in the diets of growing pigs. Conducted over a period of 60 days, the experiment involved 20 castrated male pigs of the Duroc × Spotted Poland China crossbreed, aged between 2.5 and 3.0 months, with an average body weight ranging from 30.1 to 40.0 kg. Five dietary treatments were formulated as follows: R0 – comprising 25% rice bran and 0% coffee husk meal (control); R1 – 18.75% rice bran and 6.25% coffee husk meal (25% substitution); R2 – 12.5% rice bran and 12.5% coffee husk meal (50% substitution); R3 – 6.25% rice bran and 18.75% coffee husk meal (75% substitution); and R4 – 0% rice bran and 25% coffee husk meal (100% substitution). A Completely Randomized Block Design (CRBD) with five treatments and four replications was employed for statistical analysis using ANOVA, followed by Orthogonal Contrast testing to discern differences among treatments. Differences were considered statistically significant at P < 0.05. The measured parameters included energy and protein digestibility. Results indicated no significant differences (P > 0.05) in either energy or protein digestibility across the treatment groups. These findings suggest that coffee husk meal can effectively substitute rice bran up to 100% in the diets of growing pigs without adversely affecting energy and protein utilization.  

**Keywords:** growing pigs, rice bran, coffee husk meal, energy digestibility, protein digestibility

The present study, entitled "Perlocutionary Acts in the Film *Eat, Pray, Love* Directed by Ryan Murphy," aims to identify, classify, and analyze various facets of perlocutionary acts as manifested in the utterances within the film. Perlocutionary effects are categorized into planned and unplanned outcomes, encompassing sixteen distinct aspects. Data were collected through a systematic examination of conversational exchanges in the film, with attention to both the intended and unintended effects conveyed. The researcher engaged in multiple viewings and careful readings of the dialogues, contextualizing them by observing characters’ expressions and body language. A descriptive analytical approach was employed to explicate the perlocutionary aspects evident in interactions among characters in *Eat, Pray, Love*. The findings indicate the presence of two categories of effects—planned and unplanned—and the identification of eleven specific aspects of perlocutionary acts. In total, nineteen utterances corresponded to planned effects, while five reflected unplanned effects. The eleven identified aspects include: causing the hearer to learn or acquire knowledge, persuasion, impressing, encouragement, irritation, amusement, eliciting action from the hearer, tension relief, distraction, embarrassment, and deception. Among these, the aspects of prompting the hearer to act and causing irritation were the most frequently employed by the characters. 

Keywords: Pragmatics, Perlocutionary Act, Film.

Abstract: Consumer complaints refer to the expressions of grievances and dissatisfaction encountered by consumers during the purchase or use of products or services. When customers are dissatisfied with a product or service for which they have paid, they often resort to lodging complaints. This study aims to examine the complaint behavior of consumers at Pizza Hut in Manado and to identify the factors that prompt such complaints. To accomplish these objectives, the researcher conducted in-depth qualitative interviews with 10 informants. The findings reveal that customers tend to complain when they experience discomfort, find that the food does not meet their taste preferences or expectations, or encounter substandard service at Pizza Hut. It is recommended that customers gain a better understanding of the factors contributing to their complaints. For Pizza Hut, the results of this study may assist in reducing the incidence of complaints and enhancing overall service quality. Additionally, future researchers may benefit from the insights provided by this study in conducting related investigations.  
Keywords: consumer complaint, Pizza Hut

This study seeks to investigate the impact of advertising on consumer decision-making regarding the utilization of the Go-ride feature within the Go-Jek application among students at the Faculty of Social and Political Sciences (FISPOL), Sam Ratulangi University (Unsrat) Manado. The advertising variable was assessed through four indicators, while the consumer decision variable pertaining to Go-Jek usage was measured using seven indicators. Employing a quantitative research design, the study utilized a random sampling technique to select respondents from a population of 3,314 individuals. The sample size was determined using the Slovin formula, resulting in a final sample of 97 respondents. Data collection methods included both a literature review and field observations, with subsequent analysis conducted through correlation analysis and simple linear regression. The correlation coefficient (R) obtained was 0.609, indicating a moderately strong relationship between advertising and the decision to use Go-Jek. Additionally, the coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.370, suggesting that 37.0% of the variance in the decision to use Go-Jek among FISPOL Unsrat Manado students can be explained by advertising, while the remaining 63.0% is attributable to other factors beyond the scope of this research. These findings imply that advertising represents a significant factor influencing the decision to engage with Go-Jek services. It is anticipated that the insights gained from this study will enable the company to better comprehend consumer decision-making characteristics, thereby enhancing its ability to meet consumer preferences and demands. Consequently, improved information dissemination by the company is expected to augment consumer interest in utilizing its online transportation services.

Abstract:  
The multi-level marketing (MLM) industry is experiencing significant expansion, particularly in North Sulawesi. One notable benefit of MLM businesses is their contribution to regional economic development. A prominent example of MLM in Manado is the company Oriflame. This study aims to examine consumer trust in salespersons within the direct selling context by employing various trust measurement frameworks. The theoretical foundation of the research is grounded in concepts of consumer trust and direct selling. Employing a qualitative exploratory methodology, data were collected through in-depth interviews with a sample of ten Oriflame consumers in Manado. Findings reveal that, in terms of cognitive trust, consumers generally trust the salespersons and rarely perceive breaches in commitments related to product quality consistency as compared to the salespersons’ representations. Most participants reported that the products met their expectations, thereby reinforcing their confidence. Regarding affective trust, consumers expressed respect and gratitude toward the salespersons. Lastly, generalized trust was evident as participants reported no conflicts with salespersons, indicating that the salespersons are regarded as dependable.  
Keywords: consumer trust, direct selling, multi-level marketing.

The present study seeks to enhance a rack-type dryer by integrating both electrical energy and solar power, alongside developing a system to ensure uniform heat distribution across its three drying racks, thereby maintaining optimal drying temperatures. An experimental approach characterized by iterative trial and error was employed. The research process comprised modification, testing, observation, and analysis of temperature and humidity data. Following the modification, the dryer was evaluated through the drying of cayenne peppers. The modified solar shelf dryer consists of key components including a drying chamber, a solar collector, and an electrical heating element. The drying chamber has rectangular dimensions of 100 cm in length, 60 cm in width, and 120 cm in height, while the solar collector measures 215 cm in length, 125 cm in width at the base, tapering to 50 cm at the top, with a thickness of 16 cm. Experimental findings indicated the maximum average temperatures attained on the racks were 69.80 °C on the top shelf, 66.10 °C on the middle shelf, and 57 °C on the bottom shelf. Correspondingly, the lowest relative humidity levels recorded were 11.50% for the top shelf, 14.30% for the middle shelf, and 21.30% for the bottom shelf.

In recent years, social media platforms have experienced rapid expansion, with a vast majority of the global population maintaining active accounts. Individuals across various age groups, from children to adults, increasingly utilize social media as a primary means of daily communication. Within this context, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Manado have demonstrated a growing awareness of the potential benefits afforded by social media utilization. This study focuses on SMEs in Manado, a developing city in Indonesia, where enterprises employing social media were selected as the sample for analysis. Employing a qualitative research methodology, the study aims to characterize the nature and activities of SMEs in this locale. Findings indicate that the use of social media significantly enhances sales, revenue, brand recognition, and customer base for SMEs in Manado. However, a notable challenge confronts these enterprises: the inability to promptly respond to all customer inquiries generated through social media channels. To address this issue, it is imperative for governmental authorities to improve internet connectivity, not only in urban centers but also in rural regions, where many communities remain unconnected. Enhanced internet access would enable rural SMEs to leverage social media effectively, thereby facilitating business development in these areas.

Keywords: small and medium enterprises, impact of social media, benefits of social media, challenges in social media usage

The Sulutgo interconnection system serves as the primary electrical energy supplier for the regions of North Sulawesi and Gorontalo. In 2015, there were widespread complaints regarding its performance, primarily due to insufficient electricity supply, which resulted in continuous rolling blackouts. Consequently, accurately identifying the peak electrical load within the Sulutgo system is crucial to ensure that the energy demands of the population are adequately met. This study estimates the electrical peak load for the subsequent 12 months utilizing two approaches: the artificial neural network model employing the backpropagation method and the moving average forecasting technique. The estimation procedures were based on peak load data collected over the preceding 24 months. Analysis of the estimates reveals that the backpropagation-based artificial neural network produces fluctuating results, whereas the moving average forecasting method yields more stable outcomes. Specifically, the estimated peak loads generated by the backpropagation artificial neural network for the period from July 2016 to June 2017 are as follows (in MW): 327.48, 353.99, 316.32, 316.66, 332.37, 329.79, 332.31, 356.21, 318.60, 349.56, 351.37, and 362.04. In contrast, the moving average forecasting method estimates for the same timeframe are: 325.68, 326.03, 326.39, 326.72, 327.25, 328.09, 327.94, 328.72, 329.94, 330.32, 327.65, and 326.52 MW.  
Keywords: Peak Load Estimation, Artificial Neural Network, Moving Average Forecasting Method

Ethnic diversity constitutes a fundamental component of national culture. A nation is defined as a collective group bound by shared culture, language, and habitation. Consequently, each ethnic group possesses distinct languages, traditions, and cultural practices. Papua, an island region, maintains strong adherence to its cultural heritage; however, certain areas continue to preserve their indigenous culture without significant influence from external cultures. Among the Moni tribe, the practice of finger cutting is performed as a ritualistic expression of grief and as a form of preventative reenactment. This act, which involves the amputation of fingers, impacts the individual's physical health. The experience of grief following the loss of a loved one, particularly a family member, is profoundly intense.

This study employs a descriptive qualitative methodology. Qualitative research is a systematic approach that produces descriptive data in the form of spoken or written words and observable behaviors. The qualitative method is deemed appropriate for exploring and comprehending the cultural practice of finger cutting from an emic perspective.

The Moni ethnic group holds the tradition of finger cutting in high regard as a symbolic expression of condolence and profound sorrow upon the departure of a family member. In Papua, various techniques are utilized to perform finger cutting, including the use of sharp instruments such as knives, axes, or machetes. Additionally, some individuals resort to biting segments of their fingers to cause them to fall off, while others bind the finger tightly with a rope to constrict blood flow, causing the finger joints to die before amputation occurs.

Keywords: finger cutting, grief, cultural practice

This study aims to evaluate the effects of NPK fertilizer and straw compost on the growth and yield of rice cultivated using the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) method. The research was conducted over a five-month period, from August to December 2015, in the Tara-Tara Dua Sub-District, West Tomohon District, Tomohon City. Employing a randomized group design, the experiment investigated the impact of varying combinations of straw compost and NPK fertilizer. The treatments included: P0 (100% NPK + 0% straw compost), P1 (75% NPK + 25% straw compost), P2 (50% NPK + 50% straw compost), P3 (25% NPK + 75% straw compost), and P4 (0% NPK + 100% straw compost).

Results indicated that the application of NPK fertilizer and straw compost generally enhanced the plant growth rate between 21 and 49 days after planting, with a marked increase observed from 49 to 77 days, followed by a significant decline from 77 to 91 days post-planting. The combined use of NPK fertilizer and straw compost notably influenced rice growth and productivity, as measured by dry plant weight, dry harvested grain yield per garden bed, and dry milled grain yield per garden bed. Notably, substituting NPK fertilizer with 25% to 100% straw compost, corresponding to a dosage of 4.5 kg to 18 kg, yielded comparable dry milled and dry harvested grain outputs. Specifically, dry plant weights ranged from 31.03 g to 31.75 g, dry harvested grain yields varied from 6.33 kg to 7.66 kg per garden bed, and dry milled grain yields ranged between 5.03 kg and 6.50 kg per garden bed across treatments.

Furthermore, statistical analysis revealed no significant differences in growth rate, dry plant weight, or grain yields between treatments utilizing 25% to 100% straw compost and those receiving 100% NPK fertilizer. These findings suggest that straw compost at these levels can effectively replace NPK fertilizer in rice cultivation under the SRI method. Consequently, it is recommended that farmers adopt the use of 100% rice straw compost for SRI-based rice cultivation.

Keywords: System of Rice Intensification, fertilizer impact, straw compost, Tara-Tara

This study aimed to evaluate the quality of irrigation water utilized in the rice fields of Ranoyapo Village, located in Ranoiapo District, South Minahasa Regency. The investigation was carried out over a three-month period from September to November 2018. Water samples were collected from two specific points: prior to entering the rice fields and at the exit location within Ranoyapo Village. Subsequent analyses were performed at the Manado Industrial Research and Standardization Laboratory. The results indicated that the pH levels measured before and after the rice fields were 6.71 and 6.52, respectively, both falling within an acceptable range. Electrical conductivity values (DHL) recorded before and after the fields were 0.17830 ds/m and 0.15880 ds/m, respectively, indicating good water quality. Total dissolved solids (TDS) concentrations were 244 mg/L before and 282 mg/L after the fields, also categorized as good. Nitrate nitrogen (NO3-N) levels were found to be 0.44 mg/L prior to and 0.89 mg/L following the irrigation area, both within permissible limits. Chloride concentrations remained consistent at 0.2178 me/L at both sampling points, classified as good. Boron levels were below 0.08 mg/L before and after the fields, meeting quality standards. Phosphate phosphorus (PO4-P) concentrations were 0.03 mg/L before and 0.09 mg/L after the irrigation area, both regarded as good quality. Conversely, potassium concentrations were 3.49 mg/L before and 3.59 mg/L after the fields, which were deemed to be of poor quality according to the Ayers and Wetscot (1985) standards for irrigation water. In conclusion, except for potassium, all measured water quality parameters conformed to established criteria for irrigation use.  

Keywords: irrigation water quality, water quality assessment, Ranoyapo Village, rice field irrigation

The increasingly competitive landscape of the hotel industry necessitates that hotel management comprehensively understand travelers' preferences and their decision-making processes regarding hotel selection. This study aims to identify the key factors influencing hotel choice and to assess the actual performance of these factors at Four Points by Sheraton Manado. Utilizing Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA), data were collected through a survey of 100 hotel guests. Findings indicate that employee service quality occupies Quadrant I, signifying high importance but low performance. Security, room quality, and receptionist services fall within Quadrant II, indicating both high importance and high performance. Food and recreational facilities are categorized in Quadrant III, reflecting low importance and low performance, while value is situated in Quadrant IV, denoting low importance but satisfactory performance. Based on these results, it is recommended that Four Points by Sheraton Manado maintain factors exhibiting both high importance and performance, while prioritizing improvements in areas with low performance but high importance. 

Keywords: hotel selection factors, consumer preferences, service quality, customer satisfaction, importance-performance analysis.

This study aimed to evaluate and characterize the effectiveness of the Family Planning Village (Kampung KB) Program implemented in Temboan Village, Maesaan District, South Minahasa Regency. Employing a qualitative descriptive research design, data were gathered through direct field observations, interviews with key informants, and the review of relevant documentation. The theoretical framework guiding this study was derived from Richard M. Steers’ theory on effectiveness measurement, which emphasizes key indicators including goal attainment, integration, and adaptation. Findings indicate that the Kampung KB Program in Temboan Village has achieved a satisfactory level of effectiveness. Nonetheless, several challenges were identified, notably the inadequacy of human resources within certain community segments, leading to misunderstandings regarding the program. Additionally, the socialization process was found to be insufficiently developed in both its preparation and execution stages, and there remain gaps in the provision of necessary facilities and infrastructure. The researcher recommends enhancing the socialization process to ensure more thorough preparation and implementation, thereby enabling the community to gain a clearer understanding of the Kampung KB Program. Furthermore, improvements in facilities and infrastructure are essential to ensure data are appropriately managed and stored, specifically within the MyData House.  

Keywords: Effectiveness, Family Planning Village Program, Community

Abstract:  
This study aims to elucidate the role of the Regional Employment Board in the recruitment process for structural official positions within the South Halmahera District Government. Additionally, it seeks to identify and analyze both internal and external factors influencing the Regional Employment Board's implementation of Civil Servant (PNS) recruitment for these structural roles. Employing a qualitative descriptive methodology, the research addresses the Board’s operational role through data collected via direct field observations and interviews with relevant respondents and informants. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive qualitative techniques. Normative recruitment procedures are governed by Government Regulation No. 13 of 2002 concerning the appointment of Civil Servants (PNS) to structural positions, emphasizing professionalism aligned with competencies, performance, hierarchical ranking appropriate to the role, and objective criteria that exclude considerations of gender, ethnicity, race, religion, or social class. The recruitment system for structural positions in the South Halmahera District reveals various challenges impacting employee motivation, which consequently affects organizational effectiveness and the successful implementation of future personnel development programs. To enhance workforce development outcomes, it is imperative to address these issues and optimize recruitment practices to achieve maximum work effectiveness.  

Keywords: Role of Regional Personnel Agency, Structural Recruitment

This thesis seeks to assess the contribution of local tax revenues to the Regional Original Revenue (PAD) as managed by the Department of Finance and Asset Management of South Halmahera District over the fiscal years 2010 to 2012. Additionally, it examines the factors that facilitate and hinder the enhancement of tax revenues within the South Halmahera region. Findings indicate that local taxes represent a significant portion of the district’s overall revenue, with their contributions demonstrating a consistent upward trend annually. Specifically, local tax revenues amounted to IDR 1,223,577,233.00 or 10.51% of the total revenue of IDR 11,735,130,069.82 in 2010. This share increased to IDR 2,333,993,323.00 or 29.93% of IDR 32,296,618,479.35 in 2011, and further to IDR 3,368,905,822.00 or 40.59% of IDR 43,965,874,804.28 in 2012. The factors influencing the growth of PAD from local taxes include both enabling and inhibiting elements. Enabling factors comprise organizational structure and management, availability of facilities and infrastructure, as well as intensification and extension efforts implemented by the South Halmahera Finance and Asset Management Department (DPKAD). Conversely, inhibiting factors involve limited community participation in tax payment, challenges in data collection or verification, and deficiencies in personnel quality, particularly in relation to educational background and capacity to manage local tax administration effectively.

Keywords: Local Taxes, Local Revenue

This research seeks to examine the impact of brand image and identify which variables exert the most significant influence on the purchasing decisions of Daihatsu Sigra vehicles at PT. Astra International Daihatsu Tbk. Malalayang. The study focuses on three specific variables: corporate image, user image, and product image. Conducted at PT. Astra International Daihatsu Tbk. Malalayang, the investigation employed a research model comprising observation, interviews, questionnaires, and literature review, systematically implemented to align with the research objectives. Data analysis was performed using multiple regression techniques. Subsequently, the F-test was applied to evaluate the collective influence of the brand image variables (corporate image, user image, and product image) on the decision to purchase the Daihatsu Sigra, while the T-test was utilized to identify which individual brand image variable holds the greatest impact on the purchasing decision. The findings indicate that the brand image variables, taken together, significantly affect the purchase decision for Daihatsu Sigra vehicles. Among these variables, product image was found to be the most dominant factor influencing the consumers' decision to buy the vehicle. Consequently, the proposed hypothesis is supported by the results.

The Secretariat of the Regional People's Legislative Assembly is responsible for organizing secretarial administration, managing financial administration, supporting the execution of the duties and functions of the Regional People's Legislative Assembly, as well as providing and coordinating the essential expertise required for the effective operation of the Regional House of Representatives. The effectiveness of this Secretariat as a public organization is largely contingent upon the capabilities and performance of its personnel. In practice, employee performance is influenced by a range of factors originating both internally within the employees and externally from the organizational environment in which it operates. This study aims to examine the performance of the staff within the Secretariat of the Regional House of Representatives in Yahukimo District, Papua Province. Employing a qualitative research approach with descriptive analysis, the study gathers data from informants who are knowledgeable about the contextual background and circumstances of the research setting. The investigation centers on performance indicators as articulated by Dessler, namely work quality, work quantity, supervision requirements, attendance, and communication. Data collection involved interviews, direct observations at the research site, and an extensive literature review. The findings reveal that leadership, discipline, and resource availability constitute significant factors impacting the performance of the Secretariat staff. Additionally, challenges related to inadequate archival management and fluctuations in employee workload have arisen due to changes in the working agendas of members of the Regional People's Legislative Assembly. 

Keywords: Performance, Secretariat, Regional People's Representative Assembly (DPRD)

Background: The Healthy Indonesia Program with a Family Approach (PIS-PK) is one of the Puskesmas' efforts to increase target coverage and increase community access. PIS-PK is implemented based on 12 existing indicators. However, the implementation of PIS-PK has not been maximized and various problems are still found, including in the Tabrauw Regency, West Papua. The purpose of this study is to evaluate PIS-PK in the working area of the Kwoor Health Center, Tambrauw Regency, West Papua in 2020. Methode: The method used in this research is the mixed method. The research was carried out in the working area of the Kwoor Health Center, Tambrauw Regency, West Papua in 2020. The focus of this research is on policy factors, human resources and funds, infrastructure, the process of recording and data collection and the implementation of PIS-PK. This study involved 3 informants and 30 respondents. Informants obtained data based on interview guidelines through in-depth interviews. Respondent data obtained through questionnaires. Data analysis using content analysis method (qualitative) and univariate analysis (quantitative). Result: The results of this study indicate that the policy in implementing PIS-PK at the Kwoor Health Center has been implemented but still has shortcomings in determining the implementing team at the puskesmas level and there is no PIS-PK roadmap in Tambrauw Regency. Human resources and funds in the implementation of PIS-PK at the Kwoor Health Center are available but are still inadequate. The infrastructure facilities in the implementation of PIS-PK at the Kwoor Health Center are still not optimal because they are constrained by the RKA and ASPAK filling. The process of recording and collecting family health data in the implementation of PIS-PK at the Kwoor Health Center has not been carried out properly due to lack of manpower, funds, and unstable network constraints. Most of the 12 PIS-PK indicators have been implemented, but special attention needs to be paid to the indicators that no family has access to clean water facilities, families who are members of JK, family members who do not smoke, families who take family planning, and give birth in health facilities whose implementation still low. Conclusion: The conclusion of this study is that the implementation of PIS-PK in the working area of the Kwoor Health Center, Tambrauw Regency, West Papua in 2020 has not gone well so that efforts are needed to improve the implementation of PIS-PK.

The present study aims to determine the cost, revenue, and profit associated with the UD Murni candied nutmeg agro-industry, as well as to identify its development strategies. The research was conducted between May and September 2013. Primary data were collected through direct observations and interviews with the business owner and the head of the Department of Industry and Trade of North Minahasa Regency. Data analysis employed a descriptive approach combined with SWOT analysis.

The findings revealed that UD Murni’s fixed costs amounted to Rp. 26,043, while variable costs were Rp. 2,317,650. The total revenue generated by UD Murni was Rp. 11,975,000, resulting in a profit of Rp. 9,631,307 per production cycle or per week. The development strategies for the candied nutmeg business, derived from the SWOT matrix, included sustaining and expanding marketing efforts through technological advancements, establishing partnerships with business collaborators, enhancing product quality to align with consumer preferences, utilizing technology for promotion and information acquisition, and designing packaging that is more appealing than competing products.

To further advance the business, improvements in both product quality and service are necessary to increase consumer satisfaction. Additionally, fostering cooperative partnerships with nutmeg suppliers and securing financial support from government sources are essential to provide entrepreneurs with additional capital required for business expansion.

ANALYSIS OF SOCIO-ECONOMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF EDUCATOR WITH EXTENSION IN THE DISTRICT MINAHASA. Extension workers has a strategic role in improving the welfare of farmers / ranchers. One of the factors that influence the success of the extension duties is the state socio-economic background or socio-economic characteristics of each extension. However, the extent of the relationship between socioeconomic characteristics with the implementation of the extension in Minahasa unknown. Based on these problems, the purpose of this study was to determine the relationship of these characteristics with the execution of tasks with good extension. This study uses survey data collection on respondents extension and analyzed descriptively. The collected data are presented in tables cross between variables (education and experience) were observed and analyzed by looking at the distribution Trends. The results showed that the factor of higher education Bachelor (S1) tend to be better than not on the Bachelor in execution of duty. On the other hand experience of long-serving and who have served a long time showed relatively recent trend duty (< 20 years) is better than the longtime (> 20 years). As a conclusion that the social and economic characteristics based on the educational background related to the implementation of the tasks. The higher the education the better performance of its duties educator. Keywords: Characteristics , Social Economy, Duties , Extension

ABSTRACT This study is entitled "The Use of Apposition in The Book of Isaiah (A Syntactic Analysis)". The aims of this study is an attempt to identify, classify and analyze the function of apposition found in the book of Isaiah. The data were taken from the book of Isaiah based on the Holy Bible New International Version. The method used in this study is descriptive method. There are three steps to finish this study, those are preparation, the writer reads some concepts related to the title about apposition and also browse resources from internet to find journal and skripsi. The second step is data collection. In collecting the data the writer read the book of Isaiah in order to identify and underline the use of apposition. After identifying the writer classifies the apposition based on the concept of Quirk et al. The third step is data analysis. The data were analyzed in term of the function using Aarts and Aarts theory. The results of this study shows that there are fifty four appositions found in the book of Isaiah. Concerning types of apposition, they are : 1)Full, Strict and Non-restrictive Apposition; 2)Full, Strict and Restrictive Apposition; 3)Full, Weak and Restrictive Apposition; 4)Partial, Strict and Non-restrictive Appostion; 5)Partial, Weak and Non-restrictive apposition; 6)Partial, Strict and Restrictive Apposition; 7)Partial, Weak and Restrictive Apposition. Regarding the function of apposition found in the book of Isaiah, they are: 1)Subject; 2)Direct Object; 3)Subject Attribute; 4)Object Attribute and 5)Adverbial. Key Words: Syntax, Apposition. The Book of Isaiah.

Therefore, realizing a good performance of government organizations requires serious efforts from stakeholders. This study aims to analyze the performance of the Investment Service and One Stop Integrated Services of Bitung City as an organization as a whole. This research method uses descriptive qualitative research methods. Primary data obtained from interviews, observation and documentation. The number of informants was taken as many as 10 informants consisting of 4 Heads of Section, 4 general functional (staff) of the Office of Investment and One Stop Services of Bitung City and 2 people who use the services of the Investment Service and One Stop Integrated Service of Bitung City. person. The results of research on the career development of civil servants in the Bitung City Government show that: 1) there has been a decrease in the quantity or number of services from 2017 and 2018. 2) Service quality has experienced several problems such as there are still complaints from people who still do not know about SOPs. 3) The form of accountability is divided into 2 parts, namely internally to superiors and to agencies. 4) The aspect of responsiveness is in the form of carrying out the vision and mission of the institution in accordance with the vision and mission of the mayor of Bitung. Apart from that, the responsiveness of the office is to capture the aspirations of the community through both direct and online complaint media. 5) The form of institutional responsibility is the accountability for performance by individual employees both to superiors and to fellow employees.Keywords: Performance, Organizational Performanc

Indonesia is characterized by its multicultural population, comprising diverse cultures and ethnic groups, which renders human behavior a significant factor within social dynamics. Such behavior functions as social capital, facilitating interpersonal interactions within communities. An individual’s ability to engage effectively with others is influenced by their social existence. Proficient interaction skills enhance the capacity for swift adaptation to new environments. Students originating from Tidore who pursue their studies in Manado have resided there for an extended period and continue to demonstrate ease of adaptation. This adaptability is attributed to their rapid adjustment capabilities, supported by environmental, historical, and linguistic factors. A significant number of Tidore students in Manado reside in Titiwungen Selatan, selecting this location due to its central position within the city, which provides convenient access to various universities. Furthermore, the area is characterized by a peaceful and comfortable environment, coupled with friendly and sociable residents, thereby facilitating the students' interaction and adjustment. Engagement in various social activities, including community service and religious events, further enables Tidore students to integrate with the Manadonese population. This integration process is fundamentally rooted in positive behavioral traits and adaptive competencies, culminating in effective social adaptation. 

Keywords: adaptation, interaction, students

Mostly sell daily needs like foodstuffs such as fish, fruit, vegetables, eggs, meat, cloth, clothing, electronic goods, services and others. Additionally, there is also selling pastries and other items. This research is conducted in Pasar Beriman Tomohon. The objectives of this research are to analyze the influence of price, product attributes, origin of product, and philosophy to customer loyalty, partially and simultaneously. This research is the causal type of research where it investigates the influence of price, product attributes, origin of product, and philosophy to customer loyalty. Using a multiple regression model to answer the research problem. The population in this study is a customer of Pasar Beriman Tomohon whereas sample taken by each respondents 100 respondents. The hypothesis testing, this research conduct a conclusion of there is a significant influence of price, product attributes, origin of product, and philosophy to customer loyalty partially and simultaneously.This study reveals that price,product attributes, origin of product; local producthas a strong influence to the customer in order to select, buy and to be a loyal customer at Pasar Beriman Tomohon, they prefer to purchase local products, their perception that local products is better than other products, and become the reason for customer always shop at Pasar Beriman Tomohon. ABSTRACT Nowadays, online shops are becoming the most popular shopping style. In contrast with walk-in stores, online shops enthusiasts can shops throughout different cities and countries. With cheaper prices than walk-in stores, the online shop reach, the top of the world trade in a short time. Many buyers do not look at the price of the products but the shipping fees make them cancel to order. The reason is if the product is cheap then the shipping fee makes it expensive. Customers only buy once or twice then stop buying because the shipping fee makes them uncomfortable to buy from the online shop. The specific objective of this research is to examine the significant difference in customer retention between online shops with shipping fee and online shops without shipping fee. Theories supporting this research such as consumer motivation in shopping, customer retention, and shipping fee. The population of this research is shopper either shopping in-physical store or shopping in online store with sample as many as 100 respondents and sampling design is convenience sampling. Result and conclusion is there is a significant difference in customer retention between online shop without shipping fee and online shop with shipping fee. Keywords: customer retention, shipping fee

This study aims to assess the financial performance of Manado City Government using Financial Ratio Analysis of Regional Budget for Fiscal Year 2011-2015. Type of research is the descriptif qualitative with case study approach. The processed data is the Budget Realization Report of Manado City Government for Fiscal Year 2011-2015 were obtained from the internet publication on the official website of Financial Management Board and Regional Property of Manado City. The analysis used to analyze the Regional Financial Performance is Financial Ratio Analysis by calculate the Ratio of Independence, Degree of Fiscal Decentralization, Ratio of Effectiveness, Ratio of Efficiency and Ratio of Expenditure Congruence. While the analysis used to analyze the Ability of Regional Finance is to calculate the Share and Growth, Map of Regional Finance Capability and Financial Capability Index. Based on the calculation and analysis of the Regional Financial Performance can be concluded that the pattern of the region's autonomy level relationships in Manado City is instructive criteria. Degree of Fiscal Decentralization is still lacking, but the Ratio of Effectiveness is very effective and the Ratio of Efficiency is also very efficient. Ratio of Expenditure Congruence shows the balance between expenditures are not balanced. Based on the calculation and analysis of the Regional Financial Capability can be concluded, that the condition of financial ability of Manado City is still not ideal. Share and Growth calculation results, the position of Manado City is in quadrant II and Financial Capability Index of Manado City is high. Keywords: Financial Ratio Analysis of Regional Budget, Financial Performance of Local Government.

Soybean (Glycine max (L.)) serves as a vital source of vegetable protein, valued for its nutritional properties, safety for consumption, and economical advantage compared to animal-based protein sources. Sieving refers to the process of separating solid particles of varying sizes within a mixture by employing a sieve. This method is commonly utilized for cleaning purposes, particularly for removing impurities differing in size from the raw material. The present study aims to design and conduct technical evaluations of a sieve-type cleaning apparatus integrated with the MPT001 soybean threshing machine. Research activities were carried out in a home workshop setting and involved the fabrication of the sifting device, conducting sieving experiments, and analyzing the resulting data. The development and testing of the sieve-type cleaning equipment were intended to assist farmers by expediting the soybean threshing process. Field tests, performed on soybeans still on the stalk, included three repetitions and yielded the following results: an average cleaning efficiency of 0.41%, an average cleaning capacity of 33.19 kg per hour, an average threshing yield of 1.7 kg per trial, and an average waste or foreign material of 5.86 kg. Implementation of this device is expected to streamline the processing chain and reduce overall processing time.  
Keywords: equipment design, vibrating sieve system, technical performance evaluation

This study aims to delineate the profile of the grits pearls business. Primary data were collected through direct interviews with business owners, utilizing structured questionnaires. The data analysis employed in this research is primarily descriptive, with collected information systematically presented in tabular form. Analytical methods included cost analysis, revenue calculation, profit determination, and break-even point assessment.

Findings reveal that the business generated a monthly profit of Rp. 2,097,043. The break-even point analysis indicated that producing 376 grits pearls per glass, over five production cycles, marks the threshold at which the business covers its costs. The entrepreneurs’ strategic foresight in identifying market opportunities and selecting optimal business locations has contributed to the venture’s promising outlook and its potential for enhancing household income.

The study concludes that the grits pearls enterprise operates at a household scale and currently lacks formal bookkeeping practices. Furthermore, business owners also serve as laborers within the operation. Consequently, it is recommended that owners implement systematic bookkeeping and consider expanding the workforce to support business growth. The calculated R/C ratio of 1.2 suggests the enterprise is financially viable and suitable for development. Moreover, this business possesses an aesthetic dimension, as its objectives extend beyond profit generation to include consumer service.

Rice cultivation in Indonesia frequently experiences yield reductions and even crop failure (puso) due to pest infestations. This phenomenon is largely attributable to Indonesia’s climate, which is highly conducive to the proliferation of pest populations, compounded by farmers’ continuous rice cultivation practices without crop rotation. Such agricultural practices provide an uninterrupted and consistent host environment for rice pests. Furthermore, the surge in pest populations is exacerbated by the decline of natural pest enemies, a consequence of the inappropriate and excessive application of chemical pesticides. Poigar District, located within Bolaang Mongondow Regency, represents a critical rice-producing area in North Sulawesi Province and plays a significant role in regional food security through its production of superior rice varieties. In response, this community service program (PKM) aims to motivate and guide farmers in the adoption of the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana as a biological control agent against the Leptocorisa acuta pest. The PKM activities were conducted in Wineru Village, Poigar Sub-district, Bolaang Mongondow Regency, with the objective of disseminating scientific knowledge and technology on the utilization of Beauveria bassiana for the management of Leptocorisa acuta in rice cultivation within Bolaang Mongondow Regency.
