The accounting treatment for biological assets in Indonesia does not have mutual standards so, many agribusiness companies reported their biological assets just like the standards that used to report the non-biological assets. Characteristics of different biological assets can cause mistakes in recording if we use the same standards with non-biological assets. This study aimed to comparing the accounting treatment made by the company between two types of assets that owned by the company. The result of this research found that accounting treatment between the two types of asset does not have significant differences. The differences in the accounting treatment of these assets only in the measurement of assets and discontinuation. Companies measure the value of both types of assets in accordance with the acquisition price. But the company did not recognize the depreciation of their biological assets. At the time of biological assets termination, the company immediately reclassified the biological assets to the inventories that available to sale, while for non-biological assets, there are two types of termination that is for resale and stored as damaged goods. Considering to the characteristics of the biological assets, company should establish fair value in the measurement of biological assets. Keywords: Biological Assets, fixed assets.

Abstract:  
Pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata) is a creeping plant belonging to the Cucurbitaceae family, characterized by its orange flesh which indicates a high carotenoid content. Mung beans (Vigna radiata), members of the Fabaceae family, are notable for their elevated protein and mineral levels. Snack bars are composite food products typically consisting of diverse ingredients such as cereals, fruits, and nuts, which are bound together using flour. These bars are commonly consumed by individuals managing diabetes and obesity. This study aimed to optimize the nutritional value of snack bars formulated from pumpkin flour and mung bean flour, while assessing various physicochemical properties. The experimental design employed was a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with four treatment groups, each repeated thrice. The formulations varied in the proportion of pumpkin and mung bean flours as follows: A (80% pumpkin flour, 20% mung bean flour), B (60% pumpkin flour, 40% mung bean flour), C (40% pumpkin flour, 60% mung bean flour), and D (20% pumpkin flour, 80% mung bean flour). Findings revealed that the formulation consisting of 20% pumpkin flour and 80% mung bean flour exhibited superior nutritional attributes, including protein content of 8.36%, carbohydrates at 37.21%, fat at 7.10%, ash content of 1.45%, and moisture level of 49.38%. Organoleptic evaluation yielded neutral scores for color (3.88), aroma (4.36), texture (4.32), and flavor (4.08).  
Keywords: Pumpkin Flour, Green Bean Flour, Snack Bar

Schools bear a significant responsibility in delivering quality services to their surrounding communities. Their primary function within society is to educate citizens, thereby fostering communal intelligence through both formal and non-formal educational mechanisms. It is imperative that schools effectively fulfill this role to ensure community members experience satisfaction with the services provided. However, concerns have been raised regarding suboptimal service quality within schools, evidenced by insufficiently effective student instruction and instances of inadequate professionalism among teachers in community engagement. Furthermore, the performance of teaching staff has not consistently met expectations in facilitating student learning.

This study aims to examine the quality of service in the Elementary School (Sekolah Dasar/Inpres) 6/75 Madidir, located in Bitung City. Employing a qualitative research design, data were analyzed utilizing the Miles and Huberman qualitative analysis framework. The findings indicate that the overall service quality at Inpres 6/75 Madidir Elementary School can be classified as good. Both teachers and administrative staff performed their duties competently, resulting in satisfactory experiences for their clientele, namely students and their parents. The personnel adhered to established regulations while delivering services, demonstrating courteous and friendly conduct. Such adherence facilitated the timely completion of tasks and contributed positively to stakeholder satisfaction.

Keywords: Service Quality, Elementary School

Human resources play a crucial role within organizations, as all matters pertaining to human resources significantly impact the development and enhancement of employee job performance. Enhancing employee performance is an essential objective for any organization or company, although achieving this improvement in practice is often challenging. This study aims to examine the influence of work culture, work environment, and job satisfaction on the job performance of organic employees at the Kantor Sinode GMIH in Tobelo. The research employed path analysis as the methodological approach. The findings reveal that work culture (X1) and work environment (X2) jointly exert a significant effect on employee performance within the Kantor Sinode GMIH in Tobelo, as indicated by an F-value of 17.981 with a significance level of 0.000 for Substructure 1. Further analysis of Substructure 2 demonstrates that work culture (X1), work environment (X2), and job satisfaction (Y1) collectively have a significant impact on the work performance of organic employees at the Sinode Office of GMIH, with an F-value of 36.508 and a significance level of 0.000. Individually, work culture (X1) shows a significant positive effect on employee performance, with a coefficient of 0.273 and a significance value of 0.008, while job satisfaction (Y1) also significantly influences employee performance, with a coefficient of 0.571 and a significance value of 0.000.  

Keywords: work culture, work environment, job satisfaction, employee performance.

Employee satisfaction has become a fundamental priority for contemporary organizations and companies. Employees are often regarded as the core of any organization. Prior to focusing on external customers, organizations must give due attention to their internal environment by evaluating their overall performance. The performance of an organization or company is largely contingent upon the performance of its employees, which in turn is influenced by the leadership provided by organizational leaders. This study focuses on the Service Office of State Property and Auction (Kantor Pelayanan Kekayaan Negara dan Lelang, KPKNL) in Manado, where a significant number of leaders originate from outside the local area. The introduction of new leaders brings different leadership styles, which can impact employee performance. Employees may exhibit various reactions when encountering unfamiliar leadership behaviors and approaches, subsequently affecting their work outcomes. This research emphasizes the role of ethical leadership in shaping employee performance and investigates whether leaders who consistently engage in ethical exchanges influence employee productivity. A sample of 30 employees was selected for this study, and multiple regression analysis was employed to examine the data. The findings indicate that ethical leadership is a crucial factor in enhancing or sustaining employee performance.  

Keywords: ethical leadership, employee performance, organizational behavior.

This study seeks to elucidate the role of the Regional Development Planning Agency (Bappeda) in the regional development planning process within East Halmahera. Employing qualitative research methodology alongside qualitative data analysis techniques, the study utilized multiple data collection methods, namely: (1) interviews, (2) document analysis, and (3) direct observation. The data analysis process comprised three sequential stages: (1) data editing, (2) data reduction, and (3) data interpretation. Findings from the research indicate that: (1) the Regional Development Planning Agency of East Halmahera plays a pivotal role in integrating all available resources to formulate effective local development plans; (2) although Bappeda undertakes its functions within the planning process, it encounters several challenges stemming from both internal and external factors. Internally, limitations include insufficient human resource capacity, inadequate facilities and infrastructure, and suboptimal coordination. Externally, obstacles comprise unpreparedness of planning data by other officials, lack of emphasis on certain officials in the planning process, delays in implementation activities relative to the fiscal calendar—partly due to geographic difficulties hindering access—and limited stakeholder participation in the planning process.  
 
Keywords: Role, Bappeda, regional development planning process

The ability of an organization to anticipate emergent changes is essential for achieving its objectives without encountering disruptions or obstacles. A critical factor within this dynamic is job satisfaction, as it significantly enhances employee morale. Consequently, the relationship between employees and the organization can be characterized as reciprocal. This study focuses on PT BPR Prisma Dana Manado, where Robbins (2001) defines job satisfaction as an individual's overall attitude toward their work, encompassing a broad and multifaceted aggregation of distinct job elements. Furthermore, Mathis and Jackson, as cited by Sadeli and Prawira (2001), conceptualize employee performance as essentially what employees do or fail to do in their roles.

Employing a quantitative methodology, this research was conducted over approximately one month at PT BPR Prisma Dana Manado. The sample comprised the entire population of interest, totaling approximately 30 individuals. The findings indicate that job satisfaction exerts a significant positive influence on employee performance at PT BPR Prisma Dana Manado. The correlation coefficient (R) obtained reflects a strong association between the two variables, suggesting that variations in job satisfaction substantially affect employee performance.

Based on these results, the study recommends that PT BPR Prisma Dana Manado should continue to uphold and enhance the dimensions of job satisfaction currently in place, alongside consistently monitoring employee performance to sustain and improve its effectiveness.

Keywords: Job Satisfaction, Employee Performance

This study seeks to assess the quality of the Government Internal Supervisory Apparatus (APIP) in Southeast Minahasa Regency. A prevalent issue identified in this research concerns the audits, wherein certain irregularities remain undetected by APIP as the internal auditor but are subsequently uncovered by the external auditor, namely the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK). Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, this investigation utilizes in-depth interviews and Focus Group Discussions with informants possessing relevant expertise in the subject matter. The findings highlight several critical factors influencing the quality of APIP in Southeast Minahasa Regency. Firstly, there is a necessity for APIP personnel to possess adequate competence by receiving continuous technical guidance, education, and training to enhance performance quality. Secondly, frequent personnel rotations should be avoided, and any reassignment must align with individual competencies. Furthermore, the study underscores that a strong commitment from the Regional Head towards establishing good and clean governance, alongside allocating a budget for APIP equivalent to 1% in accordance with applicable regulations, is vital. Additional recommendations include the provision of adequate facilities such as operational vehicles and other supporting infrastructure, as well as sustained technical guidance and training to foster improvements in APIP quality.

EFFECT OF UTILIZATION OF VIRGIN COCONUT OIL (VCO) IN THE DIET ON ENERGY AND PROTEIN DIGESTIBILITY OF GROWING PIGS. Utilization of virgin coconut oil (VCO) as a source of energy, not only increase the enegy in the diet, but also increase energy utilization efficiency. The increase of energy utilization efficiency depends on fat digestibility. The present study was designed to elaborate the effect of utilization of VCO in the diets on energy and protein digestibility of growing pigs. The experiment was conducted using 20 castrated male pigs aged 6-7 weeks weighing 32.5-41.5kg. The data were analyzed according to the linear model procedure for ANOVA appropriate for Randomized Block Design with 5 treatments and 4 replications. Treatments were formulated as follow: R0 = 100% control diet + VCO; R1 = 99.5% control diet + 0.5% VCO; R2 = 99% control diet + 1.0% VCO; R3 = 98.5% control diet + 1.5% VCO; and R4 = 98% control diet + 2.0% VCO. Parameters measured were: energy and protein digestibility. The result showed that the utilization ov VCO up to 4% in the diets, had no effect (P> 0. 05) on energy and protein digestibility. It can be concluded that the addition of VCO up to 2.0% in the diets has no significant influence on energy and protein digestibility of growing pigs. Keyword : Virgin coconut oil (VCO), Energy and Protein Digestibility, Growing Pigs.

The development of an online shop or online store through internet media is well known in Indonesia, and even well known by the general public, including the people of Manado. The many conveniences in shopping and the various types of products and services offered have made Manado people make online shops as an alternative shopping. This has made many Online Shop sellers offer their products in various ways to attract consumers to buy, they take advantage of the current pandemic where many people choose to shop from home.Many people in the city of Manado prefer online shops as an alternative to shopping rather than shopping at stores, malls, or other shopping places. Apart from being due to covid-19, there are several other reasons such as being practical and not complicated, no need to dress up, no need to leave the house, and no need to face heat and traffic jams.The purpose of this research is to find out how online shop as an alternative shopping for the people of Manado City. This study took data and an explanation of the Online Shop as an alternative to shopping for the people of Manado city in general. Informants were taken from various groups. The information that has been collected shows that many people in the city of Manado choose online shops as an alternative to shoppingKeywords: Online Shop, Online Shopping, Utilization of social media

Soy milk is a product processed soybean extract that resembles cow's milk. High protein content makes soy milk as highly nutritious vegetable milk. But the beany flavor of the resulting lead soy milk consumption levels are relatively low. One way of improving the quality of soy milk with a probiotic drink that process into soy milk kefir. The purpose of this study to determine the effect of the concentration of skim milk to soy milk kefir quality, namely in terms of the physical and chemical properties, microbiological and organoleptic. The study was conducted in two stages: determining the length of fermentation and then proceed with the manufacture of soy milk with the addition of different concentrations of skim milk of four treatments that control, the addition of skim milk concentration 0%, 4% and 8%. This research using completely randomized design (CRD). The result showed the addition of skim milk concentration effect on total of bacteria acid lactic (BAL), total yeast, colour, and flavor of soy milk kefir. The addition of skim milk concentration causes an increase in total BAL, total yeast and pH. For organoleptic show that the colour and flavor of soy milk kefir with a concentration of 8% skim milk is preferred compared with the three other treatments. Keywords: soy milk, kefir, skim milk, organoleptic

Abstract: Leadership is the one of the important things in organization. It will work by cooperating leader and staff to reach many goals planned. Facts show that existency of the staff is less concerned. They are just as the tools of organization. This research using correlation method. Data is collected by using quetionaires and interviews. Respondent are 50 employees worked at the Secretary Office of Tomohon City. The conclusions are: (1) Staff empowerment correlates significantly with the organization productivity at 0,4761. (2) Decision making process correlates significantly with the organization productivity at 0,2704. (3) Staff empowerment correlates significantly with the decision making process ar 0,49. (4) Staf empowerment and decision making process simultancy correlates with the organization productivity at 0,4790. It means organization productivity improvement is influenced by the staff empowerment and decision making process. Based on these results, it is suggested that the government of Tomohon City for effective empowerment of staff in the decision making process needs to be applied with the best principles of complete staff work (completed staff work). Because with this method is the responsibility of staff to help make things easier for the leadership decision will be greater. Keywords : staff empowerment, decision making and organization productivity

The manager holds a crucial position in the attainment of organizational objectives. The accomplishment of these goals is intrinsically linked to the active involvement of leadership in enhancing the performance of human resources. Consequently, one effective approach to fostering greater professionalism and optimizing employee job performance is through the provision of role models, coupled with comprehensive education and training. Furthermore, the proactive engagement of a leader is essential for offering guidance, setting directions, and supervising employee activities to ensure the efficient realization of organizational aims. This study aims to examine the extent to which managerial roles contribute to the improvement of employee performance in achieving organizational goals and to assess employee performance within the "Serbu" Retail Shop in Tomohon, employing Mintzberg’s framework of managerial roles. The study population consists of the manager and eleven employees who have collaborated with the manager over a specific period. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and subsequently analyzed. According to Mintzberg, three primary roles characterize managerial functions: (1) Interpersonal Role, (2) Informational Role, and (3) Decisional Role.  
  
Keywords: management, manager, managerial roles

This study, conducted by Seplianto Maarende as chairman, with Celsius Talumingan and Juliana Mandei as members, aims to assess the income and expenses associated with pineapple farming in Lobong Pakasi. The primary objective is to quantify the financial viability of pineapple cultivation, providing valuable insights to farmers for enhancing their income and improving farm management practices. Additionally, the research offers pertinent information for stakeholders interested in pineapple agriculture.

Data collection was performed directly from farmers in the pineapple-producing village of Lobong, located in Bolaang Mongondow. The analysis employed revenue assessment and the calculation of the Return Cost Ratio (R/C ratio), which compares total production costs against total revenue generated. Income estimations were based on five consecutive harvest cycles.

The findings reveal that the total production cost amounts to Rp 18,922,000, while total revenue reaches Rp 30,387,000. Consequently, pineapple farmers earn an average income of Rp 11,465,500 per hectare per harvest cycle. The calculated R/C ratio of 1.60 indicates that for every rupiah spent, farmers generate Rp 1.60 in income, demonstrating the economic feasibility of pineapple farming in Lobong village. These results confirm that pineapple cultivation in Bolaang Mongondow Regency offers substantial economic benefits under the supervision of Caroline B.D.

The rapid advancement of information technology and communication has profoundly permeated various facets of human life. This widespread adoption of digital technologies facilitates daily activities through the utilization of digital devices, applications, the internet, and numerous other innovations, as exemplified by the emergence of online food delivery services. This study aims to examine the impact of consumer behavior—encompassing cultural, social, personal, and psychological factors—and digital marketing strategies, including social media marketing, email marketing, and search engine marketing, on consumer purchase decisions regarding GrabFood in Manado. The research employs a sample of 100 consumers, utilizing multiple linear regression analysis alongside hypothesis testing through F-tests and T-tests. Findings indicate that, collectively, consumer behavior and digital marketing significantly influence consumer purchase decisions. However, when assessed separately, only consumer behavior exerts a significant effect, whereas digital marketing alone does not demonstrate a significant impact. Based on these results, it is recommended that GrabFood management facilitates consultation programs targeting MSME actors to engage in business incubation initiatives. Such programs, involving coaching for local enterprises, aim to enhance business development in the digital era and subsequently boost sales in Manado. 

Keywords: consumer behavior, digital marketing, purchase decision, COVID-19 pandemic.

This study seeks to identify and analyze the marketing channels of copra agricultural products from producers to consumers, serving as a basis for determining the marketing margin associated with each intermediary agency in the copra distribution process in Pinilih Village, Dimembe District, North Minahasa Regency. Additionally, it aims to ascertain the proportion of prices received by farmers, known as the Farmer's Share. The research employs a descriptive quantitative approach, specifically a survey method, which emphasizes capturing an accurate and factual depiction of the issue, followed by systematic data collection, organization, and analysis. The sample comprised 79 craftsmen as respondents, alongside four collectors. The findings indicate the existence of two copra marketing channels from Pinilih Village to the final consumer, the oil factory: Marketing Channel I involves direct sales from farmers to consumers, while Marketing Channel II includes farmers, collectors, and consumers. Among these, Marketing Channel II is predominantly utilized by copra farmers in the study area. In this channel, intermediary traders—collectors—purchase copra directly from farmers’ residences and subsequently sell it to the final consumers (oil mills). The marketing margin for Marketing Channel I was calculated at Rp. 3,000 per kilogram, which exceeds the margin of Rp. 2,500 per kilogram observed in Marketing Channel II. Furthermore, the Farmer’s Share was found to be 100% in Marketing Channel I, indicating that farmers receive the full price paid by consumers; in contrast, the Farmer’s Share in Marketing Channel II is 66.67%, signifying that farmers obtain approximately two-thirds of the consumer price. Based on these observations, it is recommended that copra farmers in Pinilih Village consider selling their products directly to end consumers (industries) to maximize returns. 

Keywords: Marketing Channels

This research endeavors to examine the implementation processes and challenges associated with the Complete Systematic Land Registration (PTSL) program at the Land Office of North Minahasa Regency. The inquiry was conducted over a two-month period, from April to May 2019, at the aforementioned Land Office. Employing a qualitative methodological framework with a descriptive approach, the study utilized both primary and secondary data sources. Data collection techniques included interviews, observations, and document analysis. Findings indicate that the PTSL implementation at the North Minahasa Regency Land Office was executed effectively. Specifically, in 2017, of the 2,500 targeted land parcels, 2,460 were classified under category K1 (certified), whereas 40 parcels fell under category K3 (unable to be certified). In 2018, with an increased target of 5,500 parcels, 3,642 were realized as K1 category, 224 as K3, and 41 as K4 (already certified). The study identified several constraints faced by the Land Office, including insufficient human resources, inadequate facilities and infrastructure, limited community engagement, and the financial burden of land taxes.

The empowerment of managers constitutes an initiative aimed at enhancing their strength, capabilities, and authority through modalities such as training and education, counseling, socialization, and support, thereby enabling them to effectively manage various types of enterprises under their supervision. Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) represent a governmental program grounded in principles of empowerment and decentralization. This program reflects a governmental commitment to restoring community trust and fostering collaborative efforts toward establishing economically self-reliant village communities. 

This study employs a qualitative research design characterized by descriptive methodology, wherein both primary and secondary data are collected through interviews. These data were subsequently analyzed to derive the study’s findings. The results indicate that the principal challenges impeding the empowerment of BUMDes managers in Batlale Village pertain to the implementation of work programs involving savings and loans, as well as business activities in the marine and plantation sectors. Despite intentions to provide infrastructure and business capital, these initiatives have either stagnated or failed to commence, primarily due to the managers’ limited skills and knowledge, which have hindered program development. 

Government-provided training focused on business management and potential development was initiated only four years prior. In addition, several obstacles have been identified, including insufficient attention, concern, and encouragement from both the community and government in supporting managers to operate and grow business programs. The scarcity of such training efforts suggests that governmental involvement has largely been restricted to outreach activities aimed at improving the performance of BUMDes managers in Batlale Village.

Keywords: Empowerment, Management, Program

This research was a survey using questionnaires. Samples were determind by purposive sampling method involving 30 smallholder of local native chicken. Chi square method was used to analyze the data. The role of extension was meansured by ordinal scale for questions given to breeders and the adoption of innovation was measured by ordinal scale of the level of knowledge, attitudes and skills of native chicken farmers. Knowledge was divided into several categories, namely high, medium and low knowledge, the attitude of the category accepts innovation, it is enough to accept innovation and reject innovation, the skill of the category was skilled, sufficiently skilled and unskilled. ABSTRACTThis research is aimed to study the phenology of angsana trees in the urban areas of Manado city. Sam Ratulangi street is divided into five observing segments with relatively the same number of trees at about 129-131 at each segment giving a total of 651 trees. The phenology observed at each tree including leaf, flower, and fruit phenomenon. The diameter of each tree are measured. Trees were then greuped into five categories:<10, 10-<20, 20-<30, 30-<40 and ≥40 cm. The results shows that angsana trees in Sam Ratulangi street had diameter of about 3.4-50.5 cm.The highest accumulation at trees was at last fourth categories ranging at 132-185 trunks. The phenology of leaves which dominate the entire segments on Sam Ratulangi street are green leaves at 89.9%of the 651 trees.The shoot phenology was performed by 11-20 trees (1.7-3.1%) and the flowering phenomena were found in 17-20 trees (2.6-3.8%). This study aimed to examine the implementation of the smart city program within the Manado City Information and Communication Department. The research employed descriptive qualitative methods. Government initiatives to realize Manado City's smart city objectives have been manifested through several public service programs, including the Smart Command Center (C3), the analysis and map-based portal (PANANDA), the latest online tax service (PONTER), and Manado Alert 112 (MS112). Nonetheless, the execution of these programs has not been fully optimal. Various challenges impede the effective operation of the smart city program, notably the insufficient number of specialized human resources within the Manado city government who possess expertise in information technology and relevant educational backgrounds. This deficiency significantly affects the capacity of personnel to comprehend and implement the programs, rendering the initiatives less effective. Furthermore, limited public awareness of the smart city program adversely influences its overall success. Additionally, the substantial budgetary requirements for information technology infrastructure have constrained the program’s implementation, resulting in only a limited number of agencies being able to participate. 

Keywords: Program Implementation, Smart City

EFFECT OF FEED RESTRICTION AND DIFFERENT CRUDE FIBER SOURCES ON THE BORILER PERFORMANCE. The research aim was to determine the performance of Lohman strain broiler were given by food restriction of 20 percent and 10 percent levels of crude fiber from different fiber sources originated from coffee peel, rice bran and coconut pulp. This research was carried out in a poultry house at the Faculty of Animal Husbandry, UNSRAT Manado, during 6 weeks using 48 unsex Lohman strain broilers at 21 days old. The research method was using a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) based on factorial pattern (2x4). Each treatment combination was repeated 3 times. Factor A was a feed restriction consisting of feed without restriction (A0) and restriction of 20% feed for 8 days (A1). Factor B was a source of fiber consisting of control (B0);coffee peel (B1); rice bran (B2) and coconut pulp (B3). In this study, the were 8 treatment combinations of A0B0, A0B1, A0B2, A0B3, A1B0, A1B1, A1B2 and A1B3. Application of feed restriction and source of fiber were applied during days of 21th to day of 28th. The birds were fed commercial feed until 42 days of age. The variables measured were feed consumption, body weight gain and feed conversion. The results showed that the restriction of feed and different fiber sources had a significant effect (P <0.05) on feed consumption, body weight gain and feed conversion. The results of this study can be concluded that the restriction of feed by 20 percent for 8 days with a source of crude fiber originated from coconut pulp in feed gave the best response compared with crude fiber originated from coffee peel and rice bran on the performance of the Lohman strain of broiler.Keywords: Broiler, feed restriction, crude fiber

CARCASS PERCENTAGE AND ABDOMINAL FAT OF BROILER CHICKEN CONSUMING DIETS PARTLY REPLACED WITH FRESHMULBERRY (Morus alba) LEAVES. An experiment was conducted to elaborate carcass percentage and abdominal fat of broiler chicken consuming diets partly replaced with fresh Mulberry (Morus alba) leaves. The present study was conducted for 3 weeks using 60 day old chicks (DOC) CP 707 broiler chicks. Birds were placed in battery cages and were assigned to each dietary treatment (4 treatments) which was replicated five times in a completely randomized design (CRD) arrangement and data were all submitted to the ANOVA procedure.Treatment diets were formulated as follow: R0 = basal diet + 0% fresh Mulberry leaves; R1 = 98% basal diet + 2.0% fresh Mulberry leaves; R2= 96.0% basal diet + 4.0% fresh Mulberry leaves; and R3 = 94.0% basal diet + 6.0% fresh Mulberry leaves. Variables measured were carcass percentage and abdominal fat. Research results showed that treatments gave a non-significant different (P>0.05) on carcass percentage; where as treatments significantly (P<0,05) affected abdominal fat. R0 (basal diet + 0% fresh Mulberry leaves) gave a significantly (P < 0.05) higher abdominal fat compared with R1, R2, and R3 treatments; while among R1, R2, and R3 treatments gave a non-significant difference on abdominal fat indices. It can be concluded that fresh Mulberry (Morus alba) leaves can be used up to 6.0% as a replacement of basal diet of broiler chicken in this study. Key words: Broiler chicken, Mulberry leaves,carcass percentage, abdominal fat.

This study seeks to evaluate the profitability and feasibility of hydroponic vegetable farming conducted by S2R Farming in Warukapas Village, Tatelu District, North Minahasa Regency. The research was carried out over a two-month period from March to April 2022. Employing quantitative analysis, this investigation focused on calculating farm profits by determining the difference between revenue and production costs within a single 40-day production cycle. Additionally, the study assessed feasibility through the computation of the Revenue-Cost (R/C) ratio and the Break Even Point (BEP) for S2R Farming. Both primary and secondary data were utilized in this research. Primary data were collected via direct interviews and observations using structured questionnaires administered to the business owners at the S2R Farming site. Secondary data were sourced from books, internet resources, theses, journals, and related materials. The findings demonstrated that the profit generated by S2R Farming over one 40-day production cycle amounted to Rp 7,423,427.05, with an R/C ratio of 2.060. Furthermore, the BEP was calculated at Rp 3,388,769.13. To achieve break-even, S2R Farming must produce 247 packs of pakcoy and 223 packs of lettuce. Consequently, hydroponic vegetable farming by S2R Farming in Warukapas Village is both profitable and operationally viable.

All enterprises, whether engaged in the production of goods or the provision of services, seek to maintain a continuous presence in the market to increase market share and generate profit. Analogous to living organisms that experience a life cycle encompassing stages of birth, growth, development, maturity, and eventual decline, products similarly undergo a life cycle. Consequently, it is imperative to devise effective strategies for managing business operations. The objective of this research is to ascertain the market position of Samsung products in Manado City in accordance with the product life cycle model, as well as to evaluate the marketing mix strategies employed for Samsung smartphones in Manado City relative to their product life cycle stage. According to Tjiptono (2015: 435), the product life cycle (PLC) visually represents the sales trajectory of a product or product category from its introduction to the market until its withdrawal. This study adopts a descriptive quantitative research design, utilizing the Polli and Cook method for data analysis, and employs interviews and documentation for data collection. Two independent variables are examined: the sales performance of Samsung products in Manado City between 2013 and 2017, and the corresponding marketing mix strategies implemented. Findings derived from the Polli and Cook calculations reveal a percentage change in sales of 2.11 (X = 2.11), with established growth and decline thresholds of 27.96 and -26.90 respectively. Since the observed sales change percentage falls within these thresholds, it is concluded that Samsung smartphones in Manado City are situated in the maturity stage of the product life cycle. Overall, the marketing mix strategy for Samsung smartphones in Manado aligns with theoretical frameworks associated with the marketing mix at the maturity stage of the product life cycle. It is recommended that the company prioritize customer retention efforts, expand distribution channels to strategically advantageous locations, and reduce less profitable outlets. 

Keywords: marketing mix strategy, product life cycle

The mangrove forest in Sambas Regency is subject to multiple pressures, both from natural factors and anthropogenic activities such as land use conversion into settlements, aquaculture ponds, and other purposes. This study aims to examine the structural characteristics of the mangrove community and the current condition of the mangrove forest in Malek Village, Sambas Regency. The research methodology involved vegetation analysis combined with remote sensing techniques. Carbon stock estimation was performed utilizing established allometric equations. Sentinel-2 MSI imagery served as the remote sensing data source, providing spatial information regarding the area and distribution of mangrove species. The findings revealed that two true mangrove species predominantly occupied the site: Avicennia marina (Importance Value Index [IVI] = 212.80) and Bruguiera gymnorrhiza (IVI = 187.20). The total mangrove area was determined to be 368.41 hectares, categorized into dense stands (63.25%), medium density (27.55%), and sparse coverage (9.19%). The above-ground carbon stock of mangrove vegetation was estimated to range between 23.09 ± 2.30 and 49.23 ± 2.59 Mg C ha⁻¹. Overall, the mangrove forest in Malek Village demonstrates considerable potential, as evidenced by its substantial density, extensive area, notable tree thickness, minimal degradation, and significant stored carbon stocks.

The successful execution of construction projects is typically evaluated by the precision with which cost, time, and quality objectives are met. Effective risk management necessitates a comprehensive approach beginning with risk identification, followed by thorough analysis and control measures, thereby minimizing the likelihood and impact of potential risks. Modifications arising during the project implementation phase can influence project performance metrics, including cost, quality, time, and scope, potentially introducing risk. Notably, risks may be categorized based on the owner’s tolerance: some may be acceptable, possibly resulting in additional costs or delays, while others—termed non-excusable scope changes—are wholly borne by the contractor.

This study aims to identify the non-excusable change factors that pose the most significant risks during the implementation phase of private building development projects in Manado. It further seeks to assess the impact of such factors on project performance and to develop a risk model incorporating mitigation strategies. The research employs a mixed-methods approach, beginning with quantitative data collection analyzed via SPSS, followed by qualitative data collection through surveys and questionnaires, also analyzed using SPSS. Subsequently, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is utilized to ascertain the risk levels associated with identified factors.

The findings reveal the predominant non-excusable risks in private building projects in Manado as follows: (1) reliance on local labor, (2) owner-initiated changes to work designs, (3) frequent modifications requested by the owner, (4) compressed execution timelines, and (5) diminished worker morale and motivation. These factors significantly affect project performance across cost, time, and quality dimensions. The study establishes correlations indicating that these risks influence changes in both schedule and budget performance.

To mitigate the most critical risks, particularly those related to the extensive use of local labor, the study recommends several strategies. These include recruiting experienced local workers, providing orientation and training prior to task commencement to enhance performance and quality, implementing incentive schemes for compliant workers, drafting robust contracts, conducting periodic work evaluations, and employing competent project management personnel. Additionally, risk transfer mechanisms may be considered to further address potential adverse effects.

Keywords: risk model, non-excusable risk, private project performance

This study aims to determine: (1) the population density of the walang sangit pest across various rice varieties in Tolotoyon Village, Bolaang Mongondow Selatan Regency; and (2) the intensity of pest infestation on these rice varieties within the same location. The research was conducted over a three-month period, from December 2019 to February 2020, in rice cultivation areas owned by local farmers in Tolotoyon Village. A Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) was employed, with treatments consisting of three rice varieties—Ciherang, Inpari 9, and Situ Bagendit—each replicated three times. The experiment was implemented at three separate sites, each approximately one hectare in size, with one rice variety planted per site. Sampling occurred three times at weekly intervals on ten-week-old plants. Parameters measured included the number of nymphs and adults captured. The intensity of pest attack was visually assessed based on the characteristic symptoms of walang sangit damage observed on rice panicles during the generative phase. The results demonstrated that the highest pest population was recorded on the Ciherang variety, averaging 6.8 individuals, followed by Inpari 9 with 5.6, and the lowest on Situ Bagendit at 3.1 individuals. Correspondingly, the levels of pest-induced damage were highest on Inpari 9 (7.0%), followed by Ciherang (6.1%), and lowest on Situ Bagendit (3.1%). Variations in pest population density and attack intensity among rice varieties are attributed to inherent varietal characteristics such as shoot number and grain color.

Keywords: Rice varieties, Leptocorisa oratorius, pest population, infestation intensity

Abstract:  
This study examines the management process of the Public Market in Pasan Sub-district, which currently operates in a manner inconsistent with established regulations. The management policy of the Pasan Sub-district market continues to face challenges due to the absence of clear technical implementation guidelines. Furthermore, not all stakeholders relevant to the management policy of the People's Market are adequately involved; for instance, only certain implementing agencies such as the Department of Trade, Industry, Cooperatives, UMKM, and Market authorities participate in its execution. Market facilities are underutilized and often inadequate to meet operational needs. The primary objective of this research is to assess the implementation of the management policy of Pasar Rakyat Pasan in South Minahasa Regency. This study employs Charles O’Jones’ policy implementation theory, specifically focusing on the dimensions of organizing, interpretation, and implementation. A qualitative methodology with a descriptive approach is adopted, wherein the researcher serves as the primary instrument and data is collected from seven informants through observation, interviews, and document analysis. Findings indicate that the policy implementation of the Pasan Village Market management in South Minahasa Regency has been suboptimal. This is attributed to the insufficient involvement of key stakeholders in policy execution, resulting in management issues such as inappropriate market utilization, limited operational funding, inadequate facilities and infrastructure, poor waste management, and lack of electricity and clean water supply. Based on these findings, it is recommended that cooperation be enhanced among the Public Market management team, policy implementers at Pasan Rakyat, and the Department of Trade, Industry, Cooperatives, UMKM, and Market. These entities should not only fulfill their roles as executors but also actively engage in ongoing monitoring and evaluation to ensure the policy achieves its intended targets.  

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Public Market Management

Customer satisfaction in the service industry constitutes a fundamental determinant of organizational performance and has garnered considerable attention from service users. Within the banking sector, customer satisfaction assumes critical importance for understanding customer needs and preferences, thereby fostering customer loyalty. Specifically, customer satisfaction serves as the initial step in promoting continuous patronage of banking services. This study aims to examine the effects of perceived value and perceived price on customer satisfaction, the impact of perceived value and perceived price on customer loyalty, and the influence of customer satisfaction on customer loyalty. The theoretical framework underpinning this research includes constructs of perceived value, perceived price, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty. The empirical investigation was carried out at the central office of PT. Bank Sulut, involving a sample of 100 randomly selected bank customers to facilitate efficient and timely data collection. Data analysis employed Path Analysis following preliminary assessments of validity, reliability, and classical assumptions. The findings indicate that perceived value and perceived price significantly and positively influence customer satisfaction; perceived value does not exert a significant positive effect on customer loyalty; perceived price significantly and positively affects customer loyalty; and customer satisfaction positively and significantly contributes to customer loyalty. 

Keywords: perceived value, perceived price, customer satisfaction, customer loyalty

This research aims to assess the population density of Tarsius tumpara across production and protected forest areas on Mount Tamata, Siau Island. The study was carried out over a one-month period in March 2014, encompassing seven sampling plots within each forest type. Population density and frequency of Tarsius tumpara were estimated using sampling techniques and analyzed through descriptive statistical methods. Comparative analyses were performed to evaluate differences in sighting density and frequency between production and protected forests. Habitat characteristics were described using the Importance Value Index (IVI). Furthermore, correlation and simple regression analyses were employed to examine the relationship between vegetation variables and the frequency of Tarsius tumpara sightings. Total basal area and shrub cover within the plots were utilized as predictors of sighting frequency. Results indicated that protected forests exhibited a Tarsius tumpara density of 3.29 individuals/ha and 0.86 groups/ha, whereas production forests showed lower densities of 2.14 individuals/ha and 0.47 groups/ha. The mean sighting frequency was 1.64 times per day (ranging from 0.02 to 3.26) in protected forests compared to 1.07 times per day (range 0.21 to 1.93) in production forests. A positive relationship was observed between shrub cover and Tarsius tumpara presence, indicating that increased shrub density corresponds with higher population density. The species was predominantly encountered in habitats dominated by Pandanus species and was absent from areas dominated by Myristica fragrans. 

Keywords: Population density, Sighting frequency, Habitat characteristics, Tarsius tumpara, Siau Island

The ongoing changes in land use driven by population growth and development activities within the development sector have been progressively intensifying. These alterations substantially influence surface runoff characteristics, leading to an increase in the runoff coefficient and consequently heightening the risk of flooding. A critical parameter in flood management is the surface runoff coefficient, commonly denoted as C, which serves as an important indicator of physical disturbances within a watershed. This study aims to quantify the surface runoff coefficient (C) across different land use types, specifically forest land, shrub land, and open land. Employing a randomized block design for data collection, the study subsequently applied analysis of variance to examine the data. Field measurements revealed that the surface runoff coefficients for forest and shrub lands differ significantly from that of open land, with values of 0.0019 and 0.0013 respectively, compared to 0.0036 for open land. Additionally, infiltration rates were recorded as 210 mm/hour for shrub land, 99 mm/hour for forest land, and 69.6 mm/hour for open land. The comparatively lower infiltration rate observed in forest land is attributed to the study area's forest being an artificial plantation characterized by specific vegetation strata and root systems that differ from those of natural forests.  
Keywords: surface runoff coefficient, infiltration rate, surface runoff

Hypertension is a non-communicable disease that often occurs in the community and causes serious health problems. The number of cases of hypertension that occurs in Indonesia increases the exploration of the use of natural ingredients, one of which is African leaves as a traditional medicine that is developed into herbal medicine and standardized herbal medicine. Flavonoids are known to have the ability to inhibit the activity of the angiotensin-converting enzyme. African leaves are one of the plants that contain flavonoid secondary metabolites that can be obtained by the MAE (Microwave Assisted Extraction) extraction method using 70% ethanol as a solvent. Induction of hypertension was carried out by giving 2% prednisone-NaCl solution for 21 days, the positive control used was the ACEI captopril group with a dose of 0.45 mg/200 g BW and the preparation of African leaf extract was made in 3 doses, namely the dose 100 mg.kg-1 BW, dose II 150 mg.kg-1 BW, and dose III 200 mg.kg-1 BW) given orally. Blood pressure was measured every 7 days using a CODA® non-invasive blood pressure measuring device. The results showed that the African leaf has an antihypertensive effect where the most effective dose in lowering blood pressure is dose III 200 mg.kg-1 BW with a blood pressure reduction time of 14 days.

This research, titled "Illocutionary Acts in the Gospel of Matthew: A Pragmatic Analysis," employs a descriptive methodological approach. The study aims to identify, categorize, and analyze the various types and functions of illocutionary acts present within the Gospel of Matthew. Data analysis was conducted utilizing the theoretical framework proposed by Searle (1979) as cited in Leech (1983). Findings reveal four primary categories of illocutionary acts in the Gospel: assertives, directives, commissives, and declaratives, while expressives were notably absent among the characters. Within assertives, the function of stating was evident; however, functions such as asserting, suggesting, complaining, and reporting did not appear in the text. The directives employed by Jesus, His disciples, and other figures included requesting, commanding, advising, and asking, whereas ordering and recommending were not observed. Regarding commissives, promising was identified as a function, although uttering was not present. Declarative functions detected in the Gospel consisted of granting and naming, while promoting and punishing were not found. This study contributes to the field of linguistics by enhancing the understanding of illocutionary acts through pragmatic analysis, thereby supporting the advancement of language development research.

Keywords: Illocutionary Acts, Types and Functions, Gospel of Matthew, Pragmatics

The contamination of gasoline has escalated in tandem with the growing number of automobiles in recent years. As a consequence of the increased presence of lead pollutant (Pb) in the air, the risk of human exposure to this hazardous substance has intensified. Lead exposure is associated with various adverse health effects, including hypertension and occupational fatigue. Workers at gas stations (SPBU) constitute a high-risk group due to their frequent exposure to gasoline fumes, vehicular exhaust, and smoke. This study aimed to examine the relationship between blood lead levels and the incidence of hypertension among SPBU workers in Manado municipality. Employing a cross-sectional design, the study included a sample of 96 respondents. Bivariate analysis revealed a positive, statistically significant, albeit weak, correlation between blood lead levels and hypertension incidence (p < 0.05; r_pb = 0.324; r_pb^2 = 0.105). Furthermore, multivariate analysis identified blood lead level as a significant predictor of hypertension (p < 0.05), accounting for an effective contribution of 6.74%. These findings indicate that blood lead levels are significantly associated with and serve as a predictor for hypertension, even after controlling for other variables. Consequently, it is imperative to implement preventive measures addressing lead exposure, including regular health screenings and the enforcement of occupational health and safety protocols for SPBU workers.

Keywords: blood lead level, hypertension

ABSTRACT Coconut oil is one of the potential coconut processing products to increase added value for farmers in the North Sulawesi area. The processing of coconut oil has actually been done quite a lot by North Sulawesi farmers, but they still use traditional equipment. This method of processing takes a long time and is inefficient. The government has distributed mechanical equipment for smallscale coconut oil processing and socialized it to several farmer groups. The purpose of this study was to technically analyze the performance of small-scale coconut oil processing systems for 2 farmer groups. This research was conducted with an experimental method in which some of the equipment was tested for its capacity. The material used is coconuts aged 11-12 months, as many as 150 coconuts. Coconut processing on the existing equipment system was carried out in 3 (three) replications, with the number of each replication being 50 coconuts. The stages of coconut processing carried out in this study were, peeling, washing, cleaning, draining, squeezing, separating and allowed to stand for 24 hours. After 24 hours, the resulting coconut cream is put in an oil cooking machine and heated at an average temperature of 1500 C for 2 hours. The results of cooking are filtered, to take the coconut oil. The results showed that the small-scale coconut oil processing equipment system can be maximized to produce commercial coconut oil products. The performance of the tool is influenced by the existing power transmission engine, and the skill of the operator in each stage of work is very important. It is recommended for maximum use of the equipments, given special training to the operators. Keywords: Coconut Oil, Processing Equipment Systems, Farmers, Operators.

Celery (Apium graveolens L.) is a widely recognized vegetable crop in Indonesia, valued for its culinary and medicinal properties. However, challenges persist in achieving high-quality celery production that meets consumer preferences. To address these challenges, suitable technologies capable of enhancing both the quality and yield of celery in accordance with market demands are essential. Among available methods, the hydroponic film engineering technique presents a viable solution, particularly for cultivation in limited spaces. Despite its potential, limited research has been conducted concerning the optimal nutrient concentrations within hydroponic systems for celery cultivation. This study aims to evaluate the impact of varying concentrations of AB mix nutrient solution on the growth and yield of celery cultivated using the Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) hydroponic system, and to identify the concentration that optimizes these outcomes. The experimental design employed was a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) comprising three nutrient concentration treatments—900 ppm (p1), 1200 ppm (p2), and 1500 ppm (p3)—each replicated four times. Findings indicate that the concentration of AB mix nutrients significantly influences both growth and yield parameters of celery plants, with the highest concentration of 1500 ppm (p3) yielding the most favorable results.

Keywords: AB mix nutrient solution, NFT hydroponics, Celery (Apium graveolens L.)

The Indonesian nation, as a constituent of the global community, must actively engage in fostering effective governance to enhance its competitiveness in the current era of globalization. Ministerial Regulation No. 113 of 2014 pertains to the management of village finances, specifically outlined in Article 5, which governs the formulation and implementation of policies related to the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget. The management of village budget revenue and expenditure is a critical factor in achieving good governance at the village level. This study aims to evaluate whether the implementation of the revenue and expenditure budget policies aligns with the provisions stipulated in Ministerial Regulation No. 113 of 2014, as well as to identify challenges encountered during the policy’s implementation. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, the research analyzes the execution of the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget policy from the stages of planning through to accountability. Findings indicate that the policy implementation in Lowian Village is generally satisfactory and complies with the regulations mandated by Ministerial Regulation No. 113 of 2014. However, certain external issues have been identified, including the presence of trees located adjacent to roads and plots of land owned by residents, alongside a lack of comprehensive understanding among village officials regarding the technical aspects of financial reporting. 

Keywords: Policy Implementation, Accountability, Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget

ABSTRACT This review explains the way how online marketing has been replacing traditional marketing in terms of marketing mix. This replacement might happen, because online marketing can give advantages, i.e., offering on-time delivery, increasing effectiveness of two way interactions between buyer and seller, and creating online communities (Szmigin, et al, 2005). The transition of atoms to bits format reflects that tangible products in traditional marketing is being digitalized. The marketing strategies also move from multi level product concept to customer customization. In online marketing, buyers can control over prices, hence pricing trend has been moving from fixed price to dynamic price. In terms of promotion, online marketing becomes a complementary of traditional communication tools, where the strategy has a tendency to move from personnel selling to direct marketing. However, there are some debates whether online marketing will replace the position of traditional marketing. This review applies Indonesia as a measurement of this transition. It could be argued that in short run, commonly, the customers in Indonesia still remains in traditional marketing, because it dominates the business systems and cultures. There are some factors impeding the shift, i.e., lack in infrastructure and capital investment. However, in long run, online marketing is supposed to replace traditional marketing but incompletely. Keywords: traditional marketing, online marketing, marketing mix

The present study, entitled "Verbs in English and Tonsawang Language: A Contrastive Analysis," seeks to identify and examine the various types of verbs in both languages and to elucidate the differences between them. Data pertaining to the English language were sourced from a range of books, internet resources, and relevant theoretical frameworks, while data on the Tonsawang language were obtained through interviews with knowledgeable informants. This investigation was conducted using a contrastive analysis approach. The analysis is grounded in Frank’s (1972) classification theory, which categorizes verbs based on their complements into predicating or linking verbs, transitive and intransitive verbs, and reflexive verbs, and based on verb form into auxiliary or lexical verbs, and finite or non-finite verbs. To facilitate the comparison between the two languages, Lado’s (1957) concept of contrastive analysis was employed, which posits that juxtaposing a target language with a learner’s first language can help predict and illustrate patterns that influence the ease or difficulty of language acquisition. The findings revealed that, while English encompasses all verb types as classified by Frank (1972), the Tonsawang language lacks linking verbs and non-finite verbs. Theoretically, this research contributes to the advancement of knowledge in contrastive analysis, particularly with respect to verb usage in English and Tonsawang. Practically, the study may serve as a valuable reference for future investigations in this domain.

Keywords: Verb Types in English, Tonsawang Language, Contrastive Analysis

The present study aimed to evaluate the impact of replacing corn with molasses in the diet on the performance of rabbits. A total of 25 weaned rabbits, each aged six weeks, were individually housed in separate cages. The experimental framework employed a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with five treatment groups and five replicates per treatment. The dietary treatments consisted of a control ration containing corn without molasses (R0), and four additional rations in which corn was replaced by molasses at levels of 25% (R1), 50% (R2), 75% (R3), and 100% (R4), respectively. Key performance indicators assessed included feed intake, weight gain, feed conversion ratio, and energy consumption. The results indicated that average daily feed intake ranged from 78.07 to 95.20 g per head, weight gain varied between 9.7 and 12.02 g per head, feed conversion ratios spanned 7.90 to 8.71, and energy consumption measured between 2732.54 and 3076.10 Kcal/kg. Statistical analysis revealed that substituting corn with molasses produced significant differences (P < 0.01) in feed intake, weight gain, and energy consumption. It is therefore concluded that molasses can effectively replace corn in rabbit diets up to a substitution level of 75%, corresponding to 35.25% inclusion in the feed formulation.  

Keywords: Molasses, corn, rabbit, feed intake, weight gain

This study aims to examine the impact of agricultural commodity prices on inflation in the city of Manado. The analysis was conducted over the period from September 2013 to February 2014, utilizing secondary data sourced from the Central Bureau of Statistics of North Sulawesi Province. The dataset comprises time series data spanning the years 2004 to 2013. Multiple linear regression analysis was employed, facilitated by SPSS Statistics version 20, to evaluate the relationship between variables. The findings indicate that the coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.860, or 86 percent, while the adjusted coefficient of determination (R²_adj) is 0.684, equivalent to 68.4 percent. An R² value of 86 percent suggests that inflation in grains, vegetables, nuts, fruits, and spices collectively accounts for 86 percent of the inflation variance observed in Manado, with the remaining 14 percent attributable to factors not incorporated in the model. Among the commodities studied, nuts demonstrated the highest contribution at 0.289 percent, whereas the commodity with the lowest impact registered at -0.438 percent.

Keywords: Agricultural commodity prices, Inflation, Contribution

The Rurukan region, characterized as a plateau area, represents a promising site for the development of strawberry cultivation. This region holds significant potential not only as a source of livelihood for local farmers but also as a key area for the advancement of strawberry commodities. The objective of this study is to examine the complete process of strawberry farming practiced by farmers, encompassing stages from cultivation to the marketing of the produce. Additionally, the study aims to assess the income levels generated from strawberry farming in Rurukan Village, located within the Tomohon sub-district. The research was conducted over a period of three months, utilizing primary data collected directly from the Kina farmer groups in Rurukan. Findings indicate that the income obtained from strawberry cultivation over one season, comprising eight harvests for 1000 plants, amounts to Rp. 20,887,043. The total production cost for cultivating these 1000 strawberry plants was Rp. 5,377,957, while the total revenue reached Rp. 26,265,000. An analysis of the Revenue-Cost Ratio (R/C) revealed a value of 4.92, suggesting that for every one rupiah spent on strawberry farming, farmers receive a return of 4.92 rupiah. These results demonstrate that strawberry farming in Rurukan Village is a profitable enterprise.

This study seeks to quantify the soil erodibility factor (K) at multiple elevations along the Manado-Tomohon road corridor. A stratified random sampling technique was employed to collect soil samples, which were subsequently analyzed for texture using the pipette method. The resulting data were plotted on a soil texture triangle to ascertain the corresponding K values at each altitude. The investigation focused on several variables: (1) slope gradient, (2) land use, (3) soil texture, and (4) the calculated K value. The collected data were categorized into three K value classes and organized into tables to facilitate assessment, followed by a descriptive interpretation. Findings revealed K values at various elevations as follows: 0.379 at 200 meters above sea level (asl), 0.393 at 300 m asl, 0.384 at 400 m asl, 0.397 at 500 m asl, 0.376 at 600 m asl, 0.370 at 700 m asl, and 0.430 at 800 m asl. These results indicate that soil erodibility K values remain relatively high across the altitudinal gradient studied.  

Keywords: Soil erodibility factor (K), elevation, soil texture, land use

Background: Response time refers to the speed at which patients receive medical treatment, measured from the moment the patient seeks care; an optimal response time is considered to be within five minutes. Violence, encompassing both physical and verbal forms, constitutes aggressive behavior that infringes upon an individual’s freedom or dignity. This study aims to examine the relationship between emergency response time, outpatient waiting time, and incidents of violence experienced by nurses at the General Hospital of Luwuk Banggai District.

Methodology: The research was conducted between August and September 2019, involving nurses employed at the Public Hospital of Luwuk. Out of a total population of 120 nurses, a sample of 60 respondents was selected. The primary variables investigated included response time, outpatient waiting time, and manifestations of violent behavior. Data were analyzed using the Chi-square statistical test.

Results: Findings indicated that 55.00% of respondents assessed the pattern of emergency response time management at the Luwuk Banggai District General Hospital as adequate. Furthermore, 53.33% of participants considered the management of outpatient waiting times to be very satisfactory. Regarding violent behavior, 63.34% of respondents reported experiencing physical violence, which predominantly involved acts such as damaging hospital property, including breaking glass, chairs, benches, and various other equipment.

Conclusion: This study concludes that there is a significant relationship between emergency response time and the occurrence of violent behavior towards nurses. Enhancing the effectiveness of response procedures, specifically through the implementation of ABCD protocols, alongside improvements in human resources, facilities, infrastructure, and the management of emergency and outpatient services, is essential. Additionally, the association between outpatient waiting time and service quality is underscored, with key dimensions including timely service delivery, ease of meeting patient needs, comfort and hospitality, aspects of human resources, attentive care, and other related factors.

This study aimed to assess the effects of the PNPM program on the welfare of residents in the rural village of Wasian, located in the Dimembe sub-district of North Minahasa District. Data collection was conducted through interviews, employing purposive sampling to select participants. The sample consisted of 22 respondents, including 17 individuals residing in the traditional, relatively disadvantaged areas, and 5 individuals living along the newly constructed road. The welfare parameters for the rural community were evaluated based on two principal indicators: social welfare and economic prosperity. Social welfare was assessed through (1) physical development components; (2) public perceptions, which encompassed (a) views on the direct impact of development activities and (b) opinions concerning social dimensions such as education, information access, sports, and social interaction; and (3) housing ownership. Economic wellbeing was measured by changes in family income levels.

Findings indicate that PNPM rural initiatives positively influenced both social and economic aspects of community welfare. From a social perspective, physical infrastructure development was fully realized, as evidenced by the construction of roads, bridges, and culverts. Community members perceived improvements in road conditions, reduced flooding due to drainage systems, and easier bridge crossings. Regarding education, schoolchildren gained access to educational facilities without the need for motorized transport. In terms of information access, residents reported enhanced ease in obtaining necessary information, facilitated by improved community infrastructure. Regarding sports, existing recreational facilities experienced increased utilization and functionality. Furthermore, social interactions within the community became more active, exemplified by more frequent greetings and engagement among residents.

Economically, there was a notable increase in home ownership and family income, indicating enhanced prosperity among the population. Overall, the PNPM program has contributed significantly to improving the welfare of the rural community in Wasian.

The rapid physical expansion of Manado city has significantly impacted its urban structure, resulting in the current city map being outdated due to the presence of newly constructed streets not depicted on existing cartographic representations. Consequently, an accurate delineation of the city’s street network is essential to effectively reflect Manado's ongoing physical growth. The utilization of the Global Positioning System (GPS) is imperative for generating a precise street network map. Such a map serves as a fundamental tool for capturing scientific data related to the street network, employing appropriate signs and information to ensure clarity and ease of comprehension.

In this study, the creation of Manado's street network map involved the employment of the Garmin 76CSx GPS model. GPS technology provides a highly accurate method for determining specific points on the earth’s surface by receiving signals from satellites and performing positional calculations based on these signals. The research methodology comprised two critical stages: the data collection phase and the computerized drawing phase.

During data collection, a comprehensive GPS survey was conducted across all streets within Manado’s geographical boundaries. Subsequently, the drawing phase involved transferring the collected GPS data to a computer system, where it was processed utilizing software tools including MapSource and AutoCAD 2008. By conducting a detailed street network tracking survey, precise coordinate points throughout Manado were established. Identifying the internal nodes of streets was a necessary step to facilitate the accurate processing of these coordinates.

The drawing procedure was executed through several phases, beginning with the calibration of GPS data for integration into the street network map. Comparative analysis between the GPS-derived map and the Bakosurtanal map revealed notable discrepancies: the GPS-based map included newly developed streets absent from the Bakosurtanal representation, while some older streets formerly depicted were no longer present, having been replaced by residential developments. 

Keywords: Map, Street Network, GPS

Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are productive economic enterprises owned by individuals or business entities. Business activities undertaken by small and medium enterprises require a financial statement that reflects the business activities undertaken during one period. The financial statements are a form of corporate management accountability by management to external and internal parties. Seeing the importance of usability, the financial statements should be structured according to the applicable standards in order to be interpreted with the same concept and understanding by its users. The generally accepted Financial Accounting Standards make it difficult for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) who only have minimal accounting knowledge in preparing financial statements. The Financial Accounting Standards Entity Without Public Accountability (SAK ETAP) comes with the aim to accommodate the needs of entities that have no significant public accountability in the conduct of their business such as SMEs. The purpose of this study is to determine the application of Financial Accounting Standards Entity Without Public Accountability (SAK ETAP) Against Manado Financial Report. This research uses descriptive-comparative research type. The results show that Manado Manado has not fully implemented the Financial Accounting Standards of Non-Accountable Public Entity (SAK ETAP) in its financial statements. This is because the financial manpower of Manado Manado does not have sufficient knowledge about the Financial Accounting Standards of Non-Public Accountable Entity (SAK ETAP) so that it becomes a factor that Manado Bahaga has not fully implemented SAK ETAP. Instead, the company employs a competent financial personnel in their field so that they can produce financial statements in accordance with SAK ETAP.Keywords: SAK ETAP, Financial Statements, SMEs

Language constitutes a fundamental characteristic that distinguishes humans from other living beings. It functions as a medium through which individuals communicate. In producing utterances, people do not merely articulate sentences but also perform actions through their speech. This phenomenon is identified as speech acts, with the illocutionary act representing a key component within this framework. The present study examines a specific category of illocutionary acts, namely conflictive acts, as manifested in the film adaptation of C.S. Lewis’s *The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe*. Data were collected by analyzing interactions among the characters within the film. The analysis employed Leech’s theoretical model, which classifies conflictive acts into four types: threatening, reprimanding, accusing, and cursing. Although the cursing category was not observed in the current research, it is anticipated that future studies may identify its occurrence. Furthermore, it is recommended that subsequent investigations apply alternative theories of illocutionary acts to diverse sources, such as native language discourse, novels, short stories, and other media.  

Keywords: Speech acts; Illocutionary acts; Conflictive acts; The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe; Film analysis.

THE EFFECT OF THE USE OF PAPAYA LEAVES SUBSTITUTED TO BASAL DIET ON THE PERCENTAGE OF CARCASS AND ABDOMINAL FAT PERCENTAGE OF BROILER CHICKEN. This study aims to determine the effect of papaya leaf meal substituted to basal diet on the carcass weight, percentage of carcass, and abdominal fat of broilers. This study used 80 unsexed broilers, day old chick (DOC). The experiment used a completely randomized design (CRD) consisting of 4 treatments and 5 replications. The arrangement of the experimental treatments was as follows: R₀ = 100% basal diet (BD), 0% papaya leaf meal (PLM), R₁ = 95% BD + 5% PLM, R₂ = 90% BD + 10% PLM, R₃ = 85% BD + 15% PLM. The results showed that partial replacement of the basal diet with with papaya leaf meal had no significant effect on carcass weight and the percentage of broiler abdominal fat. The treatment gave a very significant difference on the percentage of carcass. On carcass percentage results showed that R0 was highly significant different from R3 but not significantly different with R2 and R1. Treatment R1 was significantly different from R3 but not significantly different from R2, whereas between treatments R2 and R3 were significantly different. Based on the results of this study it can be stated that the use of papaya leaf meal up to level of 15% can produce a good proportion of carcass and abdominal fat. Keywords: broiler, papaya leaf meal, carcasses, abdominal fat.

This study aimed to evaluate the inhibitory potential of ethanol extracts derived from the leaves, flowers, and stems of the *Impatiens balsamica* plant against the growth of *Aeromonas hydrophila*. The plant is known to contain bioactive compounds such as balsamica naphthoquinone, coumarin derivatives, tannins, flavonoids, and steroids, which possess antimicrobial properties. *Aeromonas hydrophila*, an opportunistic pathogen commonly present in aquatic environments, frequently causes disease in fish subjected to stress or unfavorable conditions. The antibacterial activity was assessed using the spread plate method. Data collected included extract yields, bacterial inoculation outcomes, and inhibition zone measurements, which were subsequently analyzed, visually documented, and described in detail. Maceration extraction with 70% ethanol yielded concentrated extracts weighing 28.75 g (leaves), 12.82 g (flowers), and 29.48 g (stems). The antimicrobial assay demonstrated that all three extracts exhibited inhibitory effects on *A. hydrophila*, as evidenced by clear zones surrounding the paper discs. According to established classification criteria, the leaf and stem extracts showed strong antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones measuring 11.2 mm and 13.7 mm, respectively. Notably, the flower extract exhibited a very strong inhibitory effect, producing an inhibition zone of 21.4 mm. 

Keywords: ethanol extract, *Impatiens balsamica* L., *Aeromonas hydrophila*, antibacterial activity assay
