This study aims to analyze the current production conditions and forecast rice production and demand in the period from 2012 to 2030. The research utilizes time series data spanning from 1996 to 2011, encompassing variables such as population growth, cultivated area, production volume, and productivity. These data were analyzed descriptively using tabular presentations, with Microsoft Excel 2007 employed as the data processing tool. The findings indicate that both rice production and demand in North Sulawesi have fluctuated annually, although they exhibit an overall increasing trend. Throughout the sixteen-year period, the province was unable to fulfill its rice requirements. Projections based on an average annual population growth rate of 1.42% from 2012 to 2030 suggest that rice demand will continue to exceed supply. When population growth is assumed at 1.28% annually for 2012 to 2020, North Sulawesi remains in a rice-deficit condition despite a declining growth rate in demand, with self-sufficiency expected to be achieved between 2025 and 2030. Furthermore, under a lower average annual population growth rate of 1.1% over the subsequent nineteen years, North Sulawesi is projected to attain a rice surplus.

The majority of women continue to experience constraints related to poverty, whether these arise from structural, cultural, or natural factors. From the perspective of structural poverty—defined as poverty stemming from discriminatory policies or regulations—women’s marginalization remains a prevailing reality. This is manifested in persistent discriminatory practices affecting women’s access to education, economic opportunities (including employment, wages, and economic independence), as well as political participation.

The methodology of this study was primarily guided by the research questions posed. Accordingly, a mixed-methods approach combining qualitative and quantitative techniques was employed. The qualitative component aimed to examine the patterns of women’s empowerment initiatives directed at coastal communities by the District Government of Sangihe. In contrast, the quantitative approach sought to measure the effectiveness of these programs by assessing intermediate outcomes and to evaluate the perceived impact (final outcomes) on women following their engagement with the programs implemented by the Technical Implementation Unit of PNPM Mandiri, particularly in relation to improving the living standards of beneficiary households.

Data analysis was conducted on responses collected from a questionnaire administered to 60 female respondents, each a head or member of a household, dispersed across three sample villages within West Tahuna subdistrict, Sangihe Islands Regency. The findings are structured into three sections: the first describes factors influencing women’s empowerment, focusing on (1) educational attainment and (2) training and skill development; the second section addresses the prevailing conditions of household living standards; and the third section presents statistical analyses accompanied by a discussion of the effects of empowerment factors on family living standards.

Keywords: Coastal Women’s Empowerment Policy.

South Minahasa Regency, located in the North Sulawesi province, possesses agro-climatic conditions conducive to rice cultivation. This study employed simulation models to evaluate the growth and development of rice crops under varying agro-climatic environments within the district. The primary objectives were to assess the rice production potential and to develop a spatial distribution map of rice production potential in South Minahasa Regency. Data collection involved climatic parameters, including solar radiation, air temperature, air humidity, irradiation, and precipitation, along with geographical coordinates (latitude and longitude). The Rice Shierary V.2.1 simulation model was utilized to estimate rice production potential, while satellite imagery processed through ArcView 3.3 software facilitated the mapping of production potential.

The findings revealed that the potential rice yields were 6.11 tons per hectare in Popontolen Village, 5.73 tons per hectare in Pakuweru Village, and 9.00 tons per hectare in Karowa Village. Among these, Karowa Village exhibited the highest production potential, attributed to its optimal average temperature of 23.12 °C, mean rainfall of 293.50 mm, and evapotranspiration rate of 103.42 mm, all of which favor rice growth and development. Notably, the estimated potential yields surpass the official rice productivity data for South Minahasa District from 2010 to 2014, suggesting that rice production in the region has not been fully optimized.

The outcomes of this research are intended to inform relevant stakeholders, particularly the Department of Agriculture and Livestock of South Minahasa Regency, in enhancing rice production. Recommendations include improving access to high-quality seeds, equitable fertilizer distribution, rehabilitation of dams and irrigation infrastructure, and the promotion of mechanized agricultural tools, all aimed at increasing productivity and farmer incomes.

This research endeavors to forecast the bankruptcy of property companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the period from 2015 to 2019, employing the Altman Z-Score model, which utilizes five financial ratios as key variables. The study adopts a qualitative approach with a descriptive methodology, relying on secondary data obtained indirectly from internet sources. The analytical method applied, however, is quantitative, as the investigation involves numerical data processing. The financial data used in this study are sourced from the companies' financial statements, publicly available on the Indonesia Stock Exchange website (http://www.idx.co.id). A purposive sampling technique was implemented to select a sample of 10 companies for analysis. Corporate bankruptcy is defined as a situation in which a company fails to meet its financial obligations; such a state can be anticipated through meticulous financial statement analysis using predictive tools. In this context, the Altman Z-Score model serves as the predictive instrument for evaluating the financial health of the selected property companies. The findings indicate that, among the 10 companies in the property and real estate sector, nine exhibited consistent bankruptcy predictions throughout the 2015-2019 period, whereas one company demonstrated variable results based on the Altman Z-Score model.

This study aims to elucidate the competencies of medical personnel employed at community health centers in Taripa Subdistrict, Pamona language area, East Poso, within the framework of advancing public administration knowledge. A fundamental issue identified in these clinics pertains to the implementation of health technical units operating under the supervision of District/City Health Services, which continues to face challenges related to the capabilities of the medical staff. Employing a qualitative research design, data were gathered through interviews, observations, and documentary analysis. The collected data were then subjected to categorization and reduction processes, followed by organization into narrative form, thereby producing a coherent series of meaningful information aligned with the research questions. Subsequently, interpretation and conclusion stages were conducted based on the narrative sequence, enabling comprehensive responses to the research problems. The findings indicate that the competencies of the medical personnel at the Taripa Subdistrict community health centers—evaluated in terms of intellectual ability, interpersonal skills, adaptability, and results-oriented capabilities—have not been adequately developed. Recommendations for enhancement include improving staffing status, providing incentives commensurate with workload, and refining planning procedures through the preparation of service plans tailored to the operational conditions of the work units, as well as involving medical personnel in training activities that correspond to the health service needs, thereby fostering their competencies within the Public Health Centers.  
Keywords: Competency, Employment, Medical Personnel

The Wori District, encompassing an area of 90.704 km², is part of the North Minahasa Regency and is engaged in the cultivation and processing of oil palm plantations, coconut flour, nata de coco, coconut shell charcoal, and coconut trees. Among these products, coconut flour, an oil derivative known as integrated coconut, has garnered considerable demand, with buyers distributed across nearly all regions of the world. Historically, the primary market for coconut flour was concentrated in Eastern Europe; however, its demand has recently expanded rapidly and now spans multiple continents globally. In response to concerns regarding the availability of coconut flour, there is a pressing need to promote the development of coconut crops, particularly given the declining supply of mature coconuts. The present study aims to evaluate the land potential for coconut (Cocos nucifera L.) cultivation within the Wori District of North Minahasa Regency. This research seeks to provide valuable insights and recommendations for both governmental authorities and local communities involved in coconut cultivation efforts in the region.

The study was conducted in the Wori District, North Minahasa Regency, complemented by soil analyses performed at the Soil Laboratory of the Faculty of Agriculture, Sam Ratulangi University, Manado. The research activities took place between July 2009 and September 2011. Employing a survey methodology based on land unit classifications, the study examined variables including slope, effective soil depth, texture, erosion status, drainage, soil type, and land use. Collected data were organized into tabular formats and subsequently analyzed descriptively to classify the suitability of land as appropriate or inappropriate for coconut cultivation, based on the species’ growth requirements.

Findings indicate that the Wori region experiences a B1 climate type, characterized by 7 to 9 wet months and fewer than 2 dry months annually. The district’s elevation ranges from 0 to 610 meters above sea level, with terrain varying from relatively flat and undulating to mountainous forms. Slopes within the study area are predominantly less than 15%. Analysis of soil physical and chemical properties—including effective depth, texture, drainage, and pH—suggests that the soils possess favorable conditions for coconut cultivation. By comparing these soil and climatic conditions with the known ecological requirements for coconut growth, it was determined that the Wori region has a coconut plantation development potential across an area totaling 4,637.80 hectares.

Hemothorax denotes the accumulation of blood within the pleural cavity, characterized by a pleural effusion containing a hematocrit level that is at least 50% of the peripheral blood hematocrit. Pneumothorax is defined as the partial or complete collapse of the lung resulting from the presence of air in the space between the parietal and visceral pleura. This entrapped air exerts pressure on the lung's external surface, leading to its collapse, which typically affects only a portion of the lung. Patients with pneumothorax frequently present with pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, tachypnea, and tachycardia. On physical examination, breath sounds may be diminished, and the affected hemithorax often exhibits hyper-resonance on percussion, particularly in cases of larger pneumothoraces. Pneumothorax can be categorized into simple and tension types, and further classified as open, closed, or occult pneumothorax. 

Hemopneumothorax, characterized by the simultaneous presence of both blood and air within the pleural cavity, commonly arises from blunt or penetrating thoracic trauma, with stab wounds being a principal cause of penetrating injuries. Prompt diagnosis and management of hemopneumothorax are crucial for favorable patient outcomes. Thoracic trauma is implicated in approximately 60% of polytrauma cases. In the United States, trauma accounts for nearly 150,000 deaths annually and represents the leading cause of mortality in the general population, with approximately 50% of trauma-related deaths occurring immediately and fewer than 10-15% of patients surviving to hospital admission exhibiting critical vital signs.

Traumatic hemopneumothorax results from either blunt or penetrating injuries, and the patient’s respiratory response is influenced by various factors. Respiratory failure associated with trauma may arise directly due to lung injury or indirectly as a consequence of complications such as pulmonary infection, fibrothorax, or preexisting pulmonary disease. Needle aspiration is considered an obsolete intervention for hemopneumothorax management. The recommended therapeutic approach involves the complete evacuation of retained clots, typically achieved through tube thoracostomy. Placement of a chest tube generally suffices to effectively remove hemothorax contents and restore pulmonary function.
